items.content:
Government of India (GoI) has announced the sale (re-issue) of one dated security for a notified amount of ₹34,000 crore as per the following details:
Sr No Security Date of Repayment Notified Amount
(₹ Crore) GoI specific Notification Auction Date Settlement Date
1 6.94% GS 2036 May 11, 2036 34,000 F.No.4(1)-B(W&M)/2026 dated
November 09, 2026 November 13, 2026
(Friday) November 16, 2026
(Monday)
  Total   34,000      
2. GoI will have the option to retain additional subscription up to ₹2,000 crore against the security mentioned above.
3. The security will be sold through Reserve Bank of India Mumbai Office, Fort, Mumbai – 400001. The sale will be subject to the terms and conditions spelt out in the ‘Specific Notification’ mentioned above and the General Notification F.No.4(2)–B(W&M)/2018, dated March 26, 2025.
4. The auction will be conducted using multiple price method. Both competitive and non-competitive bids for the auction should be submitted in electronic format on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber system) on November 13, 2026 (Friday). The non-competitive bids should be submitted between 10:30 a.m. and 11:00 a.m. and the competitive bids should be submitted between 10:30 a.m. and 11:30 a.m. The result will be announced on the same day and payment by successful bidders will have to be made on November 16, 2026 (Monday).
5. Bids for underwriting of the Additional Competitive Underwriting (ACU) portion can be submitted by ‘Primary Dealers’ from 09:00 a.m. up to 09:30 a.m. on November 13, 2026 (Friday) on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber system).
6. The security will be eligible for “When Issued” trading for a period commencing from November 11, 2026 – November 13, 2026.
7. Operational guidelines for Government of India dated securities auction and other details are given in the Annex.
Ajit Prasad          
Deputy General Manager
(Communications)    
Press Release: 2026-2027/1474
ANNEX
Type of Auction
1. For multiple price-based auction, successful bids will get accepted at the respective quoted yield/price for the security. For uniform price-based auction, bids will get accepted at the cut off yield/price accepted in the auction.
2. The auction will be yield based for new security and price based for securities which are re-issued.
3. In case of a Floating Rate Bonds (FRB), the auction will be spread-based for new security and price based for securities which are reissued. At the time of placing bids for new FRB, the spread should be quoted in percentage terms.
Minimum Bid Size
4. The securities will be issued for a minimum amount of ₹10,000/- (nominal) and in multiples of ₹10,000/- thereafter.
Non-Competitive Segment
5. In all the auctions, Government security up to 5% of the notified amount for sale of individual security will be allotted to the eligible individuals and institutions under the Scheme for Non-competitive Bidding Facility in the Auctions of Government Securities. Individual investors can also place bids as per the non-competitive scheme through the Retail Direct portal (https://rbiretaildirect.org.in).
6. Each bank or Primary Dealer (PD) on the basis of firm orders received from their constituents will submit a single consolidated non-competitive bid for individual security on behalf of its constituents in electronic format on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber system).
7. Allotment under the non-competitive segment will be at the weighted average rate of yield/price of the successful bids that will emerge in the auction on the basis of the competitive bidding.
Submission of Bids
8. Both competitive and non-competitive bids for the auction should be submitted in electronic format on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber system).
9. Bids in physical form will not be accepted except in extraordinary circumstances.
Business Continuity Plan (BCP)-IT failure
10. Only in the event of system failure, physical bids will be accepted. Such physical bids should be submitted to the Public Debt Office, Mumbai through (email; Phone no: 022-22603456, 022-22603457, 022-22603190) in the prescribed form which can be obtained from RBI website (https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_ViewForms.aspx) before the auction timing ends.
11. In case of technical difficulties, Core Banking Operations Team should be contacted (email; Phone no: 022-69870466, 022-69870415).
12. For other auction related difficulties, IDMD auction team can be contacted (email; Phone no: 022-22702431, 022-22705125).
Multiple Bids
13. An investor can submit more than one competitive bid in electronic format on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber system).
14. The aggregate amount of bids submitted by an investor in an auction should not exceed the notified amount of auction.
Decision Making Process
15. On the basis of bids received, the Reserve Bank will determine the minimum price/maximum yield up to which tenders for purchase of Government Security will be accepted at the auctions.
16. Bids quoted at rates lower than the minimum price/higher than the maximum yield determined by the Reserve Bank of India will be rejected.
17. Reserve Bank of India will have the full discretion to accept or reject any or all bids either wholly or partially without assigning any reason.
Issue of Securities
18. Issue of securities to the successful bidders will be by credit to Subsidiary General Ledger Account (SGL) or to Constituents’ Subsidiary General Ledger Account (CSGL), maintained with Reserve Bank of India.
Periodicity of Interest Payment
19. Interest on the Government Security will generally be paid half-yearly other than in case of securities with non-standard maturities. The exact periodicity of coupon payment is invariably mentioned in the specific notification for the issue of security.
Underwriting of the Government Securities
20. The underwriting of the Government Securities under auctions by the ‘Primary Dealers’ will be as per the “Revised Scheme of Underwriting Commitment and Liquidity Support” announced by the Reserve Bank vide circular RBI/2007-08/186 dated November 14, 2007 as amended from time to time.
Eligibility for Repurchase Transactions (Repo)
21. The securities will be eligible for Repurchase Transactions (Repo) as per the conditions mentioned in Master Direction – Reserve Bank of India (Repurchase Transactions (Repo)) Directions, 2025 as amended from time to time.
Eligibility for ‘When Issued’ Trading
22. The securities will be eligible for “When Issued” trading in accordance with the guidelines on ‘When Issued transactions in Central Government Securities’ issued by the Reserve Bank of India vide circular No. RBI/2018-19/25 dated July 24, 2018 as amended from time to time.
Investment by Non-Residents
23. Investments by Non-Residents are subject to the guidelines on ‘Fully Accessible Route’ for Investment by Non-residents in Government Securities and other related guidelines as issued by the Reserve Bank from time to time.

items.content:
By Omeiza Ajayi
ABUJA – Nigeria’s president is not declared on the strength of a single national count. A chain of collation officers, each signing for the votes below them, builds the result from the polling unit up to the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC.
Read Also:
*Explainer: What INEC’s 2023 results in Lagos, Oyo, Osun actually reveal
*Why getting most votes is not enough to become Nigeria’s president
The chain starts when voting ends. Voters are accredited with the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System, BVAS, and the presiding officer counts the ballots in public and enters each party’s score on Form EC8A, the polling unit result sheet.
The presiding officer signs the form, and polling agents who are present countersign it. A poster version, Form EC60E, is pasted at the polling unit so voters can see what was recorded.
Collation then moves upward. INEC’s then chairman, Mahmood Yakubu, described the 2023 process as running through “four levels”: ward, local government area, LGA, state and national. At each level, an officer adds up the forms from the level below and records the total on a new form.
The election results forms
The ward collation officer adds up the Form EC8A sheets in the ward and records the total on Form EC8B. The LGA collation officer then adds up the ward sheets on Form EC8C.
At state level, the State Collation Officer for the Presidential Election (SCOPE) adds up the LGA results on Form EC8D. Katsina in 2023 shows what that form contains: 3,516,719 registered voters; 1,097,663 accredited; 1,058,673 valid votes, and 32,514 rejected.
Atiku Abubakar of the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, led with 489,045 votes against 482,283 for Bola Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress, APC.
The national stage takes place in Abuja, with the INEC Chairman acting as returning officer for the presidential election. That office is now held by Joash Amupitan, who succeeded Yakubu in October 2025.
In 2023, Yakubu set out the procedure at the national collation centre, where each state’s SCOPE presents the original Form EC8D.
“When all the SCOPES have presented their results,” the returning officer displays the sealed copies of Form EC8DA, the state-by-state summary, and Form EC8E, the declaration sheet. Polling agents are invited to comment before the winner is declared, and each agent receives duplicate copies afterwards.
Declaring winner
Declaring the winner involves more than adding up votes. The returning officer must also confirm that the candidate with the highest total reached one-quarter of the votes in enough states, as Section 134 of the Constitution requires.
The 2023 totals show the arithmetic. Yakubu put registered voters at 93,469,008; accredited voters at 25,286,616; valid votes at 24,025,940, and rejected votes at 939,278.
Tinubu polled 8,794,726; Atiku 6,984,520; Peter Obi of the Labour Party, LP, 6,101,533, and Rabiu Kwankwaso of the New Nigeria Peoples Party, NNPP, 1,496,687.
On the spread test, Tinubu’s lawyers told the election petition court that he scored 25 per cent in 29 states. They said Atiku managed that in 21 states and Obi in 16 states plus the Federal Capital Territory, FCT. Those figures come from Tinubu’s final written address, not from INEC’s declaration.
Electronic transmission
Electronic transmission has been the most contested part of the chain. INEC uploads polling unit sheets to its Result Viewing Portal, IReV. But under the Electoral Act 2022 the Supreme Court held that the portal is a public viewing tool, not a legal collation system. The court found that failure to upload could not by itself invalidate the 2023 election.
The Electoral Act 2026, which President Tinubu signed in February, changes the wording. Section 60(3) requires presiding officers to transmit Form EC8A to IReV. But where transmission fails because of communication failure, the signed Form EC8A remains the primary basis for collation and declaration.
Senate Leader Opeyemi Bamidele has described the section as mandating electronic transmission. Critics say the proviso keeps manual collation as the controlling record.
Who signs at each level, and what the form says, will matter most if the figures are challenged. Declaring the 2023 result, Yakubu said Tinubu was elected “having satisfied the requirements of the law.”

items.author: Oboh
items.content:
By Udeme Akpan, Ediri Ejoh, Obas Esiedesa & Cynthia Alo
Nigeria’s electricity generation rose to 4,020.41 megawatts (MW) on Monday from 3,500MW, but the increase has yet to translate into adequate supply for consumers across the country.
This comes as the promise last Thursday by the Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, to restore normalcy in power supply within 72 hours expired two days ago.
Data obtained from the Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO) showed that 20 power plants were connected to the national grid as of 1.0pm yesterday, producing a combined 4,020.41MW. The output was below Sunday’s peak generation of 4,253.6MW but above the off-peak figure of 3,862.17MW.
Last Thursday, generation had dropped to 3,659MW from 3,996MW recorded the previous day, worsening supply conditions across several parts of the country.
Promising restoration within 72 hours, the Ministry of Power had ruled out a major or systemic national grid failure, explaining that preliminary assessments linked the disruptions to maintenance and operational challenges across parts of the power value chain, alongside declining generation.
An analysis of Monday’s generation profile showed that Afam VI contributed the highest output of 519MW, followed by Shiroro Hydro Power Plant with 445MW and Azura-Edo Independent Power Plant with 438MW. Egbin Power Plant, with an installed capacity of 1,320MW, contributed 108MW.
Meanwhile, load allocation to the 11 electricity distribution companies (DisCos) stood at a combined 3,195MW as of 5:07pm yesterday; Abuja DisCo received 581MW; Ikeja 467MW; Eko 458MW and Ibadan 359MW.
Others were Port Harcourt, 294MW; Benin, 243MW; Enugu, 233MW; Kano, 173MW; Kaduna, 167MW; Jos, 146MW; and Yola, 74MW.
In his update on the power situation, Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, said electricity had been restored to many communities affected by recent disruptions, particularly in Lagos, Ogun, Oyo, Kwara and the Federal Capital Territory.
He disclosed that the vandalised Benin-Egbin 330kV transmission line had been repaired and returned to service, helping to raise electricity supply to the Lagos Complex to more than 1,000MW. However, he acknowledged that some locations were still experiencing outages.
“Our priority continues to be the provision of reliable electricity to Nigerians,” he said.
Speaking on a TVC programme monitored by Vanguard, Tegbe said: “Let me start by telling Nigerians, especially those in the three or four states that were recently affected by the outage, that I feel their pain, and President Bola Tinubu feels your pain. However, we are doing the best we can, and I believe it will get better.”
He disclosed that the Federal Government had paid N1.23 trillion out of the N3.3 trillion owed to generation companies (GenCos), leaving about N2 trillion outstanding, which it hoped to settle next year.
Tegbe said Nigeria’s installed generation capacity of 13,625MW translated into actual output of only about 5,000MW. He also disclosed that the government was pursuing a $2 billion East-West Super Grid project designed to support the evacuation of up to 19,000MW, with procurement underway and completion targeted within two years.
Meanwhile, the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of the Association of Nigerian Electricity Distributors (ANED), Sunday Oduntan, apologised to Nigerians over persistent power outages, acknowledging the hardship caused by weeks of prolonged outages.
Speaking on Channels Television’s Sunrise Daily, Oduntan warned against a return to the blame game among electricity sector operators, recalling that distribution companies, transmission operators, generation companies and gas suppliers had previously blamed one another for poor supply.
“Our major problem is that we have started that very wrong route that we went through between 2016 and 2019. What is that? Blame game,” he said.
He questioned the NNPC’s explanation that gas was available, urging the company to clarify whether outstanding payments were affecting supplies to power plants.
“We need to know whether gas was paid for and delivered, who did, who didn’t,” he queried, calling on the Minister of Power to bring stakeholders together to establish the actual causes of the outages.
Also, Rumundaka Wonodi, former Managing Director of the Nigerian Bulk Electricity Trading Plc (NBET), called for sustained investment and long-term planning to address the sector’s challenges.
Speaking on Arise News, he said: “Fixing Nigeria’s electricity challenges requires sustained, diligent, long-term execution rather than rushed, short-term interventions. Nigeria needs much more power than it currently delivers.”

items.content:
US President Donald Trump has said the US-Israel war on Iran is “effectively over” militarily, adding that further military action against Tehran “doesn’t seem to be a very necessary thing” at this point.
Trump made the remarks on Monday during a surprise appearance in the White House briefing room, shortly after meeting Qatar’s Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani, Al Jazeera reported.
“Iran militarily is effectively over. We’re just keeping it the status quo,” Trump told reporters. He also said Iran had been “decapitated.”
No New Strikes for Now
Trump said he saw “positive momentum” and a “good chance” that the war could end. “They’re talking to us, and they’re talking very politely, and we’ll see what happens,” he said.
However, he did not rule out a return to fighting. “The military action doesn’t seem to be a very necessary thing, but we’re locked and loaded, ready to go for any reason that changes,” he said.
The comments are among his clearest signals yet that he is moving away from threats to resume strikes after the US midterm elections. Qatar and other Gulf states have urged Washington not to restart the fighting.
Naval Blockade Stays in Place
Trump gave no sign of pulling back the thousands of US troops deployed in the waters off Iran. He said the US naval blockade, which aims to stop Iranian oil from reaching global markets, will continue.
“We’re keeping it going. We have the greatest military blockade ever,” he said.
Trump also said a long-term solution is still needed to make sure Iran cannot build a nuclear weapon.
Iran’s Conditions
Tehran, for its part, has set several conditions before it will hold nuclear talks. These include ending the US blockade of its ports, lifting sanctions, unfreezing its assets, paying compensation for war damage and ending hostilities across the region, including Israeli operations in Lebanon.
Trump has often said a peace deal with Iran was close. In a CNN interview on Sunday, he said that if talks progress and Iran signs a “strong agreement,” it is “highly unlikely” the US would need to resume strikes. He added that the US had identified infrastructure targets, including 38 bridges, it would hit if fighting restarts.
The war began on February 28 with US-Israeli strikes on Iran.

*Yari demands 1.2m votes from Ebonyi; Umahi promises 1.3m *‘If Tinubu isn’t re-elected, ongoing projects’ll stop’ — Uzodimma *APC has built Nigeria for benefit of few — Makinde *PRP accuses APC of suffocating opposition, exploiting religious fault lines
By Johnbosco Agbakwuru, Omeiza Ajayi, Ndahi Marama & Luminous Jannamike
Vice President Kashim Shettima has said President Bola Tinubu’s massive investments in security, infrastructure, agriculture and human capital development are transforming the South-East economy, promising to address the region’s longstanding development challenges.
Shettima, who spoke yesterday at the All Progressives Congress, APC, presidential campaign rally in Abakaliki, Ebonyi State, said the Federal Government’s interventions were aimed at improving connectivity, strengthening food security, expanding economic opportunities and restoring security.
He said the administration had demonstrated its commitment to Ebonyi through major infrastructure projects, federal appointments and welfare programmes.
“This campaign has been a season of triumph. We have triumphed over the falsehoods of our opponents. We have never turned our backs on you. We have answered your support with projects, and President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has honoured Ebonyi through distinguished appointments and projects across the state,” he said.
According to him, Ebonyi has benefited from the dividends of democracy and deserves to renew the President’s mandate.
“You have stood by us. You have assured us that a mandate is a debt of honour, repayable only through service. Yet democracy demands the humility of asking again. We have returned to seek the renewal of your mandate, to serve you, defend you and stand by you,” he added.
Listing the Federal Government’s infrastructure projects, Shettima identified the Calabar–Ebonyi–Benue–Kogi–Nasarawa–Abuja Superhighway, part of the administration’s Trans-Saharan highway vision, as a major initiative to strengthen trade between the South-East, North-Central and other regions.
Others are the Ndibe Bridge, which will link Ebonyi with Cross River State; the Enugu–Abakaliki–Ogoja Expressway; and the Okposi–Ohaozara–Ukawu–Cross River road.
He said the projects would ease the transportation of agricultural produce and manufactured goods, improve market access and reduce business costs.
On agriculture, the Vice President described Ebonyi as a major contributor to national food security through rice and cassava production. He listed fertiliser distribution, interest-free FarmerMoni assistance and rural road investments among measures to support farmers.
He also disclosed that thousands of Ebonyi residents had benefited from grants under the Presidential Conditional Grant Scheme, while federal employment and digital skills programmes were creating opportunities for youths.
On security, Shettima said the administration had intensified efforts to restore stability in the South-East, stressing that economic development depended on the safety of communities, businesses and infrastructure.
He cited the establishment and commencement of operations at the Nigerian Army Recruits Training Depot at Amasiri-Edda, Ebonyi State, as part of the intervention.
“The security of the South-East has changed since President Tinubu became Commander-in-Chief over three years ago. We have worked to restore order, and we will keep working,” he said.
He also highlighted the establishment of the South-East Development Commission, the launch of South-East Vision 2050 and approval of the South-East Investment Company as initiatives to attract investments and accelerate regional development.
Commending Governor Francis Nwifuru, Shettima said improved federal allocations had strengthened states’ capacity to provide infrastructure and essential services.
Yari, Umahi demand 1.3m votes
Meanwhile, Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, challenged Ebonyi APC members to deliver at least 1.2 million votes for Tinubu in the January 16, 2027 presidential election.
Yari, who said he obtained the figures from the Minister of Works, David Umahi, noted that Ebonyi had about 1.8 million registered voters, with 1.5 million PVCs collected.
“On behalf of Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu, I am setting my target. My target is a minimum of 1.2 million votes,” he declared.
Umahi, however, raised the target to 1.3 million votes, assuring the President that Ebonyi would deliver the figure.
“We are showing the whole world that Ebonyi State belongs to the APC. We all know there is no NDC or any other party in Ebonyi State,” he said.
He credited Tinubu with reviving the 65-kilometre Afikpo–Uturu–Okigwe road project, valued at N193 billion, saying it was already 40 per cent completed.
‘Ongoing projects’ll stop without Tinubu’
Imo State Governor, Hope Uzodimma, warned that ongoing Federal Government projects could be abandoned if Tinubu failed to secure re-election.
“Our responsibility will start from now to go and look for our PVC. That is the weapon, because if Bola Tinubu is not re-elected, all these ongoing projects will stop.
“There is no name on the ballot paper called President Bola Tinubu. What is on the ballot paper is APC, and I invite all of you to vote for APC,” he said.
Director of Mobilisation of the campaign council, Senator Adams Oshiomhole, attacked former Rivers State Governor and ADC vice-presidential candidate, Rotimi Amaechi, describing him as a serial loser.
He recalled Amaechi’s court challenge to former Vice President Atiku Abubakar’s emergence as the presidential candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, alleging irregularities in the nomination process.
“If Amaechi accuses his former boss of rigging, are you the ones who will disagree with him?” Oshiomhole asked.
Ebonyi Governor, Francis Nwifuru, said the state’s support for Tinubu was based on performance rather than sentiments.
“It is rooted in evidence, conviction and gratitude,” he said.
He, however, appealed to the President to address the state’s electricity infrastructure deficit, noting that Ebonyi was the only state without a 330kV transmission line.
“This has adversely affected our drive to industrialise this great state. Your Excellency, we kindly request that you consider making funds available for us to embark on the project or take over its installation,” he said.
Representing the APC National Chairman, the party’s National Vice Chairman, South-East, Ben Nwoye, urged members to vote APC at all levels in the January 16 and February 6 elections.
APC has built Nigeria for few — Makinde
Meanwhile, presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement, APM, Seyi Makinde, accused the Tinubu administration of building a Nigeria that works only for the privileged few.
Speaking at the party’s presidential campaign rally in Jos, Plateau State, Makinde alleged that the APC had appropriated his party’s policy ideas, particularly its RESET Agenda, while failing to improve Nigerians’ living conditions.
“When we unveiled our RESET Agenda, I said in Abuja that they would soon start stealing our ideas. Now they have started. They say theirs is ‘Reform to Prosperity’. They now say they want a Nigeria that will work for everybody. What have they been doing over the past three years?
“They have built a Nigeria that works only for them. Send the oppressors packing. Send them back to Lagos, and let us bring in the team that will reset Nigeria,” he said.
Makinde identified insecurity as a major obstacle to Plateau’s economic potential, promising that an APM government would prioritise security, tourism and job creation.
He said restoring peace would attract tourists, expand the state’s economy and create employment for youths.
“Security is a major pillar of the RESET Agenda. Once we start attracting tourists, our economy on the Plateau will expand, and we will create jobs for our teeming youths,” he said.
He urged supporters to take the party’s message to polling units, insisting that elections were won at the grassroots.
Earlier, the party’s vice-presidential candidate, Lawal Daura, lamented the deterioration of security in Plateau, recalling the state’s former reputation as a tourism destination.
APM National Chairman, Yusuf Dantalle, also criticised the Federal Government’s handling of fuel subsidy removal, questioning its impact on living conditions.
“Subsidy has been withdrawn, according to the Federal Government, for one purpose: to give Nigerians a better life. But are we better off after that? We are paying through our noses. Food is not available. We cannot go to our farms. We cannot do anything,” he said.
PRP accuses APC of suffocating opposition
In another development, the Peoples Redemption Party, PRP, accused the APC of undermining opposition parties and exploiting religious and ethnic divisions to retain power in 2027.
In a statement by its National Chairman, Dr Hakeem Baba-Ahmed, the party alleged that the ruling party was interfering in opposition parties’ internal affairs and deploying state power to frustrate their political activities.
“It is now clear to all Nigerians that APC is putting no stops in suffocating all opposition. From clumsy attempts to interfere in internal affairs of the opposition parties, to the use of state muscle to frustrate genuine campaigns by the opposition,” it said.
The PRP also accused the APC of exploiting religious sentiments, recalling the controversy surrounding its Muslim-Muslim presidential ticket in 2023.
It alleged that the administration was using religion and ethnicity to deepen divisions and secure electoral advantage instead of addressing insecurity and economic hardship.
“Now that it appears Nigerians are united in rejecting its failure to secure Christians and Muslims, and it has pauperised all Nigerians without regard to faith or tongue, the APC is resorting to cultivating new frontiers in our plural character in a bid to impose its electoral fortunes, even at the expense of deepening local and national divisions,” Baba-Ahmed said.

items.author: Oboh
items.content:
*NFF officials stopped me from greeting Flamingos, Obi *Don’t politicise sports, Presidency tells NDC *Keyamo accuses him of hypocrisy
By Henry Umoru
ABUJA—THE Media Office of the presidential candidate of Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Mr Peter Obi, alleged yesterday he was stopped  by officials of the Nigeria Football Federation, NFF, from greeting the victorious women’s Under-17 World Champions at Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja, on arrival of the team from Morocco, venue of the tournament.
Read Also: U-17 WWC: How we overcame opening defeat to win title – Oluebube
The Presidency in a swift reaction, faulted the NDC presidential candidate’s claim, even as the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, SAN, accused him of hypocrisy.
But in a statement signed by spokesperson of Peter Obi Media Office, POMO,  Idris Zekeri , the office said the former Anambra State governor was at the airport on his way to Enugu and saw the team that had just arrived.
It explained that as Obi tried to greet the players, officials of the NFF pleaded with him to save their jobs.
The Media Office said in his usual character, Obi respected their position but described the situation on his X handle as a new dimension of toxic politics in Nigeria.
Quoting the NDC presidential hopeful, the statement read: ‘’This is the new dimension of toxic politics that Nigeria has developed since 2025.
“I arrived at the airport at 7 a.m. this morning (yesterday) to board my flight to Enugu. There, I saw the Nigeria Under-17 girls’ team, which had just arrived and was preparing to board its vehicle into town.
“With genuine joy and enthusiasm, I asked my protocol officer, Jackie Wayas, to find out whether I could greet and welcome the team. I was informed that officials of the Nigerian Football Federation, NFF, had refused and had requested that I should not approach them because, if I did, they would all lose their jobs.
“Regrettably, this is not the first time I have been subjected to such treatment. On March 25, 2025, I was in Uyo for the World Cup qualifier. The governor warmly received me and welcomed me at the VIP stand. 
‘’Following the match, other government officials went to greet the players, but I was again prevented from doing so. I was told by the officials that they would lose their jobs if I proceeded.
“It is deeply troubling to witness the extent of toxic politics into which our nation has descended since 2025. Each year appears to bring further deterioration. This reflects how deeply Nigeria has been affected.
“The new Nigeria we aspire to build must have no room for hostility, intimidation or discrimination, regardless of political affiliation. It must be a Nigeria in which unity, mutual respect and our shared humanity take precedence over political differences. A new Nigeria is possible.”
Don’t politicise sports, Presidency tells Obi over Flamingos greeting
Replying Obi, the Presidency in a statement by the Special Assistant to the President on Social Media, Dada Olusegun, accused the opposition of attempting to politicise national sports teams and institutions.
He said national athletes, including the Flamingos, “represent the entire Federal Republic of Nigeria, not any specific political party or individual ambition.”
Olusegun said protocol guidelines for national teams were designed to protect young athletes from “political exploitation, commercial distractions, and unnecessary media circuses while on official duty.” 
He described Obi’s account as an attempt to turn standard security and administrative procedures into a case of political victimisation.
“To spin standard security and administrative protocols into a narrative of political victimisation is a disservice to the unity that sport is meant to foster in our country,” he said.
The presidential aide also accused Obi of using “unverified hearsay to build a victim narrative”, urging him to allow athletes focus on representing the country. 
Similarly, former presidential aide and National Director of Media Monitoring and Rapid Response of the City Boy Movement, Bashir Ahmad, disagreed with Obi’s description of the incident as a new dimension of toxic politics.
He said being denied access to greet the team did not automatically amount to political persecution, adding that “protocol, security and administrative considerations must have been involved.’’
He urged the former Anambra State governor to prioritise facts and responsibility and know that Nigeria was bigger than any individual or political party.
“A new Nigeria is possible, but not through perpetual political antagonism,” Ahmad said.
Keyamo accuses Obi of hypocrisy over Flamingos encounter
Also reacting to the development, the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, SAN, accused Peter Obi of hypocrisy. Keyamo, in a post on his X platform yesterday, questioned why Obi was eager to associate with what he described as a success story of the country and the present administration, despite his frequent criticisms of Nigeria. 
He suggested that Obi’s intention was merely to seek publicity through photographs with the victorious players.
He wrote: “Mr Peter Obi, in all your public vituperations, you often say things akin to the fact that ‘Nigeria is finished’. So, why are you now so anxious to associate with a success story of the country or this government? Just for photo ops? You see the hypocrisy?”
Recall that the Flamengos beat Japan 2-1 in the finals of the tournament on Saturday and returned home with the trophy yesterday.
With the victory, Nigeria remained the first African country to to win the Under-17 World World at the female level.

items.content:
Petrol pumps in Rawalpindi and Islamabad have stopped giving motorists the Prime Minister’s petrol subsidy following the recent cut in fuel prices.
Instead of selling petrol at the subsidised rate, pump owners and managers began charging motorists and motorcyclists the full price. Because of daily changes in fuel prices, many stations stopped supplying petrol altogether.
Four Days of Disputes at Pumps
The subsidy has not been applied for the past four days. This has led to growing arguments, disputes, and altercations between citizens and pump owners.
Pump owners claim their association told them to stop selling petrol at the subsidised rate.
Association Denies Giving Any Order
Nauman Butt, Vice Chairman of the All Pakistan Petrol Pump Owners Association, rejected the claim. He said the government has not withdrawn the subsidy scheme, and the association has not told any pump owner to stop implementing it.
What the Subsidy Scheme Offers
The government launched the targeted scheme in September, when PM Shehbaz Sharif announced Rs. 100 per litre relief on a limited monthly quantity of petrol for motorcycles, rickshaws, and cars up to 800cc.
Earlier this month, the prime minister ordered action against petrol pumps that fail to pass on relief to consumers. He also said the subsidy programme will continue until at least the end of December.

The National Highways and Motorway Police (NHMP) has advised travellers to prefer the 10 am to 6 pm window for safer journeys during the foggy season, after dense fog forced the closure of the M4 Motorway from Shamkot to Abdul Hakeem for all traffic.
The M4 section from Sher Shah (Multan) to Khanewal has also been closed for heavy traffic due to fog, according to Syed Imran Ahmed, spokesperson for the NHMP Central Region.
The spokesperson said the closures are meant to protect the lives and property of the public, and urged people to avoid unnecessary travel in fog and prefer daylight journeys.
Other Motorway Closures
NHMP’s 8 am road status update on Tuesday also showed the M4 stretch from Abdul Hakeem to Gojra closed for heavy traffic. Separately, the M1 Motorway from the Peshawar main toll plaza to Rashakai was closed earlier in the morning due to dense fog.
Source: NHMP
Motorway Police Safety Advice
The Motorway Police issued the following advice for drivers who must travel in fog:
Keep your speed low and maintain a safe distance from the vehicle ahead.
Stay in your lane and avoid unnecessary overtaking and sudden braking.
Use fog lights and make sure your headlights, tail lights, and wipers are working properly.
Source: NHMP
Fog regularly forces motorway closures in Punjab during winter. Last week, the M3 Motorway was closed from Faizpur to Jaranwala due to dense fog, while five major motorways were shut for the same reason in January.

items.title: Dyson Hot+Cool HF1 Fan, Dyson Cool Tower Fan Launched in India With Air Multiplier Technology: Price, Features
items.summary: The Dyson Hot+Cool HF1 fan and Dyson Cool tower fan have been launched in India, the company announced on Tuesday. The two Dyson bladeless fans will be available for purchase via the Dyson India online store and the offline Dyson Demo stores across the country, allowing customers to experience the devices. The new Dyson Hot+Cool HF1 fan and Dyson Cool Tower fan are bladeless fans powered by the Air Multiplier technology. Dyson’s technology is claimed to combine the principles used in turbochargers and jet engines to increase the volume of air surrounding the machines to amplify the airflow. The Dyson Hot+Cool HF1 fan is a two-in-one model that can blow warm air during winters and cool air during summers. The company claims that the appliance can increase the temperature of the entire room by 1 degree Celsius in about 100 seconds.

items.content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has removed 1,608,660 invalid voter registrations from the preliminary voters register and identified 54 staff members across 10 states for disciplinary action, including possible prosecution, over their alleged involvement in registration irregularities.
The commission also removed 873 records belonging to verified deceased persons following complaints and objections raised during the display of the preliminary voters register ahead of the 2027 general elections.
INEC chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, disclosed this on Monday in Abuja while briefing journalists on the outcome of the commission’s review of the preliminary register, describing the exercise as part of efforts to strengthen the credibility and integrity of the electoral process.
The integrity of the voter register has come under fresh scrutiny following allegations of artificial intelligence (AI)-generated photographs, duplicate registrations and fictitious voter identities in the preliminary register released by INEC ahead of the 2027 general elections.
The controversy sparked widespread reactions after images of questionable voter records circulated on social media, prompting calls for an investigation and greater transparency from the commission.
Addressing journalists on Monday, Amupitan said the commission had concluded the cleaning exercise covering the 2025/2026 Continuous Voter Registration (CVR), adding that all confirmed invalid registrations identified through biometric screening and public complaints had been removed.
According to him, the commission harvested 11,088,238 registration records from the three phases of the CVR exercise, out of which its Automated Biometric Identification System (ABIS) initially flagged 1,545,052 for further examination.
He explained that 1,277,052 registrations were confirmed invalid and excluded before the publication of the preliminary register.
The INEC chairman said following the subsequent display of the register between October 9 and 15, the commission received complaints, claims and objections from members of the public, prompting further investigations.
He said 268,000 cases were subjected to adjudication, out of which 217,722 were confirmed invalid and removed, while 50,278 were cleared as valid and retained.
He noted that additional screening identified another 113,886 invalid registrations, bringing the total number of invalid records removed after the review to 331,608.
The INEC chairman said the commission’s investigation also uncovered deliberate attempts by some registration personnel to circumvent established procedures and misuse provisions designed for exceptional registration circumstances, including those involving persons with disabilities.
He said the affected records had been identified and subjected to appropriate corrective measures, while the personnel implicated had been identified for administrative investigation.
“Fifty-four persons cutting across 10 states have been identified as complicit and necessary disciplinary action will be taken against them, including possible prosecution,” he said.
The commission, however, warned that the irregularities were not limited to the recent registration exercise, explaining that a significant number of the multiple registrations and questionable records circulating on social media originated from historical voter data captured between 2011 and 2023.
Amupitan said cleaning up the 2025/2026 registration records alone would not completely address the integrity challenges associated with the voter register.
He disclosed that the commission had resolved to extend its scrutiny to questionable records in the historical register, directing that already flagged cases and obvious irregularities should be removed after proper verification.
The INEC chairman recalled that the commission had earlier proposed a nationwide voter revalidation exercise to address inconsistencies in historical records but deferred it following concerns from stakeholders about the proximity of the exercise to the 2027 elections and the possibility of disenfranchising eligible voters.
He, however, stressed that the postponement did not suspend existing mechanisms for protecting the integrity of the register, including biometric screening, adjudication and statutory claims and objections.
On complaints by some Nigerians that their names were missing from the preliminary register, Amupitan said investigations revealed that many affected persons had registered between 2011 and 2023 but subsequently registered again instead of transferring their registration to their new locations.
He explained that the subsequent registrations were invalidated by the biometric system, while their original registrations remained at their previous locations.
He therefore advised affected voters to check the locations where they initially registered.
Amupitan said the distribution of Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) from the first and second phases of the Continuous Voter Registration (CVR), including transferred PVCs, was ongoing at local government areas across the country.
He said some PVCs from the third and final phase were still being delivered from overseas production centres and would be dispatched to states.
According to him, distribution would return to Registration Areas nationwide from December 1, 2026.
Amupitan assured Nigerians that the commission remained committed to removing invalid entries without compromising the rights of eligible voters.
He said the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS), alongside the commission’s election-day operational procedures, would provide additional safeguards against multiple accreditation and voting.
He explained that voters would be required to appear physically at their designated polling units for biometric authentication through fingerprints or facial recognition before being accredited.
The INEC chairman said the process would ensure that voters’ identities were verified against the register and that successful accreditation was recorded.
He said the commission would continue to communicate verifiable outcomes of the cleaning exercise while protecting personal information and the integrity of ongoing investigations.
The final register of voters is scheduled for publication on December 15, 2026.
 
‘Electoral officials’ involvement in irregularities bad news for democracy’
Political analysts have expressed concerns over the implications of irregularities in the voter register, warning that the discovery of questionable records dating back to 2011 could further undermine public confidence in the electoral process ahead of the 2027 general elections.
They also called on INEC to demonstrate transparency and take decisive action against officials found culpable in the registration irregularities.
A political analyst, Prof. Kamilu Sani Fage, said while the removal of duplicate registrations was a necessary step towards sanitising the voters register, the identification of 54 officials allegedly involved in the infractions raised serious questions about the integrity of the system.
He said the development suggested that some officials had exploited their positions to manipulate the register, adding that the extent of the alleged infractions remained unclear.
Fage described the involvement of electoral officials as bad news for democracy, arguing that INEC must take stringent action against those found guilty to restore public confidence in the commission.
He also faulted INEC’s explanation that some of the irregularities originated from historical records dating back to 2011, saying the revelation raised questions about why the commission had failed to detect and address them over the years.
According to him, the discovery could also cast doubts on the credibility of previous elections conducted with the affected register.
“Why should such a problem exist for so many years and go undetected? It shows that INEC itself is very weak,” he added.
Another political analyst, Prof. Abubakar Kari, described INEC’s decision to publicly address the controversy surrounding the voters register as timely and necessary.
Kari said the commission needed to respond to widespread allegations and public apprehension that the register had been manipulated through AI to generate duplicate or fictitious voter identities.
He said the allegations, including claims that millions of questionable entries had been introduced into the register, had created fears among Nigerians that the electoral process could be manipulated ahead of the 2027 elections.
According to him, the controversy touches on the credibility and independence of INEC, particularly amid public perceptions that the commission could be influenced to favour the ruling party.
He, however, urged Nigerians to give the commission the benefit of the doubt while insisting that its clean-up exercise must be sustained and supported with verifiable evidence.
Kari said INEC should go beyond issuing explanations and denials by publishing documentary evidence of the corrective measures taken to establish the credibility of the exercise.
He also urged the commission to respond promptly to allegations and misinformation surrounding the voters register rather than allowing them to spread unchecked.
He said the clean-up should not be treated as a one-off exercise but sustained to ensure that the register is credible before the 2027 general elections.
 
Credible voter register key to integrity of elections – Labour Party
The Labour Party has urged INEC to go beyond removing invalid entries from the voter register and build a credible and reliable database ahead of the 2027 general elections.
The party said while the commission deserved commendation for responding to public concerns over alleged manipulation of the register, it must ensure that the clean-up exercise did not result in the disenfranchisement of eligible voters.
Its National Publicity Secretary, Ken Asogwa, said, “The integrity of the electoral process depended largely on the credibility of the register.”
Asogwa described INEC’s announcement on the removal of invalid entries and the identification of officials involved in registration irregularities as heartwarming, but insisted that the commission needed to strengthen its systems to prevent a recurrence.
He urged INEC to focus on building what he described as a foolproof registration database capable of inspiring public confidence in the electoral system.
He stressed that every eligible Nigerian must be given the opportunity to exercise their constitutional right to vote, adding that the credibility of the voter register remained fundamental to the integrity of elections.
“While the Commission deserves commendation for its swift response to the concerns raised by Nigerians over the alleged infiltration of its system, it must also take proactive steps to ensure that no Nigerian of voting age who possesses a valid PVC is disenfranchised in the 2027 general elections,” he said.
 
Yiaga Africa seeks independent audit of voter register
Meanwhile, Yiaga Africa has called for an independent, comprehensive and transparent audit of the voter register following the discovery of irregularities dating back to 2011.
The organisation said the removal of invalid voter records was necessary to restore the integrity of the register, but stressed that the commission’s commitment to accountability would be measured by the consequences faced by those implicated in the irregularities.
Samson Itodo, the Executive Director of Yiaga Africa, said INEC’s decision to identify and remove invalid records and initiate accountability measures against implicated officials was an important step towards rebuilding public confidence ahead of the 2027 general elections.
Itodo, however, said the commission must ensure that investigations were thorough, transparent and conducted in accordance with due process.
He also called on INEC to publish a comprehensive report detailing the nature, geographical spread and causes of the irregularities, the corrective measures taken and reforms being introduced to prevent a recurrence.
On the irregularities from 2011 and 2023 records, the Yiaga Africa director said the development reinforced the need for an independent audit of the entire voter register.
He recommended the establishment of an independent review mechanism comprising credible civil society organisations, electoral technology experts, data protection specialists, statisticians and other relevant professionals.
According to him, the proposed mechanism should operate under clearly defined terms of reference, with appropriate access to registration data and strict compliance with data protection requirements.
He warned that the clean-up exercise must not become another source of voter disenfranchisement, stressing that every eligible Nigerian had a constitutional right to register and vote.
“Officials found to have engaged in criminal conduct should face prosecution rather than merely administrative sanctions,” he added.

items.content:
By Mohammed Ibrahim Yaba, Kaduna & Salim Umar Ibrahim, Kano
 
Three broken-down trucks on Rijana Bridge on Monday caused a major traffic gridlock on the Kaduna-Abuja highway, leaving hundreds of motorists and travellers stranded for several hours.
The congestion reportedly stretched from Akilibu to Gidan Busa. A commercial driver, who identified himself simply as Bala, told our correspondent that he spent almost three hours in the traffic before he was able to continue his journey.
“Honestly, the situation was very frustrating. I have just come out of the traffic after spending more than three hours on the road. We were told that some vehicles broke down in the middle of the road around 2am on Monday.
“Although efforts had been made to remove the trucks before I left, motorists had already spent several hours stranded. Traffic has now started moving slowly as road repairs are ongoing,” he said.
Another resident of Katari, Danjuma Katari, said the congestion extended from Akilibu to Gidan Busa, adding that motorists were still experiencing difficulties as of 5pm on Monday.
“The trailers are now moving slowly, but there is still traffic congestion as we speak,” he said.
Our correspondent observed that trucks conveying livestock and lorries loaded with goods were stranded, while smaller vehicles struggled to navigate through available spaces.
Some stranded travellers and youths were also seen standing by the roadside as officials of the Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) made efforts to clear the obstruction.
Some of the animals, which were tightly packed inside the trucks, appeared exhausted.
A commuter, Reuben Buhari, who shared his experience on Facebook, said he spent eight hours in the gridlock.
“This is the Abuja-Kaduna road today (Monday). We spent eight hours before reaching Abuja, and we were lucky to be in a small car. One thing I can say for sure is that a lot of people will spend the night on this road, especially the tanker and trailer drivers.
“Unless we Nigerians, including me, learn to obey traffic rules even when no officer is watching, to be patient and to be orderly, traffic chaos like this will keep occurring,” he said.
Another motorist, Aliyu Abu, blamed the situation partly on motorists’ impatience, saying greater discipline and patience would have eased traffic movement.
Sarah Monday, a fashion designer travelling to Abuja for a contract meeting, told the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) that she lost the meeting due to the standstill.
She appealed to the Federal Government to complete the highway soon, so that the hardship faced by its users would be reduced, especially during Salah, Christmas and other festive periods.
 
FRSC removes two trucks
The FRSC Sector Commander, Andrew Paul Longkam, who confirmed the obstruction, said the corps had succeeded in removing two of the trucks.
“Our team was able to remove two of the trucks from the road. As we speak, the report I am receiving indicates that traffic is flowing and the situation is gradually returning to normal,” he said.
Longkam attributed the severity of the gridlock partly to ongoing road construction, which leaves only one lane open to motorists.
He explained that even a minor obstruction could result in serious congestion because of the limited space available to vehicles.
The sector commander also identified the high volume of vehicles on the highway as another contributing factor, adding that many of them were believed to be travelling to Jigawa State for a political campaign.
As of the time of filing this report, patience had begun to run out. Many motorists had started turning back towards Kaduna, with a lot of them saying they would travel to Abuja through the Kachia-Bwari road instead.
 
Recurring gridlock on highway
The Kaduna-Abuja highway is one of the major transport corridors in northern Nigeria, linking the Federal Capital Territory with Kaduna and providing access to other parts of the North-West.
The road carries thousands of commuters, commercial vehicles, articulated trucks and fuel tankers daily, making any obstruction a major challenge for travellers.
The Katari-Jere stretch, in particular, has become a recurring congestion point, with ongoing construction activities narrowing some sections and forcing motorists to navigate restricted passages and diversions.
A breakdown or accident involving a heavy-duty vehicle under such conditions can quickly obstruct the available carriageway and trigger long queues.
The latest incident is among several traffic gridlocks recorded on the Kaduna-Abuja highway this year, with road construction, accidents involving heavy-duty vehicles and poor driving habits repeatedly identified as major causes.
On January 4, 2026, motorists experienced congestion between Greenville and Obasanjo Farm following increased vehicular movement after the Christmas and New Year holidays.
The FRSC attributed the situation to the resumption of road construction, the closure of some diversions, motorists’ impatience and lack of lane discipline.
Similarly, between May 24 and 26, thousands of travellers were reportedly stranded along the Jere, Katari and Azara axis during the Eid-el-Kabir travel rush, with some spending between six and 20 hours on the road.
The congestion was attributed to ongoing reconstruction, rainfall, an accident, heavy vehicular movement and dangerous overtaking.
On August 22, motorists also experienced heavy congestion around Kateri, Jere and Zuba in both directions, prompting the deployment of FRSC personnel and soldiers to manage the traffic.
 
Expert seeks truck movement restrictions, emergency response stations
A road safety expert, Munkaila Sulaiman, has called on the federal government to restrict the movement of articulated vehicles during peak traffic periods, establish emergency response stations and accelerate the reconstruction of the Kaduna-Abuja highway to end the persistent gridlock on the route.
Sulaiman, who is a retired road safety officer said the recurring congestion required more than temporary deployment of traffic personnel, urging the government to adopt a comprehensive traffic management strategy that would address the root causes of the problem.
“The Kaduna-Abuja highway gridlock should no longer be treated as an ordinary traffic inconvenience. It is a major transportation, economic and public safety challenge that requires urgent and coordinated intervention,” he said.
He identified prolonged road construction, poorly managed diversions, broken-down heavy-duty vehicles, road crashes, reckless driving and inadequate emergency response as some of the factors contributing to the congestion.
According to him, the Katari-Jere-Zuba corridor, particularly around construction diversion points, requires urgent attention because restricted traffic passages and the movement of heavy-duty vehicles could worsen the situation.
“The authorities must first identify the major points responsible for the congestion instead of relying on assumptions. We need a comprehensive traffic assessment to establish the specific challenges at different locations along the highway,” he said.
The expert urged the Federal Ministry of Works to review the performance of contractors handling the highway and enforce agreed completion deadlines, saying prolonged construction had created bottlenecks that exposed motorists to unnecessary hardship.
He said construction should be carried out in properly coordinated phases, with completed sections opened to traffic and alternative passages provided before existing lanes were closed.
“Road construction should not become an excuse for exposing motorists to unnecessary risks. Government must ensure that contractors provide safe alternative passages, clear road markings, reflective signs and adequate lighting at diversion points,” he said.
On the movement of articulated vehicles, the expert proposed designated movement periods, particularly during peak passenger traffic hours, as well as designated parking and holding areas along the corridor.
“A truck breaking down at a narrow diversion can bring traffic movement to a complete standstill for several hours. We must introduce a proper management system for articulated vehicles and ensure that recovery trucks are available at strategic locations,” he said.
He also called for regular mechanical inspections of heavy-duty vehicles, adding that any restriction on their movement should be based on traffic studies and coordinated with freight operators.

items.author: Ado Abubakar Musa, Jos
items.content:
Gunmen have reportedly killed a soldier and three civilians during an attack on Bel village in Sho community, Barkin Ladi Local Government Area of Plateau State.
Several other persons were injured in the attack, which occurred at about 9 pm on Sunday.
A resident, Mr Bulus Bot, said the gunmen stormed the community at night and opened fire on residents.
“The gunmen stormed the community at about 9 pm and opened fire on innocent citizens, leaving some people dead, and others injured,” he said.
The Publicity Secretary of the Berom Youth Moulders Association, Rwang Tengwong, also confirmed the killings, identifying three of the victims as Emmanuel Pam Dachung, 15; Joseph Gyang, 28; and Emmanuel Yohanna, 32.
He said a soldier was also among those killed and called on security agencies to identify and arrest the perpetrators.
The spokesperson for Operation Enduring Peace, Captain Polycarp Oteh, promised to respond when contacted but had yet to do so as of press time.
The attack came four days after two herders and several cattle were reportedly killed around Tafawa community in Riyom LGA on Wednesday night.
Between October 27 and November 8, at least five attacks were recorded in four local government areas of the state, leaving more than 20 people, including two soldiers and a mobile police officer, dead.
Communities in Bokkos, Barkin Ladi, Bassa and Riyom LGAs have continued to experience attacks despite security operations in the state.
The persistent violence forced the state government to impose a dusk-to-dawn curfew in affected local government areas on September 21.
However, attacks have continued, with many people, including women and children, reportedly killed since the restriction was introduced.
President Bola Tinubu visited the state on April 2, 2026, to commiserate with victims of the violence.
He promised to address the insecurity and deploy 5,000 artificial intelligence-enabled CCTV cameras to prevent further attacks.
Although some cameras have been installed within the state capital, they are yet to be deployed to communities outside Jos, where many of the attacks have occurred.
Farmers, herders trade accusations
Meanwhile, leaders of the Berom and Fulani communities have continued to accuse each other of responsibility for attacks and killings in the state.
The National President of the Berom Youth Moulders Association, Barrister Solomon Dalyop, accused members of the herding community of trying to displace Berom people from their ancestral lands.
He said several Berom communities had been attacked, with hundreds of people killed and crops worth millions of naira destroyed.
However, the Plateau State Chairman of the Miyetti Allah Cattle Breeders Association of Nigeria (MACBAN), Ibrahim Yusuf Babayo, accused members of the farming community of attacking their members.
Babayo said the attacks were aimed at driving Fulani people out of the state, insisting that they were indigenes like other ethnic groups.
He added that dozens of their members had been killed, while cattle were also killed or rustled.
Both groups called for increased surveillance and targeted patrols along routes frequently used for attacks and ambushes.
They also urged security agencies to establish reliable emergency contacts and respond promptly to distress calls.
They further called for improved security around farmlands, regular updates on investigations and security operations, and action against those spreading misinformation or inciting violence.
The groups urged security agencies to ensure that cases of killings were thoroughly investigated and perpetrators brought to justice.
Plateau to establish security camps in 17 LGAs – Mutfwang
Plateau State Governor, Caleb Mutfwang, has announced plans to establish operational camps of the state-owned security outfit, Operation Rainbow, in the 17 local government areas to strengthen intelligence gathering and tackle insecurity.
Mutfwang disclosed this on Monday during the passing-out parade of 353 retrained operatives of the outfit.
He said 11 operational camps had already been established, while vehicles and motorcycles would be provided to support their deployment.
The governor said the state government was also strengthening the agency’s intelligence-gathering capacity through technology, including drones and a command and control centre, to improve surveillance and ensure timely sharing of security information.
“The state intends that each local government will have an operational camp that will use drones in getting information in real time and passing it to other security agencies,” he said.
Mutfwang explained that Operation Rainbow was primarily an intelligence-gathering outfit and not an armed force, adding that its personnel were trained to support conventional security agencies.
He said the operatives, being residents of the communities where they work, understood the terrain and could help identify threats and respond to emergencies.
He said the state had established the Plateau State Special Activities Centre (PSAC), equipped with drones and monitoring facilities to enable security agencies to monitor developments across the state in real time.
Mutfwang described peace and security as priorities of his administration, saying the retraining was aimed at improving the operatives’ discipline, professionalism and ability to provide early warnings.
He urged them to uphold integrity and restraint, warning that they were not above the law.
The governor also directed them to work with conventional security agencies, traditional rulers and community leaders, stressing that intelligence sharing and cooperation were essential to achieving lasting peace.

items.author: Abubakar Sadiq Isah
items.content:
The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has promised to reward each of the 62 elected councillors across the six area councils with N10 million if they deliver their respective wards to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and the All Progressives Congress, APC in the 2027 general election.
Wike announced the offer on Monday during an interactive session with stakeholders of the All Progressives Congress and the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) under the Rainbow Coalition in Kwali Area Council.
The meeting was attended by the 62 elected councillors, six area council chairmen and traditional rulers, among other stakeholders.
The minister urged the councillors to see the forthcoming election as a major responsibility, saying the proposed reward would serve as an incentive and encourage healthy competition among them.
He said the Rainbow Coalition had resolved to mobilise support for Tinubu’s re-election across the country.
“So for the councillors, you have a task. I will hold a meeting with you again. I will not say the way I am going to mobilise you but I will give you a bet like what is happening in some states, which is like competition. Anybody who delivers his ward, if you deliver your ward. That is what rainbow coalition has decided to do. The rainbow coalition across the federation are mobilizing a form of support for Mr President to win this election, we are saying that any councillor that delivers his ward, go and take N10 million,” he said.
He added: “so we want to mobilise for Mr President and that is our support for Mr President. So go to your wards, go and see your leaders. I know many cannot do it but we are using you as instrumentality to your leaders. Go and meet your leaders, go and meet the youths, tell them there is something that has come, we must not allow this thing to go, let us deliver our ward to Mr President.”
Wike also promised to mobilise women’s groups across the area councils with financial support to encourage them to turn out en masse and vote for Tinubu.
He further assured the councillors that he would meet with the Permanent Secretary of the FCT Administration to review their salary structure.
The minister also urged traditional rulers, community leaders and other stakeholders to mobilise residents to vote for the APC senatorial candidate, Senator Philip Aduda, and its House of Representatives candidate for Abuja South, Danladi Chiya.
He said the stakeholders should work towards securing victory for the party’s candidates in the FCT during the 2027 elections.
On traditional institutions, Wike reaffirmed the administration’s recognition of their role and assured the recently upgraded traditional rulers that their certificates and official sports utility vehicles would be provided.
He also promised that the abandoned Kwaita-Yebu road project would be re-awarded to a more competent contractor.
The minister added that several ongoing projects in the territory would be commissioned before the end of December 2026.
Earlier, the Chairman of Kwali Area Council, Nuhu Daniel Kwali, commended Wike for providing infrastructure across the council, particularly rural roads, which he said had brought relief to residents.

items.author: Dickson S. Adama
items.content:
The Presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Seyi Makinde has called on Nigerians to come together and send the current administration of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu packing and back to Lagos.
The Oyo State Governor also accused the All Progressives Congress, APC of stealing their political ideas and strategy.
Makinde spoke in Jos, on Monday at the APM presidential campaign rally.
He charged Nigerians to return to their various units, communities and spread the message of the reset Nigeria agenda.
“Elections are won at the polling-unit level, so take this message back to your communities. If Nigeria is not working for you, then let us reset it. When we reset Nigeria, we will build a country that works for everybody.
“Let me also make something clear. When we unveiled our Reset agenda, I said in Abuja that our ideas would soon be copied. That is exactly what is happening now.
“They have come up with what they call Reform to Prosperity, and they are now talking about building a Nigeria that works for everybody. What have they been doing in the past three-plus years? Have they not been running a country that works only for them?
“It is time to send the oppressors packing. Send them back to Lagos and let us bring in a team that will reset Nigeria. Join me in building a country that works for you, works for me and works for our children,” Makinde stated.
According to him, security is one of the major pillars of the APM Reset agenda, stressing that once they restore security and attract tourists, the economy will expand, and more employment opportunities will be created for the youths.
Plateau State, he added, truly has a beautiful climate, that it is an indication that if they get security right, people will also return to Plateau State for tourism.
On his part, the APM Vice Presidential candidate, Lawal Daura said they are in Plateau State because of the importance of its people and the strategic position the state occupies in Nigeria.
Daura who was the former Director General of the Department of State Services (DSS) warned the people to be vigilant against individuals going around collecting people’s Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs), taking photographs of them and offering money in exchange for the voters’ details.
“If you come across such individuals, report them to the appropriate authorities so they can be arrested. They are attempting to undermine the electoral process and violate the law.
“Secondly, there are people who want to use money to influence your decisions. That money belongs to you. It is public money, meant to be used for your development and the provision of essential services.
“Instead of using the money to provide the services you deserve, they are distributing it to manipulate you and perpetuate their stay in power. They want the oppression, injustice and suffering in this country to continue.
“My people, take this seriously. This is no longer something to treat lightly. That is why we have decided to travel across the country to sensitise Nigerians.
“We want young people, men and women, to understand that their future is at stake. What they are trying to destroy is your future You are the ones who will bear the consequences tomorrow,” Daura said.
According to him, the APM journey is not a journey driven by empty promises or political deception, stressing that they are not liars or deceivers, and they will not exploit the people.
“You can verify this from our records. We are not coming into politics for the first time, hoping to get into government and begin to learn how to serve. We have been there before, and we have records of what we did.
“We are not making false claims, and we are not deceiving you. We have returned because we once entrusted the responsibility of leadership to people we believed could deliver, but they have disappointed us.
“That is why we are back to ask for your support and to remind you that you must be vigilant. Young people and women, open your eyes. This political movement and the struggle for a better Nigeria belong to you. You must take ownership of it and play your part,” Daura said.
The running mate also pointed out that Plateau is a great state, but unfortunately, some people have done everything possible to undermine the state’s reputation, promising that the reset agenda will put things right, not only for Plateau State but for Nigeria as a whole.

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
By Favour Ulebor
Canada has made its Rural Community Immigration Pilot a permanent programme to attract and retain skilled foreign workers in smaller communities facing persistent labour shortages.
The Minister of Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship, Lena Metlege Diab, announced the decision on Monday, November 9, 2026, in Pictou County, Nova Scotia.
According to a statement published on the website of Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC), the programme will initially retain the 14 communities currently participating in the pilot, with plans to expand to more communities in the future.
The employer- and community-driven programme is designed to address labour shortages in rural areas by connecting skilled foreign workers and their families with employers and community support services.
It also seeks to encourage newcomers to settle permanently in smaller communities and contribute to their economic development.
Speaking during the announcement, Diab said the government recognised the critical role rural communities played in Canada’s economy despite the challenges they faced in attracting workers.
“Our government understands that rural communities play a critical role in powering Canada’s economy. At the same time, many face real challenges finding the workers they need.
“That’s why we’re transitioning our successful rural immigration pilot into a permanent program—helping smaller communities attract and retain essential workers who deliver services and drive economic growth.
“We appreciate that a one-size-fits-all approach to immigration doesn’t work for rural Canada, and this permanent pathway is one part of our work to ensure that communities of all sizes can share in the benefits of responsible, sustainable immigration,” she said.
Under Canada’s 2027–2029 Immigration Levels Plan, the government has allocated 5,500 admission spaces to the permanent Rural Community Immigration Program.
The government said the initiative was part of its broader immigration policy aimed at stabilising the number of immigrants admitted into the country, reducing the temporary resident population and retaining skilled foreign workers already contributing to local communities.
It added that preliminary results from the pilot showed that foreign workers had helped address labour shortages in critical sectors, including healthcare, education, sales and services, between 2025 and 2026.
The department also disclosed that participating communities had vetted and designated more than 1,950 trusted employers experiencing persistent labour shortages that could not be addressed through the local workforce between January 2025 and August 2026.
The transition to a permanent programme is expected to provide rural employers with a more reliable supply of skilled foreign workers while supporting the long-term economic development of participating communities.

items.author: efosataiwo@vanguardngr.com
items.content:
By Efe Onodjae
Former Ogun State Governor, Olusegun Osoba has defended the role of political godfathers in Nigeria’s democracy, saying their responsibility should be to offer advice and guidance rather than impose political appointees on elected governors.
Osoba, who spoke during a podcast hosted by Reuben Abati and shared on X (formerly Twitter), said he considered himself a political godfather but had deliberately avoided interfering in the administration of his political successors.
According to him, he had never nominated anyone for appointment as commissioner, special adviser, councillor or local government chairman in the state.
He said: “I agree, I’m a godfather. But one thing that is working for me in my state is that I hardly interfere. I counsel and advise him. I have never nominated one person into his government.”
Explaining his position, the former governor said imposing candidates on an administration could undermine the governor’s authority and create unnecessary divisions among his political supporters.
He noted that appointing one person from the numerous people around him could offend others, while anyone recommended by him might be viewed with suspicion within the administration.
Osoba recalled that during his tenure as governor, he adopted a system that allowed each federal constituency to nominate candidates for commissioner positions.
He said he requested one name from each federal constituency and subsequently reviewed their credentials before assigning them portfolios, adding that the approach helped him avoid pressure from political associates.
The former governor maintained that political godfathers should ensure that people who worked for a candidate during electioneering campaigns were recognised and compensated, but should not dictate how an elected governor runs his administration.
“That’s the role of a godfather. I agree, I’m a godfather,” he said.
Osoba also defended the participation of experienced elders in candidate selection, citing his support for a presidential candidate whom he described as experienced, having served in the Lagos State House of Assembly, House of Representatives and Senate, as well as in the corporate sector.
