items.content:
To strengthen the growing trend of dialogue over disputes and wars, the United Nations Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) declared the 1970s as the decade of communication. The expectation was that every country would endeavour to become a communicating nation. Not many have successfully embraced the appeal till today because everyone has adopted a haphazard approach to the subject. Government, societal institutions and the general public have continued to relate with themselves and one another through the ‘transmission model’ which sees communication not as an exchange of ideas but as the mere transmission of messages with or without a purpose. In other words, once a message is transmitted, it does not matter whether the receiver understands it or not.
The unavoidable consequence of the approach is that communication has largely remained ineffective. The commonest of the phenomenon is the communication that is often swallowed by noise. Nothing else better exemplifies this point than the current electioneering campaigns ahead of the 2027 general elections where all that is heard is noise within and among large crowds. All our political parties appear convinced that the best way to address the masses is to demonstrate capacity to put together large crowds that are engaged in the communication of the deaf. Many people among the crowd are in attendance with different goals in mind just as many do not in essence understand the purpose of the gathering. The trend is fast becoming Nigeria’s unique contribution to the development of democracy.
In fairness to our political class, several theories of mass mobilization and information flow are put in use in the campaigns across the country. The missing point is that no one knows whether the communication theories as currently practiced add any value to the comprehension of the political messages that are being disseminated. A common scheme is the two-step flow model which posits that the media influences the public indirectly through opinion leaders, who interpret and relay information to others.  In line with this model, politicians seek to use revered leaders to pass messages to the people in addition to what the media does. The problem here is that not many people are willing to listen to some of the so-called leaders because the latter are no longer regarded as credible by the people. The case of traditional rulers for instance has virtually become a double-edge sword because they are now seen as enemies of the opponents of their preferred candidates.
Such traditional rulers are generally being robbed of the title of the people’s royal fathers that are expected to be non-partisan. This has encouraged campaign coordinators to expand to the multiple-step flow theory. In today’s Nigeria, the steps are greatly affected by the prevailing socio-economic factors in the environment.  When an international music or soccer star is introduced into a political rally, the strategy pulls a huge crowd but do the people get to hear whatever is being said? This is difficult to determine when it is realized that the same huge crowd surfaces the next day when the event is organized by another political party. Accordingly, it is getting increasingly difficult to evaluate the real support which a large crowd adds to the fortunes of each campaign team. It is however not in doubt that everyone probably gets entertained and perhaps finds some material gains before leaving making it obvious that campaigns are now sources of economic gains to many spectators.
Another strategy remains the use of the media by strong advocates who engage in interviews to sell the candidates of their parties. Here, the television networks have had a field day. Unfortunately, it has not added much value to the campaigns because most of the advocates approach the task with a fruitless mindset. A television interview which is ordinarily a great opportunity for a party chieftain is marred as most party representatives seek to change the interview format to what in political broadcast is known as ‘party talk.’ In the latter, the party representative gets a free no-interruption opportunity to say whatever he likes. But the situation changes when it is an interview. Here, questions would be asked, follow-ups would be done and indeed, interruptions will occur where critical terms are referred to while answering questions. The trend one sees now is that the party official demands not to be interrupted while answering questions. The other week, a party official said publicly that he came prepared to face the interviewer!
The professional position is that the interviewer represents the general public as his questions are generally crafted in line with comments in the public space. The guest is therefore expected to see his interviewer not as a particular person but as a typical citizen whose views he ought to respond to with a mind to changing or reducing to the barest minimum, any anxieties real or imagined that citizens hold against his party. Indeed, a party official at a public interview session is admonished to ignore the nuances of his interviewer and deal with the substance of the message in favour of his political party. To go for a television interview with a mindset to deal with a naughty interviewer is patently ill-advisable. Sadly, that is what we see these days on national television in Nigeria with a politician seeking to take control of a programme in which he is only a guest. Even if a combative approach such as aggressively demanding respect from an interviewer was what the party had planned, it is wise to realize that the posture cannot explain to the public why the party is asking for our votes.
To drive home the point, let me recall my personal experience as an interviewer with President Shehu Shagari seeking re-election in 1983. I asked Shagari if I was free to describe him as ‘the happy leader’ of corrupt politicians since Nigerians see his party the NPN as a collection of money bags and thieves.  While answering me, he said his smiles increased because he saw me displaying brilliance by playing the devil’s advocate of deliberately projecting an erroneous opinion. He admitted that the NPN may have some bad eggs as it is with all organizations but that because it was larger than all others in everything it also has the largest number of honest hardworking Nigerians. He regretted that it was because the media likes to focus on negatives that it was magnifying NPN’s few bad eggs. He then listed all the popular programmes that the NPN had implemented that should interest Nigerians instead of fake propaganda by political opponents. If that type of question is asked today not only by the NTA but also by the private media,  our law enforcement  agencies would be on 24hours red alert.
The scenario outside the television studios does not also show that political campaigns in Nigeria follow what happens elsewhere. Whether it is the ruling party that everyone is complaining about or the opposition parties that are preoccupied with complaints, almost every political campaign is violent. There are politicians who are experts in issuing threats while others are engaged in unorthodox practices that make it impossible for anyone to hear the message of any campaign. All parties as stated earlier, are busy creating crowds with noise. Anyone who thinks it is the APC alone that is busy renting crowds should check out for what the  ADC did last week in parts of Northern Nigeria. Media reports indicate that because the ADC shut down the relevant towns, those who flew to the rallies were yet to find space to drive from the airport to the rally venues when it was time for their return flight to depart.
In other parts of the country the goal was really to just create crowd and entertain people, not really to educate Nigerians on why they should vote for whom. In Bayelsa state, the home of the NDC leader, the communication of campaign messages took the form of a boat regatta. In some other states it was violence galore with thugs destroying campaign materials of other political parties in addition to state authorities disallowing the use of public media and spaces like stadia. The reported attack on Vice President Shettima’s entourage in Lafia is instructive here. In other words, we are still not ready for the politics of equality featuring a level playing field. A foreign journalist visiting Nigeria would wonder if we detest peace communication until he finds out that we actually have a national peace committee. Whereas many believe that the situation could produce an avalanche of electoral disputes, the judiciary is likely to use technicalities to deal with the development if history is allowed to remind us of the past. Put differently, the judiciary may once again be more active than our electoral body in the conduct of elections in Nigeria.
The post Nigeria’s unique political campaigns, by Tonnie Iredia appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.content:
Gradually, year 2026 is drawing to an end.  Being alive is a reason we must continuously thank God.  Brethren, have you said thank you Jesus this morning? 
Please do.  You owe the Lord gratitude.
Beloved, last week we mentioned confession as a key to a miracle. Today, we’ll return to that with more details.
I’ll start with an uncommon story of the son of a farmer whose father was regarded as poor in a town.  This young boy went to the farm with his father and he saw man drive past them in an exotic car. The boy looked back admired the car and said to himself “ I am going to drive a better car in this town”.
That was decades ago, today that boy now a man is perhaps the richest person in that town of course with the best cars in that town but he took some steps.
 We’ll return to in the article.
Brethren, let’s go to the spiritual. The word of the Lord tells us in Proverbs 18 vs. 21 ( NIV) “ the tongue has the power of life and death, and those who love it eat its fruit”.
The son of a farmer used his tongue positively and he is eating the fruits of the words that he spoke to himself today.
As Christians however, we need not use the tongue casually as the farmer’s son did.  We need to use the tongue in line with the word of God.
How then do we use the appropriate word? The answer is found in the word of Prophet Joshua in Joshua 1 vs.8: “ Do not let this Book of the Law depart from your mouth; meditate on it day and night, so that you may be careful to do every written in it. Then you will be prosperous and successful”.
The importance of tongue that God has given to all human beings is repeated in Psalm 1 vs. 2: “ But his delight is in the law of the LORD, and on his law he meditates day and night”.
Just as you need to study to pass an exam you need to study the Word of God to be able to confess it.
Confession in this case is not about the sins you have committed but it’s about saying what God has promised you and your desire to have it.
To confess it, you need to memorize that particular verse of the Bible and say it to yourself.
In other words, you need to put the words you have memorized into action by saying it to yourself and as you do so, if no human being sees you, the invisible God is watching and listening to you.
How do I know?  I knew a woman that was barren for over 20 years.
She learnt the word by going to church regularly and reading the Holy Bible on her own.  It was during one of those church services that she picked up two verses.
The first, is Deuteronomy 7 vs. 14: “ You will be blessed more than any other people, none of your men or women will be childless, nor any of your livestock without young”.
The second is Exodus 23 vs.26: “ and none shall miscarry or be barren in your land.  I will give you a full life span”.
These two passages are quite relevant for anyone waiting on the Lord for children.
Before this woman who had been waiting on the LORD for decades conceived, she made up her mind that she wanted a set of twins.
She found the word in the story of Rebecca recorded in Genesis 25 vs. 23 &24: “ The LORD said to her, Two nations are in your womb, and two peoples from within you will be separated, one will be stronger than the other and the older will serve the younger”
Verse 24: “When the time came for her to give birth, there were twin boys in her womb”.
The key word her is in verse 24. This woman began to say to herself, while bathing, “ I am a mother of twins”. Touching her stomach, she would say “ This my body would produce a set of twins”.
She did this regularly while bathing. No one heard her but God, her Creator heard her.
What she did was using her tongue to claim her right in the Lord. That was action taken.
The son of the farmer also took action by studying.  He continued to study even after he had his first degree and had begun working.  With determination despite his work schedule, he got two other degrees.
God favoured him and he got jobs as chief executive in a lucrative industry.
On her part, the woman waiting on the Lord for a set of twins first had a son and about 18 months, later because she didn’t stop confessing the birth of twins, she gave birth to set of twins; two girls.
Brethren, the two testimonies shared are about one that wanted divine prosperity and the childless woman that became fruitful.
Both used the tongue to pronounce the Word and the result was testimony.
Several examples of the use of the tongue are found in the Bible.
God used the Word and the Word produced results.
Genesis 1 vs.2&3 are my witness.
It states, “ Now the earth was formless and empty, darkness was over the surface of the deep, and the Spirit of God was hovering over the waters.
And God said “ Let there be light; and there was light”.
The idea of how to end darkness was not put into use until God made a pronouncement.   The LORD said, it and it manifested. 
 The pronouncement is an action taken by God.   That pronouncement is the reason we have day and night till today.
Brethren, what are you using your tongue for?  If you say, “ nothing can happen to me this year”, nothing is what you will get. If you say however, that “ before this month ends, I will testify to the goodness of God, that is what you will get.
What you say is what you get but you must take action.
Those that find the word and refuse to confess it and take action will get nothing.  Whereas, those that find the word, take action and confess the word always enter into a season of testimonies.
Beloved, may your testimony manifest before year 2026 comes to an end.
Dear Believer, you still have time to find the word and speak it into that situation that you want changed for the better.
Perhaps, you have remained single for years and people have concluded that you would die single. This is the time to speak the Word.   Use the Word to bring about your desired miracle.
As you confess the word daily, be confident, that Jesus, our advocate hears you and since the LORD hears you, at his own time, the challenge would end.
Victory is ours in Jesus name.

She encouraged women to be patient with themselves, noting that they might not look or feel the same as they did before childbirth.
According to her, new mothers should give themselves grace and time to adjust, while recognising the remarkable changes their bodies have undergone.
Okojie announced the arrival of her baby boy on June 24, 2026, while celebrating her birthday.
Following the birth, she shared a video of her labour room experience on Instagram, paying tribute to mothers and describing women as superheroes.
On Mother’s Day, the actress also celebrated her new role, expressing disbelief that she could now celebrate the occasion as a mother herself.
Her latest milestone offers another glimpse into her experience of motherhood, a journey she has shared with fans through personal reflections on childbirth and adjusting to life with a newborn.

items.author: Faruk Shuaibu
items.content:
The Nigerian Union of Journalists (NUJ) has stated that it is working on a bill to be proposed to the National Assembly backing a structured salary for journalists to be properly compensated for the work they do in sustaining democracy in the country.
Speaking during the fourth edition of NUJ’s Annual Milestone Recognition of Media Icons in Nigeria, on Saturday, its National President, Comr. Alhassan Yahya, said the initiative is to promote media development, professional excellence and welfare of journalists.
He lamented that the profession is left behind despite contributions to sustaining democracy in Nigeria with workers contending with poor remuneration.
“NUJ is open for discussion. This time around we are integrating and involving all professional bodies who are working in to see that we come with an initiative to a bill that will be presented before the National Assembly for ratification and at the same time to change the narrative.” he said.
2027 election will determine your future, Tinubu tells youths
Yobe APC launches counter protest Against ‘Tinubu Must Go’ Movt
He also appealed to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu to intervene in the issue of poor remuneration for journalists.
“We want to sincerely appeal to His Excellency the President of this country, President Bola Ahmed Tunubu, to look into issues of remuneration for Nigerian journalists. If the President can approve and increase salary structure for judicial workers, why not journalists? The time is now. Let’s see how we can partner together so that at the end of the day we can be able to smile together.”
He said the event was organised to celebrate outstanding achievement in the media industry and “recognise courage, professionalism, sacrifice and unwavering commitment for the individuals who believe they have done wonderfully well and distinguish themselves into service of truth, public enlightenment and nation beauty. Today we celebrate excellence.”
Those honoured include: Martuns Oloja, Sumner Shagari Sambo, Tabutha Sani Kangiwa, Chief Eric Teniola, Segun Adeniyi, Azubuike Ishiekwene, Comr. Franz Ndulue, Kingsley Datubor Uranta, Adetoro Oladapo, among others.
Speaking at the event, Delta State Governor, Sheriff Oborevwori, said democracy depends on citizens having access to reliable information, the freedom to express their views, and the opportunity to hold public officials accountable which journalism helps to make possible.
“A free press gives citizens a voice, brings their concerns to public attention, and ensures that those in authority are answerable for their actions. This accurate reporting and informed debate, responsible journalism, also helps citizens understand public issues and make sound decisions. Democracy and journalism, therefore, depends on each other.”
He added that journalists’ sacrifices for returning Nigeria to democracy must never be forgotten.
“They remind us that the press freedom we enjoy today was secured through courage, commitment, and personal sacrifice. Our constitution recognises this responsibility.”
The immediate past President of NUJ, Christopher Isiguzo, urged the media to resist every attempt to weaponise information for political advantage.
“Our loyalty must remain to the truth, the public interest and the stability of our democracy. In an age of social media and instant communication, professional journalism is more important than ever. The pressure to be first must never replace the obligation to be accurate.”

items.author: Daily Trust
items.content:
Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), has condemned President Bola Tinubu’s latest attack on his investment in education, describing it as a desperate attempt to distract Nigerians from the failure of his administration.
In a statement issued by the Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, Atiku said: “Again, Bola Tinubu has told Nigerians why they should not allow him to continue as president after his first tenure.
“He also chose to question my investment in education and ask how I built an educational institution while serving as Vice President.
“The answer is simple: my investment in education predates my time in public service. In 1993, while a U.S. court ordered the forfeiture of funds in an account in your name, describing them as proceeds of narcotics trafficking or funds involved in unlawful financial transactions, I was laying the foundation for ABTI Academy. That Academy has since grown into the American University of Nigeria.
2027 election will determine your future, Tinubu tells youths
Yobe APC launches counter protest Against ‘Tinubu Must Go’ Movt
“That moment captures the difference between us. My history is traceable. I can show Nigerians how I built my name, achieved success in business and entered public leadership. Your own history remains clumsy and foggy. You cannot erase it by attacking my record in education.
“A president who has plunged the country into a crushing cost-of-living crisis has no business asking Nigerians for another mandate. The real conversation about the 2027 election is how to repair the damage your government has done.
“You say Nigeria cannot return to subsidy and must move forward. But you cannot even tell Nigerians where you are taking them. Forward into deeper poverty, mounting debt, insecurity and mass unemployment?
“Since your inauguration in 2023, your leadership has become synonymous with hardship, pain and despair. Your record is a working example of how a country should not be led. You have created poverty on an industrial scale, pushing more than 79 million Nigerians into extreme poverty.
“Your campaign’s Director-General says hungry Nigerians are simply lazy. He delivered that statement in grammar so badly constructed it could wake the dead. This government does not even believe Nigerians are hungry. How can you solve a problem you refuse to acknowledge?
“You created poverty, then insult the people suffering from it. You attack my Affordable Life campaign, but the people you are really attacking are the millions of Nigerians desperate for relief from your failed leadership.
“Bola, Nigerians have tested your leadership. The verdict is clear: you are a disaster. In Yoruba culture, I am told, a calabash of pepper represents hostile leadership, while a calabash of honey represents hospitable leadership. Yours is a calabash of pepper.
“You say Nigeria will never return to subsidised petrol prices. You are wrong. By the grace of the Almighty and with the mandate of the Nigerian people, I will restore a transparent, production-based subsidy tied to the local refining of fuel. Nigerians will benefit directly through lower energy costs, including the prices of petrol and diesel.
“My administration will make deliberate investments in social welfare and end the opaque system your government uses to divert money meant for economically vulnerable Nigerians.
“You attack my campaign because you know what it represents: an alternative to the hardship you have imposed on the people. You want me off the ballot at all costs, but the will of the Nigerian people will prevail. I will be on that ballot, and I will beat you decisively.
“After three and a half years in office, you have no achievements to campaign on. Your own record of failure is the strongest campaign against you. My Affordable Life campaign will not be silenced by your insults or your threats. I will lead Nigeria back to prosperity, growth and development.”

items.author: Shahbaz Rana
items.content:
The government's decision to cut real estate income taxes by half has so far extended Rs34 billion in benefits to the influential sector in this fiscal year, contrary to the marginalised salaried class whose tax payments jumped by Rs13.5 billion to Rs193 billion.
The contrast between declining tax payments by the real estate sector and the growing burden on the salaried class once again exposes the government's unjust tax policies, which have put undue burden on fixed-income people.
According to provisional figures, the realty sector paid a mere Rs42 billion in withholding taxes during the July-October period of the current fiscal year, which was Rs34 billion, or 45%, less than the same period of last year. The reduction is steeper despite an uptick in the real estate sector after the government reversed its policy to discourage speculative investment.
According to real estate sector experts, the number of transactions and the value of properties have started increasing, yet their tax contributions plunged during the first four months of this fiscal year.
As a result, the gap between tax payments by the salaried class and the realty sector, which was favoured by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif through policy reversal, increased by 360% in just four months.
The salaried class paid roughly Rs193 billion in income tax, which was Rs151 billion, or 360%, higher than the realty sector contribution. Last year, the salaried class had paid Rs179 billion in four months.
In June this year, on the request of PM Sharif's government, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) endorsed a 50% cut for real estate and a fixed tax scheme for retailers.
The influential trading and real estate sectors remained largely outside the net, with the IMF either endorsing tax concessions or keeping its eyes closed. Collecting due taxes from agriculture, real estate and traders was part of the three-year $7 billion loan package. The board is tentatively scheduled to approve the fifth loan tranche next month.
In addition to Rs193 billion in income tax payments, the tax collection from professional services rose 17% to Rs111 billion during the July-October period. Some of the salaried persons are also taxed under this head.
In fiscal year 2026, the realty sector had paid Rs236 billion, but it has now been halved. In the budget, the government reduced the advance tax on sale and purchase of immovable property by 50%. On the sale of property, three slabs have been merged, and a single rate of 2.75% has been introduced against 5.5%. On the purchase of property, the tax rate has been reduced from 2.5% to 1.25%.
Because of this steep reduction, the advance income tax collection on the sale of property decreased from Rs52.7 billion to Rs27.3 billion in four months, a reduction of Rs25.4 billion, or 48%.
Likewise, on the purchase of properties, the income tax collection dipped from Rs23.1 billion to Rs14.7 billion, a reduction of Rs8.4 billion, or 37%, according to these statistics.
Official data showed that the withholding taxes paid by wholesalers and retailers almost remained stagnant during the first four months of the current fiscal year. The combined withholding taxes paid by wholesalers and retailers amounted to Rs24.7 billion. These were Rs600 million, or 2.5%, more than the last fiscal year.
Wholesalers paid Rs8.8 billion in four months, down by Rs571 million, or 6.5%. Instead of using the data of wholesalers to go after the retailers, the Federal Board of Revenue introduced a fixed tax scheme that has miserably failed. The traders, after making promises to become tax return filers, stayed outside the net amid a lack of political will to go after them.
The FBR has digitally mapped 1.2 million small shopkeepers who were required to file returns but opted to stay out. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has not yet given the go-ahead to go after them.
Retailers paid Rs16.5 billion in income tax, higher by Rs1.2 billion, or 8%, than the comparative period of the last fiscal year. The combined taxes paid by retailers and the real estate sector amounted to a mere Rs67 billion. It was Rs126 billion, or 189%, less than the taxes paid by the salaried class.
In the budget, the government claimed that it had given Rs52 billion in relief to the salaried class through a reduction of up to 3% in the tax rate and abolishing the 9% surcharge calculated on the highest tax rate of 35%. It also increased the applicability limit of the maximum tax rate of 35% from Rs4.1 million to Rs7 million annually.
The massive reduction in collection from real estate has widened the gap between income tax payments made by the salaried class and the real estate sector. Before the start of the IMF programme, the annual contribution of the salaried class was Rs391 billion, which within two fiscal years of the IMF programme increased to Rs629 billion as of June 2026.
The FBR has also booked a Rs95 billion tax shortfall for the July-October period, registering only 6.5% growth in revenues. The 6.5% growth was less than half of the prevailing nominal economic growth rate, highlighting the revenue slippages and weak enforcement.

items.author: SHAHRAM HAQ
items.content:
With the federal development budget covering barely a quarter of what the country needs, the government is looking to private investors to build the roads, hospitals, water schemes and power projects that public money alone cannot pay for. A bill now before the National Assembly Standing Committee proposes to make that easier by merging two bodies into one.
According to the Privatisation Commission (PC), this year's federal development budget is Rs1.126 trillion, against a stated need of Rs4.1 trillion. The Privatisation Commission (Amendment) Bill, 2026 will fold the Public Private Partnership Authority (P3A) into the PC, creating the Privatisation and Public Private Partnership Commission. The PC said the law would repeal the P3A Act, 2017, and place privatisation and public-private partnership (PPP) deals under a single board and a single approval framework.
Economists said the gap between needs and funds is the real reason behind the merger. PPPs let private firms finance, build and run a project, with the state generally supporting only the viability gap. That arrangement, they said, could stretch the limited public money much further, provided the contracts were sound.
For investors, the change is mostly about simplicity. Until now, the PC said, two federal bodies did related work, so investors dealt with two boards, two approval processes and two sets of advisers. The PC described the new set-up as a "one window, one law and one accountable board". Business stakeholders said the time spent moving between offices had been a hidden cost for investors, and a simpler track would help local companies take part, not just large foreign ones.
The bill aims to speed up delivery in other ways too. The PC said every project would get a fixed deadline and a dedicated team, and that ready funds for project preparation, viability funding and facilitation would remove the most common causes of delay. Four funds are proposed: privatisation, public contribution, viability gap and PPP project development. All will be non-lapsable, so the unspent money will be carried over. Analysts said the stop-start pattern of annual funding pushes up project costs, and carry-forward could ease it.
For ordinary users, experts pointed to service quality. According to the PC, private partners will have to meet performance standards written into their contracts, which make upkeep and service quality legal obligations. Analysts said maintenance was where public projects most often failed, and binding standards would be among the most useful parts of the law. New projects, they added, would create construction and operating jobs.
The question for taxpayers is what the state promises in return. The PC said a Risk Management Unit in the Finance Division would review every financial promise made by the state about a PPP before approval. Pakistan's PPP contingent liabilities already exceed Rs472 billion, according to the PC, which said the check mattered for that reason. The bill also says the state will not be liable for risks if a contract does not assign to it. Economists said the unit's value would depend on whether it could refuse a deal and whether its reviews were made public. The PC also said one board, one secretariat and one set of advisers would lower running costs and save consultancy fees.
The new commission would have 11 to 15 board members on three-year terms, of whom eight to 12 would be independent, including at least one PPP expert and at least two women. It will run a federal PPP pipeline, with transaction execution committees and PPP nodes in ministries. Disputes will go to mediation, arbitration or the Privatisation Appellate Tribunal. PPP agreements will become public documents, which experts said would help answer the long-held belief that such deals were made behind closed doors.
The PC has also tried to answer fears about the merger. It said ongoing projects would not stall and P3A staff would be retained for six months and then reassigned or released under their contract terms. It said not every deal under the merged body would be a sale of public assets, as a PPP brought in private investment and skills through a contract and did not sell the asset itself. Business representatives said investors with signed contracts would want to see the handover work smoothly before they felt fully reassured.

items.author: APP
items.content:
The Special Investment Facilitation Council (SIFC) and the Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) government have discussed measures to simplify business regulations, strengthen key Special Economic Zones (SEZs) and facilitate domestic and foreign investment in the province.
According to an SIFC press release issued on Saturday, a delegation comprising the director general and secretary SIFC visited Peshawar and held a meeting with the K-P chief secretary to discuss coordinated measures for improving the provincial business environment, facilitating investment and promoting industrial development.
During the meeting, the SIFC delegation briefed the chief secretary on the council's ongoing regulatory reform agenda, with particular focus on the implementation of the Asaan Karobar Act, development of the National Business Portal and establishment of Business Facilitation Centres.
These initiatives are aimed at simplifying business registration and licensing procedures, reducing regulatory bottlenecks and providing investors and entrepreneurs with streamlined access to government facilitation services.
The K-P government was appreciated for adopting the Asaan Karobar Act, reflecting its commitment to regulatory simplification and the creation of a more conducive environment for business and investment.
The meeting also focused on the development and optimisation of key Special Economic Zones (SEZs) in the province, particularly Hattar, Rashakai and Daraban. Discussions covered measures to improve infrastructure, operational efficiency and investment readiness of these industrial zones, with a view to attracting new enterprises, encouraging private-sector participation, promoting industrial activity and generating employment opportunities.
The K-P chief secretary appreciated SIFC's coordinating role in investment facilitation and regulatory reforms and assured the delegation of the provincial government's full cooperation in pursuing the shared agenda. The importance of sustained institutional coordination and effective implementation of agreed initiatives was also underscored.
In pursuance of the prime minister's directives, the SIFC is working in close coordination with provincial governments to simplify regulatory procedures, improve institutional coordination and create a more facilitative business environment across Pakistan.
Through a whole-of-government approach, the council is bringing federal and provincial stakeholders together to address procedural impediments, improve business facilitation mechanisms and establish a more transparent and predictable operating environment for domestic and international investors.
SIFC's engagement with the K-P government forms part of its broader efforts to translate policy reforms into practical improvements in business environment, optimise existing industrial infrastructure and unlock the investment potential of provinces.

items.author: ZAFAR BHUTTA
items.content:
Despite dissenting views from the member tariff and member development, the National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (Nepra) has increased the incremental consumption tariff by Rs2.32 per unit for agricultural and industrial consumers.
The government had earlier announced a lower tariff to encourage the increase in grid electricity consumption following a surge in solar power generation at private businesses and residences due to high electricity tariffs. But the regulator has now jacked up the electricity price by 10.1% under the incremental package.
The new rate applies to all agricultural and industrial consumers that come under power distribution companies (DISCOs) including K-Electric.
The existing incremental consumption package (ICP) tariff of Rs22.98 per kilowatt-hour (kWh) has been revised on an interim and provisional basis to Rs25.30/kWh with effect from the November 2026 billing month and for subsequent billing months until a further decision is taken following a comprehensive review.
In its decision on Saturday, Nepra said that any bill already issued for the November 2026 billing month before the notification of this decision would be adjusted in subsequent months in accordance with the statutory requirements and operating directives.
"The industrial consumption package shall not be suspended at this stage and shall continue at the provisional rate determined in the clause without prejudice to the lawful exercise of relevant statutory powers to make a further decision regarding revision, modification or termination in accordance with the applicable law and the original decision," it said.
The Power Division, in coordination with other relevant entities, as applicable, shall submit a comprehensive review and supporting information in accordance with the timelines, methodology and requirements specified. The submission shall include the outstanding assessment for the first review period and the complete assessment for the second review period from June to November 2026.
Upon receipt and examination of the comprehensive review, according to Nepra, the matter shall be placed before the regulatory authority for further determination of the appropriate rate and the future course of the incremental package on the basis of validated data and the legal and regulatory framework. "The provisional rate determined herein shall not constitute a final determination of the historical marginal cost or of any claim concerning the allocation or recovery of the difference arising before the effective date of the revised rate."
The findings for each review period shall be separately assessed for different purposes, including whether an upward tariff adjustment is required in each review. "Nothing in this decision shall be construed as waiving, suspending or deferring the requirement concerning termination where upward tariff adjustments are required for two consecutive reviews."
Member (tariff and finance) and member (development), in a dissenting note, said that multiple letters to the energy ministry requested it to undertake consultation with the stakeholders and provide the regulator with reliable data to make an informed decision. Regrettably, they said, the ministry never responded in a proper manner to the queries raised by the regulator, "which is unfortunate".
The marginal price, in proper form, was not provided to the regulator by either Independent System and Market Operator (ISMO) or Power Planning and Monitoring Company (PPMC), which were duty-bound to do so. "Since the ICP is a flagship project of the ministry, it should give due consideration to the observations of Nepra and the lack of interagency coordination among the entities working under the ministry," they said.
This determination sets timelines where each entity is required to provide information. "If the information is not provided within these timelines, the outcome of the review would be adverse, and we may have to either suspend or terminate the ICP," Nepra said. "Furthermore, any entity that fails to provide the required information within the stipulated timeline shall lead to the initiation of legal proceedings under the applicable legal framework."
Power Division's response
A spokesperson for the Power Division remarked that a wrong impression had been created that the industrial tariff had been increased and termed it "incorrect" and "misleading". "Rs25.30 per unit is the revised marginal rate under the incremental consumption package for industrial and agricultural consumers. It is not the industrial tariff," the official said.
The industrial electricity tariff has been reduced by approximately Rs18.94 per unit, inclusive of all taxes, compared with the tariff applicable in March 2024. The spokesperson stated that the average industrial rate in October 2026 stood at Rs34.40/kWh, excluding taxes.
"The package is being revised because marginal generation costs have risen due to the prevailing war situation," the official stressed and pointed to the temporary nature of the increase in the incremental package, with the revised marginal rates applicable from November 2026.
Commenting on the impact of Nepra determination, the spokesperson said that the adjustment ensured that the cost of relief under the package was not passed on to other consumers, particularly non-beneficiaries.
According to the official, the package has delivered substantial relief. Between December 2025 and September 2026, a total of 6,940 gigawatt hours (GWh) of incremental consumption was covered and an estimated Rs43.5 billion benefit had already been passed on to consumers. Industrial consumers received a benefit of Rs5 to Rs10 per unit on incremental consumption, which lowered their overall bills by an average of Rs1.5 to Rs2.5 per unit. So far, 209,335 of the eligible 518,316 consumers, about 40%, have benefited from the package.

items.title: Pakistan to Introduce 45 New Safety Standards for Cars
items.summary:
Pakistan’s new auto policy includes 45 additional vehicle safety standards aligned with the United Nations’ WP.29 code, aiming to bring locally manufactured and used vehicles in line with international safety requirements.
Adviser to the Prime Minister for Industries and Production Haroon Akhtar Khan announced the measures during a press conference alongside Information Minister Attaullah Tarar in Islamabad on Saturday.
Explaining the safety provisions, Akhtar said the government had incorporated 45 additional standards in accordance with the UN’s WP.29 code.
“When our vehicles will go through these safety codes, they will be considered the world’s safest vehicles, both manufactured and used,” he said.
The safety requirements form one of the six key pillars of the new auto policy, which also focuses on making vehicles more affordable, promoting exports, increasing localization, encouraging electric vehicle adoption and ensuring transparency.

According to a statement issued by Lamara Garba, Secretary, Media and Publicity Committee of the Task Force, the seizure followed credible intelligence received through one of the reporting platforms linked to the Task Force Command and Call Centre.
The success was recorded just a day after the Rapid Response Squad was officially launched by the Executive Governor of Kano State, Alhaji Abba Kabir Yusuf.

During the operation, the operatives recovered approximately 3,180,000 capsules suspected to be Pregabalin and arrested a 34-year-old man identified as Gregory Ogbuji.
The suspect, who is suspected to be associated with SEEMARK PHARMA LTD, registered under number 2012546, has been charged under Section 249 of the Penal Code.
Another suspect allegedly connected to the operation is currently at large.
The Chairman of the Task Force, Muhuyi Magaji Rimin Gado, described the seizure as a significant early result of the Rapid Response Squad, stressing that it demonstrated the importance of intelligence-led enforcement and effective communication between the public and law enforcement agencies.

The latest operation is one of the first major outcomes of the investment in establishing and equipping the Rapid Response Squad, which was designed to provide a coordinated and rapid response to reports of drug abuse, illicit trafficking, thuggery and other related crimes.
The Chairman warned individuals and groups involved in the illicit drug trade to desist, assuring residents that the Task Force would continue to take firm action against offenders without fear or favour.
He also expressed appreciation to members of the public for their prayers, cooperation and continued support, urging residents to make full use of the Task Force’s reporting platforms and Command and Call Centre to provide credible information on suspected drug abuse, trafficking, thuggery and other criminal activities.
He said the cooperation of residents remained essential to strengthening public safety and advancing the state government’s “Kano First” agenda.

items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
YouTube Premium allows users to watch videos without advertisements, but several free alternatives offer a similar experience without requiring a paid subscription.
Browsers such as Brave and Firefox can block YouTube advertisements, while applications including NewPipe, FreeTube, TizenTube, and SmartTube provide additional ways to watch videos without interruptions.
These options are available across Android phones, tablets, iPhones, iPads, Windows PCs, Macs, Linux computers, and compatible smart TVs. Some work directly through a browser, while others use dedicated applications with different interfaces.
Here are six ways to watch YouTube without Premium.
1. Use Brave Browser to Block YouTube Ads
Brave is one of the easiest ways to watch YouTube without advertisements. The browser includes a built-in ad blocker called Brave Shields, which automatically blocks many advertisements and trackers.
Brave is available on Android phones and tablets, iPhones, iPads, Windows computers, Macs, and Linux devices.
To use it, download Brave from its official website or your device’s app store. Open the browser, visit YouTube.com, and start watching videos.
Brave Shields blocks YouTube advertisements, including many ads that normally appear before or during video playback. Users do not need to install additional extensions.
The browser also supports background playback and picture-in-picture on supported devices, allowing users to continue listening while using other applications.
Add YouTube to Your Android Home Screen
Android users can create a YouTube shortcut on their home screen, making the website accessible like a regular application.
To do this:
Open Brave Browser on your Android phone or tablet.
Visit YouTube.com.
Tap the three-dot menu.
Select Add to Home screen.
Name the shortcut YouTube and tap Add.
A YouTube icon will appear on the home screen. Tapping it opens YouTube through Brave, allowing users to access the website without manually opening the browser.
This provides an app-like experience while keeping Brave’s built-in ad blocking enabled.
iPhone and iPad users can also use Brave to watch YouTube without advertisements.
2. Use Firefox With uBlock Origin
Firefox provides another way to watch YouTube without advertisements through the uBlock Origin extension.
uBlock Origin is a free, open-source content blocker that removes advertisements, trackers, pop-ups, and other unwanted website elements.
The combination works on Android phones and tablets, Windows PCs, Macs, and Linux computers.
To get started, install Firefox and open its extensions or add-ons section. Search for uBlock Origin, install it, and then visit YouTube.com.
The extension blocks advertisements within the browser, allowing users to watch videos without many of the interruptions found on the regular YouTube website.
Android users can also add YouTube to their home screen through Firefox.
Open YouTube.com, tap the three-dot menu, and select Add to Home Screen. The shortcut will open YouTube in Firefox with uBlock Origin enabled.
However, Firefox on iPhones and iPads does not support the same extension system. Therefore, Brave is the more suitable browser-based alternative for Apple mobile devices.
3. Use NewPipe as Another Android Alternative
NewPipe is a free, open-source Android application that allows users to watch YouTube videos without advertisements.
Unlike Brave or Firefox, NewPipe is a separate application rather than a web browser.
It provides its own interface for searching videos, exploring channels, and watching YouTube content.
The application also supports background playback, pop-up video playback, downloads, and channel subscriptions without requiring users to sign in to a Google account.
Users can download NewPipe from its official website or through F-Droid.
Once installed, they can search for YouTube videos and watch them directly through the application.
NewPipe is particularly useful for Android users who prefer a dedicated video player instead of opening YouTube in a browser.
However, its interface differs from the official YouTube application, and it does not offer the same Google account integration.
4. Use FreeTube on Windows, Mac, or Linux
FreeTube is a free desktop application that allows users to watch YouTube videos without advertisements or Google account tracking.
It is available for Windows, macOS, and Linux computers.
Unlike browser-based alternatives, FreeTube provides a dedicated application for searching videos, browsing channels, and managing subscriptions.
The application retrieves publicly available YouTube information through its own extraction system or an Invidious instance rather than relying on the official YouTube API.
FreeTube supports ad-free playback, local subscriptions, playlists, watch history, and picture-in-picture viewing.
It also includes SponsorBlock integration, which can automatically skip sponsored segments included within videos.
This is different from blocking regular YouTube advertisements because sponsored segments are usually part of the video itself.
To use FreeTube, download the application from its official website, install it on your computer, and start watching videos.
Users can manage subscriptions and viewing history locally without signing in to a Google account.
5. Use TizenTube for Ad-Free YouTube on Smart TVs
TizenTube is a free, open-source application designed to provide an ad-free YouTube experience on compatible smart TVs.
It is particularly useful for Samsung televisions running Tizen OS, where installing browser extensions such as uBlock Origin is generally not possible.
Unlike applications that completely redesign the YouTube experience, TizenTube retains an interface similar to the official YouTube TV application.
It removes advertisements and adds several features, including SponsorBlock, playback speed controls, and interface customization.
SponsorBlock can skip sponsored portions of videos, while playback speed controls allow users to adjust video playback up to 4x.
TizenTube also supports DeArrow, which provides alternative video titles and thumbnails.
Samsung TV users can install TizenTube through the TizenBrew installation process.
The official instructions involve installing TizenBrew, choosing the Install From GitHub option, and entering the project’s repository, reisxd/TizenTube.
TizenTube also offers a Cobalt version for compatible Android TV, Google TV, and Fire TV devices.
For Samsung TV owners who want a familiar YouTube interface without regular advertisements, TizenTube is one of the more suitable alternatives.
6. Use SmartTube on Android TV and Google TV
SmartTube is another free, open-source YouTube application designed for Android-based smart TVs and streaming devices.
It supports Android TV, Google TV, and compatible Android-based streaming devices.
Like TizenTube, SmartTube provides ad-free video playback and includes SponsorBlock integration.
It also supports high-resolution video, adjustable playback speeds, and several additional playback controls.
However, SmartTube uses its own television interface rather than the standard YouTube TV layout.
As a result, users will notice differences in the home screen, navigation, and overall appearance.
The application is designed for television remote controls and can be installed through its official website or GitHub project.
Users need to install the APK on a compatible Android TV device.
SmartTube does not run directly on Samsung’s Tizen OS or LG’s webOS, so users of those televisions need compatible alternatives.
Its developers also recommend downloading the application only from official sources to avoid potentially unsafe modified versions.
Which Method Works Best for Your Device?
Different devices support different methods for watching YouTube without Premium.
Device
Available Options
Android phones and tablets
Brave, Firefox with uBlock Origin, NewPipe
iPhones and iPads
Brave
Windows laptops and PCs
Brave, Firefox with uBlock Origin, FreeTube
Mac computers
Brave, Firefox with uBlock Origin, FreeTube
Linux computers
Brave, Firefox with uBlock Origin, FreeTube
Samsung Tizen smart TVs
TizenTube
Android TV and Google TV
TizenTube Cobalt, SmartTube
Compatible Fire TV devices
TizenTube Cobalt, SmartTube
For most smartphone and computer users, Brave offers the simplest setup because its ad blocker works without additional extensions.
Firefox with uBlock Origin is another effective option for Android and desktop users.
Meanwhile, NewPipe and FreeTube are useful for people who prefer dedicated applications instead of browsers.
On smart TVs, TizenTube offers an experience closer to the official YouTube interface, while SmartTube provides a different layout with additional customization options.
Final Thoughts
YouTube Premium is not the only way to watch videos without advertisements. Free browsers and alternative applications provide several options across smartphones, tablets, computers, and smart TVs.
Brave is a convenient starting point for most users, while Firefox with uBlock Origin offers another browser-based solution. Android users can also choose NewPipe, and desktop users can install FreeTube.
For televisions, TizenTube and SmartTube provide alternatives depending on the device’s operating system.
These methods block or avoid advertisements within their respective browsers and applications. They do not activate YouTube Premium or remove advertisements from the official YouTube application.
Since YouTube regularly updates its advertising systems, the effectiveness of individual ad-blocking methods can change over time. Users should keep their browsers and applications updated and download third-party software only from official sources.

items.title: IESCO: 3 Cities Will Be Up to 10 Hours Without Electricity on 8 November
items.summary:
The Islamabad Electric Supply Company (IESCO) will suspend electricity in parts of Islamabad, Rawalpindi and Jhelum on Sunday, November 8, with some areas going without power for up to 10 hours.
According to the shutdown schedule shared by IESCO, most 11kV feeders will stay off from 9:00 AM to 2:00 PM for annual maintenance, construction and development work, and grid transformer upkeep. The longest outage is in Rawalpindi Cantt, where the Islamabad Feed Mill (IFM) feeder near Baga Sheikhan will remain off from 7:00 AM to 5:00 PM.
Several other feeders will also run longer than the standard five-hour window. The New GHQ feeder in Rawalpindi Cantt is scheduled from 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM, while maintenance on the Taxila-HIT 132kV transmission line in Attock is listed from 9:00 AM to 4:00 PM. A second batch of Chaklala-area feeders will be off from 10:00 AM to 1:00 PM.

items.content:
President Bola Tinubu has called on Nigerian youths to actively participate in the 2027 general elections.
Speaking during the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential rally in Rivers on Saturday, the President said the outcome of the 2027 elections would have significant implications for the future of young Nigerians.
Addressing the youths at the rally, the President said they had a responsibility to shape the country’s future through active participation in the electoral process.
“To the youth of Nigeria, I’m looking at you. This election is about you. It’s not about me. Your future depends on this election,” he said.
Atiku to Tinubu: I laid foundation for my university during your forfeiture case in US
Hunger: I&#8217;m clearing the mess created by Atiku and others, says Tinubu
He urged those who had registered as voters but were yet to collect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) to visit the appropriate collection centres, describing the voter card as an important instrument for determining the country’s leadership.
The President appealed to young Nigerians not to disregard the opportunity to participate in the electoral process, saying their votes would give them a voice in deciding the direction of the country.
“It is left for you to use the weapon you have. And that weapon is the PVC. If you have not collected yours, please go ahead and collect it. Please. I beg you. I take God beg you,” Tinubu said.
The President also highlighted his administration’s economic policies, arguing that economic development and the distribution of prosperity were essential to improving the living conditions of Nigerians, particularly young people.
He maintained that his government was addressing outstanding financial obligations inherited from previous administrations, including unpaid pensions and gratuities owed to retirees.
According to him, billions and trillions of naira in pension and gratuity liabilities had accumulated before his administration assumed office, but efforts were being made to settle the outstanding payments.
“The people that governed before, they left unpaid pensions and gratuity in billions and trillions of naira. That is being cleared. So that every family is included. We are sharing prosperity already,” he said.
Tinubu said the ongoing efforts to settle the liabilities were part of his administration’s broader commitment to ensuring that more Nigerian families benefited from economic opportunities and government policies.

items.title: Punjab Announces Four-Subject Exam for Class 8
items.summary:
Punjab Education Minister Rana Sikandar Hayat has shared details of the assessment arrangements for students in Grades 5 and 8.
Grade 8 students will appear in examinations covering four major subjects, following the same format used last time. The examinations will be conducted on e-sheets, while online screen marking will be ensured to maintain transparency in the checking process.
Grade 5 students, meanwhile, will undergo a holistic assessment instead of a conventional examination. The minister said the assessment would follow a fair and transparent process.
Hayat shared the details in a statement, outlining the examination format for Grade 8 and the assessment approach for Grade 5.

items.author: Akshit Pushkarna
items.content:
New-age tech stocks extended their rally this week, with 54 of the 69 companies under Inc42’s coverage posting gains ranging from 0.4% to 23.3%.
CarTrade led the gainers, rebounding 23.3% after last week’s steep decline to close at ₹2,699.30. Awfis followed with a 20.4% rise to ₹281.65, while ixigo climbed 19.1%.
Recently listed Tonbo Imaging and Zetwerk touched fresh highs during the week. Lenskart, Ather Energy, Eternal, and Nykaa were also among the stocks that hit 52-week highs.
The gains lifted the combined market capitalisation of the 69 companies to $169.3 Bn from $160.9 Bn last week, an increase of 5.2%.
Among the losers, RateGain fell the highest by 9.19% to close the week at ₹725.90.
Here are some key developments from listed new-age tech companies during the week:
Kissht’s AUM Crosses ₹10,000 Cr: Kissht’s assets under management (AUM) crossed ₹10,000 Cr, driven by growth in personal loans and its expansion into loans against property. The company attributed the growth to its AI-led underwriting and digital collections infrastructure, adding that its recent ₹832.2 Cr preferential issue strengthened its capital base.
MobiKwik Secures NBFC Licence: MobiKwik received an RBI licence to operate as an NBFC, following in-principle approval in April 2026. It plans to begin operations within three to six months and disburse ₹5,000 Cr in consumer and MSME loans over three to four years through an asset-light co-lending model.
Pine Labs Partners With Stripe: Pine Labs partnered with Stripe to offer Singapore retailers a unified platform for online and in-store payments, combining Stripe’s online infrastructure with Pine Labs’ terminals and merchant tools. The companies plan to expand the offering to other Southeast Asian markets in 2027. Pine Labs served 11.6 Lakh merchants across more than 22 markets at the end of Q2 FY27.
Here’s a look at the performance of the broader markets this week.
Benchmarks Jump Over 8%
Indian equities recorded a sharp weekly recovery, with the Nifty 50 gaining 8.6%, or 1,977 points, to close at 25,030.35. The Sensex rose 8.8%, or 6,568 points, to 81,028.02. Both benchmarks advanced in all five sessions, with the Nifty ending at its weekly high.
The broader market’s gains were smaller, with the Nifty Midcap 100 and Nifty Smallcap 100 rising 5.8% and 2.8%, respectively.
Renewed foreign investor buying, strong Q2 FY27 earnings, easing geopolitical concerns, and lower crude oil prices supported sentiment. Lower bond yields and a softer dollar also helped.
Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) bought a net ₹45,960 Cr of equities across the five sessions, marking their second consecutive week of buying after a 10-week selling streak. The inflows exceeded the ₹45,162 Cr they sold during October.
Domestic institutional investors (DIIs) sold a net ₹24,197 Cr, ending an 11-week buying streak. Together, the two investor groups remained net buyers of approximately ₹21,763 Cr.
Geojit Investments’ head of research Vinod Nair attributed the improved sentiment to strong Q2 earnings, healthy October auto sales, and firm GST collections, alongside easing concerns around the Iran conflict and tariffs following the US midterm election verdict.
He also pointed to foreign investors rotating out of crowded AI trades. The Indian market’s rally coincided with a selloff in global AI and semiconductor stocks.
Private banks led the gains following renewed foreign investor interest in a segment previously weighed down by concerns over net interest margins. Automobile and consumption stocks benefited from festive demand, while IT and PSU banks recorded relatively modest gains.
The sustainability of foreign inflows, crude oil prices, and developments in West Asia will remain key market triggers. Remaining Q2 results, US inflation and jobs data, and India’s inflation print will also influence trading.
Nair cautioned that intermittent profit booking could follow the sharp gains, although the near-term outlook remains constructive. He favours large-cap companies with earnings visibility and a buy-on-dips approach.
Meanwhile, the stock market will open for a special Muhurat trading session tomorrow, from 14:20 IST to 15:30 IST, on the occasion of Diwali.
Now, let’s take a detailed look at the performance of Awifs and RateGain this week.
Awfis Rallies After Q2 Results
Awfis shares gained 20.4% this week to close at ₹281.65, following a near-doubling of its consolidated net profit in Q2 FY27. Net profit rose 92.8% to ₹30.8 Cr from ₹16 Cr a year ago and increased 28.5% from ₹24 Cr in the preceding quarter.
Operating revenue grew 19.6% YoY and 3.2% QoQ to ₹438.7 Cr. Awfis reported normalised revenue of ₹451 Cr, including an adjustment of around ₹13 Cr for actual rent received under finance lease arrangements. On this basis, coworking and allied services contributed approximately ₹376 Cr, while construction and fit-out projects under its Transform vertical generated ₹75 Cr.
Awfis added six centres during the quarter, taking its network to 254 centres with approximately 1.74 Lakh seats across 18 cities. Portfolio occupancy stood at 76.2%, rising to 84.1% at centres operational for more than 12 months.
Its premium portfolio comprised 29 Gold and 10 Elite centres. The company said incremental premium seats were being signed at prices around 35% higher than its flagship offerings.
Awfis plans to prioritise occupancy, client renewals, and capital-efficient expansion, while adding premium workspaces in Pune, Bengaluru, Mumbai, and Delhi NCR.
RateGain Falls Despite Growth
RateGain shares declined 9.2% this week to close at ₹725.90, despite reporting a 46.5% YoY increase in consolidated net profit to ₹74.7 Cr in Q2 FY27. The company’s stock plunged by over 11% on Friday, the next trading session after its quarterly disclosures.
Operating revenue surged 152.6% YoY to ₹745.4 Cr, largely reflecting the consolidation of travel marketing platform Sojern, acquired for $250 Mn in November 2025.
Sequentially, however, revenue fell 5% from ₹785 Cr, while net profit declined 21.3% from ₹94.9 Cr.
Excluding expenses related to deferred deal consideration for Sojern, adjusted net profit rose 78% YoY to ₹90.8 Cr. Adjusted EBITDA more than tripled to ₹169.1 Cr.
The acquisition has reshaped RateGain’s business mix. Marketing technology accounted for 80.2% of revenue, followed by data-as-a-service at 13.2% and distribution at 6.6%.
Its customer base stood at 14,538 at September-end, around 4.5 times the 3,224 customers reported at the end of FY25. Customers include hotel chains, online travel agencies, airlines, car rental companies, and destination marketing organisations.
RateGain’s UK subsidiary repaid another $46.3 Mn of acquisition-related debt during the quarter. Cumulative repayments reached $93.8 Mn, or 75% of the original $125 Mn facility from HSBC and Citibank, leaving outstanding debt of $31.3 Mn.
The company reported a sales pipeline of ₹660 Cr and new contract wins worth ₹277.7 Cr. Chairman and MD Bhanu Chopra said its second-half priorities included expanding the combined RateGain-Sojern offering and increasing customer adoption of its AI products.

The court also ordered the unions to cease and desist from giving effect to any strike action pending the hearing and determination of a Motion on Notice.

Those listed as defendants include NASU branch chairman, Comrade Nina Ochigbo; its secretary, Comrade Dahiru Musa; SSANU chairman, Comrade Sadiya Mustapha; and its secretary, Comrade Nicholas Allen.
The court directed the claimants to ensure that the originating summons, Motion on Notice, supporting affidavits and a copy of the enrolled order were served on the defendants forthwith.
It adjourned the hearing of the Motion on Notice to November 18, 2026.
The order was issued under the seal of the court in Abuja on November 6, 2026, and signed by Vallari Aaron Masomene, Senior Registrar II.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Building on a months-long naval blockade on Iran, the US military ‌said on Saturday it is launching a task force to help crack down on Tehran's movement of advanced weapons and other sanctioned material over its land borders and through the Caspian Sea.
Task Force Iron Gate, which was first reported by Reuters, will be based in Tampa, Florida, and will ​coordinate with other US government agencies. Beyond movement of weapons, it will also focus on halting the flow of ​dual-use technologies used by Iran and stemming what Washington calls illegal revenue streams.
The establishment of the ⁠task force is the latest illustration of how the US is still searching for ways to increase pressure on Tehran, more ​than eight months after launching with Israel a war against the Islamic Republic.
While US strikes have dealt devastating blows to Iran's ​conventional military and the US naval blockade has severely restricted its crude exports through the Strait of Hormuz and the Arabian Sea, Iran still poses a formidable threat to the region and its rulers have tightened their grip on the country.
Iran's secret network
A Reuters investigation found Iran has created a ​secret network of military agencies to import at least $2 billion in hardware, explosives and heavy-duty trucks since January 2025, evading both ​the US naval blockade and Western sanctions.
The material entered Iran by cargo ship across the Caspian Sea from Russia, by truck from Central ‌Asia, and ⁠by freight planes from China, the Reuters investigation showed.
 Read More: Iran warns US of 'devastating response' if Washington starts war
S Central Command said the task force will coordinate with other government agencies. A US military official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said that was expected to include the Treasury, State and Justice Departments but also the intelligence community.
"Strengthening CENTCOM’s collaboration with US interagency partners will further constrain Iran’s ability to finance terrorism, rebuild weapons factories, ​and replenish their military," Admiral Brad ​Cooper, the commander of ⁠Central Command, said in a statement.
Central Command estimated that its naval blockade has prevented Iran from exporting more than $25 billion in crude oil.
Still, Iran has proven resilient and gloated following US midterm election ​results that punished Trump's Republican Party, giving control of Congress to opposition Democrats. Vice President JD ​Vance blamed the Iran ⁠war for electoral rout, and appeared to question whether the conflict was worth it.
Mediators have intensified efforts in recent days to end the war between Iran and the United States amid fears it could reignite after the US midterm elections.
Trump has been threatening to carry ⁠out a ​new offensive against Iran, putting countries in the Gulf on edge, since Tehran ​has threatened broad retaliation against Gulf infrastructure.
Reuters has reported that US intelligence assessments in recent months have indicated that renewed strikes on Iran would not fundamentally ​change Tehran's negotiating position or lead to the fall of Iran's government.

The Democrats are going around threatening a lot of people, including the Attorney General of the United States, and others, with Impeachment and many other forms of punishment, even though they admit they have no reason to do so, and there have been no impeachable acts… pic.twitter.com/N8gDs2OPmJ

He characterised the alleged pressure campaign as “weaponisation and lawfare”, accusing Democrats of targeting people over their political affiliations rather than any alleged wrongdoing.
Trump also singled out Democratic Senator Elissa Slotkin of Michigan, claiming she intended to target young people who support Republican values.

items.title: Astronomers spot white dwarf star with two rings of planetary debris
items.summary:
Billions of years from now, the sun is expected to run out of fuel and greatly expand into what is called a red giant, eventually shedding its outer layers and leaving ​behind its dense core, a white dwarf. Some of the planets in our solar system would be destroyed while others might survive.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Billions of years from now, the sun is expected to run out of fuel and greatly expand into what is called a red giant, eventually shedding its outer layers and leaving ​behind its dense core, a white dwarf. Some of the planets in our solar system would be destroyed while others might survive.
Researchers have now spotted ‌a white dwarf with planetary debris swirling around it in an unusual configuration that may offer a peek into one possible outcome for our solar system in the distant future.
Unlike in similar systems previously observed, the debris disc surrounding this white dwarf appears to consist of two distinct rings. The researchers said the disc may have been shaped by two planetary or smaller rocky bodies that are embedded in ​the rings after managing to survive the star's violent death throes.
The white dwarf, named J1328−1450, is located in the Milky Way roughly 1,600 light-years from Earth, ​in the constellation Virgo. A light-year is the distance light travels in a year, 5.9 trillion miles (9.5 trillion km). The observations were ⁠made using the European Southern Observatory's Chile-based Very Large Telescope.
Prior to this discovery, astronomers had identified 21 white dwarfs with debris surrounding them, all of which had a single ​disc and not a double ring of material as the new observations reveal.
"It shows that the remnants of a planetary system can have a much more complex structure than we ​previously thought, and provides further support to the idea that planetary rocky bodies may survive the transformation of a star into a white dwarf," said astronomer Felipe Lagos-Vilches of Universidad Técnica Federico Santa María in Chile, one of the authors of the study published in the journal Nature Astronomy.
The white dwarf has a mass about 47% that of the sun, jam-packed into a diameter roughly the same as that ​of Earth.
The surviving planetary bodies may be remnants of larger and heavily disrupted planets. One of them may be around the size of the dwarf planet Pluto, with the ​other one smaller than that.
Lagos-Vilches said the original star may have hosted a planetary system before it expanded dramatically into a red giant, engulfing some of the innermost planets while ones with more ‌distant orbits ⁠survived.
"The planetary system did not completely disappear. Some surviving rocky bodies may have been gravitationally perturbed onto highly eccentric orbits that brought them close to the white dwarf," Lagos-Vilches said.
"Objects that came sufficiently close were disrupted by the white dwarf's gravitational force. Their material was spread into a debris disc containing dust and gas. However, two relatively large rocky bodies may have survived within this debris," Lagos-Vilches said.
The presence of the two bodies may help explain the distribution of the surrounding material into a pair of concentric gaseous rings, Lagos-Vilches said.
"The ​outer ring is strongly depleted in magnesium ​compared with the inner ring. This ⁠suggests that they may originate from different parent bodies, or possibly from different layers of a rocky body that was disrupted when it went too close to the white dwarf due to its strong gravitational field," Lagos-Vilches said.
A glimpse of the future
In about 5 billion ​years, the sun will become a red giant, Lagos-Vilches said.
"It will eventually lose its outer layers and become a white dwarf. ​The inner solar system ⁠will be dramatically affected. Mercury and Venus are expected to be engulfed by the expanding sun, while there is still no clear consensus on whether Earth will also be engulfed during this phase. The fate of the outer planets is different. Jupiter, Saturn and the more distant bodies should have a much better chance of surviving," Lagos-Vilches said.
After the sun becomes a white dwarf, surviving planetary ⁠remnants, moons and ​asteroids could potentially be drawn close enough to the white dwarf to be torn apart by gravitational ​forces.
"A debris disc like the one around J1328−1450 could therefore represent one possible stage in the very distant future of our own planetary system," Lagos-Vilches said.
