…Soludo cites South-East projects, urges strategic voting
By Steve Oko
The All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) has adopted President Bola Tinubu as its presidential candidate for the 2027 general election, with Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, saying the decision was informed by the need for progressive forces to work together.
Soludo made the declaration on Friday while flagging off APGA’s nationwide election campaign at Alex Ekwueme Square, Awka, Anambra State, where the party unveiled more than 253 candidates contesting various elective positions across the country.
The governor, who is APGA’s National Leader, said the decision to support Tinubu was consistent with the party’s political tradition, recalling that APGA had similarly adopted former President Goodluck Jonathan in the 2011 and 2015 presidential elections.
He said the party’s support for Tinubu was also informed by what he described as the Federal Government’s commitment to the South-East, particularly in infrastructure development.
“Today, as we unveil our campaign as the foremost progressive party in Nigeria, we are also officially adopting President Bola Tinubu as the presidential candidate of APGA.
“We did it in 2011 and 2015 for President Jonathan. We are repeating it in 2027 because progressives are working together to support a President who loves Ndi Igbo and Ndi Anambra,” Soludo declared.
Citing the dualisation and rehabilitation of the Enugu-Onitsha Expressway and other federal projects in the region, the governor urged voters to approach the 2027 elections with political pragmatism rather than sentiment.
He said voting decisions should be guided by tangible benefits, enlightened self-interest and strategic political considerations capable of advancing the interests of the South-East.
Soludo also charged APGA candidates and members to intensify grassroots mobilisation through door-to-door campaigns, assuring them that he would personally join the candidates in soliciting votes.
He expressed confidence in the party’s electoral prospects, urging voters to distinguish between reason and emotion ahead of the January 16 and February 6, 2027 elections.
At the event, Soludo presented party flags to 44 APGA candidates contesting legislative seats in Anambra State.
The candidates comprised three senatorial candidates, 11 House of Representatives candidates and 30 State House of Assembly candidates.
Earlier, APGA National Chairman, Barrister Sly Ezeokenwa, commended Soludo for what he described as transparent and competitive party primaries conducted in compliance with electoral laws.
Ezeokenwa attributed the influx of new members into the party to Soludo’s people-oriented policies, describing Anambra as APGA’s political stronghold.
He expressed confidence that the party would record a decisive victory in the forthcoming elections.

Okafor, famed for movies like “Computer Girls (2003)”, “Sting (2006)” and “Ocean Deep (2007)”, was long rumoured to have quit acting to win souls for God. In reality, he says his long absence from the screen was simply about his preference for quality movies over quantity.

items.content:
By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo
The Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN) in Chikun Local Government Area of Kaduna State has appealed to Governor Uba Sani to reinstate traditional rulers removed during the administration of former Governor Nasir El-Rufai.
The association said the move would promote reconciliation, address grievances in affected communities and strengthen political support for the All Progressives Congress (APC) ahead of the 2027 general elections.
The appeal was made when former senator and APC Kaduna Central senatorial candidate, Shehu Sani, met with 48 zonal leaders of CAN in Sabo Tasha, Chikun Local Government Area, to seek their prayers and support ahead of the elections.
The CAN chairman in Chikun urged Sani to use his relationship with Governor Uba Sani to facilitate the reinstatement of the affected traditional rulers, expressing optimism that the move would attract considerable political support for the APC-led administration.
The association also appealed to the governor to upgrade the Sa Gbagyi traditional stool to first-class status, arguing that Chikun, which hosts part of the Kaduna metropolis, deserved greater recognition for its traditional institution.
The CAN leadership further called for increased political representation for Chikun indigenes, lamenting that the local government had no commissioner in the Kaduna State cabinet.
Describing Sani’s visit as significant, the chairman said the former senator was the first politician to approach the Christian community for such an engagement.
He said the meeting provided an opportunity for the association to present its concerns and expectations.
The chairman also cautioned against portraying the APC as a party belonging to a particular religious group, insisting that it should accommodate Nigerians irrespective of their faith.
“The APC is for everybody. It should not be seen as a party belonging to one religion,” he said.
Responding, Sani urged pastors and Christian leaders to rise above religious and ethnic sentiments in making political choices, saying Nigeria needed leaders capable of building bridges across religious and ethnic divides.
He warned against selective condemnation of killings and insecurity, insisting that the lives of Nigerians should matter irrespective of their religious or ethnic backgrounds.
The former senator said the condemnation of violence should not depend on the identities of victims, stressing that every Nigerian deserved protection.
He also challenged political and religious leaders to apply the same standards of accountability to successive administrations rather than remain silent over security challenges under governments they supported.
Sani further argued that opposition to President Bola Tinubu’s administration should be based on an objective assessment of government policies and performance rather than ethnic or religious considerations.
He challenged opposition politicians to present their records in public office and explain their contributions to improving the lives of Nigerians instead of concentrating solely on criticising the current administration.
The APC senatorial candidate also encouraged pastors and Christian leaders to participate actively in politics, saying they should not completely abandon the political space to politicians.
He said his visit was aimed at strengthening relationships across religious communities, seeking prayers and building support ahead of the 2027 Kaduna Central Senatorial District election.
The meeting ended with a special prayer led by Bishop Joe Yari.

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
By Chioma Obinna
The Nigerian Institute of Medical Research (NIMR) has hit back at the Academic Staff Union of Research Institutions (ASURI) over the controversy surrounding the implementation of the Federal Government’s eight-year tenure policy for directors, dismissing allegations of victimisation and personal vendetta against affected former research directors.
The Institute maintained that the policy was neither initiated by its management nor introduced by its Director-General, Prof. John Oladapo Obafunwa, insisting that it merely implemented a directive issued by the Federal Government.
In a press statement issued by its management in Yaba, Lagos and signed by its Media Consultant, Mr. Sam Eferaro, the Institute accused ASURI National Secretary, Prof. Theophilus Ndubuaku, of fuelling what it described as a needless media controversy through allegations it said were misleading and unfair to its leadership.
NIMR said it had deliberately refrained from engaging in prolonged media exchanges but was compelled to set the records straight in the face of persistent public enquiries and what it described as attempts to portray an administrative decision as a personal conflict.
The Institute also dismissed suggestions of an internal crisis, declaring that there was no dispute between its management, the Director-General and members of staff.
“All members of staff, including researchers, are at work performing their official duties, while the Institute continues to discharge its mandate as Nigeria’s premier medical research institution,” the statement said.
On the contentious tenure policy, NIMR disclosed that the retirement of three research directors followed the implementation of the Federal Government’s eight-year tenure policy for directors.
It said the Institute received two separate government directives on the matter through the Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation on February 10, 2026, and the Permanent Secretary, Federal Ministry of Health, on February 16, 2026.
According to the management, the affected officers were also provided with copies of the relevant instructions.
The Institute insisted that it had no discretion to disregard the directives, stressing that as a Federal Government research institution, it was obligated to comply with government policies and administrative instructions.
“It is misleading to continue personalising the implementation of a Federal Government policy or attributing its origin to the Director-General,” the statement declared.
NIMR also defended the vacation notices issued to the former research directors, arguing that their continued occupation of official residential accommodation after disengagement was a separate administrative matter.
The management explained that the Institute’s Housing Policy Guidelines, amended in 2023, allow retiring staff occupying institutional accommodation to remain for a maximum of three months with pay, after which the properties are expected to be recovered by the Works and Maintenance Department.
In a significant disclosure, the Institute said the housing guidelines were introduced and amended before the appointment of the current Director-General.
It further revealed that the Housing Committee responsible for the 2023 amendment was headed by one of the directors subsequently affected by the eight-year tenure policy.
According to NIMR, the former directors had remained in the accommodation beyond the period permitted under the existing guidelines.
The management consequently rejected allegations that the vacation notices were designed to punish, humiliate or victimise the affected officers.
While acknowledging the right of workers and their unions to pursue legitimate grievances, the Institute maintained that enforcing approved housing regulations and recovering government property could not reasonably be characterised as a personal vendetta.
However, the management reserved some of its strongest words for ASURI National Secretary, Prof. Ndubuaku, accusing him of conducting a media campaign allegedly characterised by falsehoods, character assassination, intimidation and blackmail.
It described the conduct as unbecoming of a responsible union leader, insisting that union leadership should promote constructive engagement rather than personal attacks.
The Institute particularly faulted the repeated portrayal of Obafunwa as the architect of a policy it said originated from the Federal Government.
“It maintains that union leadership is a responsibility, not a licence to peddle falsehoods, malign individuals or manufacture institutional crises,” the statement said.
NIMR also challenged media organisations to independently verify the claims surrounding the controversy, urging journalists to seek clarification from the Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation, the Minister of Health and Social Welfare or the Permanent Secretary of the Federal Ministry of Health.
It argued that such enquiries would establish the origin of the tenure directives and provide a clearer understanding of the circumstances surrounding their implementation.
Reaffirming its commitment to medical research and public health development, the Institute said it would not allow the controversy to distract it from its statutory responsibilities.
In a final warning, the management declared that the Institute would not become a battleground for personal grievances or media campaigns.
“NIMR is not Prof. Ndubuaku’s personal battleground, the Director-General is not a punching bag for political theatrics, and Federal Government policies are not matters to be rewritten through media blackmail,” it stated.
The Institute added that it would not be drawn into further media exchanges over the dispute, promising to provide factual clarification through appropriate channels should fresh developments arise.
The post NIMR fires back at ASURI over tenure policy controversy, denies victimisation claims appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.content:
…demand peaceful campaigns, protection of opposition parties
By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki
A group under the aegis of Concerned Ebonyi Youth for Democracy has staged a peaceful road march in Ebonyi State to protest alleged political violence, harassment and intimidation of opposition political parties ahead of the 2027 general elections.
The group condemned reported attacks and killings of opposition party members in parts of the state, insisting that all political parties must be allowed to campaign and exercise their democratic rights without fear.
Addressing participants during the march, Nollywood actor, Steve Rostick Eze, said the demonstration was aimed at promoting peaceful campaigns and elections while condemning attacks on opposition parties.
He urged youths to shun violence and mobilise voters to support candidates of their choice without fear, favour or intimidation.
Eze also called on security agencies to provide adequate protection for all political parties and ensure compliance with electoral rules and the rule of law.
“We have gathered today to march for peace, march for freedom, march for democracy. It is time that we say no to violence. It is time that we say no to oppression. It is time for us to take back peace, freedom in our state, Ebonyi State,” he said.
The National President of Anyigaemeya Youth Assembly, Mr. Nnanna Nwangene, also condemned political intimidation and thuggery, declaring his support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid and the governorship ambition of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) candidate, Dr. Ifeanyichukwu Odii, in 2027.
Nwangene said the march was to demonstrate that Ebonyi belonged to all political parties and that citizens had the constitutional right to freely express their political preferences.
He said: “We have gathered to tell the whole world and the Ebonyians that Ebonyi belongs to all of us. Ebonyi is not a one-party state. Ebonyi belongs to all political parties.
“We want a freedom where all political parties will be allowed to participate in a peaceful campaign without being attacked. We want every Ebonyian to understand that we are marching for peace.”
He called on opposition parties to be allowed to exercise their political rights without harassment, adding that political differences should not lead to violence.
Another youth leader, Prince Igwe Udemanta, warned against a recurrence of election-related violence in the state, recalling the loss of lives during previous election cycles, particularly in 2003 and 2007.
He said Ebonyi should not become a state associated with bloodshed, stressing that political disagreements must not degenerate into violence.
Udemanta urged supporters of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), APGA and other political parties to conduct their activities peacefully.
He said the people should be allowed to decide who governs them through the ballot rather than intimidation or violence.
He added that political violence could affect anyone, warning that no individual or political group had a monopoly of it.
Also speaking, a media aide to the PDP governorship candidate, Dr. Jerry Uhuo, said the march was intended to remind political actors of the need to preserve the peace and development for which Ebonyi State was created.
Uhuo recalled that the state’s creation followed years of agitation and sacrifices, arguing that the gains should not be undermined by election-related violence.
He said every citizen had the right to determine who became governor, senator or occupied other elective positions, insisting that no individual should be prevented from exercising that right through intimidation.
Referring to previous election-related killings, he questioned the justification for shedding blood in the pursuit of political power.
“Do you seek for power with people’s blood? No! If you kill the people you want to govern, who are you going to govern?” he asked.
Uhuo further alleged that political interests and influential stakeholders had constrained the administration of Governor Francis Nwifuru, a claim he made while calling for a change in the state’s political leadership.
He said the 2027 elections should be peaceful and urged voters to prioritise competence and capacity when choosing their leaders.
“Election is not war. People should remember that there is life after politics,” he said.
Other speakers, including Mark Onuh, also condemned alleged attacks on opposition political parties and called for an atmosphere that would allow all political actors to campaign freely.
The participants urged security agencies and relevant authorities to protect citizens and ensure that the 2027 electoral process was peaceful and inclusive.

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
By Benjamin Njoku
The Confederation of African Fashion,CAFA, has called on African countries to harmonise their fashion policies, strengthen intellectual property protection and invest in local manufacturing as part of efforts to grow the continent’s fashion economy to $500 billion.
The President of CAFA, Professor Lai Labode, made the call during the unveiling of the joint stand of the organisation and the Federal Ministry of Art, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy at the ongoing CANEX WKND 2026.
Labode said Africa had no shortage of creative talent but lacked the structures and policies needed to translate its creative potential into economic value.
“In Africa, we don’t have a shortage of talent. What Africa needs is structure. Money always follows structure,” he said.
He said the African Fashion Industry Growth Charter, developed by CAFA, was built around 10 pillars designed to address challenges across the fashion value chain, including policy harmonisation, raw material cultivation and processing, intellectual property protection, counterfeiting, logistics and market access.
Labode stressed the need for African countries to process their raw materials locally instead of exporting them in largely unprocessed forms, arguing that local value addition would create jobs and retain more wealth within the continent.
Using cotton production as an example, he compared Brazil’s reported $5.3 billion cotton exports with China’s earnings from cotton production and processing, saying Africa needed to build its own processing capacity to compete more effectively.
He also identified intellectual property protection as a major priority, noting that African designers and creative businesses needed stronger systems to protect their original works from counterfeiting and unauthorised use.
On market access, Labode disclosed plans to establish about 10 African fashion houses across the continent, alongside outlets in New York, Paris, Milan and London, to promote African designers and connect them with international markets.
He called for common intellectual property rules and standards across African countries, warning that fragmented systems could weaken the continent’s competitiveness.
The CAFA president also urged member states to support the intellectual property framework under the African Continental Free Trade Area, saying the relevant protocol annexes had been passed in February 2026 but required wider participation by African countries.
Speaking in the same vein, the Minister of Art, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy, Hannatu Musa Musawa, identified private-sector partnerships, policy development and infrastructure as essential to strengthening Nigeria’s fashion industry.
Musawa said the collaboration with CAFA should translate into tangible economic benefits, particularly job creation, while promoting African unity, cultural pride and soft power.
She disclosed that the ministry was working towards establishing an intellectual property policy to protect fashion designers across Nigeria, irrespective of their backgrounds.
“Partnerships, the policies, and hubs, it is very important to put us to capacity-building, and that can only happen through infrastructure,” she said.
The minister added that the ministry was working to establish creative hubs across the country to support capacity building, stimulate economic growth and create employment opportunities.
Beyond government policies and investment, discussions at the CAFA stand highlighted the need to build sustainable fashion businesses through financial literacy, proper business structures and production-cost management.
Series of discussions at the event also highlighted the importance of preserving African textile heritage while adapting traditional designs to contemporary markets.
Participants identified technology as an important tool for improving garment sizing, production consistency and quality standards, particularly as African designers seek to serve international markets.
They also emphasised the need to document traditional textile knowledge and protect the cultural meanings associated with indigenous patterns and designs.
Speaking on local patronage, Labode said Nigerians were increasingly embracing traditional fabrics such as adire and aso-oke rather than relying exclusively on Western-style clothing.
He said Africa was already exporting about $15 billion worth of apparel and related products but could achieve greater economic returns by strengthening local production and consumption.
He encouraged Africans to incorporate locally made clothing into their everyday dressing, saying the continent needed to place greater value on its own fashion and textile products.
The four-day gathering which gathers creatives, entrepreneurs, investors, policymakers and industry stakeholders from Africa and the diaspora to explore opportunities across the creative and cultural industries will round off tomorrow, with cultural activities and a Legends football.

items.content:
By Benjamin Njoku & Tony-Okafor Favour
The 2026 edition of Creative Africa Nexus Weekend, CANEX WKND, which opened at the Professor Wole Soyinka Arts Theatre, Iganmu, Lagos on Thursday, continues this evening with a blockbuster concert.
Headlining the night are some of Africa’s biggest music stars, including Nigeria’s Davido, Congolese sensation Fally Ipupa, Flavour, Cali-Ber Tha Grime, Sabrina Francis and Nigerian DJ duo Wanni X Handi.
The concert will bring together performers from Africa and the Caribbean for an evening of live music, rhythm and cultural celebration.
The four-day gathering, themed “One People, United in Culture, Creating for the World”, has brought the once moribund Arts Theatre back to life.
It convened leading voices from film, music, fashion, sport, publishing, gastronomy and business to advance trade, investment and commercial opportunities across Africa’s creative economy.
The opening day featured a series of masterclasses and sessions, including Building Your Brand as an Independent Artist, Podcasting for Success, Fashion Masterclass: Building Profitable Fashion Brands, and Building Sustainable Business Models in the Performing Arts.
In attendance were Vice-President Kassim Shettima, Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu, Afreximbank President and Chairman of the Board of Directors, Dr George Elombi; Nigeria’s Minister of Industry, Trade and Investment, Dr Jumoke Oduwole; and African Continental Free Trade Area Secretary-General, Wamkele Mene.
Other dignitaries included the Minister of Arts, Culture, Tourism, and the Creative Economy for Nigeria, Hon Hannatu Musa Musawa; Mrs Kanayo Awani, Executive Vice President of Intra-African Trade and Export Development at Afreximbank; Hon Ginger Moxey, Minister for Grand Bahama; Emmy Award-winning actor Uzo Aduba; filmmaker Funke Akindele; and actors Richard Mofe-Damijo and Thuso Mbedu among other dignitaries.
Speaking while declaring the programme open, Shettima said the world will eventually hear about the can-do spirit of African women.
He commended Afreximbank for committing $2 billion to Africa’s creative industries by 2027, noting that the industry is not just about entertainment, but also serious economic infrastructure.
Shettima took the audience down memory lane, recalling almost 50 years ago when the same Arts Theatre hosted the second World Black and African Festival of Arts and Culture, FESTAC ’77, where the Black World declared through music, dance, literature and art that “our culture was not just a footnote to history, but the very core within it.
“In 1977, we came to celebrate our culture. In 2024, we are here to capitalize it,” he said.
He urged Africans to be proud of who they are without asking for anything in return.

By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe
The All Progressives Congress (APC) in Gombe State has appointed Alhaji Sa’adu Hassan as Director-General of its 2027 campaign organisation and constituted various directorates ahead of the forthcoming general elections.
The appointments, aimed at strengthening the party’s campaign machinery and electoral preparedness, cover key areas including strategic planning, stakeholder engagement, media, mobilisation and grassroots coordination.
According to a statement signed by the State APC Chairman, Mr Mohammed Dantata Ndus, on Thursday, the campaign structure comprises three Deputy Directors-General, a Secretary, a Deputy Secretary and directors overseeing various operational and strategic directorates.
The three Deputy Directors-General are Hon. Ismaila Mu’azu Hassan, representing Gombe Central; Hon. Umar Ahmed Sulaiman, Gombe North; and LD Farouk, Esq., Gombe South.
Mr Meshak Audu Lauco was appointed Secretary, while Ibrahim Dasuki Jalo Waziri will serve as Deputy Secretary.
In the financial and stakeholder engagement departments, Arc. Yunusa Yakubu was named Director of Finance; Alhaji Bala Magaji, the Magajin Garin Gombe, Director of Critical Stakeholder Engagement; and Engr. Aliyu Mohammed Kombat, Director of Support Groups Coordination.
Other appointments include Hon. Ahmed Yayari as Director of Traditional, Religious and Other Institutions; Rt. Hon. Abubakar Mohammed Kunuwal as Director of Parliamentary Engagement; and Malam Kabir Usman Kukandaka as Director of Contact and Mobilisation.
Hon. Mohammed A. Bello will head Planning, Research and Strategy, while Syvanus Tahir, SAN, was appointed Director of Legal Affairs. Hon. Yusuf Manu Swa will oversee Grassroots Engagement.
The party also appointed Rear Admiral Nuhu Bala Jiddere as Director of Security; Hajiya Aishatu M. B. Ahmad as Director of Welfare and Humanitarian Affairs; and Abdullahi Jalo (Castic) as Director of SMEs and Cooperatives Engagement.
In the media and communication sector, Ismaila Uba Misilli was named Director of Media and Publicity, while Sulaiman Musa Arzoo will coordinate Digital Media.
Similarly, Sa’adatu Sa’ad Mustapha (Alkyabbar Kaltungo) was appointed Director of Women Mobilisation; Mubarak Hamisu Barakbisa, Director of Youth and Students Mobilisation; Dr Ishiyaku Adamu, Director of Persons with Disabilities (PWDs); and Musa Habibu Bushasha, Director of Protocol and Logistics.
The newly constituted directorates are expected to provide strategic leadership and operational coordination for the APC’s 2027 electoral campaign across Gombe State.
They are also expected to strengthen the party’s engagement with stakeholders, consolidate its grassroots structures, coordinate support groups, expand women and youth participation, and sustain political mobilisation across the state’s 11 local government areas.
The appointments signal an early move by the ruling party to organise its campaign structure ahead of the 2027 general elections.

items.author: Maureen Onochie
items.content:
As several post trend in social media, calling on Nigerians to register and get paid N50,000 support funds from the Federal Government, the Federal Ministry of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Reduction has cleared the air, saying it is an initiative designed to support vulnerable households facing rising living costs.
In a statement, Kingsley Onuoha on behalf of the Ministry’s Director, Information and Public Relations, said the people eligible for the ₦50,000 support are very poor and vulnerable people, hence they would be selected from the National Social Register and verified national identity records.
He said the selection covers all six geopolitical zones, hence, there is no application or registration process, and no individual or agent can influence the selection process.
He said each selected beneficiary was entitled to receive ₦50,000 as a Federal Government grant, adding that the amount would be credited in full without deductions as it is not a loan and does not require repayment.
Onuoha revealed that the reliable way for people to know that they were the selected beneficiaries is through an SMS notification from one of the authorised digital financial service providers, hence the message would contain instructions on how to accept the support.
He mentioned that after receiving the SMS, beneficiaries should follow the instructions provided by their designated payment provider in order to access the money.
According to him, “the approved payment platforms and their corresponding USSD codes are
PAYMENT PLATFORM USSD CODE
ALAT by Wema Bank 94523#
MoMo PSB 6710#
NairaGram 72600#
OPay 95520#
Moniepoint 557327#.”
He said once consent was given, the ₦50,000 support gets credited directly to the beneficiary’s mobile wallet, hence beneficiaries can access the USSD service without a smartphone or internet connection.
He warned that beneficiaries should not disclose their Personal Identification Number (PIN), One-Time Password (OTP) or Bank Verification Number (BVN) to anyone, hence anyone demanding money in exchange for the grant is attempting to commit fraud.

items.author: Ayobami
items.content:
Thierno Barry extended his red-hot streak with a double as Everton beat Coventry 3-1 to climb into fifth place in the Premier League on Friday.
David Moyes’s side trailed to Yann Gboho’s goal early in the second half at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.
But Barry proved too hot for Coventry to handle, netting twice in the space of just five minutes to turn the game in Everton’s favour.
Moyes said this week that Manchester City star Erling Haaland “should be worried” about Barry replacing him as the Premier League’s most lethal striker.
While that might have been hyperbole, Barry has already reached 10 goals this season, surpassing his total for the entire 2025-26 campaign.
That miserable first season with Everton following his move from Villarreal is quickly becoming a distant memory of the in-form 24-year-old, who has six goals in his last seven appearances in all competitions.
Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall scored in the closing minutes to wrap up Everton’s third successive victory in all competitions.
It was a memorable way for Moyes to celebrate a notable milestone as he equalled Harry Catterick’s record of 592 games as Everton manager.
Catterick won the First Division title and the FA Cup with Everton, but Moyes, in his second spell in charge, is still waiting to end the club’s long trophy drought, which dates back to 1995.
Everton are heading in the right direction on the evidence of the last 10 days.
A pair of wins over Newcastle in the League Cup and Premier League were followed by the mature victory against Coventry — all achieved without Jack Grealish, who has been suspended following a breach of discipline after he reportedly skipped a training session.
– Deadly Barry –
Coventry boss Frank Lampard was left frustrated with a pair of rejected penalty appeals that could have turned the match in his side’s favour.
Lampard, who managed Everton from January 2022 to January 2023, has now seen 16th-placed Coventry beaten three times in their last four games.
In the first meeting between the sides since 2001, Lampard’s men should have taken the lead when Tatsuhiro Sakamoto threaded a pin-point pass to Jack Rudoni but the midfielder shot straight at Jordan Pickford.
Everton defender James Tarkowski escaped without punishment for pulling Caleb Yirenkyi’s hair, an offence that Coventry believed was worthy of a penalty and a red card.
Coventry were frustrated with VAR for the second time when Vitaliy Mykolenko’s shove on Taiwo Awoniyi failed to yield a penalty immediately after half-time.
They finally took the lead in the 52nd minute as Rudoni’s pass squeezed through Everton’s slack marking towards Gboho, who somehow poked past Pickford from six yards despite being surrounded by three defenders.
But the Ivory Coast midfielder’s first goal since his close-season move from Toulouse was swiftly cancelled out by Barry four minutes later.
Mykolenko swung an in-swinging cross into the Coventry area and Barry was left unmarked to thump his header past Carl Rushworth from close-range.
Everton had the momentum and they went in front after 62 minutes.
Barry’s initial shot was saved but the French striker pounced on the rebound to prod home despite Coventry’s appeals for handball.
Barry turned provider in the 81st minute, clipping a pass through to Dewsbury-Hall, who lashed past Rushworth from a tight angle to cap Everton’s stirring fightback.

items.summary:

So far in 2026, 5,182 confirmed cases of the highly contagious but highly preventable disease have been reported across the country, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), the nation’s leading public health agency.

items.author: Ayobami
items.content:
The United States has recorded more than 5,000 cases of measles this year, the highest number in 35 years, according to an official count released Friday.
So far in 2026, 5,182 confirmed cases of the highly contagious but highly preventable disease have been reported across the country, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), the nation’s leading public health agency.
That compares with 2,289 cases during all of 2025, and is the highest level recorded by the CDC since 1991.
State health officials have reported at least eight measles-related deaths, including among very young children.
Pediatrician Adam Ratner, who specializes in infectious disease, told AFP such deaths are “tragic, and that is completely preventable.”
Measles was declared eradicated from the United States in 2000 thanks to vaccination, but in recent years it has made a strong comeback, fueled by declining vaccination rates and growing public distrust of health authorities.
President Donald Trump’s Health Secretary Robert Kennedy Jr. is accused of fanning that distrust. He is known for his vaccine skepticism and has repeatedly disseminated misinformation about the measles vaccine and downplayed the dangers of the disease.
“Robert F. Kennedy Jr. does not believe that measles is a big problem and and does not want to believe that there are deaths from measles,” Ratner said.
“The burden of these diseases will fall on children, who are not the ones who are making these decisions.”
Measles causes fever, respiratory symptoms and a rash, and in some cases more serious complications such as pneumonia and brain inflammation, which can lead to severe long-term health problems or even death.
Before the vaccine was developed in the early 1960s, measles killed hundreds of children each year across the US. It continues to claim tens of thousands of lives worldwide.

items.title: Naira appreciates to N1,375/$ in parallel market
items.summary:
By Elizabeth Adegbesan
The naira today appreciated to N1,375 per dollar from N1,380 in the parallel market on Thursday.
Similarly, the naira appreciated to N1,349 per dollar in the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market, NFEM.
Data from the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, showed that the indicative exchange rate for the official market fell to N1349 per dollar from N1350.45 per dollar on Thursday, indicating N1.45 appreciation for the naira.
Consequently, the margin between the parallel and official markets narrowed to N29 per dollar from N29.55 per dollar on Thursday.
The value of interbank turnover in NFEM rose by 130.8 percent to $232.9 billion from $100.9 billion on Thursday.
The post Naira appreciates to N1,375/$ in parallel market appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.content:
Kano State Governor, Abba Kabir Yusuf, on Friday said his reelection ambition is not a do-or-die affair, insisting that power belongs to God who gives and takes authority at His will.
‎
‎The governor stated this during the swearing-in of Sanusi Bature Dawakin Tofa and Balarabe Sa’idu Gani as commissioners for Information and Internal Affairs, and Solid Minerals, respectively.
‎
‎Yusuf said those who view politics as a life-or-death struggle should rethink their position, stressing that his administration believes in divine destiny.
‎
‎”Anyone who thinks our politics is a do-or-die affair should think again. We believe in destiny, whether good or bad. We believe Allah is the One who gives and the One who withholds,” he said.
ADC PCC: We&#8217;ve appealed judgement against Mark, Atiku and notified INEC
Tinubu: Akwa Ibom visit reminds me of my Mobil days
Reflecting on previous elections, the governor said despite the setbacks his political camp suffered in 2019, they accepted that the time ordained by God had not come.
‎
‎He added that despite the challenges surrounding the 2023 governorship election, including the legal battle that ended at the Supreme Court, they believed their victory was granted by God.
‎
‎”2027 belongs to Allah and is in His hands. Is there anyone who can give besides Him? Since everything is in His hands, whatever He does is right,” Yusuf said.
‎
‎The governor spoke shortly after administering the oath of office on the two commissioners.
‎
‎He charged the new Commissioner for Information and Internal Affairs, Sanusi Bature Dawakin Tofa, to strengthen the state’s media machinery and ensure effective dissemination of government policies, programmes and achievements.
‎
‎Yusuf urged him to improve the coordination of the government’s social media platforms and work closely with the Kano State Multi-Agency Task Force on Drug Abuse and Illicit Trafficking to intensify public enlightenment campaigns, particularly among youths.
‎
‎The governor also directed the commissioner to establish stronger collaboration with ministries, departments and agencies to ensure consistent communication of government activities.
‎
‎Speaking on the Solid Minerals Ministry, Yusuf tasked Balarabe Sa’idu Gani with curbing illegal mining through effective monitoring, enforcement of regulations and collaboration with security agencies.
‎
‎He also urged the commissioner to partner with the Federal Ministry of Solid Minerals Development and other stakeholders to attract credible investors, boost revenue generation and create jobs.
‎
‎Yusuf disclosed that his administration had established a multimillion-naira Quick Response Patrol Office equipped with a 24-hour call and command centre, real-time intelligence desk and specialised laboratories for drug testing and investigations.
‎
‎According to him, the facility will provide residents with a secure platform to anonymously submit videos, photographs and voice recordings to support intelligence gathering.
‎
‎The governor urged both commissioners to discharge their responsibilities with dedication, professionalism, humility and accountability, describing public office as a sacred trust.

items.author: Nshua Cali-Dibang
items.content:
How much control do people retain over their personal information in a world increasingly shaped by AI?
Originally published on Global Voices
Illustration by Nshua Cali-Dibang, used with permission.
This post is part of Global Voices’ October 2026 Spotlight series, “Big Tech and Authoritarianism.” In this Spotlight, we explore how Big Tech facilitates and hinders authoritarian governments and practices, and how these choices influence the Global South. You can support this coverage by donating here.
Every search, social media interaction, and conversation with an artificial intelligence (AI) tool can leave behind information about its user. Individually, these digital traces may appear insignificant. Collectively, however, they can reveal interests, habits, preferences and patterns of behavior that have considerable commercial and political value.
As AI becomes increasingly embedded in everyday life, technology companies are finding new ways to use data to develop their products, personalize services and generate revenue. While these developments offer considerable benefits, they also raise a difficult question: How much control do people retain over their personal information in a world increasingly shaped by AI?
The issue extends beyond privacy policies and user agreements. It concerns the growing power of technology companies to collect information, draw conclusions about individuals, and influence the digital environments in which people communicate, work, and access information.
The business of knowing more about us
In September 2024, the United States Federal Trade Commission (FTC) published findings from an investigation into nine major social media and video-streaming companies, including Meta, YouTube, TikTok, and Amazon-owned Twitch.
The FTC reported that these companies collected extensive information about users and, in some cases, non-users. The information included personal details, interests, online activities, and data obtained from other sources. The investigation also raised concerns about lengthy data retention, inadequate privacy protections, and the use of personal information in automated systems, including AI.
The report highlighted a fundamental imbalance: Companies can accumulate substantial information about individuals, while those individuals may have limited understanding of how their data is used or how to prevent certain uses.
AI adds another dimension to this problem. Data can help train models, improve recommendations, and power automated decisions. However, the greater the volume and variety of information companies can access, the more important it becomes to establish clear limits on its collection and use.
The concern is not that every company collecting data is necessarily acting maliciously. Rather, it is that systems designed to maximize commercial value from information can create incentives to collect more data than people reasonably expect or understand.
Inclusion at what cost?
For millions of people, AI offers opportunities that were previously difficult to access. Students can use AI tools to support learning, small businesses can improve their operations, and journalists can explore new approaches to research and production.
In countries such as Nigeria, where access to resources and professional services can be uneven, these tools could help narrow certain gaps. AI systems that support local languages and reflect diverse cultural experiences could also make digital services more accessible.
Yet inclusion should mean more than allowing people to use a technology. It should also mean ensuring that they understand the conditions under which they use it and retain meaningful rights over their information.
Many digital services are governed by lengthy terms and privacy policies that users may accept without fully understanding the implications. Some AI products also raise questions about whether information submitted through prompts, uploaded documents, or other interactions may be retained or used to improve models.
The precise practices differ between companies and products. Nevertheless, users need clear explanations of what information is collected, why it is needed, how long it is retained, and whether it may be used for purposes beyond the immediate service.
Without these safeguards, the benefits of AI inclusion risk coming with an invisible cost: reduced control over personal information.
When corporate power begins to resemble surveillance
The connection between big tech and authoritarianism requires careful examination. Authoritarianism is not simply the collection of data by private companies. It involves the concentration and exercise of power in ways that undermine accountability, rights, and freedoms.
However, extensive corporate data collection can create conditions that make surveillance easier. Detailed personal information can support profiling, targeted persuasion and the prediction of individual behavior. Depending on the circumstances, businesses, governments, or other actors may exploit these capabilities.
The risks become particularly serious when personal data can be accessed or shared without adequate safeguards, when automated systems make consequential decisions without meaningful oversight, or when people have little opportunity to challenge how their information is used.
Concentrated corporate power adds another concern. When a small number of companies control widely used digital platforms, AI services, and large pools of information, individuals may have few practical alternatives. Leaving a platform may mean losing access to professional networks, customers, communities, or essential services.
This does not mean that every AI system is a surveillance tool or that every technology company intends to restrict freedom. It means that the infrastructure of digital life deserves scrutiny because its capabilities can be used in ways that extend beyond their original commercial purpose.
Nigeria’s data protection challenge
Nigeria has a legal framework intended to protect individuals against the misuse of their personal information. The Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 established the Nigeria Data Protection Commission and provides a framework for the lawful, fair and accountable processing of personal data.
Legislation is an important step, but effective protection also depends on implementation, public awareness, and regulators’ ability to hold organizations accountable.
As Nigerians increasingly adopt AI-powered services, questions about data governance become more pressing. Users need to understand their rights, while organizations must take responsibility for explaining their practices and protecting the information they collect.
There is also a wider question of representation. If AI systems are developed using data that inadequately reflects Nigerian languages, cultures, and social realities, their benefits may be distributed unevenly. Responsible AI governance must therefore address both the protection of personal information and the inclusion of communities whose experiences are often underrepresented.
UNESCO’s Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence emphasizes privacy, data protection, transparency, accountability, and fairness throughout the AI lifecycle. These principles provide a useful foundation for ensuring that technological progress respects human rights.
Innovation must not come at the expense of control
The challenge is not to reject AI or prevent companies from using data to develop useful technologies. It is to establish boundaries that allow innovation without making personal privacy an acceptable casualty.
Technology companies should minimize unnecessary data collection, communicate their policies clearly, provide meaningful choices, and strengthen protections against unauthorized access. Regulators must ensure that existing laws remain effective as AI capabilities evolve, while users need accessible information about the rights available to them.
Ultimately, digital inclusion cannot be measured solely by the number of people using AI. It must also consider whether those people can participate safely, understand the systems they rely on, and exercise meaningful control over their information.
As AI becomes more powerful, the question is no longer simply what technology can do with our data. It is who decides what can be done, who benefits from those decisions, and who has the power to challenge them.
The future of AI should not be defined only by what machines learn about us, but also by how much control we retain over ourselves.
Written by Nshua Cali-Dibang

items.author: Team Inc42
items.content:
The Directorate of Enforcement (ED) conducted searches at three premises linked to crypto exchanges CoinDCX and Delta Exchange India (DEI) over alleged unauthorised cross-border transactions involving crypto derivatives and tokenised foreign stocks.
In a statement, the agency said the searches were conducted between November 4 and November 5 across Bengaluru. The crypto trading transactions in question run into thousands of crores of Rupees, as per ED.
“ED Bengaluru has conducted search(es) at three premises linked to Neblio Technologies Pvt. Ltd. (CoinDCX parent) and Excelium Technologies Pvt. Ltd.(which operates Delta Exchange India) under FEMA 1999 in the case of large scale unauthorised cross-border financial transactions involving crypto token derivatives and real world asset tokens,” said ED in a statement.
As per the directorate, ED began its probe into the matter after receiving information of alleged forex violations by CoinDCX and Delta Exchange India.
The agency alleged that CoinDCX and Delta Exchange India facilitated spot trading, futures and options (F&O) trading and trading in tokenised shares of foreign companies – all through cryptocurrencies.
ED also claimed CoinDCX advertised these products despite not being authorised to offer them.
While CoinDCX is yet to issue a statement on the matter, Delta Exchange India said that it cooperated “fully” with the officials and furnished the information sought. In a post on X, the crypto exchange further claimed that it is not involved in “any cross-border transfer of VDAs (virtual digital assets) in any form or manner”.
“We acknowledge the Enforcement Directorate’s statement regarding their visit to our premises on 4th & 5th November… We cooperated fully with the officials and provided the information that they sought. We remain committed to extending our support and cooperation as may be required…,” said Delta Exchange India.
CoinDCX’s Alleged Modus Operandi
According to the ED, user funds (deposited in Rupees) were allegedly converted into stablecoins, primarily USDT, and then transferred to overseas crypto platforms including Binance, KuCoin, Gate.io and Bybit. The agency alleged that these transfers circumvented forex rules governing cross-border money transfers.
For spot trades, the ED alleged that CoinDCX used an account, opened in the name of a Costa Rica-based entity, to send the USDT to foreign crypto platforms. Describing the Costa Rican company as a mere “paper entity”, the agency alleged that the transactions were allegedly actually executed directly through CoinDCX APIs.
The directorate also made similar allegations for CoinDCX’s F&O product. ED said that the homegrown platform allegedly opened matching positions via APIs on foreign platforms after users placed orders, with settlements occurring overseas when positions were closed.
The ED also claimed that tokenised-stock trading on CoinDCX was routed through Hyperliquid, an overseas decentralised crypto trading platform. It said that user funds were converted into USDT to open positions, with settlements completed on the overseas platform.
The alleged volumes of spot, derivatives and tokenised-stock transactions were described as running into thousands of crores of rupees. The ED also alleged that CoinDCX paid hundreds of crores in transaction fees to foreign platforms in stablecoins. This, the agency said, contravened forex rules.
Delta Exchange India Under ED Radar
Just like CoinDCX, the Directorate of Enforcement also alleged that Delta Exchange India offered spot trading, crypto derivatives and tokenised foreign stocks via cryptocurrencies.
It alleged that a large volume of DEI’s derivatives and tokenised-stock transactions was routed through CoinDCX, which in turn executed them on foreign platforms.
The agency alleged that Delta Exchange India also transferred hundreds of crores of Rupees to overseas associate entities. These transfers are under investigation, added the ED.
In a statement, the ED said the fintech products offered by both crypto exchanges appear to have prima facie contravened norms under the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956, the SEBI Act, 1992 and the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934. The investigation remains ongoing.
The searches are part of ED’s broader clampdown on forex violations involving crypto platforms. Just days ago, the directorate launched a probe into alleged FEMA violations involving crypto platforms Mudrex and Saber.money as well as decentralised finance (DeFi) protocol Instadapp and its associated platform, Fluid, over alleged unauthorised cross-border fund transfers worth more than ₹4,940 Cr.
Prior to this in June this year, the ED had also searched six premises linked to five platforms, namely Transak, Carret, Xpat, Onramp.money and Onmeta, over alleged unauthorised cross-border crypto transfers.
The post ED Searches CoinDCX & Delta Exchange Over Alleged Illegal Cross-Border Transfers appeared first on Inc42 Media.

The price of petrol has been cut by Rs. 6.59 per litre to Rs. 346 per litre, while diesel has been made cheaper by Rs. 4.25 to Rs. 378 per litre.

items.content: Federal Reserve officials are weighing the inflationary risks from strong economic activity and the rapid expansion of artificial intelligence infrastructure, even as they signal the need for more data before determining the next steps on interest rates, Bloomberg reported.For live updates on US Markets, click here New York Fed President John Williams said inflation remained too high, although other indicators were not yet pointing to broader concerns. Speaking at an event hosted by the European Central Bank in Frankfurt on Friday, he backed the Fed's position that policymakers should gather more information before deciding the appropriate course for monetary policy."Inflation is absolutely too high," Williams said, while noting that wage growth remained consistent with the central bank's 2% inflation target and inflation expectations were well anchored.Fed weighs inflation against economic resilienceWilliams said monetary policy had an important role in preventing temporary price shocks from spreading into broader or more persistent inflation.Also Read: Federal Reserve rate hike bets strengthen as US jobs growth beats estimates"Our FOMC statement last meeting, I think, captures correctly that this is an appropriate time to accumulate more information to help us determine what the appropriate stance of policy is to make make sure we achieve a timely return to our 2% target," he said, according to the Bloomberg report.The Fed held interest rates steady at its previous meeting after raising its benchmark rate by 25 basis points in September to a range of 3.75%-4%. Policymakers have since emphasised the need for additional information while keeping the possibility of further rate increases open, Bloomberg reported.The central bank's preferred inflation gauge, the personal consumption expenditures price index, rose 3.6% in September from a year earlier. Underlying inflation measures that exclude food and energy also increased. Meanwhile, the US economy expanded at its fastest pace in a year in the quarter ended September.AI infrastructure raises fresh inflation concernsSeparately, St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem warned that the rapid build-out of AI infrastructure could add to near-term inflationary pressures, Bloomberg reported."When I look at inflation, excess inflation today, it’s coming both from negative supply shocks related to the Middle East and demand forces coming related to the AI build," Musalem said.While acknowledging AI's potential to improve productivity over time, he cautioned against shaping current monetary policy around benefits that may take years to materialise."We need to make monetary policy for the economy of the day," he said. "We cannot make monetary policy for the economy as it may be five years from now."(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

items.author: Business Desk
items.content:
Iranian health authorities have started handing out iodine tablets in Bushehr, home to the country’s only operational nuclear power plant, as part of an emergency preparedness plan launched before the June 2025 war, international media reported a short while ago.
ProPakistani checked that these reports are mostly being pushed by Israel-backed and propaganda-centered outlets. Verified sources have yet to confirm or report such an event.
Young Journalists Club (YJC) said Friday that distribution began near the plant and later expanded across the city. Crisis management authorities ordered the release of 180,000 tablets, now available to Bushehr residents only at comprehensive health centers.
The tablets are meant to protect the thyroid from radioactive iodine in a nuclear or radiological incident. Officials said they should be taken from 24 hours before possible exposure to four hours after.
Doses vary by age: infants under one month get one-eighth of a tablet; children aged one month to three years get one-quarter; those aged three to 12 get half; and people over 12 take a full tablet. Stable iodine saturates the thyroid so it absorbs less radioactive iodine.
The tablets do not protect against other radioactive substances or external radiation.
On November 1, US President Donald Trump warned Washington could strike remaining suspected nuclear facilities within 10 minutes, citing Pickaxe Mountain.
On October 16, he ruled out nuclear weapons but left the door open to further conventional strikes.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari on Friday urged the federal government and political parties to set aside their differences and engage all political, social and provincial stakeholders to tackle the economic crisis.
Speaking at the groundbreaking ceremony of a 600-bed hospital in Larkana, Bilawal warned that the fallout from the Iran war was placing an unprecedented burden on ordinary Pakistanis, saying that the economic consequences of the conflict were being felt across the world, from America to Larkana.
The fallout from the war, he said, is "breaking the back" of ordinary people. "We have not seen such a crisis in our recent history," he said. He also warned that the consequences of the Iran war could persist even after the conflict ended.
He described the situation as a major test for governments, stressing that public welfare must take precedence over political confrontation. He urged the federal government to engage stakeholders rather than continue fighting political opponents.
"If we remain engaged in fighting one another, with Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf [PTI], with Maulana [Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Fazlur Rehman], with terrorists, with India and Afghanistan, then we will not be able to alleviate the suffering of the Pakistani people," Bilawal said.
The PPP chief maintained that political differences must take a back seat to efforts to address public hardships, adding that governments would be judged by their ability to support citizens through the economic difficulties.
On electoral reforms, Bilawal urged political parties to participate in the proposed Parliamentary Committee on Electoral Reforms, describing it as a key platform for addressing complaints of rigging and strengthening democracy.
He said it was the first time he had witnessed opposition parties, coalition partners and government representatives collectively raising concerns about alleged electoral irregularities. If these grievances were shared, he argued, political stakeholders should work together to resolve them through the committee.
Bilawal also called on the PTI to nominate its representatives unconditionally, saying the opposition leaders in the National Assembly and Senate had been empowered by party founder Imran Khan to make decisions about dialogue.
"If the PTI does not take part in this committee, then the people of Pakistan should not pay heed to their cries against electoral rigging," he said, adding that the opposition also shared responsibility for strengthening Parliament.
On Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, the PPP chairman rejected claims that counterterrorism concerns were being used as a pretext to remove the elected PTI government through governor's rule. He maintained that the recent increase in terrorist activity and casualties represented a serious security challenge.
Bilawal said the threat from terrorists had increased following the change of government in Afghanistan, describing it as a ground reality. He also alleged that individuals imprisoned on terrorism charges had been released during PTI's tenure in the province.
While maintaining that elected governments were generally better placed to handle matters, including terrorism, he said the provincial administration had failed to protect its people. He also invited the PTI to resume negotiations, saying he would be the first to call for ending governor's rule if consensus was reached on countering terrorism.
"I invite the PTI to negotiate and request the government to engage with them. Do not close the door for talks," he said, recalling that his party had recommended engagement between the government and opposition.
On healthcare, Bilawal said the Sindh government was committed to ensuring that financial constraints did not prevent anyone from receiving medical treatment, describing access to healthcare as a "fundamental right of every citizen". He said efforts were under way to provide free medical services across the province.
He also stressed the need to strengthen higher education institutions and make quality education affordable. He said the provincial government was extending financial support to universities while encouraging them to become financially self-sufficient through revenue generation.
Meanwhile, Bilawal directed the government to ensure timely completion and quality execution of key infrastructure projects across Larkana division, including a revamped water and sewerage system for Larkana city and a new wholesale fruit and vegetable market.
The directives came during a meeting chaired by Bilawal at Bhutto House in Naudero, attended by Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah, Chief Secretary Asif Hyder Shah, Bilawal's Political Secretary Jameel Ahmed Soomro, parliamentarians and senior government officials. The meeting reviewed progress on three major initiatives: the water supply and drainage system in Larkana, relocation of its fruit and vegetable market, and a sewerage scheme in Shahdadkot.
Briefing the meeting, Public Health Engineering Secretary Sohail Qureshi said the feasibility study for an integrated water supply, sewerage and stormwater drainage project in Larkana had been prepared. The initiative aims to provide clean drinking water to every household while establishing a modern sewerage and drainage network across the city. The project is scheduled for completion within two years, he said.
The proposed relocation of Larkana's fruit and vegetable market also featured prominently in the meeting. Agriculture Secretary Zaman Narejo and Deputy Commissioner Larkana Tariq Manzoor informed participants that the existing nine-acre market would be shifted to a new 40-acre site equipped with modern infrastructure and facilities. Work on the new market is scheduled to begin in January 2027, with completion targeted within two years.
On the Shahdadkot sewerage scheme, Qureshi told the meeting that half of the work had already been completed and the project was expected to be finished next year.
Concluding the meeting, Bilawal directed the relevant departments to adhere strictly to the agreed timelines and ensure that development work met the required quality standards.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Saturday directed the relevant authorities to prepare a clear roadmap, with specific timelines and targets, for establishing a fully digital payment system across the country as the government steps up efforts to promote a cashless economy.
Chairing a high-level meeting in Islamabad to review progress on the government's cashless economy initiative, the prime minister said promoting digital payments was among the government's top priorities, adding that positive results had started to emerge.
According to a statement issued by the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) on X, Shehbaz called for ensuring nationwide internet connectivity and easy public access to technology to facilitate the transition.
He also directed the authorities to address customer complaints arising from the use of digital payment services without delay.
The prime minister called for promoting digital transactions between consumers and merchants through the government's Raast QR Code initiative, saying it was helping advance the vision of a cashless economy.
He also instructed the authorities to launch an effective media campaign encouraging electricity and gas consumers to pay their utility bills through QR codes printed on their bills. All ministries and government departments were directed to ensure the full implementation of the cashless economy plan.
 
TDAP
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif approved to modernise the Trade Development Authority of Pakistan to boost country's exports, enhance the access of local products to global markets, and align local industries, including Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs), with export standards.
The prime minister, chairing a high-level meeting, said that a modernised TDAP would pave the way for achieving access to global markets for manufactured industrial products with a view to boosting exports.
He directed that a complete ecosystem, including the entire value chain, be established for agricultural product exports and that highly trained human resources be inducted in the Authority through a transparent, merit-based process.
Calling for linking professional growth to performance and target achievement, he directed the hiring of a reputable private audit firm to conduct performance and financial audits of the Authority.
The prime minister said that Pakistan possessed vast export potential and an ideal geographic location and that the incumbent government was facilitating industries and SMEs to fully capitalise on these advantages to increase exports.
During the meeting, the officials briefed the prime minister on the authority's existing setup and key challenges. A comparative analysis of effective international Trade Promotion Organisations (TPOs) was presented, demonstrating how modern institutions provide integrated services for local market development, global market access, exporter capacity building, and trade expansion.
A comprehensive reform package was presented to transform TDAP into a world-class trade promotion organisation responsive to modern needs. The proposals include streamlining the authority's mandate to eight core functions, restructuring the board and management, optimising the regional network, adopting digital platforms and Artificial Intelligence (AI), and implementing measurable performance indicators alongside independent third-party evaluations.
A phased 12-month implementation roadmap comprising approval, design, execution, and independent assessment was also submitted. The prime minister directed that the reforms be completed and fully operationalised by the middle of next year.

items.author: Anadolu Agency
items.content:
The Turkish parliament has approved a bill ratifying the Makkah Agreement on Joint Defence between Turkiye, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, clearing the way for the trilateral security pact to take effect.
Lawmakers endorsed the measure by 279 votes to 119, with 398 of the chamber's 592 members taking part in the ballot.
The measure, formally titled the Bill on the Approval of the Makkah Agreement on Joint Defence between the Turkiye, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, passed after a lengthy debate among parties.
During the debate, ruling Justice and Development (AK) Party lawmaker Ziya Altunyaldiz stressed that the agreement aims to expand security cooperation in the region.
He emphasised that it contains no approach against any third country and that its main goal is to prevent conflicts rather than escalate them.
Opposition speakers raised reservations about the pact's scope and oversight. Mehmet Guzelmansur of the Republican People's Party (CHP) said clear rules are needed so the agreement does not contradict Türkiye's other international obligations.
On October 20, Turkiye had submitted the pact to its parliament for ratification. Turkiye's constitution requires separate permission from parliament to deploy troops abroad regardless of any international agreement.
On September 23, the government appointed Lt Gen Mahmood as the first secretary general of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement (MJDA).
The appointment was the first major institutional development since Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye signed the pact, and his appointment gives Pakistan the responsibility of establishing and leading the alliance's first secretariat during its formative three-year period.
The decision was taken at the inaugural meeting of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee, held under the MJDA, which brought together the foreign and defence ministers and military chiefs of the three countries in Istanbul on August 31.
Under the arrangement agreed in Istanbul, the secretary general would head the alliance's General Secretariat, based in the Saudi capital and tasked with overseeing implementation of the agreement, coordinating joint activities among the three militaries and supporting expanded defence-industrial cooperation.
(With input from News Desk)

items.content:
The controversy sparked by an interview of Federal Minister for Overseas Pakistanis Chaudhry Salik Hussain took a new turn as Defence Minister Khawaja Asif hinted at a broader conspiracy against the Punjab government—a statement that the provincial's government spokesperson endorsed.
Talking to the host of a private news channel on November 2, Salik said complaints about corruption in Punjab were commonplace, claiming that a disproportionate share of the provincial development budget was being spent in Lahore, the ruling PML-N's stronghold.
Incensed by the claim, Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz served a Rs5 billion defamation notice on Salik and the private news channel on November 3 over the allegations, demanding an unconditional apology, retraction of the statements and damages.
Commenting on the controversy on X, PML-N stalwart and Defence Minister Khawaja Asif on November 4 said the only way to interpret Salik's statement was to see it as a political move to create more space for his party in the Centre and Punjab by targeting CM Maryam's government.
However, talking to a private channel on Thursday night, Asif expressed suspicion that Salik's controversial interview might be part of a broader political conspiracy.
The defence minister said some characters, including some businessmen whom he described as "carpetbaggers", were attempting to create an alternative arrangement by discrediting the incumbent government in the country's most populous province.
He said the selective criticism of the Punjab government over corruption, when the menace was rampant across the country, appeared to be groundwork for some future political scheme.
When the anchor asked whether the proposed alternative arrangement was specifically aimed at Punjab and Maryam, Khawaja endorsed the possibility, saying others could also fall prey to the conspiracy.
However, he refrained from sharing his complete assessment, describing it as premature at this stage.
Asked whether the provincial government's aggressive response was also linked to Salik's family ties with Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, Khawaja said those ties could be a factor.
However, he added that, if one looked at whether other quarters were behind the controversy, his assessment was that certain people were doing their bidding to create space for themselves in future elections.
"They appear to believe that the possible retirement of the existing political leadership will leave room for them to present themselves as potential replacements," he said.
Responding to a question by The Express Tribune about Asif's suspicion that Salik's controversial interview was part of a broader political controversy to create an alternative political arrangement, Punjab Information Minister Azma Bukhari said these were indeed the facts the government was aware of.
PML-Q spokesperson Ghulam Mustafa Malik, however, dismissed the suggestion of a conspiracy against the Punjab government, saying that even Khawaja Asif had endorsed the corruption allegations.
He said Salik had made a routine statement and had not said anything new, but the government had turned it into a storm in a teacup. He added that his party was pleased that the ruling party was elevating its leaders' stature by reading too much into a generic statement.
Malik said his party had not made any direct allegations against anyone.
Asked whether anyone had approached the party to defuse the situation, he said no one had entered the fray so far. He added that only those close to Maryam Nawaz were issuing statements in support of the Punjab government, while the Islamabad camp of the PML-N had remained silent.
Malik said Salik would respond to the legal notice within a day or two.
Earlier in the day, Salik posted on his X account that he had received the legal notice and would respond to it soon. He added that "transparency is never meant to exist behind closed doors."
Speaking to journalists at Parliament House earlier, Salik said he would submit a comprehensive reply to the notice in court, maintaining that he stood by his allegations of corruption in Punjab.
He described claims concerning the appointment of the Gujrat deputy commissioner as fabricated and said his remarks about corruption were his personal statement.
He also ruled out the possibility of the PML-Q leaving the PML-N government, saying that, for now, the immediate task was to respond to the legal notice.
