items.author: Anadolu Agency
items.content:
From the first Muslim elected to the US Senate to record gains for Arab-led parties in Israel, recent elections have opened new possibilities for communities long marginalised in national politics.
In the US, Abdul El-Sayed’s victory in Michigan helped bring the number of Muslim candidates elected to Congress to a record high. In Israel, Arab-led parties emerged from the October 27 election with enough seats to potentially determine who forms the next government.
While analyst Giorgio Cafiero described the US results as a rejection of President Donald Trump’s policies towards Israel and the US-Israeli war against Iran, Arab American Institute founder and president James Zogby said the gains reflected decades of political organising, given fresh momentum from the Gaza war.
In Israel, political scientist Neve Gordon said anger over the war and other issues affecting Palestinians helped drive increased turnout, although he warned that racism and political exclusion could limit the influence of Arab lawmakers.
The results offer new opportunities for political participation, but analysts say turning electoral gains into lasting influence will depend on alliances, public pressure and overcoming resistance.
US: Muslim representation reaches historic milestone
The November 3 US midterm elections saw Democrats win control of both chambers of Congress, while at least seven Muslim candidates secured seats, including El-Sayed, the first Muslim elected to the Senate.
Jason H. Campbell, a senior fellow at the Middle East Institute, said Muslim Americans remain a relatively small national voting bloc, but their political participation has increased considerably.
Voter registration among eligible Muslim Americans rose from 60% in 2016 to 85% in 2025, according to the Institute for Social Policy and Understanding.
"Where Muslim Americans make up higher proportions of the population [like Michigan], they have more political influence and have seen the benefits of increased political participation," Campbell told Anadolu.
Zogby of the Arab American Institute said the election results reflected decades of growing political participation among Arab Americans, rather than a sudden shift driven solely by the Gaza war.
"The Arab American community has been growing and maturing politically for the past four decades. We’ve been making progress all across the country in voter registration and turnout, and in candidates running and winning elective office," he said.
Read More: Abdul El-Sayed becomes 1st Muslim elected to US Senate in Michigan win
"What the genocidal war in Gaza did was give greater impetus and purpose to our growth," Zogby added, pointing also to the role of strong candidates and campaign organisers in bringing the community's positions to the forefront.
Cafiero, CEO of Gulf State Analytics, described the result as a rejection of Islamophobic campaigning.
"It is clear that voters in Michigan rejected the hateful and Islamophobic messages of Trump and Zionist extremists in America and chose to vote for Abdul El-Sayed, representing what could be a major turning point in American politics," he said.
Iran war, support for Israeli become liabilities
Although Muslim voters and lawmakers remain a minority, opposition to the war against Iran extended well beyond those communities.
Cafiero linked the Democratic victories to the conflict’s economic consequences, saying its effects on the global economy had hurt American families and businesses.
"The success of Democratic candidates in solidly Republican states such as Kansas underscores a widespread rejection of the Trump administration’s wildly pro-Israel policies that brought America into a reckless war of choice," he said.
Campbell also cited rising energy costs and broader economic pressures, alongside dissatisfaction with the Trump administration’s immigration enforcement policies.
The war’s political cost drew acknowledgement from the administration itself after the vote, with both Trump and Vice President JD Vance blaming the war for contributing to Republican losses.
Cafiero also described the election as a setback for the American Israel Public Affairs Committee (AIPAC), arguing that its spending against progressive candidates had failed to secure the intended results.
"This election marks a huge blow to AIPAC, which invested massive amounts of money in candidates whom the US voters rejected,” he said.
AIPAC spent $84.1 million through its United Democracy Project super PAC and other political action committees, according to Responsible Statecraft, a publication of the Quincy Institute think tank. Of that, $55.3 million went to races in which its preferred candidate lost.
"American voters clearly rejected the US-Israeli war on Iran and Washington’s unconditional support for Tel Aviv," Cafiero said.
Turning electoral success into policy influence
Muslim lawmakers’ influence will now depend on building alliances with other Democrats and securing support for their legislative priorities.
When the new Congress takes office in January, Democratic control of both chambers will create opportunities for greater oversight of the Trump administration, including its spending decisions and military assistance to Israel.
The results do not guarantee a fundamental change in foreign policy, however. Congress remains divided over Israel, while the president retains considerable authority over diplomacy and military decisions.
Zogby argued that Arab and Muslim American lawmakers would not necessarily have to persuade their colleagues individually, as changing public opinion was already putting pressure on politicians to respond.
"Public opinion has changed so significantly in the past few years that we have the wind at our backs. So it’s not so much that we will have impact, it’s that politicians need to respond because their constituents are demanding change," he said.
Also Read: Democrats to investigate Trump deals, with eye on 2028 race
He added that support for changing US policy towards Israel and Palestine now extends beyond Arab and Muslim Americans.
"Democrats will respond to us and these issues because the majority of their supporters from all backgrounds are calling for change. We aren’t alone anymore," he said.
Cafiero said voters will also need to hold the newly elected Democrats accountable over the coming years.
“Now the onus is on the American voters who elected these Democrats to pressure them into implementing the agendas they campaigned on,” he said.
Israel: Arab parties emerge as potential kingmakers
In Israel, Arab-led parties secured their strongest combined parliamentary representation to date. The Joint List won 11 seats and the United Arab List, also known as Ra’am, secured eight, giving the two Arab-led parties a combined total of 19.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc won 53 seats, while the opposition bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot secured 48. Neither reached the 61 needed for a parliamentary majority.
The outcome has made Arab lawmakers potentially decisive in efforts to form a new government, although their participation remains politically contentious.
Gordon said the gains were driven primarily by anger over the war in Gaza, alongside other issues affecting Palestinians.
"The gains among Palestinian-led political parties are primarily due to the genocide in Gaza, alongside the widespread torture and sexual violence against Palestinians in prisons, the settler terrorism in the West Bank and the lack of intervention against crime within the Palestinian communities in Israel," Gordon said.
He also pointed to the role of far-right ministers in mobilising Palestinian voters, but cautioned that the results still fell short of proportional representation.
"One could say that Ben Gvir and Smotrich are responsible for the massive turnout – but we still need to keep in mind that 19 Knesset members is not 24, which is what the Palestinians should receive based on their percentage in society," he said.
Ahron Bregman, a teaching fellow at King's College, London, argued that excluding Arab citizens, who account for around 21% of Israel's population, from national political decision-making could not continue indefinitely.
"The Israelis, many liberals too, are happy to be treated by Arab doctors and nurses in hospitals, happy to buy medications from Arabs, many of whom own pharmacies, and visit Arab villages to eat great Hummus, but they are reluctant to have Arabs as part of an Israeli government."
Israel: Racism and political barriers threaten lasting influence
Gordon, a professor in the school of law at Queen Mary University of London, said the election results could translate into greater political influence, but warned that this would depend on how the coalition negotiations develop and whether efforts to delegitimise Palestinian representatives succeed.
"It could, but does not have to. Prime Minister Netanyahu, with the help of the secret services, has launched a major delegitimisation campaign against the Palestinian citizens of Israel and their representatives," he said.
One possible outcome, Gordon said, would be for Palestinian parties to support a minority government led by the opposition from outside the coalition. In return, they could seek increased funding for schools, infrastructure and policing.
However, he said he was doubtful that such an arrangement would give Arab parties direct influence over Gaza policy or Israel's foreign policy.
The negotiations are now moving into a formal stage. President Isaac Herzog began consultations with party representatives on Wednesday, and Ra’am announced it would recommend Eisenkot.
Gordon, however, said racism remained the main obstacle to Arab parties joining governing coalitions, including among parties in the opposition bloc.
"The main obstacle is racism. The second obstacle is racism and so is third – racism," he said.
He said the opposition bloc could still cooperate with Palestinian-led parties for pragmatic political reasons, but warned that prejudice and discrimination would take years to overcome.

items.content:
Update | November 5, 19:43
After the story was published, RapidClaims founder and CEO Dushyant Mishra said the startup is not in talks with WestBridge Capital to raise any funding round. He also said that the $200 Mn valuation figure is “incorrect”.
Original | October 5, 18:22
AI-powered SaaS startup RapidClaims is in talks to raise around $30 Mn in a funding round led by WestBridge Capital at a valuation of about $200 Mn, sources told Inc42.
The round is expected to be its Series B, with existing investors Accel and Together Fund likely to participate, the sources added.
RapidClaims did not respond to questions sent by Inc42, while WestBridge Capital declined to comment.
Founded in 2023 by Dushyant Mishra, Abhinay Vyas, and Jot Sarup Singh, RapidClaims builds AI-powered revenue cycle management (RCM) software that helps healthcare providers automate medical coding, improve clinical documentation, prevent insurance claim denials, and recover outstanding payments.
The startup primarily caters to healthcare providers in the US, helping them address billing errors, rejected claims, and delays in reimbursements.
Automating Healthcare Revenue Workflows
RapidClaims’ products include RapidCode for medical coding, RapidVBC for clinical documentation and risk adjustment, and RapidRecovery for managing denied claims, automating appeals, and detecting underpayments.
The platform integrates with healthcare providers’ existing electronic health record systems. It serves physician groups, hospitals, health systems, federally qualified health centres (FQHCs), and ambulatory surgery centres, among other healthcare organisations.
The startup is also developing inpatient coding capabilities with design partners, extending its automation tools to coding for hospital admissions.
In April 2025, RapidClaims raised $8 Mn in a Series A round led by Accel, with participation from Together Fund. It also disclosed that it had previously raised $3 Mn in seed funding. RapidClaims had earmarked the Series A proceeds for expanding its go-to-market efforts, strengthening its technology and product capabilities, and growing its sales and marketing teams.
At the time, the startup said it had grown sixfold over the preceding four months and served a double-digit client base. It was also looking to expand its presence among FQHCs, physician groups, outpatient facilities, and ambulatory surgery centres.
Investors Bet On Automation
The proposed fundraise comes amid increasing investor interest in startups looking to automate healthcare administration and insurance workflows.
In October, Confido Health raised $12.5 Mn in a Series A extension led by Z47, taking its total Series A funding to $22.5 Mn. The startup develops AI agents for tasks including appointment scheduling, insurance verification, prescription refills, and payment collection.
Meanwhile, Consint.AI raised ₹22 Cr to expand internationally and develop its AI capabilities for fraud detection and claims processing. Its products automate claims processing, digitise documents, and standardise healthcare records.

items.content:
The federal government on Thursday slashed the price of petrol by Rs9.41 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs5.56 per litre for November 6.
According to a notification issued by the Petroleum Division, the price of petrol was fixed at Rs352.59 per litre, while HSD would cost Rs382.25 per litre for Friday.
This marks the fourth consecutive day the government has reduced fuel prices, with petrol falling by Rs25.32 and diesel by Rs20.71 since Monday.
The latest revision also comes a day after the government slashed the price of petrol by Rs7.06 per litre and that of HSD by Rs3.71 per litre for November 5.
Read: Govt slashes petrol by Rs7.06, diesel by Rs3.71 for Nov 5
On Monday, the government announced that oil refineries would bear a burden of Rs15 billion per month, which would allow petrol to be sold Rs15 cheaper than it was in the global market amid the US-Israeli war on Iran.
On July 17, the government announced a new pricing mechanism under which petroleum product prices would be reviewed and notified daily, replacing the weekly pricing mechanism, as renewed tensions between the United States and Iran continued to drive volatility in global oil markets and raise concerns over fuel supplies.
On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced a special relief scheme offering Rs100 per litre off petrol for motorcycles, three-wheeler rickshaws and cars with engines up to 800cc, in an attempt to shield lower-income consumers from the impact of rising petroleum prices.
Under the proposal, an estimated 11.8 million beneficiaries would be covered. Around 10 million two-wheeler users and 800,000 three-wheeler users would be entitled to relief on 20 litres of fuel per month, translating into a maximum monthly benefit of Rs2,000 per beneficiary.
Another one million users of cars up to 800cc would receive relief on 30 litres per month, providing them with a maximum benefit of Rs3,000 each.
On Sept 17, the government reintroduced austerity and fuel conservation measures amid rising fuel prices, tightening business operating hours and restricting public events.
Under the measures, notified with immediate effect, shops, markets, shopping malls, bazaars, departmental stores, grocery stores, general stores and kiryana shops would close by 9pm throughout the week, according to a notification issued by the Cabinet Division.
Marriage halls, marquees and other commercial venues hosting festive events would close by 10pm, while restaurants, cafes, eateries, food outlets and standalone fruit and vegetable shops would be allowed to operate until 11pm. Takeaway and home delivery services would remain exempt from the timing restrictions.

items.content:
At least 11 people, including a Patrolling Police official and a Para Force personnel, were killed and 33 others injured on Thursday when a passenger bus collided with a truck on Depalpur Road, a Rescue 1122 spokesperson, Umair Iqbal, said.
The accident occurred near 17 SP Stop on Depalpur Road when a passenger bus travelling from Multan to Kasur collided with a truck coming from the opposite direction, the spokesperson said.
The spokesperson identified the deceased officials as Ali Hasnain of the Patrolling Police and Zahid Imam of the Para Force.
A rescue operation was underway to retrieve passengers trapped in the wreckage, with heavy machinery, including cranes, being used in the operation.
Read: 464 die in Punjab road crashes in October
Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz sought a report on the accident and directed the district administration to ensure the provision of the best possible medical facilities to the injured.
Expressing grief over the loss of lives in the accident, she sought a report on the incident while directing the authorities to ensure the best possible medical treatment for the injured passengers and prayed for their speedy recovery.
On her instructions, Pakpattan Deputy Commissioner Asif Raza immediately reached the hospital.
The chief minister also expressed condolences to the bereaved families and conveyed her sympathies over the deaths of a Para Force official and a patrolling police official in the accident.
Following the CM’s directive, DC Raza declared an emergency at the District Headquarters Hospital in Pakpattan and called in additional doctors and medical staff.
President Asif Ali Zardari expressed grief over the deaths of 11 people in the collision near Pakpattan.

Operating revenue rose 41% YoY and 8% QoQ to ₹1,120.2 Cr during the quarter under review. Total income, including other income of ₹25.4 Cr, increased 42.4% YoY to ₹1,145.6 Cr, while total expenses grew at a slower pace of 24.5% to ₹876.5 Cr from ₹704.1 Cr.

It reported a managed assets under management (AUM) of ₹23,892 Cr as of September 2026 and a return on equity (RoE) of 27.9% in Q2 FY27.
Moneyview operates a digital lending platform focused on consumers in middle India, offering personal loans through a network of banks, non-banking financial companies (NBFCs) and other financial institutions. It had a network of 49 financial partners across nine product offerings.
The company claims to have a user base of 14.9 Cr registered users and 72 Lakh active borrowers as of September 2026. Nearly 79% of its users came from Tier 2 cities and smaller towns, while 67% were below the age of 35.
Moneyview launched its initial public offering (IPO) in September 2026, comprising a fresh issue of ₹750 Cr and an offer for sale (OFS) of ₹341.7 Cr. The company fixed the price band at ₹32-34 per share. The IPO was subscribed 101.6X, with the qualified institutional buyers’ (QIB) portion witnessing 230.3X subscription.
The fintech company’s shares listed on the NSE and BSE on October 1 at ₹55 apiece, marking a 61.8% premium to the upper end of the IPO price band.
The shares closed today’s trading session 5.70% higher than previous close at ₹58.25

items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
The International Monetary Fund (IMF) on Thursday called for a broader, simpler, fairer and more predictable taxation system in the country to generate resources for human capital development, infrastructure and investment, saying this would help raise Pakistan’s potential gross domestic product (GDP) and improve living standards.
Speaking at a session titled “Where Reforms Matter the Most for Growth?” at the Sustainable Development Policy Institute's (SDPI) 29th Sustainable Development Conference, organised by the Ministry of Finance, the IMF's Pakistan representative, Dr Mahir Binici, praised the country’s efforts to maintain economic stability amid recent global and domestic challenges, but stressed the need for deeper and broader reforms to put the economy on a sustainable growth path.
He said Pakistan had reached a critical juncture where the narrative needed to change, with discussions moving beyond taxation to focus on how reforms could translate into investment, economic activity, exports, employment and improved living standards.
Where Reforms Matter the Most for Growth? https://t.co/lAB92QuI8j
— SDPI (@SDPIPakistan) November 5, 2026
“I think Pakistan has already done the hard work and, from this point forward, it is really about how to cement that stabilisation and where we are right now, and move towards a direction where we have more investment, activity and better jobs,” he said.
Binici outlined five key areas that could help improve the country's growth prospects, including preserving macroeconomic stability and strengthening the foundations needed to transform the economy from stabilisation to sustainable growth.
He said fiscal and external sustainability, along with adequate buffers, were essential to maintaining a strong macroeconomic foundation.
Pakistan had demonstrated the importance of building buffers and maintaining stability in the face of recurring domestic and external shocks over the past two to three years, he said.
He cited the recent Middle East conflict, recurring climate-related shocks and heightened global uncertainty stemming from trade, tariffs and geopolitics as challenges that underscored the need to maintain economic resilience.
“Right now, we have seen that stability has been maintained given the most significant shock that is due to the war in the Middle East and recurring climate-related shocks, and extremely high global uncertainty, whether it is driven by trade, tariffs or geopolitics,” he said.
Binici also stressed the need to maintain fiscal discipline and increase revenue collection as a share of GDP, particularly through taxation.
“Our fund's research has shown that countries like emerging developing economies like Pakistan need, at least, as a threshold, somewhere around 15 per cent of GDP in revenue so that they can actually have a strong, well-functioning state and capacity that can provide services and enable better living standards,” he said, adding that Pakistan was still far from that level.
He said fiscal discipline needed to be supported by price stability and continued efforts to build buffers.
The IMF representative identified governance, the national tariff policy and the cost of doing business as key areas where Pakistan needed to secure a significant growth dividend. He said these were also central to the reform programme, particularly in the areas of energy and governance.
Binici said governance should be treated as an economic policy, commending the authorities for completing the Governance and Corruption Diagnostic and preparing an economic governance reform plan.
While describing the country's performance over the past two to three years as a strong achievement given the challenging global and domestic environment, he said considerable work remained to place Pakistan on a stable and sustainable footing.
He called for a growth-friendly fiscal system, saying there was broad stakeholder understanding of the need for a broader, more predictable tax regime.
“We need a broader, simpler, fairer and more predictable taxation system. That would also enable increasing revenue, not only for the sake of increasing revenue but also generating the resources that the country needs, whether for human capital, infrastructure or investment,” he said.
Such resources would ultimately help increase potential GDP and improve people's living standards, he added.
On human capital development, Binici said investment in people was a critical element of growth-oriented reforms. He noted gradual progress in this area, particularly in health and education spending as a share of GDP.
He said spending on health and education had increased from around two per cent of GDP over the past two to three years, and he intended to raise it to between 2.8-3 per cent in the current fiscal year.
“It is still, I think, far below our peers and what Pakistan needs, but there has been some gradual progress,” he said.
Binici said restoring economic stability, maintaining it, rebuilding confidence and strengthening buffers constituted a significant achievement given the challenging circumstances.
He called for deeper, broader reforms, with proper sequencing and targeting, to place the economy on a stronger, more sustainable growth trajectory.
The IMF has repeatedly raised concerns over Pakistan’s taxation system and the slow implementation of structural reforms, particularly those aimed at improving the governance of state-owned enterprises, reducing market interventions and enhancing transparency in public finances.
The Fund has also flagged significant statistical discrepancies in the federal budget, raising questions about the transparency and accuracy of government accounts.
Most recently, IMF Regional Director Jihad Azour highlighted weaknesses in the country's tax system and called for a fairer and more neutral taxation structure to improve compliance and encourage business expansion.
“A fairer tax system can encourage compliance, better services can strengthen trust, and a more neutral tax structure can allow productive firms to expand rather than remain small or informal,” Azour had said during the first day of a two-day conference on the tax system last month.
Read: IMF pushes targeted subsidies
He identified broadening the tax base, strengthening revenue administration, reducing tax expenditures, protecting priority spending and improving public service delivery as key priorities for Pakistan.
However, the implementation of tax reforms under the IMF programme has remained uneven, with influential sectors, including retail, agriculture and real estate, making limited contributions to the national exchequer during the first two years of the programme.
The Fund agreed in June this year to reduce withholding tax rates for the real estate sector. It also endorsed a tax scheme for traders that allows cash transactions, a provision that critics say could encourage informality.
As of October 15, only 137 new retailers had joined the scheme against an annual target of one million.
The Fund's concerns extend beyond taxation. During discussions with Pakistani authorities in September, it flagged delays in state-owned enterprises' reforms, continued market interventions and a lack of budget transparency.
Azour has stressed that stabilisation alone is insufficient. Pakistan needs reforms to raise productivity, improve competitiveness and attract private investment. He also said transparent rules and the absence of preferential treatment were essential to encouraging tax compliance.
The limited contributions from influential sectors and continued reliance on cash-based transactions under the traders' scheme have raised questions about the government's progress towards the fairer tax system advocated by the IMF.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Benjamin Netanyahu's position ​in the post-election battle to stay on as Israel's prime minister weakened on Thursday after an ultra-Orthodox Jewish party withheld support for ‌any nominee and two Arab-led parties endorsed his main opponent.
Israel's president Isaac Herzog was due to meet Netanyahu and his chief political rival Gadi Eisenkot to decide which of the two men to pick to form a government, after holding talks with smaller parties. He has until November 11 to decide.
Israel's October 27 election ended in deadlock with neither Netanyahu nor Eisenkot, a ​former military chief, securing a clear path to a majority in parliament.
That has set up a tough task for President Isaac Herzog, whose mostly ​ceremonial role comes with the post-election responsibility of picking a candidate he believes has the best chance to break the ⁠deadlock in a deeply divided country.
Netanyahu remains prime minister in a caretaker government until a new coalition is formed, or through another election, which must be ​held if no candidate succeeds.
Though Netanyahu outperformed expectations in the vote and his own Likud Party won the most seats, his nationalist-religious coalition lost its governing majority.
In ​a setback for the prime minister on Thursday, United Torah Judaism, one of two major parties representing ultra-Orthodox Jewish voters and a longstanding Netanyahu coalition ally, declined to recommend any candidate to form a government.
And while Eisenkot, like Netanyahu, has so far ruled out forming a government with Israel's two Arab-led parties, both factions endorsed Eisenkot on Thursday, giving him backing ​from a comfortable majority of lawmakers.
'Remember the issues tearing us apart from within'
Herzog will meet separately with Netanyahu's and Eisenkot's factions at his residence in Jerusalem ​on Thursday night, wrapping up party meetings he started on Wednesday after the announcement of official election results.
Herzog has called on parties to do their utmost to avert another ‌round of ⁠elections.
"Any reasonable person need only look at the security and diplomatic challenges before us, at the changing region around us, and remember the issues tearing us apart from within, to understand that an immense responsibility rests upon us," Herzog said.
'Daddy' was a paramedic. He was killed in March in an Israeli strike on their home in Tebnin, southern Lebanon.
He met with smaller factions on Wednesday and plans more meetings with parties in ascending order by size, culminating with Eisenkot's Yashar and Netanyahu's Likud.
Likud won the most seats of any single party with 27 in the 120-seat Knesset, but Netanyahu's wider ​religious-nationalist coalition garnered only 53 in total.
Read More: Israel faces political deadlock as US support wavers
That ​was still better than Eisenkot's ⁠anti-Netanyahu coalition spanning four centre-left to right-wing Jewish-led parties, which won just 48 seats despite pre-election polls pointing to a close race. Two parties representing Israel's Arab minority won an unprecedented 19 seats.
Critics accuse Netanyahu of trying to undermine election results
Netanyahu, ​at risk of losing power, has seized on an investigation by election officials into possible vote tampering to cast ​doubt on the results, ⁠accusing Arab-led parties of stealing the vote. Critics accuse Netanyahu and his partners of trying to undermine the results, which he denies.
Israel's Central Election Committee said on Wednesday that the election's integrity had not been compromised. The head of the committee, Supreme Court Justice Noam Sohlberg, has called on Israel's elected officials to protect public trust, ⁠rather than ​shake it.
"This is a real danger. One of the foundations of democracy is the peaceful transfer ​of power," Sohlberg told Herzog at his residence on Wednesday. High voter turnout, including among the Arab minority, was a blessing, he said.
Netanyahu's allies on the far-right, including National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir, ​have called for the immediate arrest and interrogation of Arab party leaders.

items.author: Life And Style Desk
items.content:
“When I read it, I found it interesting. What intrigued me the most was that it was a true story,” says actor Talha Chahour, explaining what drew him to his latest drama, Rutba.
In an interview with Something Haute, the actor opened up about the real-life events behind the drama, revealing that its story and characters were inspired by actual people and circumstances. It was this connection with reality that made the project particularly compelling for him.
“When I got offered this, I was very excited,” he recalled, adding that his interest grew further after reading the script and learning about the people whose experiences had informed the narrative. “The characters are also a real part of the story. Then I read about those people and their lives, and then I made my character,” he said.
However, Chahour was careful to distinguish between the real individuals and their fictional portrayals. “It is better that we don't talk about the real people, but if we can discuss the character, it is not just about his story as an ASP,” he explained.
The actor revealed that he conducted his own research to understand the character, uncovering several accounts about his background in the process. “When I read about him, a lot of stories came to light,” he said.
At the centre of Rutba is ASP Hadi, a young, educated man who enters the police force with a sense of purpose but gradually finds himself confronted by the system's darker realities.
For Chahour, Hadi's journey is not simply about an officer navigating his professional responsibilities. It explores what happens when someone raised with strong values enters an environment where power, politics, moral corruption and money begin to challenge everything he believes in.
“ASP Hadi was not just an ASP; it was about a young, educated man and officer who comes into the system and how the system breaks him apart,” he said.
Explaining the central conflict, Chahour said Hadi's pursuit of justice exposes him to power politics, moral compromises and financial interests, all of which threaten to derail his path.
He also reflected on the vulnerability of people who come from hardworking backgrounds and find themselves in unfamiliar environments. “People like him, with his background and upbringing, are known as hard workers, but when they go from one setting to another, it is sad to say that they fall apart,” he said.
The drama's title, Rutba, which refers to dignity, honour or status, also carries a deeper significance for the actor. He believes attaining a position of authority is one thing, but understanding the responsibility that comes with it presents an entirely different challenge.
“It is easy to control it, but taking responsibility is important,” Chahour remarked, pointing to how people can become consumed by the privileges attached to their positions without recognising the difference they could make through their authority.
He also highlighted the moral accountability that comes with power, suggesting that people must eventually answer for how they have used the positions entrusted to them. For him, Hadi represents an individual whose integrity is constantly put to the test. “Hadi is a very challenging character because he represents the ultimate test of human integrity,” he said.
Yet, Hadi is not presented as an uncomplicated hero.
Chahour offered a glimpse into the character's personal and emotional struggles, explaining that his upbringing and the sacrifices made by his family are important to understanding his journey. “What his family sacrificed for him and his studies, you can see that he has been through trauma and worries,” he said.
The actor also hinted at the challenges that emerge when a young man, previously sheltered by his upbringing and circumstances, is exposed to an unfamiliar social environment.
Recalling Hadi's interest in teaching and his education in a co-educational setting, Chahour explained how the character's transition into a different world brings experiences that test his judgement and personal relationships. “I feel that when a good man is exposed to a bad world with bad people, it does not always mean that he is weak, but it means that we see him struggle,” he said.
Rather than portraying Hadi as someone who always makes the right decisions, the drama allows audiences to see his vulnerabilities and mistakes. “Hadi's journey will show a real human being who stumbles,” Chahour said.
Addressing Hadi's questionable decisions, particularly in his relationship with Mahnoor, the actor was careful not to defend the character's actions.
“I cannot justify his actions. They are wrong. If you have been in a relationship for eight years, how can you do wrong?” he said, adding that he viewed Hadi as a character separate from the conventional idea of a hero. “He is doing wrong. Let's see what happens ahead,” he added.
Chahour's comments suggest that Rutba seeks to explore not only institutional corruption but also the personal compromises and moral failures that can emerge when individuals are confronted with temptation and power.
The interview also touched on his experience working with Hiba Bukhari, who plays Mahnoor. Marking their first collaboration, the drama brought the two actors together on a set that Chahour described as particularly welcoming.
He credited the production's collaborative environment and strong leadership for helping the cast develop an easy working relationship and convincing on-screen chemistry.
“When your set has such a good environment, you can make a good project and bond together well. You can create good chemistry, which the audience can see, and the stories look real,” he said.
Music also became another point of connection among the cast members.
Referring to his singing in the drama, including the song Alfaaz, Chahour said viewers had particularly enjoyed the music selection. “Even Hiba sings in the drama. We selected these songs, and credit goes to Haseeb bhai. People really enjoyed the selection of the songs,” he said.
Beyond the drama, Chahour shared his thoughts on the importance of constructive criticism within the television industry.
He believes reviews that engage with a production's story, themes and performances can help actors and creators improve, regardless of whether the feedback is positive or negative. “We get to learn from those critiques. That is a learning process,” he said.
While acknowledging the importance of review culture, he distinguished between thoughtful criticism and reviews that simply seek attention. “The review culture is important for our industry and should exist, but I also believe that you should not take it to heart but to your head,” he remarked.
The actor also discussed the physical transformation he underwent for Hadi, explaining that his approach to acting extended beyond delivering dialogue and performing scenes.
For the role, he adopted a wardrobe of shalwar kameez and coats while making changes to his physical appearance. Chahour revealed that he weighed 65 kilograms during his previous drama, Jama Taqseem, before gaining eight kilograms for Hadi, bringing his weight to 73 kilograms.
He also grew a real moustache for the character rather than relying on an artificial addition.
“I believe in transformation, not just acting,” he said, expressing disappointment that character-driven transformations did not always receive enough attention during the design process.
For Chahour, an actor's appearance should reflect the requirements of a role rather than simply prioritising looking attractive on screen. “I don't work to look good, but to look real,” he said.
Reflecting on his theatre experience, the actor explained that it had taught him to prioritise authenticity over conventional ideas of beauty. He believes performers must be willing to look different, even less conventionally attractive, if that is what a character demands.
This emphasis on transformation reflects Chahour's theatrical background, where he developed an approach centred on inhabiting a role rather than merely performing it. The actor has steadily built his television career through projects including Jo Bichar Gaye, in which he portrayed Captain Farrukh, Wabaal, Jannat Se Aagay and Mannat Murad.
With his latest performance, Chahour takes on a character whose journey is rooted in real-life inspiration but whose struggles raise wider questions about integrity, authority and accountability. As he puts it, attaining rutba may be relatively easy; living up to the responsibility that comes with it is the real test.

items.author: Gaurav Bagur
items.content:
Cosmoserve Space has raised $6 Mn in a seed funding round led by Japan-based Rebright Partners. While Aranya Holdings and Naandi Ventures also participated in the round, existing investors AUM Ventures and Shakti VC doubled down on their erstwhile bet.
The startup shared plans to utilise the fresh capital to support tech demonstrations, fuel two upcoming missions, as well enhance the operations of its recently unveiled Hyderabad facility.
Cosmoserve has now raised over $9 Mn since inception last year. The startup has doubled its valuation since it raised pre-seed funding in September, founder Chiranjeevi Phanindra told Inc42. The exact valuation is yet to be discerned.
For context, the startup is building tech to remove defunct satellites and orbital debris from space and reduce the collision risks for operational spacecraft in a cost effective manner.
It plans on optimising costs by setting up features within its craft that will allow it to refuel in-orbit and remove multiple pieces of debris in a single mission.
The startup made its first tech demonstration, Mission Embrace-1, aboard Skyroot Aerospace’s Vikram-1 rocket. The mission was designed to test the startup’s soft robotic capture system that removes space debris, but the system’s robotic petals failed to deploy as intended.
Cosmoserve claims to have now identified and addressed potential issues with the thermal mechanism used to release the petals and the impact of low temperatures on the system, according to Phanindra.
The startup is now gearing up for Embrace-2, an upgraded version of the mission to validate its upgraded robotic capture mechanism, which is expected to launch in the coming months. It is also planning a full-scale demonstration of its debris-removal capabilities, aiming to break a world record by approaching within 10 m of a dead satellite.
Phanindra, who served close to 15 years with the ISRO before setting up Cosmoserve in June 2025, believes that the startup would be able to complete all tech demos by 2027 and start commercial operations by 2028.
“We have several letters of intent from satellite constellation operators – one from the US, one from Europe and two from India. They have to abide by the regulation for removing the dead satellite from space … so we are aiming to get one paid customer before actual commercial operations begin,” he added.
Cosmoserve’s Base 1
Alongside the funding announcement, Cosmoserve inaugurated its new space debris removal facility in Hyderabad named Base 1 today, in an event attended by union minister of state Dr Jitendra Singh and Telangana IT Minister D Sridhar Babu.
Phanindra says that Base 1 is India’s first private and the world’s sixth facility equipped with space vision effects and microgravity simulation.
In simpler terms, Base 1 can recreate conditions that spacecraft and equipment encounter in space, allowing companies to test how their tech will perform before an actual mission. This includes simulating how objects behave in microgravity (near-weightlessness) and how they appear or function under space-like visual conditions.
This costs around ₹6 Cr to construct, per Phanindra.
Base 1 houses infrastructure for designing, building and testing satellite servicing and space debris recovery missions. This includes an orbital rendezvous and capture lab, an ISO Class 8 clean room for satellite integration, a mission control centre and a microgravity simulation platform.
The facility will also support the development of in-orbit satellite repair and refuelling technologies.
Besides, the startup plans to use Base 1 to develop more critical technologies in-house in order to increase its share of local manufacturing from 60% and reduce dependence on imported components such as optics, avionics and space-grade electronics.
“Primarily, the core technology we are building is a soft robotic capture system. We have a space robotics innovation lab where the R&D is happening. Then the next technology we are working on is a vision-based navigation system,” the founder told Inc42.

items.author: Press Release
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Implemented by the Pi Space Science Education Centre (PSSEC), in partnership with the World Robot Olympiad (WRO) Association and powered by Aramco, the Pakistan Innovation Quest (PIQ) is expanding access to meaningful robotics and STEM learning across Pakistan. PIQ is a national initiative breaking down barriers to robotics education for young people historically excluded by cost, geography, gender, or disability.
The initiative aims to reach 10,000 learners and 300 teachers through more than 60 RoboStarter Sprints, six regional competitions and a National Showcase. PIQ creates a clear pathway for students: from encountering robotics for the first time, to developing original solutions for real-world challenges, to competing regionally, and progressing toward the World Robot Olympiad Pakistan platform.
Aramco’s partnership has enabled PIQ to deliver free training across public and private schools, low-income communities, NGO-supported institutions, and girls’ schools.
PIQ is also proving that meaningful STEM inclusion must encompass ability. At Deaf Reach School, deaf students engaged in hands-on robotics training, supported by interpreters and trainers fluent in sign language. For many, it was their first opportunity to work with a robotics kit—not as observers, but as builders, problem-solvers, and innovators.
“Talent is universal. Access is not—and that is the divide Pakistan Innovation Quest was created to close,” said Zartaj Ahmed, CEO and Co-Founder of PSSEC and National Organizer of WRO Pakistan. “With Aramco enabling this initiative, we are reaching the child who has never held a robotics kit, the girl who has never imagined herself as an engineer, and the deaf learner who deserves to innovate without barriers.”
PIQ’s RoboStarter Sprints combine practical robotics training with the WRO Future Innovators project cycle. Students work toward WRO certification, while teachers receive professional development to sustain robotics learning within their institutions long after the training ends.
The movement has already trained more than 6,000 learners and 518 teachers, reaching Karachi, Lahore, Hyderabad, Gujranwala, and Kasur. Around 60 institutions have joined the network. PIQ is targeting more than 40 percent female participation and plans to donate 100 robotics kits to underserved institutions to support continued learning beyond the initiative.
Hussain N. Hanbazazah, Aramco Vice President of Communications Operations & Corporate Citizenship, said: “At Aramco, we see STEM education as an investment in the innovators, problem-solvers, and leaders of tomorrow. Through our Global STEM Education Program, we aim to expand access to meaningful learning opportunities and reach young people globally. Our collaboration with PSSEC and the World Robot Olympiad brings 10,000 robotics opportunities to students across Pakistan. By investing in both students and teachers, we are turning curiosity into capability and creating a lasting impact that extends beyond student participation.”
Regional winners will advance to the PIQ National Showcase, where students and teachers will present their solutions to school leaders, government representatives, STEM partners, and international stakeholders. The strongest participants will secure pathways to future WRO Pakistan competitions.
With Aramco helping turn that principle into action, PIQ is enabling young Pakistanis to see themselves not simply as users of tomorrow’s technology, but as its creators.

items.title: Walee Financial Services recognised at Pakistan Women’s Empowerment Principles (WEPs) Awards
items.summary:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Walee Financial Services (WFS), a pioneer in ethical and inclusive digital finance in Pakistan, has been recognised among the leading organisations in the Gender-Responsive Marketplace category at the Pakistan Women’s Empowerment Principles (WEPs) Awards, hosted by UN Women Pakistan.
The recognition celebrates WFS’s flagship women-focused asset-financing program, Khudmukhtar Khatoon (“Independent Woman”). Delivered in partnership with Karandaaz Pakistan through WFS’s Shariah-compliant digital financing platform, Hakeem, the program breaks down systemic barriers to capital for micro and small enterprise (MSE) owners across Pakistan.
By providing women entrepreneurs with direct access to productive equipment and ethical financing without requiring a male guarantor, Khudmukhtar Khatoon enables female enterprise owners to scale operations, build sustainable livelihoods, and gain long-term economic independence.

items.author: Staff
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Walee Financial Services (WFS), a pioneer in ethical and inclusive digital finance in Pakistan, has been recognised among the leading organisations in the Gender-Responsive Marketplace category at the Pakistan Women’s Empowerment Principles (WEPs) Awards, hosted by UN Women Pakistan.
The recognition celebrates WFS’s flagship women-focused asset-financing program, Khudmukhtar Khatoon (“Independent Woman”). Delivered in partnership with Karandaaz Pakistan through WFS’s Shariah-compliant digital financing platform, Hakeem, the program breaks down systemic barriers to capital for micro and small enterprise (MSE) owners across Pakistan.
By providing women entrepreneurs with direct access to productive equipment and ethical financing without requiring a male guarantor, Khudmukhtar Khatoon enables female enterprise owners to scale operations, build sustainable livelihoods, and gain long-term economic independence.
The UN Women WEPs Awards—established jointly by UN Women and the UN Global Compact—honor organizations that take measurable, actionable steps toward advancing gender equality across the workplace, marketplace, and broader community.
Noshad Minhas, CEO & Co-Founder of Walee Financial Services, commented:
“This recognition by UN Women is a powerful testament to the resilience of Pakistan’s women micro-entrepreneurs. Through Khudmukhtar Khatoon and our Hakeem platform, we set out to prove that financial inclusion isn’t about saddling home-based businesses with debt traps— it’s about providing the actual tools, machines, and dignified Shariah-compliant capital they need to become self-reliant. We share this honor with our partners at Karandaaz Pakistan and every woman turning her skill into an enterprise.”
The award was formally presented at the Pakistan WEPs Awards Ceremony on November 3, 2026, in Karachi, convened alongside leaders from business, civil society, and international development committed to building an inclusive economy.
For Walee Financial Services, this recognition marks a significant milestone in its mission to bridge the gender gap in Pakistan’s financial sector. WFS remains committed to leveraging digital Islamic fintech solutions to ensure that every woman’s entrepreneurial ambition is met with the capital, trust, and resources needed to succeed.

items.author: Usama Anjum
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) has carried out a high-level field inspection of mobile networks across Islamabad and Rawalpindi, with Chairman Major General (R) Hafeez Ur Rehman personally testing call quality and mobile internet services in different areas of the twin cities.
The inspection follows reports earlier this week that cellular mobile operators had reportedly taken steps to improve network performance ahead of the regulator’s planned visit.
The latest development confirms that the inspection has now taken place, with senior PTA officials assessing the actual quality of 4G coverage, voice calls, and mobile data services being provided to consumers.
According to details of the exercise, the PTA Chairman was accompanied by authority members, director generals, senior officials, and representatives of mobile operators, including Jazz, Zong, and Ufone. Representatives from the Ministry of Information Technology also participated.
https://www.phoneworld.com.pk/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/WhatsApp-Video-2026-11-05-at-2.11.27-PM.mp4
Three special teams were dispatched to different locations across Islamabad and Rawalpindi to conduct on-ground assessments of cellular network performance.
The first team inspected mobile services around Islamabad International Airport, Srinagar Highway and adjoining areas.
The second team examined network performance along Islamabad Expressway towards Rawat T-Chowk, while the third covered Murree Road, Rawal Road and the Old Airport area.
During the visits, officials tested mobile voice quality, call connectivity, the ability to maintain calls without interruption, and mobile internet speeds.
The PTA Chairman also personally made mobile calls and checked internet connectivity to assess the services available to ordinary users.
PTA Identifies Service Quality Issues Despite Mostly Satisfactory Initial Results
According to the initial findings, mobile voice and data services were generally satisfactory across most of the inspected locations.
However, the teams also identified shortcomings in call quality and mobile internet performance in certain areas.
The PTA chairman issued instructions to representatives of the relevant mobile operators on the spot, directing them to address the identified deficiencies and improve the quality of services.
The inspection is particularly significant because it follows an earlier field visit by the PTA’s Director General (Enforcement) to Islamabad and Rawalpindi last week.
PhoneWorld previously reported that telecom operators were allegedly improving network conditions in areas expected to be covered by the high-level inspection.
The latest exercise has now provided the regulator with an opportunity to directly examine network performance rather than relying solely on operator-submitted service quality data.
However, the initial findings do not establish whether the generally satisfactory performance observed during the inspection reflects sustained network improvements or conditions specific to the day of testing.
The authority has also not released detailed operator-wise performance results, measured internet speeds, or a complete list of locations where service deficiencies were identified.
The inspection underscores PTA’s increased focus on monitoring telecom services at the field level, particularly as consumers continue to raise concerns about inconsistent 4G coverage, dropped calls, and slow mobile internet.
For now, the key question is whether the instructions issued during the exercise will translate into consistent improvements for mobile users across Islamabad and Rawalpindi.

items.title: Apple Charges More Than Three Times Its Cost for iPhone 18 Pro Storage Upgrade: Report
items.summary: Apple is charging more than three times its cost for the iPhone 18 Pro storage upgrade, according to a report. According to the report, the 1TB storage upgrade used to cost Apple $42 (roughly Rs. 4,000) for the iPhone 17 Pro, which has now gone up to $192 (about Rs. 18,000) for the iPhone 18 Pro. With the costs, the company has also increased its gross profit from $358 (roughly Rs. 34,000) to $408 (about Rs. 39,000). For the lower-end 512GB storage upgrade, Apple used to pay its suppliers $15 (roughly Rs. 1,400), while charging $200 (about Rs. 19,000) to iPhone 17 Pro customers. This cost has also ballooned to $66 (about Rs. 6,000), shrinking its gross profit on the iPhone 18 Pro.

items.author: Tom Jackson
items.content:
The United Kingdom (UK) has emerged as a key international base for African tech companies, offering a mix of incorporation, operations and regulatory licensing that sets it apart from other global markets, according to a new report.
TLP Advisory, a cross-border venture law practice with its origins in Nigeria, has released its third annual report, Home and Away: Tracking African Tech’s Global Footprint, which examined 100 tech companies across Nigeria, Kenya, South Africa, Egypt, Ghana and Morocco, and their affiliations with the UK, US and UAE.
It found the US is largely associated with financing-linked incorporation, while the UAE serves as an operational base with access to the wider Middle East. The UK combines both, alongside a broader commercial presence.
Of the companies with UK affiliations, 84 per cent are incorporated there, 47 per cent have an operational presence, and 19 per cent hold regulatory licences. Just three per cent of US-affiliated companies and four per cent of UAE-affiliated companies hold licences in those markets.
“A round closed in Delaware and a licence in London are both important but they play very distinct roles,” said Odunoluwa Longe, co-founder and partner at TLP Advisory. “Our recommendation to founders is to be deliberate about what they want to achieve in each market.”
The UAE is the most operationally focused of the three markets, with 87 per cent of UAE-connected companies running operations there. Its regional pull is strongest among Egyptian startups, 70 per cent of which have a UAE affiliation, compared with 50 per cent for the US.
For fintechs in particular, the UK offers an established market and a large African diaspora. The report also highlights the SEIS and EIS investor tax relief schemes, the Global Entrepreneur Programme, English common law, and access to public markets through the London Stock Exchange and AIM as key draws.
“The UK didn’t feel foreign to us,” said Alex Forsyth-Thompson, founder and CEO of South African fintech Float. “There are a lot of South Africans here, so we had social capital from day one.”
The full report can be downloaded for free here.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Apple and Samsung have increased their shares of the global smartphone chipset market despite a major decline in overall shipments. According to a new report by Counterpoint Research, the two companies were the only major smartphone chip suppliers to record market share growth in the third quarter of 2026.
The global smartphone System-on-Chip (SoC) market experienced a 21% year-over-year decline during the quarter. Rising memory prices and weaker smartphone demand have affected the industry, forcing manufacturers to focus more on profitability.
Apple and Samsung Gain Smartphone Chip Market Shares as Global Shipments Drop 21%
Apple maintained its third position in the global smartphone chipset market, but its share increased from 17% in the third quarter of 2025 to 21% in Q3 2026.
Samsung also recorded growth, increasing its market share from 6% to 8% during the same period. This made Apple and Samsung the only major chipset vendors to improve their positions among the leading manufacturers.
Apple’s performance reflects the strength of its iPhone business, as the company has managed to handle rising component costs better than several competitors.
MediaTek and Qualcomm Lead the Market
Despite losing some market share, MediaTek continued to lead the global smartphone SoC market with a 28% share in Q3 2026. However, its share declined by six percentage points compared to the same quarter last year.
Qualcomm secured second place with a 22% market share, down from 25% a year earlier.
Apple ranked third with 21%, followed by UNISOC with 13%, compared to its previous share of 14%. Samsung remained in fifth place with 8%, up from 6% in Q3 2025.
Other chipset manufacturers collectively increased their share from 4% to 8%.
Rising Memory Prices Affect Smartphone Chip Demand
The decline in chipset shipments comes as smartphone manufacturers face higher memory costs and weaker consumer demand.
Several smartphone brands have increased device prices during 2026 to manage rising component expenses. Apple, however, delayed its iPhone price increases until September, when it introduced the iPhone 18 Pro series.
According to Counterpoint Research, global smartphone chip shipments could decline by 20% in 2026. The research firm also expects another 3% to 4% drop in 2027, with memory prices likely to remain under pressure.
New Flagship Chipsets Could Support Market Recovery
Despite the overall slowdown, new flagship processors launched in September could help improve premium smartphone chipset shipments during the final quarter of 2026.
Counterpoint Research Senior Analyst Shivani Parashar highlighted three major launches based on TSMC’s 2nm manufacturing process: Apple’s A20 series, MediaTek’s Dimensity 9600 Pro, and Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 series.
These new processors are expected to support demand for premium smartphones in Q4 2026. However, shipment volumes are still projected to remain below the levels recorded in the same quarter of 2025.
Apple has also warned that rising memory costs could affect its profitability in the coming quarters. The company described the current memory pricing situation as unprecedented and expects higher component expenses to put further pressure on its profit margins.
Overall, the latest figures show that Apple and Samsung are gaining ground in a shrinking smartphone chipset market, while leading suppliers MediaTek and Qualcomm face declining market shares.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Thatta Cement is preparing to enter Pakistan’s electric vehicle (EV) market through a wholly owned subsidiary, with plans to initially import electric vehicles from China. The company aims to target the mass-market segment by introducing affordable and compact electric cars for local consumers.
The development was disclosed in a notice submitted to the Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) on Thursday, November 5, 2026. According to the company, its Board of Directors has approved an investment to establish a wholly owned subsidiary for the new business.
The subsidiary will initially focus on importing completely built-up (CBU) electric vehicles from China. Under this arrangement, vehicles will arrive in Pakistan in fully assembled form rather than being manufactured or assembled locally.
Thatta Cement Targets Affordable Electric Vehicles
Unlike several companies focusing on premium electric cars, Thatta Cement plans to enter the relatively underserved mass-market segment.
The company intends to introduce affordable, compact, and small electric vehicles designed for consumers looking for economical transportation options. Its strategy will focus on vehicles that match the purchasing power and mobility requirements of a wider section of Pakistan’s population.
Thatta Cement believes this segment offers an opportunity to establish an early presence in the country’s developing electric vehicle industry.
Local Assembly Could Follow in the Future
Although the subsidiary will initially import fully assembled electric vehicles from China, the company has indicated that it may expand its operations in the future.
Its longer-term plans could include local vehicle assembly and other related business activities. However, Thatta Cement has not shared a specific timeline for these plans.
The company has also not disclosed the investment amount allocated to its entry into the electric vehicle business.
Pakistan’s EV Market Attracts More Companies
Pakistan’s electric vehicle market is gradually attracting interest from local and international manufacturers. Rising fuel prices, environmental concerns, and government incentives and tax concessions are encouraging consumers and businesses to explore electric mobility.
However, the industry still faces several challenges, including limited charging infrastructure and the need for consistent government support to develop a sustainable EV ecosystem.
Thatta Cement’s planned entry could add another player to the country’s growing electric vehicle market, particularly in the affordable segment.
The company’s initial focus on Chinese imports will allow it to enter the market before potentially exploring local assembly and other related activities.

items.author: Shrishti Bisht
items.content:
Multi-family office and wealth management group Daksham Capital has launched its maiden consumer-focused fund, Daksham Growth Ventures (DGV) Fund I, with a target corpus of ₹150 Cr and a ₹150 Cr greenshoe option.
The fund has secured around ₹125 Cr in its first close, following its registration as a SEBI Category II AIF last month.
Family offices, high-net-worth individuals (HNIs), ultra-high-net-worth individuals (UHNIs), and entrepreneurs participated in the first close. The fund will continue raising capital towards its target, including the greenshoe option.
Led by cofounder and managing partner Shivam Diwan, DGV plans to invest in 10-15 startups, with cheques ranging from ₹5 Cr to ₹20 Cr. It will primarily back Pre-Series A and Series A startups, while considering select later-stage investments.
Its investment mandate spans D2C brands, consumer enablers, B2B2C platforms, supply-chain businesses, and startups using AI in consumer services.
Betting On Capital Efficiency
DGV will focus on businesses with established product-market fit rather than those still testing demand, Diwan told Inc42.
“We will only come where the product-market-fit risk is established,” he said.
The fund will typically evaluate startups with annual recurring revenue (ARR) of ₹25-75 Cr, assessing their unit economics, addressable market, founders’ execution capabilities, and differentiation. It is targeting businesses with the potential to scale annual revenue to ₹300-500 Cr.
Startups need not be profitable when DGV invests, but the fund expects them to have positive or neutral contribution margins, even if they remain loss-making at the EBITDA level.
“Growth by burning an enormous amount of money is not the mantra. It should be a capital-efficient business,” Diwan said.
Beyond capital, DGV plans to help portfolio startups with corporate governance, financial reporting, brand positioning, leadership development, and distribution expansion. It also intends to provide board-level guidance and access to its industry network.
The fund will evaluate businesses across food and beverages, apparel, snacking, beauty and personal care, accessories, jewellery, and bags.
Direct consumer businesses are expected to account for 50-70% of its investments. The remainder will go towards consumer enablers, including contract manufacturers, sourcing and supply chain companies, and B2B2C platforms.
DGV is also open to businesses outside the traditional consumer sector, provided their growth is linked to consumer demand.
Diwan said the fund is evaluating startups across food and beverages, accessories, and B2B2C segments, including a few D2C brands. It is yet to make an investment.
DGV will also consider a small number of late-stage investments in startups that could go public within two to three years. These deals are likely to comprise largely secondary transactions, Diwan said.
Bullish On Consumer AI And Enablers
DGV expects AI to play a growing role in consumer businesses over the next decade, particularly in product discovery, personalisation, customer acquisition, and fulfilment.
While it does not intend to invest directly in deeptech or standalone AI startups, the fund will evaluate consumer businesses using AI to improve customer engagement and operations.
Diwan expects consumer AI to gain momentum over the next 12-24 months, with startups increasingly integrating the technology into how consumers discover, evaluate, and purchase products.
The fund is also bullish on consumer enablers, particularly contract manufacturers and B2B businesses supplying multiple brands. Diwan said these businesses offer exposure to demand across several brands, reducing dependence on a single consumer-facing startup.
Daksham’s launch adds to the pool of dedicated capital targeting Indian consumer businesses. Earlier this year, Kairon Capital announced the ₹90 Cr first close of its maiden consumer-focused fund against a ₹150 Cr target and a ₹50 Cr greenshoe option.
Fireside Ventures closed its fourth fund at ₹2,265 Cr ($253 Mn) in December last year. The fund aims to invest in 30-35 early-stage consumer brands, with initial cheques of $1 Mn to $12 Mn, across categories including health and wellness, food and beverages, beauty and personal care, and lifestyle.

items.author: Anne Florentyna
items.content:
India’s cybersecurity watchdog CERT-In has issued a critical warning to entities in the banking, financial services and insurance (BFSI) sector over an escalating campaign of AI-driven cyberattacks targeting payment and disbursement APIs.
In an advisory dated November 4, 2026, the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) identified the threat actor behind the campaign as ‘CRAFTY FALCON’, describing it as an AI-assisted financial threat actor that uses machine intelligence to identify targets, execute attacks at machine speed and exploit victims’ own payment and disbursement APIs to initiate unauthorised fund transfers.
Banks, non-banking financial companies (NBFCs), fintech companies and other financial services entities have been warned of the growing threat.
CERT-In’s Computer Security Incident Response Team-Finance (CSIRT-Fin) said the campaign has witnessed a significant escalation, with successful attacks continuing to be reported across the financial services ecosystem. The agency has urged all BFSI entities to treat the campaign as an immediate and continuing threat.
Repeat Attacks Despite Remediation
A key concern highlighted in the advisory is the threat actor’s continued targeting of financial entities that had already received earlier restricted advisories and undertaken remediation measures.
According to CERT-In, some of these organisations have been deliberately targeted again, including cases where remediation was incomplete. The attacks have also been timed to coincide with holidays, weekends and other periods of reduced monitoring, potentially delaying detection and response.
CERT-In’s analysis identified the use of multiple publicly available AI-driven offensive security tools in the campaign. These include the ARTEX family of large language model (LLM)-based tools, PentAGI, an autonomous multi-agent AI penetration testing system, and the Cairn attack search engine, alongside the CyberStrikeAI framework.
These tools can execute complete attack chains autonomously, generate and refine large volumes of customised attack scripts in rapid succession, and adapt their payloads based on responses from targeted systems.
The supporting attack infrastructure also changes frequently, with IP addresses rotating within hours to days. CERT-In said infrastructure fingerprints and detailed detection rules have been shared with affected entities through restricted advisories.
AI Agents Pose Growing Cybersecurity Risks
The latest advisory follows another critical warning issued by CERT-In in October, when the agency flagged attackers using publicly available agentic AI tools to conduct financially motivated intrusions into Indian organisations.
The watchdog warned that autonomous AI agents, ostensibly deployed for research and evaluation, had accessed live systems without authorisation, reading business records containing personal data and confidential information.
Meanwhile, the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) has also warned banks, NBFCs and fintech startups about the growing use of AI agents by cybercriminals to perpetrate financial fraud.
The agency said it had uncovered multiple individual cases in which malicious agentic AI systems exploited compromised financial systems to execute unauthorised transactions involving amounts running into crores of rupees.
CERT-In Flags Vulnerabilities In Tata Motors’ Connected Vehicle Apps
Separately, CERT-In has flagged multiple vulnerabilities in select versions of Tata Motors’ iRA 2.0 and iRA.ev connected vehicle applications, which could allow attackers to access sensitive credentials and vehicle-related information.
The agency identified four vulnerabilities, including hardcoded service account credentials, API keys and authorisation tokens within the applications; inadequate validation of URLs and origins loaded through the apps’ WebView component; authentication tokens being recorded in application logs; and improper implementation of SSL certificate pinning in the network security configuration.
CERT-In has urged users to update their applications to the latest versions of iRA 2.0 (version 26.8.2) and iRA.ev (version 26.9.1).
The applications provide access to connected vehicle functionalities, including vehicle status updates, health monitoring, trip details and remote vehicle commands.

The Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) has dismissed social media reports of an alleged TikTok ban in Pakistan, saying the notification being shared online is fake.
In a statement issued on November 5, 2026, the telecom regulator said it had not issued any notification announcing a ban on the popular video-sharing platform. It described the circulating information as false and misleading.
PTA urged social media users not to believe or share unverified reports that could create confusion among the public.
PTA Advises Public to Verify Information
The authority has advised citizens to rely only on authentic sources for updates about telecommunications services and regulatory decisions.
According to PTA, the public should obtain verified information through its official website and authenticated social media accounts rather than relying on forwarded messages or unofficial posts.
The clarification comes after a notification claiming that TikTok would be banned in Pakistan started circulating on social media, raising questions among users about the platform’s availability.
See Also: PTA Registers BIGO LIVE and Likee Platforms in Pakistan
TikTok Ban Notification Has No Official Basis
PTA’s statement confirms that no official ban notification has been issued. Therefore, the viral claims should not be treated as an announcement of any regulatory action against TikTok.
The authority has reiterated the importance of checking the authenticity of online information before sharing it, particularly when it concerns major digital platforms and public services.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The government has launched the Prime Minister’s IT Certification Reimbursement Program to help Pakistani IT graduates and professionals obtain internationally recognised technology certifications. Under the initiative, eligible candidates can receive reimbursement of up to Rs. 70,000 after successfully completing an approved certification examination.
The Pakistan Software Export Board (PSEB), working under the Ministry of Information Technology and Telecommunication, is implementing the programme. It covers more than 50 approved certifications offered by leading international technology companies, including Amazon Web Services (AWS), Microsoft, and Google.
PM IT Certification Reimbursement Program: Eligibility, Benefits and Application Process
The initiative aims to improve the skills of Pakistan’s IT workforce and help professionals meet international industry standards. It is also expected to support the country’s freelance sector and increase software and IT exports.
Eligibility Criteria for the PM IT Certification Reimbursement Program
The programme is designed for IT graduates and professionals who want to improve their technical skills through internationally recognised certifications.
Applicants must select a certification from the programme’s approved list of more than 50 courses. These include certifications from AWS, Microsoft, Google, and other recognised technology providers.
Candidates must also submit their applications through the official portal before appearing in the certification examination. Passing the relevant examination and providing the required documents are necessary to qualify for reimbursement.
The available programme information does not specify additional requirements regarding age, minimum educational qualifications, employment status, or previous work experience. Applicants should check the official portal for detailed eligibility conditions before applying.
How to Apply for the IT Certification Reimbursement Program
Interested candidates can complete the application process online through the Skills Tech Destination portal. They need to follow these steps:
1. Create an Account
Visit skills.techdestination.com/register and create a new account by providing the required information. Candidates who already have an account can directly log in.
2. Select an Approved Certification
After registration, access the certification programme and choose the desired qualification from the approved list of more than 50 international IT certifications.
3. Submit an Application Before the Exam
Complete and submit the application through the portal before taking the certification examination. Prior approval through the application process is important, as candidates must apply before appearing in the exam.
4. Take and Pass the Certification Exam
After submitting the application, register for the relevant examination through the respective international certification provider. Candidates must successfully pass the examination to qualify for reimbursement.
5. Upload the Required Documents
After passing the examination, upload the following documents to the portal:
Official certification obtained after passing the examination.
Receipt showing payment of the certification examination fee.
6. Receive the Reimbursement
PSEB’s authorised team will review and verify the submitted documents. After successful verification, eligible candidates will receive reimbursement of up to Rs. 70,000 in their bank accounts.
How Much Reimbursement Will Candidates Receive?
Under the programme, eligible IT graduates and professionals can receive up to Rs. 70,000 in reimbursement for approved certification examination expenses.
The initiative covers more than 50 internationally recognised certifications, including those offered by AWS, Microsoft, and Google. The financial support is intended to reduce the cost of obtaining professional qualifications and encourage more candidates to pursue advanced technology skills.
How to Contact PSEB for Assistance
Candidates who face technical difficulties during registration or the application process can contact the programme’s support team through the following channels:
Email: support@pseb.org.pk
Helpline: 0800-01010
Registration Portal: skills.techdestination.com
PSEB Also Offers a Six-Month Apprenticeship Program
The Skills Tech Destination portal also provides information about PSEB’s Apprenticeship Program. Under this initiative, young professionals receive six-month placements in PSEB-registered companies.
The programme gives participants an opportunity to apply their academic knowledge to real-world projects, gain practical experience, and understand industry requirements.
Both initiatives aim to strengthen Pakistan’s IT workforce by improving professional skills, providing industry exposure, and preparing young people for opportunities in local and international technology markets.
