items.content:
By Ebunoluwa Sessou
As Nigeria prepares for another general election in 2027, the question of women’s participation in politics and access to elective offices remains a subject for debate.
Read Also: Elections: INEC struggles to get 14m PVCs to voters
Adeola Azeez, a daughter of the late Afenifere leader, Pa Ayo Adebanjo and one of the Founders of Women in Management, Business & Public Service, WIMBIZ, a founding member of Women in Politics (WIMPol) and a former Deputy Country Representative, Nigeria, of Deutsch e-Bank; was recently declared winner at the Ijebu Central Federal Consistency primary election on the platform of the Social Democratic Party (SDP) in Ogun State.
In this interview, she speaks on her experience contesting for the House of Representatives, the challenges of securing a party ticket, the influence of party structures on women’s political ambitions and her determination to contest again in 2027.
She also discusses the need for women who have secured elective positions to support aspiring female politicians and explains why she believes women must remain committed to political participation despite the barriers they face.
Excerpts:
You transitioned from the corporate world to politics after your retirement in 2020. What informed that decision?
 I have always believed in the importance of women’s participation in leadership. By the time I retired in 2020, I had prepared myself for a career in politics. From 2013, I knew that politics was something I wanted to pursue, so I began preparing for it.
I eventually contested for the House of Representatives in 2023 to represent Ogbomoso Central Federal Constituency. I approached the contest with the same seriousness, preparation and determination as any other candidate.
What were the major challenges you encountered as a woman contesting for political office?
The challenges women face in politics are well known. They include political violence, limited access to funding and other barriers.
Interestingly, funding was not a major challenge for me because of my corporate experience and the relationships I had built over the years. Having supported, mentored and nurtured women in business, I had established a strong network of sponsors and supporters. My reputation also helped me attract people who believed in my ambition.
However, the major challenge was the political structure itself. Nigeria’s political system is not structured to accommodate women adequately.
Despite your corporate experience, network and supporters, you did not secure your party’s ticket in 2023. What went wrong?
I believe the challenge was the party structure and the people who control access to political opportunities.
I had expected that my pedigree, experience and contributions to society would count for something. I did my research, reached out to my constituency and carried out the necessary groundwork.
I wanted to become a symbol of a new chapter for women in Nigerian politics. I believed that if more women with experience, credibility and the capacity to lead could successfully navigate the political system, it would encourage others to participate.
Unfortunately, I did not secure the ticket.
You have said that funding was not a major problem for you. Did you face pressure to engage in money politics?
I was determined not to engage in money politics or buy votes. I believed doing so would compromise my principles and disappoint the people who had supported me, including my family.
I wanted to run a campaign based on my record, ideas, engagement with the people and the support I had earned.
Although I had supporters and people who believed in my ambition, that was not enough to overcome the challenges within the party structure.
There was also the question of whether I would play politics in the same way as others. I believe women should be able to participate in politics without being expected to compromise their values to gain acceptance.
Do you think the political system discriminates against women who refuse to play by the established rules?
The political structure presents significant challenges for women. My experience made me realise that having the qualifications, resources, networks and willingness to serve does not automatically translate into securing a party ticket.
Women must navigate party structures and the interests of those who control them. This is one of the reasons we must continue to examine the barriers preventing women from participating fully in politics.
We need a system that recognises competence and allows women to compete meaningfully for elective positions.
What lessons did you learn from your 2023 electoral experience?
 I learnt that political participation requires persistence. I did not give up after 2023 and I remained committed to my constituency.
Although I did not secure the ticket, the experience gave me visibility. People in my constituency came to know me, my ambition and the kind of campaign I ran.
I believe political participation should not begin and end with winning an election. There is a responsibility to continue contributing to the development of the people, regardless of whether one occupies political office or not.
What are your plans for the 2027 general election?
I am preparing to contest again in 2027, this time on a different party platform.
My experience in 2023 has strengthened my resolve. The people in my constituency know me, and I believe my previous campaign helped establish a relationship with them.
I am determined to continue and look forward to the next election.
Beyond your political ambition, what have you done to improve the lives of people in your constituency?
I have continued to support initiatives that respond to the needs of the people.
This year, I facilitated the establishment of a technology hub and supported a back-to-school initiative. These projects were funded with the support of my partners.
For me, leadership is about impact. Even when you are not holding an elected office, you can still contribute to the development of your community.
I want people to understand that political aspirations should not prevent anyone from serving. We must continue to identify needs and provide support where possible.
Some women who have secured elective offices are criticised for not doing enough to support other aspiring female politicians. Do you share this concern?
There is still a lot of work to be done. We have women who are interested in politics, women who are preparing themselves and women who have the capacity to lead. The challenge is creating an environment where they can participate meaningfully.
One concern is that some women who eventually get elected may not use their positions and influence to create opportunities for other women.
When women get into the Senate or the House of Representatives, they should remember the challenges they faced on their way to those positions.
They should use their influence to support other women who are trying to enter the political space. Women’s political representation should not be about individual achievement alone but creating a pathway for others.
What practical steps should political parties take to improve women’s representation?
We must move beyond simply encouraging women to participate, we must address the structural barriers that prevent them from securing party tickets and winning elections.
Women need support, access to political opportunities and a system that recognises their capacity to lead.
We must also build stronger networks of women who are willing to support one another. Those who have the resources, experience and influence should help aspiring female politicians navigate the political process.
There are women who are prepared to serve, but we must create an environment where their preparation and capacity can translate into meaningful political participation.
What is your message to women who are discouraged by the challenges of Nigerian politics?
 Women must not give up. We are trying, and we are rebuilding. There is a growing pool of women who are interested in politics and willing to contribute to national development.
However, the fact that many women are trying but are not making significant progress in representation shows that there is still much work to do.
We must continue to organise, support one another, build networks and challenge the barriers within the political system.
I remain committed to that cause, and I believe women must keep pushing for their place in leadership.
Vanguard News

items.author: Oboh
items.content:
•Declares no vacancy in Aso Rock, Plateau Govt House •Says no rainbow coalition, Plateau going APC
By Golok Nanmwa
JOS — Plateau State governor, Caleb Mutfwang, has said President Bola Tinubu inherited an economy that was tottering on the brink of collapse from the administration of former President Muhammadu Buhari in 2023.
Read Also: Elections: INEC struggles to get 14m PVCs to voters
He also declared there was no vacancy in the Presidential Villa (Aso Rock) and Plateau Government House in 2027, equally dismissing any talks of rainbow coalition.
Mutfwang, who stated this during the formal inauguration of  All Progressives Congress, APC, Campaign Council in Jos yesterday, also defended Tinubu administration’s economic reforms and urged Plateau residents to support the President in the 2027 election.
“Where did President Tinubu meet Nigeria in 2023? He met Nigeria tottering on the brink of collapse; Nigeria that could not service its external debts; Nigeria that would not even allow businesses outside the country to take their proceeds back home.  And that is why some international airlines stopped flying to Nigeria because they could not get the dollars to take back their money.
“Our external reserve was down to just a little over $3 billion, from the over $40 billion it had accumulated for decades.  Today, by the grace of God, we have a healthy external reserve of over $50 billion,” the governor said.
He alleged further that the previous administration resorted to printing money to manage the economy, claiming more than N30 trillion was printed.
Governor Mutfwang said:  “When the President took over in 2023, the government he succeeded had run out of ideas on how to manage the economy and they resorted to printing money in the Central Bank.
“They printed over N30 trillion which went down the drain.  Today, by the grace of God, Central Bank has stabilised and that deficit has been done away with.’’
On fuel subsidy, Mutfwang described the system under the previous administration as fraudulent, alleging that the country borrowed money to pay claims supported by what he called fictitious documents.
“I say it was a fraud because we were borrowing money to pay people who brought fictitious documents. They never brought any wealth. They brought fictitious documents, claimed monies and subsidies.
“You cannot continue to borrow money to give to thieves. You have to stop it at some point. And when it is stopped, there will be a payback; there will be a recovery time,” he said.
The governor said the availability of fuel had improved, despite the increase in its cost, recalling the long queues that previously characterised fuel stations across the country.
“Today, by the grace of God, we have solved one side of the equation. Today, fuel is available. It may not be cheap but it is available.
“Those of us who are of my age bracket or little below will remember the times we spent days in petrol stations queuing for fuel that we could hardly get. But we have been able to resolve that,” Mutfwang said.
He also claimed that the previous administration had sold crude oil in advance, saying the country was now servicing obligations arising from such arrangements.
“Part of the problem of the Buhari regime is that they got to a point that they didn’t know what to do, so they sold our future crude. The crude we are yet to dig from the ground has been sold in advance.  And today, we are paying that debt. And so we cannot expect things to simply change overnight,” he said.
The governor said his administration was taking steps to cushion the effects of the economic adjustment on Plateau residents, citing the introduction of metro buses and revival of the railway system within Jos metropolis.
“I’m glad that Plateau people have commended us for the metro buses we bought early in the regime. I’m glad we’re able to revive the railway system within the metropolis.  I’m glad that we’re able to reduce school fees for our students in tertiary institutions by 50 per cent. I’m glad that we’re able to raise their allowances by about 300 per cent,” he said.
He also commended the federal government’s student financing initiatives, saying Plateau indigenes studying in universities had benefited from the scheme.
“It is also a great joy in my heart that the President also came up with a new scholarship for students called NELFUND.  Today, hundreds of millions have been given to Plateau indigenes who are studying in different universities. Some are getting N20,000 monthly, N40,000 monthly. It has never happened before,” he said.
On the 2027 elections, Mutfwang called for power rotation between the North and South, saying political arrangements should be respected.
“We must agree that power should rotate between the North and the South. And if the North spends eight years, which we have nothing to show for, it is only fair that we allow the South to do eight years because if we don’t respect that sharing arrangement, it will come back to haunt us someday,” he said.
Mutfwang also declared that there was no vacancy in Plateau State Government House, ahead of the 2027 governorship election.
“That is why in Plateau State, we have already agreed that it is two terms per senatorial zone. Except the northern zone does not want to produce a governor until 2035, then you can toy with my mandate,” he said.
Governor Mutfwang urged APC candidates and campaign council members to communicate the achievements of the administration to the electorate and avoid actions capable of deepening divisions.
“We must, therefore, go about this campaign with facts, with honesty, with seriousness. Part of the reason people are still apprehensive is because we have not communicated the real message, and we have a responsibility to ensure that that message is properly communicated.
“I’d like to urge all our candidates for the various positions, you must lead from the front. You must be bridge-builders.”
“I am confident that come January 16, 2027, by the grace of God, Plateau State will return President Bola Ahmed Tinubu with a resounding victory. And two weeks later, the people of Plateau will renew their mandate for us to continue on the good journey we have started,” he said.
On security, Mutfwang acknowledged the persistence of insecurity, adding that his administration was taking steps to strengthen security and facilitate the return of displaced persons to their communities.
“On security, I know our opponents will say there is hunger in the land. We don’t deny it. They will say that the insecurity situation has not abated. We don’t deny it.  But if they say we have not taken steps at all to address those issues, they know they are lying.
“Insecurity is not like tap water, where you simply turn on the tap and it flows down. It requires concerted, deliberate, intentional, sustained efforts before you get results.
“By the grace of God, we have understood what the issues are, and we have begun to make sure we propose solutions in the right places that matter,” he said.
The governor said his administration would continue to protect communities and disclosed plans to deploy additional security personnel.
“One thing I have committed myself to is that I will ensure the protection of every inch of land in Plateau State.
“Very soon, we are going to be taking practical steps to facilitate the return of internally displaced persons back to their communities.  And so, all we are asking is for Plateau people to trust us, be patient with us, and by the grace of God, you will not regret it.”
No rainbow coalition, Plateau going APC
The governor dismissed talks of any “rainbow coalition” ahead of the 2027 elections , declaring that there was no vacancy in Aso Rock and the Plateau Government House as he inaugurated the presidential and state campaign councils of the All Progressives Congress, APC.
Mutfwang said Plateau people had chosen the APC as their political vehicle for the 2027 elections, urging party faithful and campaign officials to mobilise across the state.
“Some people are talking about rainbow, we are talking about a unification movement. Plateau people have decided 2027 to go one direction.  And we have chosen that the wings on which we have chosen to fly in 2027 are the wings of the APC,” the governor declared

CALABAR — Vice President Kashim Shettima has assured Cross River residents that the proposed Bakassi Deep Seaport and Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway will be delivered, urging them to re-elect President Bola Tinubu and Governor Bassey Otu in 2027.
Shettima gave the assurance yesterday while representing Tinubu at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally at the U.J. Esuene Stadium, Calabar.

“Over the past three years, you have shown us support, and you have resisted the lies and propaganda intended to misrepresent us,” he said.

He added that the project would create thousands of direct and indirect jobs, while opening up economic opportunities for communities along the corridor.
On the Bakassi Deep Seaport, the Vice President said the project had received Federal Government approval, expressing optimism that it would become an international maritime gateway upon completion.

Shettima said the seaport and coastal highway were central to efforts to position Cross River as a major beneficiary of Nigeria’s maritime economy.

items.author: Oboh
items.content:
By Yinka Kolawole
The Federal Government has fully disbursed the N75 billion Manufacturing Sector Fund to 104 manufacturing businesses, while N65.8 billion has been disbursed to 15,018 micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) to boost domestic production, expand businesses and create jobs.
Minister of Industry, Trade and Investment, Dr Jumoke Oduwole, disclosed this in an address on “Harnessing Nigeria’s Economic Potential for Greater Prosperity”.
Oduwole said the interventions were part of the Federal Government’s efforts to strengthen local industries, improve productive capacity and drive sustainable economic growth.
The disbursements were made under the Federal Government’s N200 billion intervention package, managed by the Bank of Industry (BoI), to support businesses, boost domestic production and create jobs.
The package comprises the N50 billion Presidential Conditional Grant Scheme for nano businesses, the N75 billion FGN MSME Intervention Fund for micro, small and medium-sized enterprises, and the N75 billion FGN Manufacturing Sector Fund for manufacturing businesses.
Oduwole noted that the N75 billion Manufacturing Sector Fund had been fully disbursed to 104 manufacturing businesses, while N65.8 billion had been disbursed to 15,018 businesses under the MSME Intervention Fund as of the first quarter of 2026.
She, however, stressed that the impact of government funding should be measured by stronger businesses, increased production and improved livelihoods rather than the amount disbursed alone.
The minister acknowledged that access to finance remained a major challenge for manufacturers seeking to acquire equipment, purchase raw materials, expand production capacity and create employment.
She said Nigeria’s economic transformation required fiscal discipline, monetary stability and policies that supported domestic production and competitiveness.
According to her, the government is working to remove barriers to investment, production and trade while creating an enabling environment for businesses to thrive.
Highlighting developments in the manufacturing sector, Oduwole said cement manufacturing grew by 11.53 per cent in the first quarter of 2026, while motor vehicle assembly expanded by 5.44 per cent during the period. She added that vehicle assembly grew by 40.6 per cent in 2025, while cassava starch production recorded growth of 474.74 per cent.
“Processing locally grown cassava into industrial starch will support manufacturers, while vehicle assembly will create opportunities for engineers, technicians and supply-chain businesses,” she said.
The minister also highlighted opportunities under the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), noting that intra-African trade had grown by 21 per cent.

items.author: Oboh
items.content:
*Taraba, Plateau, Jigawa, Bayelsa, Benue among states with thousands of cards awaiting collection *Sokoto, Nasarawa, Zamfara, Yobe record significant increase in voter population *Kano yet to compile collection figures; Borno, Bauchi, Kebbi withholding data *Lagos, Ondo, Ogun, Ekiti, Osun, Kaduna, Adamawa report growing voter numbers *INEC intensifies mobilisation ahead of January 16 presidential election
By Soni Daniel
ABUJA — Three weeks after the collection of Permanent Voters Cards, PVCs started across the country, the failure of no fewer than 14 million eligible voters to collect their PVCs, is emerging as a major concern for the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC.
Read Also: Critics of Rainbow Coalition can’t unite their families – Wike
Investigations by Vanguard across several states show that while the Continuous Voter Registration, CVR, exercise attracted millions of new registrants, a significant number of produced PVCs remain uncollected, potentially denying their owners the opportunity to participate in next year’s elections.
Vanguard’s checks showed that 6.26 million PVCs were not collected before the 2023 general elections. In the last Continuous Voters Registration, CVR, exercise, the electoral commission registered 10,772,421 new voters. At press time, many states are yet to release their tallies of uncollected voter’s cards estimated at over 14 million.
The situation is particularly worrying in states like Plateau, Taraba, Jigawa, Benue and Bayelsa, where INEC has disclosed substantial numbers of cards awaiting collection.
In Plateau, about 95,000 PVCs from previous registration exercises remain unclaimed. Taraba has 29,314 outstanding cards, while Jigawa has 33,079 cards ready for collection. Bayelsa, on its part, has 52,225 PVCs from the first phase of the recent registration exercise awaiting collection.
Benue has also recorded considerable activity, with 58,581 PVCs collected during the recent display of the voters’ register, although thousands of additional cards are still being processed or await collection.
Beyond the collection challenge, voter registration figures indicate growing electoral participation across the country, with Sokoto, Zamfara, Nasarawa, Benue, Ogun, Kano and other states recording significant additions to their voter registers.
However, the picture is incomplete in some states. While Kano is yet to compile its PVC collection figures across its 44 local government areas, INEC officials in Borno, Bauchi and Kebbi declined to provide updates, describing the requested information as sensitive.
In the South-West, Lagos says its final register will not be available until December 15, after conclusion of the claims and objections exercise. Ondo, Ogun, Ekiti and Osun have reported increases in registered voters, although some are still compiling their PVC collection figures.
The findings raise questions about whether the increasing number of registered voters will translate into participation in the 2027 elections, beginning with the presidential and National Assembly polls on January 16.
Taraba: 29,314 PVCs uncollected
In Taraba State, the number of registered voters stands at 2,254,380, according to INEC.
However, no fewer than 29,314 PVCs remain uncollected across the commission’s offices in the state.
The Resident Electoral Commissioner, REC, Dr Sa’ad Umar Idris, said the outstanding cards comprise 13,826 legacy PVCs from previous electoral cycles between 2011 and 2023 and 15,488 cards processed during the latest registration exercise.
He explained that the commission processed 31,676 cards arising from new registrations, voter transfers and replacements during the 2025–2026 exercise. Of these, only 16,188, representing about 51 per cent, had been collected.
Expressing concern over the low collection rate, Idris appealed to political parties, traditional rulers, religious leaders and civil society organisations to mobilise residents to visit INEC local government offices and collect their cards.
Plateau: 121,821 new voters, 95,000 PVCs uncollected
In Plateau State, INEC recorded 121,821 new voters during the latest CVR exercise, while about 95,000 PVCs from previous registration exercises remain uncollected.
The REC, Prof. Samuel Egwu, disclosed this during a meeting with political party leaders and other stakeholders in Jos.
He said women accounted for 65,928 of new registrants, while men represented 55,893.
The commission also received 38,399 requests for voter transfers within and outside the state.
Egwu said the outstanding PVCs remained a major concern as INEC intensified preparations for the 2027 elections.
Jigawa: 33,079 PVCs ready for collection
Jigawa State has 2,351,298 registered voters, according to the REC, Prof. Muhammad Bashar.
Bashar said 33,079 PVCs are ready for collection by people who registered for transfers, corrections and replacements between August and December 2025.
He also disclosed that the state recorded 515,878 new voters during the three phases of the recent CVR exercise.
Jigawa has 27 local government areas, 287 registration areas and 4,522 polling units.
Zamfara adds 313,115 voters
In Zamfara State, INEC recorded 313,115 new voters under the CVR exercise as of August 2026.
The REC, Dr. Mahmud Isa, disclosed this to Vanguard in Gusau, explaining that the new registrants are additional to the 1,952,060 registered voters recorded in the state for the 2023 general elections.
Kaduna: 61,494 PVCs collected
In Kaduna State, 61,494 PVCs had been collected as of October 28, according to figures obtained from INEC.
An official of the commission, Hajiya Rukaiyatu, said the figure comprised 12,741 old PVCs and 48,753 newly-issued cards.
Women collected 32,589 cards, comprising 6,782 old and 25,807 new PVCs, while men collected 28,905, comprising 5,959 old and 22,946 new cards.
The figures indicate a higher collection rate among female voters.
Nasarawa: Voter population hits 2.1m
Nasarawa State’s registered voter population has risen to approximately 2.1 million, following registration of 247,000 new voters between 2025 and July 2026.
The REC, Mallam Mohammed Abullahi Sadiq, disclosed this, commending residents for their response to the registration exercise.
He urged those yet to collect their PVCs to visit INEC offices in their respective local government areas.
Sokoto: 2.63m registered voters
Sokoto State has recorded 2,633,113 registered voters, including 461,057 captured during the latest CVR exercise.
The commission’s Public Relations Officer, Hassan Kaoje, said the figure represented 2.55 per cent of the national voter register.
He said INEC was intensifying efforts to ensure that all eligible registrants collected their PVCs before the 2027 elections.
Kaoje urged those who had completed registration but were yet to collect their cards to visit designated INEC offices and collection centres.
Adamawa: 2.43m million registered voters
Adamawa State has 2,431,146 registered voters as of July 2026.
INEC’s Head of Voter Education and Information in the state, Alhaji Aliyu Shaba Lafiagi, disclosed that 49,304 PVCs had been collected as of October 23.
He also reported that 11,725 voters’ cards had been transferred into the state, comprising 6,255 belonging to men and 5,520 belonging to women.
Borno, Bauchi, Kebbi withhold figures
In Borno State, INEC declined to provide the latest figures on registered voters and PVC collection, describing the information as sensitive.
Officials said the commission is yet to ascertain the actual number of newly-registered voters and PVCs collected because the exercise is ongoing.
However, the 2023 register put the state’s voter population at 2,564,197.
A similar situation played out in Bauchi, where INEC officials declined to release requested figures, insisting that the information is not for public consumption.
Efforts to obtain updated figures from Kebbi also proved unsuccessful.
Benue: 3.05m registered voters, 279,498 new registrants
Benue State has 3,057,225 registered voters, including 279,498 new registrants across its 23 local government areas.
The REC, Mallam Aminu Idris, said INEC received 101,695 PVCs from its headquarters for the first phase of the CVR and voter transfers.
The consignment comprised 54,724 new PVCs and 46,971 transferred cards.
During the display of the voters’ register between October 9 and 15, 2026, at registration area level, 58,581 PVCs were collected.
The breakdown showed that 9,139 were old cards previously held in storage, 28,854 were new CVR cards, 12,707 were transferred cards and 7,881 were replacement cards.
Idris said all existing PVCs remained available for collection at INEC offices in the state’s 23 local government areas.
He added that the commission would announce the availability of cards processed during the second and third phases of the CVR exercise after receiving official notification from its headquarters.
Kano yet to compile PVC collection figures
Despite having one of the country’s largest voter populations, Kano State is yet to determine the total number of PVCs collected across its 44 local government areas.
INEC’s Public Relations Officer, Nahila Bello Dandago, said the commission was still compiling the figures because the collection exercise was ongoing.
She disclosed that Kano had 6,570,276 registered voters, making it the state with the second-highest voter population after Lagos, which has 7,488,633.
Yobe: 283,525 new voters
In Yobe State, the voter population has increased from 1,485,146 in 2022 to 1,768,671 in 2026, representing an addition of 283,525 voters.
In Damaturu Local Government Area, 11,911 PVCs had been collected, leaving 9,137 unclaimed.
The Electoral Officer for Damaturu, Ahmed A. Waziri, said INEC had 21,048 cards available for collection, comprising 8,100 outstanding cards from the 2023 exercise and 12,948 received during the first phase of the latest distribution.
He said Damaturu was yet to receive cards under the second and third phases of the distribution exercise.
Waziri added that the commission’s ICT department was better positioned to provide comprehensive figures for the state’s 17 local government areas.
Lagos: Final register expected December 15
In Lagos State, INEC said the final Register of Voters would not be available until the conclusion of the claims and objections exercise on December 15, 2026.
The commission’s Public Affairs Officer, Tope Adenuga, said the final figures for newly registered voters could not be provided until the exercise was completed.
He said: “The final Register of Voters requested will be made available until after the conclusion of the ongoing claims and objections exercise.”
According to him, the final list is expected to be ready on December 15.
The state recorded 7,488,633 registered voters in the figures available to Vanguard.
INEC was yet to provide the latest PVC collection statistics.
Ondo: 2.05m registered voters
In Ondo State, the total number of registered voters stands at 2,053,061, with 76,285 new registrants.
The Head of Voter Education and Publicity, Olayinka Ogunseye, disclosed that 1,771,326 PVCs had been collected.
He, however, cautioned that the figures were preliminary and not final.
Ekiti: Voter population rises to 1.05 million
Ekiti State’s registered voter population has increased to 1,055,708, according to INEC.
The figure represents an increase of 68,061 over the 987,647 registered voters recorded during the 2023 general elections.
The commission could not immediately provide the latest PVC collection figures because the exercise was ongoing.
Ogun: 348,703 additional voters
Ogun State has recorded an increase of 348,703 registered voters, bringing its voter population to 3,037,008 as of October 2026.
The figure represents an increase from the 2,688,305 registered voters recorded for the 2023 general elections.
INEC officials said PVC distribution was still ongoing at the commission’s local government offices.
Osun: 2.33m registered voters
In Osun State, the total number of registered voters stands at 2,339,233.
The INEC Public Relations Officer, Musa Olurode, said the figure was the same as that used for the August 2026 governorship election because no fresh CVR exercise was conducted after the poll.
He disclosed that 1,906,390 PVCs had been collected as of August, adding that the figure would be updated after the ongoing collection exercise.
He said: “As at today, the total voters register in Osun State is 2,339,233. This is the figure for the governorship election and it cannot change because the Continuous Voters Registration did not take place in the state after the August poll.”
He added that the number of collected PVCs would change as more registered voters collected their cards.
Delta: INEC declines to release PVC figures
In Delta State, INEC officials declined to provide statistics on PVC collection, directing enquiries to the ICT department.
The Head of Voter Education, Nse Abasi Udom, said the ICT unit was responsible for monitoring and keeping the relevant records.
However, she declined to provide the contact details of the department’s head, saying officials were in an important meeting.
A similar experience occurred during a previous visit to a PVC collection centre at Uzor Igwe Primary School, Nnebisi Road, Asaba, where an INEC official declined to disclose the number of cards available or collected.
The official, however, acknowledged an impressive turnout of residents.
“What I can tell you, which you can verify from the atmosphere here, is that the turnout is impressive. People are coming and collecting,” the official said.
The commission’s inability to provide the figures has made it difficult to establish the number of PVCs still awaiting collection across the state.
Bayelsa: 52,225 PVCs await collection
In Bayelsa State, INEC has put the total number of registered voters at 1,200,691, with 52,225 PVCs from the first phase of the recent CVR exercise awaiting collection.
Ekeremor and Sagbama local government areas recorded the highest numbers of registered voters, with 12,023 and 10,080 respectively.
Ogbia recorded the lowest figure of 3,132, followed by Nembe with 3,620 and Kolokuma/Opokuma with 3,712.
INEC said collection commenced at registration area level on October 9 and ended on October 15, after which the exercise was moved to the commission’s offices across the state’s eight local government areas.
The commission urged eligible registrants who missed the ward-level distribution to visit the respective local government offices to collect their cards.
With thousands of PVCs still awaiting collection in several states, the findings underscore the challenge facing INEC as it prepares for the 2027 general elections.
While the increasing number of registered voters points to growing interest in the electoral process, the commission’s ability to translate registration into actual voter participation will depend significantly on the success of its PVC collection and mobilisation campaigns.
Clifford Ndujihe, Dayo Johnson, Umar Yusuf, Ndahi Marama, Femi Bolaji, Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo, Peter Duru, Hadiza Yusuf, Maryam Abdul-aziz Usman, Musa Ubandawaki, Idris Salisu, Edwin Philip, Golok Nanmwa, Muhammad Inuwa, Christopher Ameh, Egufe Yafugborhi, Rotimi Ojomoyela, Olayinka Ajayi, Shina Abubakar, Emem Idio & James Ogunnaike contributed to this report.

The M3 Motorway has been closed from Faizpur to Jaranwala due to dense fog, according to Syed Imran Ahmed, spokesperson for the National Highways and Motorway Police (NHMP) Central Region.
The spokesperson said the closure is meant to protect the lives and property of the public. He described driving in fog as extremely dangerous and urged people to avoid unnecessary travel.
Safer Hours to Travel

Motorway Police Safety Advice
The Motorway Police also issued the following advice for drivers who must travel in fog:
Keep your speed low and maintain a safe distance from the vehicle ahead.
Stay in your lane and avoid unnecessary overtaking and sudden braking.
Use fog lights and make sure your headlights, tail lights, and wipers are working properly.
If visibility drops sharply in heavy fog, stop at a safe place.
Fog regularly forces the closure of motorway sections in Punjab during winter. Earlier this year, five major motorways were closed due to fog, while parts of the M2, M3, and M4 were shut down for the same reason in December 2024.

items.content:
By John Alechenu
ABUJA — The presidential candidate of the Young Progressives Party (YPP), Arch. Peter Agada, has called for an end to the export of Nigeria’s raw materials without adding value, saying the practice deprives the country of greater economic benefits.
Agada spoke in an interview in Abuja on Monday while outlining his economic blueprint ahead of the 2027 general elections.
He said his proposed administration would prioritise electricity supply and promote industrialisation from the ward level to ensure that value was added to Nigerian produce before export.
“The industrialisation we all talk about can only happen when we fix power and put in place policies that will promote investments from the ward level upwards,” Agada said.
He said rural communities would be made attractive to agro-allied industries capable of processing agricultural produce for export and generating foreign exchange.
“Our rural communities will attract agro-allied industries to promote export of produce after value has been added to earn foreign exchange. Enough of sending raw materials only to collect peanuts in return,” he said.
The YPP candidate also said his proposed administration would mobilise Nigerians at home and in the diaspora to build a country citizens would be proud to call home.
He said this would involve building on the country’s strengths while addressing areas of weakness.
On politics, Agada urged members of the political elite, irrespective of party affiliation, to allow Nigerians to freely choose their leaders at all levels.
He said the practice of imposing leaders on the electorate on the basis of ethnic or religious considerations should become a thing of the past.

By Umar Yusuf, Yola
The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) has appointed Deputy Comptroller Mamman Ali as the Acting Area Comptroller of its Adamawa/Taraba Command.
Ali, who was until his appointment the Coordinator of the Customs Anti-Smuggling Unit, Operation Whirlwind, Zone E, takes over from Mohammed Tako, who has been promoted to Assistant Comptroller-General of Customs in charge of Zone B, Kaduna.
At a brief handing-over ceremony in Yola on Monday, Tako said the command recorded significant achievements during his tenure despite directives on strict border closure.

Tako disclosed that the total Duty Paid Value (DPV) of seizures recorded by the command during his one-year tenure stood at ₦535,975,190.

items.content: Mumbai: Overseas investors' holdings in nearly 70% of India's top 100 companies are at multi-year lows amid unabated selling of blue-chip stocks over the past two years, reflecting diminished appetite for local equities.The decline in foreign ownership has been broad-based but has been more pronounced in the largest companies, especially banks and information technology.Godrej Consumer Products, Jindal Steel, Maruti Suzuki, Dr Reddy's Laboratories, Adani Enterprises, HCL Technologies and Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) saw foreign ownership fall to levels not seen in more than two decades.135477407Holdings in another 10 companies, including DLF, Reliance Industries, Bajaj Holdings & Investment, UltraTech Cement, Kotak Mahindra Bank, Axis Bank, Trent, Eicher Motors, Britannia Industries and Shriram Finance, are at more than 15-year lows.The decline in foreign ownership reflects a repricing of growth prospects as global investors shifted allocations towards markets offering stronger earnings growth, according to Rahul Bhutoria, director and co-founder of Valtrust Capital, a New Delhi-based portfolio manager.Read more: Explained: Why gold investors should tone down expectations as yellow metal plunges to a 1-year low"This is not an exit from India; it is a repricing of where growth sits," he said.India's weight in the MSCI Emerging Markets index has declined from about 20% at its 2024 peak to roughly 11%, while Taiwan and South Korea together now account for nearly half the index as global investors chase the artificial intelligence (AI) cycle.Bhutoria said a significant portion of the selling was mechanical, with passive funds adjusting their portfolios in line with changes in benchmark weights.Relatively slower earnings growth in India has added to the pressure. While the S&P 500 and Nifty 50 trade at roughly 18-19 times one-year forward earnings, S&P 500 earnings are expected to grow about 33% in calendar year 2026, compared with 14-15% growth for the Nifty in FY27.FPI holdings in LTM, Power Grid Corporation, SBI Life Insurance, Varun Beverages, HDFC Life Insurance, ICICI Bank, Mahindra & Mahindra, Tata Consumer Products, Cipla and Larsen & Toubro are at seven-to-eight-year lows.Stakes in 15 other companies such as CG Power & Industrial Solutions, Adani Power, ITC, Sun Pharma, Max Healthcare, Eternal, ABB India, Siemens, Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles, Bharat Electronics, Hindustan Aeronautics, HDFC Bank, NTPC, Cholamandalam Investment and InterGlobe Aviation - are at three-to-five-year lows.Read more: Diwali 2026: 77 stocks knock down D-St bears to deliver multibagger returns of up to 4,700% in a yearSome of these stocks may have seen marginal increases in foreign ownership during the September quarter, but their holdings remain close to multi-year lows. The number of Indian companies in which foreign investors hold more than 1% has also increased from around 900 in 2021 to 1,300. FPIs continue to participate in primary issuances and block deals even as they sell in the secondary market.Lokesh Manik, senior analyst at Vallum Capital, said India had historically traded at a 25-40% valuation premium to other emerging markets because of its higher return on equity (RoE) and growth rates.

items.content:
….Receives over 1,000 APC defectors into PDP
By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta
ABEOKUTA — The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Ogun State, Hon. Oladipupo Adebutu, has described the omission of his name from the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) list of governorship candidates as a temporary distraction, insisting that it would not stop him from contesting the 2027 election.
Adebutu spoke on Monday while receiving more than 1,000 defectors from the All Progressives Congress (APC) into the PDP at the party’s state secretariat in Abeokuta.
The defectors were led by a former member of the House of Representatives, Hon. Segun William, and received by Adebutu alongside other party leaders, including the PDP’s Ogun Central senatorial candidate, Iyabo Obasanjo.
Addressing the gathering, Adebutu expressed confidence that the controversy surrounding his omission from INEC’s list would be resolved, maintaining that he remained a bona fide member of the PDP.
He cited his participation in elections under the party’s platform over the past two decades as evidence of his loyalty and challenged those questioning his membership to provide evidence that he had defected.
“I have been the candidate of the PDP for the last 20 years, in every election cycle. My question is: at what stage did I leave or vacate the party? Where is the proof that, for one day, I have even visited the APC office, let alone joined the party?” he asked.
Adebutu also said he played an active role in organising and financing the party’s recent membership registration exercise in Ogun, which he claimed recorded more than 19,800 members.
He said his registration number in the exercise was 1536, describing it as further evidence of his continued membership of the party.
The PDP chieftain alleged that the controversy over his omission from the INEC list was intended to distract the opposition and disenfranchise voters.
He, however, urged party members to remain focused, saying the development would not disrupt the PDP’s mobilisation activities across the state.
Adebutu disclosed that the party’s campaign team had visited 12 of the state’s 20 local government areas and more than 140 of its 236 wards.
He said the grassroots mobilisation exercise would continue despite what he described as attempts to distract the party.
“We have visited 12 of the 20 local governments. Of the 236 wards, we have visited over 140. Tomorrow, we continue again because we know that the trick is to get us distracted. We will not be distracted. We will keep our eyes on the ball, and we shall win,” he said.
Earlier, William said the defectors decided to leave the APC because of their dissatisfaction with the party’s approach to governance and what he described as its failure to uphold democratic principles and deliver development in Ogun State.
Recounting his political journey, William said he joined partisan politics in 2007 and eventually aligned with the APC, despite earlier advice from friends and associates to join the PDP.
He said his experience in the ruling party had convinced him that it no longer represented the democratic ideals and developmental aspirations he believed in.
William said the defectors were joining the PDP to contribute to the political and socio-economic development of Ogun State, expressing confidence in the party’s leadership.
He also described the APC as no longer capable of accommodating the democratic aspirations of its members and residents of the state.
“We are seeking the progress of our dear Ogun State. My sincere appreciation goes first and foremost to our incoming governor, who has made this occasion possible, with the assistance of our deputy governor, our senator, the directors-general, party members, the party hierarchy and the state chairman,” William said.
The defection comes as political parties intensify mobilisation and positioning ahead of the 2027 general elections.

By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa
YENAGOA — Governor Douye Diri of Bayelsa State has urged anyone aspiring to succeed him to seek God’s approval through prayer, saying the next governor must be a God-fearing person.
Diri spoke on Monday during the state’s 15th Thanksgiving service at the Ecumenical Centre, Igbogene, Yenagoa, where he declared that Bayelsa had been handed over to God.
He said nobody could stop anyone chosen by God to lead the state, adding that the Almighty would always have the final say in its affairs.
The governor also urged residents to remain united, tolerant and peaceful, describing these as essential conditions for the state’s development.
He reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to improving the lives of residents, saying it had the political will to transform Bayelsa, which he described as one of the states with the best environments for development.
Diri thanked the people for their support over the past six years and urged them to sustain their cooperation with the government.
“All who want to be governor, go and seek the face of God. Anyone who wants to be governor must be God-fearing. If God said yes, nobody can say no, not even me,” he said.
He added: “Let us continue to worship God. Let us be tolerant and patient as we will become victorious at the end of the day.
“As I keep saying, those of us who were born in Yenagoa or know Bayelsa of old can see the difference today. It is enough to give thanks.
“We have one of the best environments in Nigeria, and with the political will, we are bringing development to our people.”
In his sermon, the guest preacher and former Bayelsa State Chairman of the Christian Association of Nigeria, Very Rev. Joseph Opelema, urged Christians to combine their religious faith with responsible citizenship.
Speaking on the theme, “Called to be Good Christians and Good Citizens,” Opelema said Christians had dual responsibilities as members of the church and citizens of society.
Drawing his message from Matthew 22:15-22, where Jesus addressed the question of paying taxes, he said the biblical instruction to give to Caesar what belongs to Caesar and to God what belongs to God underscored the importance of responsible citizenship.
The cleric said Christians should demonstrate sacrifice, prudence, accountability, justice, love, care and charity wherever they found themselves, particularly in public office.
He lamented what he described as a gap between religious participation and the practice of Christian values, urging believers to become witnesses, the salt of the earth and the light of the world.
Opelema also described Bayelsa as richly endowed with natural and human resources, favourable weather, land and rivers, which he said could make the state a tourism destination.
He expressed optimism that the state could realise its potential with God-fearing leadership.
Highlights of the thanksgiving service included the unveiling of a book titled Lively Oracle, containing scriptural declarations made by the governor during morning devotions, and musical performances by gospel artistes.
Those present included the governor’s wives, Dr Gloria Diri and Justice Patience Diri; Deputy Governor Dr Peter Akpe and his wife, Dr Favour Akpe; former deputy governors Rt. Hon. Peremobowei Ebebi and Rear Admiral Gboribiogha John Jonah (rtd); and senators representing Bayelsa Central and East, Dr Konbowei Benson and Chief Benson Agadaga.
Also in attendance were Minority Leader of the House of Representatives, Chief Fred Agbedi; other federal lawmakers from the state; the Speaker of the Bayelsa State House of Assembly, represented by Deputy Speaker Michael Ogbere; and the state’s Chief Judge, represented by the President of the Customary Court of Appeal, Justice Daniel Ayah.
Other guests included National Chairman of the Pan Niger Delta Forum, Dr Boladei Igali; Chairman of the Bayelsa State Traditional Rulers Council, King Bubaraye Dakolo; Managing Director of the Niger Delta Development Commission, Dr Samuel Ogbuku; Chairman of Azikel Group, Dr Azipapu Eruani; and former governor Chief David Lyon.

Bengaluru-based wealthtech startup PowerUp Money has raised $10 Mn (₹95 Cr) in a fresh funding round led by Flourish Ventures, with participation from existing investors Peak XV Partners, Accel, Blume Ventures, Kae Capital, 8i Ventures and DeVC.
The startup plans to use the capital to expand its AI-led wealth management offerings, scale its managed advisory business and develop personalised financial planning solutions for Indian investors.
“We started by making high-quality investment advice accessible to every Indian. Today, AI makes it possible to deliver a much more comprehensive, wealth-manager-like experience digitally and at a fraction of traditional costs. A significant portion of this investment will go towards building an AI-powered wealth manager that brings personalised financial planning and ongoing portfolio guidance to every Indian,” PowerUp’s founder and CEO Prateek Jindal said.
Jindal, who has also cofounded fintech major Uni Cards, launched PowerUp in 2025 to help customers manage their mutual fund portfolios. It claims to have over 15 Lakh customers, who track mutual fund portfolios worth over ₹2.5 Lakh Cr on its platform. Its mutual fund advisory subscription, PowerUp Elite, has over 1 Lakh paid members.
Beyond mutual funds, the startup is now looking to combine investment advice, managed wealth services and digital advisory, becoming a full-stack financial planning platform in essence.
The first step towards its new avatar has now come with the launch of its end-to-end digital wealth advisory offering, Elite Prime. The service includes an AI wealth coach and personal assistant, considers users’ financial goals, risk profiles and existing portfolios while helping them manage their portfolios and supporting their investment decisions.
It is also seeking to scale up its managed wealth advisory offering, Infinite, to a broader customer base.
Aimed at investors seeking more hands-on financial support, Infinite combines personalised financial planning, portfolio construction, multi-asset allocation, goal-based strategies, ongoing portfolio management and dedicated adviser support.
PowerUp claims that Infinite has scaled to nearly ₹500 Cr in assets under management (AUM) within around nine months of launch.

items.author: efosataiwo@vanguardngr.com
items.content:
North Korea on Tuesday slammed the FBI’s allegations that Pyongyang was behind the theft of $6 billion from cryptocurrency platform Binance, with Kim Jong Un’s powerful sister labelling it a “grave political provocation”.
Kim Yo Jong, in a statement released Tuesday by the KCNA state news agency, said the FBI’s claim was “absurd rhetoric and nothing new,” given prior US allegations that North Korea was behind last year’s major hack of Bybit.
“It is a grave political provocation against the DPRK that the US misleads the international public opinion as if all the cyber crimes in different parts of the world are our deeds,” Kim said, using the acronym for North Korea’s official name.
The FBI said on Saturday that a North Korea-affiliated hacking group called TraderTraitor had been behind the hack.
TraderTraitor is the same group blamed for a $1.5 billion theft from the Bybit platform in February last year, which had been the largest crypto theft until the Binance hack.
“This is a sinister attempt to damage the international image of the DPRK and undermine its dignity and national prestige and another grave violation of the sovereignty of the DPRK,” Kim said.
“It is the consistent policy stand of the DPRK government to resolutely oppose all sorts of malicious acts in cyberspace,” she added.
Binance is the world’s largest crypto exchange by daily trading volumes. News of the hacking attack caused the prices of most major cryptocurrencies to fall sharply on Friday.
After the FBI released its statement on Saturday, US President Donald Trump cast doubt on North Korea’s involvement in the hack.
“I’m not concerned. We’re learning about it. We don’t know if it’s North Korea,” Trump told reporters at his residence in Florida.
Trump has made repeated overtures to nuclear-armed North Korea since returning to office, and said he was open to meeting with supreme leader Kim Jong Un this year.
Those gestures have been met with silence from Pyongyang.
Kim Yo Jong, in her statement, said the new allegations “confirmed Washington’s hostile attitude toward the DPRK once again.”
“We have issues to reconsider in diverse aspects as regards the very unpleasant US hostile attitude,” she added.

Wike spoke on Monday in Abuja at the commissioning of the Gwagwalada Civic Centre and an interactive session with stakeholders of the All Progressives Congress APC and the Peoples Democratic Party PDP in Gwagwalada Area Council.
The minister said the coalition, which brings together political stakeholders from both parties, was formed in the interest of unity, cooperation and development in the FCT.
“Some greedy and selfish politicians do not understand what we call unity. They have no capacity to hold their space, they have no capacity to even hold their families, and they have no capacity to hold their communities. So they can open their mouths and say there is no Rainbow Coalition,” he said.
Wike challenged critics of the alliance to explain why political leaders who once disagreed could not come together to pursue common interests.
He described the development in Gwagwalada as a departure from the politics of confrontation, insisting that the FCT needed cooperation rather than needless political hostility.
Commending political leaders in the area for setting aside their differences, he said their decision showed that the collective interest of the people outweighed individual political ambition.
Wike also urged residents not to repeat what he described as the mistake of the 2023 general elections, and called for credible representation at the National Assembly.
The minister canvassed support for a former senator, Philip Aduda, and other candidates endorsed by the coalition, saying political representatives must be accessible and familiar with their constituents.
Wike also declared support for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu and urged residents to turn their endorsements into votes in 2027.
“On the day of the election, it will not be a day for market or fishing. It is the day all of us have decided to come together and demonstrate our strength through our votes. Go to the polling units, districts and communities and mobilise the people to vote for Bola Ahmed Tinubu,” he said.
APC chair
Earlier, the FCT APC Chairman, Ishaku Tanko Yamawo, described the gathering as historic, saying Wike’s intervention had brought together leaders who previously operated on opposing sides.
The FCT PDP Chairman, Alhaji Ismaila Mohammed Dogara, praised Wike for his development interventions, particularly the revival of a project abandoned for 16 years in Gwagwalada.
The Aguma of Gwagwalada, Alhaji Muhammadu Magaji, also commended Wike’s contributions to the development of the territory. He said the revival of the abandoned project underscored the importance of continuity in governance.
A former Chairman of Gwagwalada Area Council, Zakari Angulu Dobi, recalled that the Civic Centre was almost 80 per cent completed when he left office, but suffered vandalism during the 16 years it was abandoned, reducing its completion level to about 40 per cent.
In his welcome address, the Chairman of Gwagwalada Area Council, Kassim Mohammed, listed road projects executed by his administration in Gwagwalada metropolis, Tungan Wada, Abum-pe and other communities. He thanked Wike for approving a new facility in Gwagwalada, but appealed for intervention on the road linking the Army checkpoint to the Specialist Hospital.

Jaissle desperately needs a win at fellow strugglers Fulham on Saturday to ease the mounting scrutiny.

items.content:
Everton increased the pressure on under-fire Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle as Thierno Barry sealed a 1-0 win at St James’ Park on Monday.
Barry netted early in the second half to lift Everton into seventh place in the Premier League and leave Newcastle languishing in 13th.
Newcastle midfielder Jacob Ramsey was sent off in the final seconds for a crude foul on Harrison Armstrong.
It was a fitting end to another painful defeat for Saudi-funded Newcastle, who have lost four of their past five matches in all competitions, winning just twice in their last seven.
Jaissle and his players were booed off at half-time and again after the final whistle as the German coach begins to feel the heat in his first season in charge.
Hired following Eddie Howe’s surprise close-season exit, former Red Bull Salzburg and Al-Ahli boss Jaissle has struggled to make an impact on Tyneside.
Jaissle desperately needs a win at fellow strugglers Fulham on Saturday to ease the mounting scrutiny.
Bizarrely, Newcastle have lost 22 of their last 33 Premier League matches on a Monday and many of their supporters headed for the exits well before the final whistle on a miserable rainy night.
Barry’s eighth goal this season, including four in his last six matches, gave Everton their second win against Newcastle in the space of five days following their 3-1 victory in the League Cup fourth round on Thursday.
Everton ended their run of two successive league defeats after losing against Arsenal and Chelsea.
It was Everton’s first away league win since February 28 when they took three points on their previous visit to Newcastle.
Jack Grealish was absent from the Everton squad for a second successive game after being axed for the Newcastle match last week due to a “breach of club discipline”.
– Ramsey sees red –
The on-loan Manchester City winger, who has been criticised for his off-field behaviour for much of his colourful career, reportedly skipped training prior to the League Cup clash.
Everton said he was “not match fit” for the rematch with the Magpies, but his team coped just fine without him.
Newcastle made a lively start and went close when Harvey Barnes fired just wide before Joelinton was narrowly off target from 25 yards.
But chances were at a premium for both sides in a scrappy first half more notable for perspiration than inspiration.
Everton’s opener four minutes after half-time was in keeping with the grimy fare that preceded it.
Newcastle’s dismal marking let in Tyrique George for a shot that drew a weak save from Lukas Hornicek.
Hornicek could only push it straight into the path of Barry for a simple tap-in that survived a lengthy VAR check for offside.
It was a chance so easy that even the notoriously erratic Barry couldn’t fail to hit the target, although Newcastle were aggrieved by the VAR decision to let it stand.
Fabian Schar wasted a good opportunity to equalise when he blazed wide.
And Jaissle’s men came within a whisker of levelling through Anthony Elanga, whose close-range shot clipped the post and rolled along the goalline before Everton scrambled it clear.
Summing up their inconsistent display, it took 86 minutes for Newcastle to finally register a shot on target and even then Yoane Wissa’s effort was routine for Pickford.
Wissa did manage to force a better save from Pickford in stoppage time.
But Ramsey saw red for two bookings in the space of 60 seconds to complete Newcastle’s misery.

items.content:
By Edwin Philip, Lafia
Property worth N1.3 billion has been saved from destruction by fire in Nasarawa State, while assets valued at N2.1 billion were exposed to fire hazards.
The incidents resulted in estimated property losses of N800 million and one recorded death.
However, fire crews successfully rescued eight victims from life-threatening situations during the period. These figures were recorded across approximately 97 emergency calls received from January to date.
This was revealed by the Nasarawa State Controller of Federal Fire Service (FFS) Commander of Fire, Eno Kelechi Nwachukwu, during the flag off ceremony of the 2026 National Fire Week Awareness Campaign, which took place on Monday at the Federal Secretariat Lafia, the Nasarawa State capital.
In her opening speech, Nwachukwu reaffirms Fire Service commitment to maintaining rapid response capabilities, while urging residents, business owners, and market associations to prioritize fire safety precautions and report emergencies immediately to minimize casualties and property damage.
She said ” Fire safety is not the responsibility of the Federal Fire Service alone, It is a collective responsibility that requires the active participation of government, private organizations, institutions, families, community leaders, and every individual”.
Delivering this year’s address under the theme “Building a Fire Resilient Nigeria: One Community at a time, the State Controller of Federal Fire Service, highlighted the critical need to shift from reactive emergency responses to proactive, community-driven prevention strategies.
Defining the vision of a fire-resilient nation, the State Controller described it as a state where families, schools, businesses, and industrial centers possess the awareness, capacity, and infrastructure needed to prevent disasters, respond effectively, and recover swiftly when emergencies occur.
​
The Fire Service chief warned against negligence, noting that fire disasters do not discriminate between government establishments, private residences, commercial markets, or places of worship.
​To mitigate risks, the Federal Fire Service announced an intensified public education drive focusing on common household and commercial hazards.
” Key priorities include educating community members on Safe handling and storage of Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG/cooking gas, ​prevention of illegal and improper electrical connection​Curbing the indiscriminate burning of refuse​Proper storage of petroleum products and combustible materials
​She stressed that the nation’s overall security and economic stability begin at the local level, urging residence of the State to embrace safety standards in their daily activities to protect years of hard work, investments, and human lives.
Addressing participants at the event, the Head of Civil Service in Nasarawa, Abigail Waya Esq. represented by the Permanent service in her office, Mrs Belinda Oyigbenu Atinuke, called for a robust collaboration between the Federal Fire Service and their
Nasarawa State counterpart, in intelligence, knowledge sharing and quick mitigation of fire disasters and other rescue operations.
“And for the states, not long ago, a number of officers were employed to do the same thing that you are doing, with your own collaboration, you will help us avert disaster” she said.
She however urged residents of the State to prioritise safety by ensuring that they switch off their power sources and appliances when not in use, promptly report fire incidents before they escalate.
Commending the firemen and women, she said: when you hear fire, it means there’s disaster, so you see people running here and there, running up and down, to make sure that that disaster is arrested, here we have these people in red, the staff of FFS”
“I give you big kudos, I pray that in the course of your duty, you will not be eaten up by fire, keep up the good work and keep doing it” she added.
In his keynote address, Dr. Abubakar Alhasan of the Department of Geography and Environmental Management, Federal University of Lafia, gave technical and simple approach in preventing and managing fire disaster.
“70 percent of fire of incidents are as a result of electricity, as a result of our surges, overload of the cables, extensions is homes, our residential houses see most of these fires and as well as the markets are the places where deaths occur” .
​
“See in 2025 reports, residential houses recorded the highest premise in which all these fire incidents were recorded, about 693 houses were affected, markets 190 and other places were 105, the markets record the highest number of deaths. about 39 were recorded,”he said.
According to him, illegal storage of petroleum products, the cigarettes and the bush burning, gas related fires, accident and vehicular incidents, account for several fire outbreaks.
He cautioned against engaging unqualified electricians in house wirings, replace damaged cables, storing fuel and safely, should be stored in residential buildings.
“So it’s the federal fire service that is the hub of all the stakeholders because they are in charge to equip, train, and also coordinate the community fire safety committees”
​”The markets and trade associations, the schools and universities, our faith and traditional leaders, also the State fire services, the media, and also the non-governmental organizations for collaborations” he added.
The event featured plenary sessions of sharing of experiences about fire disasters, success stories and the way forward.
Participants in the event were drawn from security outfits, educational institutions, hospitality sector, market men and women, traditional and religious leaders as well as the media.
The event also featured award presentation to individuals and groups on their efforts towards managing fire disasters and supporting the Federal Fire Service.

items.author: efosataiwo@vanguardngr.com
items.content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has pledged to strengthen electoral accessibility for persons with disabilities (PwDs) ahead of the 2027 general elections.
The commission said it would provide assistive materials, improve polling unit accessibility and train electoral officials to ensure inclusive participation.
Gombe State Resident Electoral Commissioner, Alhaji Umar Gajiram, gave the assurance on Monday during a sensitisation workshop in Gombe.
Gajiram, represented by the Administrative Secretary, Hajiya Fadimatu Bakari, said every Nigerian deserved equal opportunities to participate in democratic processes.
He stressed that disability should never prevent eligible citizens from exercising their constitutional voting rights.
According to him, INEC recognises that persons with disabilities have equal rights and that their votes, voices and contributions matter.
He said the commission was implementing measures to remove barriers preventing PwDs from participating fully in elections.
These include providing assistive materials, ensuring accessible polling units, training electoral officials and collaborating with disability organisations.
Gajiram stressed that disability inclusion must be integrated into every electoral activity rather than treated as an additional responsibility.
“Disability inclusion should not be treated as an additional responsibility but as an important part of our work,” he said.
He urged Disability Desk Officers (DDOs) to maintain regular engagement with PwDs and communicate their challenges to the commission.
He also encouraged participants to speak openly about their experiences and recommend improvements to electoral arrangements.
“As we look forward to 2027, our goal is simple: to ensure that no eligible Nigerian is left out of the electoral process because of disability,” he said.
He said INEC wanted wheelchair users to access polling units easily and visually impaired voters to receive appropriate assistance.
Similarly, he said, persons with hearing impairments should have access to election information, enabling every eligible voter to participate with dignity and confidence.
Also speaking, Gombe State Chairman of the Joint National Association of Persons with Disabilities (JONAPwD), Mallam Gambo Ahmad, commended INEC for organising the workshop.
He described the arrangements as exceptional compared with previous engagements, particularly the provision of accessible communication materials.
Ahmad specifically appreciated INEC for providing Braille materials for visually impaired participants and an interpreter for effective communication.
He said the arrangements ensured participants could understand the discussions and contribute meaningfully to the proceedings.
He identified intellectual disabilities, hearing impairments, physical disabilities, visual impairments, spinal cord injuries and leprosy-related disabilities among conditions represented in Gombe.
Others, he said, included persons with albinism, adding that people with different disabilities remained members of the same community.
“We are all part of this community, although we face different challenges,” Ahmad said.
He, however, urged INEC to ensure adequate representation of persons with disabilities among its temporary electoral personnel during the elections.
Ahmad said many PwDs possessed the necessary qualifications and capacity to serve in different electoral positions.
“Some can serve as electoral officers, while others can perform different supporting roles,” he said.
He argued that employing PwDs in election administration would encourage greater participation and strengthen public confidence.
According to him, seeing persons with disabilities administering elections would demonstrate INEC’s commitment to genuine inclusion.
Ahmad urged the commission to sustain and strengthen its disability inclusion initiatives beyond the 2027 general elections.
Also, the Gombe State Director of the National Orientation Agency (NOA), Hajiya Maimuna Abubakar, commended INEC for organising the workshop.
She described the initiative as an important step towards promoting justice and equal opportunities for persons with disabilities.
Abubakar maintained that electoral participation was a fundamental right, not a privilege.
She said every eligible Nigerian, including persons with disabilities, had the right to register, vote and participate in choosing national leaders.
She encouraged PwDs not to isolate themselves because of their conditions but to register and participate actively in elections.
The NOA director also pledged the agency’s readiness to collaborate with INEC in providing necessary information and support.
She said the collaboration would help ensure persons with disabilities were adequately informed and equipped to participate in the electoral process.

Arole made the appeal in a video shared on Instagram on Monday, describing the late singer as a great talent whose death had left friends and colleagues grieving.
“I want to speak on behalf of Toluwanisings’ demise, and this is what God asked me to say. We’ve lost a great guy, a great gift to a generation. Even we, his friends and colleagues, have not recovered. For some of us, he is so close to us, and his death is really painful. A big elephant has gone,” he said.
He also criticised people he accused of using the controversy to attract attention on social media, saying public discussion should instead focus on Toluwanisings’ wife and children.
“It’s saddening and sad that a lot of people are now beginning to want to start to use it as a means for social media traction. You are m***. I have a right to say it. A young man had died in almost his prime, and the discussion is not even about the wife left behind and two kids? No. What you want to start doing is unlicensed, ungoverned, unnecessary talk, interviews and nonsense. A lot of people speaking about him this way never spoke about him while he was alive, about his music, please, please,” Arole said.
He urged those involved to let the burial arrangements proceed and allow the singer to be laid to rest with dignity.
“This is why it is a burden in my spirit, and I have to speak, and this is what the Lord is laying in my heart. The Bible says: Let the dead bury their dead. Whatever process, anything that needs to be done within that corner, let it be done. Let the young man be given a befitting burial,” he said.
View this post on Instagram
Woli Arole added that the burial dispute could not erase the singer’s musical legacy and called on the public to support his family and preserve his work through his children.
“Nobody can ruin his legacy; he lived a good life, please. He sang songs that are eternal; his songs rang in our hearts. Whichever way he is buried, Toluwanisings is in our hearts forever; his sound is forever. So, please, I want to beg us in the name of Jesus, you should focus our energy on what is left: how his legacy will be preserved in his children and the wife,” he said.
He concluded: “God bless Toluwanisings’ legacy, God bless his wife and his children, let the noise and unnecessary nonsense die down in the name of Jesus.”
Toluwanisings’ family announced that the singer died in the early hours of October 14, 2026, but did not disclose the cause of death.
The singer’s burial arrangements have drawn public attention following disagreements over where he should be laid to rest.
Vanguard previously reported that a family representative rejected a cemetery burial and threatened to exhume the singer’s remains if he were buried there. His paternal grandmother also said she opposed a cemetery burial and wanted him buried at his home.

items.content:
Health tech startup Clinics On Cloud has raised ₹120 Cr (around $12.5 Mn) in its Series A funding round from Model42, the medtech-focused investment arm of UAE-based backer Enlightened Minds Investments.
The Pune-based startup raised the fresh funds at a valuation of ₹600 Cr ($63.3 Mn)
In a statement, the startup said that it plans to utilise the fresh capital to bolster its AI-led healthcare capabilities, expand research and development (R&D), and accelerate the growth of its micro-clinic ecosystem.
A chunk of the funding will also be used to strengthen its manufacturing capacity, scale strategic partnerships with healthcare providers and expand global footprint.
“For eight years, we have built Clinics On Cloud with a simple belief that quality healthcare should never depend on someone’s pincode. This investment gives us the opportunity to take that vision global…,” said Clinics On Cloud cofounder and CEO Abhay Agarwal.
Founded in 2018 by Abhay and Manashrri Agarwal, Clinics On Cloud manufactures and deploys AI-powered “health ATMs”, portable box clinics and mobile medical units that deliver point-of-care preventive health checkups and telemedicine consultations. These solutions enable hospitals and government agencies to set up temporary micro-clinics.
It claims to have so far seen more than 3,500 deployments across 200 cities in India and seven other countries. Having screened more than 1.2 Cr patients so far, the startup claims to cater to the Indian Army, Navy and the Border Security Force (BSF).
The Pune-based startup now plans to position UAE as its global expansion hub, with an eye on exploring new markets across Africa, the US and Southeast Asia.
The fundraise comes amid growing investor interest in the healthtech sector, which is seeing renewed funding activity on the back of AI adoption. In September this year, smart ring maker Ultrahuman raised $70 Mn to fuel its integrated healthtech playbook.
In July, another AI-powered healthtech startup CARPL.ai also bagged $10 Mn in its Series A funding round led by International Finance Corporation (IFC). In the same month, actor Kunal Kapoor banded together with crowdfunding platform Ketto’s cofounders Varun Sheth and Zaheer Adenwala to launch healthtech startup MetaGO.
At the heart of all this is the homegrown healthtech market, which is projected to become a $37 Bn opportunity by 2030.
