items.author: AFP
items.content:
In a sprawling palace in western India, the "queen" or Maharani of Baroda welcomes guests with fragrant rose petals, presenting torchlit dances of Hindu myths.
Dressed in glittering finery, Radhikaraje Gaekwad is a queen in name only, a modern businesswoman presiding over a world her ancestors once ruled.
"The key has been that we have adapted," 48-year-old Gaekwad told AFP in her vast Lakshmi Vilas Palace, describing how India's former royals have found new roles, from cultural ambassadors to politics.
"My work has always been to try and bring in change for what I feel would be for the betterment of society," said Gaekwad, who works to preserve art accumulated by generations of rulers. "A glimpse of what was left behind... can bring that sense of identity and pride back in their roots, and help them in the future."
Under British rule, more than 565 princely states enjoyed nominal autonomy across roughly 40% of the land. Baroda, today Vadodara in Gujarat state, was among the most powerful.
The maharajas joined democratic India after independence in 1947 and became ordinary citizens, but their enduring cultural influence is something politicians of all parties seek to harness.
"This cultural capital has been banked on by the descendants of the erstwhile maharajas to get into active politics," said historian Manu S Pillai.
Quest for heroes
Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Hindu-nationalist government has sought to draw on a royal past outside foreign control to reinforce its national narrative. Modi's party includes elected lawmakers such as Communications Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia, of the Gwalior dynasty, and Rajasthan Deputy Chief Minister Diya Kumari, of Jaipur's royal family.
"There is a quest for heroes," Pillai added. "Nationalist history has become very popular and... the Hindu right is very keen to tap into cultural icons."
Modi last year laid the foundation stone for a $39 million "Museum of Royal Kingdoms" celebrating their history. The site near Vadodara lies beside the world's tallest statue, a 182-metre monument to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, whom Modi honoured with its inauguration in 2018 for his role in bringing princely states into India.
Visitors were divided over the role of royals today. "I hold the royal families in high regard," said Arti Shukla, visiting from Vadodara. Nishant Kulkarni, a bank worker from Mumbai, was more cynical. "I only came to see this massive statue," he said. "The royal families certainly played a role in the past, but there is no real need for their services anymore."
Storytellers
Beyond politics, many maharajahs see themselves as stewards of tradition, said Siddhaant Mohta, director of Sopaan, which organises cultural exhibitions in royal sites—including in Vadodara's palace. "The royal families are custodians of heritage," Mohta said, pointing to work to overhaul Vadodara's Maharaja Fateh Singh Museum, which houses more than 30 works by celebrated 19th-century painter Raja Ravi Varma.
A Varma work fetched $17.9 million at auction in Mumbai in April, an Indian record.
Deborah Swallow, former director of London's Courtauld Institute of Art, is advising on the project, praising the legacy of royal patronage that helped fund it. "That tradition is being beautifully followed today," she said.
Others, such as Raseshwari Rajya Laxmi, Maharani of Jaisalmer, said their titles open doors—explaining how her family has helped twin the historic walled city with Carcassonne in France. "We are sharing ideas on promoting and preserving their culture," she said.
For Gaekwad, her work includes social entrepreneurship, promoting social inclusion through initiatives such as a transgender-run cafe, as well as supporting traditional crafts and customs.
Her father, Ranjitsinh Jhala, 87, took a different path. Born into Wankaner's ruling family in 1939, before India's princes surrendered their powers, he was raised in a world where tiger hunting was a royal passion.
But he became a civil servant, drafted India's wildlife protection law, and helped turn vast tracts of princely hunting grounds into national parks. "If that was what the princes left behind, it compensates far more than what they shot," he said.
Akshita Bhanj Deo, in her 30s, daughter of the 47th ruler of Odisha's Bhanja dynasty, represents a younger generation seeking modern meaning in historic titles. She has turned her palace into a hotel, and runs a foundation to support marginalised groups.
"A lot of erstwhile royal families see themselves in a space where they can actually make a sense of community happen," she said. "We're just the bards and storytellers between the past and future."

items.author: Mumini AbdulKareem, Ilorin
items.content:
The Kwara State Police Command has rescued one of four family members abducted by suspected kidnappers in Abangbe Dilu community, Ilorin East Local Government Area of the state.
Three other victims are still in captivity in the kidnappers’ den.
The victims were identified as Hajia Mansurat Musa, her son, Ramadan Musa, Semiu Ahmed and Sofia Ahmed.
The Magaji of Abangbe Dilu community, Ilorin East, Alhaji Jamiu Akanni, appealed to the Federal Government, the Kwara State Government and security agencies to intensify efforts to secure the release of the remaining victims.
You&#8217;ve abandoned retired police officers, Atiku tells Tinubu
Police Trail Kidnappers Of Father, Son Abducted On Kwara Farm
In an appeal on behalf of the community, Akanni said the abduction had heightened fear among residents, relatives and other members of the community, who were anxiously awaiting the safe return of the victims.
He urged security agencies to deploy the necessary resources, pursue credible leads and strengthen surveillance to ensure the remaining abductees were rescued.
The community also called on Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq to work with federal security agencies, local authorities and community leaders to coordinate efforts towards securing their release.
It further appealed for improved security measures and sustained operations to prevent further abductions and restore confidence among residents.
The community urged members of the public with credible information that could assist the rescue operation to report to the appropriate security authorities.
Confirming the incident to Daily Trust on Monday, the state Commissioner of Police, Adekimi Ojo, said one of the victims had been rescued, while the remaining three were still being held by the kidnappers.
He, however, said security operatives were closing in on the abductors and would sustain the operation until all the victims were released.
“It happened a few days ago. We are closing in on the kidnappers and we will continue until we get the victims released,” Ojo said.

items.author: Arsalan Khattak

Lahore traffic police have started legal proceedings against motorists who have failed to pay their digital traffic challans and will issue court summons to those who ignore payment notices for 10 days.
Officials said motorists who fail to clear their outstanding fines despite receiving notices will face legal action. Traffic wardens are also assisting judicial authorities at courts across Lahore to facilitate the recovery of unpaid fines.
Under the existing procedure, traffic fines double if motorists fail to pay within 10 days. Officials then forward unpaid challans to the courts for further legal proceedings. The increased penalties have discouraged several motorists from retrieving their seized documents from the courts.
The number of pending digital challans and documents seized over non-payment has approached 800,000, highlighting the scale of outstanding traffic violations in Lahore. Officials said some motorists have chosen to obtain duplicate identity cards and driving licenses rather than pay the increased fines and recover their original documents.
Lahore traffic police have urged motorists to clear their outstanding e-challans and collect their seized documents by following the prescribed legal procedure. The legal action aims to recover unpaid traffic fines and improve compliance with Lahore’s digital traffic enforcement system.

items.author: Team Inc42
items.content:
Fireside Ventures’ cofounder and partner Vinay Singh is stepping down from the investment firm after a nearly decade-long stint.
In a statement, the venture capital (VC) firm said that Singh would “transition out of the firm”. The consumer-focused fund has so far not named his successor.
On his future course of action, Singh said that he now plans to explore the “frontiers of agentic commerce and its implications for the future of consumption”.
“… As AI reshapes commerce faster than most of us expected, I want to spend more time exploring the frontiers of agentic commerce and its implications for the future of consumption. I am excited for this next chapter, and deeply grateful to the Fireside family, and to every founder and LP (limited partner) who trusted us on this journey,” said Singh.
An alumnus of IIM Bangalore, Singh counts nearly two decades of experience under his belt. He previously worked at companies like Hindustan Unilever and Bankbazaar. He earlier also cofounded car servicing platform Stepni, which was later acquired by Quikr.
He eventually cofounded Fireside Ventures alongside Kanwaljit Singh, Kannan Sitaram and Dipanjan Basu in 2017. Over the past decade, the VC firm has emerged as one of India’s biggest consumer-focused venture funds and counts more than 65 startups in its portfolio.
It currently claims to oversee more than $650 Mn in assets under management across four funds. The VC firm last closed its fourth fund at about $253 Mn in December last year. The investment firm currently claims to be helmed by a team of 12 principals and vice presidents.
The development comes as a host of seasoned fund managers depart major VC firms to set up their own funds. Earlier this year, Ashish Agrawal, Ishaan Mittal and Tejeshwi Sharma quit Peak XV Partners to establish their own fund, Mettle Capital.
Private equity (PE) firm L Catterton’s partner and co-head of India investments, Anjana Sasidharan, also stepped down from the company in March this year to set up Asthrum Capital. Another former Peak XV trio, comprising Shailesh Lakhani, Harshjit Sethi and Mayank Porwal, has launched Ambition Capital and is looking to raise $250 Mn for the maiden fund.

items.author: Press Release
items.content:
Fatima Fertilizer celebrated farmers’ outstanding achievements at the Sarsabz Ki Jeet Wheat Yield Competition Prize Distribution Ceremony. Farmers using Sarsabz Nitrophos and Calcium Ammonium Nitrate (CAN) secured the top three positions at the provincial level and 119 out of 120 district-level positions in the Punjab Wheat Yield Competition 2025–26, announced by the Government of Punjab.
Federal Minister for National Food Security & Research, Mr. Rana Tanveer Hussain, addressed the ceremony virtually. The event was also attended by Additional Chief Secretary (ACS), Punjab, Mr. Iftikhar Ali Sahoo ; Secretary Agriculture, Punjab, Mr. Shakeel Ahmad Mian and President, Pakistan Kissan Ittehad, Mr. Khalid Khokhar among other dignitaries.
Sarsabz farmers secured first position in 39 out of 40 districts and claimed all three provincial positions. Mr. Sajjad Hussain from Muzaffargarh secured first provincial position with a yield of 69 maunds and 39.4 kilograms per acre, followed by Mr. Shafiq Ahmed from Attock with 69 maunds and 39.1 kilograms per acre. Mr. Muhammad Asghar from Rahim Yar Khan secured third position with 69 maunds and 24.1 kilograms per acre.
As part of the prize distribution, three tractors were awarded to the provincial winners. At the district level, Honda CD 70 motorcycles and LED TVs were presented to all district level positions.
Federal Minister for National Food Security & Research, Mr. Rana Tanveer Hussain, addressed the ceremony virtually and said: “I congratulate Fatima Fertilizer and all the farmers using Sarsabz fertilisers on securing all three provincial titles and 119 out of 120 district-level positions in the Punjab Wheat Yield Competition. This remarkable achievement is a source of pride for Pakistan. Increasing wheat production and improving crop yields are essential for strengthening Pakistan’s food security.
The government is committed to ensuring the procurement of every grain of wheat in coordination with provincial governments. We are also introducing initiatives to improve farmers’ access to quality seeds, modern technology and agricultural financing. I appreciate Fatima Fertilizer’s efforts in promoting balanced fertiliser use and providing farmers with modern agricultural knowledge and advisory services. The government, private sector, research institutions and farmers must work together to transform agricultural productivity and achieve national food security.”
Additional Chief Secretary (ACS) Punjab, Mr. Iftikhar Ali Sahoo said that farmers are the backbone of Pakistan’s economy and food security, adding that the government is committed to supporting them through farmer-friendly policies and timely agricultural initiatives. He appreciated Fatima Fertilizer for recognising Punjab’s leading wheat growers and encouraging excellence in agriculture. He said the announced wheat support price of Rs 4,500 per maund, alongside Rs 150 billion in interest-free loans extended to one million farmers through the Kissan Card since October 15, would help farmers access quality seeds and fertilisers on time and strengthen wheat production.
Speaking at the event, Director Marketing and Sales at Fatima Fertilizer, Ms. Rabel Sadozai said, “Last year (2024-25), Sarsabz users also claimed all three provincial positions and 97 of 120 district positions. This year’s results reflect an improvement on last year and highlight the potential to improve wheat produce through balanced crop nutrition and agronomic guidance. Through Sarsabz, we encourage informed farming practices that help farmers make every acre count, strengthen their livelihoods and contribute to Pakistan’s food security.”
The results also highlight the potential to achieve nearly two acres’ worth of national wheat yield from a single acre. While successful Sarsabz farmers recorded yields of approximately 69-70 maunds per acre, the indicative national average stood at around 33 maunds per acre, thus doubling their yield. Fatima Fertilizer supports farmers through agricultural advisory services and soil testing facilities, helping them make informed decisions about their land’s nutritional requirements.”
Through its Sarsabz range, including Nitrophos and CAN, Fatima Fertilizer continues to promote balanced crop nutrition and improved farming practices to help farmers increase productivity and contribute to the country’s food security.

items.author: Abdul Rahman
items.content:
Importers and exporters could soon pay customs duties, taxes and other trade charges through a pre-funded digital wallet, as Pakistan Single Window (PSW) plans a new Unified Payment System (UPS) for cross-border trade payments.
The wallet will be run by a licensed bank or fintech company under a structure permitted by the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP), using its existing infrastructure rather than building a new system.
How the Wallet Will Work
Traders will be able to keep reusable balances and top them up through inter-bank fund transfers (IBFT), Raast, banking apps and portals, or over-the-counter deposits. They can also withdraw funds remotely.
The wallet will settle payments against payment advice generated within the PSW ecosystem. This covers the PSW platform, Maritime Single Window and Port Community System, Air Community System, Customs Clearance System and other PSW-linked services.
The service provider will handle fund custody, balances, top-ups, withdrawals, refunds, reversals and settlement, along with customer due diligence and anti-money laundering checks.
PSW itself will not hold, intermediate or settle customer funds. The wallet will connect to PSW only through the UPS, and PSW will be able to add more payment providers later without major changes to the system.
What This Means for Traders
At present, trade payments within PSW go through Pre-Deposit (PD) accounts and bank or payment-gateway-based mechanisms. The wallet will be an extra option alongside these, not a replacement, and existing PD accounts will not be migrated.
For businesses, the main gains are convenience and visibility. They can park funds in advance, pay several charges from one balance, and track each transaction, its settlement and reconciliation, which should make trade payments faster and more transparent.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
The non-energy and non-food inflation eased for the second consecutive month to 7.5% in October, putting a question mark over the central bank's assumption that increasing energy and food prices may "seep into core inflation", which was used to raise its policy rate.
With the slowing pace, the difference between core inflation and the policy rate has substantially widened to 4.5% for the benefit of commercial banks, but at the expense of borrowers, mainly the finance ministry.
Pakistan Bureau of Statistics (PBS) reported on Monday that the urban core inflation rate, calculated after excluding volatile energy and food prices, slowed down to 7.8% and rural inflation further fell to 7.1% in October. It was the second straight month when core inflation eased after peaking at 8.8% in August.
Core inflation gauges the underlying inflationary pressures without taking into account the highly volatile energy and food prices. The indicator was used as a base by the State Bank to increase the policy rate to 12% last week.
"There is a risk that elevated food and energy inflation may further increase inflation expectations, which may seep into core inflation going forward," said the monetary policy statement issued by the central bank after the policy rate decision.
The central bank noted that re-escalation in the Middle East conflict and domestic wheat supply frictions were the two major factors keeping inflation at elevated levels and their expected continuation over the next few months had worsened the inflation outlook.
It added that elevated prices of energy and wheat and its allied products contributed significantly to the headline inflation in September, which turned out to be higher than the Monetary Policy Committee's (MPC) expectation.
However, according to the PBS, the headline inflation slowed down to 9.6% last month, which was largely in line with the finance ministry's forecast for the month.
The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has raised Pakistan's inflation forecast to 9.9% for the current fiscal year, which is above the official target of 8.2% and is said to be a reason for the recent rate hike. The Planning Commission of Pakistan has projected a 7.5% inflation rate, even lower than the target.
According to the PBS, inflation went down both in urban and rural areas, reaching 9.5% in urban areas and 9.8% in rural areas. Food inflation slowed down from 8.1% to 7.8% in urban areas while it dropped to 7.1% in rural areas. The energy group saw a southbound movement in both urban and rural areas. The pace decelerated to 10.6% in urban areas and 12.1% in rural areas.
During review talks last month, the IMF asked Pakistan to adjust both exchange rate and interest rate policies to tame inflation and keep the current account deficit under check.
However, the cost of housing, water, electricity, gas and fuel remained the main concern in addition to transportation charges, according to the official bulletin.
PBS reported that petrol price was 42% higher in October compared to a year ago. Within one month, there was a 3% increase in prices of petrol, which was a steep rise given the overall high rates. The per-litre petrol cost was Rs379 on Friday last week and the price was Rs402 for high-speed diesel, which was keeping transport charges elevated.
The cost of transport services went up 27% last month compared to a year ago, according to the PBS. The national data collecting agency stated that electricity tariffs rose 23% in October. The high cost of electricity is already driving consumers away from the national power grid. Motor vehicle taxes jumped 39% over a year ago, contributing to the increase in expenses.
PBS said that onion prices were 82% higher year-on-year in October followed by a 39% increase in wheat prices. Owing to serious wheat management issues, the government is already in the process of importing 765,000 tonnes of wheat. Meanwhile, wheat flour prices surged 35% compared to a year ago, according to the PBS.
But prices of tomatoes, potatoes, sugar, eggs and pulses were lower in the range of 55% to 10% last month. The closure of border with Afghanistan and the subsequent suspension of trade have helped keep prices low for these commodities, which are either exported or smuggled, but contributed to an increase in prices of fruits that were imported from the western neighbour.

items.author: ZAFAR BHUTTA
items.content:
The government is set to announce an incentive package to tap the full potential of copper and gold reserves, estimated at $8 trillion, in the National Mineral Policy – 2026. A model of the package, drawn up by Wood Mackenzie, has incorporated reduced withholding tax rates on local goods and services – 4% for local goods and 8% for local services – together with deferral until mine production.
The incentive package had been submitted to the Finance Division during the current year's budget but the inability to introduce a comprehensive programme at that time reflects major challenges in the way of finalising an investment-oriented National Mineral Policy. The government plans to offer these incentives to foreign investors during the upcoming Mineral Forum scheduled for November 12-13.
The prime minister had directed the Petroleum Division to develop and finalise the National Mineral Policy. However, sources said the policy document was ready but without a corresponding fiscal package it may not achieve the desired objectives and address the key challenges facing the mineral sector.
The Finance Division is the authority that can approve these fiscal packages, therefore the Petroleum Division has requested it to accord due importance and priority to the proposals and facilitate their early approval. These measures may be announced at the Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum (PMIF).
Sources told The Express Tribune that there was a proposal to grant a 30-year exemption from general sales tax (GST) on the import and local purchase and supply of goods and services for mining projects during the exploration and development phase until the commencement of commercial production.
Another proposal says the exemption may continue after the commencement of production, particularly considering the fact that a substantial proportion of mineral production is export-oriented and input sales tax may remain unadjusted. Furthermore, it is proposed that the withholding tax applicable to contractors and suppliers for mining projects may be reduced during the exploration and development phase and payment/deposit of such taxes may be deferred until the commencement of commercial production.
The government has proposed that import duties on capital goods and project-related equipment for mining companies may be exempted during the exploration, development and construction phases. The Wood Mackenzie model treats customs/import duty exemption as an important component of the fiscal package.
A major proposal is to replace the conventional corporate income tax with a 1% presumptive tax on export proceeds together with a 0.5% development surcharge, aimed at providing a simple and predictable fiscal framework while encouraging investment. The Wood Mackenzie analysis identifies corporate income tax treatment as the single largest driver of improvement in an investor's internal rate of return (IRR).
Stability of fiscal regime
The consultancy firm has proposed that appropriate fiscal stability clauses be incorporated to protect the fiscal terms applicable at the time of award of an exploration concession/agreement, broadly along the lines of the stability framework available to the oil and gas sector. Fiscal stability is particularly important for mining because project development can span several years and investment decisions are made against long-term assumptions regarding taxation and government take.
It has suggested that mining projects may be exempted from super tax for at least 30 years to improve project economics and maintain competitiveness with other mineral-producing jurisdictions. Also, the withholding tax on dividends distributed by mining projects may be exempted for 15 years from commercial production. Inter-corporate dividends within mining project structures are also proposed to be exempted to avoid tax cascading within project structures.
Exploration losses
The consultancy firm proposes that exploration losses may be carried forward perpetually for mining projects, recognising that exploration expenditure can precede commercial production by several years and may also be incurred on unsuccessful exploration programmes. Additionally, losses from failed exploration projects may be adjusted against successful mining projects within the same mining group, subject to appropriate safeguards.
It suggests that carry-forward depreciation allowance for mining projects may be allowed for 10 years after the commencement of commercial production. Apart from that, accelerated depreciation up to 100% may be permitted for mining projects.
In its model, Wood Mackenzie has highlighted a 10-year carry-forward for the depreciation allowance together with 100% accelerated depreciation, by increasing the standard depreciation rate from 15% to 30%. It proposes that the fiscal regime applicable to mining projects may, where appropriate, be aligned with the special fiscal framework available to the oil and gas sector under the Fifth Schedule of the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001, recognising similarities in terms of exploration risk, capital intensity, long gestation periods and the need for fiscal stability.

items.title: Pakistan's quiet resilience in first quarter of FY27
items.summary:

Conflict in the Middle East disrupted oil and gas supplies, energy prices climbed, and even major economies struggled to keep their balance. So how did Pakistan fare? For a country that imports most of its energy and has long battled foreign currency shortages, July to September 2026 was a serious test.
The answer may surprise you. Pakistan didn't just hold its ground; it moved forward. items.author: news.desk
items.content:
Let's be honest: the past few months have been hard on almost everyone. Conflict in the Middle East disrupted oil and gas supplies, energy prices climbed, and even major economies struggled to keep their balance. So how did Pakistan fare? For a country that imports most of its energy and has long battled foreign currency shortages, July to September 2026 was a serious test.
The answer may surprise you. Pakistan didn't just hold its ground; it moved forward. The latest economic scorecard reflects steady policy under Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's government, close coordination with the military leadership under Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, and an economic team led by Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb that kept reforms on course. Above all, it reflects the hard work of ordinary Pakistanis.
Start with the number that matters most in a crisis. The State Bank's foreign exchange reserves reached $21.5 billion, an all-time high, up 52% in a year. This safety net has kept the rupee stable, even gaining 1.5%, and keeps fuel, medicine and other essential imports flowing. Import cover has risen from 2.2 to 3.3 months, a vital breathing room in turbulent times.
Pakistan's earners didn't slow down either. Exports grew 11% to $11.2 billion, with September's goods exports the highest in 20 months. Technology stood out: IT exports rose 18% to $1.25 billion, and freelancers earned a record $550 million, up 46%. Picture a young developer in Multan or a designer in Peshawar winning clients in London and Dubai from a laptop.
Overseas Pakistanis once again showed how much home means to them. Remittances rose 14% to $10.9 billion, mainly from Saudi Arabia, the UAE, the UK and the EU, while the Roshan Digital Account has drawn $14.3 billion across nearly 976,000 accounts. Every dollar is a vote of confidence in Pakistan's future.
That confidence is spreading. Foreign direct investment rose 20% to $720 million while investors worldwide held back. All three major rating agencies have upgraded Pakistan into the 'B' category with stable outlooks, rewarding the fiscal discipline and steady engagement with lenders central to Finance Minister Aurangzeb's approach. The IMF programme is firmly on track, with a staff-level agreement reached for $1.2 billion.
Pakistanis at home are investing too. Stock market investors jumped 55% to over 656,000, and 85% of new investors are Gen-Z and Millennials. Four companies listed this quarter, raising Rs4.6 billion, roughly five times last year's total.
Pakistan's voice abroad is growing as well. On November 1, Pakistan became chair of the G-24, the bloc of developing countries founded in 1971 to coordinate positions on global finance. Finance Minister Aurangzeb, who will lead it, put it powerfully: "The future of developing economies is not peripheral to the future of the global economy. It is central to it." Pakistan will push for affordable development financing, fairer debt solutions and climate resilience. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif called it a "significant diplomatic milestone", and President Asif Ali Zardari termed it an important opportunity to represent the developing world.
What does this mean for businesses and jobs? The policy rate, which hit 22% in June 2024, now stands at 12%, and cheaper money is flowing. Loans to small and medium businesses rose 66% to Rs1.14 trillion, housing finance grew 72%, and lending to farmers and auto buyers rose roughly 31% and 34%. That means shops opening, homes built, harvests financed and jobs created.
The country is also learning to stand on its own feet. The FBR collected Rs3.1 trillion in three months, beating its target, while income tax filers jumped 45% to 5.77 million, reflecting the tax reforms and digitisation championed by the finance ministry. Government debt has fallen to 68% of GDP from 75% in FY23.
Momentum is visible on the ground too. Car sales rose 28%, cement and petroleum sales grew, and large-scale manufacturing is expanding. Privatisation of power distribution companies – Fesco, Gepco and Iesco – is advancing, drawing local and foreign interest. And when fuel prices rose, a Rs75 billion relief scheme reached more than 12 million citizens who depend on motorcycles, rickshaws and small cars.
Is the job done? Not yet. Global events have pushed up prices at home, many families still feel the squeeze, and sustaining reforms will require patience. But stronger reserves, a wider tax base, lower debt and returning investor confidence are the foundation for what people need: stronger support for low-income families, new schools, hospitals and roads, and, over time, real relief from the cost of living.
This achievement belongs to everyone who made it possible: the worker and the farmer, the young freelancer, the overseas Pakistani sending money home, and a leadership and economic team that held their nerve through a turbulent quarter.
The writer Jamella Zarif is an Islamabad-based investigative journalist.

items.author: APP
items.content:
The Ministry of Finance and the government are reviewing the possibility of tokenising Pakistan's existing Eurobond debt, Federal Minister for Finance and Revenue Senator Muhammad Aurangzeb said, as he pressed banks to adopt digital assets responsibly while keeping restrictions on their own holdings of virtual assets.
Addressing a dialogue on digital assets and the future of banking organised by the Pakistan Banks' Association and LUMS, he said financial innovation should deliver lower-cost remittances, faster business payments, accessible financing for entrepreneurs and increased productive investment.
"Pakistan needs financial innovation, and digital assets must complement the broader digital transformation," he said.
He said digital transformation must be accompanied by strong regulatory safeguards, financial stability and institutional oversight so that technological advancement did not create unnecessary risks.
He said the government had achieved macroeconomic stability and was now focused on export-led growth through economic discipline, higher exports, foreign direct investment and private-sector participation.
He also said banks needed to facilitate businesses, particularly small and medium enterprises and agriculture, through easier access to financing.
Pakistan established a statutory framework through the Virtual Assets Act 2026, assigning the Pakistan Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority responsibility for licensing and supervising virtual asset service providers.
He said the next priority was effective implementation through capable supervision and institutional coordination.
The State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) has introduced a conditional mechanism for extending banking facilities to licensed entities, subject to due diligence and segregation of client funds.
The minister said accounts opened for entities holding no-objection certificates would serve a limited purpose until licensing was complete, and that banks remained responsible for foreign exchange compliance.
He said restrictions on banks investing, trading or holding virtual assets through their own funds or customer deposits would remain.
Aurangzeb said tokenisation could improve remittance channels, including transactions linked to Roshan Digital Accounts.
Pakistan received $41.6 billion in remittances last fiscal year, and first-quarter trends suggest inflows could exceed $44 billion.

items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
Spotify is reportedly preparing to launch a new AI-powered feature that will let users create their own versions of popular songs, but it could cost an additional $4 to $5 per month.
According to a Financial Times report, the music streaming company is planning to introduce the feature in the first quarter of 2027, possibly around the Grammy Awards in February.
The service will be available as a paid add-on for Spotify Premium subscribers, allowing them to create AI-generated covers and remixes of songs from participating artists.
However, Spotify has not confirmed the final pricing or launch date.
Spotify Will Let Users Create AI Song Covers and Remixes
The upcoming tool will allow Spotify subscribers to use artificial intelligence to change how existing songs sound.
For example, users could turn a folk song into a dance track or create a version that sounds like a different artist is performing it.
Instead of creating entirely new songs, the feature will focus on modifying existing music with permission from participating artists and record labels.
Spotify is also reportedly developing a way for users to add their AI remixes to playlists.
According to the report, streams of these remixes could also count toward the original songs on Spotify’s music charts.
The company has said that artists and songwriters behind the original recordings will receive royalties from fan-made versions of their songs.
AI Remix Feature Could Cost Up to $5 Extra
Spotify is reportedly considering charging between $4 and $5 per month for the new AI tool.
This would be an additional fee on top of the regular Spotify Premium subscription.
For reference, Spotify Premium Individual currently costs $12.99 per month in the United States.
If the reported pricing is introduced, users would pay approximately $16.99 to $17.99 per month for Premium with the AI remix feature.
However, the company has not finalized the price, and the amount could change before launch.
Spotify previously considered introducing a more expensive Music Pro subscription with additional features, including AI remixing tools.
That plan did not launch as originally expected, while lossless audio was eventually added to Premium without an extra charge.
Spotify Signs Deals With Major Music Companies
Spotify has already signed agreements with several music companies to make the AI remix feature possible.
In May 2026, the company announced a licensing deal with Universal Music Group, allowing users to create AI covers and remixes of songs from participating artists.
Spotify has also reached agreements with Merlin, Kobalt, and Believe, expanding the number of artists and songs that could be supported.
However, the company is still negotiating with Sony Music and Warner Music.
Even when a record label signs an agreement, individual artists will have the option to decide whether their music can be used.
According to the report, Spotify has found it more difficult to convince some of today’s biggest artists to participate compared with older, established performers.
This means the feature may initially support only a limited selection of songs.
Expected Launch Date
Spotify is reportedly targeting the first three months of 2027 for the new AI remix service.
The company could announce the feature around the Grammy Awards in February, although this remains unconfirmed.
Spotify has declined to comment on the reported launch schedule and pricing.
If introduced, the service would give Premium subscribers a new way to interact with their favorite music while creating an additional source of income for participating artists.
For now, users will have to wait for an official announcement to find out which songs will be supported and how much the service will cost.

items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
Google is working with NASA to develop an AI-powered robot that could help astronauts handle medical emergencies during future missions to the Moon and Mars.
The robot is being designed to assist astronauts with medical tasks, move equipment, organize supplies, and perform routine maintenance.
According to Google, the experimental system has already achieved an 85% success rate in an early laboratory test involving locating and moving a medical bag.
However, the robot is still in development and is not ready to perform medical procedures independently.
Why Astronauts Could Need an AI Medical Robot
Astronauts traveling to Mars could face serious problems if someone becomes sick or injured during a mission.
Because Mars is so far from Earth, communication between astronauts and doctors on the ground could experience significant delays.
According to Google, messages sent between Earth and Mars could take up to 44 minutes for a round trip.
This means astronauts may not be able to receive immediate medical advice during an emergency.
To address this problem, Google and NASA are developing a robot that could assist crew members when medical help from Earth is delayed.
The project builds on the Crew Medical Officer Digital Assistant, an AI medical support system that Google and NASA began testing in 2025.
The earlier system was designed to help astronauts understand health problems and make medical decisions when immediate assistance from Earth is unavailable.
The new project aims to add physical assistance through a robot that can move around and handle equipment.
How Google’s AI Robot Would Work
The robot is being designed to follow spoken instructions from astronauts and help with different tasks inside a spacecraft.
For example, if an astronaut experiences severe back pain that could indicate kidney stones, the robot could retrieve an ultrasound machine and prepare it for use.
The astronaut responsible for medical care would then examine the results and decide what treatment is necessary.
Google says the robot could eventually help with simple medical tasks, such as checking vital signs or assisting with ultrasound examinations.
However, it would not replace human medical personnel or make treatment decisions independently.
When medical assistance is not needed, the robot could perform other duties, including moving cargo, organizing tools, securing equipment, and helping with routine maintenance.
This could allow astronauts to spend more time on scientific research and other important tasks.
AI Robot Achieves 85% Success Rate in Early Tests
Google and NASA have already started testing the technology in laboratory conditions.
During one experiment, the robot was asked to locate a medical bag and move it to another location.
The system completed the task successfully in approximately 85% of the initial tests.
Although the result shows progress, it does not mean the robot is ready to perform medical examinations or assist during serious emergencies.
Researchers are also working on improving how the robot understands its surroundings and handles objects.
NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory is adapting technology originally developed to track objects in space to help the robot navigate inside a spacecraft.
The team is also using Google DeepMind’s MuJoCo simulation software to test the robot’s movements in a virtual environment before trying them on physical hardware.
Google says researchers have tested around 15 different computing devices to identify hardware that can run the AI system efficiently without consuming too much power.
This is important because spacecraft have limited electricity and computing resources.
When Will NASA Send the Robot to Space?
Google has not announced when the AI medical robot could be sent into space.
The project is currently in its early testing stage, and the company has not confirmed that a fully working, space-ready version has been completed.
The system is being developed through a collaboration involving Google Cloud, NASA’s Human Research Program, Johnson Space Center, and the Jet Propulsion Laboratory.
Researchers still need to improve its reliability, movement, and ability to perform tasks safely around astronauts.
Google’s long-term goal is to develop a robot that can understand simple voice commands and help crew members with both medical and everyday tasks.
If successful, the technology could provide additional support to astronauts on future missions where immediate help from Earth is impossible.

items.title: Fly Jinnah’s Airbus A320neo Completes Test Flight in France
items.summary:
Fly Jinnah’s upcoming Airbus A320neo has completed its first test flight in France, bringing the aircraft closer to joining the Pakistani airline’s fleet.
The aircraft, currently operating under French registration F-WWBD, completed test flight AIB01BD on Monday, November 2. It departed from Toulouse, France, at 12:08 p.m. and returned to the same airport at 2:10 p.m.
The flight lasted two hours and two minutes, during which the aircraft reached a maximum altitude of 39,000 feet.
The aircraft is expected to receive the Pakistani registration AP-BQA before entering service with Fly Jinnah.
The addition of the A320neo would expand Fly Jinnah’s fleet as the airline continues to develop its domestic and international operations.

Google has announced that it is shutting down Jules, its AI coding assistant, as the company shifts its focus toward its Antigravity AI development platform.
The company confirmed that Jules will officially shut down on December 31, 2026, with users given until November 11 to finish their ongoing coding tasks.
After November 11, Jules will become a read-only service, meaning users can view their existing projects but will no longer be able to continue working on them through the platform.
The decision comes just over a year after Jules became publicly available in August 2025.
Why Is Google Shutting Down Jules?
Google introduced Jules as an AI assistant designed to help developers write, fix, and improve code.
Unlike traditional coding assistants that require constant interaction, Jules could work on tasks independently in the background.
Developers could connect their GitHub repositories, assign coding tasks, and allow Jules to work on them while they focused on other activities.

items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
Google has announced that it is shutting down Jules, its AI coding assistant, as the company shifts its focus toward its Antigravity AI development platform.
The company confirmed that Jules will officially shut down on December 31, 2026, with users given until November 11 to finish their ongoing coding tasks.
After November 11, Jules will become a read-only service, meaning users can view their existing projects but will no longer be able to continue working on them through the platform.
The decision comes just over a year after Jules became publicly available in August 2025.
Why Is Google Shutting Down Jules?
Google introduced Jules as an AI assistant designed to help developers write, fix, and improve code.
Unlike traditional coding assistants that require constant interaction, Jules could work on tasks independently in the background.
Developers could connect their GitHub repositories, assign coding tasks, and allow Jules to work on them while they focused on other activities.
However, Google now wants to bring its AI coding efforts together under a single platform called Antigravity.
In its official announcement, Google described Jules as an experiment that helped the company understand how AI agents could assist software developers.
The company said the experience gained from Jules is helping shape other Google products, including Antigravity.
Google has not disclosed how many people were actively using Jules or whether low usage contributed to its closure.
What Happens to Existing Jules Users?
Google has confirmed two important dates for Jules users.
The first is November 11, 2026, which is the deadline for completing ongoing coding sessions.
After that date, the platform will switch to read-only mode.
The second is December 31, 2026, when Google plans to shut down Jules completely.
To help users save their work, Google has introduced a data export process.
Users can download their account settings, connected repositories, saved information, scheduled tasks, setup instructions, and previous coding sessions.
The export also includes details such as task instructions, plans, activity logs, and code changes.
Google explained that code, branches, and pull requests already stored on GitHub will remain available there after Jules closes.
However, users should export information stored directly inside Jules before the shutdown.
Google Shifts Focus to Antigravity
Google’s decision to discontinue Jules is part of its larger effort to simplify its AI coding products.
The company is now focusing on Antigravity, an AI-powered development platform designed to help developers manage coding tasks through AI agents.
Like Jules, Antigravity aims to reduce the amount of manual work involved in software development.
However, Google has not confirmed that every Jules feature will become available in Antigravity.
It has also not announced an automatic transfer process for moving existing Jules projects and settings to the new platform.
Google faces strong competition in the AI coding market from services such as OpenAI Codex, Anthropic’s Claude Code, and GitHub Copilot.
By bringing its development efforts together under Antigravity, the company aims to build a more unified AI coding experience.
For now, Jules users have until November 11 to complete their active projects and should save their data before the service closes permanently on December 31.

items.author: Anadolu Agency
items.content:
US commentator Tucker Carlson claimed on Sunday that the Trump administration could be days away from launching a nuclear strike on Iran, alleging that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was pressuring President Donald Trump to authorise an attack on a suspected nuclear site in central Iran.
In a lengthy post on X, Carlson identified the potential target as Pickaxe Mountain, where Israeli intelligence allegedly believed Iran had resumed its nuclear enrichment program.
Carlson is a conservative political commentator and former Fox News host whose program, Tucker Carlson Tonight, aired from 2016 to 2023.
Under pressure from Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu, the Trump administration may be within days of launching a nuclear strike on Iran. The target would be Pickax Mountain in central Iran, where Israeli intelligence claims the Iranian government has restarted its…
— Tucker Carlson (@TuckerCarlson) November 2, 2026
He now hosts an independent political show on X, where he regularly comments on US foreign policy and international affairs.
Carlson claimed conventional US weapons could not penetrate the estimated 300 feet of solid granite protecting underground tunnels at the site, leaving a nuclear strike as the only military option.
Read: Trump says US will strike reported Iranian nuclear site at Pickaxe Mountain 'very heavily'
"Bibi (Netanyahu) calls Trump about it every day," Carlson quoted an unnamed informed observer as saying.
Carlson argued that Netanyahu's political survival was driving his push for further military action. He claimed Netanyahu needs Trump's intervention to secure a 61-seat majority in the Knesset following the latest election results, warning that otherwise he could lose power and face investigations and possible imprisonment.
He also alleged that Netanyahu has been pressing senior US officials, including Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth and US Central Command chief Adm Brad Cooper, to resume major combat operations.
Carlson also claimed that Secretary of State Marco Rubio and CIA Director John Ratcliffe were following Netanyahu's lead.
He further said former president Barack Obama had also opposed the Iran peace agreement being drafted in Doha.
Fears of regional escalation
Carlson said US allies in the Middle East were increasingly concerned about renewed fighting. He claimed Netanyahu secretly travelled to Abu Dhabi on September 27 to persuade the UAE to support a final attack on Iran, but Emirati officials refused.
Warning of the economic consequences, Carlson said eight months of conflict had severely affected Gulf economies, as well as global energy and fertiliser markets. He claimed 11 of the world's approximately 850 oil supertankers were badly damaged in the Strait of Hormuz in October alone.
He also warned that a nuclear explosion at Pickaxe Mountain could contaminate the Gulf and threaten the water supply of around 100 million people.
Carlson argued that a US nuclear strike could establish a dangerous precedent, potentially encouraging Russia to use nuclear weapons against Ukraine, triggering renewed nuclear tensions between India and Pakistan, and prompting North Korea to attack Seoul.
"After the first nuclear strike, World War Three is inevitable. That war would be short and final," he wrote.
BIG: Tucker Carlson says Trump may decide by Nov. 7 on a nuclear strike on Iran’s Pickaxe Mountain under Netanyahu’s pressure.
“After the first nuclear strike, World War Three is inevitable,” Carlson wrote.https://t.co/h0UMiAa1YH
— Clash Report (@clashreport) November 2, 2026
He further alleged that the Trump administration had quietly revised US nuclear doctrine since February to make the first use of so-called "battlefield nukes" easier and more likely.
Vance, Witkoff urge Trump to pursue diplomacy
Carlson said Trump could decide by November 7 whether to authorise the use of nuclear weapons, adding that Vice President JD Vance and special envoy Steve Witkoff were urging him to pursue a diplomatic agreement with Tehran.
Although acknowledging that negotiations would be difficult, Carlson said people who had spoken with Iranian decision-makers believed there was a consensus that further conflict would benefit no one and that an agreement was worth pursuing.
He concluded by warning that the consequences of a nuclear strike would extend far beyond Iran, arguing that the international public had been excluded from decisions that could threaten millions of lives.
"Now would be the time for them to speak up," Carlson wrote.
US could strike remaining Iranian nuclear sites 'within 10 minutes'
Carlson's claims follow Trump's remarks to reporters at his Mar-a-Lago estate in Florida on Saturday that one or two Iranian nuclear facilities remained potential targets and that the US could strike them within 10 minutes.
US President Donald Trump says American forces have destroyed much of Iran's naval, air defense and military capabilities, along with its nuclear infrastructure. He says one or two sites remain, including Pickaxe Mountain, and asserts that the US could destroy them in just 10… pic.twitter.com/RNI2WP5xcM
— Al Arabiya English (@AlArabiya_Eng) November 1, 2026
Trump specifically mentioned Pickaxe Mountain, saying he had military plans for the area, but did not indicate that a nuclear strike had been authorised.
Read More: What is Pickaxe Mountain, the Iranian nuclear-linked site threatened by Trump?
"You probably could look at Pickaxe Mountain, you have to take care of that. We can do that all very quickly," he added.
In an October 16 interview with Newsmax, he explicitly ruled out using nuclear weapons against Iran.
Separately, Axios reported that Trump and Netanyahu held a tense phone call on Saturday, citing Israeli and US sources. According to the report, Netanyahu is pushing for renewed military action immediately after Tuesday's US midterm elections, while Trump prefers to allow diplomatic negotiations to continue.
Netanyahu is pressing Trump to resume strikes on Iran immediately after Tuesday’s U.S. midterm elections, but Trump wants to give diplomacy more time.
The two held a tense phone call Saturday, described as “tough” by an Israeli source and “direct” by a U.S. source.
Source:… pic.twitter.com/Ux1PREksnD
— Clash Report (@clashreport) November 1, 2026
A White House official said the administration does not comment on sensitive military plans, adding that Trump is keeping all options open to prevent Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon.
Secretary of State Rubio has also said no final decision has been made on resuming strikes.
Iran, meanwhile, denies any nuclear activity at the Pickaxe Mountain complex. Its supreme leader has warned Washington and Tel Aviv against launching further attacks.

items.content:
The federal government on Monday slashed the price of petrol by Rs3.4 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs7.76 for November 3.
A press release from the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority said the new petrol price was Rs374.51 while HSD was Rs395.2.
Earlier today, the government announced that oil refineries would bear a burden of Rs15 billion per month, which would allow petrol to be sold Rs15 cheaper than it was in the global market amid the US-Israeli war on Iran.
On July 17, the government announced a new pricing mechanism under which petroleum product prices would be reviewed and notified daily, replacing the weekly pricing mechanism, as renewed tensions between the United States and Iran continued to drive volatility in global oil markets and raise concerns over fuel supplies.
On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced a special relief scheme offering Rs100 per litre off petrol for motorcycles, three-wheeler rickshaws and cars with engines up to 800cc, in an attempt to shield lower-income consumers from the impact of rising petroleum prices.
Under the proposal, an estimated 11.8 million beneficiaries would be covered. Around 10 million two-wheeler users and 800,000 three-wheeler users would be entitled to relief on 20 litres of fuel per month, translating into a maximum monthly benefit of Rs2,000 per beneficiary.
Another one million users of cars up to 800cc would receive relief on 30 litres per month, providing them with a maximum benefit of Rs3,000 each.
On Sept 17, the government reintroduced austerity and fuel conservation measures amid rising fuel prices, tightening business operating hours and restricting public events.
Under the measures, notified with immediate effect, shops, markets, shopping malls, bazaars, departmental stores, grocery stores, general stores and kiryana shops would close by 9pm throughout the week, according to a notification issued by the Cabinet Division.
Marriage halls, marquees and other commercial venues hosting festive events would close by 10pm, while restaurants, cafes, eateries, food outlets and standalone fruit and vegetable shops would be allowed to operate until 11pm. Takeaway and home delivery services would remain exempt from the timing restrictions.

The GSMA re-elected Bharti Airtel executive vice chairman Gopal Vittal as chair for its 2027-2028 board term, while Vodafone Group CEO Margherita Della Valle was named as co-deputy chair alongside MTN Group CEO Ralph Mupita.
Vittal’s tenure has been extended to December 2028, having served as chair since 2025 and been part of the GSMA board for 10 years. He is also non-executive chair of Airtel Africa and Airtel Payments Bank, as well as a non-executive director on the BT Group Board.

Mupita was re-elected as co-deputy chair, a position he has held since April last year, while Della Valle joins him in the role for the first time.
Mupita has led MTN Group as president and CEO since September 2020, having previously served as its CFO. Della Valle became Vodafone CEO in January 2023 after previously serving as its CFO.
Vittal added that the two deputy chairs’ “experience, geographical scope and insight will be a great strength as we take this agenda forward”.
The appointments follow a reshuffle last month, which saw six new companies including NTT Docomo, Axiata Group and Telstra join the GSMA’s 26-member board.

Pakistan Telecommunication Company Limited (PTCL) has announced the appointment of Amad Khan as Chief Marketing Officer (CMO), following approval by the Company’s Board of Directors.
Amad brings over two decades of experience across telecommunications, technology and digital transformation, with a career spanning Pakistan, Australia and the Middle East. His experience encompasses commercial strategy, product management, revenue growth, customer experience and large-scale technology transformation.
Since joining PTCL, Amad has held senior commercial leadership responsibilities across the company’s wireline portfolio, including Fiber, Voice, TV, OTT and IoT. He has played a pivotal role in advancing PTCL’s Fiber strategy, contributing to its position as Pakistan’s leading Fiber operator, while driving revenue growth, customer experience improvements and digital transformation initiatives.
Prior to PTCL, Amad held senior roles at Optus Australia, where he contributed to Fiber and 5G Fixed Wireless Access strategy and led product and technology transformation initiatives. His earlier career includes roles at Warid Telecom, Huawei, International Turnkey Systems and Saudi Business Machines, providing broad exposure to telecommunications operations, product innovation and technology-led business transformation.
As Chief Marketing Officer, Amad will lead PTCL’s marketing and customer growth agenda, encompassing brand strategy, product positioning, customer experience, digital engagement and go-to-market execution. His focus will be on strengthening PTCL’s market position, building stronger customer preference and supporting sustainable growth across its connectivity and digital services portfolio.
Amad holds an MBA from Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS), where he earned a place on the Dean’s Honors List, and a Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science from FAST-NUCES.
His appointment comes as PTCL continues to strengthen its position as an integrated technology and ICT company, expanding high-speed connectivity and developing innovative digital services to meet the evolving needs of customers.

Imran has been in custody since August 2023, serving a sentence in a £190 million corruption case. He also faces pending trials under the Anti-Terrorism Act in connection with protests on May 9, 2023. He and Bushra Bibi remain incarcerated in Rawalpindi's Adiala jail. They were sentenced on December 20, 2025, to 17 years in prison in the Toshakhana-II case, which pertains to allegations that the couple unlawfully retained a Bulgari jewellery set gifted by the Saudi crown prince during an official visit to Saudi Arabia.
The PTI has been consistently protesting and demanding that the authorities allow Imran's weekly meetings with his friends, relatives and legal team.
In a post on X today, Barrister Safdar said he met the PTI founder and Bushra Bibi for about 40 minutes for a meeting arranged by the jail authorities at 4:30pm.
Imran Khan’s lawyer, Barrister Salman Safdar, was finally allowed to meet with him in Adiala Jail for 40 minutes after 7 months.

According to Barrister Safdar, the meeting took place after multiple requests and marked his first meeting with Imran in seven months and with Bushra in 11 months.
“The session was insufficient to cover all cases/legal matters,” the legal counsel lamented in the social media post, adding that the two him of their health and the conditions in which they were being kept in prison.
Safdar added that both had also conveyed fresh instructions regarding certain legal matters and ongoing cases.
The lawyer did not provide further details about the specific legal instructions discussed during the meeting.

The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on September 2 directed the jail authorities to ensure meaningful human interaction, family access, exercise, reading material and other facilities for Imran and his wife, Bushra.
The court held that lawful incarceration did not authorise the avoidable deprivation of human dignity.
In August, the Supreme Court ordered that Imran be shifted to Shifa International Hospital for treatment and directed the government to arrange weekly meetings between him and his family.
On June 18, the IHC had directed Islamabad's advocate general to ensure that a meeting was arranged within seven days between Imran, Bushra and their legal counsel to facilitate the completion of legal formalities and the prosecution of appeals against their conviction in the £190 million reference case.
Barrister Safdar last held a meeting on April 9 with Imran for legal consultation regarding the £190m case.
Read: Imran in good health, high spirits: lawyer
He stated that Adiala jail authorities had facilitated his meeting in compliance with IHC orders, adding that the meeting lasted 60 minutes.
The SC had previously ordered the formation of a medical team to examine Imran's eye after Barrister Safdar's report quoted the PTI founder as stating that "only 15%" vision remained in his right eye. The court also directed that both the medical examination and telephonic contact with his children be completed before February 16.

Further details about the identity of the perpetrators and the whereabouts of the kidnapped workers were not immediately available.
In a separate incident, two members of a polio vaccination team were abducted by armed men in the Azam Warsak area of Lower South Waziristan. However, both vaccinators were later released.
Sources said the suspects were affiliated with the proscribed Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan.

A day earlier, the National Emergency Operations Centre (NEOC) for Polio Eradication confirmed Pakistan's seventh polio case of the year, reported from K-P. The infected child was a 13-month-old girl belonging to Jan Baz Union Council in Bara tehsil, the NEOC said.
It was the second polio case reported from Khyber district this year.
Of the seven cases reported across the country so far this year, six have emerged from K-P and one from Sindh, according to the NEOC.

items.title: New cyberattack on supermarket fridges sweeps across Europe
items.summary:
A hacking attack on European supermarkets spread across the continent on Monday, hitting fridges and ​freezers from Sweden to Belgium and forcing stores to throw away food in an incident that echoed a similar attack in France last month.
The attack, which raised temperatures in refrigerator and ‌freezer units at dozens of stores, hit supermarket groups Ahold Delhaize and Colruyt in Belgium and Luxembourg, as well as Swedish grocers ICA and Coop. Furniture-to-meatballs retailer IKEA also saw at least one store affected.
"Everything is destroyed," Engla Ingwall, sales manager at an ICA franchise store in Stockholm, told Reuters during a visit to the store on Monday, adding the attack occurred at 2 am (0100 GMT) but was only noticed hours later.
Fridges and freezers at supermarkets in Belgium, Sweden, Luxembourg and Ireland warmed overnight, about three weeks after France.

A hacking attack on European supermarkets spread across the continent on Monday, hitting fridges and ​freezers from Sweden to Belgium and forcing stores to throw away food in an incident that echoed a similar attack in France last month.
The attack, which raised temperatures in refrigerator and ‌freezer units at dozens of stores, hit supermarket groups Ahold Delhaize and Colruyt in Belgium and Luxembourg, as well as Swedish grocers ICA and Coop. Furniture-to-meatballs retailer IKEA also saw at least one store affected.
"Everything is destroyed," Engla Ingwall, sales manager at an ICA franchise store in Stockholm, told Reuters during a visit to the store on Monday, adding the attack occurred at 2 am (0100 GMT) but was only noticed hours later.
Fridges and freezers at supermarkets in Belgium, Sweden, Luxembourg and Ireland warmed overnight, about three weeks after France.
They were hacked.https://t.co/d3QpzqYU41
— Clash Report (@clashreport) November 2, 2026
"There has been a cyberattack and all our freezers reached 50 degrees (Celsius)."
A spokesperson for privately held ICA said the company ​was aware that a "limited number of stores were affected by an incident overnight, which impacted their refrigeration and freezer systems".
The latest incidents follow an attack in France last month when police said hackers seized control of ​cooling units at hundreds of supermarkets, causing fires and food losses. Ahold also reported a cybersecurity incident to police last month.
Read: Investigators hunt French supermarket fridge hackers, no claim of responsibility
While no one has claimed responsibility for either attack, ⁠the incidents have heightened concerns among European authorities about hybrid threats to infrastructure amid growing security tensions since Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine.
Moscow has repeatedly denied involvement in sabotage or hybrid warfare operations. Reuters could not establish who was ​behind Monday's attacks or whether they were linked to the incidents in France.
"It is not known who is behind this attack, and it may never be determined," said Katrien Eggers, spokesperson for Belgium's Centre for Cybersecurity, adding she was concerned ​about the growing number of incidents, in part due to AI.
"All IT systems are potentially vulnerable, and AI can now be used to successfully exploit these weaknesses — especially by sophisticated actors," she said.
'Retail is an easy target'
From refrigerators and heating systems to security cameras and alarms, an expanding range of devices once largely mechanical can now be monitored and controlled remotely, creating new opportunities for cybercriminals.
At least some of the refrigerator units affected on Monday used temperature control technology from Danish firm Danfoss that was also targeted in the French ​attack. The firm said it had been working with customers to implement fixes.
The European Commission said the latest incidents highlighted how digital threats are becoming increasingly disruptive.
Read More: French supermarket fridges hacked
"They are a deliberate attempt to disrupt our food supply chain and undermine ​consumers' confidence in it – a warning that we must take seriously," said EU commissioner for agriculture Christophe Hansen. "The repeated occurrence of these cyberattacks is deeply concerning."
A spokesperson for Colruyt Group, which operates Spar stores in Belgium under a franchise system, said five shops ‌had their ⁠fridge systems attacked.
In Ireland, wholesaler Musgrave said the incident affected systems in 13 of its SuperValu stores, forcing it to remove some chilled and frozen products from sale.
"Our monitoring systems alerted us to the issue, and we took immediate action," it said in a statement. "Our investigation is ongoing."
Tom Hegel, a researcher at cybersecurity firm SentinelOne, said such attacks were typically linked to extortion, political motives or nation-state operations, with the absence of financial demands in recent cases pointing instead to sabotage.
"Retail is an easy target because retail chains run enormous estates of refrigeration controllers, building management systems, door access panels and point-of-sale gear," he said, adding it was hard to trace hackers targeting such systems.
🚨 NEW: Britain is on alert to protect Tesco and Sainsbury's fridges amid cyber attacks on similar fridges across Europe
Hackers are remotely accessing them and turning temperatures up to as high as 80C pic.twitter.com/kQqyqSos82
— Politics UK (@PolitlcsUK) November 2, 2026
"An attacker who logs into ​an exposed control panel leaves almost nothing behind ... A teenager ​and an intelligence service would look much the ⁠same from the defender's side."
'It's very scary'
Carrefour, which was badly hit in last month's French attack, said 15 of its 700 stores in Belgium were affected. IKEA said one store in Belgium had been impacted and that it could not rule out disruptions at other locations.
Privately held Swedish grocery chain Coop said that 7 of its 800 stores were ​affected by a cyber incident involving unauthorised tampering with its refrigeration systems. It said Danfoss was among its suppliers.
Luc De Laet, founder and owner of Belgian butchery ​chain De Laet & Van Haver, said ⁠he was woken at 3:30 am by an employee telling him there was a problem. He rushed to his store south of Antwerp and found the fridges turned up as high as 18 C.
He estimated the incident ruined about €15,000 ($16,800) worth of meat.
"It's very scary. They are hacking the system that is doing the registration of the temperature, and they can program it at a distance," he told Reuters, adding that it was infuriating to throw away so much food.
De Laet said he believed ⁠the hackers were ​trying to destabilise European economies. He had contacted police but did not know whether an investigation had been launched.
"I only have two words ​for them: wake up, please, because there's something going on," he said.

items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Federal Minister for Information Technology and Telecommunication Shaza Fatima Khawaja has welcomed the Supreme Court’s transition towards paperless operations, describing it as a positive step towards modernizing Pakistan’s judicial system.
Speaking at an international training workshop, the minister highlighted the growing importance of artificial intelligence (AI) in judicial institutions and stressed the need to strengthen technological expertise across different sectors.
She said technology is becoming an essential part of institutional development, making it increasingly important for professionals to develop skills in emerging digital tools.
Shaza Fatima also welcomed participants from China, Uzbekistan, Azerbaijan, Türkiye and Bangladesh, highlighting the importance of international cooperation and knowledge-sharing in advancing digital transformation.
Artificial Intelligence Can Support Pakistan’s Judicial Digitalization
During her address, Shaza Fatima emphasized that artificial intelligence has an important role to play in the judicial system as institutions increasingly adopt digital technologies.
She appreciated the Supreme Court’s move towards paperless operations, which represents a shift away from traditional paperwork and towards electronic administrative processes.
The minister also referred to Pakistan’s broader digital transformation agenda, saying that the government’s journey towards Digital Pakistan continues under the direction of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif.
She highlighted the approval of the Digital Nation Pakistan Act as an important development in strengthening the country’s digital governance framework.
Shaza Fatima further stressed that trust remains a fundamental requirement for meaningful discussions and cooperation, particularly when institutions collaborate on technological initiatives.
She congratulated the Ministry of Law and other relevant stakeholders for their contributions towards judicial modernization.
Her remarks reflect the government’s emphasis on adopting technology across public institutions, with artificial intelligence and paperless operations emerging as important areas for future development.
However, the minister did not announce a new AI-powered judicial system or provide a timeline for additional AI integration in courts.

items.author: Shrishti Bisht
items.content:
Shares of insurtech major PB Fintech hit a fresh 52-week low today, plunging about 8% to ₹926 apiece on the BSE. The stock closed the day’s trading session 7.19% lower at ₹928.10 apiece on the BSE.
The company’s stock is down 48% since September 23, since the IRDAI floated its consultation paper to overhaul the insurance distribution industry
Its market capitalisation stood at ₹42,948.08 Cr ($4.53 Bn). PB Fintech commanded a market cap of $9.07 Bn at the end of the first week of September, over twice of its market cap now.
The dip today comes after the company’s quarterly disclosures last Friday. PB Fintech’s consolidated net profit rose 42.5% YoY to ₹192.4 Cr in Q2 FY27, compared with ₹135 Cr in the year-ago quarter. Sequentially, profit increased 18% from ₹163 Cr in Q1 FY27.
Operating revenue grew nearly 35% YoY to ₹2,177.7 Cr, from ₹1,613.6 Cr in Q2 FY26. It rose 15% sequentially from ₹1,888.3 Cr in the June quarter. While total income stood at ₹2,277.6 Cr, total expenses increased 32.6% YoY to ₹2,067.7 Cr.
The company’s core online business, which includes Policybazaar and Paisabazaar, generated ₹1,336 Cr in revenue, up 39.5% YoY. Revenue from new initiatives rose 28% YoY to ₹842 Cr. Adjusted EBITDA increased 39% to ₹216 Cr, while adjusted EBITDA margin remained flat YoY at 10%
Brokerages have given mixed outlooks for the stock post the disclosures. HSBC and Dolat Capital retained their ‘Hold’ and ‘Reduce’ ratings, respectively, while Bernstein maintained its ‘Outperform’ call.
HSBC kept its target price at ₹1,100 but cut its FY27-29 earnings per share (EPS) estimates by 2-4%, citing higher operating costs and regulatory uncertainty. Bernstein retained its target price of ₹1,085, citing 38% YoY growth in consolidated premiums and 22% growth in core credit disbursements.
Dolat Capital retained its ‘Reduce’ rating but cut its target price to ₹1,090 from ₹1,150. The brokerage said Q2 revenue rose 35% YoY to ₹2,177.7 Cr but was 4.2% below its estimate. EBIT also missed estimates by 32.7%, mainly due to higher advertising and other expenses.
It flagged concerns that proposed IRDAI rules could reduce insurance distribution payouts and affect PB Fintech’s PoSP model. Dolat cut its FY27-FY29 EPS estimates by 3%, 3.9% and 4.1%, respectively, due to uncertainty over the impact of the proposed rules.
PB Fintech’s Future Outlook
PB Fintech has said its PoSP insurance distribution business may need to be restructured if the IRDAI’s proposed rules are adopted in their current form.
During the earnings call, chairman and CEO Yashish Dahiya said the proposals could limit the scope of the existing PoSP model. The company will wait for the final regulations before deciding on its next steps.
Dahiya said PB Fintech was in informal discussions with the regulator about other options, which it would announce only after receiving certain regulatory approval. He added that the proposals could open up opportunities to offer non-insurance services, including potentially charging for claims support that Policybazaar currently provides for free, subject to the final rules.
PB Fintech has begun reducing costs, with hiring in October at a “very, very small fraction” of earlier levels, the management said. The company also plans to move existing executives into newer businesses and use AI to improve efficiency. Advertising and promotion expenses rose 59% YoY to ₹447 Cr in Q2, outpacing revenue growth.
Core credit disbursements rose 22% YoY to ₹2,791 Cr but were broadly flat sequentially. Management said it had focused on adding lending partners before pursuing further growth.
