items.title: Republicans, Democrats make midterm closing arguments as Michigan rift roils Senate race
items.summary:
Democrats sought to contain a rift in Michigan's US Senate race after one of their own crossed party lines to endorse the Republican, while President Donald Trump pressed his legal efforts on Monday to ​intervene in ballot-counting as both parties made their closing arguments a day before midterm elections that will determine control of Congress.
Over a fast-moving weekend, US Representative Haley Stevens, who lost the Michigan Democratic Senate primary to Abdul ‌El-Sayed in a bitter contest, suddenly switched to backing Republican Mike Rogers and appeared with him at a Detroit church. The race is critical to Democrats' hopes of ending the 53-47 Senate majority held by Trump's Republicans in Tuesday's vote.
Stevens' Sunday surprise came the same day a federal judge dismissed a US Justice Department lawsuit seeking to block certification of election results in Alaska if Republican incumbent Senator Dan Sullivan narrowly loses in the battleground state.
I am endorsing Mike Roge
items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Democrats sought to contain a rift in Michigan's US Senate race after one of their own crossed party lines to endorse the Republican, while President Donald Trump pressed his legal efforts on Monday to ​intervene in ballot-counting as both parties made their closing arguments a day before midterm elections that will determine control of Congress.
Over a fast-moving weekend, US Representative Haley Stevens, who lost the Michigan Democratic Senate primary to Abdul ‌El-Sayed in a bitter contest, suddenly switched to backing Republican Mike Rogers and appeared with him at a Detroit church. The race is critical to Democrats' hopes of ending the 53-47 Senate majority held by Trump's Republicans in Tuesday's vote.
Stevens' Sunday surprise came the same day a federal judge dismissed a US Justice Department lawsuit seeking to block certification of election results in Alaska if Republican incumbent Senator Dan Sullivan narrowly loses in the battleground state.
I am endorsing Mike Rogers for the United States Senate today. pic.twitter.com/pQgfSBuhOJ
— Haley Stevens (@HaleyforMI) November 1, 2026
An undeterred Trump, who has been holding daily rallies around the country for Republican candidates, filed an emergency request with the US Supreme ​Court on Monday to temporarily block California from counting mail-in ballots from more than 20,000 registered voters who federal officials allege are likely non-US citizens.
California said the lawsuit could disenfranchise 20,000 voters based on vague accusations and that ​the administration's process for identifying noncitizens was flawed and prone to error.
The president, who continues to falsely claim that his loss to Joe Biden in 2020 was caused by widespread ⁠fraud, was due to deliver remarks at 2 pm ET (1900 GMT) at the belated reopening of Washington's Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool. An earlier renovation as part of his beautification efforts for the US capital was botched by contractors, leading to the "American ​flag blue" liner peeling away, which Trump had wrongly blamed on vandals.
"They call it the House of Satan."
President Donald Trump takes aim at Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, citing reports about his campaign's signature-gathering efforts centered around radical mosques that called the United States "the House of Satan."
Trump rejects the… pic.twitter.com/wrnRKjOWCM
— Fox News (@FoxNews) November 2, 2026
A spokesperson for El-Sayed's campaign said it raised $2.4 million on Sunday, its largest single-day fundraising haul, fueled by small-dollar donations averaging $36.74 from more than 65,000 donors.
Michigan Democrat Abdul El-Sayed’s Senate campaign said it raised $2.4 million on Sunday after his former primary opponent, US Representative Haley Stevens, withdrew her endorsement and publicly backed Republican Mike Rogers https://t.co/BV9UNqGha5
— Bloomberg (@business) November 2, 2026
Nonpartisan analysts generally favour Democrats' chances ​of winning a majority in the House of Representatives. Winning control of the Senate will be trickier, with those analysts now seeing races in traditionally Republican-leaning states including Texas, Kansas and Iowa as competitive for the opposition party, giving it more options for a path to the majority.
Control of either chamber would constrain Trump's ability to pass legislation and empower Democrats to investigate his administration, while a Senate majority would also allow them to block his appointees to federal courts, including the Supreme Court.
According to the University of Florida Election Lab, 55 million votes have been ​cast in person and by mail already, more than the 45 million cast in the 2022 midterm elections.
Michigan rift
Stevens called on El-Sayed to condemn an outside group's ad that she said blames Israel for high grocery prices.
"That ad was very painful," ​Stevens told CNN on Sunday night. "There are so many Democrats who want to vote for our Democratic nominee, and they're just being told, 'Hey, this is a party you don't belong in, or this is a campaign you don't belong in.'"
El-Sayed rejected Stevens' demand, saying she ‌was creating ⁠a distraction by revisiting a primary election she lost months prior.
"You guys love to play the condemn game," he told reporters on Saturday when asked about Stevens' demand. "I've already been clear that that ad was not made by me, and I do not agree with the contents of that ad."
When asked about Rep. Haley Stevens’ endorsement of Mike Rogers, Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed said his focus is on the voters.
Read more: https://t.co/wTWxQDUcr2 pic.twitter.com/Lz2SLnmS75
— The Wall Street Journal (@WSJ) November 2, 2026
El-Sayed, an Egyptian American Muslim born in Michigan, has been targeted by Trump and other Republicans who have repeatedly questioned his loyalty to the US and baselessly called him a terrorist sympathiser whose election would invite attacks on Americans. El-Sayed has called questions about his loyalty to the US "shameful".
Read More: Republican ‘Muslim Brotherhood’ attacks on El-Sayed seek to exploit Democratic divisions
The verbal attacks fit a broader pattern of inflammatory rhetoric from some Republicans targeting Arab Americans, Muslims and transgender people and portraying Democrats as communists and dangerous radicals ahead of the ​midterms.
"He's lied about his relationships with the Muslim Brotherhood, a terrorist organization that's banned in eight Muslim countries."
Mike Rogers takes aim at Abdul El-Sayed, accusing him of concealing alleged connections to the Muslim Brotherhood and accepting money from… pic.twitter.com/7Tmq6uQNes
— Fox News (@FoxNews) November 2, 2026
Stevens' mother, Maria Marcotte, said her daughter decided to endorse ​Rogers because of what she described as dangerous political ⁠rhetoric from El-Sayed, pointing in part to his past appearances with Hasan Piker, a left-wing streamer who has been criticised for his comments about Israel and American Jews.
"She's really reached a point where she felt like her constituents, the people that she cares about, and the people she knows and loves are scared and frightened by some rhetoric that's coming out," Marcotte said ​in an interview with Reuters from the porch of her home in Birmingham, a northern Detroit suburb.
Democratic voter Pamela Johnson, 72, criticised Stevens after casting her ballot for El-Sayed ​in Warren, a Detroit suburb: "Haley Stevens ⁠is a traitor."
Democratic Congresswoman Haley Stevens is heckled while appearing alongside Republican Mike Rogers, whom she has endorsed in the Michigan Senate race.
Her endorsement of Rogers over Democrat Abdul El-Sayed has sparked backlash, with members of her own team resigning in protest. pic.twitter.com/HkTipNPpP4
— Middle East Eye (@MiddleEastEye) November 2, 2026
Alaska intervention falters
The Trump administration's attempt to intervene in Alaska's Senate race faltered when a federal judge dismissed the US Justice Department's lawsuit on Sunday that sought to block certification of the results if Republican incumbent Senator Dan Sullivan narrowly loses.
The Justice Department argued voters may be confused by the presence of a challenger named Daniel Sullivan Jr on the same ballot.
The issue has roiled the campaign over the last several days after the New York Times reported that Democrat Mary Peltola's campaign was involved ⁠in recruiting the latter ​Sullivan into the race as a spoiler.
The senator said on Sunday he would accept the results of Tuesday's election even as the Trump administration ​presses a criminal investigation into the issue.
Peltola has denied involvement, and Sullivan Jr has denied coordinating with Peltola's campaign.
"I think it's great that it got thrown out," said Aileena Bird, a 24-year-old resident of Wasilla, Alaska, who said she voted for Peltola. "I think that more should be done to fight against what ​Trump has been doing in trying to suppress the voters."

Mr. Liu Haixing, the Minister of the International Department of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China (IDCPC) called on the Prime Minister Mr. Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif in Islamabad today.
Welcoming Mr. Liu Haixing and his delegation, the Prime Minister… pic.twitter.com/Resnht2Ea2
— Prime Minister's Office (@PakPMO) November 2, 2026
Welcoming the Chinese official and his delegation, the prime minister said, “Pakistan and China enjoy an ironclad, time-tested and All-Weather Strategic Cooperative partnership.”
PM Shehbaz also underscored that Pakistan-China friendship was anchored in mutual trust, mutual respect and deep-rooted bonds between the peoples of both countries.
He also appreciated the role of the IDCPC in promoting institutional linkages and cooperation between the political leadership of the two countries, while emphasising the importance of sustained political engagement and inter-party exchanges to bolster ties.
Reaffirming Pakistan's commitment to working closely with Beijing, the prime minister highlighted the shared focus on expanding cooperation in trade, investment, connectivity, infrastructure development, information technology and agricultural modernisation.
The prime minister later hosted a banquet in honour of the visiting Chinese dignitary and his delegation.
Meeting with CDF Munir
Earlier today, Haixing called on Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir at the General Headquarters in Rawalpindi, according to the military’s media wing.
Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir has emphasised the importance of sustained high-level engagement, stronger institutional linkages, and expanded cooperation in areas of mutual interest between Pakistan and China.@OfficialDGISPR… pic.twitter.com/GnamMvBgd0
— Radio Pakistan (@RadioPakistan) November 2, 2026
The Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said in a statement, “During the meeting, both sides discussed matters of mutual interest, evolving regional and international security dynamics and bilateral relations,” adding that the two officials expressed their shared resolve to further strengthen the all-weather strategic cooperative partnership between Islamabad and Beijing.
It further underscored that during the meeting with the IDCPC minister, CDF Munir highlighted the historic and time-tested bonds between the two countries.

He also emphasised the importance of sustained high-level engagement, stronger institutional linkages and expanded cooperation across areas of mutual interest.
The ISPR said the visiting dignitary appreciated Pakistan’s contributions to regional peace and stability and expressed confidence in further advancing the longstanding strategic partnership between Pakistan and China.
The visit also coincides with the 75th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between Pakistan and China. The two countries established diplomatic ties on May 21, 1951, and have since expanded their cooperation across political, economic, diplomatic and security domains.
DPM Dar highlights political consensus in Pakistan for stronger Sino-Pak ties
Deputy PM and Foreign Minister Mohammad Ishaq Dar also highlighted the broad-based political consensus in Pakistan supporting the longstanding friendship with China, according to a statement issued by the Foreign Office.
DPM Dar said this while co-chairing the Symposium on Xi Jinping Thought on Party Building and Seminar on China-Pakistan Governance in Islamabad alongside Haixing.
Addressing the gathering, the deputy PM underscored the vital role of political parties in effective governance, institution-building as well as national development.
In his keynote address, Haixing thanked Pakistan's leadership for its continued efforts to promote political goodwill, saying such engagement played an important role in furthering bilateral cooperation.
Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar @MIshaqDar50 co-chaired the “Symposium on Xi Jinping Thought on Party Building and Seminar on China-Pakistan Governance” with Mr. Liu Haixing, Minister of the International Department of the CPC Central Committee… pic.twitter.com/91AKRYZoMT
— Ministry of Foreign Affairs - Pakistan (@ForeignOfficePk) November 2, 2026
Haixing's maiden visit to Pakistan reflects Beijing's push to deepen ties beyond conventional government-to-government diplomacy.
The IDCPC, which Haixing heads, serves as Beijing's principal channel for party-to-party diplomacy, maintaining links with ruling and opposition political parties and facilitating exchanges on governance, development and international affairs.

In May this year, PM Shehbaz's visit to China culminated in a renewed commitment by both countries to deepen their partnership, maintain high-level exchanges and strengthen defence and security cooperation under the 2025-2029 action plan.
Defence cooperation has remained a key pillar of bilateral relations.
During CDF Munir's visit to Beijing in July 2025, he held meetings with senior Chinese political and military leadership, including Vice President Han Zheng and officials of the People's Liberation Army.
Discussions covered defence and security cooperation, counterterrorism collaboration, joint training, defence modernisation and stronger institutional linkages.
Both sides also reaffirmed their commitment to expanding military-to-military cooperation and promoting regional peace and stability.

items.author: Shrishti Bisht
items.content:
Bengaluru-based spacetech soonicorn Pixxel’s founder and CEO Awais Ahmed has dismissed questions over the startup’s Indian ownership and control following online criticism over the launch of its US subsidiary, Pixxel Federal.
In a post on X, Ahmed said Pixxel remains headquartered, owned, managed, and controlled in India, rejecting allegations questioning its corporate structure and national credentials.
“First, Pixxel is Indian-HQed, Indian owned, Indian-managed and Indian-controlled,” he said, adding that its primary Indian entity was incorporated in 2018, before any of its international entities.
Ahmed said the Indian entity is not a subsidiary of a US company and remains the primary vehicle for executing Pixxel’s Indian government, space, and defence programmes. Pixxel Federal’s board and CEO would have authority only over the US subsidiary and its operations, with no control over the startup’s Indian government programmes or domestic business, he added.
The clarification follows Pixxel’s announcement that it had established Pixxel Federal to pursue US government contracts across civilian, defence, and intelligence agencies.
Pixxel’s Ownership Structure
Ahmed said Pixxel has faced targeted social media attacks, anonymous emails to government customers, and attempts to cast doubt on its ownership, technology, and credentials.
Addressing its shareholding, he said Indian investors, including the founders, collectively hold the largest share by percentage, followed by investors from Singapore, the UK, and the US. No international investor has unilateral control over Pixxel beyond customary investor protections, he added.
Ahmed also said intellectual property developed for Indian government projects remains under Indian ownership and control, with these programmes executed through Indian entities and governed by Indian laws.
He said Pixxel’s overseas presence predates Pixxel Federal, with its existing US entity incorporated a few months after the Indian company in 2018 to serve American and international customers. Pixxel plans to set up entities in more countries as it expands globally.
“We intend to build a global space company rooted in Indian engineering. That means selling Indian technology worldwide, hiring internationally, establishing local entities where required, and complying with each country’s laws,” he said.
The CEO said separate entities are necessary in regulated sectors such as space and defence to meet national security, export control, licensing, and customer confidentiality requirements.
“Having one entity isn’t some extraordinary achievement in governance, and having several isn’t evidence of questionable patriotism,” he said.
He added that Pixxel plans to go public in India in a few years, when its complete corporate structure would be disclosed for public scrutiny.
Ahmed’s response follows comments by fellow Bengaluru-based spacetech startup GalaxEye, which said it consciously chose to remain headquartered in India despite considering other locations.
In a post on X, GalaxEye said its founders and investors had decided to build the business from India. It also highlighted its single-entity corporate structure, saying all its contracts and bids had been pursued through GalaxEye.
“Every contract and every bid we have applied for has come from a single entity: GalaxEye. We have kept our corporate structure simple and our governance clean,” it said.
Without naming any company, GalaxEye referred to the practice of setting up multiple entities across jurisdictions to qualify for and secure projects, saying it had chosen not to follow that approach.
“That discipline has a cost in the short term. We believe it pays back in trust, and trust is what a space company is ultimately built on,” it added.
Pixxel Expands Its Government Business
Founded by Ahmed and Kshitij Khandelwal, Pixxel develops hyperspectral imaging satellites that capture data across multiple narrow wavelength bands, revealing details on the Earth’s surface that conventional satellite imagery may miss.
Its new subsidiary, Pixxel Federal, will offer Earth observation technologies, satellite mission systems, and geospatial intelligence services to US government agencies. It also plans to establish an office near Washington, DC, to work more closely with government customers and partners.
The expansion builds on Pixxel’s existing engagements with NASA and the National Reconnaissance Office (NRO), including a contract under NASA’s Commercial SmallSat Data Acquisition Programme and an NRO Strategic Commercial Enhancements contract.
In September, Pixxel raised $100 Mn in a Series C funding round co-led by Temasek and Seraphim, taking its total funding to around $195 Mn.
In India, a Pixxel-led consortium is developing a 12-satellite Earth observation constellation under a public-private initiative with IN-SPACe.

items.author: Life And Style Desk
items.content:
Actor and musician Junaid Khan believes Pakistan's entertainment industry needs to move beyond its established commercial formulas, arguing that independent music deserves greater investment and television needs to make room for stories beyond its predominantly female-centred programming.
From the decline of dedicated music channels to the lack of male-centred narratives on television, Khan believes there is considerable room for the industry to diversify. He is particularly interested in exploring action and crime-based projects, genres he feels deserve greater representation in Pakistani entertainment.
In a conversation with Atiqa Odho, Khan discussed his journey across music and acting, the emergence of independent musicians, the commercial priorities shaping television content and his aspirations to move into production.
Khan believes Pakistan's music industry has enormous potential, particularly with the emergence of younger artists and the accessibility of digital platforms. However, he feels the industry has not invested enough in creating independent opportunities for musicians.
"Now music is played more on YouTube so brands invest those into their dramas," he explained, pointing to the shift in how music is consumed and commercially supported. "I think most of our channel heads invest music in drama because that is where the money is. If needed, they could have invested in a music channel," he added.
He recalled how dedicated music channels once provided artists with an important platform before the availability of free Indian music and copyright-related challenges contributed to their decline.
For Khan, music should not have to depend on a drama's popularity to attract investment. Dedicated music channels, independent productions, music videos and live performances could give musicians more opportunities to build their careers.
"The future of music in Pakistan is very bright," he said, adding, "There are so many artists, post-Spotify. So many kids in our homes make music on their computers and now they have a free stream platform."
He is particularly encouraged by younger musicians experimenting with sounds and genres rather than limiting themselves to conventional styles. "Kids these days make such good music and are very creative. There are different genres, not just classic," he said.
Khan also praised Young Stunners and Hasan Raheem. "Young Stunners are very good. Hasan Raheem is very interesting and has a good tone. There are many who are doing good and keep coming." He believes Pakistani music has also reached international audiences, while Karachi's concert culture has grown considerably since his early days performing live.
His concerns about commercial investment extend to television, where he believes audience demographics have a considerable influence on the stories broadcasters choose to finance.
Khan acknowledged that television research points towards a predominantly female audience, which influences the industry's programming decisions.
"TV is a female-centred audience, that is what research says. Women see it more," he said. He explained that broadcasters tend to prioritise the larger audience segment rather than invest in content aimed at smaller demographics.
While female-centred dramas have an established audience and an important place in Pakistani television, Khan's observations point to an opportunity to explore a wider range of experiences and genres.
Action, crime and thrillers, in particular, are areas he would like to see receive more attention. "I like action and crime. As a guy, that is where my interest lies despite it being difficult," he said.
Having spent considerable time in front of the camera, Khan is also interested in moving towards content creation and production. "I have produced a couple of my own music videos but want to start on television," he revealed.
His career across music and acting, however, was not necessarily the result of a carefully laid-out plan. Khan described himself as someone who has always needed to stay occupied, rather than someone who consciously set out to develop multiple talents.
"I have never thought of myself to be a man of multiple talents. I did not see talent that way. I always wanted to be doing something in life. I hated being free. I want to keep myself occupied," he added.
Recalling his college years, he said he was balancing education, employment and music. "I was studying, working, and then going for jams later in the night. Then life went in a way where I stayed like that. There was never a time when I was just free."
For Khan, music and acting have served different creative purposes. "Music for me was a mode of expression. With acting, I wanted to explore human scripts and minds. How people do these things and how actors work. I was interested in that from the very beginning," he said.
His interest in performance also extended to theatre. When Odho suggested he would be suited to musical theatre, Khan agreed, recalling watching Chicago in Pakistan and attending Broadway productions in New York. "I salute actors in Pakistan working in theatre," he added.
Away from his professional commitments, Khan also discussed the importance of balancing work, fitness and family life. He has two children, aged 12 and seven, and makes a conscious effort to dedicate time to them.
"I make sure that I give certain times in the day to family such as dropping kids to school. I then start my day early, go to gym, and go to work. I try to work five days a week and take at least Saturday or Sunday off. There should be balance in everything from fitness, work life, to family life," he said.
He also spoke candidly about the challenges fame can bring to married life, particularly when an artist receives attention from fans. "Salute to all the wives. Media wives are challenged by this. Even if they are aware if my man is next to me or close to me, they will always have that feeling that your partner is loved by others. That is a thing to bear."
Khan believes maintaining a healthy relationship requires involving one's partner in professional life while also respecting personal boundaries. "I try to involve myself and also distance. The plus and minus factor. Involve yourself but keep distance and don't let small issues make an impact," he said.
He added that he makes a conscious effort to leave his on-screen persona behind when returning home, ensuring that the pressures and attention associated with fame do not affect his family.

items.summary:
An Islamabad Additional District and Sessions Court sentenced Raja Haris Naveed to seven years of rigorous imprisonment in a cybercrime case involving the harassment of a 16-year-old boy and the recording of an objectionable video without his consent, it emerged on Monday.
Additional District and Sessions Judge Muhammad Afzal Majoka announced the verdict after finding the main accused in the case “guilty”, according to the order dated October 29.
The accused was convicted under Section 22 (child pornography) of the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (PECA), 2016, read with Sections 34 (acts done by several persons in furtherance of common intention) and 109 (Punishment of abetment if the Act abetted committed in consequence and where no express provision is made for its punishment) of the Pakistan Penal Code, 1860.
The court also imposed a fine of Rs1 million on the convict under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (PECA) amended in 2025.

items.author: Fiaz Mahmood
items.content:
An Islamabad Additional District and Sessions Court sentenced Raja Haris Naveed to seven years of rigorous imprisonment in a cybercrime case involving the harassment of a 16-year-old boy and the recording of an objectionable video without his consent, it emerged on Monday.
Additional District and Sessions Judge Muhammad Afzal Majoka announced the verdict after finding the main accused in the case “guilty”, according to the order dated October 29.
The accused was convicted under Section 22 (child pornography) of the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (PECA), 2016, read with Sections 34 (acts done by several persons in furtherance of common intention) and 109 (Punishment of abetment if the Act abetted committed in consequence and where no express provision is made for its punishment) of the Pakistan Penal Code, 1860.
The court also imposed a fine of Rs1 million on the convict under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (PECA) amended in 2025.
Read: Two held for involvement in child abuse case
In case of non-payment of the fine, the judge said the convict will have to serve an additional six months in prison.
According to the case details, the accused lured a 16-year-old matriculation student into a drawing room and confined him. He then threatened and harassed the minor at gunpoint before recording an objectionable video without his consent.
The court acquitted co-accused Shahzaib Miraj, granting him the benefit of the doubt, as the prosecution failed to establish his involvement in aiding or abetting the crime.
In a similar case, an Islamabad court on October 22 sentenced two men to 10 years in prison each for blackmailing a 12-year-old girl and sharing her objectionable pictures.
Judge Majoka awarded each convict seven years' imprisonment and a fine of Rs1 million under Section 22 of PECA.
Under Section 24 (cyber stalking) of the same act, both convicts were sentenced to an additional three years in prison each and fined Rs1 million each, bringing their total prison term to 10 years each and the fine to Rs2 million each.
The case was registered by the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency on the complaint of the minor girl's father, according to The Express Tribune.

items.author: Akshit Pushkarna
items.content:
Fintech company MobiKwik reported a consolidated net profit of ₹11.8 Cr in the September quarter of FY27 as against a net loss of ₹28.6 Cr a year earlier, supported by revenue growth and lower payment processing and lending operational costs.
Operating revenue rose 9.4% to ₹295.7 Cr from ₹270.2 Cr in Q2 FY26.
Sequentially, net profit increased 55.4% from ₹7.6 Cr, while operating revenue grew 5.1% from ₹281.5 Cr.
The company said it recorded its highest-ever quarterly net profit and fourth consecutive profitable quarter.
EBITDA stood at ₹22.7 Cr, compared with an EBITDA loss of ₹6.4 Cr in Q2 FY26 and a profit of ₹15.8 Cr in the June quarter.
Other income declined 22.5% YoY to ₹7.1 Cr. However, total income increased 8.4% to ₹302.8 Cr from ₹279.3 Cr.
Total expenses, including finance costs and depreciation, declined 1.8% YoY to ₹290.9 Cr from ₹296.1 Cr.
Payment processing charges, MobiKwik’s largest expense, fell 10.8% YoY to ₹119.5 Cr from ₹133.9 Cr. Lending operational expenses declined 88.1% to ₹1.5 Cr from ₹12.8 Cr.
The year-ago quarter also included an ₹11.8 Cr exceptional charge related to allegedly fraudulent merchant settlements. There was no exceptional charge in Q2 FY27.
Payments Revenue Remains Flat
MobiKwik’s gross merchandise value (GMV) for the payments vertical, including its payment gateway Zaakpay, grew 35% YoY to ₹59,677 Cr, supported by growth in consumer and merchant payments.
Consumer payments accounted for ₹46,375 Cr, or 77.7%, of overall payments GMV. Merchant payments contributed the remaining 22.3%, up from about 17% a year earlier.
However, the increase in transaction value did not translate into higher payments revenue. Revenue from the business remained largely flat at ₹208.8 Cr as against ₹208.9 Cr in Q2 FY26.
The company attributed this to a change in transaction mix towards payments that generate lower revenue relative to their value. Its payments take rate – revenue earned as a proportion of GMV – declined to 0.35% from 0.47% a year earlier.
Despite this, direct payments costs fell 12.6% YoY to ₹129 Cr, helping gross profit rise 30% to ₹79.8 Cr. Gross margin expanded to 38.2% from 29.4%.
Lending Disbursals Pick Up
Meanwhile, revenue from MobiKwik’s financial services business, which includes its ZIP EMI credit offering, increased 41.8% YoY to ₹86.9 Cr.
The growth was supported by a 34.1% increase in lending disbursals to ₹1,082.6 Cr. Disbursals also rose 46.9% sequentially from ₹736.7 Cr, recovering from a temporary dip linked to technology infrastructure migration for the transfer of its lending business.
MobiKwik increased its number of major lending partners to 11 from six a year earlier. It counts partners with quarterly disbursals exceeding ₹5 Cr as major lenders.
The company said 21% of disbursals came through its distribution model, while the remaining 79% were under its first-loss default guarantee (FLDG) model, through which it shares credit risk with lending partners and manages loan origination, servicing, and collections.
Lending-related expenses, comprising lending operational and financial guarantee expenses, declined 16.4% YoY to ₹29.8 Cr. The company attributed the reduction to improved credit quality.
Consequently, financial services gross profit more than doubled to ₹57.1 Cr from ₹25.6 Cr, while gross margin expanded to 65.7% from 41.8%.
Higher Margins Offset Costs
While both businesses improved gross margins, MobiKwik’s fixed costs rose 18.3% YoY to ₹121.2 Cr. Employee benefit expenses increased 59% to ₹56.2 Cr.
The company attributed higher employee costs to scaling its merchant business and expanding into new business areas.
Overall, the results highlight the gap between MobiKwik’s payments transaction growth and revenue, while financial services delivered stronger revenue growth. Lower direct costs across both businesses helped offset higher fixed costs and improve profitability.
“We have crossed the ₹1,000 Cr milestone in lending disbursals and clocked 150% year-on-year revenue growth in merchant payments, highlighting the growing scale of our business,” cofounder, MD, and CEO Bipin Preet Singh said.
He added that the company expects operating leverage to improve with greater AI adoption, alongside continued cost optimisation and operating efficiencies.
Shares of MobiKwik ended today’s trading session 5.57% higher at ₹225.70 apiece on the BSE.

items.author: Usama Anjum
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Pakistan’s 5G network is gradually expanding, with telecom operators deploying more sites across major cities. However, for ordinary smartphone users, there is still an important question: how can they determine whether 5G is actually available in their neighbourhood?
According to the latest figures shared by the government, Pakistan now has 1,782 deployed 5G sites across 24 cities. Jazz leads with 1,015 sites, followed by Zong with 640 and Ufone with 127.
These figures indicate progress in network deployment. However, they do not provide a clear picture of how much of each city is covered or which residential and commercial areas can access the service.
For example, a consumer living in Islamabad, Lahore, or Karachi may own a 5G-compatible smartphone but still be unable to connect to a 5G network at home or at work.
This is because the presence of 5G sites in a city does not automatically mean that the entire city has reliable coverage.
Why Neighbourhood-Level 5G Coverage Matters for Pakistani Users
Pakistan’s telecom operators are rolling out 5G in phases, meaning some areas will receive access earlier than others.
However, the government figures released so far focus mainly on the number of deployed sites and the cities where services have been introduced. They do not include a detailed, publicly verified breakdown of coverage at the neighbourhood level.
This creates uncertainty for people considering an upgrade to a 5G smartphone.
The government has reported that the cheapest locally available 5G handset costs approximately Rs. 36,000. For consumers spending money specifically to access faster mobile internet, knowing whether their preferred network supports 5G in their area is an important consideration.
There is also the question of network performance. Even where 5G is available, the actual experience can depend on signal strength, network congestion, indoor coverage, and the capabilities of the smartphone being used.
Another important factor is device compatibility. Not every 5G smartphone necessarily supports all the frequency bands used by mobile operators in Pakistan.
Although existing 4G SIM cards can generally support the transition to 5G, users still need a compatible device and an active 5G signal from their operator.
This makes more detailed coverage information particularly useful. Regularly updated network maps showing where 5G is available could help consumers make informed decisions before purchasing new smartphones or switching operators.
Pakistan has already taken the first major step by allocating spectrum and starting commercial 5G deployment. As networks expand, providing consumers with clear and reliable information about actual service availability will become equally important.
For now, Pakistani smartphone buyers should confirm 5G availability directly with their network operator and check device compatibility before spending extra money on a new handset.
The post Pakistan’s 5G Is Expanding, But Can Users Actually Find Coverage in Their Area? appeared first on PhoneWorld.

items.author: Shrishti Bisht
items.content:
Update | November 2, 15:41 IST
Shares of Delhivery ended today’s trading session 5.8% higher at ₹408.75 apiece on the BSE. The company’s market capitalisation stood at ₹30,636.7 Cr ($3.2 Bn).
Original | November 2, 12:58 IST
Shares of Delhivery jumped 9.7% to an intraday high of ₹423.35 on the BSE after the logistics company reported a consolidated net profit of ₹40.6 Cr in Q2 FY27, against a net loss of ₹50.5 Cr a year earlier.
The stock later pared some gains to trade 7.6% higher at ₹415.40 apiece at 12:12 IST. The company’s market capitalisation stood at ₹31,135.2 Cr (about $3.3 Bn) at the time.
Brokerage firm Equirus Securities upgraded Delhivery to ‘Long’ from ‘Reduce’, with a target price of ₹505. This implies an upside of 30.8% from the stock’s previous closing price of ₹386.
Equirus expects Delhivery’s revenue, EBITDA, and express parcel volumes to grow at compound annual growth rates of 21%, 39%, and 22%, respectively, between FY26 and FY29, driven by market share gains, improving part truckload (PTL) margins, and operating leverage.
The brokerage estimates revenue of ₹12,963.3 Cr in FY27 and ₹15,107.3 Cr in FY28, with net profit of ₹381.4 Cr and ₹694.5 Cr, respectively.
Revenue Growth Outpaces Expenses
Delhivery’s consolidated operating revenue rose 19.8% to ₹3,066.4 Cr in Q2 FY27 from ₹2,559.3 Cr a year earlier. Sequentially, revenue increased 4.6% from ₹2,930.7 Cr.
Including other income of ₹66.6 Cr, total income stood at ₹3,133 Cr, compared with ₹2,651.5 Cr in Q2 FY26.
Total expenses increased 14.2% to ₹3,093 Cr from ₹2,708.1 Cr. Freight, handling, and servicing costs, its largest expense head, rose 19.1% to ₹2,195.1 Cr.
The company posted a pre-tax profit of ₹39 Cr against a loss of ₹53.2 Cr a year earlier. A net tax credit of ₹1.6 Cr took its consolidated net profit to ₹40.6 Cr.
However, Delhivery’s acquisition of Ecom Express affected the comparison. Excluding the acquisition impact, the company said its net profit in Q2 FY26 and Q1 FY27 would have stood at ₹59 Cr and ₹62 Cr, respectively.
Express Parcel Volumes Rise
Delhivery’s express parcel volumes rose 32.1% YoY to 325 Mn shipments, driven by market share gains and customer demand. Equirus said growth exceeded its FY27 guidance of 20-30%.
PTL volumes increased 14.2% to 5.45 Lakh metric tonnes, while revenue grew 23.2% on higher volumes and yields. Equirus attributed less than 30% of the yield increase to inflation-linked pricing revisions.
Adjusted EBITDA rose 48% YoY to ₹123 Cr, with margins improving to 4% from 3.3%.
Supported by pricing revisions and higher network utilisation, Delhivery expects express parcel service EBITDA margins to reach 16-18% and PTL margins to exceed 15% by FY27-end. Overall transportation margins are expected to expand 130-150 basis points during FY27.
Delhivery Local Revenue Run Rate Doubles To ₹200 Cr
Delhivery is expanding its intra-city, international, and financial services businesses. Delhivery Local operates across Delhi NCR, Bengaluru, Mumbai, Hyderabad, Ahmedabad, Jaipur, Pune, and Chennai. Its annualised revenue run rate doubled sequentially to around ₹200 Cr in Q2 FY27.
The company raised the platform’s FY27 exit run rate target to ₹280 Cr from ₹250 Cr, targeting ₹800-1,000 Cr in annualised revenue within two years.
Its board also approved an equity investment of up to ₹36 Cr in wholly owned subsidiary Delhivery Fintech Distribution, supporting financial product distribution across its vendor network and co-lending partnerships.
Delhivery said AI automation cut customer support and proof-of-delivery validation costs by over 50% without affecting quality. It has begun manufacturing customised autonomous mobile robots through Delhivery Labs and plans to deploy 100 self-developed autonomous pallet transportation vehicles by Q4 FY27.
October volumes exceeded the company’s initial expectations.

items.author: Anjali Jain
items.content:
In September 2019, a swarm of low-cost drones launched by Houthi rebels struck Saudi Aramco’s oil processing facilities, knocking out nearly half of Saudi Arabia’s oil production. The attack sent shockwaves across the world, exposing how inexpensive flying machines could bring critical infrastructure to a standstill.
Back home, the founder of Indrajaal, Kiran Raju, was closely observing everything, including a rise in drone incursions along India’s borders. He foresaw that Indian security agencies would soon need technology to detect hostile drones and stop them before they could launch an attack.
Indrajaal is looking to tackle this growing threat through its AI-powered counter-drone technology designed to detect, track and neutralise hostile drones, protecting military installations and critical infrastructure from aerial threats. Founded in 2020, the defence tech startup is developing an advanced, AI-powered counter-drone systems that combine proprietary hardware, computer vision and machine learning. It has so far raised about $5.5 Mn in external funding from the likes of India Accelerator and Finvolve.
The founder’s journey into autonomous robotics began long before Indrajaal. After studying at Carnegie Mellon University, he founded Grene Robotics in 2006 to develop autonomous technologies for defence applications. As drones became cheaper and more advanced, he spun off Indrajaal from Grene Robotics to develop systems capable of detecting and countering aerial threats.
Inside Indrajaal’s Defence Tech Capabilities
Traditional counter-drone systems typically rely on standalone technologies to jam or shoot down hostile drones. However, this approach becomes less effective when friendly and hostile drones operate in the same airspace.
Indrajaal addresses this limitation through SkyOS, its AI-powered platform that brings together multiple detection and defence systems.
SkyOS uses real-time data from radars, radio-frequency sensors and cameras to detect, track and identify aerial threats. Based on this information, it can recommend or automatically execute countermeasures.
The startup also offers an AI-powered mobile counter-drone vehicle, Ranger, designed to detect and neutralise threats while on the move. Once a hostile drone is identified, the system can jam its signals, use Repulsor to interfere with its navigation or deploy SkyCop, an autonomous interceptor drone.
All these products operate within Indrajaal’s integrated defence architecture, allowing the company to offer different solutions for different security requirements.
Indrajaal Spreads Its Wings
The startup operates in India’s growing defence tech sector, which is projected to become a $19 Bn market opportunity by 2030. Government incentives, homegrown innovation and the push for self-reliance in defence are driving this growth.
The startup has already deployed its systems at critical installations belonging to the Indian Army, Indian Navy and agencies under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
Indrajaal makes money through these deployments, supplying customers with a combination of hardware, software, installation and long-term maintenance services tailored to their security requirements.
Here’s how its growth trajectory looks like:
Revenue grew from around ₹34 Cr in FY25 to ₹100 Cr in FY26, with a target of ₹300 Cr in FY27
Plans to raise ₹420 Cr in its upcoming Series A round
Looking to ramp up manufacturing capacity, strengthen R&D and enter markets across the Middle East and Europe
Plans to expand its workforce from around 100 to nearly 160 employees over the coming year
Aims to develop a broader autonomous airspace ecosystem supporting civilian drone corridors and autonomous aerial transport
Inc42 Take: Government Contracts Could Be Indrajaal’s Achilles’ Heel
Indrajaal appears to have found its financial footing in the market with its novel tech stack. But, the startup is heavily tied to government contracts, which carry long validation windows and multi-year sales cycles. This could expose the startup to high working-capital strain.
On top of this, Indrajaal operates on a customised business model, which can strain gross margins and make scaling unit economics significantly harder. There are also supply chain risks and cost inflation that can quickly erode profitability and margins.
Meanwhile, competition also shows no signs of slowing down. As more global giants enter the fray, the startup will be up against players with deeper pockets and mature distribution channels. Domestically, too, rapid defence indigenisation has encouraged rivals to launch rival counter-drone systems, threatening pricing power.
While Indrajaal has built a battle-tested defence business, sustaining its ambitious financial trajectory will require transitioning beyond defence contracts to roping in private enterprises and successfully executing its international expansion across high-budget defence markets.
The post Can Indrajaal Build A ₹100 Cr Business Protecting India’s Skies? appeared first on Inc42 Media.

items.author: Usama Anjum
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The federal government has proposed establishing a National Cybersecurity and Social Media Awareness Council to address growing online threats, misinformation,, and the misuse of artificial intelligence across Pakistan.
Federal Minister for Information and Broadcasting Attaullah Tarar presented the proposal during Cyber Security Awareness Week 2026, organized by the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) in Islamabad.
According to the minister, the proposed council would bring together federal ministries, provincial governments, regulatory bodies, and other relevant institutions to develop a coordinated approach towards cybersecurity awareness and digital safety.
Tarar said Pakistan needs a more effective system to protect citizens from emerging online threats, particularly as artificial intelligence and social media platforms continue to evolve.
He also called for mandatory labeling of AI-generated content on social media platforms, warning that deepfakes and manipulated digital material are making it increasingly difficult for users to distinguish authentic information from misleading content.
The proposed labelling requirement would help users identify material created through artificial intelligence and make more informed decisions about the information they encounter online.
PTA Could Lead Proposed Council as Government Pushes Digital Awareness
Attaullah Tarar suggested that PTA could take the lead in coordinating the proposed National Cybersecurity and Social Media Awareness Council, with support from federal and provincial institutions.
He also recommended holding consultations with relevant stakeholders to move the initiative forward.
The minister stressed that cybersecurity awareness should not be limited to occasional campaigns. Instead, institutions should work throughout the year to educate citizens about digital threats, online scams and misinformation.
He further proposed establishing dedicated digital literacy cells within government organisations to train officials in identifying and responding to cybersecurity risks.
Tarar also emphasized the need to include digital literacy in educational curricula, allowing students to understand online privacy, cyber threats, and responsible use of emerging technologies.
The proposal comes as Pakistan continues efforts to strengthen its cybersecurity framework and improve coordination between regulatory bodies and digital platforms.
However, the National Cybersecurity and Social Media Awareness Council has not been formally established, and no implementation date has been announced.
Similarly, mandatory AI-content labeling remains a recommendation rather than a newly enforced requirement for social media companies in Pakistan.

items.author: Anjali Jain
items.content:
UPI transaction volume rose 5.8% MoM to a record 25.47 Bn in October from 24.07 Bn in September, according to data released by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI).
The value of transactions processed through the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) increased 7.4% MoM to a record ₹31.53 Lakh Cr from ₹29.37 Lakh Cr in the previous month.
On a YoY basis, transaction volume grew 23%, while transaction value rose 16%.
October marked the first month in which UPI processed more than 25 Bn transactions and payments worth over ₹30 Lakh Cr. Average daily transaction value also crossed ₹1 Lakh Cr for the first time.
UPI processed an average of 822 Mn transactions a day in October, up from 802 Mn in September. Average daily transaction value increased to ₹1,01,707 Cr from ₹97,913 Cr.
The daily averages provide a clearer comparison of payment activity because October had 31 days against September’s 30. Based on NPCI’s figures, average daily volume increased 2.5% MoM, while average daily value rose 3.9%.
The increase coincided with the festive season. October’s growth followed a marginal decline in September, when transaction volume fell 1.8% MoM and transaction value dropped 1.5%.
Merchant Charges On Horizon
The latest figures come ahead of the proposed introduction of merchant discount rate (MDR) charges on select UPI payments.
The NPCI deferred the rollout, originally scheduled for October 15, until after Diwali, saying the new implementation date would be notified separately.
MDR is the fee merchants pay banks and payment companies to process digital transactions. Under the revised framework, eligible person-to-merchant (P2M) payments above ₹2,000 will attract a 0.4% charge, capped at ₹300 for transactions of ₹75,000 and above. Person-to-person (P2P) payments will remain free of MDR.
The revised structure would create a revenue stream for banks and payment service providers processing eligible transactions, potentially improving monetisation across the UPI ecosystem. However, merchant bodies have raised concerns over the additional payment acceptance costs and sought relief ahead of the rollout.

items.author: Rizwana Omer
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
WhatsApp text actions are now rolling out to some Android and iOS users. The feature spots phone numbers, dates, addresses and email addresses in a message and underlines them with a dotted line.
Tapping the underline opens a small menu of shortcuts; the rollout is expected from 2 November 2026.
The Dotted Underline That Turns Chat Text Into a Button
The underline appears on both incoming and outgoing messages. Users who tap it see a popup. The detected text shows at the top, so people can confirm the app picked up the right thing.
Anyone who doesn’t want the shortcut can ignore it and keep chatting. The feature is passive by design.
Four Kinds of Text, Each With Its Own Menu
What the popup offers depends on what WhatsApp found.
Phone numbers: copy, add to contacts, or call through the phone carrier. Business numbers also show the business’s information.
Dates and times: add to the calendar, copy, or create an event inside WhatsApp.
Addresses: copy or open in a map.
Email addresses: open in the mail app, or copy.
No AI Involved: How the Detection Works
WhatsApp builds these suggestions on the device. As per WABetaInfo, the app uses regular expressions, a method that scans text for fixed patterns such as the shape of an email address.
Because the scanning stays local, WhatsApp never receives the message content or the suggestion. This means the feature leaves end-to-end encryption unchanged.
That choice stands out at a time when many chat features lean on cloud AI. A pattern matcher is less flexible than a language model. It is also easier to verify and keeps message text on the phone.
The Feedback Button That Doesn’t Send Your Message
After someone uses an action, WhatsApp asks whether it was useful. A “not useful” answer opens two follow-up choices: the app detected the wrong text, or the action wasn’t needed. This sends only a flag and never the message content. WhatsApp can use the flags to improve how reliably it detects formats.
Why the Events Hub Needed This Shortcut
The timing connects to another change. WhatsApp recently added an Events hub in the app settings, where users can create and review events with a name, date, time, location and optional call link.
The “create event” action on a detected date gives that hub a way in from the chat itself. A date typed in a message becomes a calendar entry or a WhatsApp event in a few taps.
The Bigger Point: A Smarter Chat That Doesn’t Read Your Chat
Most messaging features that add intelligence do it by processing more of the user’s data. This one adds convenience while keeping processing on the device.
That makes it a useful test case. If people use these shortcuts, WhatsApp gains a way to make chats more useful without changing its privacy claims.
The limit is accuracy. A regex tool cannot guess meaning, only match shapes. The feedback flag suggests WhatsApp expects misses, and how it handles them will decide whether the underline helps or distracts.

Pakistan has earned international recognition for its efforts to advance technology entrepreneurship, with Ignite – National Technology Fund’s National Incubation Centers (NICs) Program winning the Digital Policy & Regulatory Excellence Award at the Commonwealth Telecommunications Organisation (CTO) Digital Excellence Awards 2026 in London.
Presented during the CTO’s 125th anniversary celebrations, the award recognises the NIC Program as a significant initiative in fostering innovation, entrepreneurship and digital economic development. Pakistan also secured recognition in two other categories, distinguishing itself among the organisation’s 56 member countries.
The achievement reflects Pakistan’s growing commitment to building an inclusive, sustainable and globally competitive technology ecosystem.
Leadership and Vision
The recognition highlights the strategic leadership of Federal Minister for Information Technology & Telecommunication, Ms. Shaza Fatima Khawaja, whose focus on digital transformation, entrepreneurship and institutional collaboration has helped reinforce Pakistan’s technology development agenda.
Her emphasis on empowering young innovators, strengthening the startup ecosystem and creating opportunities in the digital economy aligns with Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif’s vision of a digitally empowered Pakistan.
Under the Ministry’s guidance, Ignite has continued to develop the NIC Program as a flagship national initiative, connecting entrepreneurial talent with the resources, expertise and networks needed to establish and scale technology-driven businesses.
The international distinction underscores the importance of sustained policy commitment, effective institutional leadership and public-private collaboration in advancing Pakistan’s digital ambitions.
Transforming Innovation into Opportunity
Through its nationwide network, the NIC Program provides startups with structured incubation, mentorship, business development support, industry connections and access to potential investors.
By bringing together public investment and private-sector expertise, the program helps bridge the gap between innovative ideas and commercially viable enterprises.
Its contribution extends beyond individual startups. By supporting emerging technologies, encouraging entrepreneurship and expanding access to innovation opportunities, the NIC Program is helping strengthen the foundations of a knowledge-based economy.
The award also recognises the collective efforts of Ignite’s leadership, NIC operators, consortium partners, mentors, investors and entrepreneurs who continue to contribute to Pakistan’s evolving startup ecosystem.
A Milestone for Pakistan’s Digital Future
The CTO recognition is more than an international accolade. It demonstrates how sustained investment in entrepreneurial infrastructure, institutional capacity and innovation can contribute to national economic development.
For Pakistan, the achievement offers an opportunity to build further momentum through stronger industry partnerships, greater investment linkages and continued support for technology entrepreneurs.
As the country pursues its digital transformation agenda, the success of the NIC Program provides an encouraging example of how strategic public-sector initiatives can help unlock private-sector potential.
Ultimately, Pakistan’s technological future will be shaped by the ingenuity of its people and the opportunities created for them to succeed. Ignite’s NIC Program is helping turn that potential into enterprise, innovation and economic; opportunity—earning recognition well beyond Pakistan’s borders.

items.author: Rizwana Omer
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The Anthropic AI watermark is about to cover a lot more of what Anthropic’s chatbot writes. From November 3, text from Claude Mythos 5, Opus 4.7, Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 will carry the same hidden marker. The marker was first limited to the company’s latest models.
Four More Claude Models Get a Hidden Signature on November 3
Anthropic first introduced the watermark after EU legislators pushed for AI-generated text to carry a hidden mark that could help tell human writing from machine writing.
The first rollout reached only the newest Claude versions. The November 3 update widens it to four older models.
Anthropic says the technology is the same one already running in Opus 5.5. The company has not said, in the details reported so far, why it is extending the watermark now.
What “an Imperceptible Pattern in Word Choice” Means
Anthropic describes the watermark as an imperceptible pattern in word choice. In practice, text watermarks of this kind nudge which words a model picks, in a way no reader would notice. A detector with the right key can later check whether the pattern is present.
Anthropic says the pattern does not change the accuracy or readability of Claude’s output. It also says the watermark carries no identifying information about the user or organization working with Claude.
That last point matters for privacy. On Anthropic’s account, the marker would show that text came from Claude, not who asked for it.
Why Lawyers, Novelists and Researchers Keep Making Headlines
The story is tied to a wider pattern of people hiding AI use. It lists lawyers caught using AI-generated citations, novelists caught relying on AI to write entire books, and scientists caught using AI in peer review.
These cases have one thing in common. The tool worked as designed, and the person using it skipped the checking and then said nothing.
AI creates a strong incentive to cut corners and lie about it. A watermark does not stop that behavior. It only makes it easier to catch.
What Readers in Pakistan Should Watch
The report does not say whether the watermark applies by region or to every user worldwide. Anthropic’s notice does not mention country limits.
Pakistani freelancers, students, translators and content writers who use Claude should assume their output may carry the marker. Anyone who delivers client work or submits assignments should check what disclosure rules apply to them.
Whether a detection tool will be available to publishers, universities or employers is also unclear. The report does not say.
The Real Test: Does a Watermark Change Behavior?
The older-model expansion closes an obvious gap. When only the newest models carried the marker, someone who wanted unmarked text could have used an older Claude version. Covering Opus 4.6, Opus 4.7 and Sonnet 4.6 removes that easy route.
It does not remove every route. Rewriting a passage by hand or running it through another tool may weaken a word-choice pattern. The reporting does not say how well the mark survives edits.
The larger question is who can read it. A watermark only matters if someone can check for it, and Anthropic has not said, in the reported details, who gets that ability. Without a detector in the hands of editors, schools or courts, the marker stays a promise to regulators.
The next signals are whether Anthropic publishes a way to verify the mark and how EU rules shape what it must offer. Those will show whether this is a compliance step or a real change in how AI text gets labelled.

Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The Honor 700 Pro and the standard Honor 700 will reportedly support a 200mm teleconverter, a lens attachment that extends a phone camera’s zoom reach. The claim comes from the tipster Digital Chat Station (DCS) on Weibo, and Honor has not confirmed it.
The 700 series is expected to launch in China next month. Treat everything below as rumor until Honor says otherwise.
The Lens Add-On That Could Define the 700 Series
A teleconverter is a small optical accessory that attaches to a camera to magnify the view beyond what the built-in lens delivers. Phone makers usually rely on periscope telephoto cameras for zoom. A teleconverter adds optics on top of that.
Leaker, DCS says both the 700 and the 700 Pro support a 200 mm version. The tip does not explain how the attachment connects or whether Honor will sell it separately.
A second tipster, Smart Pikachu, also lists teleconverter support among the series’ selling points. Two independent mentions make the claim more credible, but neither source has shown a product image.
A Spec Sheet Built Around the Camera and the Battery
DCS lists several other features for the series: a mid-size screen with ultra-narrow bezels, a large battery, a built-in rear screen and a Snapdragon chipset. The tipster does not name the exact chip.
A periscope telephoto camera is also on the list. That fits the teleconverter story, since both are about reaching distant subjects.
Last week DCS gave more detail on the 700 Pro’s engineering prototype. It reportedly has a 6.57-inch 1.5K screen with ultra-narrow bezels on all four sides and a 1.72-inch rear screen.
The camera setup is said to be a 200MP main sensor and a 50MP periscope telephoto lens. The battery is around 9,000 mAh, which DCS says is the largest in the series.
DCS also says there are three 700 models in total. The colors roughly translate to Cool White, Clear Sky, Blues and Pink Mist.
Reservations, Live Photos and a Celebrity Tease
Smart Pikachu says reservations for the 700 series are about to open. The tipster lists 100MP-class imaging, ultra-long battery life, a “creative” rear screen and a trendy design.
Live Photos from both the front and rear cameras are also on the list. The tipster mentions a new brand ambassador as well.
The post was tagged with the name of Chinese actress Ju Jingyi, which hints at her as the ambassador. DCS also mentions an “A-list celebrity”, but neither tipster names the person directly, so the link is an inference.
Who Is This For Outside China?
Nothing in the tips mentions markets beyond China. For readers in Pakistan, that means no confirmed global release, local pricing or warranty plan.
If the series does expand later, the teleconverter is the part to watch. An accessory like that depends on local stock, and buyers would want to know whether it ships in the box or is sold separately.
The Bigger Story: Honor Is Selling a System, Not a Sensor
Camera marketing has leaned on megapixel counts for years. A teleconverter shifts the argument from the sensor to the optics around it.
Honor appears to be building a package: a 200MP main camera, a periscope lens, a lens attachment and a rear screen. The rear screen could act as a viewfinder for rear-camera selfies, though the tips don’t say that.
That approach carries risk. A removable lens works only if it is easy to attach and the image quality justifies carrying it. The leaks say nothing about either point.
The next signals to watch are Honor’s official teasers and any hands-on images. They will show whether the teleconverter is a real feature or a footnote.

items.content:
Indian VCs And The Deeptech Dilemma
Skyroot has proved that homegrown startups can build rockets, but the bigger challenge may lie in funding them. A recent viral critique of Indian venture capitalists has reignited the debate over deeptech funding gaps, risk appetite of investors and slow diligence.
Founder Grievances: For many early stage founders, deeptech funding in India remains plagued by prolonged due diligence, demands for commercial traction before validation and an over-reliance on founder pedigree. Their criticism is aimed at the current system, which may be underwriting very little genuine technological risk and backing a handful of startups.
Concentration Problem: Data adds further nuance to the debate. Deeptech funding surged 176% YoY in Q3 2026, but the deal count barely moved. This is because most of the capital was heavily concentrated among a few players and that too in Bengaluru. The pattern suggests that the capital is largely flowing to technically validated companies, while early stage founders pursuing unproven scientific experiments still struggle to secure their first cheque.
Why Investors Hesitate? Indian VCs have historically been hesitant towards deeptech bets due to the sector’s long gestation cycles, uncertain exits, specialised diligence and substantial follow-on capital. Venture funds also operate under pressure from limited partners to mint returns and liquidity within defined timelines. As a result, most VCs hesitate to underwrite these uncertain scientific bets.
Changing Ecosystem: However, the picture is not entirely bleak. Founder-led vehicles and specialist funds are expanding and raising big bucks for moonshots. Government initiatives, like the ₹1 Lakh Cr RDI Fund, are also creating more optimism around deeptech. But capital alone will not solve the problem as local frontier ventures still need stronger follow-on funding, patient limited partners and the corporate willing to buy early products.
Indian founders have proved that they can build rockets, but can VCs now step in and show that they can finance these moonshot bets? Let’s find out…
From The Editor’s Desk
Weekly Funding Rundown
Indian startups cumulatively raised $130.2 Mn last week, down 29% from $184 Mn in the preceding week. However, deal count zoomed 88% week-on-week to 32. Cent and Simplismart took the biggest cheques home at $15 Mn and $14 Mn, respectively.
Ecommerce emerged as the most funded sector last week, bagging $33 Mn across nine deals. Following suit were AI ventures, which bagged $30 Mn across five deals.
On the investor front, Blume Ventures and Antler emerged as the most active investors last week and backed three startups each.
E2W Sales In October
Electric two-wheeler registrations grew a marginal 2.9% month-on-month to 2.1 Lakh units in October. Sales also rose 48% YoY from 1.4 Lakh units a year earlier.
Legacy giants TVS Motor and Hero MotoCorp recorded gains and improved their market share to 27.2% and 13.4%, respectively. However, Bajaj Auto reported a decline in sales in October, which led to its market share falling to 21.7% from 23.4% in September.
Growth also tapered off for new-age EV makers in October. Ather’s registrations declined 1.8% to 30,380 units from 30,942 units in September, while its market share slipped to 14.2%. Ola Electric’s sales also tanked 13.7% MoM to 11,614 units last month.
Kickback Allegations At Flipkart
Walmart has launched a probe into allegations that employees at the ecommerce giant received over ₹150 Cr in kickbacks from vendors. The charges have been directed against employees in Flipkart’s smartphones and luggage and travel accessories divisions.
The complaints allege the certain employees accepted payments and favours from vendors in exchange for preferential treatment on the ecommerce platform, including greater visibility that helped drive sales.
This is Walmart’s third investigation into alleged financial misconduct at Flipkart in the past three years. A previous probe resulted in three dismissals two-and-a-half years ago, while another investigation found wrongdoing by an employee barely six months ago.
eMudhra & Accountability
The cybersecurity firm came under fire last month after researchers discovered that its private keys were weak and could be recovered in under a second. The row saw eMudhra exit the global TLS certificate business altogether.
The episode demonstrates that global browser makers, rather than local regulators, became the first line of accountability for eMudhra. This raises a governance question for India: who investigates and prevents a similar failure domestically?
Experts now flag that eMudhra’s exit means that Indian websites may increasingly depend on foreign certificate authorities for trust. This could affect India’s digital sovereignty and its ability to build a domestic public-key infrastructure ecosystem.
Bullish Week For Startup Stocks
Of the 69 new-age tech stocks under Inc42’s coverage, 40 gained between 0.2% and 26.8%, last week. However, the remaining 29 declined by up to 22.3%. Startup stocks largely saw gains as quarterly earnings drove sharp moves in individual counters.
Ather Energy and Zetwerk emerged as the biggest gainers, while shares of CarTrade and AceVector shed the most. The combined market-cap of these 69 stocks jumped to $160.9 Bn at the end of last week, up 5.7% from $152.3 Bn in the week-ago period.
Going forward, investors will track the upcoming US midterm elections, Brent crude oil prices, geopolitical developments and quarterly earnings for market cues this week.
upliance.ai Eyes $4 Mn
The D2C home appliance maker in advanced talks to raise $3 Mn to $4 Mn in its Series A round. The fundraise will likely see participation from a fresh investor, while existing backers, including Khosla Ventures, will also double down.
Founded in 2021, upliance.ai sells AI-powered kitchen appliances like food processors and air fryers. The D2C brand had last raised ₹34 Cr in a seed round led by Khosla Ventures in 2024 at a valuation of ₹143 Cr.
The development comes amid growing activity in India’s smart kitchen appliances market, which is being driven by growing demand for automated products and rising disposable incomes. The space is projected to become a $3 Bn opportunity by 2032.
Inc42 Markets
Inc42 Startup Spotlight
How D-Propulse Is Rethinking Jet Engines
India has pursued indigenous jet-engine capability for decades now, but to no avail. This has created heavy dependence on overseas vendors and costly testing. D-Propulse is betting on a new technology to build lighter, cheaper propulsion for high-speed drones and missiles.
The RDE Approach: Founded in 2025, D-Propulse is developing rotating detonation engines (RDEs), which use supersonic detonation waves to generate thrust. It has already tested a 5 kN air-breathing RDE that is currently at technology readiness level-5. The startup claims its engine will be 15-25% more efficient and at least 60% less expensive than conventional ramjets.
Eye On The Prize: To scale its ambitions, the startup is also building a 5,000+ sq ft combustor test facility at IIT Madras, with air mass flow capacity of around 10 kg/sec and an in-house HPC cluster. It is also exploring infrastructure rental as an early revenue stream while its jet engine business takes shape.
Building For Defence: D-Propulse is targeting the Indian Armed Forces as its intended first customers. It now plans to conduct flight tests between June and December 2027 and limited series production by the end of 2028. The pre-revenue startup also plans to raise a Series A round by early next year.
With the global RDE opportunity projected to surpass $2.4 Bn by 2030, can D-Propulse build commercially viable jet engines for India?

items.title: Vietnam's Son Doong: world's largest cave holds jungle, found by local in 1990
items.summary: Venture into the depths of Vietnam's Son Doong Cave, where a hidden world unfolds beneath ancient limestone. Initially stumbled upon by Ho Khanh in 1990, it wasn’t until 2009 that this enchanting cavern was fully mapped, revealing colossal rock formations and a flowing river carved by nature over eons. Since 2013, tours have allowed adventurers to glimpse this delicate ecosystem while promoting sustainable tourism efforts.

Initially stumbled upon by Ho Khanh in 1990, it wasn’t until 2009 that this enchanting cavern was fully mapped, revealing colossal rock formations and a flowing river carved by nature over eons.
