items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
Pakistan is well ahead in operational readiness to counter drone threats from Afghanistan and India and has the capability to intercept any drones sent across its borders, Inter-Services Public Relations Director General Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said, adding that the military was incorporating artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies to keep pace with the changing nature of warfare.
The remarks, made during a wide-ranging interview with an international outlet on Friday, were shared by state media on Sunday amid continuing tensions between Islamabad and Kabul.
During the interview on Friday, Lieutenant General Chaudhry said the Pakistan Army was adapting to developments in conventional and non-contact warfare, including drone operations, cyber capabilities and long-range munitions. He added that Pakistani forces had brought down dozens of sophisticated Indian drones during the previous conflict with India.
Director General Inter-Services Public Relations Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry has said that India is the biggest sponsor of terrorism in Pakistan, while the Afghan Taliban regime is acting as a proxy.@OfficialDGISPR @PakistanFauj @GovtofPakistan #DGISPR… pic.twitter.com/ZsKlYnGps8
— Radio Pakistan (@RadioPakistan) November 1, 2026
Asked whether Pakistan was concerned about the Afghan Taliban's use of drones, particularly in light of the Houthis' use of the technology against Saudi Arabia, DG ISPR said the character of warfare had changed and the military was adapting accordingly.
He stated that the army was preparing for developments in both contact and non-contact warfare, including cyber operations, drones and long-range munitions, while assessing the capabilities needed to address present and future challenges.
He added that the proliferation of non-contact warfare capabilities among non-state actors, including the Taliban, groups referred to as Khawarij and the Houthis, posed a threat to all countries. "These states will have to reconsider and re-evaluate their security architecture," he said.
Asked whether he feared a situation similar to that between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia developing between Afghanistan and Pakistan, he said Afghanistan's drone capabilities were not indigenous.
"There is no drone industry, there is no technology of that sort in Afghanistan. So it's been provided by the sponsors, the terror sponsors, because the biggest terror sponsor here is India," he said.
He alleged that the Afghan Taliban were acting as India's proxy in the context of terrorism in Pakistan.
Read: DG ISPR says Pakistan ‘cautiously optimistic’ on Iran-US mediation, warns against spoilers
Referring to the previous conflict with India, he said New Delhi had sent dozens of sophisticated drones, which Pakistani forces had brought down.
"So we are much ahead where we stand in our own operational readiness," he said, adding that Afghanistan could attempt to send drones but Pakistan had the capability to intercept them.
He also said Afghanistan could not absorb the retaliation Pakistan was capable of delivering.
Asked whether Pakistan's military used artificial intelligence to identify targets, as well as other emerging technologies, Lt Gen Chaudhry said the army was incorporating all technologies required to keep pace with the changing nature of warfare.
He said the rapid transformation of warfare and the pace at which new technologies were being introduced meant professional armies could not afford to fall behind.
However, he declined to discuss specific applications of artificial intelligence, quantum technology and cyber capabilities, saying he could not disclose how the military was using them.
"We use all technologies, absorbing all sorts of technologies that are essential in the changing character of war," he said.
"We are using all sorts of technologies. We are a technology-savvy army," he added.
He again alleged that the Afghan Taliban's drone capabilities had been provided by their sponsors, particularly India, arguing that Afghanistan had neither a drone industry nor technology of its own.
Also Read: Security forces respond to unprovoked firing from Afghan border posts: DC South Waziristan
Lt Gen Chaudhry also described India as the "prime contractor" behind militant groups operating against Pakistan, with the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA) acting as its proxies.
Responding to reports that the Afghan Taliban had accused Pakistan of hosting anti-Taliban elements and coordinating former Afghan government generals and other groups opposed to the regime, he rejected the allegations and accused the Taliban of using non-state actors, militias and mercenaries to pursue their objectives.
"So that's how you play the victim card. They are apt in using non-state actors, militias, mercenaries for their objectives. So they think everyone does that," he said.
"We are a state. Afghanistan is not a state. Afghanistan is still being run by a non-state actor. It's a regime."
He said decades of foreign intervention by the Soviet Union and the United States had allowed multiple agencies and proxy groups to establish roots in Afghanistan. The country, he added, had experienced more than 40 years of foreign interventions, making its situation different from that of Pakistan and other states.
"The forces have gone physically, but still that front of Afghan Taliban is a proxy to multiple parties," he said.
He said the presence of these groups was not merely his assessment but was also reflected in United Nations reports and intelligence assessments by the United States and several other countries.
"How could so many terrorist organisations, the whole alphabet, thrive over there?" he asked.
Questioning the credibility of allegations made by the Afghan Taliban, he cited previous claims by the regime that a person picked up from a street in Kabul was a Pakistani pilot captured in Shalwar Kameez and that Pakistani tanks had been seized.
"It's the same regime which the world has seen, some day picked up a random person from the street in Kabul and said this is a Pakistani pilot that we have captured in Shalwar Kameez. It's the same regime that paraded its own tanks in the streets and said that we have captured Pakistani tanks," he said.
He said Pakistan had drawn conclusions from its experience and believed that armed groups, militias and mercenaries could not be tolerated in any state.
Asked whether isolating the Taliban would help Afghanistan, particularly amid concerns about the impact of the opium ban and reduced foreign assistance to farmers, Lt Gen Chaudhry said Pakistan was not advocating the country's isolation.
Instead, he said, the international community and regional countries should ask the Taliban authorities to act like a state and stop producing opium and supporting militant groups.
"Afghanistan is producing right now; it has only two products: terrorism and drugs. And both are not good for the world and the region and everyone," he said.
He stressed that engagement with Afghanistan was necessary and said Pakistan was also engaging with the authorities in Kabul. However, he said Islamabad demanded that Afghan territory should not be used to support terrorism inside Pakistan.
"We only ask you that don't support terrorism inside Pakistan. Stop harbouring the terrorist leaders," he said.
He alleged that militant groups operating inside Pakistan received their instructions and weapons from Afghanistan. He also claimed that Afghan citizens, including personnel of the Afghan Taliban regime, had been found among militant formations targeted by Pakistani forces.
"We ask them not to do it. If you do it, then there will be a cost, and we are capable of imposing that cost," he said, adding that Pakistan had a clear strategy for imposing such a cost.
The remarks came amid strained relations between Pakistan and Afghanistan due to recurring cross-border terrorism and security concerns. Islamabad has repeatedly urged the Afghan Taliban administration to prevent terrorist organisations, particularly the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), from using its territory to launch attacks inside Pakistan.
A day earlier, the Information Ministry maintained that the Taliban regime’s continued refusal to address terrorism was the principal barrier to normal relations and took issue with Kabul’s characterisation of the matter.
“The Taliban leadership continues to blame Islamabad’s policies while conveniently ignoring the single most important issue poisoning bilateral relations: its persistent failure to address terrorism emanating from Afghan soil,” the statement said.
Pakistan maintains that the terrorist nexus extended beyond the movement of terrorists across the border to their training, arming and operational support.
Security officials estimate that up to 70 per cent of the Fitna al-Khawarij terrorists infiltrating Pakistan were of Afghan origin. They further claim that the Taliban regime had allowed leftover US and NATO weapons to reach terrorist groups, including Fitna al-Khawarij and Fitna al-Hindustan.
The security establishment also linked the escalation in attacks to the presence of terrorist infrastructure inside Afghanistan.
In 2026 alone, terrorism emanating from Afghan soil claimed the lives of 1,327 Pakistanis and injured another 2,484, according to figures cited by Pakistani authorities.
Read More: Pakistan warns Afghanistan after Kohat attack, says it can eliminate terror threats ‘wherever they are’
Officials said that whenever Pakistani forces targeted terrorist hideouts, the Taliban regime instead moved to defend the militants and their sanctuaries rather than dismantling the infrastructure. The issue, Pakistan has argued, was not confined to TTP.
UN assessments have continued to document the presence of several other militant organisations in Afghanistan, including al Qaeda, the East Turkestan Islamic Movement and Islamic State-Khorasan, reinforcing concerns about the broader militant ecosystem operating from Afghan territory.

items.title: How to Download and Use Instagram on Apple TV: A Step-by-Step Guide
items.summary: Instagram's dedicated Apple TV app brings Reels, longer videos and live shows to the television screen. Users can search for creators and resume playback across supported devices. According to the ministry's website, applicants must have at least 5,000 Qatari riyals in cash or an equivalent amount available through a valid credit card to qualify for the visa.
"The applicant should hold the amount of (5000 QR) or the equivalent of a valid credit card," the ministry stated.
Visitors must also present a confirmed return ticket and hold a passport with at least six months' validity.
#Qatar offers #Pakistanis an on-arrival tourist #visa valid for 30 days. @MOI_QatarEn lists the requirements, including funds and a return ticket.⁠ pic.twitter.com/5o1ZfZWfhw
— Doha News (@dohanews) November 1, 2026
The ministry further specified that travellers arriving directly from Pakistan must provide a polio vaccination certificate.
"Those coming directly from Pakistan should receive a certificate of vaccination against polio," it said.
The visa is valid for 30 days and can be extended for a further 30 days, provided travellers have a confirmed return ticket before the extension is granted, according to the ministry.
Meanwhile, Pakistani nationals travelling to Qatar for business purposes can arrange visits only through accredited companies.

items.title: Meesho’s Next Monetisation Engines
items.summary:
Meesho has spent much of its journey building scale in India’s value commerce market. Its low-cost marketplace model has helped it expand its reach beyond large cities, bring more sellers online and attract consumers looking for affordable products. items.author: Gargi Sarkar
items.content:
Meesho has spent much of its journey building scale in India’s value commerce market. Its low-cost marketplace model has helped it expand its reach beyond large cities, bring more sellers online and attract consumers looking for affordable products. But as the company moves towards its next phase of growth, the goalpost is shifting from acquiring users and expanding transactions to extracting more value from the ecosystem it has built.
Advertising is emerging as one of the key opportunities. With 284 Mn annual transacting users (ATUs) and 1.13 Mn annual transacting sellers as of Q2 FY27, Meesho has a large marketplace that it can potentially monetise through sponsored listings and other advertising products. The company expects advertising to become a more meaningful contributor to its revenue mix from FY28.
At the same time, Meesho is exploring newer business lines, including lending products for consumers and sellers, while expanding branded commerce through Meesho Mall and discovery-led shopping through content commerce. These initiatives could open up additional revenue streams, although their contribution to the company’s financials remains at an early stage.
The opportunity comes as Meesho makes progress on its marketplace economics.
Its Q2 FY27 performance shows that the core marketplace is growing and its operating economics are improving. Revenue from operations increased 34% year-on-year to ₹4,119.9 Cr, while net merchandise value (NMV) grew 23% to ₹12,911 Cr.
In the reported quarter, its contribution margin improved to 6% of net merchandise value (NMV), compared with 4.6% in the previous quarter and 3.3% a year earlier. Its marketplace adjusted EBITDA loss also narrowed to ₹130.5 Cr from ₹371 Cr in Q2 FY26.
However, management cautioned that the 6% contribution margin recorded in Q2 FY27 should not be viewed as the new normal, as some of the logistics efficiency gains may be passed on to consumers and sellers to support growth.
The question, therefore, is whether Meesho can turn its growing consumer and seller base into higher-value revenue streams without compromising the affordability that underpins its marketplace.
Advertising: Can Meesho Monetise Its Scale?
Advertising offers Meesho a way to generate more revenue from the traffic and transactions already flowing through its platform. As its user base and seller ecosystem expand, the company has an opportunity to charge sellers for better visibility and access to consumers who are actively browsing products.
For sellers, sponsored placements can help products stand out in a crowded marketplace. For Meesho, they can create an additional revenue stream without requiring it to take ownership of inventory or significantly change its core marketplace model. This is particularly relevant in a business where affordability and low prices remain central to customer acquisition.
The scale of the opportunity is supported by Meesho’s operating metrics. Its ATUs grew 21% year-on-year to 284 Mn in Q2 FY27, while annual transacting sellers increased 60% to 1.13 Mn. Placed orders rose 17% to 819 Mn during the quarter, and NMV grew 23% to ₹12,911 Cr.
“A larger marketplace gives Meesho more opportunities to connect seller advertising with consumer discovery. However, the size of its user base alone does not determine how much it can earn from ads. The company will need to demonstrate that sellers are willing to spend consistently on advertising and that paid placements generate measurable returns through product views and orders,” an ecommerce analyst said.
Advertising monetisation is still at a relatively early stage. On the Q2 FY27 earnings call, it said the sequential improvement in contribution margin was primarily driven by logistics efficiencies, rather than a significant increase in advertising monetisation. It also expects advertising to become a more meaningful contributor as a percentage of NMV in FY28.
Motilal Oswal expects higher advertising monetisation to support contribution margin expansion from FY28, citing seller demand for advertising and the potential to improve the platform’s monetisation.
However, Meesho will have to balance monetisation with the shopping experience. Its value-commerce positioning depends on offering consumers affordable products and a wide selection. If sponsored placements make discovery less relevant or push sellers towards higher advertising expenditure that is eventually reflected in product prices, the company could risk weakening some of the advantages of its model.
The other consideration is the distribution of advertising benefits across sellers. Larger and more established sellers may have greater capacity to spend on visibility, while smaller sellers could find it harder to compete for prominent placements. Meesho will need to build an advertising ecosystem that delivers returns for sellers across different sizes and categories, the analyst added..
The key monitorable, therefore, is not simply the growth in advertising revenue, but how much of that revenue Meesho can retain as incremental contribution after accounting for the cost of serving the marketplace. If advertising can scale without materially increasing operating costs or affecting affordability, it could become a more durable margin lever.
New Initiatives: Lending, Mall And Content Commerce
Beyond advertising, Meesho is looking to deepen its engagement with consumers and sellers through a wider set of services. These initiatives could increase the number of ways in which the company earns from its ecosystem, although they are at different stages of development.
One area is lending. During the earnings call, management confirmed that Meesho is working on both consumer-side and seller-side lending products. The company is expanding its network of non-banking financial company (NBFC) partners and is also looking to work with banks.
For consumers, access to credit could potentially support purchases on the platform, while seller financing could help merchants manage working capital and grow their businesses. If structured effectively, these offerings could strengthen Meesho’s relationship with both sides of the marketplace.
However, the company has not disclosed lending-related assets under management, revenue targets or the expected financial contribution of these products. It is also not clear how much of the lending opportunity Meesho intends to capture directly versus through its lending partners. For now, it is better viewed as an emerging business opportunity than an established monetisation engine.
Meesho Mall and content commerce represent another route to deepen marketplace engagement. Meesho Mall, which had around 1,800 brands in Q2 FY27, recorded 81% YoY growth in NMV. NMV from Tier 3 and smaller markets grew 89%, while around half of Mall customers during the quarter were first-time buyers on the branded-commerce offering.
The growth indicates that Meesho is making progress in bringing branded products to a consumer base that has traditionally been associated with unbranded and lower-priced merchandise. A broader product mix could help the platform attract new customer segments and increase the range of purchases made by existing users.
Content commerce is also expanding. Its NMV grew 160% YoY in Q2 FY27, while the number of content pieces generating orders increased 144% to 2.2 Mn. The ecosystem had more than 4 lakh sellers participating in content-led commerce.
The proposition is to use videos and other content formats to help consumers discover products, rather than relying entirely on search-led shopping. This could create more product discovery opportunities and potentially improve engagement. Meesho has also said that the share of orders coming from discovery-led recommendations has increased, alongside time spent on the platform.
However, rapid growth from these offerings does not automatically translate into a meaningful revenue contribution. Meesho has not disclosed the share of total NMV generated by Mall or Content Commerce, nor has it provided specific monetisation targets for either. Their longer-term value will depend on whether they can increase purchase frequency, attract higher-value transactions and create additional opportunities for advertising.
AI is another part of this effort. Meesho is using AI across product discovery, ranking, fraud prevention and logistics, while also deploying AI agents in engineering and other internal functions. The company said 65% of its engineering pods were operating with one engineer directing AI agents. It reported a 41% reduction in code-review approval time and a reduction in data-science model deployment time from 17 days to three days.
These productivity gains could help the company develop products and improve operations faster. But AI also brings infrastructure costs. Meesho’s GPU footprint increased 150%, while server costs rose to 2.3% of NMV in Q2 FY27 from 1.9% in the previous quarter. Management expects these costs to normalise towards the previous baseline as a percentage of NMV by Q4 FY27, but that remains an expectation to be tested.
The newer initiatives are also still investment-heavy. Management has indicated that it is keeping investments in these businesses within a cap of around ₹200 Cr, while emphasising that product-market fit and unit economics will be important before scaling further. This suggests that Meesho is not yet positioning these offerings as immediate contributors to profitability.
The Profitability Test
The monetisation opportunity has to be seen alongside Meesho’s broader effort to improve its marketplace economics. The company reported a contribution margin of ₹775 Cr in Q2 FY27, up from ₹531 Cr in Q1 FY27. As a percentage of NMV, the margin improved to 6% from 4.6% sequentially.
The improvement was largely driven by lower logistics costs, supported by better order density, network redesign, improved route utilisation and efforts to reduce return-to-origin (RTO) orders. Management also indicated that it intends to recover some of the logistics-related margin spread lost in FY26 towards FY25 levels during FY27.
However, it has cautioned against extrapolating the Q2 contribution margin as the new normal. Some of the savings could be passed on to sellers and consumers through lower prices, while a part may be retained to improve profitability. The timing and extent of this balance will matter as Meesho enters the festive period and continues to invest in growth.
There are also costs that could absorb some of the gains. Meesho’s advertising and sales promotion expenses increased ahead of the festive season, taking growth spending to 2.9% of NMV in Q2 FY27 from 2.1% in Q1. Server costs also rose, reflecting the higher computing requirements of the platform.
The company reported a consolidated adjusted EBITDA loss of ₹172.1 Cr in Q2 FY27, while its consolidated net loss narrowed to ₹132.4 Cr from ₹411.4 Cr a year earlier. Although the marketplace business is moving towards better unit economics, its newer initiatives continue to add to the overall loss.
Cash flow also needs to be viewed over a longer period. Meesho reported positive consolidated free cash flow of ₹345 Cr in Q2 FY27, compared with an outflow of ₹226 Cr in Q1. But its last-twelve-month consolidated free cash flow remained negative at ₹565 Cr. The quarterly improvement was partly supported by seasonal working-capital movements, as collections from consumers ahead of the festive sale preceded settlements with sellers.
This makes the quality and durability of cash generation an important measure of progress. Advertising could help improve margins because it allows Meesho to monetise marketplace activity without taking on inventory. Lending and other initiatives may create additional revenue opportunities, but their economics will depend on partner arrangements, customer adoption and the cost of scaling.
Brokerage views reflect both the opportunity and the execution risks. Motilal Oswal sees advertising as a medium-term margin lever and expects contribution margins to remain well above FY26 levels. Nomura, however, has flagged the possibility of some margin improvement reversing in Q3 FY27 as the company reinvests gains into growth and category expansion during the festive season.
Ultimately, Meesho’s next phase will depend on how effectively it monetises the scale it has already built and whether new businesses can add revenue and improve customer and seller engagement without pushing up costs or weakening Meesho’s low-price proposition. For a platform that has built its position on affordability and scale, monetisation will have to deepen the business without changing what makes it attractive to consumers and sellers.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Pakistan is exploring the development of local microchip technology to improve passport security and strengthen the protection of citizens’ personal information. The initiative was discussed during a meeting between Director General of Immigration and Passports Muhammad Ali Randhawa and a delegation from the National University of Sciences and Technology (NUST).
The meeting focused on research into locally developed microchip technology and its potential use in improving passport data security. The NUST delegation briefed the passport authorities on ongoing research projects aimed at developing microchip technology within Pakistan.
Pakistan Explores Local Microchip Technology to Strengthen Passport Data Security
During the discussion, participants highlighted the importance of developing indigenous technology to reduce reliance on foreign solutions and improve the country’s technological self-sufficiency. They also discussed how locally developed solutions could help protect sensitive information and strengthen national digital security.
NUST Shares Research on Local Microchip Development
Muhammad Ali Randhawa appreciated NUST’s research efforts and stressed the need to develop modern, locally produced technology solutions for securing passport data.
Both sides also discussed opportunities for technical knowledge sharing, joint research projects, and institutional cooperation. They reviewed the possibility of signing a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the Directorate General of Immigration and Passports and NUST to establish a framework for future collaboration.
Pakistan Eyes Modernisation of Passport System
The meeting also explored the potential use of locally developed microchip technology to modernise Pakistan’s passport system.
Such technology could help improve the security of passport information while supporting the country’s broader efforts to strengthen its digital infrastructure.
However, the discussions focused on research, potential cooperation, and future possibilities. No specific timeline or implementation plan for introducing locally developed microchips in Pakistani passports was announced.
The post Pakistan Explores Local Microchip Technology to Strengthen Passport Data Security appeared first on PhoneWorld.

items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) has confirmed that North Korea’s TraderTraitor hacking group was behind last week’s theft of approximately $6.4 billion in cryptocurrency from Binance. The agency has urged cryptocurrency companies and blockchain service providers to block transactions linked to hundreds of wallet addresses associated with the stolen funds.
In a statement issued on Saturday, the FBI revealed that the attackers had been converting much of the stolen cryptocurrency into Ethereum. The agency expects the hackers to continue moving the funds through cryptocurrency swap services and decentralised finance (DeFi) platforms to hide their origins.
FBI Links $6.4 Billion Binance Crypto Hack to North Korea’s TraderTraitor Group
The FBI, along with the U.S. Secret Service (USSS) and the Internal Revenue Service Criminal Investigation division (IRS-CI), has asked private-sector companies to take action against the laundering network. The request covers blockchain node operators, instant exchanges, DeFi services, blockchain analytics companies, and other virtual asset service providers.
The FBI’s notice included more than 600 Ethereum wallet addresses, fewer than 20 Bitcoin addresses, and one Solana address linked to the stolen assets.
North Korea’s TraderTraitor Group Behind Binance Attack
Binance suffered a major security breach on Thursday, resulting in the theft of around $6.4 billion in cryptocurrencies. Several blockchain analytics firms and security experts linked the incident to TraderTraitor, a North Korean hacking group associated with the notorious Lazarus Group.
The Lazarus Group has previously been connected to several major cryptocurrency exchange attacks and other high-profile cybercrime incidents.
Following the breach, stablecoin issuers froze more than $2.4 billion of the stolen funds. However, the attackers have continued moving and laundering a significant portion of the remaining assets.
Binance said on Saturday that it had replenished 90% of the stolen cryptocurrencies. The exchange also announced plans to resume customer withdrawals on Sunday.
Thousands of Wallet Addresses Used to Move Stolen Funds
Although the FBI identified hundreds of cryptocurrency addresses in its warning, blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis believes the attackers have already used thousands of addresses to move the stolen funds.
Chainalysis CEO Jonathan Levin warned that the number could increase to tens of thousands over the coming weeks as the money passes through a wider network of services and intermediaries.
According to Levin, the attackers may turn to cryptocurrency bridges, instant exchanges, and swapping platforms because their usual money-laundering channels may not be able to handle such a large amount.
Chainalysis also reported that the hackers were using automated methods to make it harder to track the stolen cryptocurrency. These techniques involve moving funds between multiple wallet addresses before transferring them to other services.
The analytics firm believes the high volume of transactions indicates the use of automated tools designed to hide the movement and origin of the stolen assets.
The FBI’s warning highlights the growing challenge of tracking large-scale cryptocurrency thefts. Authorities are now relying on exchanges, blockchain service providers, and other industry participants to identify and block transactions connected to the attack.

The centre said polio was an incurable disease but could be prevented through vaccination.
A special anti-polio campaign will begin on Monday (Nov 2) in 97 selected districts across the country and continue until Nov 8, the NEOC said.
During the sub-national immunisation campaign, more than 24 million children under the age of five would be administered polio drops.
The NEOC urged parents to ensure their children received polio drops during every campaign and completed their routine immunisation schedules on time.
It also appealed to all segments of society to play their role in eliminating polio from the country.
Pakistan has reduced polio cases by 99.8%, according to the NEOC. The estimated number of cases fell from around 20,000 in the early 1990s to 31 in 2025. Seven cases have been reported so far this year.
Also Read: First wild polio case of 2026 confirmed in Sindh
According to the NEOC, Pakistan has conducted four large-scale polio vaccination campaigns this year, targeting more than 45 million children. These efforts have been complemented by smaller, targeted oral and injectable vaccination campaigns in high-risk areas.
A subnational campaign in September vaccinated more than 29.3 million children across the country, the NEOC said. The next vaccination campaign is scheduled to run from November 2 to 8, targeting nearly 24 million children in 97 districts, including all districts of Karachi.

items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
A newly discovered Android security vulnerability could allow attackers to crash smartphones by sending a specially crafted text message. Known as the “SMS of Death” exploit, the flaw can interrupt mobile network services, disconnect ongoing calls, and even force affected devices into repeated reboot cycles without requiring users to open or respond to the message on Android.
The vulnerability, identified as CVE-2026-58882, was discovered by security researcher Mark Blaszczyk. He informed Google about the issue in May 2026 and published his findings along with a working demonstration on October 29.
Android ‘SMS of Death’ Exploit Can Crash Phones With a Single Malicious Message
During testing, the researcher successfully reproduced the attack on Google Pixel and Samsung Galaxy smartphones. Although Google has developed a security fix, not all Android devices have received the update.
Which Android Phones Are at Risk?
The vulnerability is not limited to a particular smartphone manufacturer. Instead, the risk depends on the Android version installed on a device and whether it has received the required security patch.
According to the researcher, Google included the fix for Android 14, 15, 16, and 17 in its October 2026 security updates. However, the vulnerability was not specifically mentioned in Google’s October security bulletin.
Older smartphones running Android 12 and 13 have not received the fix, leaving devices without ongoing security support potentially vulnerable.
Android users should check their phone’s security patch level and install the latest available software update. They can usually find this information under Settings, although the exact menu location may vary depending on the smartphone manufacturer.
How Does the ‘SMS of Death’ Exploit Work?
The vulnerability targets the way Android handles WAP Push messages. These messages are processed by the operating system and do not necessarily appear in the phone’s regular SMS inbox.
Normally, users do not need to interact with these messages. However, the researcher discovered that a specially crafted message could trigger an error in Android’s telephony framework. This can crash the system process responsible for maintaining cellular connectivity.
As a result, an affected smartphone may lose its mobile network connection and disconnect ongoing calls. The problem could also affect emergency calls if the crash occurs while someone is contacting emergency services.
The situation can become more serious if a mobile carrier repeatedly attempts to deliver the same malicious message. According to the researcher’s testing, around 20 malicious messages were enough to push a smartphone into a continuous reboot loop.
Can Users Recover Their Phones?
Recovering an affected smartphone may require more than a normal restart. Although a factory reset is one possible option, it is not the only way to fix the problem.
The researcher explained that users could also remove the problematic messages through Android Debug Bridge (ADB). However, this method requires technical knowledge and may be difficult for ordinary smartphone users.
The vulnerability is classified as a denial-of-service attack rather than an attempt to steal passwords, personal information, or other sensitive data. There is currently no confirmed evidence of widespread attacks targeting Android users.
For now, installing the latest available Android security updates remains the most practical precaution. Users with older devices that no longer receive security updates should be particularly cautious.

items.content:
China will adopt a "two launches, lunar orbit rendezvous" architecture for its manned lunar exploration program, a senior engineer said on Saturday, as development work for lunar landing advances steadily.
Wang Xiang, deputy chief designer of China's manned space program and chief designer of the lunar exploration program, outlined the plan at the 7th Manned Space Symposium in Beijing.
Under the scheme, two rockets would separately send the Lanyue lunar lander and Mengzhou crewed spaceship into the Earth-moon transfer orbit, and the two spacecraft would perform a rendezvous and docking in the lunar orbit. Astronauts would then transfer from the Mengzhou spaceship into the Lanyue lander for the descent to the lunar surface and subsequent scientific work.
Wang said the approach matches China's existing technical capabilities and infrastructure, and the separate development of the spaceship and lunar lander can help standardize production and support the formation of a long-term family of vehicles.
While the plan also presents considerable challenges, Wang said the new system for mobilizing resources nationwide is the fundamental advantage for addressing them.
He said the program has established system plans, technical standards and quality requirements under a single development framework, and has adopted an integrated design approach with emphasis on interface verification between subsystems.
So far, the development of the Long March-10 carrier rocket, the Mengzhou crewed spaceship and the Lanyue lunar lander has been progressing smoothly.
Read More: China's first shipborne stealth combat drone completes maiden carrier landing
Major tests already completed include the Mengzhou spaceship's zero-height abort and maximum dynamic pressure escape tests, the Lanyue lander's landing and takeoff test, plus the low-altitude demonstration and validation test for the Long March-10 rocket.
Wang said future lunar exploration should follow the principle of building knowledge and capability before moving into resource utilization, with a prolonged survey phase needed to understand the moon in a steady, step-by-step manner.
He added that manned lunar landing and unmanned lunar exploration share many common elements in key technologies, infrastructure and personnel, and that achievements from the Chang'e lunar exploration program will also support the manned landing effort.

items.content:
A group of international researchers has reported the first fully marine species of stem amphibian, Gerrothorax maritimus, in a recent research article published in the journal Nature Ecology & Evolution.
Based on two nearly complete skeletons measuring at least 737 millimeters from the Late Triassic (about 237 million years ago) discovered in southwest China's Guizhou Province, the researchers reconstructed the appearance of Gerrothorax maritimus: a flattened body covered with heavy bony armor, a broad and flat head, a wide mouth, and sturdy, well-developed gill arches, according to a report by China Science Daily.
More than 8,000 amphibian species exist today, but none of them lives entirely in the sea. Amphibian skin is permeable, which aids respiration but causes water loss in seawater, where high salinity adds physiological challenges.
Some living amphibians can tolerate brackish habitats where freshwater meets seawater, and fossils of ancient species have been found in coastal sediments. But previous evidence was insufficient to confirm that any amphibian ever had a fully marine lifestyle.
Read More: Strange beaked 'hell chicken' is the first fruit-eating dinosaur
Gerrothorax maritimus is therefore recognized as the first stem amphibian known to date to have lived entirely in a marine environment, said Jiang Dayong, the article's corresponding author.
The researchers suggested that Gerrothorax maritimus's flattened body suited life on the seafloor, allowing it to hide in sediments.
The species' heavy bony armor helped prevent water loss through the skin, while adults retained their gills and could breathe underwater, possibly without needing to surface to breathe air with their lungs.
The researchers of this study come from the Geological Museum of Guizhou, Peking University, and the University of California, Davis.

The Saudi-led coalition said on Sunday that it intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile and a drone launched by the Houthis toward southern Saudi Arabia.
In two separate statements on X, coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki said air defences had intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile, followed by an announcement that a drone had also been shot down.
Both were launched by the Houthis toward the kingdom’s southern region, according to the statements.
🔴 BREAKING: The Saudi-led coalition in Yemen says it intercepted and destroyed a drone launched by the Iran-backed Houthi militia toward Saudi Arabia’s southern region. pic.twitter.com/78r34uaw1M
— Al Arabiya English (@AlArabiya_Eng) November 1, 2026
These were the coalition’s first interception announcements on Sunday. Neither statement specified the intended targets or reported casualties or damage.
Early on Sunday, Saudi authorities issued emergency warnings in Abha city and Khamis Mushait governorate in southwestern Saudi Arabia before announcing that the danger had passed in both areas.
​​​​​​​Saudi Arabia has faced repeated missile and drone attacks by the Houthis in recent weeks.
Saudi-led coalition launches operation to ‘neutralise’ Houthi military resources in Yemen
The Saudi-led coalition said on Sunday that it had carried out a military operation to “neutralise vital resources” used by the Houthi group to support its war effort and strengthen its military capabilities, particularly ballistic missiles and drones.
Coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki said in a statement that the operation took place on Sunday morning following continued Houthi attacks against civilians and civilian infrastructure in Yemen and Saudi Arabia.
The coalition’s joint forces command had monitored the Houthis’ “continued use of vital resources to support their war effort and bolster their military capabilities, especially ballistic missiles and drones,” he said.
Coalition: We Have Carried Out Precision Operation to Neutralize Vital Resources Used by the Terrorist Houthi Militia to Support Their War Efforthttps://t.co/g4tdTGYaji#SPAGOV pic.twitter.com/2PS5qoO1Sy
— SPAENG (@Spa_Eng) November 1, 2026
Al-Maliki said the continued attacks posed a direct threat to civilian lives and the safety of civilian infrastructure.
The operation sought to “neutralise” resources used by the group to carry out repeated attacks and threaten the security of Saudi Arabia and Yemen, as well as shipping lanes in the southern Red Sea, he added.
The statement did not identify the targeted locations or specify the nature of the resources it said had been neutralised. It also provided no details on casualties or material damage.
There was no immediate comment from the Houthis.
Since October 5, Yemeni government forces have launched Operation “Dawn of Yemen” to restore state institutions from Houthi control and retake the capital, Sanaa.
Military escalation between government forces and the Houthis resumed in July, killing and wounding thousands and displacing more than a quarter of a million people, according to UN reports.
The escalation ended a period of relative calm that had prevailed in Yemen since April 2022, while the humanitarian crisis has worsened amid continued fighting and displacement.
Yemen has been at war since the Houthis seized Sanaa and several provinces in September 2014, prompting a Saudi-led coalition to intervene in March 2015 in support of the internationally recognised government.
Strike at industrial complex in Saudi Arabia's Dammam causes huge fire: Iranian state media
A strike at an industrial complex in Saudi Arabia's Dammam caused a huge fire on Sunday, Iran's state-run IRNA News Agency reported.
"A Yemeni strike hit an industrial complex in Dammam, eastern Saudi Arabia, sparking a large fire at the facility," IRNA said in a post on X.
A major blaze erupted at an industrial site in Dammam.
A Yemeni strike hit an industrial complex in Dammam, eastern Saudi Arabia, sparking a large fire at the facility. pic.twitter.com/jq7IAhMiBm
— IRNA News Agency ☫ (@IrnaEnglish) November 1, 2026
The development comes amid escalating hostilities between the Iran-backed Houthis and Saudi Arabia, which supports Yemen's internationally recognised government. The two sides have exchanged daily attacks since a fragile truce collapsed over the summer.
Read: Houthis claim strike on strategic Saudi targets
The Houthis on Thursday reported that 12 people had been killed and three others critically injured in what they described as Saudi strikes on residential areas in western Yemen. The group's health ministry said the casualties occurred when homes belonging to two families were targeted in Al-Barah, in Maqbana district.
The claims could not be independently verified. The Houthis had reported at least 14 deaths in Saudi strikes on a petrol station and market on Wednesday, while the group also targeted the airport in Aden, a stronghold of Yemen's internationally recognised government, wounding civilians.
The latest escalation follows a breakdown of the 2022 truce in July, after the Houthis allowed an Iranian plane to land in Sanaa in defiance of Saudi control over Yemeni airspace. The move triggered renewed attacks, with the rebels subsequently targeting Saudi territory, shipping and oil facilities.
The Houthis have also intensified attacks on Saudi Arabia, including strikes on Riyadh airport that forced its closure for two weeks and prompted the cancellation of major events, threatening the kingdom's economic diversification plans.
Read More: Missile attack triggers alerts, blasts in Riyadh
Yemen has endured conflict since 2014, when the Houthis seized the capital, Sanaa, prompting a Saudi-led coalition to intervene the following year in support of the government. More than 1,600 people have been killed and over 275,000 displaced since hostilities resumed, according to United Nations figures.
Yemeni government appoints governors for two provinces partly controlled by Houthis
Separately, Yemen’s Presidential Leadership Council issued two decrees on Sunday appointing new governors for al-Bayda in central Yemen and al-Jawf in the north, two provinces partially controlled by the Houthis.
The government-run version of Saba News Agency said that Major General Hussein al-Ajji Ali al-Awadhi was appointed as governor of al-Bayda. Major General Amin Ali al-Akimi was also named as governor of al-Jawf and commander of its military axis, the agency added.
Al-Awadhi replaces former al-Bayda governor Nasser al-Sawadi, while al-Akimi takes over al-Jawf from al-Awadhi, who had served as the province’s governor.
The appointments come as both provinces face a complex military situation, with clashes continuing between government forces and the Houthi group over control of strategic positions.
The Houthis control most areas of al-Bayda, while control of al-Jawf is divided between the group and government forces.
Al-Bayda holds strategic importance because of its central location in Yemen and its borders with eight other provinces, four in the north and four in the south.
Al-Jawf is also of military and geographic significance because it shares a land border with Saudi Arabia and lies near the Houthi-controlled provinces of Saada, Amran and Sanaa. It also borders Marib and Hadhramaut, which are under government control.
Since October 5, Yemeni government forces have launched Operation “Dawn of Yemen” to restore state institutions from Houthi control and retake the capital, Sanaa.
Military escalation between government forces and the Houthis resumed in July, killing and wounding thousands and displacing more than a quarter of a million people, according to UN reports.
The escalation ended a period of relative calm that had prevailed in Yemen since April 2022, while the humanitarian crisis has worsened amid continued fighting and displacement.
Yemen has been at war since the Houthis seized Sanaa and several provinces in September 2014, prompting a Saudi-led coalition to intervene in March 2015 in support of the internationally recognised government.

Users can choose whether to enable the integration and what information to share. Alibaba said user requests and generated responses would not be used to train its AI models.
The feature will be available on compatible iPhones whose device location and Apple Account region are both set to China.
Alibaba CEO Eddie Wu said the partnership would bring new AI-powered services to Chinese users.
Wang Xiaojie, an AI expert at Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications, said this marked the first time a major global consumer hardware maker had adopted a Chinese large language model as its primary system-level AI backbone in the Chinese market.

Ufone is getting closer to becoming Pakistan’s largest cellular operator as its subscriber base approaches Jazz, with the two companies now separated by just 150,000 users. The development comes as Pakistan’s total cellular subscriber base crossed 211 million in September 2026.
According to data cited by Arif Habib Limited, Pakistan had 211.47 million cellular subscribers in September, compared to 200.56 million in December 2025. This represents an increase of 5.4% in the first nine months of the year, with mobile operators collectively adding 10.91 million subscribers.
Jazz remained Pakistan’s largest cellular operator with 76.44 million subscribers, accounting for 36.15% of the market. Ufone followed closely with 76.29 million subscribers and a market share of 36.08%.
Ufone Closes Gap with Jazz as Pakistan’s Cellular Subscriber Base Crosses 211 Million
The difference between the two operators narrowed to just 150,000 subscribers in September, compared to 210,000 in August. This puts Ufone within reach of overtaking Jazz in terms of total subscribers.
Zong ranked third with 56.62 million subscribers, representing 26.78% of the cellular market. Meanwhile, the Special Communications Organization (SCO) had 2.12 million subscribers, accounting for approximately 1% of the market.
Ufone Leads Subscriber Growth in 2026
Ufone recorded the highest net addition of subscribers among Pakistan’s cellular operators during the first nine months of 2026. The company added 4.83 million subscribers, showing strong growth in its customer base.
Zong ranked second with 3.48 million new subscribers, while Jazz added 2.58 million users during the same period.
The figures indicate that Ufone’s subscriber growth has helped it significantly reduce the gap with Jazz. If this trend continues, the competition for Pakistan’s largest cellular operator could become even closer in the coming months.
Pakistan’s Cellular Market Continues to Grow
Pakistan’s total cellular subscriber base increased by approximately 300,000 users in September, representing monthly growth of 0.14%.
The market has maintained a steady upward trend throughout 2026. The number of subscribers increased from approximately 202.6 million in January to 211.47 million in September.
The latest figures highlight continued growth in Pakistan’s mobile telecom sector, with Ufone emerging as a major competitor to Jazz. The coming months will show whether Ufone can overtake Jazz and secure the top position in the country’s cellular market.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Pakistan’s automotive industry has taken another step towards international expansion as Sazgar Engineering Works Limited has inaugurated a three-wheeler assembly plant in the Philippines. The development marks the company’s entry into the Southeast Asian market and strengthens the international presence of Pakistan-made vehicles.
Philippine President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. inaugurated the new manufacturing facility on Thursday. The Pakistan Embassy in the Philippines announced the development through a post on social media platform X, stating that Pakistani-made three-wheelers had officially entered the Philippine market.
Sazgar Opens First Overseas Three-Wheeler Plant in the Philippines
The embassy facilitated Sazgar’s entry into the country, where the company plans to introduce passenger, commercial and electric three-wheelers. The new facility will assemble both electric vehicles and models powered by internal combustion engines.
According to the Philippine President’s official website, the plant has an annual assembly capacity of approximately 12,000 three-wheeled vehicles. The facility is expected to support the country’s manufacturing sector while expanding access to alternative transportation options.
Speaking at the inauguration ceremony, President Marcos said the project represented an important step towards strengthening local manufacturing and promoting cleaner and more sustainable transportation.
He also appreciated Sazgar’s decision to select the Philippines as its first manufacturing base outside Pakistan and a regional hub for Southeast Asia. He noted that the company had been manufacturing vehicles in Pakistan for more than three decades before choosing the Philippines for its international expansion.
Sazgar Expands Its International Presence
Sazgar Engineering Works Limited is a publicly listed Pakistani automotive manufacturer headquartered in Lahore. The company has established its presence in the international market by exporting three-wheelers and automotive parts to more than 20 countries.
Its export destinations include Japan, the United Arab Emirates, Sri Lanka and Nigeria, among others.
The inauguration of the Philippine plant represents a significant development for Pakistan’s automotive sector. It also provides Sazgar with a manufacturing base closer to other Southeast Asian markets, potentially creating further opportunities for regional expansion.
With an annual assembly capacity of 12,000 vehicles, the new facility could help the company increase its international production and strengthen the position of Pakistani-made three-wheelers in overseas markets.

items.title: Tim Seifert powers New Zealand victory
items.summary:
Tim Seifert narrowly missed a maiden international century but did enough to steer New Zealand to a seven-wicket win over India in the fifth and final T20 on Sunday.
Opener Seifert found some form with the bat, blasting 93 off 50 balls as the home side eased to 195-3 off 18 overs, after Adam Milne had earlier taken 4-19 to restrict the target to 192.
The result wasn't enough for New Zealand to salvage the series, which the tourists won 3-2 after winning the first three games.
Seifert scored just 36 runs across the first four matches but the big-hitting right-hander found his touch at Seddon Park, swinging the game in New Zealand's favour by blasting 11 fours and five sixes.
However, he looked devastated when he played on to Nitish Kumar Reddy in the 16th over, having posted an 18th half-century but failing once again to reach three figures.
Glenn Phillips finished on 65 not out to complete an exceptional series with the bat, which included 107 when New Zealand won game four in Auckland
items.author: AFP
items.content:
Tim Seifert narrowly missed a maiden international century but did enough to steer New Zealand to a seven-wicket win over India in the fifth and final T20 on Sunday.
Opener Seifert found some form with the bat, blasting 93 off 50 balls as the home side eased to 195-3 off 18 overs, after Adam Milne had earlier taken 4-19 to restrict the target to 192.
The result wasn't enough for New Zealand to salvage the series, which the tourists won 3-2 after winning the first three games.
Seifert scored just 36 runs across the first four matches but the big-hitting right-hander found his touch at Seddon Park, swinging the game in New Zealand's favour by blasting 11 fours and five sixes.
However, he looked devastated when he played on to Nitish Kumar Reddy in the 16th over, having posted an 18th half-century but failing once again to reach three figures.
Glenn Phillips finished on 65 not out to complete an exceptional series with the bat, which included 107 when New Zealand won game four in Auckland on Friday.
Phillips's 341 runs across the five games was the most scored by any batsman in a bilateral T20 series.
The previous record was held by England's Phil Salt, who scored 331 runs against the West Indies in 2023.
Earlier, Milne's pace proved hard to handle as India were restricted to 191-8, boosted by rapid half-centuries to Ishan Kishan and captain Shreyas Iyer.
The pair combined for 93 off 7.1 overs for the third wicket after both openers fell cheaply to Milne, before Kishan departed for 61 and Iyer for 50.
The teams will next contest a five-match one-day international series, starting in Auckland on Wednesday, before playing two Tests.
Sports Desk added:
New Zealand’s captain Mitchell Santner said it was a very tight series.
“It was a very tight series. It's a very good team. Those small moments like you said in the first couple games where, we probably could have won those games or should have. So the series could have looked a lot different. But in terms of a cricketing point of view, there's a lot of good stuff,” Santner said.
“The batting was really well, and then the bowling. Guys adapted brilliantly the last couple games. There's a lot of positives. Obviously, the scoreline shows 3-2 to India, but could have been the other way around. Bowlers mixing the lengths Yeah, I thought we mixed it up really nicely. Yorker's wide, a little bit straight with length,” Santner said.
India’s skipper Shreyaz Iyer said it was plausible, honestly. 
“We could have been better, considering the start we got in the middle overs, the way Ishan and I recreated the momentum. And then from there on, we lost back-to-back wickets, and then suddenly pressure on the new batsmen,” he said.
“It wasn't an easy wicket to play on, especially when the ball was seeming and holding a bit, and also skidding through at times. You must have seen a couple of time, myself and Tilak we got out in a similar fashion. It was challenging, especially of that hard length, but to get to 194, it was reasonable, I feel. I think we still could have been better with our bowling and fielding. We were a bit sloppy, but great learning,” he said.

items.author: Gargi Sarkar
items.content:
What if Netflix’s next big hit in India is not an expensive scripted original, but a reality show with a ready-made fan base? The streaming giant appears to be warming up to an idea it once seemed determined to move away from: television.
Netflix is increasingly turning to established television franchises, reality formats and non-fiction programming to reach a wider audience in India. Its recent content choices, including Lock Upp, The Great Indian Kapil Show and deals for MTV Hustle and MTV Roadies, point to that shift in India.
The change is significant for a platform that initially built its India proposition around premium, urban-focused originals and international programming. In the fourth quarter of 2021, Netflix cofounder and the then CEO Reed Hastings described India as a “frustrating” market. He also stated that the company had not managed to get its flywheel spinning here as it had in other major markets.
Nearly five years later, Netflix emerged stronger. In the July-September quarter of 2026, its India revenue grew 18% year-on-year (YoY) on a foreign-exchange-neutral basis, while viewing hours increased 24%. The company also recorded its largest-ever quarter of paid net additions in the country.
The growth was driven by a content lineup featuring Lock Upp, Netflix’s first daily reality series, as well as scripted titles such as Musafir Cafe and Operation Safed Sagar. Netflix said Lock Upp generated the highest viewing hours of any title on its platform in India, measured over the first 91 days.
So, was this simply a strong quarter or evidence of a more fundamental shift in Netflix’s India playbook?
Netflix Looks Beyond Its Urban Comfort Zone
Netflix’s growing interest in reality television is becoming difficult to miss. The platform has even bought MTV Roadies to Netflix India in a deal worth around ₹18 Cr with JioStar, as per media reports. And the strategy is not limited to one show.
Over the past year, non-fiction content has assumed greater importance in Netflix’s strategy. This is also part of a larger effort to move beyond its Tier I, urban-centric audience.
According to an industry analyst at one of the Big Four consulting firms, if Netflix wants to deepen its penetration and crack the Indian market, it cannot continue catering largely to the same urban viewers. It needs formats and stories that resonate with audiences across smaller cities and towns as well.
Reality and unscripted formats could help bridge that gap. Lock Upp’s performance on Netflix offers an early indication of the format’s potential.
Regional programming is another part of this effort. Netflix is working with local production houses and regional OTT players to deepen its presence in language markets. Netflix has partnered with Bengali streaming platform Hoichoi to bring its upcoming series to a wider audience. Under the two-year deal, the shows will premiere in Bengali on Hoichoi and also be available on Netflix in Hindi, Tamil and Telugu.
Going All In On Bollywood Blockbusters
Netflix has continued to expand its film catalogue by securing streaming rights to established Bollywood titles and major theatrical releases. Its partnership with Yash Raj Films (YRF), announced last year, is one example.
The deal brought a curated selection of YRF films to Netflix in phases, including nine Shah Rukh Khan films such as Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge, Mohabbatein and Veer-Zaara, along with Salman Khan blockbusters Ek Tha Tiger, Sultan and Tiger Zinda Hai. The lineup also included classics such as Chandni and Silsila, and Ranveer Singh films including Band Baaja Baaraat and Gunday.
The strategy extends beyond catalogue licensing to recent theatrical releases. Netflix also picked up the streaming rights to Dhurandhar, which landed on the platform in January 2026 following its release in theatres. For its sequel, Dhurandhar: The Revenge, Netflix secured international streaming rights, while JioHotstar acquired the India rights.
An Ormax Media analysis of 126 films that crossed one million domestic footfalls in 2025 found that Netflix held a 36% share of streaming rights across the titles, the highest among platforms. Its share in Hindi theatrical films stood at 57%, up from 50% in 2024.
The Race To Grab Eyeballs Gets Fiercer
Netflix’s India strategy is taking shape against the backdrop of an increasingly crowded streaming market. According to JustWatch’s Q2 2026 report, Netflix and Amazon Prime Video were tied at the top, each accounting for 22% of measured consumer interest.
Netflix is also seeing stronger traction on the ground. In Q3 2026, the company recorded its highest-ever quarterly paid net additions in India, crediting a strong local content slate and its first transaction-based loyalty bundle with Flipkart. The partnership gives Netflix another route to consumers beyond direct subscriptions, tapping into Flipkart’s existing commerce ecosystem.
Its competitors, meanwhile, are not sitting still. Amazon Prime Video is doubling down on Indian intellectual property, multilingual programming and established franchises, while also looking to take Indian stories to global audiences. At its 2026 content showcase, the platform unveiled nearly 55 Indian original series and films, with more than 100 projects in development or production.
JioHotstar, on the other hand, is banking on a combination of television content, live sports, originals and regional programming to hold on to its mass-market audience. In January 2026, it introduced monthly subscription plans across its Mobile, Super and Premium tiers, starting at ₹79, making access more flexible for smartphone viewers and connected-TV households.
Apple TV+ is also widening its distribution reach. After gaining four percentage points in JustWatch’s rankings over the past year, it has expanded its India offering through an iCloud+ subscription bundle that combines access to Apple TV and Apple Arcade with cloud storage.
But audience growth is only one part of the equation.
Netflix’s financial performance in India offers another measure of its progress. Netflix Entertainment Services India LLP reported a 63% increase in net profit to ₹85 Cr in FY25, while revenue from operations grew 32% to ₹3,769 Cr, according to filings with the Ministry of Corporate Affairs.
The cost of that growth, however, remains significant. Total expenses rose 32% to ₹3,711 Cr during the year. Other expenses, which include content production, marketing and related operating costs, increased 35% to ₹3,616 Cr, while personnel costs declined to ₹88 Cr from ₹106 Cr.
With content and related operating expenses accounting for most of its cost base, the company will need to ensure that its investments in new formats, wider audiences and distribution partnerships translate into sustained revenue growth and stronger returns on content spending.
Can It Go Mass Without Losing Its Edge?
Netflix’s position in India’s content market also varies across language industries. The South Indian film market is more fragmented, with producers having multiple streaming platforms to sell their content to, giving them greater bargaining power. On the other hand, the Hindi film industry has become more dependent on Netflix, according to industry sources.
For Netflix, however, the bigger challenge is balancing audience expansion with its premium content positioning. Its growing focus on reality shows, established television franchises and mass-market formats could help it reach viewers beyond its traditional urban audience.
But moving too far towards familiar, broad-appeal programming also carries the risk of diluting the distinctive content proposition that helped build Netflix. The platform will need to widen its audience without losing the storytelling ambition and premium identity that set it apart from other streaming services.
This tension was also evident when Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos questioned, on Nikhil Kamath’s podcast, whether the platform had introduced Sacred Games too early in its India journey. His remarks irked sections of India’s creative community, which raises concerns over whether Netflix’s evolving strategy could come at the cost of the creative ambition that defined its early India slate.
That balancing act will be central to Netflix’s next phase of growth in India. Reality shows and established television franchises can bring in viewers who may not have been drawn to its earlier slate of premium scripted originals. Regional partnerships can deepen its presence across language markets, while distribution tie-ups can make subscriptions more accessible. However, the early growth signals need to translate into sustained engagement and subscriber additions for the strategy to deliver lasting results.
One strong quarter, even with record paid net additions, does not necessarily mean Netflix has cracked India. The company continues to face competition from Prime Video and JioHotstar, alongside a growing number of platforms competing for viewers, content and production partnerships. Can Netflix turn its new mass-market appeal into a lasting winning formula without losing its DNA?

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Youngsters Saad Baig and Arafat Minhas played pivotal roles in Pakistan's three-wicket victory over Sri Lanka in the ODI tri-series final, producing impressive performances to help the hosts chase down a challenging target of 326 at Gaddafi Stadium in Lahore on Saturday.
Saad struck a fluent 74 off 75 balls, while Arafat smashed a blistering 61 off just 31 deliveries as Pakistan recovered from early setbacks to seal the title with nine balls to spare.
Saad, who shared a crucial 149-run third-wicket partnership with Fakhar Zaman, said the team's collective effort throughout the tournament had been outstanding.
“The chase was not easy, but the way we played today was tremendous. It was an outstanding performance from our team,” Saad said.
The wicket-keeper batsman admitted that he felt the pressure after failing to make significant contributions in his previous three outings but said he was determined to bat deep in the final.
“Definitely, there is pressure when you come into the international circuit. I got out inside 30 runs in last few games, so this time I planned to bat deep. We had lost two early wickets, but the way Fakhar Bhai played that outstanding innings made things easier for us,” he said.
Meanwhile all-rounder Arafat Minhas said that he and Hasan Nawaz knew that they could chase that.
Minhas said he and Hasan Nawaz backed each other when they came together at a crucial stage of the chase.
“When I went out to bat, I spoke to Hasan and told him that we had already been through such situations. We tried to build a partnership and reminded each other that we had the ability to chase the target. We backed each other, waited for the bad deliveries and had confidence in one another,” he said.
“I am extremely happy that we have won the series. I think such opportunities will come in the future as well, and we will keep winning,” he added.
Minhas also dedicated his performance to his family, who were present at the ground to witness his contribution.
“I dedicate my performance to my family, as they have been supporting me for a long time. They were also present at the ground today and must have enjoyed the game,” he said.
His explosive 61, which included four sixes and three fours, came at a crucial stage after Fakhar's dismissal and helped Pakistan move closer to victory.
The young all-rounder's contribution, alongside Hasan Nawaz's unbeaten 37, ensured that Sri Lanka's late fightback could not prevent Pakistan from lifting the trophy.

items.author: Sports Desk
items.content:
Sri Lanka’s top order batsman Kamindu Mendis said the dew factor played a significant role in Pakistan's three-wicket victory in the ODI tri-series final at Gaddafi Stadium in Lahore on Saturday, while admitting that his team were 20 to 30 runs short of a competitive total.
Kamindu, who struck a brilliant 131 in the final, said he enjoyed his innings but was disappointed that his team ended up on the losing side.
“First of all, I enjoyed my knock, but we are still on the losing side. I think we were 20 to 25 runs short, to be honest,” he said at the post-match news conference.
He also praised Pakistan's Fakhar Zaman for his match-winning century but acknowledged that Sri Lanka made mistakes in the field.
“I think Fakhar Zaman played really well. We made some mistakes in the field, but that can happen in the game of cricket. Still, Fakhar played a very good innings,” Kamindu said.
He said Sri Lanka would now look forward to red-ball cricket, adding that the team had several positives to build on.
“It's a good sign to move on to red-ball cricket. We have been doing really well in red-ball cricket as well. I think we have a good coach and a good environment. There are so many positives within our team, and going forward, we are doing much better. We are improving each and every day and in every game. I think we will be doing really well soon,” he said.
Reflecting on the final, Kamindu said Sri Lanka's bowlers had made a good start but gave credit to Fakhar and Saad Baig for their outstanding batting.
“It was a really good start from our bowlers, but credit goes to Saad and Fakhar. I think they played really well. The dew factor was also a huge advantage for them, but they played really good cricket,” he said.
Kamindu also welcomed the concept of tri-series tournaments, saying they provided competitive cricket.
“I think playing a tri-series is really good because there is always competition. Whoever performs better on the day wins the game. So I think a tri-series is a good thing to have,” he said.
The Sri Lankan batter also spoke highly of his compatriots Pavan Rathnayake and Janith Liyanage.
Talking about Rathnayake, Kamindu said they had played together at the same club in Sri Lanka for a long time and he had always believed his teammate had the potential to become a world-class player.
“I have been playing with him since my early days. We played for the same club in Sri Lanka. I always thought he would become a great, world-class player. He is a really good player,” he said.
Praising Liyanage, Kamindu said he had been performing consistently in ODI cricket since making his debut.
“Talking about Janith, I think he has been doing really well in ODI cricket since his debut. He is a great player as well,” he added.

items.title: Iran ready for both ‘defence and diplomacy’, says Araghchi as Tehran, Qatari mediators hold third day of talks
items.summary:
Iran's Foreign ⁠Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Sunday that Tehran was prepared for "both defence and diplomacy", adding that the purpose of the "ongoing and progressing" talks ​was to continue consultations with the Qatari mediators.
Iranian negotiators were in Doha on Sunday for a third consecutive day of talks with Qatari mediators aimed at pushing for a deal to end the United States-Israeli war on Iran, an official briefed on the discussions told Reuters.
Speaking ​to state media, Araghchi said discussions on a "two-day proposal" were continuing, but that no final conclusion had been reached.
Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi in an interview with ICANA News Agency:
🔹 The Iranian delegation’s visit to Qatar took place at the deputy foreign minister level. Its purpose was to continue consultations with Qatari mediators, who had also visited Tehran in… pic.twitter.com/2DIvhRnH7c
