By Ayo Onikoyi
Destiny does not always play fair. Sometimes, it goes overboard or hits below the belt. It is convenient to see Burna Boy today as the “African Giant” without paying much attention to the circumstances that brought the moniker about. It was, in fact, a controversy that Damini Ogulu, popularly known as Burna Boy, took advantage of after feeling diminished and disrespected.
Burna Boy’s “African Giant” moniker originated from a 2019 controversy over the size of his name on the Coachella music festival’s promotional poster. What began as a protest against how he was billed eventually became the title of his breakthrough album and a defining identity in his career. Yet, in retrospect, destiny was playing fair, with an all-seeing eye.
In response to the perceived disrespect, he took to social media to assert his stature, describing himself as an “African Giant”. The statement attracted considerable attention, with some Nigerians criticising him as arrogant, while others supported his insistence that African musicians deserved greater recognition.
If respect is earned rather than demanded, Burna Boy is an exception. He demanded it and earned it. His achievements on the global stage as an African artiste tell the whole story, and 2026 has been a stupendous year for the *Twice as Tall* global hitmaker.
In less than one week, he has recorded two historic firsts: performing at the NFL’s first regular-season game in France and becoming the first Nigerian artiste to present an award at the Ballon d’Or.
These milestones follow his World Cup feat, where he performed alongside Colombian superstar Shakira at the first-ever halftime show at a FIFA World Cup final, helping bring Afrobeats to one of football’s biggest global stages.
Burna Boy also made history as the first Afrobeats artiste to perform on the Grammy Awards stage. His performance featured Brandy and 21 Savage, marking a significant moment for the genre at the prestigious US music ceremony.
In July 2023, Burna Boy became the first African artiste to sell out a stadium in the United States when he performed at Citi Field in New York. The milestone demonstrated the commercial appeal of African music in the American live-music market.
In the same vein, Burna Boy headlined the 80,000-capacity London Stadium during his *Love, Damini* tour, becoming the first African artiste to headline the venue. The concert was another landmark for African performers in the United Kingdom.
Burna Boy also performed at the opening ceremony of the UEFA Champions League final in Istanbul, Turkey, sharing the stage with Brazilian singer Anitta. The appearance placed Nigerian music before a huge international football audience.
He further joined Tems and Rema for a performance at the NBA All-Star Game halftime show in Salt Lake City, Utah. The trio showcased African music during one of American basketball’s biggest annual events, with Burna Boy among the Nigerian stars to perform on the stage.
Burna Boy won Best Global Music Album for *Twice as Tall* at the 63rd Grammy Awards in 2021. The victory was a major breakthrough for Nigerian music, although Nigerian-born musicians and Nigerian-linked acts had received Grammy recognition in other circumstances before then.

By Ayo Onikoyi
Actress and filmmaker Bukola Ikuomola, popularly known as MZNicollet, has said women should be recognised for their intellect, achievements and contributions to society rather than their sexuality.
In a chat with Potpourri, Ikuomola, who expressed her views on women flaunting their sexuality on social media, said she admired women who distinguished themselves through their intelligence and accomplishments.
“There is more to women than sexuality. I admire women who are known for their intellect and other great achievements,” she said.
The Ondo State-born actress, who also has Urhobo roots in Warri, Delta State, said she developed a passion for acting from an early age and had always admired the profession. She is a graduate of Novena University, Ogume, Delta State, and also runs Nickiscollections as its chief executive officer.
Speaking about the sacrifices she has made to build her acting career, Ikuomola said she had invested considerable time, effort and the little money available to her in improving her craft.
She described working with veteran actors, including Saheed Balogun, Jobola Dabo, Ayo Mogaji and Muyiwa Ademola, as some of her memorable experiences in the industry. She also expressed pride in producing her first movie, *Enemy Within*.
On the kind of roles she enjoys playing, Ikuomola said she preferred heroic characters who demonstrate strength and determination and contribute meaningfully to a story. However, she noted that her versatility allows her to approach different roles with passion.
The actress said her ambition was to become a megastar with an international reputation, extending her influence beyond Nollywood.
On relationships, Ikuomola said respect and a good sense of humour were qualities she valued in a man, adding that she preferred men to make the first move.
She also declared a preference for money over love, explaining that past experiences had left her feeling used in relationships because of how much she gave to the people she loved. “Now I go for money. And if love comes with it, I grab it too,” she said, adding that love becomes sweeter when money is involved.

items.author: Emmanuel Okogba
items.content:
By Ayo Onikoyi
When Nigerian comedian and actor Anita Alaire Asuoha, popularly known as Real Warri Pikin, won the Best Stand-Up Comedian award at the 2026 African Muzik Magazine Awards (AFRIMMA), it marked another milestone in a career built on hard work, persistence and an unmistakable brand of humour.
The honour, presented at the awards ceremony held in Dallas, Texas, on September 12, placed her ahead of several established comedy stars, including Basketmouth, Bovi, Godfrey, Eric Omondi, Trevor Noah, Patrick “Salvado” Idringi and Ty Ngachira. Her victory was a significant recognition of her growing influence in African comedy and her expanding international profile. <u> </u>
“This award means a lot to me because it is a recognition of the journey, the work and the years of showing up even when I didn’t know where it would lead,” she said.
“To be recognised as Best Comedian at AFRIMMA, representing Nigeria and Africa, is a huge honour. It also reminds me that staying true to who you are and using your story to connect with people can take you places you never imagined,” she added.
For Asuoha, the AFRIMMA triumph represents more than a trophy. It reflects years of building an entertainment career that spans stand-up comedy, acting, digital content creation, live shows and television and web productions.
Known for her energetic stage presence, Warri-inflected expressions and use of Nigerian Pidgin, Real Warri Pikin has developed a comic identity rooted in everyday experiences, relationships and the peculiarities of Nigerian life. Her ability to turn familiar situations into humorous stories has helped her connect with audiences across different age groups and cultural backgrounds.
Her journey from online comedy skits to major entertainment stages has also demonstrated the growing opportunities available to Nigerian comedians who can build audiences through digital platforms and translate that popularity into live performances.
One of the defining projects in her career is “Real Warri Pikin Unfiltered”, a comedy show that expanded beyond Nigeria to audiences in Ghana and the United Kingdom, including Milton Keynes, Manchester and London. The show established her ability to headline performances outside her home country while retaining the distinctive humour that first endeared her to Nigerian audiences.
She has also performed at established Nigerian comedy platforms and events, including “AY Live”, “Warri Again?” and Bovi’s “Man on Fire”, sharing stages with some of the country’s recognised entertainers.
Her international ambitions gathered further momentum in 2026 with the “In My Element” tour. The American leg included performances in Dallas and Houston, Texas, while the Canadian leg covered Winnipeg, Toronto, London, Saskatoon, Regina and Vancouver. The Canadian run was reported as a sold-out six-city tour, underlining her appeal among Nigerians and other African comedy enthusiasts living abroad.
The United States shows also featured veteran actor Richard Mofe-Damijo, popularly known as RMD, while Uche Jombo and Chioma Chukwuka were among the Nollywood personalities associated with the tour events.
Another major milestone awaits her in London, where she is scheduled to headline *In My Element* at indigo at The O2 on November 29, 2026. The performance is expected to make her the first African female comedian to headline a solo show at the venue, marking a significant moment for Nigerian women in stand-up comedy.
Beyond the international tours, Real Warri Pikin has built an impressive record of awards. In 2022, she won Stand-Up Comedian of the Year and Most Creative Comedy Show at The Humour Awards. She also received the Comedy Act of the Year honour at the African Choice Awards that year, consolidating her reputation as one of Nigeria’s leading female comedy performers.
Her transition into acting has further widened her entertainment portfolio. She has appeared in Nollywood productions, including *Fate of Alakada*, *Prophetess*, *The Ghost and the Tout Too*, *Merry Men 2* and *Aki and Pawpaw*. These roles have allowed her to extend her comic abilities beyond the stage and social media into mainstream film.
On television and digital platforms, she has also explored original storytelling. Her comedy web series *School of Thought*, launched in 2021, featured her as Teacher Afoke and used humour to address issues affecting students and young people. The project was accompanied by a music single featuring singer Teni.
In November 2024, she introduced another web series, *Base on Street*, on her YouTube channel. The story follows two sisters who leave Warri for Lagos in search of better opportunities but encounter difficulties as they attempt to establish themselves in the city. Through the series, she combines comedy with social commentary on survival, difficult choices and the risks confronting young people seeking a better life.
Her achievements also extend beyond entertainment. Through the Real Warri Pikin Foundation, she has pursued initiatives focused on women, children, education and mental wellness. Her willingness to speak openly about personal challenges has also contributed to conversations about emotional well-being and the importance of seeking support.
These different aspects of her career reveal an entertainer who has moved beyond the limits of social media comedy to build a broader presence across live entertainment, film, digital storytelling and social advocacy.
The AFRIMMA award therefore arrives at a time when Real Warri Pikin is extending her reach beyond Nigeria through international tours and increasingly ambitious stage productions. Her journey also reflects the potential of Nigerian comedy to travel across borders without losing the local expressions and experiences that give it character.
From the comedy stages of Nigeria to audiences in Europe and North America, Asuoha has continued to build on the identity that made her popular. With the AFRIMMA recognition adding to her growing list of honours, her career offers another example of how a distinct Nigerian voice can find an audience far beyond its place of origin.

Former Speaker of the House of Representatives, Rt. Hon. Yakubu Dogara, has said Nigeria’s security challenges predate the administration of President Bola Tinubu, noting that terrorism, insurgency and banditry had been entrenched in the country before 2023 when Tinubu assumed office.
Dogara, who is the Chancellor of Achievers University, Owo, Ondo State, spoke at the institution’s 16th convocation ceremony, where 836 graduands received various academic qualifications.
He said the country’s security problems were rooted in years of porous borders, illegal arms proliferation, youth unemployment and the spread of extremist ideologies.
“Insecurity in Nigeria did not begin with this administration. This is no excuse, because the facts need no defence. Terrorism, insurgency, banditry, kidnapping and communal violence did not arrive in 2023,” he said.
Dogara added that the challenges had developed over several years, stressing that their roots went deep before Tinubu assumed office in May 2023.
He, however, noted that Tinubu had consistently identified national security as a major responsibility of his administration. He also congratulated the graduands, saying the country needed their talents, creativity and innovation.
In his address, the Pro-Chancellor of the university, Prof. Bode Ayorinde, said Nigeria had made significant progress in expanding access to tertiary education but expressed concern about the prospects of graduates after leaving school.
Ayorinde cited figures from the National Universities Commission, which put the number of universities in the country at 312 as of June 2026, comprising 77 federal, 67 state-owned and 168 private institutions.
He said the institutions represented a huge investment in human capital, with parents, governments and lecturers making sacrifices to produce skilled professionals, but questioned what opportunities awaited graduates after completing their studies.
The Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Omolola Irinoye, said the university had remained committed to providing quality education that combines intellectual development, practical skills, character building and social responsibility since its establishment.

items.author: Gaurav Bagur
items.content:
The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has arrested Armstrong Exchange founder Sagar Dash in connection with an alleged online gaming and betting scam.
In a statement, ED said that Dash was arrested on October 27 under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002. A special PMLA court in Mumbai has now remanded Dash to ED custody for three days.
The directorate said that the probe was initiated after three FIRs were filed in connection with online betting and cyber fraud involving All Panel Exchange (APX). Afterwards, the ED began probing the operations of APX and related financial transactions.
The agency subsequently uncovered an alleged network of mule accounts and shell entities, which were used to route proceeds of crime worth hundreds of crores.
The agency alleged that Dash used fabricated documents and KYC details of an account, maintained on behalf of an entity called Armstrong Exchange Pvt Ltd and set up by Dash, with Nagarbhavi Credit Cooperative Society to open a cryptocurrency account.
The ED further claimed that hundreds of crores were routed through the cooperative society’s bank account, with a substantial portion directly linked to proceeds generated through illegal gaming and betting platforms.
According to the ED, the proceeds of the crime were initially routed through multiple mule accounts maintained with Jubilee Hills Mercantile Cooperative Bank in Hyderabad. The money was then transferred to various shell entities, and significant amounts were moved to the aforementioned nodal account at Nagarbhavi Credit Cooperative Society in Bengaluru.
The ED said it is continuing its investigation in the matter to trace the alleged financial network and identify other entities involved in routing the proceeds of crime.
The latest arrest follows searches conducted by the ED across Pune, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, and Surat and Mehsana in Gujarat, which resulted in the seizure of incriminating documents and the freezing of nearly ₹9 Cr in cash held across multiple bank accounts.
The agency had also arrested Ram U Ramdhani, CEO of Edsom Fintech Pvt Ltd, in connection with the probe.
The arrest is part of ED’s broader clampdown on money laundering. Just days ago, the directorate launched investigations into alleged FEMA violations involving crypto platforms Mudrex and Saber.money as well as decentralised finance (DeFi) protocol Instadapp and its associated platform, Fluid, over alleged unauthorised cross-border fund transfers worth more than ₹4,940 Cr.
Prior to this in June this year, the ED had also searched six premises linked to five platforms, namely Transak, Carret, Xpat, Onramp.money and Onmeta, over alleged unauthorised cross-border crypto transfers.

Among the dignitaries in attendance were His Eminence the Sultan of Sokoto, the Etsu Nupe and the Emir of Gwandu.
Following their oaths of office, Governor Lawal presented staff of office to 11 first class emirs and eight second class emirs.
Each newly coronated emir also received a GAC ULTRA SUV (2025/2026 model), a MIKANO ZNA HILUX vehicle and an EV ANTIQUE MODEL car (DDP). The vehicles are intended to support their travels and help them engage more closely with their communities.
In his remarks, Governor Lawal said the ceremony reflected his administration’s recognition of the traditional institution as an enduring part of society and an important partner in promoting peace, stability and development.
He noted that the ceremony also reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to giving traditional rulers the recognition and institutional support they need to carry out their responsibilities effectively.
He said, “The staff of office being presented today signifies the authority entrusted to you by the State,” he said.
“It also represents a responsibility to govern your respective domains with fairness, wisdom, integrity, and compassion.
“I expect every emir to carry out their responsibilities without discrimination, uphold justice, and ensure that the traditional institution remains accessible to all members of the community.
“Our people must find guidance, fairness, and reassurance in their traditional rulers.
“Recognising the importance of royal palaces as centres of traditional authority and community engagement, I reaffirm our commitment to completing the reconstruction and rehabilitation of the remaining royal palaces.
“This is part of our broader effort to strengthen these institutions and improve the conditions in which traditional rulers carry out their responsibilities.
“We are also providing official vehicles to the 19 emirs. These include GAC ULTRA SUVs (2025/2026 models), MIKANO ZNA HILUX vehicles, and EV ANTIQUE MODEL cars (DDP).
“This provision is intended to facilitate travel across your respective emirates, encourage closer engagement with your communities, and improve coordination with government institutions.
“I expect these vehicles to be properly maintained and used responsibly in support of your official duties.”
The governor also urged the royal fathers to build a productive partnership between their emirates and the State Government.
Earlier, the Sultan of Sokoto, Alhaji Sa’ad Abubakar, urged the newly coronated emirs to remain fully loyal to the authority. He also encouraged them to respect and uphold the dignity of the traditional institution as they discharge their duties.

items.author: Peter Moses
items.content:
Former President Olusegun Obasanjo and his lookalike daughter, Senator Iyabo Obasanjo, turned a public symposium into a comedy arena of sort on Friday evening as they exchanged playful banter.
The mild drama unfolded at the main auditorium of the Olusegun Obasanjo Presidential Library (OOPL), Abeokuta, Ogun State, venue of the Ajibosin Platform, an annual symposium organised as part of the celebration of the Odun Omo Olowu festival.
Iyabo, a former commissioner for health and candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) for the Ogun Central Senatorial District election, was one of the panellists at the event, where discussions centred on the theme: “Leveraging Artificial Intelligence to Solve Grassroots Problems and Accelerate National Development.”
When the moderator, Prof. Yemi Oke, SAN, gave Iyabo the floor to share her thoughts on the theme, the former senator began by acknowledging the dignitaries present, including the Olowu of Owu Kingdom, Oba Saka Matemilola; the two-time Minister of Industry, Mrs Onipeko Akande; and her father, who is also the Balogun of Owu Kingdom.
Over 30 Bandits Killed As Security Forces Repel Attack in Zamfara
NCDC identifies two suspected Ebola cases in North-East
However, Iyabo concluded her brief salutations by acknowledging former President Obasanjo, “who I don’t know.”
Her remark immediately threw the audience into laughter.
Shortly afterwards, Obasanjo grabbed the microphone to contribute to the discussion on the day’s theme, but his first move was to take a playful swipe at his daughter.
The former president, who admitted that he knew little about artificial intelligence (AI), warned that anything beyond one’s control could be abused.
“Anything that is not in your control can be abused against you,” he said.
Taking a swipe at Iyabo, he added: “And you can see it (abuse) has already started.
“Iyabo doesn’t know her father. That’s abuse of AI already.”
The audience erupted in laughter.
The Ota-farmer also spoke extensively about the challenges facing the Nigerian economy, including what he described as the blind adoption of economic prescriptions from young, foreign-trained experts.
“They are brilliant boys and girls, so they went to Ivy League universities, Oxford, Cambridge, and all that,” he said.
Turning to Iyabo, Obasanjo continued: “And some of my children, including Iyabo here, went to those universities. She went to one of the Ivy League universities. But how can Iyabo now be the one who will tell me how I will run my home?”
Daily Trust reports that Obasanjo and his daughter, had reunited after they publicly fell out following a scathing letter written by Iyabo to her father.
Speaking with TVC recently, Iyabo dismissed speculation about a possible rift between her and her father, describing their relationship as a close bond that has grown beyond the traditional father-daughter connection.
The former Ogun State senator explained that their relationship had evolved over the years, with friendship becoming an important part of their connection.
She said, “I am the oldest child, I don’t even know how to describe our relationship, we are more than friends now. I will be 60 next year and he will be 90 next year. At this age I don’t need a lot of fathering, we are more like friends but friends with a deep connection”.
Daily Trust reports that Iyabo returned to active politics in her home state early this year after 15 years.
She represented Ogun Central in the Senate between 2011 and 2017 but lost her re-election bid.
Upon her return to active politics, the former commissioner joined the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) and declared her intention to run for the governorship seat.
In May, she rejoined the PDP after losing the APC governorship ticket to Senator Solomon Adeola, who represents Ogun West.
In June, the PDP handed her the senatorial ticket for Ogun Central ahead of the 2027 general election.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry on Saturday said the capital's anti-encroachment campaign would continue regardless of political influence.
He also questioned the legality of placing a security cabin and generator outside the Islamabad residence of JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman, and termed the defence of encroachments "inappropriate".
The remarks came a day after the Capital Development Authority (CDA) issued an encroachment notice for Fazl's residence, identifying illegal constructions and encroachments and directing their removal within 15 days.
The notice came amid an escalating war of words between the government and Fazl, who earlier this week criticised the government's alleged violation of the Constitution. Federal ministers hit back, accusing the JUI-F chief of overlooking his own role in forming and toppling governments.
"There will be no encroachments of any kind, and there will be zero tolerance for this," Chaudhry said during a televised address, adding that the campaign had been running for more than a year and a half. He added that notices had gone out in "every other street" of Islamabad. "Whoever committed any illegal encroachment received one," he said.
Chaudhry noted that a notice was issued "in routine" to Amanullah, the owner of the residence. It was, the minister said, a "completely simple notice" pasted on the house, giving 15 days to remove a four-by-four security cabin.
Chaudhry described the cabin as a "cage-like structure" in which a guard sits in summer and winter, outside a house large enough to park some 10 cars worth millions.
The minister said for the guard inside, "there is no shaded place," calling this a "human matter" but also a legal one. The same applied to the generator, he said, adding that the house was not on a one-or-two-marla plot but stood in one of the capital's large upscale areas where neighbours had received and complied with similar notices.

items.author: ​ Our Correspondents
items.content:
Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz has publicly voiced her dismay over derogatory remarks made by her husband, Captain (retd) Muhammad Safdar, about women advocating for bodily autonomy.
Speaking at a Khatm-e-Nabuwwat rally in Chiniot earlier this week, Safdar took aim at the slogan "mera jism, meri marzi" (my body, my choice).
Maryam responded to a post on X regarding the speech, which stated: "Maryam Nawaz's husband, Captain Safdar, also lost his mother-in-law to cancer, yet here he is mocking women who are battling cancer."
"The silent battles a woman, a wife, fights behind closed doors … The strength she must find even when she feels like breaking. Some battles are fought in silence and some wounds are invisible," she said.
Meanwhile, lawyers' bodies on Saturday strongly condemned Punjab Chief Minister Maryram Nawaz husband Capt (retd) Muhammad Safdar for his remarks about Asma Jahangir – a renowned senior lawyer and human rights activist who passed away in 2018.
During a rally, Safdar had called the late lawyer "cursed".
Pakistan Bar Council (PBC) Vice Chairman Pir Muhammad Masood Chishti, as well as the 28th executive committee of the outgoing Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA), regretted the remarks and urged public representatives to exercise restraint and uphold dignity in their statements.
Chishti called upon the relevant authorities to take immediate notice and initiate appropriate legal action.
"The use of disparaging language and references to her religious identity to malign her is highly regrettable and deserves strong condemnation," the PBC vice chairman regretted, adding that making such remarks against a deceased woman, who was no longer alive to defend herself or respond, was particularly "deplorable and reflects a lack of decency and respect".
The PBC vice chairman observed that differences of opinion must never become a pretext for personal attacks, hate speech, character assassination or religious intolerance.
"The invaluable services and contributions of the late Asma Jahangir to the legal fraternity, human rights and the rule of law deserve respect and recognition," he emphasised.
Likewise, the 28th executive committee of the SCBA strongly and unanimously took exception to the recent remarks by Safdar.
"These remarks are highly condemnable and have deeply wounded the sentiments of the entire legal community," the SCBA said, adding that Jahangir was a devout Muslim who dedicated her life to justice, humanity, and the rights of all people, without discrimination.
"Her services to humanity and human rights transcended religious boundaries and to make such hateful remarks about her was not only deeply disrespectful but also an insult to all those who continue to honour her legacy. She stood for the rights of every individual without discrimination."

The deadline set by the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) for mobile network operators to improve services in Islamabad and Rawalpindi ends today, October 31.
The telecom regulator had directed mobile companies to address network coverage gaps and resolve service-related issues in the twin cities by the given deadline. The move aims to improve mobile connectivity and ensure better internet and voice services for consumers.
As part of its monitoring efforts, PTA Director General Enforcement Brigadier (R) Amir Shahzad conducted mobile network drive tests at several locations across Islamabad and Rawalpindi. These included Blue Area, Kashmir Highway, Margalla Road, Iran Avenue, Peshawar Road, 26 Number Chungi, Tarnol and Islamabad International Airport.
PTA Deadline for Mobile Network Improvement in Islamabad and Rawalpindi Ends Today
The PTA team also assessed mobile network performance along the Express Highway and at T-Chowk Rawat. During the drive tests, the DG Enforcement also contacted representatives of mobile network operators by telephone to discuss service quality and network-related issues.
Following the expiry of the deadline, PTA Chairman will personally review the quality of telecom services in the twin cities. The authority will also hold mobile operators accountable for poor network performance and ask them to explain any remaining service issues.
According to the DG Enforcement, the PTA will share network coverage gap reports with mobile companies and direct them to resolve the identified problems without delay.
Brigadier (R) Amir Shahzad said providing quality mobile and internet services to consumers remains the authority’s top priority. He added that the PTA would not compromise on quality of service standards.
The latest monitoring exercise is part of the regulator’s efforts to improve telecom services in Islamabad and Rawalpindi. Mobile users in both cities have reported connectivity and coverage issues, prompting the authority to push operators to improve their network performance.
With the deadline ending today, mobile companies are expected to address the identified gaps, while the PTA’s upcoming assessment will determine whether operators have met the regulator’s requirements.

The Zamfara State Police Command said its personnel, working alongside local civil security outfits, repelled an attempted attack on Bukuyum town during ongoing clearance operations against armed bandits in the area.
In a statement issued by the Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Yazid Abubakar, the command said the operation began on December 28, 2026, following an attempt by armed bandits to invade the town.
According to the police, security operatives engaged the attackers in a fierce exchange of gunfire, preventing them from advancing into the community.

The command said more than 30 bodies believed to be those of neutralised bandits were subsequently discovered in surrounding farmlands, suggesting that the attackers might have suffered heavy casualties.

items.author: Anne Florentyna
items.content:
StockGro-parent AssetGro Fintech Ltd net profit for the fiscal year FY26 jumped threefold while its operating revenue doubled year-on-year.
The company, which filed for an IPO confidentially earlier this month,net profit surged 226.6% to ₹113 Cr during the reported year, compared to ₹34.6 Cr in FY25, according to its consolidated financial statement.
It reported a profit before tax (PBT) of ₹99 Cr in the fiscal, up from ₹35.9 Cr in FY25. However, it reported a net tax credit of ₹14 Cr, comprising a deferred tax credit of ₹15.9 Cr and a current tax expense of ₹1.9 Cr. This catapulted its profit after tax to ₹113 Cr.
The IPO-bound company reported an operating revenue of ₹226.1 Cr in the fiscal, about double of ₹113.3 Cr in the previous year.
A majority of 99.9% of its operating revenue comes from subscription fees and the remaining is from service fees.
Including other income of ₹4.8 Cr, the company’s total income stood at ₹230.9 Cr in FY26, compared to ₹125.5 Cr a year earlier.
AssetGro’s EBITDA stood at approximately ₹118.7 Cr in FY26, compared to ₹59.5 Cr a year ago, marking a growth of around 99.3%.
The growth comes amid India’s expanding retail investment ecosystem, which reached 13.66 Cr unique NSE-registered investors as of September, the company said. This presents StockGro with opportunities to expand its user base while increasing paid subscription adoption among existing users.
Incorporated in 2020, StockGro operates a platform that allows users to research, learn and invest in stocks and alternative assets. The platform combines market research with a social layer, allowing users to track stocks, study portfolios, follow other investors and interact with market experts.
It also offers users research and trade ideas from SEBI-registered analysts, along with tools for deeper analysis. Its AI-powered research assistant Stoxo helps users analyse stocks, markets, mutual funds and other investment themes.
The investment advisory company pre-filed its draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) with the SEBI back in September. StockGro is looking to raise up to ₹2,000-2,500 Cr via the IPO, which could include a fresh issue of around ₹800 Cr and an offer for sale (OFS) by existing shareholders.
Recently, StockGro raised ₹110 Cr (around $10.4 Mn) as a part of its ongoing Series B round, from existing investor BITKRAFT Ventures, along with Aditum Venture Capital Fund, India SME Growth Fund, and actor Suniel Shetty.
Magnifying StockGro’s FY26 Expenses
On the expenditure front, the company’s total expenses increased 47.3% to ₹132 Cr in FY26 from ₹89.6 Cr in the previous fiscal. Here is a breakdown of the total expenses:
Employee Benefit Expenses: Constituting half of the total expenses, employee expenses emerged as the largest cost component, increasing 96.3% to ₹65.8 Cr in FY26 from ₹33.5 Cr in the previous fiscal.
Technology Charges: Spending under this head rose 34.6% to ₹17.9 Cr in the year under review, compared to ₹13.3 Cr in FY25.
Media And Advertising: Costs under this category stood at ₹23.2 Cr in FY26, marking a 61.1% increase from ₹14.4 Cr a year ago.

items.author: ZAFAR BHUTTA
items.content:
The government's surprise move to change the petrol pricing mechanism has set off alarm bells with oil refineries, which call it a "serious setback" to the industry.
In its decision, the federal cabinet has directed Pakistan's refineries to deposit Rs49 per litre into the petroleum levy account to offset the reduction of Rs14.71 per litre in the levy. Responding to the sudden revision in the pricing system, the refineries say they are being forced to sell petrol below production cost following a policy change announced without prior consultation.
On Friday night, the cabinet decided that a reduction of Rs14.71 per litre in the petroleum levy would be compensated through a contribution of Rs49 per litre by refineries to the oil levy account. "The decision has effectively shifted the financial burden of providing relief to consumers on to domestic refineries," industry officials argued.
According to a Petroleum Division letter issued on October 30, the federal cabinet approved a revised pricing mechanism under which refineries would receive an ex-refinery petrol price calculated by fixing the premium, incidentals and customs duty at their March 7, 2026 levels for the next 30 days. The difference between the import price determined on the basis of Pakistan State Oil's actual import costs and the revised ex-refinery price must be surrendered by refineries under the petroleum levy account.
Industry officials said the mechanism would require refineries to surrender approximately Rs49 per litre, substantially exceeding the Rs14.71-per-litre reduction in the petroleum levy. They questioned the rationale for requiring refineries to contribute Rs49 per litre to facilitate a much smaller reduction in the levy, particularly when the mechanism could force them to sell petrol below the actual cost.
Refinery executives said the decision came as a complete surprise and was taken without consultation with the industry. The move raises questions about the government's earlier assurances about stakeholder consultation. Federal Minister for Petroleum Ali Pervaiz Malik had previously said, while defending the diesel price reduction, talks with refineries had been held. However, company officials said no such consultation preceded the latest decision on petrol pricing.
Negative margins
The vice chairman of Cnergyico Pk expressed serious concern over the cabinet's decision, cautioning that the latest intervention could push the company's gross refining margins (GRMs) into negative territory. He mentioned that Cnergyico had been importing higher-priced crude oil from the United States, which gave a higher gasoline yield than the Middle Eastern crude grades traditionally processed by the refinery.
"We are bringing US crude, which is high-priced, and we are already not recovering the actual diesel crack because of the government's intervention in restricting diesel cracks," he said.
The vice chairman explained that the US crude produced a higher proportion of gasoline compared with the Middle Eastern grades that Cnergyico previously imported, making the latest petrol pricing intervention particularly damaging for the refinery's economics. "US crude has more gasoline than the Middle Eastern grades we used to import. With this change in the pricing formula, our gross refining margins can go into negative territory," he said.
The executive's remarks highlight the cumulative impact of government interventions in both diesel and petrol pricing on refinery profitability. Industry officials said refineries were already facing pressure from restrictions on diesel cracks and the latest petrol pricing formula could further erode their margins. They warned that such interventions could discourage crude oil diversification, including imports from the US, at a time when Pakistan was seeking to strengthen its trade and energy relationship with Washington.
Regulatory uncertainty
The chief executive of another leading refinery also voiced concern over the unpredictable regulatory policies. "Nowhere in the world do policies change this quickly. The regulatory regime has become a joke and then the government expects foreign direct investment to flow into the country," the executive remarked.
He questioned how international investors could be expected to commit billions of dollars to Pakistan's refining sector when pricing policies could be changed overnight without consultation. Industry officials cautioned that abrupt interventions could undermine the financial viability of existing refineries and damage investor confidence at a time when the government was seeking substantial investment in refinery upgrades and expansion.
They maintained that while providing relief to consumers was important, the government should not achieve this objective by imposing additional financial burdens on domestic refineries. The latest decision has once again brought into focus concerns about regulatory uncertainty, policy inconsistency and the long-term implications for investment in Pakistan's petroleum sector.
Attock Refinery CEO Adil Khattak said that the latest change in the petrol pricing mechanism caused serious setback to refineries. "The refineries, which had already agreed on two occasions to cap their spread on high-speed diesel, first at $41.89 and subsequently at $38, are now confronted with yet another serious loss," he said.
The government's decision to incorporate pre-war premiums and incidentals into motor spirit pricing will reportedly cost refineries approximately Rs35 per litre. An additional diversion of Rs14 per litre from their customs duty recovery towards reducing the petroleum levy will bring the total adverse impact to Rs49 per litre.
"This decision strikes at the very foundation of the Brownfield Refineries Up-gradation Policy, which specifically requires that proceeds of 10% customs duty will be deposited into dedicated refinery accounts to partially finance their upgrade projects. Diverting these funds for other purposes defeats the objective of this provision," he said. "This decision undermines the policy's explicit assurance of protection against adverse changes during the project execution period. Such assurances are fundamental to establishing the financial viability and bankability of these multibillion-dollar investments."

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
The Pakistan Stock Exchange's (PSX) benchmark KSE-100 index declined 2.1%, or 3,560 points, in October to close at 166,409, as geopolitical uncertainty, foreign portfolio outflows and profit-taking in heavyweight stocks weighed on investor sentiment. The market staged a four-day recovery towards the end of the week, gaining more than 4,800 points to reclaim the 167,000 level on Thursday, before profit-taking pulled the index back below the threshold on Friday.
On a day-on-day basis, the market commenced the last trading week of October with a volatile session, but despite that the KSE-100 index gained 664 points (+0.41%) to close at 163,039, reclaiming the 163,000 level. On Tuesday, monetary policy caution and diplomatic optimism caused a balance, helping the bourse surge 1,429 points (+0.88%) to cross the 164,000 mark at 164,467.
On Wednesday, the index extended its recovery, rising 1,269 points (+0.77%) to close at 165,736. PSX continued the positive trend the next day, Thursday, where the benchmark index added 1,457 points (+0.88%) at 167,193, surpassing the 167k level. However, profit-taking dragged it below 167k on Friday after a four-day rally as the index fell 784 points (-0.47%) to settle at 166,409.
Arif Habib Limited (AHL) noted that the KSE-100 index dropped 3,560 points (-2.1%) in Oct'26 to close at 166,409. Persistent geopolitical tensions kept investor sentiment subdued, while oil price movements added to cautious trading. Also, the State Bank increased the policy rate by 50 basis points to 12% at its Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meeting on October 26, citing higher energy prices and geopolitical uncertainty that impacted the domestic inflation outlook.
Earlier, AHL mentioned, Pakistan and the IMF reached a staff-level agreement on the fourth Extended Fund Facility (EFF) and third Resilience and Sustainability Facility (RSF) reviews, paving the way for $1 billion and $210 million in disbursements, respectively, subject to the executive board approval, which would bring total disbursements under both programmes to $5.7 billion.
During the month, the committee reviewing Pakistan's Automotive and Auto Parts Manufacturing Policy 2026-31 proposed reforms to boost exports, accelerate New Energy Vehicle (NEV) adoption and enhance competition. Key measures included lower sales tax on NEVs, reduced import tariffs, mandatory export targets for manufacturers, localisation requirements and incentives for incremental exports.
Treasury bill cut-off yields rose in Oct'26, largely following the SBP's 50-basis-point rate hike. The one-month yield went up from 11.68% to 12.11%, three-month from 11.99% to 12.43%, six-month from 12.45% to 12.65% and 12-month from 12.49% to 12.89%. Additionally, the central bank doubled the minimum capital requirement for banks to Rs20 billion, to be met by Dec'30, with statutory reserves now eligible.
Power generation rose 5% year-on-year to 13,217 gigawatt hours (GWh) in Sept'26, driven by higher hydel, local coal, imported coal and wind generation. The cost of generation soared 32% YoY to Rs9.35 per kilowatt-hour due to a higher share of re-gasified liquefied natural gas, high-speed diesel and furnace oil along with elevated crude prices, prompting distribution companies to seek a positive fuel cost adjustment of Rs2.56/kWh.
Gross Roshan Digital Account (RDA) inflows reached $14.2 billion as of Sept'26. Of these, $2.1 billion was repatriated and $8.9 billion utilised locally, leaving a net liability of $3.1 billion. Meanwhile, the KSE-100 index profitability (based on 96% of the index weight) increased 26% YoY in 9MCY26, reaching Rs1,638 billion. Average trading volumes at the PSX fell 21.8% month-on-month to 471.9 million shares in Oct'26, while average traded value dipped 20.2% to $70.1 million, AHL said. Topline Securities stated that the KSE-100 index declined 2.09% on a MoM basis during October 2026, primarily due to geopolitical uncertainty, foreign portfolio outflows, profit-taking in heavyweight stocks and cautious investor sentiment amid global financial market volatility and domestic macroeconomic concerns.
Major developments during the month included a moderation in Pakistan's CPI inflation to 10.26% in September 2026, compared to 11.15% in August 2026, while remaining above 5.76% recorded in September 2025. Automobile sales declined 12% YoY and 3% MoM to 15,104 units, as reported by the auto manufacturers association. Average daily traded volumes and value during the month stood at 600 million shares (up 27% MoM) and Rs23 billion (up 19% MoM), respectively, Topline added.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Pakistan and Saudi Arabia have discussed early signing and implementation of the Pakistan-Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) Free Trade Agreement, with Federal Minister for Commerce Jam Kamal Khan saying it would enhance market access, expand bilateral trade and strengthen economic engagement.
He raised the agreement at a meeting with the newly appointed Saudi Ambassador to Pakistan, Dr Rajeh Albugamy, in Islamabad, according to a statement issued on Saturday.
The minister said Saudi Arabia's economic diversification under its Vision 2030 and Pakistan's production and industrial capabilities offered considerable opportunities for greater economic integration, highlighting the potential for cooperation in scaling up production, improving product quality, adopting modern technologies and strengthening industrial competitiveness.
He noted that collaboration in these areas could enable Pakistani businesses to better meet the requirements of the Saudi market while creating mutually beneficial economic opportunities.
The minister also underscored the importance of expanding Pakistan's export base and strengthening private-sector partnerships to translate the growing economic engagement into tangible trade outcomes.
He said the government had made sustained efforts over the past three years to strengthen bilateral relations through enhanced government-to-government, business-to-business and people-to-people engagement.
The Saudi ambassador reaffirmed the enduring bonds of brotherhood between the two countries and assured continued support for strengthening bilateral economic relations, highlighting opportunities for enhanced regional connectivity and cooperation, particularly in the agriculture sector.
The Saudi ambassador expressed his commitment to maintaining close engagement with the Ministry of Commerce to facilitate greater bilateral economic cooperation and identify new avenues for mutually beneficial partnerships.
Both sides agreed to maintain regular coordination and follow-up engagement to advance bilateral trade, investment and agricultural cooperation, with the stated objective of translating longstanding friendship into stronger economic ties.
The statement said the two sides discussed strengthening bilateral trade, economic cooperation and investment opportunities between the two countries.

items.title: S&P revises Meta outlook to 'negative'
items.summary:
S&P Global Ratings on Friday revised its outlook on Meta Platforms to "negative" from "stable", citing significant uncertainty around the social media giant's capital spending and free operating cash flow.
Big Tech has spent heavily on cloud computing, online advertising and e-commerce, but the AI boom has pushed capital expenditure to dizzying levels, stoking investor concerns about whether the sector can generate returns quickly enough. Last week, Meta forecast annual capital expenditure between $135 billion-$145 billion after reporting a free cash flow deficit of $2.12 billion in Q3.

items.title: Thousands attend Masussuka’s maiden religious peace summit
items.summary:
Thousands of followers of the late Sheikh Yahaya Ibrahim Masussuka and religious leaders from across Nigeria and some African countries on Saturday attended the maiden edition of a religious peace summit held at the Muhammadu Dikko Stadium in Katsina.
The summit, initiated by the late cleric, who was shot dead at his residence in Dutsin-Ma Local Government Area of Katsina State last Monday, was organised by the Quranic Believers Harmony for Peace Initiative.
In his welcome address, the Secretary of the initiative, Dr Mustapha Haruna, said the programme was organised to promote religious tolerance and peaceful coexistence among different religious groups in the country in particular and Africa as a whole.
He said although the death of Masussuka who initiated the move, was a major setback, the initiative considered it important to fulfil the late cleric’s dream by going ahead with the programme, saying it is important for the late Masussuka’s wish to be honoured.

Also speaking, the Katsina State Chairman of the Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN), Reverend Richard Sha’aibu Liti, described the summit as a historic initiative that could help address religious intolerance and strengthen peaceful coexistence for a better Nigeria.
He said the initiative would continue to enjoy the support of people from different religious backgrounds across the nation, stressing that the summit would not be a wasted effort, but a legacy to be upheld.
Similarly, Sheikh Muhammad Nuru Khalid of Abuja, popularly known as the ‘Digital Imam’, said the late Masussuka’s efforts to promote religious tolerance and peaceful coexistence would remain part of his enduring legacy.
He said the killing of the cleric would not stop the movement, urging his followers to remain calm, sustain prayers for the unity of Nigeria and continue to promote the ideals for which he stood.
The Islamic scholar also called on the relevant authorities to ensure that those responsible for his death were identified and brought to justice.
The event was attended by several prominent religious leaders and personalities, including former Minister of Youth and Sports Development, Solomon Selcap Dalung, who served under former President Muhammadu Buhari, among others.

items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
Samsung is reportedly planning to bring back the under-display selfie camera with the Galaxy Z Fold9, allowing users to enjoy the phone’s large inner screen without a visible camera cutout.
According to a new leak, the upcoming foldable smartphone could also feature major internal improvements while keeping a design similar to its predecessor.
The Galaxy Z Fold9 is expected to arrive in 2027, although Samsung has not officially confirmed the device or its features.
Samsung Could Bring Back Its Hidden Selfie Camera
Samsung first introduced an under-display selfie camera with the Galaxy Z Fold3 in 2021.
The technology places the camera underneath the screen, making it less noticeable when users are watching videos, playing games, or reading.
Samsung continued using this camera design through the Galaxy Z Fold6. However, the company switched back to a traditional punch-hole camera with the Galaxy Z Fold7 in 2025.
Both the Galaxy Z Fold8 and Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra also use visible selfie camera cutouts on their inner displays.
According to tipster @kro_roe on X, Samsung could reverse that decision with its next-generation foldable.
The source claims that Samsung is preparing a device featuring an under-display camera, along with major changes to its internal hardware.
However, the exact camera specifications remain unknown.
It’s coming next year. I’m calling it a year ahead of everyone else: Samsung will unveil a device with UDC, major internal changes, and minimal changes to its overall thickness and design. https://t.co/wxJ6XigTAa
— kro (@kro_roe) October 29, 2026
Galaxy Z Fold9 Could Also Become Much Thinner
Earlier this month, the same tipster claimed that Samsung had already started developing the Galaxy Z Fold9.
According to the leak, the company is targeting a thickness of just 3.9mm when the phone is unfolded and 7.9mm when folded.
For comparison, the wide Galaxy Z Fold8 measures 4.5mm when unfolded and 9.7mm when folded.
If the rumored measurements are accurate, the Galaxy Z Fold9 would be 0.6mm thinner when opened and 1.8mm thinner when closed.
However, there is some uncertainty surrounding these figures.
The latest leak suggests Samsung is planning minimal changes to the phone’s overall thickness and design, which does not fully match the earlier claim of a noticeably thinner device.
It is possible that the reported dimensions are early development targets or refer to another version of the Galaxy Z Fold9.
Samsung Preparing to Compete With Apple’s Foldable
The tipster also claims Samsung is developing the Galaxy Z Fold9 as a direct competitor to Apple’s iPhone Duo.
Apple’s first foldable smartphone features a 4MP under-display selfie camera on its inner screen.
Samsung’s reported decision to bring back the technology could help it offer a similar viewing experience without a visible camera hole.
However, an under-display camera can also present challenges for image quality because it must capture light through the display.
Samsung has not revealed whether it has developed an improved version of the technology for its next foldable.
Expected Launch Date
Samsung has not announced a launch date for the Galaxy Z Fold9.
Based on the company’s usual release schedule, the device could arrive in the second half of 2027.
There is also no confirmed information about its processor, battery, cameras, display sizes, or pricing.
For now, the under-display camera and thinner design remain unconfirmed rumors from a single source.
More details are likely to emerge as Samsung moves further into the development of its next-generation foldable smartphones.

items.title: New-Age Tech Stocks Gain This Week Led By Ather & Zetwerk, CarTrade Sinks 22%
items.summary:
New-age tech stocks largely advanced this week, with quarterly earnings driving sharp moves in individual counters. Of the 69 stocks under Inc42’s coverage, 40 gained between 0.2% and 26.8%, while the remaining 29 declined by up to 22.3%.
Ather Energy led the gainers after reporting its maiden quarterly net profit. The stock rose 26.8% to close at ₹1,755.05, having touched a fresh all-time high of ₹1,782.05 during the week.
Recently listed Zetwerk followed with an 18% gain, while Tonbo Imaging rose 15.3%. Besides Ather, Nykaa, Eternal, and Shadowfax touched fresh 52-week highs.

Here are some key developments from listed new-age tech companies during the week.
ESDS’ CTO Resigns: AI cloud provider ESDS’ chief technology
items.author: Akshit Pushkarna
items.content:
New-age tech stocks largely advanced this week, with quarterly earnings driving sharp moves in individual counters. Of the 69 stocks under Inc42’s coverage, 40 gained between 0.2% and 26.8%, while the remaining 29 declined by up to 22.3%.
Ather Energy led the gainers after reporting its maiden quarterly net profit. The stock rose 26.8% to close at ₹1,755.05, having touched a fresh all-time high of ₹1,782.05 during the week.
Recently listed Zetwerk followed with an 18% gain, while Tonbo Imaging rose 15.3%. Besides Ather, Nykaa, Eternal, and Shadowfax touched fresh 52-week highs.
However, 15 stocks, including Swiggy, FirstCry, MapmyIndia, and LEAP India, hit fresh lows during the week.
Gains in larger companies helped lift the combined market cap of the 69 stocks to $160.94 Bn, up 5.7%, or $8.62 Bn, from $152.32 Bn at the end of the previous week.
Here are some key developments from listed new-age tech companies during the week.
ESDS’ CTO Resigns: AI cloud provider ESDS’ chief technology officer and chief information officer Sajiv Nair resigned, citing personal reasons. He will leave the company on or before January 27, 2027.
Nazara Funds Acquisition Tranche: Nazara Technologies infused $77 Mn into its UK subsidiary, Nazara UK, to fund the second tranche of its acquisition of Spanish gaming companies Bluetile Games and Bestplay Systems. Nazara UK paid the amount to the sellers, taking the total consideration paid to $303.02 Mn.
Zelio Adds Manufacturing Capacity: Zelio E-Mobility began commercial operations at its new Haryana plant, adding annual capacity of 72,000 vehicles, comprising 48,000 electric two-wheelers and 24,000 electric three-wheelers. It invested over ₹20 Cr in the facility, primarily towards backward integration, under its approved capex plan.
E2E Expands AI Infrastructure: E2E Networks expanded its AI infrastructure capacity by 5.4 MW, or 58.7%, to approximately 14.6 MW. The expansion will include NVIDIA HGX B300 systems and other Blackwell GPUs for AI model training, fine-tuning, and enterprise inference.
GlobalBees Raises JW Brands Stake: FirstCry’s subsidiary GlobalBees Brands acquired an additional 14.2% stake in watch and jewellery brand owner JW Brands for ₹18.7 Cr in cash, increasing its holding from 75.1% to 89.3%. JW Brands, which operates Joker & Witch, Bewitched, and Teejh, reported turnover of ₹105.5 Cr in FY26, up 8.4% from ₹97.3 Cr in FY25.
Markets Recover, FIIs Turn Buyers
The Sensex gained 1.8% this week to close at 74,459.53, while the Nifty 50 rose 2% to 23,053.10, recovering most of the previous week’s losses.
The benchmarks opened the week higher, consolidated over the next two sessions, and recovered sharply on Thursday, when the Sensex gained over 900 points. Buying continued yesterday, helping the Nifty close above 23,000.
Softer crude oil prices and easing bond yields initially supported risk appetite, according to Geojit’s research head Vinod Nair. However, renewed West Asia tensions pushed crude higher towards the weekend, prompting profit booking in the broader market.
Quarterly earnings also drove stock-specific moves, with strong results from select large companies supporting sentiment despite mixed performances across sectors.
Global monetary policy remained another focus. The US Federal Reserve held its benchmark interest rate at 3.75%-4%, although two members favoured a 25-basis-point increase. Nair said the Fed, ECB, and Bank of Japan’s continued caution on inflation tempered expectations of early monetary easing.
FIIs turned net buyers of Indian equities worth ₹6,305 Cr during the week, ending a 10-week selling streak, according to Bajaj Broking’s deputy vice president of research Pabitro Mukherjee. They bought shares in three of the five trading sessions, supporting the market recovery.
DIIs remained net buyers for the 11th consecutive week, purchasing ₹3,110 Cr of equities, although their buying moderated from ₹10,942 Cr in the preceding week.
The reversal in foreign flows followed a prolonged sell-off. A recent research report by JM Financial noted that FIIs had sold approximately $64 Bn worth of Indian equities over the 24 months through October 2026.
The brokerage argued that attractive valuations alone may not draw foreign investors back, identifying crude prices as a key influence. Its analysis associated Brent crude above $105 a barrel with FII selling, while prices below $90 coincided with a more favourable flow environment.
Investors will track next week’s US midterm elections, Brent prices, developments in the US-Iran and Russia-Ukraine conflicts, and quarterly earnings, Mukherjee said.
CarTrade Falls After Earnings
CarTrade shares declined 22.3% this week to close at ₹2,189.95 after its September-quarter results fell short of brokerage expectations despite revenue and EBITDA growth.
The automotive classifieds company’s consolidated net profit rose 3% YoY to ₹66 Cr, while operating revenue increased 10.2% to ₹213.1 Cr in Q2 FY27. EBITDA grew 20% to ₹76 Cr, with its margin expanding to 36% from 33% a year earlier.
However, JM Financial flagged slowing growth in the core consumer business, which includes CarWale, BikeWale, and CarTrade. Its revenue increased 4% YoY to ₹79.5 Cr, compared with growth of 18% in Q1 FY27 and 25% in Q4 FY26, and was 12.4% below the brokerage’s estimate.
OLX India’s revenue grew 26.4% to ₹70.2 Cr but missed JM Financial’s estimate by 9.7%. Meanwhile, monthly unique visitors across the consumer business fell 17.9% YoY and 8.5% QoQ to about 43 Mn. The brokerage flagged concerns over traffic growth and the potential impact of AI on classifieds platforms.
JM Financial downgraded CarTrade to ‘ADD’ from ‘BUY’ and cut its 12-month price target by 25.4% to ₹2,650 from ₹3,550. It lowered its FY27-FY29 revenue estimates by 3%-6% and EBITDA estimates by 8%-13%.
Ather Rallies After Turning Profitable
Ather Energy shares gained 26.8% this week to close at ₹1,755.05 after the electric two-wheeler maker reported its maiden quarterly net profit in Q2 FY27.
Its consolidated net profit stood at ₹1.3 Cr against loss of ₹154.1 Cr a year earlier and ₹51.1 Cr in Q1 FY27. Operating revenue increased 62.9% YoY to ₹1,464.2 Cr.
EBITDA stood at ₹74.2 Cr, with its margin improving to 4.9% from negative 9.6% a year earlier. However, other income of ₹62.7 Cr remained crucial to the bottom line, with operating revenue falling ₹61.5 Cr short of total expenses.
Sales rose 42% YoY to 93,211 units, customer enquiries increased 109% to around 10 Lakh, and pre-orders more than doubled to 1.8 Lakh. CEO Tarun Mehta said supply constraints persisted, with internal estimates indicating potential sales of around 20,000 units a month were going unrealised.
Ather plans to invest ₹122 Cr to add 2.25 Lakh units of annual manufacturing capacity across its Hosur and upcoming AURIC facilities. This would take combined installed capacity to about 11.4 Lakh units by Q2 FY28.

items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
OnePlus has quietly revealed its new Buds Pro 4 wireless earbuds on its official global website, featuring improved sound quality, stronger noise cancellation, and several AI-powered features.
The earbuds offer up to 53 hours of battery life with the charging case, along with support for AI translation, Google Gemini, and wireless charging.
The company has also confirmed two color options, although it has not announced the official price or release date.
Design and Audio
The OnePlus Buds Pro 4 feature two audio drivers in each earbud, including an 11mm woofer for bass and a 6mm tweeter for higher-pitched sounds.
Each driver has its own digital-to-analog converter (DAC), which helps control sound output.
OnePlus developed the audio system with Danish audio company Dynaudio.
According to the company, the new design delivers 50% stronger bass than the previous Buds Pro 3.
The earbuds also support Hi-Res Audio through LHDC 5.0, allowing compatible devices to play high-quality audio at up to 24-bit/192kHz.
Other audio features include Spatial Audio with head tracking, which adjusts the sound as users move their heads, and Golden Sound, which personalizes audio settings based on the user’s hearing.
The Buds Pro 4 come in Titanium Shadow and Polar White. They also have an IP55 rating for dust and water resistance. However, the charging case does not have the same protection.
Noise Cancellation and AI Features
OnePlus claims the Buds Pro 4 can reduce twice as much background noise as the previous generation.
The earbuds feature adaptive active noise cancellation (ANC), which automatically adjusts the level of noise reduction based on the surrounding environment.
Each earbud also has three microphones and a sensor that detects vibrations from the user’s voice. These work together to improve call quality, particularly in noisy places.
The earbuds include AI Live Translation, which can help translate conversations between different languages when used with compatible OnePlus phones.
Users also get access to Google’s Gemini assistant, allowing them to interact with AI using voice commands.
Another feature is Clear Audio Recording, which uses Dolby technology to improve recorded audio.
The earbuds also support Neck Health monitoring, designed to remind users about their posture.
For gaming, OnePlus claims audio delay can be reduced to as little as 39 milliseconds when paired with supported OnePlus smartphones.
Users can also connect the earbuds to two devices simultaneously.
Battery and Charging
Battery life is one of the main highlights of the OnePlus Buds Pro 4.
According to OnePlus, the earbuds can provide up to 13 hours of music playback on their own when noise cancellation is turned off.
With the charging case, total battery life increases to 53 hours.
However, enabling active noise cancellation reduces the combined playback time to 26 hours when using the AAC audio format.
The company also claims that a 10-minute charge can provide up to 14 hours of listening time when using the charging case.
The case supports wireless charging, allowing users to recharge it without connecting a cable.
Price and Availability
OnePlus has listed the Buds Pro 4 on its global website but has not confirmed their official price, launch date, or availability in different markets.
The earbuds will be offered in Titanium Shadow and Polar White.
The Buds Pro 4 also share several features and design elements with the recently introduced Oppo Enco X4, suggesting that the two models may use similar hardware.
The Oppo Enco X4 costs approximately $255 in Europe, although this does not confirm the price of the OnePlus model.
More details about pricing and availability are expected when OnePlus makes its official launch announcement.

items.title: NCDC identifies two suspected Ebola cases in North-East
items.summary:
The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) has identified two suspected cases of Ebola disease in the North-East region.
The agency said both individuals had been isolated, while contact identification and listing were ongoing and laboratory tests were being conducted.
In an update on Saturday, the NCDC cautioned against treating the suspected cases as confirmed infections, noting that confirmation would depend on laboratory results.
“Being classified as suspected cases does not mean they are confirmed Ebola cases; confirmation is subject to laboratory results,” the agency said.

items.title: Island nation’s treaty with Australia raises concerns over loss of cultural heritage
items.summary: Tuvalu's recent treaty with Australia allows its citizens to migrate for work and study opportunities abroad. While migration offers new options, concerns exist regarding the preservation of cultural heritage. Traditional buildings and construction skills might be at risk as populations shift. Researchers are documenting Tuvalu's architectural history through photographs and digital models. Decisions on migration and land use should integrate considerations of cultural heritage and community identity.

items.author: Yasir Ali
items.content:
The Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Advocate General’s Office has issued notices to the governor and other relevant authorities, including the provincial assembly speaker, seeking detailed replies and comments on separate writ petitions challenging the imposition of governor’s rule and emergency in parts of the province.
The petitions, filed in the Peshawar High Court by Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan and others, contend that the imposition of emergency in certain districts and governor’s rule in others is unconstitutional and illegal.
The petitioners argued that the situation in K-P was not beyond the control of the provincial government to warrant such extraordinary measures. They maintained that the federal government had exceeded its constitutional authority by imposing emergency and governor’s rule, effectively depriving an elected provincial government and its representatives of their powers.
Read: K-P governor's rule to end in six months, emergency to continue until peace restored: Tariq Fazal
The petitions further stated that governor’s rule could only be imposed in exceptional circumstances when the situation in a province deteriorated beyond control, with the provincial government itself expected to recommend such action.
They also challenged the invocation of Article 245 to call in the armed forces, arguing that the deployment of troops in aid of civil administration fell within the provincial government’s domain. The petitioners alleged that several constitutional requirements had been disregarded while taking these decisions.
Meanwhile, the Advocate General’s Office has directed the governor, chief secretary, provincial assembly speaker and secretary of the Home and Tribal Affairs Department to submit their respective reports and comments before the court through officers of Grade 17 or above by November 7.
However, questions have been raised over how the provincial assembly speaker would submit his response, as the provincial government maintains that he is currently in protective custody. The Advocate General’s Office has also been informed of the situation.
The high court will take up the petitions for further hearing on November 10.
PHC orders release of 23 more PTI workers
In another case, the high court has granted interim relief to 23 more PTI workers arrested under Section 3 of the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance, ordering their release on bail.
A bench comprising Justice Sahibzada Asadullah and Justice Inamullah heard writ petitions challenging the detention of 23 individuals, including Akbar Sher, Shehzad, Razaullah, Saqib, Ehsanullah and Momin Khan.
The petitioners were represented by lawyers Yasir Khattak and Azhar Rahim Khan, while K-P Advocate General Sanaullah and the relevant officials also appeared before the court.
According to the court order, the deputy commissioner of Mardan had been issued a notice at the previous hearing, directing him to explain the reasons and circumstances under which the petitioners were detained and sent to jail.
Also Read: PM criticises PTI's 13-year rule in K-P, urges PML-N leadership to prioritise public welfare projects
However, the concerned authorities have yet to submit their report despite the court’s directions.
The bench observed that, in the absence of the required report, it had no option but to examine the available record and provide relief to the petitioners. It noted that similar relief had previously been granted in cases involving comparable circumstances.
Consequently, the court ordered the release of each petitioner against two surety bonds worth Rs100,000.
The bench clarified that the petitions would continue to be heard on merit and that the interim relief did not amount to a final decision on the legality of the detentions.
The deputy commissioner of Mardan was once again directed to submit the relevant report and record before the court.
The hearing was adjourned until November 12.

items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
WhatsApp has announced four new features for group chats, including Group Status updates, permanent message pins, improved chat history sharing, and a new filter for important messages.
The changes are designed to help users manage busy group conversations and find relevant messages more easily.
The new features are rolling out to WhatsApp users on Android and iOS.
Group Status Lets You Share Updates With Specific Groups
WhatsApp has introduced Group Status, which allows users to share status updates with members of a particular group.
Unlike regular WhatsApp Status updates, which are shared with selected contacts, Group Status updates are visible only to members of the chosen group.
Group members can view the updates, react to them, and share their own statuses.
Like regular WhatsApp statuses, these updates automatically disappear after 24 hours.
The feature could be useful for sharing photos, announcements, or everyday updates with specific groups without making them visible to other contacts.
WhatsApp Now Lets You Pin Messages Forever
WhatsApp is also removing the time limit for pinned messages in group chats.
Previously, users could pin messages for 24 hours, seven days, or 30 days.
With the new update, users can keep important messages pinned permanently.
This means group members no longer need to pin the same message again after its time limit expires.
The feature can help groups keep important information, such as meeting details, addresses, and announcements, easily accessible.
Share Old Messages With Members After They Join
WhatsApp is expanding its Group Message History feature, which allows new members to catch up on earlier conversations.
Previously, group members could share recent chat history when adding someone to a group.
Now, they can also share older messages after that person has already joined.
To use the feature, users can tap the new member’s name within the group chat and choose to share recent messages.
This can help new members understand previous discussions without asking others to repeat information or forward individual messages.
WhatsApp says the shared messages remain protected by end-to-end encryption.
New Filter Shows Mentions and Direct Replies
The fourth feature is a new chat filter called “Mentions and replies.”
It displays unread group conversations where someone has mentioned the user or replied directly to one of their messages.
The filter also includes messages containing the @all mention, which is used to notify everyone in a group.
This means users can quickly find conversations that need their attention without scrolling through every unread group message.
The feature could be particularly useful for people who belong to several active WhatsApp groups.
When Will These Features Be Available?
WhatsApp announced the four updates on October 29, 2026.
The company is introducing them gradually, so some users may receive the features before others.
The updates are being released for both Android and iPhone users.
Users should install the latest available version of WhatsApp from the Google Play Store or Apple App Store to receive the new features as they become available.

items.content:
Governor Uba Sani has bagged the Distinguished Human Capital Development Champion Award, in recognition of his outstanding investments in education, skills development, youth empowerment and sustainable development.
The Chartered Institute of Human Capital Development of Nigeria (CIHCDN), which honoured him with the award, noted that it celebrates the Governor’s people-centred policies.
The award which was presented at the Institute’s National Conference held at Merit House, Maitama, Abuja, applauds Governor Uba Sani’s initiatives in expanding access to education, healthcare, vocational skills, economic opportunities and improved living conditions of citizens of Kaduna State.
The Institute stated that the award recognises exceptional leadership in advancing education, healthcare, skills development, rural transformation, financial inclusion, youth empowerment and capacity building.
It described Governor Uba Sani’s initiatives as a model of people-centred governance capable of delivering sustainable development and improved opportunities for Kaduna State citizens.
Speaking after receiving the award, the Commissioner of Information and Culture, Malam Ahmed Maiyaki, expressed the Governor’s appreciation to the Institute, for recognising the commitment of Kaduna State to human capital development.
“This recognition is a testament to Governor Uba Sani’s unwavering commitment to placing people at the centre of governance. His Excellency firmly believes that the greatest investment any government can make is in its people, particularly the young, women and the vulnerable,” Maiyaki stated.
He cited the establishment of three Vocational Training and Skills Development Centres in Rigachikun, Soba and Samarun Kataf, designed to equip approximately 32,000 young people annually with practical, industry-relevant skills across 14 trades.
“These centres represent a deliberate shift towards building a productive, skilled and economically independent generation. Our objective is to transform young people from job seekers into skilled professionals, entrepreneurs and employers of labour,” he explained.
The Commissioner further noted that the administration has made substantial investments in education, including the construction of 736 new classrooms, renovation of over 1,200 classrooms, recruitment of 10,000 teachers and training of more than 33,000 teachers to strengthen quality education and enhance access.
He recalled the reduction of tuition fees in state-owned tertiary institutions by up to 50 per cent, alongside expanded scholarship and bursary interventions, demonstrating the Governor’s determination to remove financial barriers to education.
On agricultural development, Maiyaki disclosed that the administration has distributed 1,400 trucks of free fertiliser to 420,000 smallholder farmers, describing the intervention as a major investment in rural livelihoods, food security and economic empowerment.
“Governor Uba Sani recognises that human capital development goes beyond the classroom. It includes empowering farmers to become more productive, equipping young people with employable skills, strengthening healthcare delivery and creating opportunities for families to achieve economic independence,” he said.
Maiyaki also highlighted the Governor’s investments in healthcare, including the revitalisation of 255 Primary Healthcare Centres, improved welfare for healthcare professionals and initiatives to expand access to quality medical services, particularly in underserved rural communities.
He stressed that the administration’s development agenda is anchored on inclusive governance, by ensuring that opportunities and government interventions reach communities, irrespective of political, religious and ethnic affiliations.
“This award is not merely a recognition of achievements recorded; it is an encouragement to do even more. His Excellency remains resolute in building a Kaduna State where every child has access to quality education, every young person has an opportunity to acquire productive skills, and every citizen has a fair chance to prosper,” Maiyaki added.
The Commissioner assured the Institute that the recognition would further strengthen the Governor’s determination to consolidate ongoing reforms and accelerate investments in human capital development.
