items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
Iranian strikes on more than two dozen United States military bases and other sites in the Middle East have caused billions of dollars in equipment damage, with attacks initially targeting early-warning systems before expanding to aircraft, warehouses and troop accommodation, an Associated Press report revealed.
The AP independently verified damage to American targets through satellite imagery from multiple providers and spoke to four regional officials who were briefed on the attacks or had firsthand knowledge of the damage. The analysis found that, through August, more than 115 drone and missile strikes claimed by Iran or Iran-backed groups had damaged or destroyed structures at 26 military bases and other sites housing US equipment.
According to the report, Iran initially focused on aircraft hangars and systems designed to detect incoming strikes, before broadening its targets to warehouses, troop accommodation and other facilities. The attacks, the analysis said, were aimed at weakening the systems that helped protect US bases and enabled them to function.
Read: 81 US aircraft lost or damaged during Iran war, congressional document shows
The attacks have significantly altered the American military presence in the region, with the US moving many of its assets out of the Persian Gulf, two regional officials told the AP. These included aircraft, air defence and communications systems, as well as other equipment crucial to base operations, the report said.
The report said the damage raised questions about the effectiveness of American defences in the region as President Donald Trump considered fresh strikes after Tuesday's midterm elections and Tehran vowed major retaliation. It warned that a resumption of hostilities could cause further costly damage to military bases, deepening uncertainty over whether Washington would rebuild its installations and replace equipment in the region after the war.
The analysis found that Iranian strikes had damaged or destroyed hundreds of buildings and other structures at US bases between April 1 and June 30. The report said its findings offered a broader picture of the destruction than previously released independent assessments, including those by the Pentagon's inspector general.
The Trump administration and US military have disclosed few details about the conflict's toll on personnel and equipment. Delays in releasing satellite imagery have also hampered independent assessments, the report further said.
US Central Command declined to comment on the damage, citing operational security. Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell, however, said US forces and bases were well protected and the military was stronger than ever.
“Our service members in CENTCOM have everything they need to continue their historic success ensuring Iran never obtains a nuclear weapon,” he said in a statement.
Kuwait bears brunt of attacks
Most Iranian attacks have targeted Kuwait, although US installations in Bahrain, Iraq, Jordan, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates have also been hit, the AP analysis of satellite imagery showed.
The deadliest known strike on US troops during the war took place in Kuwait, where six soldiers were killed in a drone attack at Port Shuaiba on March 1.
Ali Al Salem Air Base was struck at least 30 times, damaging or destroying 15 aircraft hangars, several warehouses and 10 buildings near a residential area.
Also Read: US costs of Iran war rise to over $47 billion, according to Pentagon estimate
Camp Buehring, also in Kuwait, suffered extensive damage. Most of its hangars were rendered inoperable, while its gym was destroyed in March and a store for troops was hit in late July. A separate strike severely damaged the garage and dining room, two regional officials told the AP.
The officials and two other regional military officials spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss sensitive details about the damage.
Although the strikes inflicted far greater damage on Iran, American equipment losses were inevitable, said Raphael Cohen, director of the National Security Programme at the RAND School of Public Policy.
Modern warfare had made militaries “susceptible to large-scale, cheap drone attacks”, he said.
“This should be a wake-up call for the United States,” Cohen added.
Early-warning systems among first targets
Iran began its retaliation by striking systems designed to detect incoming attacks before expanding its targets to buildings and equipment that kept US bases operational, the report said.
Within the first two days of the war in late February, Iran destroyed protective enclosures housing US radar systems at Camp Arifjan in Kuwait and Naval Support Activity Bahrain. It also struck portable radars at Prince Sultan Air Base in Saudi Arabia and Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan.
Iran prioritised key early-warning radars that form the backbone of the US air defence system and are difficult and expensive to replace, said N.R. Jenzen-Jones, director of Armament Research Services.
A radar in Jordan was reportedly destroyed. It was one of only 13 such systems possessed by the US Army worldwide, with each costing about half a billion dollars, according to the AP report.
Another radar in Qatar was significantly damaged, although it remains unclear whether it was destroyed. The system was purchased under a 2013 deal worth $1.1 billion and appeared to be the only one of its kind in the region.
The attacks were likely “intended to disrupt and degrade the U.S. and allies’ ability to respond to further strikes”, Jenzen-Jones said.
Read More: It's going to get wrapped up soon: Trump on Iran war
After hitting the radar, Iran carried out more than 50 successful strikes on 18 locations housing US military equipment during the first month of the war, prioritising sites with aircraft.
The attacks damaged refuelling aircraft, communications systems, fuel bunkers and troop accommodation, two regional officials said. A strike on Prince Sultan Air Base damaged the rear half of a Boeing E-3 Sentry surveillance aircraft, while another hit a CIA unit at the US Embassy in Riyadh.
A regional military official who recently visited the Saudi air base described damaged equipment, debris and bombed-out barracks and dining halls. He said the attack on the surveillance plane also damaged several other aircraft, including two aerial refuelling tankers.
A Congressional Research Service report updated in October said 15 US aircraft had been damaged at bases across the region.
Al Dhafra Air Base, south of Abu Dhabi in the United Arab Emirates, was also frequently targeted early in the war. A regional military official said aircraft hangars, other installations, an early-warning radar system and surveillance drones had been damaged.
Satellite imagery delays hamper assessment
Major satellite imagery providers with US contracts blocked or delayed the public release of images at the request of American officials, sometimes citing national security concerns, the report revealed. This limited independent verification until imagery became available from OneAtlas, a satellite provider owned by Airbus.
At Camp Buehring, high-quality imagery from reliable providers was unavailable until late August. More than 30 structures were damaged or destroyed between the suspension of imagery in early March and its return in August. The report said it confirmed repeated strikes on the base in March, April, May and July.
With neither side outlining a clear end to the conflict, further damage remains possible if hostilities resume, the report said.
The conflict could signal a new operating environment for US forces, Cohen said, warning that military installations and equipment were increasingly vulnerable to relatively inexpensive drone attacks.
“This is the operating environment that we’re going to face in the future,” he said.
“The idea that we can rely on fixed infrastructure in the way that we have during the global war on terrorism is over.”

items.title: Kano Has No Speech Physiotherapist – Health Commissioner
items.summary:
The Kano State Commissioner for Health, Dr Abubakar Labaran, says the state has no speech physiotherapist, forcing patients in need of specialised rehabilitation services to travel to other locations for treatment.
Labaran said the state government is taking steps to address the shortage by sponsoring physiotherapists for specialised training to ensure that residents could access the services locally.
The commissioner spoke at the 66th Annual Scientific Conference and 67th Annual General Meeting of the Nigeria Society of Physiotherapy held in Kano.
The conference featured sub-themes on strategic advocacy and policy engagement for integrating physiotherapy into Nigeria’s public health system, as well as rehabilitation across the lifespan, focusing on disabilities arising from non-communicable diseases, trauma and infectious diseases.

items.author: Taiwo George
items.content:
The Kano State Commissioner for Health, Dr Abubakar Labaran, says the state has no speech physiotherapist, forcing patients in need of specialised rehabilitation services to travel to other locations for treatment.
Labaran said the state government is taking steps to address the shortage by sponsoring physiotherapists for specialised training to ensure that residents could access the services locally.
The commissioner spoke at the 66th Annual Scientific Conference and 67th Annual General Meeting of the Nigeria Society of Physiotherapy held in Kano.
The conference featured sub-themes on strategic advocacy and policy engagement for integrating physiotherapy into Nigeria’s public health system, as well as rehabilitation across the lifespan, focusing on disabilities arising from non-communicable diseases, trauma and infectious diseases.
Angry youths confront policemen, &#8216;retrieve bribe&#8217; collected at Checkpoint
Sanwo-Olu: Hamzat Stepped Down for Me in 2018 without grudges
According to Labaran, the state government has expanded physiotherapy units across four of its hospitals in recognition of the vital role the profession plays in healthcare delivery.
He added that plans were underway to establish a centre of excellence in physiotherapy at the Murtala Muhammad Specialist Hospital, Kano.
“We realised that we don’t have a single speech physiotherapist in Kano and perhaps in the entire North. We either have to bring a specialist from Ibadan or travel there.
“We have therefore decided to sponsor physiotherapists to specialise in this area so that the services will be available in Kano,” he said.
The Registrar of the Medical Rehabilitation Therapists Board of Nigeria, Professor Rufai Ahmed, who represented the Minister of State for Health, Dr Isaac Salako, emphasised the importance of training physiotherapists in specialised fields where services were unavailable.
Ahmed said the board would send a team to assist state-owned hospitals in securing the necessary accreditation for physiotherapy services.
He reaffirmed the ministry’s commitment to the profession, stressing the need to strengthen training institutions to improve service delivery despite existing challenges.
The President of the Nigeria Society of Physiotherapy, Dr Felix Oyinlola Odusanya, said the conference theme reflected a renewed commitment to advancing the profession and expanding its contribution to healthcare delivery.
He said the association was looking forward to the approval of a national rehabilitation policy and the release of the Doctor of Physiotherapy scheme of service in the health sector.
According to him, Nigeria has 60 physiotherapy training institutions, while the National Universities Commission has recently approved a five-year Doctor of Physiotherapy degree programme.
Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf, represented by the Secretary to the State Government, Umar Faruk, said the conference provided an important platform for discussions on reducing disability and pain while highlighting the role of physiotherapy in public health.
The governor stressed that physiotherapy should be recognised as an integral component of comprehensive healthcare services for injured persons, older people and persons with disabilities.
Senator Bello Hayatu Gwarzo, who attended the event in a wheelchair, shared his rehabilitation experience following surgery in Germany, which he said had enabled him to stand and move without support.
In his presentation, the guest speaker, Dr Felix Abraham Obi, lamented that although Nigeria trains physiotherapists, the healthcare system does not adequately deploy them to leadership positions where they could contribute to policy formulation and decision-making.
He noted that there was no physiotherapist serving as a director in the Federal Ministry of Health or at the state level.

US President Donald Trump has expressed optimism about reaching a peace agreement between Russia and Ukraine, saying a deal could be close ahead of the December G20 summit at his Trump National Doral resort in Florida.
Speaking in an interview with conservative commentator Benny Johnson released on Saturday, Trump said there was a “real good chance” of resolving the conflict, pointing to the possibility of an agreement between the two leaders.
“I think we’re getting very close to making a deal there,” Trump said, acknowledging the deep hostility between Russian President Vladimir Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky.
Asked about reports of a possible Russia-Ukraine agreement at the G20, Trump did not rule out the prospect, expressing confidence that negotiations could produce a breakthrough.
Read More: Trump administration plans to deport Afghan refugees to Pakistan: report
“I think there’s a real good chance we’re going to have that one worked out. Also, we’re working out a lot of deals,” he said.
He also addressed Iran, saying the US was determined to prevent the country from acquiring nuclear weapons. Trump claimed Iranian military capabilities had been severely weakened, adding that Washington would “finish that off”.
Turning to Cuba, Trump predicted that the country’s communist leadership would not remain in power much longer, suggesting Washington could turn its attention to the island after Venezuela.
“It’s a failed country. We’re going to get people back there very soon,” he said, adding that Secretary of State Marco Rubio was monitoring the situation closely.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
While dinosaurs ate a lot of different things, including each other, fruit long seemed to have been absent from their menu. But scientists now have found fossils of ​a turkey-sized and toothless dinosaur possessing a parrot-like head that exhibited multiple adaptations for a specialized fruit diet.
This first-known frugivorous dinosaur, named Infernogallus jamesi, lived about ‌66 million years ago during the Cretaceous Period at the twilight of the age of dinosaurs and displayed traits on its beak and jaws for mashing soft food like fruit. It is known from fossils unearthed in Montana and North Dakota.
The name Infernogallus means "hell chicken," a nod to its bird-like appearance and the fact that its fossils were found in the Hell Creek rock formation, which spans the US states of Montana, North Dakota, South Dakota and ​Wyoming and has yielded the remains of some of the most famous dinosaurs.
It would have eaten fruit and other soft plants in the subtropical coastal floodplain ecosystem it ​shared with the likes of apex predator Tyrannosaurus, three-horned herbivore Triceratops and tank-like armored plant-eater Ankylosaurus.
Infernogallus was about 5 feet (1.5 meters) long and weighed around ⁠25 pounds (11.3 kg). While the fossils — one nearly complete skeleton and isolated bones from a jaw and palate — did not reveal feathers, the researchers believe Infernogallus was covered in them, based on ​fossils of close relatives.
It belonged to a group called theropods that includes T. rex and all the meat-eating dinosaurs, as well as some that took to eating plants and the entire bird ​lineage.
"This definitely expands the range of lifestyles we thought dinosaurs had, and it shows how adaptable theropods were," said paleontologist Greg Funston of Stony Brook University in New York, lead author of the research published in the journal Nature Communications.
Fruits are the reproductive structures of angiosperms, also called flowering plants. Angiosperms first appeared earlier in the Cretaceous, around 130 to 140 million years ago, and subsequently took over landscapes previously dominated by plants called gymnosperms ​like conifers and ginkgoes.
Infernogallus shows that some dinosaurs may have had a close ecological relationship with flowering plants.
"It has been proposed before that some groups of dinosaurs ate fruits, but there was ​never evidence to back it up," said study co-author Thomas Dudgeon, a postdoctoral researcher at the Royal Ontario Museum in Toronto.
"The discovery of Infernogallus shows that dinosaur diets were likely far more diverse than we ‌previously thought. Prior ⁠to this discovery, there was a bit of a mystery in dinosaur evolution. The evolution of flowering plants introduced a brand-new food source that undoubtedly had consequences for the animals living alongside them," Dudgeon said.
The fruit available for Infernogallus may have included various berries as well as drupes, a broad category that today includes types with a central pit like peaches and cherries as well as others like mangoes and olives.
Three key features
Infernogallus showed a range of features indicating a frugivorous diet. The three most important, Funston said, were the organization of jaw muscles that powered back-and-forth chewing ​motions, a mobile joint that enabled the jaw ​to slide forward, and a series of ⁠ridges and grooves on the beak to help mash and shear soft plants like fruits.
"We see these features separately in birds and turtles today that eat soft foods, like the fig-eating vulturine parrot or green sea turtles that chew soft sea grass. But no living animal has all ​three adaptations, showing just how specialized Infernogallus was," Funston said.
Infernogallus also shows how adaptable beaks are compared to teeth.
"Once you've lost your teeth ​and developed a beak ⁠instead, the range of foods available dramatically increases, including plants, as long as you have some way to digest them," Funston said.
Most herbivorous theropods used stomach stones called gastroliths to grind food. But Infernogallus and other members of a lineage called caenagnathids chewed their food instead.
Fruit-eating animals play an important role for angiosperms by dispersing seeds.
"Mammals and birds would probably also have eaten fruit, but they didn't show the ⁠same kinds ​of specializations for a frugivorous diet that Infernogallus does, so it might have been a less important resource for ​them. Mammals and birds also were quite small in the Cretaceous, so it's unlikely that they were spreading very large seeds, or that they were spreading them big distances," Funston said.
"We know that these big-seeded fruits were proliferating and spreading, ​and it seems like caenagnathids could have fit this role — although we feel more evidence is needed before drawing that link confidently," Funston said.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
US electricity prices had flown under the radar in past national elections, but they have become a major political issue in this year's midterms as Americans grow angry over rising utility bills and deals for power-hungry ​data centers.
Nationwide, according to Energy Information Administration data, electricity prices for homes have risen more than 10% since 2024 when President Donald Trump was elected along with Republican majorities in ‌both houses of the US Congress. Higher electricity prices have outpaced the rise in costs for other goods and services.
Power bills have grown even faster in political battleground states of Ohio, Michigan and Pennsylvania, which are also hot spots for new data centers. In some cases, electricity bills have soared by triple the inflation rate.
Many politicians vying for top statehouse seats across the country this year have backed cracking down on utilities. Some have proposed freezing utility rate increases and slashing guaranteed returns, steps ​that could have sweeping consequences for the country's utility industry.
"It could be the first election to feature utilities and electricity, specifically, as a prominent issue in the midterms," said Charles Hua, executive ​director of PowerLines, a nonprofit that advocates reforming utility policy to favor consumers. "Part of that is because people's utility bills have gone up and up, and ⁠they don't see any end in sight."
Utilities are heavily regulated. State regulators generally must approve utilities’ requests to spend on the grid and to recover those costs through rate increases. Regulators also set the return on equity ​utilities can earn on their grid investments.
This year, utilities are on track to match last year's record high $31 billion in rate increase requests to regulators, a PowerLines survey showed. Last year's spending was double the previous record.
The investor-owned ​companies are also expected to carry out a record of nearly $1.3 trillion in capital spending over the next five years, according to an analysis by S&P Global’s Regulatory Research Associates.
Utilities spotlighted
Seats on nine state public utility commissions are up for election this year, nearly all the US states where voters elect their utility regulators. These include burgeoning data center hubs Arizona and Georgia.
Governors will be chosen in 36 US states this year, and governors appoint utility regulators in states where commissioners are not ​directly elected.
In Ohio, Democrat Amy Acton has promised to lower energy bills if she is elected governor. Her campaign said she will also appoint a public utilities commission that was "not beholden to utility companies" and ​work with the state attorney general to crack down on "excessive rate hikes and predatory practices."
Ohio's residential electricity bills have grown by more than 20% over the last two years, according to EIA data.
Acton has also said she supports a ‌data center ⁠moratorium. Her Republican opponent Vivek Ramaswamy said he would assure Ohioans living near data centers would not pay electricity bills at all.
Bully pulpit
Some governors who are up for reelection have used their political weight to pressure the power industry to keep prices down.
Read More: Pope Leo first pontiff to cast US ballot
In April, Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro announced that prominent utility, PECO Energy Company, had acceded to his demand that it withdraw its proposal with state regulators to increase rates. Shapiro, a Democrat running for reelection, said the move would reduce future utility bills by as much as $34 a month.
He followed up with a letter to more utility CEOs seeking changes in how utilities justify spending and returns ​on equity.
"The governors are using this crisis on energy ​affordability as an opportunity to take a ⁠deeper dive into the utility regulatory model and see if it makes any sense," said Jamie Van Nostrand, senior fellow at the Kleinman Center for Energy Policy at the University of Pennsylvania and former chair of the Massachusetts Department of Public Utilities.
Power bills tracked low inflation for roughly a decade, and were not an ​issue in most mainstream elections until last year, when Mikie Sherrill successfully ran for New Jersey governor on the promise of freezing utility bills. She ​did so the same day ⁠she took office.
In Virginia, home to the largest concentration of data centers in the world, Governor Abigail Spanberger took a similar approach, which industry analysts said could offer a playbook for those who win this year’s elections.
Utility advocates say reducing guaranteed returns and freezing rates will not make a meaningful difference in household bills but could lead to a long-term reduction of investments in the grid.
"The grid is America's greatest machine, and it doesn't operate on ⁠the political calendar,” ​said Drew Maloney, president of Edison Electric Institute, a trade organization for investor-owned electric utilities. “It requires consistent investment every year to ​deliver reliable energy to our customers."
Credit rating agency Fitch downgraded the North American utility sector to "deteriorating" from "neutral" in June, citing political pressure in the midterms to limit electricity bills and utility profits.
For an industry that plans in decades, it is hard to predict the ​result of short-term political moves aimed at saving money for households.
"I do think the real meat will come after the election," Hua said.

Delhi NCR-based D2C skincare brand Numour is in talks to raise nearly $3.1 Mn (about ₹30 Cr) in a funding round led by Sharrp Ventures, sources told Inc42.
The brand, which combines skincare formulations with beauty devices, is currently backed by Indian Silicon Valley Capital.
Questions sent to Numour and Sharrp Ventures did not elicit a response till the time of publication.

Its product portfolio includes sunscreens, dual-phase serums, collagen-based skincare products, LED-equipped jars, sonic massagers, and facial devices. Some products incorporate red or blue LEDs, while others feature sonic massage technology.
Numour says its product development centres on three areas: active ingredients, skin barrier care, and delivery technology. The brand claims its formulations combine clinically validated ingredients with delivery systems designed to carry active ingredients beyond the skin’s surface barrier.
It positions itself at the intersection of skincare and consumer technology.
Sharrp Ventures is the investment office of the Harsh Mariwala family. Its investments span businesses across categories such as beauty and personal care, consumer technology, health and wellness, food and beverages, and lifestyle.
In July, it led ₹100 Cr funding round of beauty and personal care contract manufacturer Naturis Cosmetics.
Numour’s fundraising talks come amid investments in skincare brands. In May, CHOSEN raised $5 Mn in a Series A round led by Fireside Ventures, with participation from L’Oreal’s venture capital arm BOLD and Alkemi Growth Capital. The brand earmarked the capital for strengthening R&D, expanding its product pipeline, and scaling its team and centre of excellence.
At the heart of these investments is India’s growing D2C market, which is projected to grow from $65 Bn in 2026 to $310 Bn by 2031, at a CAGR of around 37%.

items.author: Anjali Jain
items.content:
US retail giant Walmart has launched an investigation into allegations that employees at its subsidiary Flipkart received over ₹150 Cr ($16 Mn) in kickbacks from vendors.
The probe follows whistleblower complaints involving employees in Flipkart’s smartphones and luggage and travel accessories (LTA) divisions, Moneycontrol reported, citing people familiar with the matter.
Employees allegedly accepted payments and favours from vendors in exchange for preferential treatment on the ecommerce platform, including greater visibility that helped drive sales.
According to the report, some employees allegedly used Flipkart’s B2B operations to facilitate these arrangements. In the smartphones category, employees allegedly took cuts from vendors when devices moved between businesses.
The investigation is ongoing, and the exact quantum and nature of the alleged wrongdoing are yet to be established, the report added.
Responding to Inc42’s queries, a Flipkart spokesperson said, “Flipkart has robust governance processes and controls and is committed to the highest standards of integrity and compliance. We take any concerns seriously and address them through established processes. We remain committed to ensuring the highest standards of ethical conduct across our business.”
According to Moneycontrol, this is Walmart’s third investigation into alleged financial misconduct at Flipkart in less than three years.
An investigation into employees in the LTA division around two-and-a-half years ago resulted in at least three dismissals. Another probe in the smartphones division around six months ago reportedly found wrongdoing by an employee, who resigned before being dismissed.
Flipkart Grapples With Multiple Challenges
The investigation comes amid senior leadership exits, former employees’ concerns over ESOP liquidity, and uncertainty surrounding Flipkart’s IPO timeline.
At least 14 vice presidents and senior vice presidents have left Flipkart over the past year. These include smartphones VP Kanchan Mishra, product and technology VP Amit Sachan, and corporate tax VP Kamal Chopra.
More than 1,000 former Flipkart Group employees recently approached Walmart’s board, seeking equal access to stock buyback opportunities offered to current employees.
They also sought an extension of the window to exercise their vested stock options and a designated point of contact to address their concerns.
Meanwhile, Flipkart Group CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy said in July that the company did not have a timeline for going public. Earlier reports said Walmart had asked Flipkart to prioritise profitability and target EBITDA breakeven by the end of FY27 before pursuing an IPO or another external fundraise.
Flipkart Internet reported an 18% YoY increase in consolidated operating revenue to ₹1,45,880 Cr in FY26. Its consolidated net loss narrowed marginally to ₹8,468 Cr from ₹8,646 Cr in FY25.
These consolidated results reflect the Flipkart Group’s performance, including businesses such as Myntra and Cleartrip, following its redomiciliation to India.
Flipkart also continues to invest in newer businesses, including quick commerce platform Flipkart Minutes, which competes with Blinkit, Zepto, and Swiggy Instamart. The company is also exploring opportunities in food delivery and event ticketing.

According to recent leaks, the upcoming Oppo Find X10 Ultra could feature the MediaTek Dimensity 9600 Pro, marking a major change for the company’s Ultra flagship lineup.
The information comes from tipster Smart Pikachu, who shared the details on China’s social media platform Weibo. Another leaker, Abhishek Yadav, has also reported similar information on X and shared some additional details about the upcoming device.
Oppo Find X10 Ultra May Ditch Qualcomm for MediaTek Dimensity 9600 Pro
If the reports prove accurate, Oppo will move away from Qualcomm for its next Ultra flagship. The previous-generation Find X9 Ultra, launched earlier this year, uses Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 processor. The company appears ready to explore MediaTek’s latest flagship platform for its successor.
MediaTek is also gaining ground in the premium smartphone market. Oppo’s recently launched Find X10 Pro Max reportedly features the 2nm Dimensity 9600 Pro chipset, suggesting that the company is increasingly considering MediaTek processors for its high-end devices.
Apart from the processor, the Find X10 Ultra could bring major improvements to its camera system. According to earlier leaks, the smartphone may feature a 200MP primary camera with a large 1/1.12-inch sensor and LOFIC technology. This technology could help the camera capture a wider range of light and preserve more details in challenging lighting conditions.
The main camera could work alongside a 200MP periscope telephoto sensor with a 1/1.3-inch sensor size. Oppo may also include a 50MP camera with 10x optical zoom, giving users more flexibility when capturing distant subjects.
See Also: OPPO Launches Find X10 Series Globally, Bringing Triple 200MP Hasselblad Imaging to Pakistan Soon
The front camera could receive a significant upgrade as well. Reports suggest that Oppo is considering a 100MP square selfie sensor with a 1:1 aspect ratio. However, the company has not confirmed these camera specifications.
The Find X10 Ultra is expected to compete in the premium camera phone segment, following the strong camera-focused approach of its predecessor. Its reported combination of high-resolution sensors and advanced imaging technology could make it an interesting option for photography enthusiasts.
For now, Oppo has not officially confirmed the processor, camera specifications or launch timeline of the Find X10 Ultra. These details remain based on leaks and should be treated with caution until the company makes an announcement.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) police have integrated anti-drone systems and surveillance drones across the province with the Safe City Peshawar Command and Control Centre to strengthen counterterrorism operations and improve security monitoring.
The new system will allow senior police officers to monitor live video feeds from police drones operating in different parts of the province. These feeds will also cover field operations and offensives conducted by the police and the Counter Terrorism Department (CTD) against militants.
Speaking at a news conference, KP Safe Cities Project Director Deputy Inspector General Ijaz Ahmad said the integration would help police detect and neutralise hostile quadcopters and other drones more quickly. The KP police have connected anti-drone systems installed in Peshawar and other districts to the central monitoring centre.
KP Police Integrates Drone Surveillance and Anti-Drone Systems into Safe City Network
According to the DIG, modern anti-drone systems are already operational in Peshawar, Dera Ismail Khan, Lakki Marwat, Tank and Bannu. Police personnel in remote and sensitive areas have also received anti-drone guns to respond to potential aerial threats.
The central system will also provide live monitoring of police surveillance drones across the province. During an operation, drone footage will reach the Command and Control Centre, allowing senior officers to assess the ground situation and provide timely support to teams working in the field.
However, limited internet connectivity in some remote areas remains a challenge. DIG Ahmad said the police were working with the Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission (Suparco) to address this issue and improve communication coverage.
Alongside the technology upgrade, the KP police have established a specialised human resource division to conduct unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) operations. The move comes as militants increasingly use drones for surveillance, ammunition drops and more advanced attacks, including coordinated swarm operations.
See Also: Pakistan Targets Nordic Countries to Boost IT Exports to $15 Billion
The specialised division has trained personnel in modern drone operations, aerial surveillance, intelligence gathering and counterterrorism. Their training also covers the protection of sensitive installations and the use of UAV technology during high-risk operations.
The personnel can also conduct electronic warfare against hostile drones, allowing them to support counter-drone operations rather than relying only on surveillance equipment.
The KP police say this is the first specialised UAV division established by a police department in Pakistan. Its creation reflects the growing need to prepare law enforcement agencies for emerging aerial threats.
The integration of drone surveillance, anti-drone technology and centralised monitoring is expected to improve coordination between police units and strengthen their ability to respond to militant activities across the province.

items.author: Imran Asghar
items.content:
The Rawalpindi police on Saturday initiated legal proceedings following the death of a 30-year-old man at the Gangu Police Check Post in Taxila, with a police spokesperson assuring that a fair investigation would be conducted and those responsible would be held accountable.
The incident reportedly occurred when a man, travelling from Khanpur towards Taxila, was stopped by police personnel at the Gangu checkpost for a search of his vehicle.
Read: Afridi alleges police brutality
Local residents and the victim's family alleged that the man was subjected to severe physical assault by police personnel during the search. His family claimed that the man repeatedly pleaded with the officers to stop beating him with batons, while children at the scene also cried and appealed to the police to spare him.
According to the family, the 30-year-old died at the scene as a result of the alleged police torture.
News of his death triggered protests in the area, with angry residents blocking the Taxila-Khanpur Road and surrounding police personnel, The Express Tribune witnessed on the site.
According to Rawalpindi Police Spokesperson Inspector Sajjadul Hassan, senior police officials reached the scene after the incident sparked the road blockade and widespread protest.
“Legal proceedings are underway, and the matter would be investigated on merit to apprehend those found guilty of homicide,” Inspector Hassan told The Express Tribune.
Eyewitnesses said some protesters also assaulted police officers, leaving one policeman seriously injured.
Read more: Casualties reported after JAAC, police clash in AJK's Rawalakot
The incident sparked tensions in the area, prompting senior police officials to reach the site.
The police spokesperson said the road, which had been blocked during the protest, had subsequently been reopened to traffic.
The incident comes amid a series of allegations of police brutality and misconduct reported in Rawalpindi this year. In several of these cases, police authorities announced inquiries or departmental action following complaints and the emergence of video footage. The latest incident at the Gangu checkpost in Taxila, however, has raised further questions about police conduct during roadside checks and the use of force against civilians.
In August, a police constable was suspended and issued a charge sheet following the emergence of a video showing the alleged mistreatment of a citizen at Gujjar Khan Police Station.
In April, three students accused plainclothes police personnel of assaulting them at the Dahgal checkpoint on Adiala Road before taking them to Adiala Police Post, where they were allegedly tortured and threatened with false charges. One of the students subsequently approached the Rawalpindi city police officer, seeking legal and departmental action against the officials involved.
In February, a 12-year-old boy was allegedly tortured at Rawat Police Station, prompting the suspension of three police officials and an inquiry into the incident. The same month, a resident accused personnel at RA Bazaar Police Station of torture, blackmail and extortion, while another case involved a 45-year-old man who sustained severe burn injuries after allegedly setting himself on fire at a police post. His family accused police personnel of torture, although the police disputed the allegations and said an inquiry had been initiated.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Motorola’s upcoming flagship smartphone, the Motorola Signature 27, has appeared on Geekbench ahead of its official launch on November 5, 2026. The listing reveals some details about its processing power, memory configuration, and expected performance.
The Motorola Signature 27 will succeed the original Motorola Signature, which arrived in January 2026. The company has already confirmed that the new smartphone will feature Qualcomm’s latest Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 chipset, built using a 2nm manufacturing process.
Motorola Signature 27 Appears on Geekbench Ahead of November 5 Launch
According to the Geekbench 7.1 listing, the Motorola Signature 27 runs Android 17 and appears to feature 12GB of RAM. The benchmark identifies approximately 10.94GB of available memory, suggesting that the device will come with a 12GB RAM configuration.
The listing also provides details about the processor’s eight-core configuration. It includes three cores clocked at 3.74GHz, another three running at 4.03GHz, and two high-performance cores reaching speeds of up to 5.01GHz.
In the Geekbench CPU tests, the Motorola Signature 27 scored 3,313 points in the single-core test and 11,088 points in the multi-core test. These results offer an early indication of the phone’s processing capabilities ahead of its official release.
The new chipset also represents an upgrade over the previous Motorola Signature. The earlier model uses the Snapdragon 8 Gen 5 processor, which is based on a 3nm manufacturing process and offers CPU clock speeds of up to 3.8GHz. The move to a 2nm chipset suggests that Motorola is focusing on improved performance and processing efficiency with its next flagship.
Motorola has also confirmed several premium features for the Signature 27. These include a 165Hz display, a 200MP periscope telephoto camera, and a sound system developed in partnership with Bang & Olufsen.
The 165Hz refresh rate should offer smoother scrolling and animations, while the high-resolution periscope camera is expected to provide advanced zoom capabilities. The Bang & Olufsen audio system will also add to the phone’s premium multimedia experience.
With its Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 processor, high-refresh-rate display, and advanced camera hardware, the Motorola Signature 27 is shaping up to be a powerful flagship smartphone.
Motorola will officially unveil the device on November 5. More details about its pricing, availability, and remaining specifications are expected around the launch.

items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
vivo today announced that the vivo Y32 is now on sale across Pakistan. Built around the theme “Power Long, Grow On.”, the Y32 pairs an 8000 mAh BlueVolt Battery with 44W FlashCharge and reverse charging. Its 6-Year Battery Health design retains at least 80% battery health after 1,500 charge cycles in vivo laboratory testing. For everyday durability, the Y32 offers IP69 dust and water resistance, Titan Glass, and the SGS 5-Star Premium Performance Mark for overall unit drop resistance.
A New Mobile Experience for Busy Days: vivo Y32 Unites Premium Styling with Effortless Longevity
Power for a Full Day Away: Uncompromising Endurance and Longevity
For mobile workers and field specialists operating in environments where “Business Never Stops,” reliable energy is a fundamental necessity. The vivo Y32 addresses this demand with an expansive 8000 mAh BlueVolt Battery, providing a reliable power cell built to support relentless daily tasks without forcing users to pause for frequent charging breaks. Whether a delivery rider is navigating complex urban intersections, a logistics manager is coordinating cross-dock operations, or a sales executive is traveling between off-site appointments, the device supplies uninterrupted power from early morning through the late evening hours.
This high-capacity battery is designed to handle demanding workflows with ease. In everyday work scenarios, a single full charge easily covers prolonged sessions of continuous GPS navigation, extensive voice and video communications, real-time job-site photography, and steady cloud data synchronization. In a simulated 12-hour day of mixed work and personal use, the Y32 still had 20% battery remaining. That extra power gives users the freedom to enjoy digital entertainment, stream media, and connect with family on the commute home. This dependable stamina also brings practical meaning to the promise of “Power for a Full Day Away”, freeing users from the inconvenience of carrying bulky power banks.
See Also: TECNO Stays Ahead of Samsung and vivo in Pakistan’s Latest Local Mobile Rankings
Complementing this daily endurance is a strong focus on long-term operational health. The Y32 incorporates 6-Year Battery Health engineering, which has been verified under rigorous laboratory testing to maintain at least 80% of its original effective capacity after 1,500 complete charge and discharge cycles. Based on an average charging cadence of once every 1.5 days, this performance translates to roughly six years of dependable daily operation, ensuring that the phone remains a trusted tool years into its service life. Rigorous lab tests also show that Y32 can stand by for 4 hours at -20°C and can maintain storage function for 24 hours at -40°C. The stable performance in extreme environments also gives users another layer of peace of mind.
To protect the battery over time, the Y32 features Overnight Charging Protection and a Battery Life Extender. Bypass Charging supports everyday use, and 44W FlashCharge provides fast top-ups during the day.
Sophisticated Design and Craftsmanship
The vivo Y32 pairs its large battery with a refined design. The rear features a metallic camera module in a volcanic crater shape, finished with a premium texture. The Y32 is available in three colors: Twilight Red, Sunset Orange, and Meteor White. A side-mounted capacitive fingerprint sensor also completes the design.
Practical Durability for Braving the Real World
The vivo Y32 is built for demanding everyday environments. It carries IP69 dust and water resistance, supported by a triple-module water-resistant structure, with Wet-Hand Touch and One-Tap Water and Dust Ejection for use in real-world conditions. For impact protection, the Y32 combines Titan Glass with a comprehensive cushioning structure. It has also earned the SGS 5-Star Premium Performance Mark for Overall Unit
Drop Resistance and passed military-grade shock resistance testing, and an AirSpring Technology drop-resistant phone case is included.
First-Sale Availability
Starting today, the vivo Y32 is available for purchase across Pakistan in Sunset Orange, Twilight Red and Meteor White. The 6GB+128GB and 6GB+256GB variants cost PKR 82,999 and PKR 99,999, respectively.
Consumers can purchase the vivo Y32 through vivo’s official online e-store, authorized online commercial partners and physical retailers like Experience Store Packages Mall Lahore, Experience Store Hall Road Lahore, Experience Store Hyderabad, Experience Store Karachi and other authorized retailers too.
The post A New Mobile Experience for Busy Days: vivo Y32 Unites Premium Styling with Effortless Longevity appeared first on PhoneWorld.

items.author: Shrishti Bisht
items.content:
AU Small Finance Bank (AU SFB) is investigating a potential data leak involving a Salesforce-hosted software platform holding limited information on its vehicle loan customers, after a hacker group claimed to have accessed sensitive customer and internal records.
The Jaipur-headquartered lender confirmed the investigation, while maintaining that its own systems remain unaffected and all banking services are operating normally.
Separately, a threat actor has allegedly offered administrator access to electronics retailer Vijay Sales’ systems for $25,000. Neither the extent of the alleged access nor the extraction of any data has been independently confirmed.
The AU SFB investigation follows a post flagged by cybersecurity tracking account Hackmanac on X. A group calling itself ScarlettGroup claimed to have breached the lender’s records and threatened to publish the allegedly stolen information.
According to the group, the information includes KYC records, PAN and Aadhaar details, credit reports, bank statements, loan applications, signed agreements, and insurance records.
It also claimed to have accessed customer relationship management (CRM) data, employee information, and audit logs. Inc42 could not independently verify these claims.
“AU Small Finance Bank is investigating a potential data leak involving a software-as-a-service (SaaS) platform managed and hosted by Salesforce, which holds limited data relating to our vehicle loan customers,” a bank spokesperson told ThePrint. “We reaffirm that the Bank’s own systems remain unaffected and all banking services are operating normally.”
The lender did not confirm whether the Salesforce-hosted platform was the source of the data the group claims to hold. It also did not disclose how many customers may have been affected.
AU SFB partnered with Salesforce in 2024 to digitise onboarding for its vehicle loan customers and streamline their journeys. At the time, Bhaskar Karkera, head of retail assets at AU SFB, described Salesforce as the bank’s partner in digitising customer journeys for vehicle loans.
Salesforce customers have previously faced cyberattacks involving social engineering and compromised third-party application connections. In one campaign, attackers used voice phishing to trick employees into connecting malicious applications to corporate Salesforce accounts, potentially exposing customer data.
However, there is no verified evidence linking the AU SFB incident to those campaigns or establishing that Salesforce’s core platform was compromised.
Vijay Sales Access Claim
Separately, an actor using the handle ‘shinymontanna’ claims to be selling super administrator access to Vijay Sales’ internal systems for $25,000, according to a post shared by the X account DarkWeb Informer.
Super administrator access typically gives a user broad control over a system, including the ability to manage other users and their permissions.
The listing claims access to more than 3 Mn order records, information on 15,000 employees, and billing records relating to approximately 1.4 Lakh vendors.
The actor further claims that the access covers customer information, payment and bank transfer records, inventory, financial reports, and internal applications, with permissions to view, modify, and export data.
Screenshots purportedly showing administrative dashboards and super administrator privileges have also been circulated.
However, the claims remain unverified. There is no independent confirmation of the extent of the alleged access or whether any customer or corporate information has been extracted.
Vijay Sales did not respond to Inc42’s queries on the matter.
The developments follow other recent cybersecurity incidents involving customer data exposure and vulnerabilities in digital systems.
Earlier this month, SBI flagged the exposure of 3,897 customer records on the dark web. The records reportedly included personal information such as mobile numbers, dates of birth, email addresses, and residential addresses.
Separately, two critical vulnerabilities in PHP, an open-source programming language widely used to build websites, came to light, prompting governments and companies worldwide to take emergency action.
Cybersecurity company eMudhra also recently announced plans to voluntarily wind down its global secure sockets layer and transport layer security (SSL/TLS) certificate business following a certificate security incident.
A researcher found that private keys associated with eight of its intermediate certificate authorities (CAs), which issue digital certificates used to secure website connections, could be recovered.
eMudhra said it revoked all eight affected intermediates and that no certificates had been issued from them. It also said its infrastructure had not been compromised and no data had been breached.
The post AU SFB Probes Potential Data Leak, Vijay Sales’ Admin Access Allegedly Listed For $25K appeared first on Inc42 Media.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he was open to calls for a formal apology for Britain's historical role in slavery, ​before attending next week's Commonwealth summit at which he is likely ‌to face demands for financial reparations.
Writing in the Guardian newspaper, Burnham said Britain was "offering a structured dialogue with those affected by the transatlantic slave trade", in which at ​least 12.5 million Africans were abducted and sold into slavery.
"Listening to ​calls for a formal apology on behalf of the British ⁠state will form an important part of this process, and I am ​open to them," he added.
But Burnham rejected calls for financial reparations, writing: "I do ​not think that British people today can be held liable for historical wrongs, however heinous, that happened in a different age under different laws and in which they played ​no personal part."
From the 15th to the 19th century, millions of Africans ​were sold into slavery by European traders, with Britain transporting an estimated 3.2 million ‌people ⁠across the Atlantic, according to the Transatlantic Slave Trade Database.
Ahead of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in Antigua and Barbuda next week, King Charles, who is touring the Caribbean, said it was "only right that we should ​acknowledge the great suffering ​and injustices of ⁠the past".
Caribbean leaders are expected to press demands for reparations, which they have often framed in terms of ​debt relief, development finance, education, healthcare and climate resilience.
Burnham ​also wrote ⁠in the Guardian that he wanted to "launch a new drive on debt", including by helping more vulnerable countries "repay over a longer time period and with better ⁠rates".
Read more: King Charles' sorrow over slavery faces test as reparations movement gains ground
Antigua ​and Barbuda Prime Minister Gaston Browne welcomed Burnham's ​comments and proposals for practical assistance, though he added in a Facebook post: "The Caribbean's longstanding ​position on reparatory justice remains unchanged."

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Pakistan is exploring new business and investment opportunities in Nordic countries following the participation of a 30-member Pakistani technology delegation in Oslo Innovation Week 2026 to boost IT exports.
The delegation, organised by the Pakistan Software Houses Association (P@SHA), held important meetings with Norwegian investors, business leaders, policymakers, and technology stakeholders to explore potential cooperation between Pakistan and Norway.
Pakistan Targets Nordic Markets to Boost IT Exports to $15 Billion
The discussions focused on strengthening partnerships in information technology, artificial intelligence (AI), and deep technology. Pakistani companies also explored opportunities for joint ventures, investment, and business expansion in Oslo and other Nordic markets.
A business networking session at the Norwegian Parliament brought Pakistani and Norwegian business leaders together to discuss potential areas of cooperation. The session provided an opportunity for Pakistani technology companies to present their expertise and connect directly with European businesses and investors.
During the event, Pakistani companies highlighted their capabilities in artificial intelligence, software engineering, enterprise automation, and green technology. The participation also showcased Pakistan’s engineering talent and growing capacity to provide technology solutions to international markets.
P@SHA aims to use these international engagements to help Pakistani software houses establish direct connections with European companies and investors. The association is also working to expand Pakistan’s IT exports beyond traditional markets and introduce local technology businesses to new international opportunities.
According to P@SHA Chairman Dr. Shoaib Ahmad Khan, the delegation received positive feedback on Pakistani engineering talent during Oslo Innovation Week. He highlighted the importance of connecting local technology companies with international businesses to create opportunities for investment and long-term partnerships.
See Also: Pakistan Targets 50% Localisation in New Mobile Phone Manufacturing Policy
P@SHA has set a target of increasing Pakistan’s IT exports to $15 billion by the financial year 2031. Expanding into Nordic and other European markets is part of the broader effort to achieve this goal.
The association plans to follow up on the connections established in Oslo and turn them into formal agreements, business partnerships, joint ventures, and investment opportunities.
The participation in Oslo Innovation Week 2026 marks another step towards strengthening Pakistan’s position in the global technology industry. By building international business relationships and showcasing local expertise, P@SHA aims to create new growth opportunities for Pakistani IT companies and increase the country’s presence in emerging technology markets.
The post Pakistan Targets Nordic Countries to Boost IT Exports to $15 Billion appeared first on PhoneWorld.

Key Startup Funding Highlights Of The Week
Ecommerce led the sectoral funding charts this week, with nine deals bringing in $33.4 Mn. Troovy’s $10.5 Mn and Ace Blend’s $9.9 Mn rounds did much of the heavy lifting, together accounting for 61% of the sector’s funding this week.
AI was second-placed this week, with five startups raising $30.4 Mn. Simplismart’s $14 Mn round and Live2.ai’s $13.7 Mn infusion contributed 91% to the total haul this week.
Five advanced hardware and technology startups bagged $6.8 Mn this week, while the enterprise services sector also saw three deals worth $9.5 Mn.
On the investor front, Blume Ventures and Antler emerged as the most active investors this week and backed three startups each.
Startup IPO Updates Of The Week
SEBI has greenlit appliance maker Atomberg’s proposed ₹450 Cr IPO, which comprises a fresh issue of shares worth up to ₹450 Cr and an OFS component of up to 7.65 Cr shares.
Edtech startup Imarticus Learning plans to file its DRHP via the confidential pre-filing route in the next two to three months. It is eyeing a ₹1,000 Cr IPO, up from its earlier planned issue size of ₹750 Cr.
Startup Fund Updates This Week
Unacademy cofounders Gaurav Munjal and Roman Saini are raising a ₹700 Cr venture capital fund, Longshot Capital, to back AI and deeptech startups.
Startup M&As This Week
Nasdaq-listed Freshworks has acquired Israel-based AI startup Robusta Dev for an undisclosed amount to strengthen its Freshservice platform and bolster its AI stack.
AI-native cybersecurity startup Protectt.ai plans to acquire a controlling stake in AIShield, an AI security platform incubated at Bosch Global Software Technologies, through a deal involving primary and secondary components. Bosch will retain a minority stake in the latter.
Other Developments Of The Week
AI unicorn Sarvam AI is in talks to raise around $300 Mn from Nasdaq-listed IT services company Cognizant in a round that could value the Bengaluru-based AI giant at $3.5 Bn-$4 Bn, more than double its previous valuation of $1.5 Bn.
Aerospace technology startup Parsec Aerospace is in talks to raise around $10 Mn in a round led by Nexus Venture Partners, with participation from existing backers, including Lightspeed Venture Partners.
AI-powered trading platform Tradl has raised $4.1 Mn in a seed round led by Nexus Venture Partners and Stellaris Venture Partners.
Fintech startup axiTrust is in talks to raise around $5 Mn in its Series A round, likely to be led by Singapore-based Argor.vc.
Traveltech startup Holiday Tribe is also in discussions to raise around ₹50 Cr from the likes of RPSG Capital Ventures and others. The round is yet to be finalised.
Two funds managed by Baillie Gifford have marked down their holdings in VerSe Innovation, the parent of DailyHunt and Josh, by as much as 80% over different time periods.
D2C cat food startup Smylo is in advanced talks to raise around ₹30 Cr via a mix of equity and debt. While a new VC firm is likely to join its cap table, existing backer DSG Consumer Partners is also expected to participate.
CCI has cleared Prosus’ proposal to invest $100 Mn in IPO-bound fintech startup Navi for a minority stake. This is Navi’s first institutional fundraise.

items.author: Palak Sharma
items.content:
D2C home appliance startup upliance.ai is in advanced talks to raise $3 Mn to $4 Mn (around ₹28-₹37 Cr) in a Series A funding round, sources told Inc42.
A new investor is expected to join the startup’s cap table, while existing backers, including Khosla Ventures, are looking to invest further, the sources said.
The startup could use the fresh capital to strengthen R&D, improve its interface, and expand into international markets, they added.
Inc42 has reached out to upliance.ai for comment. The story will be updated based on the startup’s response.
The startup previously raised ₹34 Cr in a seed funding round led by Khosla Ventures in February 2024, at a valuation of ₹143 Cr (about $15 Mn).
Founded in 2021 by former Ather Energy executive Mahek Mody and former Chaayos employee Mohit Sharma, upliance.ai builds smart kitchen appliances. Its portfolio includes the upliance 2.0+ cooking assistant and a 12L Smart Air Fryer Oven launched in July.
The startup uses generative AI to translate recipes into instructions its cooking assistant can execute. For instance, its YouTube recipe feature breaks cooking videos into steps and maps them to the appliance’s capabilities, including chopping ingredients and adjusting cooking sequences.
In an earlier interaction with Inc42, Mody said customers can also access recipes through the company’s app and leave a voicemail if something goes wrong while cooking. The team responds to these queries and uses ratings and feedback to improve recipes over time.
The funding talks come amid growing activity in India’s smart kitchen appliances market. According to MarkNtel Advisors, the market is estimated to be worth $800 Mn in 2026 and is projected to reach $2.99 Bn by 2032, growing at a CAGR of 25%. Cooking appliances account for about 48% of the market in 2026.
The segment includes both startups and established appliance brands offering varying degrees of cooking automation.
Wonderchef entered the automated cooking appliance space in April 2024 with the launch of Chef Magic, an all-in-one kitchen robot. The device automates functions such as chopping, stirring, steaming, sautéing and kneading, and comes with an in-built weighing scale, touchscreen interface and more than 600 preloaded recipes.
More recently, Philips launched OneChef in India in March 2026, combining functions such as air frying, stir frying, steaming, and boiling in a single appliance.

items.content:
By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto
SOKOTO — The governorship candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) in Sokoto State, Hon. Manir Muhammad Dan’iya, has reportedly escaped unhurt after suspected gunmen opened fire on his convoy near the Sultan Abubakar III International Airport on Friday night.
The incident occurred at about 9pm on October 30, 2026, shortly after Dan’iya had escorted former Sokoto State Governor and Senator representing Sokoto South, Aminu Waziri Tambuwal, to the airport.
The candidate’s bulletproof sports utility vehicles were reportedly damaged in the shooting.
Confirming the incident, the Sokoto State Police Command’s Public Relations Officer, DSP Ahmad Rufae, said the command had received a report of the incident at the airport and would take necessary action.
He added that anyone found culpable would be dealt with in accordance with the law.
In a statement issued by his media aide, Aminu Abdullahi, Dan’iya alleged that personnel of the Sokoto Marshal and the Sokoto State Community Guard blocked his convoy and prevented it from passing through the airport area.
According to the statement, the personnel claimed they were acting on directives from their superiors not to allow ADC members into Sokoto State.
It further alleged that attempts by members of Dan’iya’s security team to resolve the confrontation failed before gunshots were fired, damaging the candidate’s bulletproof vehicles.
The statement also claimed that two Department of State Services (DSS) operatives attached to the candidate’s security team were detained during the confrontation.
Dan’iya described the incident as a threat to his personal safety and a development capable of undermining democratic freedoms, political participation and peaceful coexistence in the state.
The ADC candidate also alleged that earlier on Friday, his team had observed unusual deployments of Sokoto Marshal and Community Guard personnel at various entry points into the state, where vehicles bearing ADC inscriptions were allegedly stopped from entering.
He said what initially appeared to be routine security operations had raised concerns about a possible attempt to restrict the movement and political activities of opposition members.
“If security personnel can block a gubernatorial candidate, fire gunshots during a confrontation, damage his vehicle and detain officers assigned to his protection, then the people of Sokoto deserve urgent answers.
“No one should be above the law, and no security outfit should be used to threaten political opponents,” Dan’iya was quoted as saying.
The candidate disclosed that he had visited the Commissioner of Police in the state to formally report the incident, present his account of what transpired and seek intervention.
He called on the Inspector-General of Police, the Director-General of the DSS and other relevant security authorities to investigate the incident, identify those responsible and determine whether any unlawful orders had been issued.
Dan’iya also demanded the immediate release of the two DSS operatives, if they remained in custody, and urged the authorities to preserve available video footage, operational records, eyewitness accounts and other evidence for an impartial investigation.
He appealed to the Federal Government, the National Assembly, human rights organisations and the international community to pay attention to the security situation in Sokoto, warning that political intimidation and violence could threaten the credibility of the democratic process.
The ADC candidate also challenged the Sokoto State Government to clarify the alleged directives attributed to the security personnel and ensure that state-controlled security outfits operated within the law and without political interference.
“Sokoto is not the property of any government or political party. Every Nigerian has the right to enter the state, move freely and participate in lawful political activities. Any order intended to exclude ADC members from Sokoto would be unacceptable and must be investigated,” he said.
Despite the incident, Dan’iya urged his supporters to remain calm, avoid provocation and refrain from retaliation, insisting that neither intimidation nor violence would make him or the ADC abandon their constitutional and democratic rights.
He said he would continue to pursue his political ambition peacefully and lawfully, while urging security agencies to protect citizens irrespective of their political affiliations.
The allegations contained in the ADC statement had yet to be independently verified as of the time of filing this report.
There was also no official response from the Sokoto State Government, the Sokoto Marshal or the Community Guard explaining their account of the incident.
The police and other relevant security authorities are expected to clarify the circumstances surrounding the reported shooting, the alleged detention of the DSS operatives and the damage to the candidate’s convoy.

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
Omoyele Sowore, presidential candidate of the African Action Congress (AAC), and the Ekiti State Police Command have given conflicting accounts of an incident at a restaurant in Ado-Ekiti, Ekiti State, on Friday.
While Sowore insisted that he and members of his team were violently attacked, the police described the incident as an altercation with some individuals, saying the activist sustained a minor injury.
The Police Public Relations Officer, Sunday Abutu, said the command received an alert that Sowore was having issues with some individuals at a restaurant in Ado-Ekiti and immediately deployed operatives to the scene.
Abutu said the operatives rescued the AAC presidential candidate and took him to the Police Hospital, Ado-Ekiti, where he was receiving treatment.
However, Sowore, in a statement published on his social media accounts, rejected the police description of the incident as an “altercation”.
“There was no altercation! We were attacked!” he declared.
He accused the Ekiti State Police Command and the Department of State Services (DSS) of attempting to suppress evidence relating to the incident.
Sowore alleged that security operatives seized CCTV footage from the restaurant where the incident occurred, claiming that the attackers were captured on camera and accusing the agencies of attempting to shield those responsible.
He also faulted the state Commissioner of Police, CP Falade Adegoroye Michael, for describing the incident as an altercation, saying the police commissioner had visited the scene and seen the injuries sustained by the victims but subsequently played down their severity.
Sowore further alleged that DSS operatives had been trailing and harassing him since his arrival in the state on Thursday.
He claimed that the operatives also threatened the manager of a restaurant where he and his team had earlier eaten, warning him against allowing them to use the premises again.
He said the attack occurred shortly after he concluded an interview at MIDAS FM 90.5 in Ado-Ekiti on Friday.
Sowore also alleged that some of the attackers came from the Ekiti State Government House and received operational support from DSS operatives.
Police Response
The police, however, denied reports that the activist was kidnapped, following a social media post claiming that he had been seized by armed thugs and his whereabouts were unknown.
Abutu said in a statement that the command wished to clarify that Sowore was not kidnapped but was rescued by police operatives after they received information about the incident.
“The command wishes to categorically clarify that Mr. Sowore was not kidnapped. Rather, preliminary information indicates that he had an altercation with some individuals at a restaurant in Ado-Ekiti, following which the police were immediately alerted.
“Upon receiving the report, police operatives swiftly mobilised to the scene and successfully rescued him. He, however, sustained a minor injury and is currently receiving medical attention at the Police Hospital, Ado-Ekiti,” the statement read.
The police spokesman said the Commissioner of Police, Michael Falade, had ordered a discreet investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident, identify those involved and ensure that anyone found culpable was brought to justice.
The command urged members of the public to remain calm and refrain from circulating unverified information capable of creating panic and tension.

items.author: Ayobami
items.content:
Achraf Hakimi rose to the occasion scoring a glorious hat-trick on Friday as a heavily rotated Paris Saint-Germain thumped rock-bottom Le Havre 5-1 in Ligue 1.
PSG’s nearest Ligue 1 rivals Rennes lost 5-2 at Nice to allow the champions to open a four-point gap atop the table with 20pts after nine games.
Lille host Lens later Friday and can close to within two points of PSG should they win, while Monaco can do the same if they win at Paris FC on Sunday.
Le Havre gave PSG a game early on as they suddenly surged forward in numbers with the PSG backline scampering in retreat before striker Josh Maja hammered in the opener against the run of play on 18 minutes.
Pushing for a second, Le Havre were carved open in a quick-fire move with Belgian winger Mika Godts racing onto a Hakimi through-ball to level on 26min.
Two minutes later Hakimi left the defence trailing and his blistering low drive just inside the near post made it 2-1.
The European champions were running the Normandy side ragged before Hakimi scored his second with a fierce free-kick that curled low past the ‘keeper Arnaud Bodard to put PSG 3-1 up.
On a lightning break the hosts poured everyone forward in a brave but naive effort to get back into the game, only for PSG to burst back, catching the home goalkeeper way off his line with not a single defender in his half.
Senny Mayulu ran around the horrified stopper, and his cool long-range finish hit the back of the net with nobody in the box effectively ending the contest, just after the hour.
Hakimi’s hat-trick arrived when he threaded a shot through a forest of players on 69 minutes and had hardly finished a triumphant celebration when coach Luis Enrique subbed him off.
Luis Enrique left stars Desire Doue, Vitinha and Joao Neves on the bench while Ousmane Dembele and Georgian attacker Khvicha Kvaratskhelia were missing through injury.

items.content:
By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi
The Bauchi State Police Command has arrested a 26-year-old man, John Umar Shehu, for allegedly impersonating a Nigerian Army personnel, assaulting a prospective employer and stealing his vehicle in Bauchi.
The suspect, a resident of Bassa Local Government Area of Plateau State, was also accused of criminal breach of trust and theft.
The Police Public Relations Officer, SP Habib Nafiu, disclosed this in a statement issued on behalf of the Commissioner of Police, CP Sani-Omolori Aliyu, on Friday in Bauchi.
According to the statement, the suspect was arrested following a petition received by the command on October 22, 2026, from one Salisu, a resident of the Gida Dubu area of Bauchi.
The petitioner reportedly told the police that the suspect had contacted him on October 18, seeking employment as a driver at his pure water factory. He was subsequently invited for an interview and driving assessment.
However, during the assessment on October 22, the suspect allegedly attacked the factory owner and his neighbour’s son before fleeing with the employer’s vehicle.
The stolen vehicle, a white H-Jet motor vehicle with registration number AE-278-ALK, was later recovered by police detectives in Jos, Plateau State.
The police also recovered a green Infinix Smart 5X phone allegedly stolen alongside the vehicle.
Nafiu said a search conducted on the suspect led to the recovery of various Nigerian Army uniforms and items, including desert and green camouflage uniforms, a jungle hat, an Army raincoat, a camouflage vest and an Army sweater.
He added that the suspect allegedly presented himself as Private Umar Shehu, with service number NA/22/82/1064, claiming to be attached to the 7 Division, Maimalari Barracks, 134 Special Forces Battalion, Borno State.
The police spokesman said the arrest followed an intelligence-led investigation by detectives of the command.
Meanwhile, the Commissioner of Police, CP Sani-Omolori Aliyu, condemned the alleged impersonation, warning that the command would not tolerate the use of the identities and uniforms of security agencies to perpetrate criminal activities.
Aliyu assured that the suspect would be thoroughly investigated and charged to court.
He urged residents to exercise caution when engaging strangers for employment, particularly in sensitive positions, and advised members of the public to verify the identities and credentials of individuals claiming to be personnel of security agencies.
The commissioner also called on residents to promptly report suspicious activities to the police, assuring them of the command’s commitment to protecting lives and property across the state.

By Daniel Abia, Port Harcourt
The Rivers State chapter of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) has met with leaders of the Ikwerre ethnic nationality to seek support for its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, and his running mate, Chibuike Rotimi Amaechi, ahead of the 2027 general elections.
The party’s leadership, led by its state chairman, Dr. Chukwudi Dimkpa, visited Ogbakor Ikwerre, the apex socio-cultural organisation of the Ikwerre people, to present its candidates and solicit the elders’ support.
Dimkpa told the elders and community leaders that the party considered it important to present its candidates to them as respected statesmen and custodians of Ikwerre cultural heritage.
He said an Atiku-Amaechi presidency would focus on moving the country forward, adding that the ADC chose the duo because of their experience and readiness to turn around the nation’s fortunes.
The state chairman also used the opportunity to formally present the party’s governorship candidate, Dr. Gabriel Pidomson, his running mate, Mr. David Okumgba, as well as its senatorial, House of Representatives and State House of Assembly candidates of Ikwerre extraction, seeking the elders’ prayers and support.
“The ADC as a party recognises Ogbakor Ikwerre as a foremost socio-cultural institution representing the identity, heritage and collective interests of the Ikwerre ethnic nationality,” he said.
In his address, Pidomson reminded the elders of the significance of Amaechi’s vice-presidential candidacy, describing him as an illustrious son of Ikwerre who is running alongside Atiku on the ADC presidential ticket.
He expressed hope that the Atiku-Amaechi ticket would emerge victorious in the 2027 presidential election, with Atiku becoming president and Amaechi vice-president.
Pidomson described the prospect of an Ikwerre son occupying the nation’s second-highest political office as significant to the political history and national participation of the ethnic nationality.
He also pledged inclusive governance if elected governor of Rivers State.
“If I am elected Governor of Rivers State, I promise to be a governor for all Rivers people, irrespective of ethnic background, political affiliation or other differences.
“We will build a new Rivers State that will reflect the collective aspirations of its people, with emphasis on inclusive governance, unity, development and the wellbeing of citizens,” he said.
In his remarks, the ADC Deputy National Chairman and Chairman of the Rivers State Governorship Campaign Council, Senator Andrew Uchendu, commended Ogbakor Ikwerre for its contributions to the development and continued existence of Rivers State.
Uchendu recalled the roles played by prominent personalities, including centenarian Prof. Otonti Nduka, Chief Samson Agbaru and Prof. Augustine Ahiazu, in the struggle for greater recognition, inclusion and political representation for the Ikwerre people.
He said their sacrifices and sustained efforts contributed to the emergence of three governors of Rivers State from Ikwerre extraction.
The ADC delegation was received by the President-General of Ogbakor Ikwerre Cultural Organisation Worldwide, HRM King Godspower W. Onuekwa, PhD; its First Vice-President, Prof. Hilary Wordu; Prof. Otonti Nduka; Chief Samson Agbaru; Prof. Augustine Ahiazu and other prominent members.
The Ogbakor Ikwerre leadership welcomed the ADC delegation and offered prayers, blessings and advice.
