The Lagos State Government has warned residents to prepare for possible extreme heat and associated environmental and public health challenges as climate outlooks indicate rising temperatures across parts of Africa, including Nigeria.
The Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Tokunbo Wahab, gave the advisory on Friday, urging residents to take preventive measures to protect their health and wellbeing.
Wahab said the strengthening El Niño climate pattern, alongside the seasonal transition into the dry season, could contribute to unusual temperature conditions, increased heat discomfort, dry spells, dust and deteriorating air quality.
He noted that although the intensity and local impact would depend on prevailing weather patterns, residents should take the emerging climate risks seriously.
According to him, Lagos, as a densely populated and rapidly urbanising coastal city, could face heightened exposure to extreme heat.
“The concentration of buildings, roads and other heat-absorbing infrastructure, coupled with limited green spaces and inadequate ventilation in some neighbourhoods, could intensify temperatures in built-up areas,” he said.
Wahab warned that prolonged exposure to excessive heat could lead to dehydration, heat exhaustion and heatstroke, with potentially serious consequences.
He identified children, older persons, pregnant women, outdoor workers, street traders, construction workers, waste handlers and people with underlying health conditions as particularly vulnerable.
The commissioner urged families, employers, schools and community leaders to pay special attention to these groups and ensure that protective measures were put in place.
He also cautioned that extreme heat could worsen air-quality challenges during the dry season, when dust and haze increase respiratory irritation.
He added that increased reliance on petrol and diesel-powered generators during power interruptions could further worsen local air pollution.
Wahab urged residents to avoid open burning of refuse and adopt environmentally responsible practices.
He advised residents to drink sufficient water regularly, wear lightweight and breathable clothing, seek shade and well-ventilated spaces, and reduce strenuous outdoor activities during the hottest periods of the day.
He also encouraged schools, markets, workplaces and other public facilities to provide adequate ventilation, access to drinking water and shaded areas.
The commissioner urged residents to watch out for warning signs of heat-related illnesses, including excessive sweating, dizziness, headache, weakness, nausea and muscle cramps.
“Anyone experiencing these symptoms should be moved to a cooler environment, given appropriate cooling assistance and taken for medical attention where necessary.
“Sudden collapse or loss of consciousness should be treated as medical emergencies requiring immediate attention.
“Residents with respiratory conditions are also advised to limit exposure to dusty environments and follow relevant health and air-quality advisories,” he said.
Wahab stressed that preparedness must go beyond individual precautions, calling for stronger collaboration among government agencies, environmental experts, health institutions, businesses and community stakeholders.
He urged residents and businesses to support efforts to reduce urban heat by protecting existing trees, promoting tree planting, preserving green spaces, ensuring proper waste disposal and discouraging environmental degradation.
The commissioner said environmental sustainability and climate resilience required collective responsibility, particularly as Lagos continued to address the impacts of climate change and rapid urbanisation.
He assured residents that the ministry, through its relevant agencies, would continue to engage stakeholders and promote public awareness.
He added that the ministry would work with the Nigerian Meteorological Agency (NiMet), Lagos State Ministry of Health and Lagos State Emergency Management Agency (LASEMA) to strengthen preparedness and response.

By Favour Ulebor, Abuja
The Federal Government has assured the Economic Community of West African States, ECOWAS, of its commitment to conducting peaceful, credible, transparent and inclusive general elections in 2027.
In a statement on Friday, the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Bianca Odumegwu-Ojukwu, gave the assurance during a meeting with the ECOWAS Pre-Election Fact-Finding Mission to Nigeria, led by former Vice-President of Sierra Leone, Victor Bockarie Foh, at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Abuja.
Odumegwu-Ojukwu said the Federal Government was committed to ensuring that the electoral process complied with the provisions of the Nigerian Constitution and relevant electoral laws.
She described the 2027 general elections as a defining moment for Nigeria’s democracy, expressing optimism that the process would strengthen democratic governance in the country and the West African sub-region.
The minister said institutional preparedness, transparent voter accreditation, effective management of election results and timely resolution of electoral disputes were important to building public confidence in the electoral system.
She also stressed the need for effective coordination among security agencies to protect candidates, electoral officials, observers and voters before, during and after the elections.
According to her, security personnel must perform their duties professionally and impartially while respecting the country’s human rights obligations.
The minister further highlighted the importance of voter education and effective enforcement of electoral laws, noting that political parties, civil society organisations, traditional institutions and the media had important roles to play in ensuring peaceful elections.
She expressed concern over the dangers of misinformation and disinformation, calling for accurate, accessible and timely information on the electoral process.
Odumegwu-Ojukwu also identified the need to improve measures that would encourage the participation of persons with disabilities and other vulnerable groups in the elections.
Earlier, Foh said the mission was in Nigeria to assess the country’s preparedness for the 2027 general elections through consultations with relevant institutions and stakeholders.
He said the mission had engaged the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, political parties, security agencies, civil society organisations and the media.
Foh disclosed that its earlier engagements with stakeholders, including the Inter-Party Advisory Council, the Nigerian Civil Society Situation Room and the Nigerian Union of Journalists, had been constructive.
He said the mission’s preliminary assessment suggested a favourable environment for the forthcoming elections, adding, however, that consultations were still ongoing.
According to him, the mission would submit a report outlining its findings and recommendations at the end of the exercise.
The former Sierra Leonean vice-president welcomed the assurances given by the minister and expressed optimism about Nigeria’s preparedness for the elections.
He stressed the importance of sustained engagement with stakeholders and addressing identified concerns, noting that Nigeria’s ability to conduct credible elections in 2027 would have wider implications for democratic governance and stability across West Africa.
The meeting ended with both sides reaffirming their commitment to promoting democracy, peace, stability and prosperity in the sub-region.

By Henry Ojelu
Counsel to Pastor Chris Okafor, Mr Ife Ajayi, has faulted the sentimental support for Nollywood actress Doris Ogala over her cyberbullying trial, insisting that freedom of expression does not confer the right to make false and malicious allegations against others without regard for the law.
Ajayi, who spoke in an interview with Vanguard, was reacting to comments by activist Omoyele Sowore and Ogala over alleged injustice in the ongoing trial.
He argued that the right to freedom of expression was not absolute and must be exercised within the limits prescribed by law, particularly where allegations, blackmail and extortion were involved.
According to him, the issues leading to the criminal proceedings should not be treated as a mere disagreement between individuals, but viewed against the background of alleged violations of the rights of others.
Ajayi advised the public to obtain copies of the charges proffered against her. He described her unlawful conduct as a deliberate act that violated the rights of his client and was capable of inciting the public against an individual.
He also urged members of the public to exercise caution in endorsing false allegations made by the actress, insisting that such claims should be subjected to legal scrutiny rather than public sentiment.
Expressing confidence in the judiciary, the lawyer said he was optimistic that the court would deliver justice based on the overwhelming print, audio and video evidence in compliance with the applicable laws.
“I am 100 per cent optimistic that the court will do what is right. The court, in all fairness, even after the defendant’s lawyer pleaded with it to release her on bail and offered to take responsibility for her conduct, gave the prosecution 48 hours to respond,” he said.
Ajayi also faulted Ogala’s conduct during the court proceedings, alleging that her outburst and disruption of proceedings raised questions about her ability to abide by the conditions of her release.
He said the incident suggested that even her counsel might have difficulty guaranteeing her conduct if she were granted bail.
The lawyer maintained that the courtroom was not a place for emotional outbursts or disrespect, stressing that parties to a legal proceeding were expected to conduct themselves in accordance with established rules.
“You cannot behave disrespectfully at a police station or anywhere else and expect to do the same in a court of law. The court is where logic and legal accountability prevail,” he said.
Ajayi further called on the National Assembly to consider stricter legislation against the practice of publicly calling out individuals over private disagreements, particularly where such actions could damage reputations or violate the rights of others.
He argued that personal grievances should be addressed through appropriate legal channels rather than through public accusations and campaigns.
“The law is not about emotion or sentiment. It is about logic and legal accountability. It is a place where people are held accountable for their unlawful conduct,” he said.
He urged members of the public not to accept allegations made in the course of the dispute as established facts, stressing that the court remained the appropriate institution to determine the issues before it.

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
‎
‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru
‎
‎ABUJA — MANAGING Director and Chief Executive of the Nigeria Social Insurance Trust Fund (NSITF), Mr. Oluwaseun Faleye, has urged the judiciary to strengthen the interpretation, adjudication, and enforcement of the Employees’ Compensation Act (ECA) 2010, so that Nigerian workers can fully enjoy the justice and protection the law guarantees.
‎
‎The Act provides compensation for employees—or their dependants—who suffer death, injury, disability, or occupational disease arising from employment.
‎
‎Faleye, in his welcome address at the opening of the NSITF 2026 Legal Stakeholders’ Engagement in Abuja,
‎emphasised that legislation alone is not enough; workers need timely dispute resolution, fair hearings, and effective compliance with court orders to turn statutory rights into real benefits.
‎The theme of the two-day event is “Enhancing Judicial Interpretation, Adjudication and Enforcement under the Employees’ Compensation Act (ECA), 2010.”
‎
‎Mr. Faleye noted that while last year’s engagement focused on strengthening collaboration for the sustainable administration of the Employees’ Compensation Scheme, this year’s edition addresses a deeper question: how statutory rights can be translated into practical justice.
‎
‎Drawing on the experience of everyday Nigerian workers — mothers, construction workers, factory employees and drivers who leave home each day expecting to return he observed that a workplace accident instantly becomes a human crisis with financial, emotional and social consequences.
‎
‎”Does the law provide a framework for protection? Yes. Does the Employees’ Compensation Act establish a system for compensation for work-related injury, disease, disability or death? Yes. But the existence of a law does not by itself guarantee that its promise will be fulfilled,” Mr. Faleye said.
‎
‎He explained that the effectiveness of the ECA depends on three interconnected stages — interpretation, adjudication and enforcement:
‎”First, are the provisions being understood and applied in a manner consistent with their wording, purpose and legal context?
‎
‎”Second, are disputes being resolved fairly, on evidence and applicable law, without avoidable delay? Third, are lawful decisions and orders being given effect so that justice does not end with the pronouncement of judgment? Weakness at any stage can undermine confidence in the entire system.”
‎
‎The NSITF Managing Director underscored the pivotal role of the National Industrial Court of Nigeria (NICN) in labour justice, noting that the Court’s interpretation of the Employees’ Compensation Act has consequences beyond the immediate parties to a dispute.
‎
‎Such decisions, he said, clarify rights, guide the conduct of employers and employees, and shape the resolution of future disputes.
‎
‎For workers, he said, justice means the practical realisation of their entitlements; for employers, it means a predictable legal environment. The credibility of the Scheme, he added, rests on workers’ confidence that legitimate claims will be addressed and on employers’ confidence that their obligations will be determined fairly.
‎
‎Mr. Faleye, a legal practitioner, affirmed that the Fund will continue to strengthen its administrative processes, improve claims handling, promote awareness and encourage employer compliance. He acknowledged, however, that the NSITF cannot achieve these objectives in isolation.
‎
‎He urged participants to treat the engagement not as a ceremonial gathering, but as an opportunity to identify practical solutions, highlight areas requiring greater legal clarity, improve cooperation, reduce avoidable disputes and promote compliance.
‎
‎”The value of a stakeholder engagement lies not merely in the quality of speeches delivered but in the clarity of understanding it produces and the improvements that follow,” he said, calling for frank, informed and constructive deliberations that will yield actionable recommendations for strengthening the administration of the Scheme.
‎
‎”May our deliberations strengthen the rule of law and ensure that the promise of protection becomes a reality for Nigerian workers,” he added.
‎
‎In his goodwill message, the Honourable Minister of Labour and Employment, Alhaji Muhammadu Maigari Dingyadi, stated that the strength of a nation lies not merely in the laws it makes, but in the wisdom with which those laws are applied and the integrity of the institutions entrusted with their administration.
‎
‎While laws may establish rights and define obligations, the Minister said, public confidence ultimately rests on the assurance that justice will be administered fairly, impartially and with due regard for the dignity of every individual.
‎
‎Recalling the enduring words of the late Justice Chukwudifu Oputa that “the judiciary is the last hope of the common man,” the Minister observed that “…this statement carries a profound responsibility.
‎
‎It reminds us that for many citizens, the justice system represents their final recourse when other avenues have failed. Such trust must never be taken lightly.” Such trust, he said, demands wisdom in judgment, integrity in public service and an unwavering commitment to fairness.
‎
‎The Minister reaffirmed the Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment’s belief that a just and productive society must be built on respect for the law, responsible institutions and a shared commitment to the public good, and urged all stakeholders in the administration of the ECA to approach their responsibilities with these values in mind.
‎
‎”The credibility of our institutions is strengthened not by words alone, but by the quality and integrity of their actions,” he stressed.
‎
‎He commended the NSITF Management under Mr. Faleye for convening the engagement, describing it as an important national initiative aimed at strengthening the implementation of the ECA 2010.
‎
‎ He also expressed appreciation to the President of the National Industrial Court, distinguished members of the Bench and Bar, and all participants for their commitment.
‎
‎”May your deliberations be guided by wisdom, enriched by experience and directed towards outcomes that strengthen public confidence in our institutions,” the Minister said.
‎
‎Delivering the keynote address, the President of the National Industrial Court of Nigeria, Hon. Justice Benedict Bakwaph Kanyip, advocated institutional synergy to strengthen the Employees’ Compensation Scheme and ensure that its benefits reach the intended beneficiaries.
‎
‎He commended the NSITF for creating a platform that will enhance the Scheme in the overall interest of Nigerians and the workplace, adding that robust engagement with the judiciary will further boost the Fund’s impact on service delivery under the Scheme.
‎
‎The event drew senior government and judicial officials, including the President of the National Industrial Court of Nigeria; the Permanent Secretary, Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment; Honourable Justices of the National Industrial Court; members of the Bench and Bar; Employers’ Associations; organised labour; and development partners.
The post ‎NSITF seeks stronger enforcement of Employees’ Compensation Act to protect workers’ rights appeared first on Vanguard News.

— Beg Tinubu to intervene
By Johnbosco Agbakwuru
ABUJA — CONTROVERSY over the recent approval of ₦70,000 for Federal Government workers has continued unabated, as the Federal Parastatals and Private Sector Pensioners Association of Nigeria (FEPPPAN) has appealed to President Bola Tinubu to extend the newly approved ₦70,000 monthly transport allowance for public servants to pensioners.
The retired government workers lamented that retirees were being left behind in government efforts to cushion the effects of rising living costs.
FEPPPAN said pensioners also pay transportation fares to hospitals for medical care, markets to purchase essential commodities, and other destinations for economic activities they undertake to supplement their pensions and sustain their livelihoods.
In a statement jointly signed by its President-General, Elder Benjamin Maisamari Amako, and General Secretary, Mr Franklin Erinle, the association questioned why retirees should be excluded from transportation support when they equally bear the burden of rising fares and other costs of living.
According to the statement: “The association questioned the rationale behind excluding pensioners from transportation support when they equally bear the burden of rising transport fares and other costs of living.
“FEPPPAN expressed further disappointment over the continued non-payment of the ₦25,000 monthly subsidy-removal palliative announced by the Federal Government in October 2023, lamenting that eligible pensioners were still awaiting the promised relief even as another support package had been approved for serving workers.”
It called for immediate presidential intervention to address the concerns of pensioners.
The statement said: “FEPPPAN expresses concern that eligible pensioners are yet to receive the promised support, describing the continued wait as a source of frustration for retirees who had hoped that the intervention would provide some relief from the prevailing economic hardship.
“Against this background, the association called on President Tinubu to urgently intervene by directing the relevant government agencies to ensure the payment of the outstanding ₦25,000 subsidy-removal palliative to eligible pensioners.
“It also urged the President to ensure that pensioners are included in the new ₦70,000 monthly transport allowance arrangement, stressing that retirees should not be left out of policies intended to protect Nigerians from the effects of rising living costs.”
It clarified that its appeal was not against the transport allowance approved for serving workers, but against the apparent neglect of retirees in the government’s response to the economic hardship confronting Nigerians.
It lamented that pensioners, many of whom depend on fixed monthly incomes to pay for food, medication, transportation and other necessities, were being left to contend with rising expenses without comparable relief.
FEPPPAN recalled that on October 1, 2023, the Federal Government announced a ₦25,000 monthly palliative for three months to cushion the effects of petrol subsidy removal, with vulnerable pensioners among the groups identified for assistance. It said the continued wait for the promised relief had deepened retirees’ frustration and hardship.
The association urged Tinubu to direct the relevant government agencies to expedite the payment of the outstanding palliative to eligible pensioners and ensure their inclusion in the new ₦70,000 monthly transport allowance arrangement.
FEPPPAN maintained that pensioners deserved the same consideration in government policies intended to ease economic hardship, stressing that their years of service to the country should not leave them forgotten when relief measures are being implemented.

By Kingsley Omonobi
The Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Rilwan Disu, has secured an offer of specialised training for up to 5,000 Nigeria Police Force personnel in Italy as part of efforts to strengthen the country’s response to terrorism and other security threats.
The proposed training, focusing on counter-insurgency operations and policing in difficult rural and forested terrains, followed Disu’s working visit to Italy, where he held discussions with Italian law enforcement authorities on security cooperation, technology transfer and institutional development.
The initiative is aimed at enhancing the operational capacity of the police to tackle terrorism, kidnapping, arms trafficking and other criminal activities through intelligence-led policing and improved tactical capabilities.
A statement issued on Friday by the Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Ani Iniedu, said the proposed training would cover tactical operations, intelligence-led patrols, protection of critical infrastructure, digital and scientific forensics, cybercrime, explosives detection, financial investigations, asset tracing and anti-extortion techniques.
It said the programme would extend beyond the Police Mobile Force to include specialised units such as explosive ordnance disposal and forensic teams.
During the visit, Disu met with the Commander General of the Italian Carabinieri, Lieutenant-General Salvatore Luongo, to explore opportunities for technical assistance, specialised training and institutional cooperation.
The IGP and his delegation also visited the Carabinieri Centre of Excellence for Stability Police Units (CoESPU) in Vicenza, where they assessed training facilities and explored ways of adapting specialised programmes to Nigeria’s security challenges.
Among the proposals discussed were command courses for 40 senior police officers, leadership training for 100 junior commanders and the deployment of a mobile assistance team to support Police Mobile Force training schools in Gwoza and Ila-Orangun.
The delegation also sought Italian support for developing a national stability policing doctrine and standard operating procedures to promote professionalism, operational consistency and civilian protection, particularly in communities recovering from conflict.
Further discussions focused on possible cooperation in canine operations, forensic science and mounted policing, including horse breeding and local capacity development for public order management and other policing responsibilities.
To facilitate the implementation of the proposed initiatives, Disu proposed a memorandum of understanding covering training, technology transfer and operational doctrine.
He also invited an assessment team from the Italian Carabinieri to Abuja to identify priority areas and develop practical implementation strategies.
The Inspector-General reaffirmed the commitment of the Nigeria Police Force to international partnerships aimed at strengthening operational readiness, improving investigative capacity and enhancing the protection of lives and property.
The Force said it would continue engaging relevant international partners to advance the proposals in line with Nigeria’s security priorities and efforts to build a more professional, capable and responsive police institution.

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta
Former President Olusegun Obasanjo has criticised President Bola Tinubu’s defence of government borrowing, declaring that debt is worse than leprosy because of its devastating consequences for present and future generations.
Obasanjo also warned Nigeria and other African countries against allowing foreign interests to dominate artificial intelligence, AI, saying the emerging technology could become another instrument of exploitation and digital colonialism if the continent failed to develop its own technological capacity.
The former president spoke on Friday in Abeokuta, Ogun State, at the Ajibosin Platform, a public forum themed, “Leveraging Artificial Intelligence to Solve Grassroots Problems and Accelerate National Development”.
Reacting to Tinubu’s earlier assertion that borrowing was not leprosy, Obasanjo argued that the accumulation of public debt could mortgage the country’s future and impose an unbearable burden on generations yet unborn.
“And for anybody to say debt is no leprosy, is absolute nonsense. Debt is worse than leprosy because leprosy destroys only one person. Debt destroys generations,” he declared.
Tinubu had defended his administration’s borrowing policy in April, insisting that borrowing was not inherently wrong if the country had the capacity to repay.
“If we have to borrow, we borrow. Borrowing is not leprosy; we just have to work hard to be able to pay for it,” the President had said during a meeting with Plateau State leaders, led by Governor Caleb Mutfwang and the National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, at the State House.
The President’s position came amid concerns over Nigeria’s rising debt profile and the increasing proportion of government revenue committed to debt servicing.
Obasanjo also questioned Nigeria’s economic performance over the years, particularly the depreciation of the naira against the United States dollar.
Recounting his experience as a farmer, he said the naira was stronger than the dollar when he established his farm 47 years ago.
“When I started my farm, 47 years ago, naira to the dollar was one naira to $1.85. Forty-seven years ago. What has Nigeria done in 47 years that we now have 1,500 naira to a dollar? What have we done?” he asked.
He challenged the country’s political leadership to demonstrate its understanding of Nigeria’s problems and identify practical solutions to the challenges confronting the nation.
“What do our leaders know? And what do they not know? And from what they know, what can they do for us?” he queried.
The former president also faulted Nigeria’s dependence on the World Bank and International Monetary Fund (IMF), arguing that their economic prescriptions were not necessarily designed to address the country’s peculiar circumstances.
“World Bank and IMF were not designed for us. They were not built by us. They were built before we became independent. And that’s the people who would determine what we do,” he said.
He urged Nigerian leaders to scrutinise foreign economic prescriptions and ensure that national policies reflected the country’s interests and development priorities.
Turning to artificial intelligence, Obasanjo warned that Africa risked repeating the mistakes of its colonial past if it allowed foreign interests to control the technology and its applications.
Although he acknowledged that he was not technically knowledgeable about AI, he said ownership and control were critical to ensuring that the technology served African interests.
“I don’t know too much technically about AI, but I know that anything that is not under your control can be abused against you. And you can see that this has already started,” he said.
Drawing parallels between AI and Africa’s historical experiences with slavery, colonialism and economic dependency, Obasanjo urged African leaders to approach the technological revolution with caution.
He also questioned the concept of technology transfer, asking African countries to examine the terms and benefits of their engagements with foreign technology providers.
“But what exactly is technology transfer? Who transferred technology to them, and what did they pay for it?” he queried.
Obasanjo further criticised what he described as unequal international economic arrangements, citing restrictions on agricultural subsidies for developing countries despite continued support for farmers in developed economies.
He expressed concern over the estimated 24 million Nigerian children out of school, warning that the situation could create serious challenges for future generations.
“We have 24 million Nigerian children who should be in school but are not. If you are looking for the disasters of tomorrow, these children represent one of them,” he said.
He challenged policymakers and technology stakeholders to explore how AI could improve access to education and address learning challenges.
On agriculture, Obasanjo advocated the deployment of artificial intelligence to help farmers identify suitable crops, improve productivity and strengthen food and nutrition security.
Also speaking at the event, guest speaker and historian, Dr Umar Ardo, warned that Africa could be entering another phase of economic exploitation through artificial intelligence if it failed to secure ownership and control of its data, technological infrastructure and intellectual resources.
In a presentation titled, “From Slave Ships to Server Farms: Artificial Intelligence and Africa’s Unbroken History of Extraction”, Ardo argued that although AI offered significant opportunities for economic transformation, it could deepen existing inequalities if African countries remained dependent on foreign technology companies.
He said the continent must move beyond adopting foreign innovations and address fundamental questions surrounding ownership, control, regulation and the distribution of economic benefits.
“AI offers Africa important opportunities, but without ownership, safeguards and public purpose, it could extend a long history in which Africa supplies value while others control and capture it,” he said.
Tracing Africa’s economic history over five centuries, Ardo identified the transatlantic slave trade, colonial exploitation of natural resources and post-independence economic dependency as major phases of external extraction.
He explained that while the slave trade commodified African lives, colonialism focused largely on exploiting mineral and agricultural resources, while many post-independence economies remained dependent on exporting raw materials and importing finished products.
According to him, infrastructure and technologies introduced during colonial rule, including railways, steam engines and administrative systems, were largely organised around extracting African resources and transporting them to foreign markets.
“We supplied resources and labour; others controlled the machinery and captured much of the value,” he stated.
Ardo also identified the migration of highly trained African professionals, including doctors, nurses, engineers and scientists, to foreign countries as another dimension of the continent’s continuing resource losses.
He warned that data could become the next major commodity in Africa’s history of external extraction, noting that information generated by citizens, hospitals, farmers, businesses, indigenous communities and public institutions was increasingly valuable to the global digital economy.
“Data may become the fourth commodity in this long history of extraction,” he cautioned.
The historian expressed concern that the infrastructure for processing information, developing AI models and generating intellectual property and commercial profits remained disproportionately controlled outside Africa.
He questioned who benefited when farmers’ agricultural practices, patients’ medical records, indigenous languages, traditional medicine and cultural knowledge were incorporated into AI systems developed by foreign companies.
“When farmers’ planting patterns are recorded, who controls that knowledge; the farmer or the platform?” he asked.
Ardo canvasses local AI development, data sovereignty
To prevent artificial intelligence from becoming another instrument of economic dependency, Ardo proposed a framework anchored on technological sovereignty, data protection, indigenous innovation, grassroots development and continental cooperation.
He called for stronger legal and institutional safeguards against the uncontrolled exploitation of personal data and traditional knowledge.
While acknowledging the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 as an important step towards protecting citizens’ information, he said privacy protection alone was insufficient to guarantee data sovereignty.
He advocated additional mechanisms to protect community knowledge, ensure fair compensation and guarantee Africans a reasonable share of the commercial value generated from their data and intellectual resources.
Ardo urged the Federal Government to increase investment in domestic computing capacity, reliable energy infrastructure, semiconductor technology, research institutions and indigenous AI development.
He maintained that Nigeria, with a population exceeding 230 million, should not remain merely a consumer market for foreign technology.
“A country of over 230 million people should be more than a market for foreign technology,” he declared.
He also called for the development of locally controlled datasets and AI models capable of understanding African languages, agricultural practices, medicinal traditions and customary knowledge under African ownership and appropriate safeguards.
On grassroots development, Ardo urged governments to ensure that communities benefited directly from AI applications in primary healthcare, agricultural extension services, local government administration, revenue collection, conflict resolution and disaster management.
He further advocated comprehensive AI training programmes in universities, polytechnics and colleges of education to develop software developers, technicians, data stewards and other professionals.
On continental cooperation, he urged Nigeria to work with other African countries to harmonise data governance regulations, develop shared technological infrastructure and strengthen the continent’s bargaining power in engagements with international technology companies.
He identified the African Union’s Data Policy Framework, adopted in 2022, as an important foundation for coordinated continental action.
Warning that digital extraction could be more difficult to identify and resist than the exploitation of physical resources, Ardo said information could cross national borders without the knowledge or meaningful understanding of the people and communities generating it.
“One of the most efficient systems of extraction is the one its subjects volunteer to use,” he warned.
He urged African leaders to approach the AI revolution with a clear understanding of the continent’s history, insisting that Africa must become a builder, owner and rule-maker in the global technology ecosystem rather than remain a passive consumer of foreign innovations.
Drawing a comparison between Africa’s historical experiences and the emerging digital economy, he said: “Five centuries ago, they came for our bodies. Then they came for our land and its riches. Then our commodities and trained minds. Today, they come for our data.”
He, however, maintained that Africa still had the opportunity to determine its technological future.
“The choice is ours. Artificial intelligence can become another instrument through which Africa is managed, or an instrument through which Africa begins to manage its own destiny,” he added.

items.content:
By Olasunkanmi Akoni
Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu has urged residents to support his deputy, Dr Obafemi Hamzat, describing him as an experienced administrator capable of sustaining the state’s development if elected governor in 2027.
Sanwo-Olu made the appeal on Friday at the official unveiling of Hamzat’s seven-pillar development manifesto, tagged PROMISE, at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and Creative Arts, formerly the National Theatre, Iganmu, Lagos.
The governor cautioned residents against experimenting with the state’s leadership, insisting that Lagos required continuity to consolidate its development gains.
The event attracted former Governor Babatunde Fashola, members of the Lagos State Executive Council, party chieftains, religious leaders, traditional rulers, media executives, local government chairmen, captains of industry and other dignitaries.
Speaking as Special Guest of Honour, Sanwo-Olu described Hamzat, the All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate, as a dependable partner who had demonstrated commitment to the state’s development throughout their seven years in office.
Using a relay race as an analogy for political succession, he said Lagos needed an experienced successor who understood the administration’s policies and ongoing projects.
Recalling the political developments of September 2018, Sanwo-Olu said Hamzat had stepped aside from his governorship ambition following appeals by party leaders and agreed to become his running mate.
“In seven years, there has not been one day—not one—when I had to wonder whose side my deputy was on.
“Governors and their deputies have torn states apart in this country. In Lagos, there has been one government, one direction, and one voice,” he said.
Sanwo-Olu cited Hamzat’s involvement in critical government decisions, including the management of the COVID-19 pandemic, the October 2020 unrest and the execution of major infrastructure projects such as the Blue and Red rail lines and the Lekki Deep Sea Port.
He also traced Hamzat’s public service career to 2005, when he served as Commissioner for Science and Technology under the administration of former Governor Bola Tinubu.
He subsequently served as Commissioner for Works and Infrastructure under Fashola, during which he was involved in major infrastructure projects, including the Lekki-Ikoyi Link Bridge, before becoming deputy governor in 2019.
The governor said Hamzat’s experience across three successive administrations had equipped him with an understanding of the state’s governance structure and development priorities.
On the transition of power, Sanwo-Olu described a peaceful succession as one of the most important legacies an outgoing governor could leave behind.
“Lagos is going to change governors without a quarrel. In May, one governor will hand to another a state that is whole. There is no greater gift a governor can leave his people than a handover that does not break the house,” he said.
He urged Hamzat and his running mate, Princess Damilola Sonayon-James, to maintain close engagement with residents, complete ongoing infrastructure projects and sustain the state’s development framework.
Sanwo-Olu also called on APC members to mobilise support across the state’s wards, while urging residents to scrutinise the manifesto and make informed choices ahead of the 2027 elections.
Presenting his manifesto, Hamzat unveiled a seven-pillar development agenda, tagged PROMISE, which he said would guide his administration if elected.
The acronym represents People First, Renewal, Opportunity, Machinery of Government, Inclusion, Security and Resilience, and Everyday Dignity.
He said the agenda was designed to consolidate the achievements of successive APC administrations while addressing the challenges of a rapidly expanding megacity through inclusive growth, efficient service delivery and improved living standards.
Describing a promise as a responsibility, Hamzat said: “A promise is a debt. In Yoruba, we say: Gbese ni Ileri. A promise has weight.”
He identified respect, work and truth as the principles that would guide his proposed administration, adding that the manifesto contained specific commitments against which residents could assess his performance.
Hamzat said his understanding of governance was shaped by his upbringing, particularly his father’s involvement in the administration of former Governor Lateef Jakande, as well as his own experience in public service.
He recalled growing up in Mushin, where he witnessed challenges such as poor drainage and unreliable electricity, adding that the experiences had influenced his commitment to responsive governance.
On healthcare, the APC candidate promised to increase the number of Maternal and Child Centres from 10 to 15 and expand the Ilera Eko health insurance scheme to cover one in three Lagos residents, with priority given to low-income households.
He also pledged to build two new general hospitals in Ogombo and Ibeju-Lekki, upgrade 100 primary healthcare centres to flagship status and recruit more doctors, nurses and midwives to strengthen the state’s healthcare workforce.
Hamzat further highlighted ongoing hospital projects, including the 150-bed Massey Children’s Hospital, the 280-bed Ojo General Hospital and the 150-bed Somolu General Hospital.
In education, he promised to strengthen the EKOEXCEL programme, which operates in 1,028 public primary schools, and expand access to quality education from early childhood to university level.
He also proposed establishing a University of Medicine and Health Sciences to train more healthcare professionals and provide opportunities for them to develop their careers in Lagos.
The candidate pledged sustained investment in teacher development, noting that more than 33,000 teachers had been trained in the state over the past seven years.
He also promised to reactivate the proposed multi-billion-dollar Fourth Mainland Bridge project.
Hamzat said his manifesto built on the current administration’s THEMES Plus agenda and the Federal Government’s Renewed Hope Agenda, while outlining his proposed priorities for healthcare, education, economic development, infrastructure and social welfare.

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
The Chairman of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), Mr Ola Olukoyede, has described developments in Zamfara State under Governor Dauda Lawal as evidence of transformational leadership.
Olukoyede spoke on Thursday while delivering the keynote address at the 30th anniversary lecture of Zamfara State, held at the Grand Chamber of the Government House in Gusau.
He said he accepted the invitation to speak at the event after conducting personal checks on the governor and the state’s development trajectory, particularly over the past three years.
The EFCC chairman explained that his office’s ethical demands generally kept him away from political events and government houses, but that what he discovered about Zamfara persuaded him to attend.
“By virtue of the ethical demands of my office, I don’t attend political events; I don’t go to the government house as a matter of principle. But when I received this invitation, something told me to accept and see what was going on there,” he said.
Olukoyede said he had also discussed his findings with President Bola Tinubu, who encouraged him to attend the anniversary celebration.
He said his arrival in Gusau offered him an opportunity to observe some of the infrastructure projects and changes taking place in the state.
“As I arrived in Gusau, the first thing I noticed was the new airport. It is noticeable even to first-time visitors. The capital city speaks of visible transformation, as we have seen. Newly paved roads align with street solar lights,” he said.
According to him, Zamfara had for years remained among Nigeria’s less-developed states despite its natural potential and efforts by successive administrations.
He, however, said the state’s outlook was changing, adding that the physical development of Gusau reflected broader changes across Zamfara.
The EFCC chairman also commended the state government’s reported progress in education, particularly its performance in national examinations conducted by the National Examinations Council (NECO) and the West African Examinations Council (WAEC).
He attributed the developments to what he described as deliberate reform initiatives by the Lawal administration, noting that they aligned with the anniversary lecture’s theme, “Accountability and Responsibility in Transformational Government”.
Olukoyede said the decision to invite the EFCC chairman to address the state anniversary reflected the governor’s commitment to transparency and accountability.
In his remarks, Governor Lawal said the anniversary theme, “Reflections, Achievements, and the Future”, was designed to provide an opportunity to examine the challenges that had shaped the state’s journey and consider the responsibilities of leaders in securing a better future.
He said the anniversary lecture had provided a platform for intellectual engagement on critical issues, including public accountability, community participation in tackling insecurity, preservation of history and culture, and the relationship between security and socio-economic development.
Lawal said the discussions were central to his administration’s development agenda, particularly its Six-Point Rescue Agenda and the Zamfara State Development Plan 2025–2034.
According to him, the development plan provides a long-term framework for the state’s economic growth, infrastructure, social welfare, human capital development, governance and environmental sustainability.
“We must turn these commitments into measurable improvements in people’s lives,” the governor said.
He expressed appreciation to the speakers, discussants, organising committee and other participants for their contributions to the anniversary programme.
Other speakers at the anniversary lecture included Professors Tijjani Muhammad Bande, Sulaiman Kura, Murtala Rufai and Taofik Aminu.

items.author: Peter Moses
items.content:
Former President Olusegun Obasanjo on Friday warned against what he called blind adoption of economic instructions from foreign-trained experts without considering Nigeria’s realities.
Obasanjo spoke in Abeokuta, Ogun State, at the Ajibosin Platform, a public forum themed: “Leveraging Artificial Intelligence to solve grassroots problems and accelerate National Development.”
The former President expressed worry that Nigeria relies on young and unmarried boys and girls who have never managed a household for an economic advice.
He further criticised Nigeria’s dependence on foreign institutions, particularly the World Bank and International Monetary Fund (IMF), arguing that their policies were not necessarily designed to address the country’s peculiar circumstances.
He recalled how Nigeria was discouraged from subsidising agriculture despite what he described as the agricultural support available to farmers in developed countries.
“World Bank and IMF were not designed for us. They were not built by us. They were built before we became independent. And that’s the people who would determine what we do,” he said.
Speaking on the foreign-trained experts, Obasanjo said: “They are brilliant boys and girls, so they went to Ivy League universities, Oxford, Cambridge, and all that.
“These brilliant boys, then they put it, it’s good academically. And they tell us, and we take it, lock, stock and barrel, and we use it.”
He questioned why a country with a population of about 250 million people would depend on the recommendations of young experts who, according to him, might have little experience managing households or understanding the country’s complexities.
“For a country of 250 million people, it is boys and girls who are not even married, let alone manage a home, who will tell us how, what will we do to manage our country? And we swallow it. And we destroy ourselves,” he said.
On the role of Artificial Intelligence in Nigeria’s development, Obasanjo urged the country to approach the technology from the standpoint of its own interests rather than accepting everything presented by foreign powers.
He recalled the historical experiences of slave trade, colonialism, globalisation and structural adjustment programmes, arguing that initiatives introduced to Africa as opportunities had often come with disadvantages.
According to him, Nigeria must take ownership of artificial intelligence and deploy it to address pressing national challenges.
“Can AI help us? We have 24 million Nigerian children that should be in school that are not in school. And if you are looking for disasters of tomorrow, they are the disasters of tomorrow,” he said.
He also identified agriculture, food security, healthcare delivery and pharmaceutical production as areas where artificial intelligence could make significant contributions.
“Can AI help us to know the type of fruit, food that we should, crop that we should produce and produce them adequately, quantitatively, so that we can have food and nutrition security?” he asked.
In his address, the Guest speaker and Convener League of Northern Democrats, Dr Umar Ardo, warned that Artificial Intelligence could become Africa’s new form of extraction, describing unchecked data harvesting as “the slave ship, refitted as the server farm.”
Ardo said history shows Africa has moved from exporting human beings during the transatlantic slave trade, to raw materials under colonialism, and to crude commodities and skilled labour after independence, warning that data may become the fourth commodity.
He argued that Africa generates abundant data through its young population, languages, farms, hospitals and businesses, yet has almost zero hardware and model-building capacity, while its data is collected by platforms it does not own, stored outside its borders and monetized abroad.
“Too often, value flows outward, as it has for centuries. We are told this is ‘leveraging AI for development’. But plainly speaking, without safeguards, this is not leveraging. It is the slave ship, refitted as the server farm,” Ardo said.
The historian, however, said he was not dismissing AI, noting it can help agricultural extension workers detect crop diseases, support primary healthcare where doctors are scarce, improve land records and revenue collection, and help traditional institutions like Owu Kingdom preserve oral traditions and connect artisans to wider markets.
He called for a guarded embrace of AI, urging Nigeria to move beyond the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 to true data sovereignty, build local computing infrastructure, own African datasets, direct AI to grassroots governance, and work through the African Union’s Data Policy Framework to ensure Africa becomes an owner, not just a quarry, in the intelligence age.

“However, sustained pressure on foreign currency demand could limit further gains.”

items.author: Ayobami
items.content:
A record 47.9 million Americans have already voted in next week’s US midterm elections, with participation surging in key battleground states and registered Democrats outpacing Republicans, figures showed Friday.
The University of Florida’s Election Lab had recorded 47,922,669 early votes nationwide by midday, surpassing the previous midterm record of 45.9 million cast ahead of Election Day in 2022.
The surge is especially pronounced in states with fiercely contested Senate races that could determine control of the chamber during the final two years of President Donald Trump’s presidency.
In Texas, more than six million people had voted early by Wednesday, according to official figures, with in-person turnout running around 50 percent ahead of the same stage in 2022.
North Carolina’s election board reported early voting up nearly 37 percent on the same point four years ago, while South Carolina surpassed its entire 2022 early vote total on Monday, with five days of early voting still to go.
In Kansas, where Republican Senator Roger Marshall faces a tough re-election fight, advance ballots were running around two-thirds ahead of 2022 last week, according to the secretary of state’s office.
In states that record voters’ party affiliation, registered Democrats have accounted for a substantially larger share of early ballots than Republicans.
Election Lab figures showed Democrats making up around 44 percent of early voters in those states, compared with 31 percent for Republicans and 25 percent for unaffiliated or minor-party voters.
University of Florida political scientist Michael McDonald, who oversees the Election Lab, has pointed to rising participation among Black and Hispanic voters in states that report racial and ethnic data, with particularly strong turnout in heavily Hispanic communities along the Texas-Mexico border.
In Georgia, where early in-person voting broke the state’s midterm record on Thursday, women accounted for 56 percent of ballots cast by that day, compared with 44 percent for men.
“Georgians continue to head to the polls in record numbers because they trust the system,” top elections official Brad Raffensperger said Thursday.
But experts warn against interpreting the figures as a prediction of the election outcome.
A voter’s party registration does not reveal which candidates they supported, and tens of millions more Americans are expected to cast ballots on Tuesday.
In recent elections Republicans have tended to turn out in greater numbers on Election Day, potentially narrowing or reversing the Democrats’ early advantage.
And higher early participation does not necessarily translate into higher overall turnout, since some voters may simply be casting ballots sooner than in previous elections.

items.content:
The IT ministry (MeitY) has proposed a consent-based framework to facilitate data sharing for training AI models in India.
Called the Data Empowerment and Protection Architecture (DEPA) for AI training, the framework aims to help startups, businesses and academic institutions access large-scale, India-specific datasets to develop AI models while protecting citizens’ privacy and ensuring compliance with the DPDP Act.
The DEPA for AI training also proposes a techno-legal architecture to enable organisations to collaborate on AI model training without directly transferring underlying datasets.
With this, the ministry aims to foster access to datasets for researchers and businesses looking to train AI models. The guidelines have been formulated in collaboration with think tank iSPIRT.
Explaining The New Proposed Framework
The proposed architecture builds on India’s existing DEPA framework, which already supports consent-based data sharing through initiatives such as Account Aggregator. The new framework encompasses the following technical pillars:
Confidential Clean Rooms: Secure computing environments where organisations can collaborate on data processing and AI model training without exposing the underlying datasets to one another
Differential Privacy: A privacy-preserving technique used to ensure that individual-level information cannot be identified or extracted from an aggregate dataset
Electronic Contracts: Machine-readable agreements that define and enforce data-sharing conditions, including permitted uses, data protection and security requirements
Zero-Trust Security: An approach where every access request is authenticated and authorised, with encryption, continuous monitoring and auditing to protect data
The proposed framework also defines key stakeholders for enabling safe sharing of data for training AI models:
Training Data Providers (TDPs): Organisations that make their data accessible through the framework. For instance: banks, hospitals, government agencies
Training Data Consumers (TDCs): Startups, enterprises, researchers and individuals seeking access to datasets to train AI models
Data Collectives or Data Collabs: Intermediaries that aggregate, standardise, and organise data from various sources and define data-sharing policies and governance rules for participants
Under the DEPA framework, TDPs would first register their datasets on a data exchange platform after anonymising and encrypting them. The datasets would then be tagged with metadata and cryptographic identifiers for traceability.
TDCs can then request a dataset for their specific use cases, and an electronic contract system checks their requests against data-sharing policies and governance rules before granting access.
Once access is given, the model is then trained within a secure data environment using differential privacy methods, ensuring that the raw data remains inaccessible to consumers.
The framework also proposes that trained models must undergo independent checks for bias, fairness, security, safety and explainability. Only models that pass receive approval for pilot deployment and scaling.
Even after deployment, the oversight will continue in the interest of long-term trust and accountability. In line with this, the framework will ensure that TDCs remain subject to continuous monitoring, periodic reviews, and traceability of the model’s outputs back to the data and contracts used in its training.
Govt’s Focus On AI Governance
The launch of the new DEPA framework for AI training comes soon after TRAI also released draft guidelines on the responsible use of AI in telecom networks and service delivery. The telecom regulator has sought inputs from stakeholders by November 27.
As per TRAI, its draft guidelines are rooted in the IndiaAI Governance Guidelines. The centre had earlier released these guidelines to focus on fostering innovation and safe development and deployment of AI offerings, while mitigating risks posed by the technology.
A few weeks ago, union IT minister Ashwini Vaishnaw had also said that the centre will release a consultation paper for regulation on AI safety and security within a month. Earlier reports had also hinted that the Centre was looking at formulating a new framework for AI regulation.

items.content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye
The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) has warned that the Ebola outbreak spreading across parts of Africa remains uncontrolled, with more than 10,200 confirmed cases and over 5,000 deaths recorded across the continent.
The Director-General of Africa CDC, Jean Kaseya, gave the warning on Friday during an interview on Channels Television’s Morning Brief programme, raising concerns about the continued transmission and changing geographical spread of the disease.
Kaseya said the assessment followed a virtual ministerial meeting held on October 28, which brought together more than 42 ministers and over 600 participants, including representatives of international organisations and development partners, to review the outbreak and ongoing response efforts.
“We analysed the data and we saw that the outbreak is not yet under control,” he said.
He disclosed that the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) had recorded more than 10,000 confirmed infections, while the combined number of confirmed cases across the continent had exceeded 10,200.
“We have achieved what is a number of 10,000 people confirmed cases in DRC and also, if we put together, it’s more than 10,200 confirmed cases across the continent,” Kaseya said.
Kaseya said more than 5,000 people had died from the outbreak, although figures published by health authorities showed a slightly lower confirmed death toll.
“We also saw that we have more than 5,000 people already passed on due to this outbreak,” he added.
Kaseya also expressed concern over changes in the geographical spread of the disease, noting that its epicentre was shifting.
The current outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus and has affected several African countries, including the DRC, Kenya and Nigeria.
The DRC remains the worst-affected country, accounting for the overwhelming majority of infections and deaths. Data from the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control showed that the country had recorded 10,193 confirmed cases and 4,960 related deaths as of October 28.
Kenya has also reported nine confirmed cases, including two deaths, following an imported infection linked to the DRC.
Nigeria confirmed its first Ebola case in more than a decade on October 20, after a 42-year-old Swiss woman tested positive for the Bundibugyo strain in Abuja.
The woman, who had travelled from Uganda to Nigeria, was isolated and treated by Nigerian health workers before being medically evacuated to Switzerland on October 26 for further treatment after her condition stabilised. Her husband, who was identified as a close contact, was also evacuated.
Following their evacuation, the World Health Organisation (WHO) Regional Director for Africa, Mohamed Janabi, said Nigeria had no confirmed Ebola cases.
However, the WHO clarified that the development did not mean Nigeria had been declared Ebola-free, explaining that health authorities were still monitoring people who had contact with the patient.
The organisation said Nigeria must complete the required 42-day monitoring period before an official Ebola-free declaration could be made.
In its October 29 situation report, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control (NCDC) said 62 contacts linked to the index case had been identified and were being monitored.
The agency added that no new contacts or symptomatic contacts had been identified in the preceding 24 hours.
The continued spread of the disease has heightened concerns about cross-border transmission and the capacity of African countries to contain infectious diseases amid increased movement of people across the continent.

The warning highlighted how the shift towards AI powered search is disrupting the traditional flow of visitors to websites that have long depended on Google for audience reach, Reuters reported.Reddit stock plunged 29.45% to $91.51, having hit a low of $89.28 earlier in the day.Reddit said its total daily active unique visitors could decline by a low double digit percentage in the fourth quarter from around 130 million if referral traffic continues to weaken. The warning added to pressure on the stock, which had already fallen about 44% this year through Thursday's close.For live updates on US Markets, click hereGoogle's AI search shift puts Reddit traffic at riskThe growing use of AI Overviews and AI Mode in Google Search is changing how users discover information online, potentially reducing the need to visit individual websites for answers.JPMorgan analysts said Google's expansion of AI powered search features, alongside changes to the ranking of machine translated content, had contributed to the decline in search traffic.Also Read: Intel stock plunges 30% as weak PC demand and AI costs trigger global chip selloffPiper Sandler analysts said a reset in expectations was appropriate, adding that the near term outlook was increasingly clouded.Despite the traffic concerns, Reddit disclosed that it had extended its cloud services agreements with Amazon Web Services and Google through 2029. Under the agreements, the company has committed to spending $880 million and $580 million, respectively, over three years, according to a regulatory filing cited by Reuters.Pinterest also falls on weak revenue outlookReddit was not alone in facing investor concerns. Pinterest shares declined 7.86% to $18.16 after the company issued a weaker than expected fourth quarter revenue forecast, Reuters reported.The image sharing platform reported third quarter revenue of $1.17 billion, missing analysts' estimates of $1.21 billion, according to LSEG data. Its fourth quarter revenue guidance of $1.425 billion to $1.475 billion also fell short of Wall Street expectations.RBC analysts said changes to the European Union's de minimis exemption affected cross border sellers sooner and more severely than expected, leaving Pinterest's European revenue flat.Pinterest shares had fallen about 23% this year through Thursday. If premarket losses held, Reddit stood to lose $5.7 billion in market value, while Pinterest faced a decline of more than $800 million, according to Reuters.

items.content:
Former President Olusegun Obasanjo has criticised President Bola Tinubu over his comment that borrowing is not leprosy, describing the position as “absolute nonsense”.
Obasanjo spoke on Friday in Abeokuta, Ogun State, at the Ajibosin Platform, a public forum theme “Leveraging Artificial Intelligence to solve grassroots problems and accelerate National Development.”
In April, Tinubu said his administration would continue to borrow whenever necessary, insisting that it should not be viewed negatively.
Tinubu spoke at the State House during a meeting with Plateau leaders led by Caleb Mutfwang, the governor, and Nentawe Yilwatda, national chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC).
Kidnapping: I&#8217;ll go into the bush to Rescue Victims if Elected – Peter Obi
Obi: Tinubu has borrowed nearly $100bn with nothing to show
“If we have to borrow, we borrow. Borrowing is not leprosy, we just have to work hard to be able to pay for it,” the president had said.
His remarks came amid rising public concern over Nigeria’s growing debt burden and the increasing share of national revenue committed to debt servicing.
Reacting to Tinubu’s comment, Obasanjo hit him hard, maintaining that leprosy can only destroy one person at a time while debt destroys generations.
The former president said: “And for anybody to say debt is no leprosy, is absolute nonsense. Debt is worse than leprosy. Because leprosy destroys only one person. Debt destroys generations.”
Obasanjo questioned Nigeria’s economic management, recalling that when he started his farm 47 years ago, the naira exchanged at N1 to $1.85.
“When I started my farm, 47 years ago, naira to the dollar was one naira to $1.85. Forty-seven years ago. What has Nigeria done in 47 years that we now have 1,500 naira to the dollar? What have we done?” he asked.
He also questioned the capacity of the country’s political leadership to make decisions that would improve the lives of Nigerians.
“What do our leaders know? And what do they not know? And from what they know, what can they do for us?” he asked.
The former president further criticised Nigeria’s dependence on foreign institutions, particularly the World Bank and International Monetary Fund (IMF), arguing that their policies were not necessarily designed to address the country’s peculiar circumstances.
He recalled how Nigeria was discouraged from subsidising agriculture despite what he described as the agricultural support available to farmers in developed countries.
“World Bank and IMF were not designed for us. They were not built by us. They were built before we became independent. And that’s the people who would determine what we do,” he said.
Obasanjo also warned against blindly adopting economic prescriptions from foreign-trained experts without considering Nigeria’s realities.

items.author: Press Release
items.content:
Chief Minister of Punjab Maryam Nawaz Sharif officially launched the Punjab Innovation, Value Addition and Economic Transformation (PIVOT) Plan 2026–29, a comprehensive Rs1,995.3 billion economic strategy aimed at positioning Punjab as an export-led industrial hub. The roadmap targets $6.8 billion in incremental exports, 162,000 new direct jobs and support for over one million livelihoods.
Speaking at the launch, Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif said: “Punjab is ready to move towards a new model of economic growth—one driven by industry, innovation, value addition and exports. Our objective is to create an environment where businesses can invest with confidence, industries can expand and our people can access better employment and livelihood opportunities.”
The unveiling brought together an unprecedented gathering of leading corporate figures, economic policymakers, international development agencies and diplomats invited by Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz. Prominent business icons including Mian Mansha, Arif Habib, Fawad Mukhtar, Ziad Bashir and Osman Khalid Waheed attended the launch, signalling private-sector engagement with the initiative.
Financial sector leadership was represented by State Bank of Pakistan Governor Jameel Ahmad, alongside heads and senior executives of major commercial banks and financial institutions. International participation included foreign ambassadors, members of the diplomatic corps and representatives of key international development partners, including the World Bank, the Asian Development Bank (ADB) and United Nations organisations.
Senior government figures, led by Senior Minister Marriyum Aurangzeb and Chief Secretary Zahid Akhtar Zaman, provincial cabinet ministers, administrative secretaries and district focal officers, were also present to outline the government’s operational commitments.
Addressing the business community, the Chief Minister said:“My message to investors and industrialists across Pakistan and around the world is clear: Punjab welcomes your investment. We want to work with you, facilitate your businesses and create the conditions in which enterprise can grow. Government will facilitate, industry will lead.”
A primary pillar of the PIVOT framework is the Strategic Trade Enhancement Programme (STEP), supported by a newly introduced digital portal. Under this mechanism, the government envisages Rs300 billion in concessional financing at rates ranging between zero and five per cent for eligible commercial categories, giving businesses access to lower-cost capital for expansion, subject to programme terms and conditions.
This financing structure forms part of an overall investment framework combining Rs1,089 billion in public investment with a target of Rs906 billion in private-sector investment.
The Chief Minister said:“We are not looking at economic growth as a government-only responsibility. Sustainable growth requires private investment, a strong industrial base and a partnership in which the public sector enables the private sector to innovate, produce and compete. PIVOT is designed to turn that partnership into measurable economic progress.”
The plan directs Rs753.7 billion towards strengthening industrial output, encouraging value addition and building long-term export competitiveness.
To address operational costs and energy challenges, the government has earmarked Rs50 billion for solar power installations and Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS). An additional Rs50 billion has been allocated for machinery duty reimbursements to incentivise manufacturers to upgrade factories, adopt advanced technology and meet international quality standards.
The programme focuses on key manufacturing value chains, including garments and textiles, sports goods, leather and footwear, surgical instruments, pharmaceuticals, fans, cutlery, steel and ceramics. Modern testing laboratories, certification facilities and plug-and-play industrial infrastructure are also envisaged to help businesses meet international compliance requirements and access export markets.
The Chief Minister said: “Our industries must not be limited to producing more; they must produce better, add greater value and compete in international markets. We want Punjab’s manufacturers to have access to modern technology, reliable energy solutions, quality infrastructure and the financing they need to expand their businesses and exports.”
AGRICULTURE AND AGRO-PROCESSING: MOVING UP THE VALUE CHAIN
To move agriculture beyond raw commodity production towards higher-value processing, PIVOT includes four specialised agro-processing parks in Sargodha, Khanewal, Okara and Bhakkar.
These facilities are designed to reduce post-harvest losses, modernise food-processing infrastructure and integrate agricultural producers into higher-value supply chains.
Agricultural value-chain interventions include wheat value enhancement and improved quality and market access for citrus, potato and mango crops, alongside targeted export financing for horticulture and floriculture. The programme also envisages dedicated Horticulture Authorities in 20 districts.
The initiative further supports commercial expansion across livestock, dairy, aquaculture, halal meat and milk value chains, with the objective of improving productivity and developing export opportunities.
TOURISM, TECHNOLOGY AND SKILLS DEVELOPMENT
Beyond industrial and agricultural manufacturing, the plan extends to tourism, digital services and workforce development.
Tourism infrastructure will be upgraded to develop destination-economy opportunities, improve facilities for visitors and encourage private-sector investment in hospitality and related services.
To address the gap between vocational education and workplace requirements, the programme envisages training 402,060 individuals over three years. The focus will be on industry-aligned, demand-driven skills required by modern manufacturing, emerging commercial sectors and technology-oriented enterprises.
The Chief Minister said: “Our young people must be prepared for the jobs of tomorrow. Skills development must respond to the actual needs of industry and the changing demands of the economy. We want training to lead to employment, entrepreneurship and better livelihoods.”
BUSINESS REFORMS AND DIGITAL INVESTOR FACILITATION
To improve the business environment, PIVOT introduces regulatory and administrative reforms aimed at simplifying commercial operations and attracting long-term investment.
Through the E-Biz digital initiative, the provincial government aims to digitise 300 public administrative services to make business processes more accessible and transparent. The programme also envisages bringing 2,000 firms onto e-commerce platforms, alongside modernised labour laws, public-private partnership reforms and approved schemes for state land leases across nine productive economic sectors.
The Chief Minister said: “Investors should spend their time building businesses, creating jobs and expanding production—not navigating unnecessary administrative hurdles. We are working to make government services simpler, more accessible and more transparent.”
TRACKED, TRACEABLE AND ACCOUNTABLE IMPLEMENTATION
Execution and accountability are embedded through a central governance model led by a PIVOT Board chaired by Senior Minister Marriyum Aurangzeb on behalf of the Chief Minister.
Operational coordination will be handled by a dedicated PIVOT Secretariat in the Planning and Development Department, alongside a PIVOT cell within the Chief Secretary’s Office. Deputy Commissioners will serve as district-level focal persons.
Implementation will be monitored through a central PIVOT Dashboard and an Industry Scorecard, with defined milestones, measurable performance indicators and regular reviews to track progress, identify bottlenecks and strengthen departmental accountability.
Chief Secretary Zahid Akhtar Zaman outlined the implementation arrangements and confirmed that the concept would be operationalised within six months.
The Chief Minister said:“PIVOT will not remain a document of targets and commitments. Its implementation will be tracked, its progress measured and its results assessed. Every initiative must translate into real investment, stronger businesses, more exports and better opportunities for the people of Punjab.”
PRIVATE-SECTOR CONFIDENCE AND INVESTMENT MOMENTUM
Senior Minister Marriyum Aurangzeb emphasised that the Chief Minister’s vision for PIVOT was to position government as an enabler and facilitator of enterprise, allowing the private sector to drive economic expansion.
Demonstrating private-sector investment interest at the launch, real estate developer Arif Habib announced plans to construct Pakistan’s tallest commercial tower at Lahore CBD One, highlighting investment activity associated with Punjab’s development agenda.
PIVOT sets out a three-year framework to translate Punjab’s economic potential into investment, stronger industrial capacity, higher exports, improved skills and employment.
The Chief Minister concluded: “Our ambition is to build a Punjab where businesses can grow, industries can compete globally, our farmers can earn more from their produce and our young people can find meaningful opportunities. We are opening the doors to investment and partnership. Together, we can turn Punjab’s economic potential into prosperity.”

items.content:
Your phone can be infected with spyware simply by loading an online advertisement, without you clicking anything, the National Cyber Emergency Response Team (National CERT) has warned.
In its latest advisory, National CERT said attackers are exploiting online advertising networks to target mobile devices. Users do not need to click a suspicious link, open an attachment, or take any action for the attack to work.
What Is AdFection
The advisory mentioned a technique known as “AdFection.” It lets attackers misuse digital advertising systems to profile users and deliver mercenary spyware through ads shown on websites and mobile apps.
The warning is based on research published by Citizen Lab on October 15, 2026. The same research found that Pakistan was among the most targeted countries in the ad-based spyware campaign.
According to the advisory, Citizen Lab documented a high-confidence finding that devices at Al Jazeera were targeted and infected with Candiru spyware using this method.
The attack may involve delivering malicious code through ads, picking out selected devices, and exploiting flaws in browsers, apps, or operating systems to gain access.
However, National CERT clarified that simply seeing an advertisement does not confirm that a device has been targeted or compromised.
What Is at Risk
National CERT warned that a successful infection could expose private communications, photos, files, account passwords, and other sensitive data.
It also flagged risks of unauthorized surveillance, device takeover, and leaks of government, corporate, research, and media-related information. The actual damage depends on the flaws exploited, the device’s software version, and the spyware’s capabilities.
How to Stay Safe
National CERT advised users to:
Keep operating systems, browsers, and apps updated
Use devices that still receive regular security updates
Install apps only from trusted sources
Turn on multi-factor authentication for important accounts
Organizations were advised to consider ad-blocking and browser-level protections, preserve security logs, strengthen device monitoring, and seek specialist digital forensics help in suspected cases.
The agency, which recently warned staff about another security risk, said credible signs of spyware activity or targeted cyber incidents can be reported through its official incident-reporting mechanism.
