items.author: Palak Sharma
items.content:
The Indian gaming industry has been forced to rethink its growth strategy after the government banned real money gaming (RMG) in 2025, a major revenue stream for the industry till then.
In trying to regain footing, many gaming startups are aggressively doubling down on adjacent businesses — esports, tournaments and brand-led gaming. Let’s Game Now also wants to tap this opportunity by building a franchise-based gaming league that brings together competitive gaming, sports and entertainment.
To fuel this ambition, the Bengaluru-based gaming and esports company has raised ₹30 Cr in an investment round led by industrialist Anand Mahindra, Bestvantage Investments and an undisclosed UAE-based family office
The funding will be used to accelerate the development of the Indian Super Gaming League (ISGL), the company’s proposed gaming and entertainment property.
Founded in 2018 by Santanu Basu, Let’s Game Now is an Indian esports platform that connects brands with gamers. The startup also provides live broadcasting services across South Asia and Southeast Asia and organises online competitions and offline events.
The gaming platform claims to have so far organised more than 2,000 events and serves over 30 clients. It also has a presence in 18 countries and claims to have a total reach of over 50 Mn viewers.
Building A Franchise-Based Gaming League
The Indian Super Gaming League sits at the centre of Let’s Game Now’s expansion plans. The startup aims to bring competitive gaming, sports, entertainment and technology together through a franchise-based format.
The model offers an opportunity to build a recurring gaming property around teams, players and fans, rather than relying solely on individual tournaments and brand-led events.
Mahindra’s backing brings experience from the sports and business ecosystem, including associations with properties such as the Pro Kabaddi League and Chess League.
However, the commercial viability of ISGL will depend on its ability to attract franchise owners, sponsors, broadcasting partners and a consistent audience. The startup has not disclosed the league’s launch timeline, franchise structure, expected revenue or monetisation strategy.
Let’s Game Now’s Commercial Bet
India’s gaming market is valued at nearly $3.8 Bn and is projected to reach $9.2 Bn by FY29. The country is home to an estimated 59.1 Cr gamers.
For Let’s Game Now, the opportunity lies in converting this audience into a commercially viable ecosystem for teams, sponsors, broadcasters and other partners.
The startup claims it has built a community of over 14 Lakh members and a grassroots network spanning more than 400 colleges across 80 cities. Its reach also includes over 7 Lakh students, supported by 20+ events and 30+ college club partnerships.
This network could help the startup acquire participants and audiences for ISGL. Its existing relationships with brands and experience in organising tournaments may also provide a starting point for building commercial partnerships.
However, the startup will need to demonstrate repeat viewership, sponsor demand and a format that can sustain interest across seasons. Its next phase will hinge on three factors:
Franchise and sponsorship demand: Whether the league can attract teams, franchise owners and brands willing to commit capital over multiple seasons.
Audience monetisation: Whether its existing gaming community can translate into consistent viewership and revenue from sponsorships, media rights and other commercial partnerships.
League economics: Whether the revenue generated can cover the costs of organising competitions, running broadcasts, acquiring audiences and maintaining franchise participation.
The ₹30 Cr investment provides capital to advance the league, but Let’s Game Now has not disclosed how much of the funding will go towards league operations, marketing, technology or other business functions.
Inc42 Take: Can Let’s Game Now Build A Scalable Esports Business?
Let’s Game Now is looking to build on India’s large gaming audience by creating a franchise-based property rather than relying only on individual tournaments and events.
Its existing community, grassroots network and investor backing offer a starting point. However, these are not proof of a sustainable esports business. The key question is whether ISGL can generate recurring commercial demand from the stakeholders while retaining audiences across seasons.
Economics will also matter. League operations, production, marketing and franchise development can require significant spending, while revenue depends on the ability to secure and retain commercial partners.
The real test will be whether it can turn its gaming community into a repeatable commercial property, with consistent viewership and revenue beyond the initial investment.

The 29-year-old German was already assured of finishing the season top of the ATP rankings but, in the absence of current incumbent Jannik Sinner, two-time Grand Slam champion Zverev will now take that crown in next week’s updated standings after winning his opening two matches in the Austrian capital.

items.content:
Alexander Zverev accelerated his ascension to number one in the world rankings for the first time in his career on Thursday as he beat Tallon Griekspoor 6-4, 7-5 to reach the quarter-finals of the Vienna Open.
The 29-year-old German was already assured of finishing the season top of the ATP rankings but, in the absence of current incumbent Jannik Sinner, two-time Grand Slam champion Zverev will now take that crown in next week’s updated standings after winning his opening two matches in the Austrian capital.
Long seen as tennis’ nearly-man, Zverev has enjoyed a stellar 2026, breaking his major duck by picking up the titles at the French and US Opens.
Now he has broken further ground by becoming only the 30th man to claim top spot since the rankings were first published in 1973.
He will be aged 29 years and 196 days when Monday’s new rankings are published, making him the second-oldest first-time number one after Australian John Newcombe.
Due to a knee injury Italy’s Sinner decided to end his season at the start of October, opening the way for Zverev to dethrone him.
And the big-serving Hamburg native ensured he did just that ahead of the season-ending ATP Finals next month by seeing off Martin Landaluce and Griekspoor in his opening two matches in Vienna.
Zverev needed to save four match points against Spain’s Landaluce in his first-round match on Tuesday, but was much more comfortable as he defeated Griekspoor in straight sets to write his name into the history books.
He raced out of the blocks on Thursday, breaking the 30-year-old Dutchman in the very first game and then confidently serving his way into a one-set lead.
The second frame went to 5-5 before Zverev pounced on Griekspoor’s serve to get his nose in front.
The match met an unexpected stoppage as Zverev brought up match point when a smash off the German’s racquet caused part of the electronic board behind Griekspoor to malfunction.
But once the umpire covered the problematic panel up with a towel, Zverev then sealed his new ranking with an unreturnable serve.

“On the succession process for the revered Awujale stool, Abiodun assured the people that his administration was committed to facilitating a smooth, peaceful and widely acceptable process leading to the emergence of a new monarch,” the statement said.
The governor acknowledged the significance of the Awujale institution to the cultural heritage, identity and unity of Ijebuland, urging residents to remain calm and patient while the necessary procedures were being concluded.
He added that his administration was giving the matter the attention it deserved to ensure that the process was completed peacefully and that the eventual emergence of a new monarch enjoyed the acceptance and support of the people.
The Awujale stool became vacant in July 2025 following the death of Oba Adetona, who ruled for 65 years and was widely regarded as one of Nigeria’s longest-reigning traditional rulers.
The Ogun State Government halted the succession process in January 2026, citing petitions from security agencies and other stakeholders. The suspension followed an earlier halt in December 2025 over procedural concerns.
A total of 95 aspirants—94 princes and one princess—reportedly emerged from the Fusengbuwa ruling house nomination exercise held in Ijebu-Ode in December 2025 before the government suspended further proceedings.

items.content:
By Efosa Taiwo
Stablecoins could transform cross-border payments by reducing transaction delays, improving liquidity and making money transfers faster and more accessible, speakers at Moonshot 2026 have said.
The speakers made the remarks during a panel session titled “The New Payment Backbone: Stablecoins as Core Infrastructure for Global Liquidity” on the Emerging Tech Stage, where industry leaders discussed how stablecoins could reshape payments across Africa and the global financial system.
Mercy Emmanuel, Stablecoin & Blockchain Vertical Lead, Flutterwave, said stablecoins could simplify international transfers, which often involve multiple intermediaries and take several days to complete.
“Sending money from Lagos to Nairobi goes through a lot. It could take two to five days before it gets to its destination. Stablecoins collapse all these,” Emmanuel said.
She likened the technology to a moving train that operates without the restrictions of banking hours and time zones, arguing that it could make payments almost instantaneous and allow businesses to conduct transactions seamlessly alongside their online operations.
According to her, stablecoins could also encourage businesses to rethink their payment processes and build more efficient financial operations.
“Stablecoins are here to optimise the financial system, not displace the traditional way,” she said, adding that the financial industry was moving towards a system in which the focus would be on how quickly and efficiently money could move from one point to another.
Tayo Oviosu, Group Chief Executive Officer of Paga, said widespread stablecoin adoption would require collaboration among financial technology companies, sufficient liquidity and simpler access for everyday users.
He argued that consumers were more concerned about the cost and speed of financial services than the underlying technology powering their transactions.
“Ultimately, it is giving them what they want: they want to go from fiat to fiat. Stablecoin can be used in between,” he said.
Oviosu added that solving liquidity challenges would make stablecoin transactions easier to access and use, stressing that no single company could independently make the technology a mainstream part of everyday financial life.
“We want to make it simple. The way you can come to Paga and get a naira wallet, get a stablecoin wallet. That is the part of the user,” he said.
He also called for industry players to work together to expand the use of stablecoins, noting that stronger collaboration would be necessary to improve access to the infrastructure and liquidity required to support wider adoption.
Ife Johnson, co-founder of JuicyWay, also emphasised the need for shared infrastructure, urging industry players to move away from isolated systems towards solutions that could support the wider financial ecosystem.
“The mind shift that needs to happen is moving from silos to shared infrastructure for industry players,” Johnson said.
On regulation, Johnson said collaboration between businesses and regulators would be critical to ensuring the technology could develop responsibly.
He noted that adoption could take time because of the broader implications of introducing new payment systems into existing financial structures.
He expressed confidence that demonstrating responsible implementation and addressing potential concerns would help build
regulatory trust and encourage progress.
Oviosu also pointed to changing conversations around stablecoins and digital payments in Nigeria, saying engagement between industry stakeholders and regulators had become increasingly encouraging.
“Three, four years ago, who could have said CBN will support stablecoins, NCC welcomes the idea? It is interesting to see that dialogue,” he said.
He added that Nigeria could help set an example for other African markets if stakeholders maintained constructive engagement and worked together to address the challenges surrounding adoption.
Emmanuel similarly welcomed what she described as growing support from the Federal Government, saying cooperation among industry participants and policymakers would be important to the development of the ecosystem.
Vanguard News

By Efosa Taiwo
Juliet Ehimuan, founder of Beyond Limits and former Director of Google West Africa, has urged African creatives and technology entrepreneurs to move beyond content creation to building sustainable businesses that own intellectual property and capture value from their work.
Ehimuan made the call while speaking on artificial intelligence (AI) and the future of African creativity at Moonshot 2026 during a keynote speech on Thursday.
She said Africa’s creative economy remained underdeveloped, stressing the need to turn the continent’s creative talent into commercially viable enterprises capable of generating greater economic value.
“Our creative economy is still less than 2% of GDP,” she said, highlighting the need for a shift from producing content to building businesses around it.
According to her, African creators must focus on owning the intellectual property behind their work and exploring different ways to commercialise it.
“We need to move from content creation to value capture. We need to move from having creative talents to building enterprises. We should move from content creation to IP,” Ehimuan said.
She explained that intellectual property ownership could open up multiple revenue streams, noting that a book could be adapted into a series, while a podcast could generate additional commercial opportunities.
“There are so many ways to monetise content if you have the IP for that,” she said, emphasising the importance of owning intellectual property and the infrastructure needed to distribute and commercialise creative products.
Ehimuan outlined three priorities for Africa’s creative and technology sectors: adopting and developing AI capabilities, building and owning valuable assets, and establishing businesses capable of reaching wider markets.
On AI adoption, she encouraged African businesses to develop their capabilities and stay ahead of technological changes, noting that the technology could improve productivity and create new opportunities across industries.
She also urged creators and businesses to protect their rights and permissions while developing distinctive intellectual property that could be commercialised over time.

items.author: Oboh
items.content:
One in four stroke cases in Nigeria affects people below 50, raising concerns about the disease’s growing burden among young adults.
Prof. Kolawole Wahab, Head of the Stroke Unit at the University of Ilorin Teaching Hospital (UITH), disclosed this on Thursday in Ilorin.
He spoke on the sidelines of a medical rally commemorating the 2026 World Stroke Day, with the theme ‘Every Minute Counts’, which highlights the importance of prompt treatment.
Wahab said research published in 2017 had documented the prevalence of stroke among younger Nigerians.
“When we talk about stroke in the young, we are talking about those who are below the age of 50.
“One out of every four cases of stroke in Nigeria could be a case of stroke in the young. The prevalence is as high as 25 per cent.
“We see people who are in their 40s, some in their 30s, coming down with stroke,” he said.
The neurologist described the stroke burden in the region as epidemic, adding that UITH’s emergency department receives one or two stroke patients daily.
He identified hypertension as Nigeria’s leading stroke risk factor, warning that poor blood pressure control could increase the likelihood of the condition.
According to him, up to nine out of every 10 stroke cases have hypertension as an underlying factor.
Wahab expressed concern that some patients abandon prescribed medication in favour of unproven remedies, leaving their blood pressure uncontrolled.
He also identified diabetes as another major risk factor, noting that some people remain unaware they have the condition.
Others, he said, neglect proper diabetes management in spite of knowing their status.
“It is until they have suffered from stroke that they become aware they have diabetes,” he said.
Wahab listed imbalances in blood fats among other risk factors, explaining that abnormal levels of good and bad fats could contribute to stroke.
He warned against smoking, excessive alcohol consumption, hard drugs and sedentary lifestyles, urging Nigerians to adopt healthier habits.
The expert also advised people to moderate their salt intake, particularly those diagnosed with hypertension.
He cautioned against adding table salt to meals after preparation, stressing the importance of controlling blood pressure.
Also speaking, Dr Wemimo Olaofin, a consultant neurologist at UITH, urged Nigerians to check their blood pressure regularly.
Olaofin said stroke could occur suddenly at any time, but preventive measures and proper health management could reduce the risk.
He encouraged the public to monitor their blood pressure and embrace healthier lifestyles to prevent the condition.
Mrs Tejumola Olayinka, Deputy Director of Nursing in charge of UITH’s Stroke Care Unit, said the commemoration aimed to promote awareness and early hospital presentation.
“Stroke case is an emergency case that requires timely intervention. We can reduce the number of mortality and also reduce the number of people with stroke,” she said.
Olayinka described stroke as a sudden occurrence, “like a slap”, and highlighted facial drooping, arm weakness and slurred speech as warning signs.
She urged people displaying these symptoms to be rushed to hospital immediately for medical attention.
The nursing director also warned stroke patients against failing to take prescribed medication, noting that some patients did not adhere to treatment in spite of knowing their condition.
As part of the commemoration, UITH organised an awareness rally across the hospital and medical outreach programmes at the teaching hospital and Kwara Government House.
Two beneficiaries, Mr Jimoh Abdullateef and Mrs Fatima Abdulazeez, commended the medical team for providing free medical services and distributing drugs.
Vanguard News

items.content:
The Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (OGRA) will use artificial intelligence and analytics tools to monitor Pakistan’s petroleum products supply chain, after Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif directed the regulator to introduce the system in partnership with Alibaba Group.
The directive came during a meeting in Islamabad on Wednesday that reviewed progress on the use of AI and digitalisation in the economy and governance, as well as the government’s cooperation with Alibaba Group.
According to the Prime Minister’s Office, OGRA is being provided with AI and business intelligence tools to analyse fuel supply chain data.
What the System Will Do
The government has not yet shared technical details or an implementation date for the system. However, the analytics tools are meant to help the regulator study supply chain data and improve oversight of how petroleum products move from ports and refineries to petrol pumps.
The prime minister directed relevant ministries to complete all necessary measures for the Alibaba-backed projects by November and submit a progress report. He said all projects under the partnership should have clear targets, timelines and effective monitoring to deliver tangible results.
Builds on OGRA’s Existing Digital Monitoring
OGRA already runs several digital monitoring tools.
In July 2026, the regulator briefed the prime minister that a National Monitoring Dashboard, a Tanker Track and Trace system, depot tank telemetry, the Rahguzar mobile app, a digital sales entry system at petrol pumps and a Central Monitoring Cell were active to track petroleum stocks, movement and sales.
The regulator also said a data-driven enforcement campaign in July 2026 had identified multiple cases of hoarding and unnecessary supply disruptions, leading to show-cause notices and legal action. The authority had earlier launched a nationwide track and trace system to digitise Pakistan’s oil supply chain.
Other AI Projects With Alibaba
The OGRA system is part of a wider set of projects under the government’s strategic partnership with Alibaba Group.
The prime minister also directed the early implementation of an AI-assisted cancer diagnosis system and the launch of a 15-day AI training program for IT graduates under the Ministry of IT’s Ignite program.
The meeting was told that work is under way on AI-based models for agriculture, track and trace technology for tobacco, and digital platforms to support exports of citrus fruits and olives.
Digital and AI initiatives in higher education, railways, postal services and urban management are also nearing completion.
“The secret to Pakistan’s development lies in artificial intelligence and digitalisation,” the prime minister said, according to the PMO. Earlier this month, Pakistan also sought World Bank financing for a national AI program.

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
Human rights lawyer, Femi Falana, SAN, has called for the recovery of more than $123 billion and N66.4 billion allegedly owed to the Federation Account by the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL) and other oil and gas companies.
Falana, in a letter dated October 28, 2026, addressed to the Senate President and copied to the Speaker of the House of Representatives, urged the authorities to initiate measures to recover the funds, which he said comprised outstanding oil royalties, proceeds of alleged crude oil theft, unpaid dividends, taxes and other revenues.
The senior lawyer warned that failure to initiate recovery measures within 14 days of receiving the letter would prompt his firm to institute legal proceedings at the Federal High Court to compel the relevant authorities to act.
The letter, signed by Falana, outlined five categories of alleged outstanding funds and cited court judgments, government reports and legislative investigations in support of the demand.
On royalties, Falana said an estimated $62 billion had remained uncollected from international oil companies over 18 years following the non-implementation of provisions of the Deep Offshore and Inland Basin Production Sharing Contracts Act.
He cited a Supreme Court consent judgment delivered on October 20, 2018, directing the Federal Government to collect outstanding royalties under the law and pay oil-producing states their 13 per cent derivation entitlements upon recovery.
According to the letter, the Federal High Court subsequently entered judgments in favour of Akwa Ibom and Rivers states for a combined $3.3 billion, while Bayelsa State obtained a separate judgment for $951 million.
Falana alleged that the Federal Government had yet to comply with the judgments.
On alleged crude oil theft and undeclared exports, he cited findings attributed to a team of Nigerian lawyers engaged by the Nigerian Maritime Administration and Safety Agency, which reportedly identified about 60.2 million barrels of crude oil, valued at $12.7 billion, allegedly discharged at a port in Philadelphia, United States, between 2011 and 2014.
He also referred to a House of Representatives ad hoc committee’s investigation into undeclared crude oil and liquefied natural gas exports during the same period. According to the letter, the committee found that oil and gas exports worth $17 billion had been shipped without proper records.
Falana urged the authorities to pursue the recovery of the combined $29 billion from the companies allegedly involved, while acknowledging that civil cases filed by NIMASA were pending before the Federal High Court.
The lawyer further alleged that NNPCL had failed to remit $23.1 billion in dividends attributable to the Federal Government’s 49 per cent stake in Nigeria LNG Limited to the Federation Account.
He said NLNG had paid more than $47 billion in dividends to its shareholders over 26 years, with the Federal Government’s share channelled through NNPCL.
Falana argued that the alleged failure to remit the funds contravened Section 162 of the 1999 Constitution, as amended. He added that resolutions of the Senate and House of Representatives calling for the remittance had not been implemented.
The letter also cited the Nigerian Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative’s 2022/2023 oil and gas industry report, which reportedly put outstanding collectible revenues due to the Federal Government at $6.071 billion and N66.4 billion as of June 2024.
Falana urged the National Assembly to support NEITI in recovering the outstanding amounts.
On refinery rehabilitation, he called for the recovery of about $2.9 billion paid under contracts for the rehabilitation of the Port Harcourt, Warri and Kaduna refineries.
He said the Federal Executive Council approved a $1.5 billion contract in April 2021 for the rehabilitation of the Port Harcourt refineries and another $1.48 billion in August 2021 for the Warri and Kaduna facilities.
Citing NNPCL’s subsequent announcements about the refineries’ operational status, Falana alleged that the foreign contractors had breached the terms of their contracts and urged the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission to investigate and pursue recovery of the contract sums.
He argued that recovering the money would enable the Federal Government to engage competent contractors to undertake the rehabilitation projects.
Falana said the recovery of the alleged outstanding revenues would reduce the need for further foreign borrowing by the Federal Government and state governments.
He also argued that his firm had sufficient grounds to pursue legal action, citing its involvement in preparing a bill to amend the Deep Offshore and Inland Basin Production Sharing Contracts Act. The bill, he said, was subsequently adopted, modified and passed by the National Assembly.
The letter’s stated totals, however, contain an apparent discrepancy: while its heading and opening paragraphs cite $123.17 billion, the concluding paragraph refers to $118.67 billion, alongside N66.4 billion. The figures were presented as claims requiring recovery and were not independently verified for this report.

items.content:
By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief
Former Commonwealth Secretary-General, Chief Emeka Anyaoku, has condemned the reported xenophobic attacks against African nationals in South Africa, describing them as distressing and regrettable.
Anyaoku expressed sadness that South Africans, who endured years of apartheid and received support from across Africa in their struggle for liberation, were now turning against fellow Africans from other countries.
The 94-year-old statesman spoke in an interview on the sidelines of the MasterClass on Penetrative Leadership in an Increasingly Chaotic World Order in Abuja.
He recalled his role in efforts to end apartheid and facilitate negotiations between the former white-minority government and the country’s black majority, saying the current attacks were particularly painful given the sacrifices made by other African countries.
“The attacks are regrettable,” Anyaoku said, recalling how he worked to secure support from Commonwealth leaders for efforts to facilitate negotiations in South Africa following the release of Nelson Mandela in 1990.
He recounted that Mandela visited Abuja in May 1990 for a meeting of Commonwealth foreign ministers responsible for South Africa and attended his first official dinner as secretary-general.
Anyaoku said the visit marked the beginning of a friendship with Mandela and his then-wife, Winnie Mandela.
He explained that in 1991, he secured a mandate from Commonwealth Heads of Government to visit South Africa and explore ways to help the country’s then-president, F.W. de Klerk, organise talks aimed at ending apartheid.
According to him, his meeting with de Klerk on November 1, 1991, focused on rebuilding confidence among South Africa’s major ethnic groups.
Anyaoku said de Klerk initially questioned how the Commonwealth could assist South Africa, given its support for sanctions against the apartheid government.
He said he explained that the Commonwealth could help build confidence among the country’s black, white and Asian communities, using the diversity of his delegation as an example.
Anyaoku added that he intervened when the negotiations threatened to collapse, helping to keep the process on course.
He recalled that the agreement concluding the negotiations was signed at 3:30 a.m. on November 17, 1993, in his presence.
Shettima warns against misinformation
At the event, Vice-President Kashim Shettima urged Nigerian elites to exercise restraint in the narratives they promote about the country, particularly in the age of social media and artificial intelligence.
Represented by his Special Adviser on Economic Matters, Dr Tope Fasua, Shettima said the rapid spread of digital information made it necessary for citizens to verify claims before sharing them.
“Digital success is an asset. It gives Nigerian businesses access to customers, young people access to opportunities and citizens access to information. But it also places a greater responsibility on all of us to distinguish reliable information from manipulation,” he said.
Adesina stresses national reputation
Also speaking, Group Managing Director of Sahara Power Group, Mr Kola Adesina, said reputation was built on three pillars: performance, character and goodwill.
He urged Nigerians to pay greater attention to how their actions and public communications shape the country’s image.
Adesina said younger generations could learn valuable lessons from experienced leaders such as Anyaoku, particularly by studying their responses to crises and avoiding past mistakes.
He also cautioned against the tendency to share information instantly without verifying its accuracy.
“Your reputation is a matter of choice; it’s a decision,” he said.

items.author: Daily Trust
items.content:
The Zamfara State Government says it will commission more than 70 completed projects across the state as part of activities marking the 30th anniversary of its creation.
The projects cover healthcare, education, infrastructure, commerce, sports, security and public administration.
The state was created in 1996.
According to a statement issued by the Ministry of Information and Culture on October 20, Governor Dauda Lawal will commission the projects as part of activities marking the anniversary.
In the health sector, the projects include the rehabilitation of general hospitals in Gummi, Kasuwar Daji in Kaura Namoda and Shinkafi, as well as the construction and equipping of the General Hospital in Talata Mafara.
Others are the rehabilitation of the Women and Children Hospital in Kaura Namoda, including staff quarters, and the remodelling and furnishing of administrative blocks at the Drugs and Medical Consumables Agency.
In education, the projects include the renovation of the Smart School in Gusau, construction of a safe school in Anka, and rehabilitation of Government Secondary School, Maru, and Government Science Secondary School, Gusau.
The government also listed hostels and a clinic at the College of Education, Maru; hostels at Abdu Gusau Polytechnic, Talata Mafara; and a Faculty of Education, clinic and store at the state university in Talata Mafara.
Other projects include classroom and office blocks at the Federal University Gusau, alongside an administrative block and rehabilitated classrooms at the Zamfara College of Arts and Science (ZACAS), Gusau.
Under infrastructure and commerce, the government listed the Fanna Bridge, a 300-metre surfaced approach road and the Magami link road.
The projects also include the first phase of an ultra-modern market in Gusau, comprising 165 shops, 25 bus stops across the metropolis and parking facilities at the J.B. Yakubu Secretariat Complex.
In the sports, recreation and cultural sector, the Sardauna Memorial Stadium in Gusau has been upgraded.
Other projects include the rehabilitation of Gusau Amusement Park, construction of a monument sculpture at Gada-Biyu Roundabout, a small city garden and renovation of the Sambo Dan Ashafa Juma’ah Mosque in Yardole.
The statement further listed renovation, remodelling and furnishing works at several ministries, departments and agencies, including the Ministry of Information and Culture, Zamfara State AM Radio Station, Ministry of Agriculture, Ministry of Women Affairs, Civil Service Commission and Office of the Auditor-General.
Other institutions covered include the Bureau of Statistics, Teaching Service Board, State Pension Board, Hospital Services Management Board, ZAROTA, Ulama’u Council, and state housing and electrification agencies.
At Government House in Gusau, the projects include the renovation of chalets and one-bedroom suites, remodelling of the Chief of Staff’s office, rehabilitation and automation of the auditorium conference hall, and renovation of the First Lady’s office and 38 staff offices.
The government also listed the construction of a central kitchen, recreational centre and perimeter fence at the Government House.
In the security and justice sectors, completed projects include the remodelling of the police command headquarters, construction of an ammunition depot and administrative block at the Nigerian Army Cantonment in Gusau, and rehabilitation of the residence of the 1 Brigade Commander.
Other works include the renovation of a High Court judge’s residence, fencing of the Group of Courts and construction of a doctors’ quarters block at the Federal Medical Centre, Gusau.
The government said the projects were aimed at improving public service delivery, expanding access to healthcare and education, boosting economic activities and strengthening security.
The Commissioner for Information and Culture, Mahmud Muhammad Dantawasa, urged the media and the public to cooperate with the anniversary planning committee.
He added that the schedule for the commissioning would be announced later.

items.author: Business Desk
items.content:
Small and medium enterprises (SMEs) can now apply for bank financing online through SMEConnect, the State Bank of Pakistan’s (SBP) new digital portal. The process takes a few steps: create an account, verify your business bank account, fill in your business details, and submit a financing request to your bank.
SBP has shared a step-by-step video tutorial on how to use the platform, which is available at smeconnect.sbp.org.pk. The portal connects SMEs and banks on a single platform and can be used in either English or Urdu.
The guide matters because, from November 1, 2026, all SME financing applications will be received only through SMEConnect, as ProPakistani reported earlier. Here is how to apply.
Step 1: Check Eligibility and Create an Account
Visit the SMEConnect portal. Its home page shows the eligibility criteria for SME financing, an outline of the application process, and quick links to related bodies such as the SBP, SECP, FBR, SMEDA, and the SBP’s Sunwai complaint service.
Existing users can log in with their email address and password or continue with Google. New users should click “Please Register” to create an account.
On the registration form, enter your full name, mobile number, email address, gender, CNIC, and a password, then accept the terms of service. You will receive a security code on your email address or mobile number. Enter it to complete registration.
Step 2: Verify Your Business Bank Account
Next, enter the IBAN of the bank account you mainly use for business transactions. The portal fills in the bank’s name automatically from the IBAN and verifies it.
If you don’t have a bank account, you will need to open one first. If you have accounts in more than one bank, enter the IBAN of the bank from which you want to receive the financing.
Step 3: Add Your Business Information
Once the IBAN is verified, the portal lets you fill in your business details. These include the business name, owner’s CNIC, business email address, nature of business, NTN, business status, address, year of establishment, annual sales, business premises, and registration authority.
Click “Save & Continue”, check the summary of your business profile, and confirm to save it. You will then land on your dashboard, which shows the number of applications that are in draft, submitted, under review, approved, rejected, and disbursed.
Step 4: Apply for Financing
On the dashboard, click “Apply for New Financing”. The application has three stages: business information, financing, and review.
In the financing section, enter the details of the loan you need, such as the mode of financing, the amount you are requesting, and the tenor. The tutorial shows Islamic financing as one of the available modes.
Step 5: Review and Submit
After filling in all the details, review the information carefully. If you are not ready to apply yet, you can save the application as a draft and come back to it later.
 
To apply, click “Submit Application”, read the undertaking, and click “Agree & Submit”. The portal will then show your application reference, including a case ID, the submission date, the assigned bank, and the status of the application. The SBP notes that approval of the financing is subject to the bank’s own assessment.
What Happens After You Apply
You can check the status of your application at any time through the “Track Application” option. The relevant bank will contact you on the mobile number or email address you provided for further processing.
According to the SBP, if the information and documents you provided are complete and correct, the bank will decide on your financing application within the time frame set under the central bank’s instructions.
To log in again later, enter your registered email address and password, followed by the six-digit OTP sent to your mobile number or email. If you forget your password, you can reset it through the “Forgot Password” option.
Where to Get Help
For more information or guidance on SMEConnect or SME financing, you can contact your bank or the SBP helpline. The portal lists the email address smeconnect@sbp.org.pk and the number +92 21 111 727 273 for queries.
Complaints can be filed through the SBP’s Sunwai portal or its mobile app. The platform is part of the SBP’s push to expand credit to small businesses, which earlier saw the central bank raise SME financing limits to up to Rs. 500 million.
The post How to Apply for Small Business Loans Through SBP Online appeared first on ProPakistani.

items.author: Business Desk
items.content:
Financing approved under the Prime Minister’s Apna Ghar Program has jumped 245 percent since June 2026 to Rs. 511 billion, according to Advisor to the Finance Minister Khurram Schehzad.
In a post on X, Schehzad said approved financing under the affordable housing scheme had risen from Rs. 148 billion in June to Rs. 511 billion as of October 23, 2026.
Disbursements grew even faster, rising 333 percent from Rs. 21 billion to Rs. 91 billion during the same period.
Approval Rate Rises to 40 Percent
According to the data shared by the advisor, banks have received 217,001 applications under the program so far. Of these, 86,896 applications have been approved, while 15,584 housing loans have been disbursed.
The approval rate has also improved, rising to 40 percent from 28 percent in June, an increase of 12 percentage points.
“More financing. More families closer to owning their homes,” Schehzad said in his post.
Gap Between Approvals and Disbursements
The figures were also discussed at the sixth meeting of the Access to Finance (A2F) Steering Committee, chaired by Federal Minister for Finance and Revenue Senator Muhammad Aurangzeb.
The committee noted the progress in housing finance and discussed steps to speed up disbursements and address housing supply constraints, including financing for builders and under-construction projects.
Despite the faster growth in disbursements, only around 18 percent of the approved financing, Rs. 91 billion out of Rs. 511 billion, has so far reached borrowers.
The program has gained pace in recent months. In August, ProPakistani reported that housing finance had surged 94 percent under the PM loan scheme. The government has set a target of financing 150,000 homes under the scheme by June 2027.

items.author: Anne Florentyna
items.content:
The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has launched investigations into alleged violations of the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA) involving crypto platforms Mudrex and Saber.money, as well as decentralised finance (DeFi) protocol Instadapp and its associated platform Fluid, over alleged unauthorised cross-border fund transfers worth more than ₹4,940 Cr.
The agency said its Bengaluru Zonal Office conducted searches at three premises in Bengaluru and one in Madhya Pradesh on October 27 under Section 37 of FEMA, 1999.
The investigations centre on the alleged use of cryptocurrencies, particularly stablecoins such as USDT and USDC, to facilitate cross-border money transfers outside authorised channels.
The ED said its preliminary investigation into the Mudrex and Saber.money operations indicated alleged FEMA violations exceeding ₹4,600 Cr. Separately, the agency alleged contraventions amounting to approximately $40 Mn (around ₹380.6 Cr) in the Instadapp/Fluid case.
ED Flags Alleged Unauthorised Transfers Through Crypto Platforms
The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has searched four premises in Bengaluru and Madhya Pradesh as part of an investigation into alleged unauthorised cross-border financial transactions involving cryptocurrency worth more than ₹5,000 Cr.
The agency’s Bengaluru Zonal Office conducted the searches earlier this week on October 27 under the FEMA regulations. In a post on X, the ED said its probe had uncovered the alleged use of shell entities in tax-haven jurisdictions, large over-the-counter (OTC) transactions and foreign payouts through cryptocurrency platforms such as Binance and Bybit. <
It has identified Bengaluru-based RPFAS Technologies Pvt Ltd, which operates platforms Mudrex and Saber.money, among the entities which allegedly use crypto currencies for unauthorised cross border transactions and trading.
“The entity is openly advertising instant money transfer across borders using cryptocurrencies despite not being authorised with RBI,” the agency said.
The platforms also allegedly offered crypto on-ramp and off-ramp services, allowing users to convert traditional currencies such as INR, USD and EUR into digital assets and subsequently withdraw the proceeds into bank accounts.
The ED alleged that these services were used to facilitate cross-border transfers through stablecoins, bypassing authorised channels for international remittances.
In a separate investigation, the ED examined Instadapp, a DeFi protocol deployed on the Ethereum blockchain, and its associated platform Fluid. Instadapp provides tools for decentralised finance activities, including lending, borrowing and swapping crypto assets through smart contracts.
The ED alleged that entities associated with the protocol were incorporated in foreign jurisdictions but managed from India. These entities were reportedly registered across jurisdictions including the US, Singapore, the British Virgin Islands and Dubai.
According to the agency, searches and preliminary investigations indicated that some of these entities did not have physical offices or employees at their registered addresses, while their operations were allegedly managed from India.
The ED further alleged that funds received from overseas investors were routed through foreign bank accounts and subsequently transferred to India to meet expenses and other payments.
This is the second such investigation that the agency has revealed in recent months. In June, the ED searched six premises linked to five Bengaluru-based platforms — Transak, Carret, Xpat, Onramp.money and Onmeta — over alleged unauthorised cross-border crypto transfers.
The agency froze bank accounts holding around ₹6 Cr, alleging the platforms circumvented FEMA by using stablecoins to route remittances outside authorised channels. It said the entities lacked RBI authorisation for such transfers and operated through foreign-registered entities controlled from India.
It is pertinent to note that cryptocurrencies remain unregulated in India, while also attracting a 30% capital gains tax and 1% TDS on every transaction.
Authorities continue to flag risks in the ecosystem, with the parliamentary standing committee on finance last month classifying the asset class as “high risk” citing rampant money laundering, trafficking, radicalisation and suspicious crypto transaction.

items.author: Anne Florentyna
items.content:
Delhi-based B2B ecommerce startup Bijnis has rebranded as Zorit and raised ₹27 Cr in a funding round led by Sparrow Capital, as it doubles down on an inventory-led quick-commerce model for offline retailers.
The round saw participation from existing investors Info Edge and WaterBridge Ventures, Better Capital, and angel investors including Shaadi.com founder Anupam Mittal, the founders of Shiprocket, Xpressbees CEO Mohit Sardana and Sarthak Misra of SoftBank, as per its press note.
The fresh capital will be used to strengthen its quick commerce infrastructure, expand its product assortment and deepen engagement with retailers across its operating markets.
Founded in 2015 by Siddharth Vij, Chaitanya Rathi, Siddharth Rastogi and Sachin Chauhan, the startup initially built a digital marketplace connecting manufacturers with retailers. It shifted to an inventory-led B2B quick-commerce model in late 2024, stocking products in local dark stores to enable faster replenishment for neighbourhood retailers.
As Bijnis, the startup had raised over $43 Mn, including a $30 Mn funding round. However, the startup ran into severe operational and financial trouble by 2023.
In its new avatar, the startup allows retailers to source products locally stocked dark stores, with delivery in as little as 60 minutes. This compares with the seven-to-eight-day delivery cycles of its earlier online B2B model and the 24–48-hour fulfilment typically offered by local wholesale traders.
Zorit currently claims to operate 12 dark stores across 12 cities and claims to have reached ₹120 Cr in annualised sales. Nearly half of its stores have achieved break-even, including the cost of liquidating unsold inventory, the company said.
The startup said that monthly ordering frequency has increased fivefold compared with its previous model, while retailer retention beyond the sixth month has improved fourfold.
“Zorit’s quick commerce model has brought a new segment of retailers into digital sourcing, with nearly 60% having never used an online B2B platform before. Compared with its previous model, retailer retention beyond month 6 has improved 4X,” cofounder and CEO Siddharth Vij said.
Info Edge wrote off its entire ₹76.6 Cr investment in Bijnis in 2023. The investor cited continuing cash burn, limited cash availability relative to potential liabilities linked to investor buyback obligations, and uncertainty over future fundraising back then.
On the fresh investment, Info Edge Ventures’ partner Kitty Agarwal said, “Zorit’s manufacturer-first approach has now evolved into a powerful quick-commerce layer for small retailers – enabling access to a wide assortment with speed and ease. This has unlocked incredible frequency and retention among retailers, while simultaneously creating deeper demand for manufacturers.”

items.author: Business Desk
items.content:
The Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) has launched a dedicated trading counter for investors who want to buy and sell shares and other securities that comply with Islamic principles.
The launch follows approval of the Shariah Trading Counter Regulations by the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP). The new system provides retail and institutional investors with a dedicated platform for Shariah-compliant investments.
A total of 39 brokerage firms have joined the initiative through their Islamic windows, while two other brokerage houses are licensed to operate exclusively as Shariah-compliant brokers.
Trading on the counter is restricted to Shariah-compliant shares, government Ijarah Sukuk and corporate Sukuk. Interest-based financing products, short selling and derivatives trading are not allowed.
Instead, investors can use Murabaha Share Financing (MSF), a Shariah-compliant alternative to conventional share financing. Investors can also sell non-compliant holdings to help bring their portfolios into line with Islamic investment principles.
PSX has also introduced a Shariah portal on its Data Portal, where investors can check which shares and Sukuk are eligible for Islamic investment.
Investors can open regular trading accounts or Sahulat Accounts using a Shariah-compliant customer relationship and risk disclosure document.
PSX Managing Director and CEO Farrukh H. Sabzwari said the new system would improve access to Islamic investment opportunities and strengthen investor confidence.
He added that the number of investor accounts at the exchange had crossed 650,000, with Millennials and Gen Z contributing significantly to new participation.
SECP Commissioner Imtiaz Haider said the initiative could attract more investors and create opportunities for brokerage firms.
The SECP also plans to expand digital retail Sukuk and introduce Shariah-compliant tools for liquidity and risk management.
The post PSX Launches Islamic Trading Counter Just for Investors appeared first on ProPakistani.

items.author: Gaurav Bagur
items.content:
Bengaluru-based Pixxel has set up a new subsidiary in the US, Pixxel Federal, to tap into the US government market and build on its existing engagements with NASA and the National Reconnaissance Office (NRO).
The startup, which just raised $100 Mn last month, is now planning to set up an office around Washington, DC to work more closely with government customers and partners.
The US subsidiary intends to offer earth observation technologies, satellite mission systems and geospatial intelligence to American government agencies across civilian, defence and intelligence sectors.
“The US government market represents a significant opportunity for Pixxel as we expand our capabilities beyond hyperspectral imaging into advanced sensing technologies, software, and satellite systems,” said the startup’s founder and CEO Awais Ahmed.
Pixxel executive Allyson Jenkins – previously Vice President, Public Sector – has been appointed CEO of Pixxel Federal. She had already been leading the company’s US government business since joining in January 2025.
Important to mention that Pixxel recently secured a contract through NASA’s Commercial SmallSat Data Acquisition Programme and a Strategic Commercial Enhancements contract from the NRO. The new subsidiary will build on these relationships to pursue additional federal contracts and strengthen the company’s position in the US space and geospatial intelligence market.
It will leverage Pixxel’s hyperspectral satellites, Earth intelligence software and satellite mission systems for applications such as camouflage detection, terrain characterisation, critical mineral and rare earth element detection, environmental monitoring and agriculture.
Founded in 2019 by BITS Pilani alumni Ahmed and Kshitij Khandelwal, Pixxel claims to operate the world’s highest-resolution constellation of commercial hyperspectral satellites, which can capture light across a large number of narrow wavelength bands to identify details or changes on the Earth’s surface that conventional imagery may miss.
Besides its US government contracts, Pixxel has won multiple iDEX challenges in India from the Ministry of Defence and is currently developing a public-private Earth observation satellite constellation under IN-SPACe. The proposed constellation, which is expected to be India’s first of its kind, will comprise 12 satellites carrying different types of imaging sensors.
In September, the startup raised $100 Mn in a Series C round co-led by Temasek and Seraphim, marking the largest single investment round for an Indian spacetech company.
With the round, Pixxel’s total private funding now is around $195 Mn. Investors like Google, Radical Ventures, growX ventures, Lightspeed Venture Partners, 360 ONE Asset, are on its cap table.

items.author: Shazia Tasneem Farooqi
items.content:
Pakistan's efforts to attract investment and encourage innovation will remain constrained unless businesses can navigate a simpler, faster and more predictable regulatory system, experts warned at a seminar held at the Institute of Business Administration (IBA) Karachi on Thursday.
Titled "Transforming the Regulatory State: Pathways to a Dynamic and Competitive Economy", the seminar provided a platform for representatives from international regulatory reform practice, business and government to examine how overlapping rules, outdated procedures and complex licensing requirements affect the country's competitiveness.
Pakistan had approved 557 reforms across multiple sectors, Scott Jacobs, managing director of Jacobs, Cordova and Associates and recipient of the Prime Minister's Regulatory Reform Champion award, said, outlining the country's reform journey under the Regulatory Guillotine and SMART initiative led by the Board of Investment. He said the approvals marked progress in efforts to simplify the regulatory environment.
However, he stressed that the next phase required a fundamental change in the approach of regulators, from controlling markets to facilitating them. This would mean moving beyond the simplification of individual licences and permits towards a broader system of regulatory governance that enables businesses to operate and expand more efficiently. "The next phase must change the 'regulatory DNA' of Pakistan's regulators, from controlling markets to facilitating them," Jacobs commented.
He noted that Pakistan's transition towards wider regulatory reform reflected international good practice, although the programme was being pursued at a much faster pace and with potentially greater impact. Ultimately, the success of these measures would depend on whether they changed investors' perceptions of the returns and risks associated with investing in Pakistan. He also highlighted the limited financial depth available to venture capitalists in Pakistan compared with regional counterparts, which restricts funding for new and innovative firms. Without adequate access to capital and a supportive regulatory environment, entrepreneurs may find it difficult to develop new ideas into viable businesses.
Jacobs explained, using battery manufacturing as an example, that entrepreneurs seeking to establish innovative businesses must navigate multiple layers of regulations, certifications and licences. Such requirements can turn the process of setting up a business into a prolonged administrative challenge. He said the system needed to be transformed from an obstacle course into a fast-moving highway for entrepreneurs.
The Pakistan Business Council's CEO, Javed Kureishi, highlighted the burden that numerous and complex rules impose on businesses. He cited the foreign exchange manual as a case in point, describing it as badly outdated and a significant deterrent for foreign investors. Outdated regulations can create uncertainty for investors assessing whether to enter or expand in Pakistan, while complicated procedures increase the time and effort required to conduct business. Simplifying such rules is therefore an important part of making the country a more attractive investment destination.
Federal Board of Revenue Member Ambreen Iftikhar said the government needed to play a more constructive role in enabling businesses. She pointed to the duplication of regulatory requirements by different agencies across Pakistan that had been established for similar purposes.
Such overlapping oversight creates additional hurdles for businesses, particularly innovative firms that must comply with multiple requirements while trying to develop and scale their operations. Better coordination among public-sector agencies could help reduce duplication and make regulatory processes more effective, she said.
The panellists also emphasised the need for stronger engagement between academia, policymakers and the business community. They said universities and researchers should contribute evidence-based analysis, examine the effects of existing regulations and engage directly with those responsible for designing and implementing reforms.
Academia's role should extend beyond studying policy issues in isolation to helping identify practical solutions that reflect the needs of businesses and the wider economy. Regular exchanges among government, industry and academic institutions could help ensure that reforms are informed by evidence and address problems faced by businesses in practice.
The speakers stressed that Pakistan's ability to improve its competitiveness and create better opportunities for the next generation would depend on fundamentally transforming its regulatory framework. A simpler and more responsive system, they said, would help businesses innovate, encourage investment and support a more dynamic economy.
The seminar was followed by an interactive question-and-answer session with the participants.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Federal Minister for National Food Security and Research Rana Tanveer Hussain has directed that a proposed 12 to 18-month fast-track approval mechanism for imported cotton seed be examined within the existing legal framework, against the roughly seven years required under current procedures.
The proposal, supported by cotton-sector stakeholders, will not compromise mandatory scientific testing, biosecurity or biosafety standards, according to an official statement issued on Thursday after a meeting chaired by the minister on the Cotton Revival Strategy. The meeting reviewed the persistent decline in cotton cultivation, particularly in Punjab, where falling yields, rising production costs and declining profitability have pushed farmers towards sugarcane, maize and other competing crops. Cotton Leaf Curl Virus, pest infestations, climate variability, poor-quality seed and inadequate mechanisation were identified as major constraints.
A three-pronged strategy was considered, focusing on strengthening locally developed cotton seed, facilitating imports of improved seed and introducing the fast-track mechanism.
A three-member committee comprising the Pakistan Agricultural Research Council (PARC), National Seed Development and Regulatory Authority (NSDRA) and Pakistan Central Cotton Committee (PCCC), led by PARC, will be constituted to facilitate acquisition of exotic cotton germplasm.
The minister directed the Department of Plant Protection to expedite pending Pest Risk Analyses and Controlled Import Permits. China has submitted its technical dossier, with additional information requested. Engagement with Türkiye, Syria, Kenya, the United States, Mexico, Kyrgyzstan and Australia remains dependent on their responses.
On crop zoning, NSDRA was directed to expedite processing of promising varieties and ensure basic seed availability, with varieties approved on performance in specific agro-climatic regions rather than uniform national criteria.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
The benchmark KSE-100 index of the Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) extended its recovery for the fourth consecutive session on Thursday, gaining over 1,450 points to close near 167,195 – its highest finish since early October.
Arif Habib Limited (AHL), in its report, noted that the KSE-100 extended its recovery for the fourth session in a row, rising 0.88% (+1,456.68 points) to close at 167,193.44, a nearly one-month high. Breadth was modestly positive, with 55 constituents advancing against 43 decliners, and the bulk of index points came from fertiliser (FFC) and bank (HBL) names, while NBP, DGKC and POL were the principal drags.
Among corporate results, PPL posted 1QFY27 earnings of Rs9.26 per share (+25% year-on-year), driven largely by a 26% jump in oil prices, and PSO reported earnings of Rs54.44 per share (+172% year-on-year), supported by higher volumes, petroleum prices and inventory gains.
AHL flagged that the index had moved into the weekly resistance, leaving the technical downside reference near 160,000 still open. In geopolitical developments, Qatari mediators presented Iran with a revised draft proposal aimed at ending hostilities with the US and Israel, though Iranian officials did not give any indication of acceptance.
"The market continues to recover from the mid-October sell-off, with gains concentrated in banks and fertiliser stocks while oil-linked names registered mixed results with price support. Volume was the heaviest in several weeks, confirming broad participation in the bounce, yet the proximity to resistance and the still-open 160k level keep the near-term technical picture two-sided," AHL added.
Topline's market review highlighted that the PSX extended its bullish momentum for the fourth consecutive session, where the benchmark index advanced 1,457 points (+0.88%) to close at 167,193. The bourse maintained its upward trajectory throughout the session, reflecting sustained buying interest across key sectors and an improvement in investor sentiment amid ongoing corporate earnings announcements.
The index traded within the intra-day range of 165,907 to 167,483, demonstrating resilience and a strong recovery from its intra-day lows. The positive momentum was primarily driven by renewed buying interest in heavyweight banking and fertiliser stocks, while encouraging market participation further reinforced the bullish sentiment, Topline said.
Market activity was strong as overall trading volumes were recorded at 816.83 million shares compared with the previous session's tally of 578.12 million. The value of shares traded during the day was Rs31.54 billion.
Shares of 499 companies were traded. Of these, 232 stocks closed higher, another 232 fell, and 35 remained unchanged.
Cnergyico Pk was the volume leader with trading in 184 million shares, gaining Rs1.28 to close at Rs14.08. It was followed by Pervez Ahmed Consultancy with 81.1 million shares, gaining Rs0.73 to close at Rs4.40 and K-Electric with 46.8 million shares, gaining Rs0.13 to close at Rs5.96. Foreign investors sold shares worth Rs1.2 billion, the National Clearing Company reported.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Federal Minister for Finance and Revenue Senator Muhammad Aurangzeb met with Dr Rajeh Tami Albugamy, Ambassador of Saudi Arabia to Pakistan, who called on him to discuss bilateral economic cooperation, trade, investment and shared priorities.
The finance minister reaffirmed the longstanding bonds of friendship and brotherhood between Pakistan and Saudi Arabia. He appreciated Saudi Arabia's continued support for Pakistan and emphasised the importance of further strengthening the economic relationship between the two countries.
The Saudi ambassador underscored the historic relationship between the two countries, rooted in shared faith, history, mutual trust and respect. He emphasised that stronger business-to-business engagement could further deepen people-to-people connections and create mutually beneficial economic opportunities.
Aurangzeb highlighted Pakistan's progress in restoring macroeconomic stability, noting improvements in foreign exchange reserves and inflation, as well as recent upgrades by international credit rating agencies.
He also referred to Pakistan's return to international capital markets through its recent $3 billion Eurobond issuance and its access to China's capital market. He highlighted the importance of building on recent economic gains to strengthen investor confidence and support sustainable, investment-led growth.
The two sides discussed opportunities for cooperation in agriculture, minerals and mining, and other sectors with investment potential. They emphasised the need for translating shared priorities into tangible outcomes and strengthening commercial engagement between the two countries.
The meeting also included an exchange of views on the prevailing regional situation and ongoing conflict, with emphasis on the importance of peace, stability and continued cooperation to address emerging challenges and safeguard regional economic prospects.
The discussion highlighted Pakistan's strategic geographical location and its potential to serve as a regional trade and transit hub, facilitating connectivity and creating opportunities for wider economic cooperation.
The finance minister reiterated the government's commitment to staying the course on structural reforms and maintaining a stable, predictable investment environment to support domestic and foreign investment.
The meeting reaffirmed the commitment from Pakistan and Saudi Arabia to strengthening their strategic partnership and expanding cooperation in trade and investment. Both sides underscored the importance of continued engagement to advance shared economic priorities.

items.author: Business Desk
items.content:
The State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) has launched SMEConnect, a centralized digital platform through which small and medium enterprises (SMEs) can apply for financing from banks and development finance institutions (DFIs) across the country.
The platform, available at smeconnect.sbp.org.pk, will serve as a single digital window for SME loan applications. According to the central bank, it will streamline the application process and improve accessibility, efficiency, and transparency in SME financing.
Real-Time Tracking and Rejection Reasons
Besides simplifying the loan application process, SMEConnect will let applicants track the status of their applications in real time. If an application is rejected, the applicant will also be able to see the reasons for the rejection.
The platform also has a live dashboard that will give the SBP complete visibility of SME financing applications and their status. It will provide real-time data on applications received, processed, approved, disbursed, and rejected, both at the level of individual banks and DFIs and across the industry.
Mandatory From November 1
From November 1, 2026, all SME financing applications will be received exclusively through SMEConnect. SME applicants who visit bank or DFI branches, or try to apply through their websites, will be directed to the platform.
The SBP has advised all banks and DFIs to prominently display the SMEConnect link on their websites. They have also been told to ensure that their SME teams and field staff fully understand the platform and guide applicants through it.
How to Apply for Small Business Loan
A tutorial video is available on the portal to help applicants apply for financing.
The move is the latest in the central bank’s efforts to expand credit to small businesses. Earlier, the SBP raised SME financing limits to up to Rs. 500 million and released draft prudential regulations for SME financing for public consultation.

items.content:
Apple reportedly relaxed quality inspection standards for the iPhone Duo to increase production ahead of the holiday shopping season, even as some users reported problems with the foldable phone’s inner display.
According to a report from Chinese publication Jiemian News, an unnamed Foxconn employee claimed that Apple had lowered its quality checks to speed up shipments.
The report comes after several iPhone Duo owners complained about cracked inner screens, with some pointing to a possible problem with the phone’s folding mechanism.
Apple has acknowledged the display issue but says it affects only a small number of devices.
Apple Reportedly Relaxed Quality Checks
According to Jiemian News, Apple has been working to increase iPhone Duo production to meet demand ahead of the holiday season.
The company is reportedly targeting shipments of 7.5 million units before the end of 2026.
An unnamed Foxconn employee claimed that quality inspection standards had been lowered to help get more devices into stores.
However, the same source said the iPhone Duo production line had already replaced a batch of components and that its quality control standards had not been changed.
These conflicting claims make it unclear whether Apple actually reduced its inspection requirements.
Apple has not publicly confirmed the allegations.
Users Report Cracked Inner Displays
The latest report follows complaints from early iPhone Duo buyers who discovered damage to their phones’ folding screens.
Several users reported cracks appearing near the hinge, sometimes accompanied by unusual cracking or popping sounds.
Apple responded to the complaints on October 26, acknowledging that a small number of devices were experiencing inner display problems.
The company advised affected customers to contact AppleCare for a replacement.
However, Apple has not identified the exact cause of the issue or announced whether changes to the hinge design are planned.
New Video Points to Possible Hinge Problem
A separate investigation by YouTube creator CuriousHagi has raised further questions about the iPhone Duo’s hinge mechanism.
The video highlights a small connecting component inside the hinge that appears to come into contact with an upper support plate when the device folds.
&&&&&&&
The component sits behind the middle section of the inner display and appears thinner than surrounding hinge parts.
According to the analysis, contact between these components could explain the cracking sounds reported by some affected users.
The findings suggest that pressure from the hinge mechanism may be contributing to screen damage.
However, the explanation remains a theory, and Apple has not confirmed that this particular component is responsible for the failures.
Apple Faces Questions Over iPhone Duo Durability
The iPhone Duo has faced concerns about durability since its launch, including reports of hinge damage and unsuccessful bend tests.
The latest claims have raised additional questions about whether Apple can increase production while maintaining consistent manufacturing quality.
For now, Apple maintains that only a small number of devices are affected and that customers experiencing display problems should request a replacement.
The company has not confirmed the reported changes to quality inspections or explained whether the replacement components mentioned in the Foxconn report address the screen failures.

items.author: Danial Saigra
items.content:
Macquarie University in Sydney, Australia, is accepting applications for its Road to Research Scholarship, which provides a living allowance of AUD 40,900 and tuition fee coverage for students pursuing a Master of Research (MRes) degree.
The scholarship is available to eligible applicants who are already living in Australia and plan to begin full-time research studies in Session 1 of 2027.
According to the university’s scholarship information, applications will close on October 31, 2026, at 11:00 pm Australian Eastern Daylight Time (AEDT).
The scholarship provides financial assistance for up to one year and supports students undertaking research projects as part of their postgraduate studies.
Macquarie University has also encouraged current postgraduate coursework students who are expected to complete their degrees in Session 2 of 2026 to apply.
Scholarship Benefits
The Road to Research Scholarship provides financial assistance to students pursuing a Master of Research degree at Macquarie University.
Successful applicants will receive a tuition fee offset for a maximum period of one year, along with an annual living allowance of AUD 40,900 at the 2027 scholarship rate.
The funding is intended to support students during their research studies and reduce the financial costs associated with postgraduate education.
In addition to the main scholarship, recipients may receive supplementary minor awards and earn income through eligible part-time employment.
The university also allows stipend top-up funding of up to 100% of the scholarship’s stipend value, subject to the applicable conditions.
Additional financial support may be available for research-related expenses, including fieldwork, equipment, and other costs not covered by the primary scholarship.
Who Can Apply for the Scholarship
The Road to Research Scholarship is available to eligible students who are already present in Australia at the time of application.
Applicants must intend to live in Sydney throughout their research candidature and commence the Master of Research program on a full-time basis in January 2027.
Both domestic and eligible international applicants may be considered, provided they meet the university’s admission and scholarship requirements.
International students must hold a valid visa that allows them to begin their studies in Australia.
Applicants must also satisfy Macquarie University’s English-language requirements and meet the academic admission criteria for the Master of Research program.
The university requires applicants to obtain confirmation of supervision from an eligible Macquarie University researcher.
Academic and English-Language Requirements
According to the published scholarship listing, applicants are expected to have a minimum GPA of 3.0.
The listing also provides several English-language test scores, including IELTS 6.5, TOEFL iBT 83, PTE Academic 58, and Duolingo English Test 115.
However, applicants must meet the English-language requirements specified by Macquarie University for their chosen research program.
The scholarship covers several academic disciplines, including arts and social sciences, business, criminology, education, engineering, health, information technology, languages and linguistics, law, media, medicine, and psychological science.
Candidates must also meet the academic requirements for admission to the Master of Research program.
How Will Students Be Selected
Macquarie University will select scholarship recipients through a competitive academic ranking process.
The university generally ranks applicants according to their Weighted Average Mark (WAM), which reflects their academic performance.
However, applicants who completed their qualifications before 2020 or graduated from another university will be assessed using their Grade Point Average (GPA).
For students holding overseas qualifications, Macquarie University will assess their academic credentials according to Australian Government guidelines.
The assessment determines how international qualifications compare with the Australian Qualifications Framework.
Meeting the minimum eligibility requirements does not automatically guarantee selection, as applications are assessed competitively.
Required Documents
Applicants must prepare the academic and supporting documents required for admission and scholarship consideration.
According to the published scholarship listing, these include academic transcripts, previous degree certificates, an application essay, and two recommendation letters.
Candidates must also fulfil the university’s supervision requirements and provide relevant information regarding their eligibility to study in Australia.
International applicants must ensure that their visa permits them to commence their studies in 2027.
Students should review the university’s official application instructions to confirm the complete documentation requirements before submitting their applications.
How to Apply for the Road to Research Scholarship
Interested candidates can apply for the Road to Research Scholarship through Macquarie University’s official scholarship application process.
Before applying, students must ensure they meet the university’s academic admission, English-language, residency, and supervision requirements.
Applicants must also be present in Australia when submitting their applications and intend to remain in Sydney throughout their candidature.
Applicants for the Master of Research program must be ready to begin full-time studies in January 2027.
The university has set the application deadline for October 31, 2026, at 11:00 pm AEDT.
