items.title: Patrick Stewart, Shakespearean actor turned 'Star Trek' and 'X-Men' star, dies at 86
items.summary:
Patrick Stewart, who rose from poverty in England to become an accomplished Shakespearean stage actor and then achieved global stardom as the erudite Captain Jean-Luc Picard in TV's "Star Trek: The Next Generation" and the telepathic Professor Charles Xavier in the "X-Men" movies, has died at the age of 86.
Stewart, knighted in 2010 by Queen Elizabeth II for his contributions to drama, died at his home in Los ​Angeles, according to a statement on his X account.
"We announce with great sorrow the passing of Sir Patrick Stewart yesterday at his home in Los Angeles, in the loving care of ‌his beloved wife Sunny following a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer's Disease and Lewy Body Dementia," it said.
In lieu of flowers, memorial contributions may be made to:
Johns Hopkins Alzheimer’s Disease Research Center Fund https://t.co/luC5CdcWDy
Alzheimer’s Foundation of America Caregiver Resources https://t.co/zvNptfyuNd
Photo Credit: Tommy Gar
items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Patrick Stewart, who rose from poverty in England to become an accomplished Shakespearean stage actor and then achieved global stardom as the erudite Captain Jean-Luc Picard in TV's "Star Trek: The Next Generation" and the telepathic Professor Charles Xavier in the "X-Men" movies, has died at the age of 86.
Stewart, knighted in 2010 by Queen Elizabeth II for his contributions to drama, died at his home in Los ​Angeles, according to a statement on his X account.
"We announce with great sorrow the passing of Sir Patrick Stewart yesterday at his home in Los Angeles, in the loving care of ‌his beloved wife Sunny following a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer's Disease and Lewy Body Dementia," it said.
In lieu of flowers, memorial contributions may be made to:
Johns Hopkins Alzheimer’s Disease Research Center Fund https://t.co/luC5CdcWDy
Alzheimer’s Foundation of America Caregiver Resources https://t.co/zvNptfyuNd
Photo Credit: Tommy Garcia pic.twitter.com/XNncEVq56X
— Patrick Stewart (@SirPatStew) October 29, 2026
Stewart became an actor at age 18 and gained acclaim on the stage as a member of the Royal Shakespeare Company beginning in the 1960s. But it was not until after he was hired at age 47 for "Star Trek: The Next Generation" - a TV series that ran from 1987 to 1994 as a sequel to the original 1960s "Star Trek" - that he gained mainstream fame, acting into his 80s.
"Make ​it so," his character Picard often said, instructing a subordinate to carry out a command, or sometimes deploying the similar catch phrase, "Engage."
It was a role he had debated even taking after his longtime ​friend and fellow Shakespearean Ian McKellen advised him to spurn "Star Trek" and remain in theater. Stewart did take the role and became both a fan favorite and an ⁠indispensable part of a lucrative sci-fi franchise, playing Picard not only in 176 episodes over seven seasons of that series but also in several "Star Trek" films and in the later streaming series "Star Trek: Picard" that began ​airing in 2020 when he was 79.
"As the seven seasons of TNG ("The Next Generation") went by, the distinction between Jean-Luc Picard and Patrick Stewart became thinner and thinner, until I couldn't know where he ​left off and I began. So much of what I believed and felt went into that show," Stewart told the Guardian newspaper in 2022.
Stewart also initially balked at being cast as the wheelchair-using mutant Professor X in the "X-Men" movies, based on the popular Marvel comic book character.
"I said, 'Look, I know this isn't science fiction, but it's fantasy, and I've done that.' But they persuaded me that it wouldn't be like 'Star Trek,' so I did it. And yet again I was proved wrong," Stewart told the ​Guardian.
He became a critical part of another big-money franchise starting with the first entry "X-Men" in 2000 and followed by several more.
Acting was safe space
Stewart was born on July 13, 1940, in the English town of Mirfield in ​Yorkshire. He was raised in poverty, with a father who he said returned from World War Two an alcoholic who suffered from post-traumatic stress syndrome and physically abused Stewart's mother. Stewart recalled putting his body between his father and mother ‌to try to ⁠protect her.
As a child, Stewart said, acting became a "safe space" after a schoolteacher introduced him to Shakespeare - specifically "The Merchant of Venice" - during a class when he was 12. He started losing his hair at age 17 and was bald by 19. He was embarrassed at the time, but eventually embraced it.
"Star Trek," created by Gene Roddenberry, presented a hopeful vision of the future, with humankind venturing into the cosmos in spaceships exceeding the speed of light and encountering alien races. The enduring popularity of the original series and the success of spinoff films prompted Roddenberry to create "The Next Generation" sequel series.
The Picard character was the opposite of the swashbuckling and sometimes unintentionally buffoonish Captain ​James T. Kirk, played by William Shatner, of the ​original series - envisioned as more cerebral and disciplined, ⁠though sometimes coming across as stuffy, humorless, or self-important.
The handprints, footprints and signature in cement of actor Patrick Stewart are pictured at a ceremony in the forecourt of the TCL Chinese Theatre in Los Angeles, California, US, January 13, 2020. Photo: Reuters
Stewart recalled being a little bit too serious toward his castmates early on.
"I tell the story of calling a meeting of my principal fellow cast members and telling them that I thought we were not disciplined enough, that we should not be fooling about on the set ​as much as we were but taking everything seriously," Stewart told the New Yorker in 2023.
"And one of the cast members said, 'Oh, come on, Patrick, we've ​got to have some fun.' ⁠And I thumped the chair and said, 'We are not here to have fun' - which they have never let me forget. They taught me so much about loosening up and being freer," Stewart added.
Stewart also felt the series improved as it went along, faulting his own portrayal of Picard in the first two seasons.
"I found it lacking intimacy. It was very authoritative, but there were few other qualities in him," Stewart said, adding that his work got better in subsequent seasons.
Actor Patrick Stewart poses with his knighthood after he was knighted by Britain's Queen Elizabeth at Buckingham Palace in London June 2, 2010. Photo: Reuters
In ⁠fact, the ​finest work for the entire cast may have been the two-part, time-bending series finale.
He became Sir Patrick Stewart when he was knighted ​by the queen at Buckingham Palace in 2010. He told reporters that his heroes were British actors Laurence Olivier, John Gielgud and Alec Guinness, who also had been knighted, adding that being "in that company is the grandest thing that has professionally happened to me".
Stewart was married ​three times and had two children. His third marriage, in 2013, was to American musician Sunny Ozell.

items.author: Danial Saigra
items.content:
International students, including those from Pakistan, have until October 31, 2026, to apply for a fully funded PhD graduate assistantship at the University of Florida in the United States, offering an annual salary of $30,000 along with tuition coverage and additional benefits.
The opportunity is available in fisheries ecosystem modeling and focuses on research related to marine ecosystems, fisheries management, and environmental changes.
The selected student will join the University of Florida’s Institute of Food and Agricultural Sciences (UF/IFAS) Nature Coast Biological Station and work under the supervision of Dr. David Chagaris.
The research will also provide opportunities to collaborate with scientists and faculty members from the University of Florida and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA).
According to the published scholarship details, the PhD program is expected to begin in 2027, while applications will close at the end of October 2026.
Scholarship Benefits
The University of Florida graduate assistantship provides an annual salary of $30,000 to the selected PhD student.
In addition to the yearly salary, the position includes tuition coverage and other benefits, making it a fully funded graduate research opportunity.
The selected candidate will conduct research at the UF/IFAS Nature Coast Biological Station, where the work will focus on fisheries ecosystem modeling and natural resource management.
The assistantship also provides opportunities to work with researchers from the University of Florida and NOAA on scientific projects related to fisheries and marine ecosystems.
Research Areas and Program Details
The PhD position focuses on ecosystem modeling and quantitative analysis to address challenges affecting fisheries and natural resources.
The selected student will develop ecosystem models and conduct quantitative research to understand how fish populations and marine ecosystems respond to fishing activities and environmental changes.
The research will support ecosystem-based fisheries management in the Gulf of Mexico and the southeastern United States.
The project may cover several environmental and fisheries-related topics, including climate change, habitat conditions, water quality, forage fisheries, harmful algal blooms, invasive species, and fisheries productivity.
The research aims to improve scientific understanding of marine ecosystems and provide information that can support fisheries and natural resource management decisions.
The selected candidate will pursue a PhD through either the School of Forest, Fisheries, and Geomatics Sciences or the School of Natural Resources and Environment at the University of Florida.
Who Can Apply
The scholarship listing includes applicants from several countries, including Pakistan, India, Bangladesh, Nepal, Sri Lanka, China, and other nations.
The opportunity is intended for students interested in pursuing doctoral research in ecology, fisheries, aquatic sciences, and related disciplines.
The position particularly focuses on fisheries ecosystem modeling, quantitative analysis, natural resource management, and marine ecosystem research.
According to the scholarship snapshot, the listed academic requirement is a minimum GPA of 3.0.
The published information also lists an IELTS score of 6.5 or a TOEFL iBT score of 80 as English-language requirements.
However, the detailed position description does not specify all academic qualifications or eligibility conditions. Interested candidates should therefore confirm the requirements with the university before applying.
Required Documents
According to the published scholarship information, applicants are expected to submit academic transcripts and previous degree certificates as part of the application process.
Candidates must also prepare an application essay and two recommendation letters. The documents will form part of the application for the PhD graduate assistantship.
Applicants should review the university’s official admission and application guidelines to confirm the complete documentation requirements.
How to Apply for the University of Florida Scholarship
Interested candidates should review the graduate research opportunity and application requirements before submitting their applications.
The selected PhD student will work under Dr. David Chagaris at the UF/IFAS Nature Coast Biological Station.
The candidate will pursue doctoral studies through either the School of Forest, Fisheries, and Geomatics Sciences or the School of Natural Resources and Environment.
Applicants should prepare their academic documents and confirm the application procedure with the relevant university department or research supervisor.

Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Pak Telecom Mobile Limited (PTML)’s brand, Telenor Pakistan has secured the No. 1 position for the third consecutive year in Cybersecurity Excellence at the Telecom Cyber Security Awards 2026, hosted by the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA). The award reinforces company’s steadfast focus on regulatory compliance and the protection of critical telecom data and infrastructure.
Federal Minister for IT and Telecommunication, Shaza Fatima Khawaja presented the award to PTML Chief Technology Officer, Awais Vohra, and Chief Corporate Affairs Officer, Shan Haq, at a ceremony attended by senior government officials, the PTA Chairman, and leaders from the telecommunications and technology industries.
The award follows PTA’s rigorous audit and revalidation process, which recorded one of the highest compliance scores in the industry for Telenor Pakistan under the Critical Telecom Data and Infrastructure Security Regulations (CTDISR). The score highlights the consistency of the company’s cybersecurity governance and its efforts to maintain robust security standards across its operations.
As telecommunications networks underpin an increasingly connected digital economy, safeguarding critical infrastructure and protecting data remain essential to maintaining the reliability and resilience of digital services. Ufone and Telenor Pakistan’s continued efforts in this area set a strong precedent for the industry.
Commenting on the achievement, Awais Vohra, Chief Technology Officer, PTML, said, “Cybersecurity is fundamental to building trust in a hyper-connected society like ours. We are thrilled to secure the top position for the third consecutive year, in recognition of our robust security standards, compliance with regulatory requirements, and efforts to protect critical telecom data and infrastructure. We remain committed to contributing to a more secure and resilient digital environment in the country.”
The award highlights the broader importance of cybersecurity in strengthening trust in Pakistan’s telecommunications sector, as digital connectivity becomes increasingly central to businesses, institutions, and everyday life of users nationwide.

items.author: Akshit Pushkarna
items.content:
Fino Payments Bank posted a second consecutive quarter of loss in Q2 FY27, reporting a net loss of ₹20.9 Cr against a net profit of ₹15.4 Cr in the year-ago period.
This is the second consecutive loss making quarter for the company after the operational disruptions it faced in February. Net loss widened 52.3% from ₹13.7 Cr loss incurred in the previous quarter.
The company attributed the losses to revenue decline, margin compression and the impact of depreciation.
“… Profitability dipped due to margin compression and the depreciation impact of our core banking migration. While these investments may pressure short-term earnings, we remain committed to building a resilient and sustainable bank through product innovation, financial discipline, and targeted growth,” said Fino Payments Bank’s interim CFO Anup Agarwal.
The losses came as the company’s total income for the quarter declined 16.6% to ₹333.6 Cr from ₹400.1 Cr in the year-ago quarter. It increased 8.7% from ₹306.9 Cr in the preceding June quarter.
Fino’s other income, which includes fees and commissions from its banking and payment services, declined 23.8% to ₹259.2 Cr from ₹339.9 Cr in Q2 FY26. The company also earned ₹74.5 Cr in interest from investments, balance with RBI and advances in Q2 FY27, up 24% YoY.
EBITDA tanked 43% to ₹35.1 Cr in Q2 FY27 as against ₹61.6 Cr in the year-ago quarter. The payments bank attributed this to investments in technology, infrastructure, talent and operational capabilities. On similar lines, EBITDA margin also contracted to 10.5% from 15.4% in Q2 FY26.
Meanwhile, Fino’s total expenditure, excluding provisions and contingencies, declined 6.4% YoY to ₹354.5 Cr in the quarter under review from ₹378.8 Cr in Q2 FY26.
In the quarter, the company’s digital payment services business remained non-operational and contributed nil revenue in Q2 FY27. This wiped off a key top line driver. For context, the vertical accounted for 16%, or ₹63.4 Cr, of Fino’s total revenue in the year-ago quarter. It now plans to relaunch the service by Q4 FY27.
Giving a breakdown of its revenue, Fino said that current accounts and savings accounts (CASA) accounted for 52% (₹174 Cr) of its top line in Q2 FY27, while transaction business contributed 17% (₹54.9 Cr). Cash management services contributed another 8% (₹26 Cr) to Fino’s Q2 FY27 revenue.
On the operational front, the payments bank opened 8.2 Lakh new current and savings accounts during the quarter. With this, the total number of CASAs under its belt grew 20% YoY to 19.1 Cr at the end of September 2026.
As per Fino’s investor presentation, the average total deposits on its platform zoomed 34% YoY to ₹2,490 Cr during the quarter under review. The number of digitally-active customers also rose 13% YoY to 64.9 Lakh in Q2 FY27.
Overall, Fino processed 92.8 Cr digital transactions during the quarter under review, up 6% YoY, worth ₹64,023 Cr, up 2% YoY. It had also deployed soundboxed at 5,383 merchants at the end of September 2026, which processed payments worth ₹17.3 Cr in Q2 FY27.
Fino’s loan referral segment, which it sees as a pilot for its proposed small finance bank (SFB), saw disbursals surge 286% YoY to ₹762 Cr, while the number of borrowers rose a marginal 5.5% to 10,467.
On the SFB front, the company said that it has onboarded senior leadership across areas such as branch banking, liabilities, MSME and credit risk. It also claims to be deploying the necessary technology and infrastructure to meet the SFB requirements.
“The Bank is in (the) consolidation phase and is working towards strengthening its core retail business and restoring growth momentum in B2B businesses. Further, growth in referral loan business is a testimony towards our preparation for future transition and validation of our differentiated SFB model,” said Fino’s interim CEO Ketan Merchant.
Shares of Fino ended Thursday’s trading session 1.03% higher at ₹123.05 apiece on the BSE.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
DoorDash said on Thursday it would buy Instacart ​in a deal valued at about $17 billion, stepping up its push into the fast-growing US grocery delivery market as competition intensifies among app-based ‌platforms.
The deal, DoorDash's biggest yet, will give the company greater scale as it expands beyond restaurant delivery into groceries and other retail categories, helping it take on deep-pocketed retailers such as Walmart and Amazon, which have built vast store, warehouse and delivery networks.
"Grocery is one of the hardest things to get right online," said Tony Xu, co-founder and CEO of ​DoorDash, adding Instacart has spent years learning to do that well for grocers.
Read: Online grocery shopping gains traction
Instacart founder Apoorva Mehta said the two companies had explored a ​combination on and off for years.
DoorDash has struck a deal to buy food-delivery rival Instacart for about $17 billion in cash and stock, adding a major grocery delivery partner to its growing roster of services https://t.co/yzbSLYejuV
— The Wall Street Journal (@WSJ) October 29, 2026
The companies began talks about a potential deal over the summer, and in early ⁠September, Instacart's CEO signalled to DoorDash's CEO that the company was exploring strategic alternatives, according to a source familiar with the matter.
Instacart also held preliminary ​deal talks with Uber, but the ride-hailing company ultimately did not pursue a transaction, in part because it had announced a $14.8 billion acquisition of German food ​delivery platform Delivery Hero just a few months earlier, the source said.
DoorDash and Instacart did not immediately respond to Reuters' request for details regarding when the deal talks began.
"Restaurant delivery is maturing, and growth now lies in more frequent, higher-value orders: weekly grocery shops, convenience items, and retail," said Martin Szumski, analyst at Morningstar.
Meanwhile, consolidation has gathered pace globally as companies ​navigate an environment of slowing orders, rising costs and tighter regulatory scrutiny of the treatment of gig workers.
Online grocery delivery has gained traction as consumers increasingly ​prize convenience. Spiking gasoline prices during the war in Iran could give shoppers another reason to avoid trips to stores.
AI-native companies have been disrupting the way consumers shop online. More shoppers have been ‌making purchases ⁠using agentic AI platforms such as Meta's Muse and personal assistant app Instinct.
Inside the deal
DoorDash has offered Instacart shareholders $65 per share held, a premium of about 26% to the stock's closing price on October 22 before reports of deal talks first emerged.
The consideration will be at least 75% cash, with Instacart shareholders able to elect cash, DoorDash stock or a combination of the two, the companies said.
Shares of Instacart, formally known as Maplebear, were flat at $58.35 in early ​trading. They had hit a record high ​of $62 on Monday.
DoorDash shares jumped ⁠nearly 6% after the company also reported better-than-expected quarterly revenue. They have declined about 25% so far this year through their last close.
Regulatory hurdles loom
The transaction is expected to close at the end of 2027 or the first half ​of 2028.
"The main risk is regulatory approval," analysts at CFRA Research said in a note, adding that the ​long timeline for the ⁠closing of the transaction suggests both sides expect an extended antitrust review.
"The current regulatory backdrop is generally favourable, but the long closing window leaves the deal exposed to changes in policy," they added.
New York City's Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP) said on Wednesday that a potential merger continued a "troubling trend" of corporate consolidation.
DoorDash agreed to buy rival Instacart in a deal that values the company at about $17 billion, the latest sign of consolidation in an increasingly competitive delivery market where Walmart Inc. and Amazon loom large https://t.co/RQcEkT0flf pic.twitter.com/8XO44otQtS
— Bloomberg TV (@BloombergTV) October 29, 2026
DoorDash ⁠plans to retain ​Instacart's brand and app after the deal closes and combine the companies' membership programs, while ​pledging not to require grocers to use its delivery services exclusively.
Instacart would be required to pay DoorDash a termination fee of $650 million, while DoorDash would have to pay $1.25 billion if the deal ​is ended under certain circumstances, according to a regulatory filing.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Eutelsat (ETL.PA) expects commercial ‌services revenue of more than €10 billion ($11.1 billion) between 2032 and 2040 as it takes a leading role in the European Union's planned alternative to Elon Musk's Starlink satellite internet service, ​it said on Thursday.
The Franco-British operator had been chosen to lead ​the low Earth orbit (LEO) segment of the EU's IRIS² network that ⁠will feature 330 satellites. The first IRIS² satellites are scheduled for launch ​in 2029, with initial services expected from 2030.
Eutelsat has gained prominence as Europe tries ​to reduce the bloc's reliance on US technology after President Donald Trump's return to office, since it owns OneWeb, the only LEO satellite network alternative to SpaceX's (SPCX.O) Starlink. 
In a trading ​update, the Paris-based company said its backlog now includes €8.9 billion of revenue ​from designing and building IRIS², to be recognised primarily between 2027 and 2031. That alone ‌is ⁠more than seven times the €1.24 billion of revenue Eutelsat generated last year, and lifts its total backlog to €12.1 billion from €3.4 billion at end-June.
The forecast is a major boost for a company aiming to offset its waning video broadcasting business with ​satellite internet services.
OneWeb has ​more than 600 ⁠satellites and 229 more are planned in a €1 billion expansion.
Eutelsat said it will invest a combined €3.39 billion in shared ​and commercial infrastructure on the IRIS² network between 2027 and ​2034, ⁠in return for access to more than twice OneWeb's current bandwidth.
Despite the upbeat outlook, first-quarter revenue fell short of expectations. Revenue from its four operating businesses fell ⁠2.1% like-for-like ​to €278.3 million in the three months to ​end-September. That was below the €291 million average of a company-compiled analyst poll.
Eutelsat confirmed its financial targets for ​2026-27 and 2028-29.

items.author: Shrishti Bisht
items.content:
Update | October 29, 19:45 IST
A week after the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) took action against seven ecommerce platforms over listings of unauthorised hazardous explosives, the regulator has now imposed an ₹10 Lakh fine on Justdial.
In an exchange filing today, Justdial said it received an order dated October 28 imposing the penalty for listing and hosting ammonium nitrate, a regulated and hazardous substance, on its platform.
The order also directed the company to immediately remove listings of ammonium nitrate and any other substance classified as an explosive under the Explosives Act, 1884, or other applicable laws.
Justdial said it had discontinued the listings and was reviewing the order. It added that the financial impact would be limited to the penalty amount, with no impact on its operations or other activities.
Original | October 20, 16:42 IST
The Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has taken regulatory action against seven ecommerce platforms, including IndiaMART and Justdial, over the listing and sales of unauthorised hazardous explosives.
The material listed on these platforms included ammonium nitrate, gun powder, picric acid and pentaerythritol tetranitrate (PETN).
Except for ammonium nitrate, all of the aforementioned chemicals are exclusively used in manufacturing explosives.
The regulatory action has resulted in the delisting of 3,940 sellers and listing entries, while the authority has imposed penalties totalling ₹30 Lakh on Dial4Trade and ExportersIndia, the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution said in a statement yesterday.
IndiaMART accounted for the highest number of affected sellers and listings, with 3,092, followed by ExportersIndia with 421, Justdial with 206 and TradeIndia with 166, according to the ministry. Other platforms facing regulatory action include Dial4Trade, Sigma-Aldrich India and Ibuychemikals.
In its statement, the consumer protection body shared that it had issued notices to both Justdial and IndiaMART over the listings. Following the notices, Director General – Investigation investigated the matter and shared their reports with the companies.
IndiaMART submitted its reply to the investigation report and, subsequently, approached the Delhi High Court challenging the SCN issued by the CCPA. Meanwhile, Justdial has sought adjournments in the matter till now and is yet to respond to the investigation. The next and final hearing in the matter is scheduled to be held on October 23.
Meanwhile, the CCPA has imposed a penalty of ₹10 Lakh on Dial4Trade for facilitating the sale of ammonium nitrate. ExportersIndia was fined ₹10 Lakh in two separate cases, one involving ammonium nitrate and Pentaerythritol Tetranitrate (PETN), and the other involving picric acid.
The CCPA’s action covers both marketplaces that host third-party sellers and platforms that sell products directly. Sigma-Aldrich Chemicals and Ibuychemikals have told the authority that they sell their own products and do not host third-party sellers. Investigations into TradeIndia, Sigma-Aldrich Chemicals and Ibuychemikals are ongoing.
Dial4Trade challenged the order before the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (NCDRC), which dismissed its appeal on October 9. The commission held that the listings amounted to misleading advertisements and unfair trade practices under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.
ExportersIndia has also appealed against the CCPA’s orders before the NCDRC. The appeals are expected to be listed for hearing in the coming period.
Consumers can report listings of explosives on online platforms through the national consumer helpline at 1915.
Under the Explosives Act, 1884, the sale and purchase of these substances require prescribed licences. The CCPA expects platforms to ensure sellers display valid licences issued by the petroleum and explosives safety organisation (PESO) and verify buyers’ identities and licence status before allowing purchases.
“The action reinforces the Government’s commitment to ensuring that digital marketplaces do not facilitate unauthorised access to regulated or dangerous substances in violation of applicable laws and consumer safety standards,” the ministry said.

items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
High-speed diesel (HSD) snuck past the Rs400 mark on Thursday after the federal government increased its price by 85 paisas per litre while keeping petrol unchanged for October 30.
According to a notification issued by the Petroleum Division, petrol would continue to be sold at Rs377.91 per litre, while HSD would cost Rs400.67 per litre on Friday.
The latest revision comes a day after the government increased the price of petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs1.85 and Rs1.75 per litre, respectively, for October 29.
Read: Govt increases petrol by Rs1.85, diesel by Rs1.75 for Oct 29
On July 17, the government announced a new pricing mechanism under which petroleum product prices would be reviewed and notified daily, replacing the weekly pricing mechanism, as renewed tensions between the United States and Iran continued to drive volatility in global oil markets and raise concerns over fuel supplies.
On September 13, PM Shehbaz announced a special relief scheme offering Rs100 per litre off petrol for motorcycles, three-wheeler rickshaws and cars with engines up to 800cc, in an attempt to shield lower-income consumers from the impact of rising petroleum prices.
Under the proposal, an estimated 11.8 million beneficiaries would be covered. Around 10 million two-wheeler users and 800,000 three-wheeler users would be entitled to relief on 20 litres of fuel per month, translating into a maximum monthly benefit of Rs2,000 per beneficiary.
Another one million users of cars up to 800cc would receive relief on 30 litres per month, providing them with a maximum benefit of Rs3,000 each.
On Sept 17, the government reintroduced austerity and fuel conservation measures amid rising fuel prices, tightening business operating hours and restricting public events.
Under the measures, notified with immediate effect, shops, markets, shopping malls, bazaars, departmental stores, grocery stores, general stores and kiryana shops would close by 9pm throughout the week, according to a notification issued by the Cabinet Division.
Marriage halls, marquees and other commercial venues hosting festive events would close by 10pm, while restaurants, cafes, eateries, food outlets and standalone fruit and vegetable shops would be allowed to operate until 11pm. Takeaway and home delivery services would remain exempt from the timing restrictions.
Global geopolitical developments continue to pose significant risks. International oil prices are influenced by decisions taken by OPEC+, conflicts in the Middle East, sanctions on oil-producing nations, and disruptions in critical shipping routes such as the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea. Any interruption in these supply chains can immediately increase crude oil prices and freight costs. Since Pakistan imports the majority of its petroleum requirements, these developments quickly translate into higher domestic fuel prices.
Oil prices fell on Thursday in a choppy session as hopes for peace ​talks between the US and Iran offset some concerns over Middle East supply disruptions from an escalating regional conflict.
Brent crude ‌futures were down 40 cents, or 0.35%, to $114.92 a barrel by 1:35 pm EDT. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures were down 66 cents, or 0.64%, at $102.12.
The Yemeni army targeted Saudi Aramco in a massive wave of missile ​attacks, according to a media report.
Those reports of a new spate of attacks helped oil recoup some losses later in the session, said ​John Kilduff, partner at Again Capital.
Earlier, US Vice President JD Vance sought to revive peace negotiations by sending a ⁠letter to Mohsen Rezaei, the head of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, the Wall Street Journal said on Wednesday, citing US officials and people familiar with ​the matter.
"Oil prices are under pressure today amid renewed diplomatic efforts to de-escalate the conflict in the Middle East," UBS analyst Giovanni Staunovo said.

items.author: Shrishti Bisht
items.content:
For hardware and deeptech startups, the challenge does not end with a working prototype. Moving to commercial production requires manufacturing partners that can consistently meet technical specifications at scale.
Bengaluru-based Venttup is helping businesses bridge this gap. Founded in 2021 by Sandeep Nair, M. Wasim Ankli, and Joseph Panakkal, the startup combines in-house engineering with a network of manufacturing partners, primarily MSMEs, to support component development, testing, and production.
It has raised $3 Mn in a Pre-Series A round led by Rainmatter by Zerodha and Unicorn India Ventures. The capital will fund engineering hires, precision manufacturing and rapid prototyping infrastructure, and AI adoption for B2B sourcing, supplier intelligence, and operational efficiency.
From Prototypes To Production
Venttup works with original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), technology companies, and deeptech startups, including businesses seeking domestic alternatives to imported components.
Customers can approach it with designs or component requirements. Venttup coordinates engineering, supplier selection and qualification, prototype testing, quality inspections, and production.
Its capabilities span precision machining, casting and forging, sheet metal fabrication, box builds, special purpose machines, industrial automation, and robotics.
“India’s next phase of manufacturing growth requires strong engineering capabilities that can translate complex requirements into validated, production-ready components,” said cofounder and CEO Nair.
“At Venttup, we are building an engineering-first manufacturing startup that brings together design standardisation, rapid prototyping, testing and scalable production through India’s capable MSME ecosystem,” he added.
Venttup operates across four verticals: energy transition and data centres; aerospace, defence, and space systems; smart infrastructure and future mobility; and electronics, automation, and smart manufacturing.
Building A Commercial Base
Incubated at Kerala Startup Mission, Venttup’s founding team brings experience across Hitachi Energy, Siemens, L&T, and Kalpataru Power.
Since its undisclosed seed round in 2024, revenue has grown fivefold to ₹10 Cr in FY26, the startup said. It added more than 15 blue-chip customers over the past 12 months and built an approximately ₹30 Cr business opportunity pipeline across new energy, mobility, and smart infrastructure.
The fresh funding will help the startup expand its manufacturing capabilities and support customers from product development to production.
Venttup’s services overlap with Zetwerk’s precision manufacturing operations and CapGrid’s component sourcing, localisation, and manufacturing services. Karkhana is another peer in taking hardware products into production, with a stronger electronics manufacturing focus.
Inc42 Take: Can Venttup Become More Than A Sourcing Partner?
Venttup’s opportunity lies in taking responsibility for the engineering, validation, and manufacturing work that sits between a component design and commercial production. Its planned Bengaluru facility could give it greater control over this process, while its MSME network offers access to a wider range of manufacturing capabilities.
The test is whether customers see lasting value in keeping Venttup involved once a component is validated and production stabilises. Consistent quality, delivery, and support for subsequent product development will matter more than access to suppliers alone.
Winning repeat production contracts will be the clearest test of whether Venttup can become a long-term manufacturing partner rather than a supplier customers use only during product development.

items.author: AFP
items.content:
New York has become the latest US state to crack down on artificial intelligence companies, passing sweeping new restrictions that prevent chatbots from acting as companions to children.
Governor Kathy Hochul signed the law on Wednesday, making New York one of the first states to impose broad limits on how AI tools can interact with young users.
The new rules force chatbot operators like OpenAI’s ChatGPT to verify users’ ages and strip back features when someone under 18 logs on. The technology cannot pretend to be human, alive or capable of feeling emotions. It also cannot suggest it has a personal or professional relationship with the user, or present itself as an authority figure.
Read: How teachers are remaking classrooms for the AI age
Chatbots will also be banned from framing their responses as personal opinions when used by minors.
“No longer will minors have access to chatbots that pretend to be their friends, boyfriends and girlfriends,” Hochul said at Wednesday’s signing ceremony. “No longer will chatbots be able to keep sensitive information about a minor’s emotional and physical health.”
While California and other states have passed similar measures, New York’s law uses some of the broadest language yet to regulate the technology. That has drawn criticism from the tech industry.
Tech: NYC, an advocacy group representing the sector in New York, aimed criticism at what it called the law’s “vague language”.
Keeping kids safe online should not mean cutting them off from tools that help them learn and prepare for careers.
The bill @GovKathyHochul signed could restrict access to tutoring, homework help, coding assistants, and critical career platforms, while putting more children’s… https://t.co/nfdbQGbhEd
— Tech:NYC (@TechNYC) October 28, 2026
“Keeping kids safe online should not mean cutting them off from tools that help them learn and prepare for careers,” the group said in a statement
AI giants OpenAI and Anthropic both declined to comment when contacted by AFP.
But Common Sense Media, a nonprofit that provides parents with guidance on age-appropriate content, praised the move. The group called it “the strongest kids’ AI safety bill in the country”.
“AI companies offer chatbots with features that are dangerous, and even deadly, for kids and teens,” said Jim Steyer, the organisation’s chief executive. “Now, those harmful features will be outlawed in New York.”

items.title: FCC votes to ban all Chinese labs from testing US electronics
items.summary:
The Federal Communications Commission on Thursday voted to bar all Chinese ​labs from testing electronic devices, including smartphones, cameras and computers for use ‌in the US, expanding a previous agency action targeting Beijing.
The FCC said it will prohibit test labs and certification bodies in countries including China that deny reciprocal treatment to US-based test labs. The FCC prohibitions are slated ​to take effect in December 2028. FCC Chair Brendan Carr said that in 2025, 82% ​of electronics were tested in China, which does not have an agreement ⁠with the US.
"These labs are a critical gateway into American communications infrastructure -- and their privileged ​role gives them access to sensitive and confidential information about electronic products often months before ​the devices enter the market," Carr said, adding they could "allow insecure gear into the US market, disrupt communications networks, or even steal intellectual property."

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
The Federal Communications Commission on Thursday voted to bar all Chinese ​labs from testing electronic devices, including smartphones, cameras and computers for use ‌in the US, expanding a previous agency action targeting Beijing.
The FCC said it will prohibit test labs and certification bodies in countries including China that deny reciprocal treatment to US-based test labs. The FCC prohibitions are slated ​to take effect in December 2028. FCC Chair Brendan Carr said that in 2025, 82% ​of electronics were tested in China, which does not have an agreement ⁠with the US.
"These labs are a critical gateway into American communications infrastructure -- and their privileged ​role gives them access to sensitive and confidential information about electronic products often months before ​the devices enter the market," Carr said, adding they could "allow insecure gear into the US market, disrupt communications networks, or even steal intellectual property."
Read: US banning Chinese AI DeepSeek from government agency IT systems
The Chinese Embassy in Washington did not immediately respond to a ​request for comment.
In 2025, the FCC banned testing of US electronics by labs owned or controlled by ​the Chinese government, and several dozen labs were barred.
About 4% of all electronic devices are tested in labs in the US, Carr said.
Separately, the FCC streamlined its approval process for devices tested in US labs or in labs in countries that do not pose national security risks.
This is the latest move by Washington to crack down on China over technology issues and equipment.
In December, the FCC banned the ​import of all new ​models of Chinese drones ⁠and also banned imports of new models of Chinese-made consumer routers, the boxes connecting computers, phones and smart devices to the internet.
In July, ​the FCC voted to bar sales of devices in the US ​that contain key ⁠hardware from Chinese companies deemed to be national security risks.
The FCC maintains a list of firms, including Chinese telecom company Huawei and ZTE, whose equipment is barred for sale in ⁠the US ​due to national security concerns.
In June, the FCC ​banned the import of more equipment from a group of Chinese manufacturers, including Huawei and ZTE, and has ​proposed to ban the import of most military-grade drones.

items.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday said that Pakistan and Turkiye had transformed their historic ties into a "multifaceted strategic partnership", while stressing the need for stronger economic cooperation, investment and joint ventures between the two countries.
Addressing a dinner hosted at the residence of the Turkish ambassador in Islamabad to mark Turkiye’s 103rd Republic Day, PM Shehbaz said Turkiye had stood firmly alongside Pakistan when it had faced Indian aggression during Marka-e-Haq in May 2025.
The premier noted: "Our historic friendship has matured into a multifaceted strategic partnership spanning political dialogue, trade and investment, defence, education, culture and people-to-people ties."
Read: Pakistan, Turkiye to deepen ties
PM Sharif addresses Turkiye's 103rd Republic Day Ceremony https://t.co/5XRicmdAga
— Pakistan TV (@PakTVGlobal) October 29, 2026
“Last year, during Marka-e-Haq, when Pakistan faced flagrant aggression from India and our sovereignty was put to a great test, Turkiye stood firmly by our side with unwavering commitment and dedication,” he stated.
#BREAKING
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif says the Makkah Defence Agreement strengthens collective deterrence. Speaking at celebrations marking Turkiye’s 103rd Republic Day, he praised Ankara’s steadfast support during the May 2025 war with India and its assistance during… pic.twitter.com/WagmuFGbOe
— Pakistan TV (@PakTVGlobal) October 29, 2026
The premier added that the Makkah agreement, signed on August 7 by Pakistan, Turkiye and Saudi Arabia, marked an important milestone between the two countries, further adding that the agreement "strengthened collective deterrence" and reaffirmed the shared commitment to regional peace and stability.
“While we strengthen our defences, we continue to champion dialogue, diplomacy, respect for international law and the peaceful settlement of disputes,” he remarked.
The premier underlined that Pakistan and Turkiye maintained cooperation in economic, trade, educational, cultural and defence sectors, further adding that Turkiye was playing a leading role in various fields, including defence technologies.
#BREAKING
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif hails the deep fraternal bonds between Pakistan and Turkiye, saying Turkiye has emerged as an economic powerhouse on the world stage. Addressing a ceremony marking Turkiye’s 103rd Republic Day, he extends warm congratulations to the… pic.twitter.com/KvHA5hW89H
— Pakistan TV (@PakTVGlobal) October 29, 2026
PM Shehbaz underscored that the economic relationship must now "rise to the level of the two countries’ political and strategic ties", urging Turkish business leaders to explore investment opportunities in Pakistan.
“Our economic partnership must now match the height of our political and strategic bond,” he stated.
While recalling his announcement at the Pakistan-Turkiye Business Conference in Istanbul in July, PM Shehbaz said Pakistan had proposed establishing the President Tayyip Erdogan Special Economic Zone in Karachi to encourage Turkish investment.
The premier invited Turkish businessmen to explore Pakistan’s investment potential, adding that Pakistan had a young population, strategic location and growing economic opportunities.
Read More: Pakistan, Turkiye set $5b trade target
“Let us translate the goodwill between our two peoples into joint ventures, shared prosperity and meaningful jobs for our young people,” he added.
“Pakistan and Turkiye are two bodies with one soul,” the premier remarked at the conclusion of his speech.
In an earlier post on X, PM Shehbaz said the two countries shared an exceptional bond of brotherhood, rooted in common history, mutual trust and unwavering solidarity.
"Our enduring friendship, which continues to expand in scope and substance, transcends borders and generations, strengthened by our shared values and common aspirations. As we join the people of Türkiye to celebrate this momentous occasion, I am confident that Pakistan and Türkiye will continue to work together to advance peace and stability in our region and beyond."
On the 103rd anniversary of the founding of the Republic of Türkiye, I extend my heartfelt felicitations to my very dear brother, President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, the Government and the brotherly people of Türkiye.
Türkiye’s proud history, rich heritage and remarkable journey as…
— Shehbaz Sharif (@CMShehbaz) October 29, 2026
Turkish Republic Day felicitations
Meanwhile, President Zardari emphasised the importance of strengthening Pakistan’s "historic partnership" with Turkiye through closer cooperation in trade, investment, defence, education, culture and other areas of mutual interest.
In a statement on X, the Office of the president said that President Zardari highlighted the "exceptional bond of brotherhood between the two countries, rooted in common history, faith, shared values and enduring ties between their peoples".
President Zardari Highlights Pakistan-Türkiye Brotherhood and Defence Cooperation on Republic Day
President Asif Ali Zardari has emphasised the importance of strengthening Pakistan’s historic partnership with Türkiye through closer cooperation in trade, investment, defence,… pic.twitter.com/JOVlhHgVrI
— The President of Pakistan (@PresOfPakistan) October 28, 2026
According to the statement, President Zardari said that Pakistan deeply valued the solidarity and generous support extended by the Turkish leadership and people during challenging times, further expressing confidence that the historic partnership between the two countries would continue to flourish through enhanced political engagement and closer cooperation across areas of mutual interest.
"Referring to the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, the President expressed confidence that the agreement would further strengthen bilateral and trilateral relations, deepen strategic cooperation among Pakistan, Türkiye and Saudi Arabia and contribute to lasting peace, security and stability in the region and beyond," it further added.
Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari also congratulated President Erdogan and the Turkish people on the "completion of 103 years since the establishment of the Republic of Turkey".
In a post on X, Bilawal said that in Pakistan, the name of Turkey was always uttered with a special affection, adding that "this sense of kinship" was our precious asset, and that it was his "wish that every new generation of both countries contribute to this love".
پاکستان میں ترکیہ کا نام ہمیشہ ایک خاص محبت سے لیا جاتا ہے، جیسے کسی اپنے کا ذکر ہو، یہ اپنائیت ہمارا قیمتی اثاثہ ہے اور میری خواہش ہے کہ دونوں ملکوں کی ہر نئی نسل اس محبت میں اپنا حصہ ڈالے، جمہوریہ ترکیہ کے قیام کے 103 برس مکمل ہونے پر صدر رجب طیب اردوان اور ترک عوام کو مبارک…
— Bilawal Bhutto Zardari (@BBhuttoZardari) October 29, 2026
He added: "Today, we Pakistanis are also sharing in the joys of the Turkish people. Although the colors of our flags are different, seeing the bright moon and stars on both evokes a single prayer from the heart: may both homelands remain safe, and may the people of both countries live with their heads held high."
Pakistan-Turkiye bilateral relations
Pakistan and Turkiye share comprehensive bilateral relations that encompass political, economic, cultural and military domains.
On October 21, Pakistan, Turkiye, Qatar, and Indonesia signed an agreement to boost defence cooperation and strengthen defensive capabilities. 
The Turkish Defence Ministry said the Badr accord would strengthen ties between the countries' defence industries and bolster collaboration to promote security and achieve shared objectives.
On August 7, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye formalised their longstanding strategic relationship through the newly signed Makkah Joint Defence Agreement (MJDA). Islamabad and Ankara maintain close defence ties through military training, naval cooperation and defence equipment.
On July 5, Pakistan and Turkey expressed their commitment to increase bilateral trade volume to $5 billion and discussed ways to increase bilateral trade and investment in special economic zones.
Erdogan stated that Turkiye aimed to deepen cooperation with Pakistan in energy, transport, critical minerals, information technology and defence.
On June 26, Pakistan and Turkiye signed three memorandums of understanding (MoUs) aimed at promoting institutional cooperation, strengthening technical collaboration and enhancing the exchange of knowledge between their energy sector institutions.
The MoUs cover cooperation on post-privatisation governance frameworks, electricity market development and regulations governing ancillary services. They will also promote training programmes, study visits and joint projects between the relevant institutions.

items.content:
A delegation of the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) and Tehreek-e-Tahafuz-e-Ayin-e-Pakistan (TTAP) on Thursday expressed full support for Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman’s speech in the National Assembly and condemned what it described as his character assassination by government ministers following their strong criticism.
During today's NA session, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi and Defence Minister Khawaja Asif unleashed a barrage of criticism on the JUI-F chief for remarks about Asif's absence from talks in Tehran, saying no defence agreement was being negotiated there. The minister's remarks came a day after Fazl criticised Asif in the NA, questioning the government's role in discussions related to the Makkah defence pact in Tehran while the prime minister and defence minister remained in Pakistan.
In a statement shared on X, former National Assembly speaker Asad Qaiser said a delegation comprising him, PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan and TTAP spokesperson Hussain Ahmad Yousafzai met Fazl at his residence in Islamabad.
"The visiting delegation expressed full support for Maulana Fazlur Rehman's speech in the National Assembly and strongly condemned the character assassination of the Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam chief by government ministers," the statement said.
It added that the delegation stated that turning political differences into personal attacks and character assassination was contrary to democratic values, and that respect for political leadership must be upheld in all circumstances.
چیئرمین پاکستان تحریک انصاف بیرسٹر گوہر خان، سابق اسپیکر قومی اسمبلی اسد قیصر اور ترجمان تحریک تحفظ آئین پاکستان حسین احمد یوسفزئی پر مشتمل وفد نے امیر جمعیت علمائے اسلام مولانا فضل الرحمٰن سے ان کی رہائش گاہ پر ملاقات کی۔
ملاقات میں مہمان وفد نے قومی اسمبلی میں مولانا فضل… pic.twitter.com/gX4JEpKuqB
— Asad Qaiser (@AsadQaiserPTI) October 29, 2026
The meeting's members also condemned the imprisonment of former prime minister Imran Khan’s sisters, alleging that they were being deprived of basic rights and denied access to family and lawyers.
"The participants warned that if any unpleasant situation arises as a result of this conduct, full responsibility will fall on the relevant authorities."
They also jointly demanded the public appearance of suspended Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, K-P Assembly Speaker Babar Saleem Swati and PTI K-P President Junaid Akbar Khan.
The latest exchange comes amid an escalating war of words between the government and opposition leaders over the political and security situation in K-P.
In mid-October, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi took a swipe at JUI-F chief Maulana Fazl over his opposition to the imposition of governor's rule in the province, suggesting that the religious-political leader was unhappy at not being offered a role in the new provincial setup.
Other government figures, including Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz, also assailed his stance, with allegations that he was supporting people accused of backing terrorism.
Federal ministers once again took to task the JUI-F chief on October 18, accusing Fazl of politicising the security situation and opposing measures they said were intended to combat terrorism.
Responding to the allegations, Fazl described the remarks as character assassination and maintained that his criticism was directed at government policies rather than state institutions. He then called for parliament to hold an in-camera session to examine the country's counterterrorism strategy.

items.content:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has fired US Army Lieutenant General Brett Sylvia, a senior military planner on the Pentagon's Joint Staff, over accusations he leaked classified information to the public, officials said on ​Thursday.
Sylvia's firing is one of the highest-profile consequences to date from Hegseth's sweeping hunt for officials suspected ‌of leaking information to the news media as the unpopular Iran war enters its ninth month.
Hegseth's effort includes a Pentagon task force to identify the source of leaks and the widespread use of polygraph exams on senior officials as part of these investigations.
Read: Trump's top general seeks path out of Iran war as military options narrow: report
Last year, he introduced a media policy ​that raised legal concerns among press organizations, and revoked the press credentials of journalists who refused to sign it.
A ​senior Pentagon official, speaking on condition of anonymity, accused Sylvia of failing three polygraphs questioning ⁠him about leaking classified information.
"The extent of his leaking became so critical that Secretary Hegseth took immediate action and ​fired Sylvia to protect national security. Urgent action was needed and could not wait another second," the official ​said.
US President Donald Trump, who misidentified Sylvia as a woman, said the senior US general has "got problems."
"We're very much looking for leakers, and she's going to have big problems, long-term problems," Trump told reporters.
Sylvia could not be immediately reached for comment.
Key position
Sylvia led the Directorate for ​Strategy, Plans, and Policy at the Joint Staff, known inside the military as the J5, a key position that helps ​advise the top US military official, General Dan Caine, the chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff.
He previously led the US Army's ‌101st ⁠Airborne Division. His dismissal was first reported by The Atlantic magazine.
His removal comes as the US military plans for a potential resumption of intensive bombings in Iran, something Trump has called "another little Epic Fury." The Pentagon has fumed about leaks during the Iran war, including about its planning and the expenditure of munitions.
Reuters reported on Wednesday that an internal US military analysis ​estimates it would cost more than $29 ​billion in munitions alone ⁠to restock weapons used against Iran so far. That's the bulk of the more than $47 billion spent on operations in the war.
Sean Parnell, the chief Pentagon spokesperson, said the decision ​followed an extensive investigation by the Air Force Office of Special Investigations.
"This matter, along ​with others, has been referred to the Justice Department for potential further legal action," Parnell said, without identifying other officials who may also be targeted.
Parnell added: "Our commitment was not an empty promise. We vowed to find you, and we meant it."
A spokesperson for the Joint ⁠Staff withdrew ​an initial statement expressing gratitude for Sylvia's 32 years of service, ​saying "we determined the statement did not appropriately reflect the full circumstances."
"Out of respect for the service member and the ongoing personnel process, we will not ​comment further," the spokesperson said.

items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
OnePlus has confirmed several key specifications of its upcoming Ace 7 smartphone ahead of its launch in China. OnePlus Ace 7 will feature a Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 V Series processor, a massive 9,000mAh battery, and a high-refresh-rate display designed to deliver a smoother gaming experience.
The company is also introducing the OnePlus Ace 7 Pro, which will use the standard Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 chipset. Both phones focus on performance, battery life, and gaming features.
OnePlus Ace 7 Confirmed With Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 V Series Chip and 9,000mAh Battery
The standard OnePlus Ace 7 will be powered by Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 V Series processor. The chipset features two main CPU cores clocked at up to 4.6GHz and six performance cores running at up to 3.62GHz.
The V Series version has slightly less cache memory and one fewer graphics unit than the standard Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5. However, it is still designed to handle demanding applications and mobile games.
The OnePlus Ace 7 Pro will use the standard Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 processor, giving it a different hardware configuration from the regular model.
Both smartphones will also feature OnePlus’ self-developed Esports Triple Chip system. The company is combining this technology with a Dual-Path Glacier Air Cooling System to manage heat during demanding tasks. OnePlus claims the cooling system can reduce the phone’s temperature by up to 10 degrees Celsius during extended gaming sessions.
9,000mAh Battery With 100W Fast Charging
Battery capacity is another major highlight of the OnePlus Ace 7 series. The phones will pack a 9,000mAh battery, which is considerably larger than the batteries commonly found in mainstream smartphones.
The large battery is intended to provide longer usage for gaming, video playback, and other demanding activities. Both models will also support 100W SuperVOOC fast charging, allowing users to recharge the battery more quickly.
Actual battery life will depend on factors such as screen brightness, network conditions, gaming sessions, and background activity.
185Hz Display and 200MP Camera
The OnePlus Ace 7 will feature a display with a refresh rate of up to 185Hz. A higher refresh rate can make animations, scrolling, and supported games appear smoother. This feature could appeal particularly to users who play competitive mobile games.
On the camera side, OnePlus has confirmed a 200-megapixel primary rear camera. The company has not yet disclosed the full specifications of the remaining rear cameras or the front-facing camera.
The combination of a high-resolution main camera and performance-focused hardware could make the phone suitable for users who want gaming capabilities without giving up high-resolution photography.
RAM, Storage, and Colour Options
The OnePlus Ace 7 will be available with up to 16GB of RAM and 512GB of internal storage. These configurations should provide room for demanding applications, large games, photos, and videos.
The phone will come in three colour options: Flowing Night, Polar Night Black, and Quenching.
See Also: OnePlus Ace 7 Pro Camera Specs and Samples Revealed Ahead of Launch
OnePlus Ace 7 Series Launch and Availability
OnePlus is launching the Ace 7 and Ace 7 Pro in China on October 29, 2026. The company has not confirmed pricing or availability in other markets in the information currently available.
With its Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 V Series processor, 9,000mAh battery, 185Hz display, and dedicated gaming features, the OnePlus Ace 7 is shaping up to be a performance-focused smartphone. More details about pricing, availability, and the complete camera system will help determine how it compares with other devices in its segment.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Internet services have remained suspended for around two weeks in Bara tehsil of Khyber district, affecting local businesses, digital financial services, and students who rely on online learning. Traders fear losses worth tens of millions of rupees as the prolonged disruption continues to hurt commercial activity.
Local traders and students have urged the authorities to restore internet connectivity fully, saying the outage has made everyday transactions difficult and interrupted education.
Bara Internet Outage Disrupts Businesses and Online Education
Syed Ayaz Wazir, president of the Bara Traders Association, said the suspension had seriously affected businesses in Bara Bazaar and nearby areas. According to him, the market has nearly 10,000 shops, and the disruption has affected sales, purchases, and other commercial activities. Traders estimate that their combined losses have reached tens of millions of rupees.
Digital Payment Services Hit by Internet Suspension
The outage has also disrupted Easy Paisa and other internet-based financial services that many shopkeepers and customers use for daily transactions. These platforms allow people to send and receive money, pay bills, and manage routine financial needs.
Wazir said the disruption has created additional difficulties on Saturdays and Sundays, when banks and ATMs in Bara Bazaar remain closed. Residents also rely on digital financial channels to receive money transfers from other parts of Pakistan and remittances from overseas Pakistanis.
Farooq Afridi, an Easy Paisa shopkeeper in Bara Bazaar, said more than 100 shops in the market depend on Easy Paisa and other online business services. He added that business at these outlets had slowed considerably during the past two weeks, causing problems for both shopkeepers and customers.
Traders have called on the authorities to restore internet services as soon as possible to reduce further financial losses and allow commercial activities to return to normal.
Students Struggle to Continue Their Education
The prolonged internet suspension has also affected students, particularly those who depend on online classes, recorded lectures, and digital study materials.
Lubna Afridi, a 12th-grade student from Shalobar, said much of her course material and study resources require internet access. The two-week disruption has made it difficult for her to continue her studies. She added that many female students from Bara who attend colleges are facing similar challenges.
Alina Afridi, a first-year student from Bara, also highlighted the importance of internet connectivity for education. She said students use online platforms to attend classes, watch lectures, conduct research, and access educational information from home. The ongoing outage has made it difficult for them to meet their academic needs.
Students have appealed to the authorities to restore the service so they can resume their studies without further disruption.
Internet Services Suspended After Protests
The internet disruption reportedly followed protests held in Bara Bazaar against the federal government’s imposition of Governor’s Rule and an emergency in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa.
According to the report, traders held three days of protests beginning October 11, and clashes occurred at some locations during the demonstrations. Mobile networks and internet services were suspended afterwards and have yet to be fully restored.
The continued suspension has raised concerns among residents, who say the lack of connectivity is affecting both their livelihoods and access to education.
Traders and students have urged the authorities to consider the local law-and-order situation while addressing the difficulties faced by the public. They have called for the full restoration of internet services to help businesses resume normal operations and allow students to continue their education.
The prolonged outage highlights the growing dependence of local communities on internet connectivity for financial transactions, commercial activities, and education. Residents say restoring the service is essential to reducing further economic losses and easing the difficulties faced by students and families.

items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) has detected 326 significant cyber threats through Dark Web monitoring in a year, including 174 website defacement incidents, 87 data leaks and 41 distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) threats, highlighting persistent vulnerabilities in Pakistan’s digital infrastructure.
According to the PTA’s Cyber Security Annual Report 2025-26, website defacement was the most frequently identified cyber threat, accounting for 53 percent of all indicators recorded by the National Telecommunications Security Operations Centre (nTSOC) between July 2025 and June 2026.
PTA Identifies 326 Cyber Threats, 87 Data Leaks Through Dark Web Monitoring
Data leaks accounted for 27 percent of the identified threats, while DDoS-related incidents represented 13 percent. Another 24 cases, or seven percent, involved the advertisement or sale of sensitive information through Dark Web forums and illegal online marketplaces.
The report highlighted the exposure of compromised credentials and organisational information through data leaks, warning of the potential exploitation of such information by cybercriminals.
Website defacement remained the dominant threat category, reflecting continued attempts to compromise online platforms.
DDoS-related threats, meanwhile, underscored the risk of disruption to internet-facing systems and digital infrastructure.
The PTA said continuous Dark Web intelligence monitoring had strengthened its ability to identify emerging cyber threats, compromised digital assets and malicious activities that might remain undetected through conventional monitoring mechanisms.
The nTSOC monitors Dark Web forums, illegal marketplaces, commercial threat intelligence platforms, and open-source intelligence channels to identify compromised digital assets, data leaks, website defacements, and other malicious activities that could threaten the telecommunications sector and critical information infrastructure.
The intelligence gathered from these sources is correlated with information from other threat intelligence feeds to establish the context of threats, assess potential impacts, and identify actionable findings for further investigation and response.
See Also: PTA Chairman Warns of Growing Cyber Threats, Fake Calls and OTP Scams in Pakistan
The report also highlighted trends in the blocking of URLs, applications, and social media accounts during the reporting period from July 2025 to June 2026.
The monitoring data showed a sharp increase in the number of URLs and social media accounts flagged for blocking in September 2025, followed by a decline in subsequent months. Social media blocking indicators remained comparatively higher than URL and application blocking figures during much of the period.
The PTA said continuous monitoring of deep and Dark Web sources, commercial threat intelligence platforms and open-source intelligence channels enhanced threat visibility and helped identify malicious infrastructure, emerging threats and indicators of compromise from diverse sources.
The findings underline the growing importance of proactive cyber threat intelligence in identifying vulnerabilities, limiting the exposure of sensitive information, and strengthening the resilience of Pakistan’s telecommunications networks and digital services.

items.author: Usama Anjum
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Pakistan’s local mobile phone manufacturing and assembly industry continued to expand during the first nine months of 2026, producing 20.08 million handsets between January and September, compared to just 2.85 million commercially imported devices.
According to official data, locally assembled handsets included approximately eight million smartphones and 12 million 2G feature phones, highlighting the growing contribution of domestic assembly plants to Pakistan’s mobile phone market.
The figures show that local assembly accounted for the vast majority of finished handsets produced domestically or imported commercially during the period, reducing the country’s dependence on imported ready-to-use mobile phones.
Meanwhile, Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) data reveals that smartphones now account for 71 percent of active mobile devices on local networks, while the remaining 29 percent are 2G phones.
Despite the rising share of smartphones in active usage, feature phones continue to represent a significant portion of local handset production.
Pakistan’s Mobile Phone Import Bill Falls by 16.6%
Alongside the growth in local assembly, Pakistan recorded a notable decline in mobile phone imports during the first quarter of fiscal year 2026-27.
The import bill fell by 16.6 percent to $417.24 million during July-September 2026, compared to approximately $500.01 million in the corresponding period last year.
However, September witnessed a monthly increase in imports, with the bill rising by 7.1 percent to $143.14 million from $133.66 million in August.
Despite this recovery, imports remained 28.2 percent lower than the $199.27 million recorded in September 2025.
In Pakistani rupees, mobile phone imports reached Rs. 39.75 billion in September, compared to Rs. 37.17 billion in August. On a year-on-year basis, the figure declined by 29.2 percent.
Overall, the mobile phone import bill stood at Rs. 116.01 billion during July-September FY27, reflecting an 18 percent decrease compared to Rs. 141.42 billion during the same period last year.
The figures highlight the increasing importance of domestic mobile phone assembly in Pakistan’s handset market.
However, local assembly operations still depend on imported components, meaning that lower imports of finished devices do not necessarily translate into an equivalent reduction in the industry’s overall foreign exchange requirements.
With domestic production continuing to meet much of the country’s handset demand, Pakistan’s mobile manufacturing sector remains an important part of the local technology industry.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Apple’s iPhone Duo display issue may be more serious than initially reported. A new report claims that Apple relaxed some quality control standards during production to maintain supplies of its first foldable iPhone despite manufacturing challenges.
According to Chinese media outlet Jiemian News, a Foxconn employee revealed that Apple had eased certain quality checks to ensure enough devices were available for launch. If the claim is accurate, some phones that might not have passed stricter inspections could have reached customers.
The report also claims that the iPhone Duo production line has urgently replaced a batch of components following reports of display problems. However, the overall production and shipping plans have reportedly remained unchanged.
iPhone Duo Faced Manufacturing Challenges Before Launch
Concerns about the iPhone Duo’s manufacturing quality had emerged before its official launch. Reports in September suggested that the final assembly yield was only slightly above 60%, meaning that a relatively small proportion of devices were successfully assembled during the reported production stage.
The hinge and foldable display were reportedly among the biggest challenges for Apple and its manufacturing partners. These components are particularly important in foldable phones because they must withstand repeated folding while maintaining the display’s performance and durability.
The reported production difficulties raised questions about whether Apple could manufacture enough devices while maintaining its usual quality standards.
Users Report Cracked Displays and Screen Failures
Less than a week after the iPhone Duo’s launch, several users reportedly began sharing complaints about cracked inner displays and other screen-related problems.
These reports have added to concerns about the durability of Apple’s first foldable phone. Although early user complaints do not establish how widespread the problem is, their timing has drawn attention to the reported manufacturing challenges before launch.
The alleged replacement of components on the production line has also raised questions about whether Apple is making changes to address potential defects in the initial batch of devices.
However, neither the reported component replacement nor the alleged relaxation of quality checks independently confirms that Apple knowingly shipped defective phones.
See Also: iPhone Duo Owners Report Screen Cracks Along Hinge Shortly After Launch
Questions Remain About Apple’s Quality Standards
If the Foxconn employee’s claims are true, Apple could face questions about the quality checks applied to the first batch of iPhone Duo devices. Customers may also want to know whether the company identified potential risks before launch and what steps it took to address them.
For a premium device, particularly one with a complex foldable display and a high price tag, reliability is an important consideration. Buyers expect the screen and hinge to withstand normal use without developing serious defects shortly after purchase.
Apple has not confirmed that it deliberately accepted a higher failure rate to meet its initial shipment targets. The available claims also do not establish whether the reported display failures are linked to any changes in manufacturing standards.
For now, the situation remains based on reported employee claims and early customer complaints. Further clarification from Apple or its manufacturing partners would help establish whether the reported quality control changes occurred and whether they affected devices already sold to customers.

The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) has established 17 cyber patrolling units to monitor social media activities and take action against cybercrime across Pakistan. The initiative aims to improve the monitoring of online platforms and strengthen efforts to identify illegal activities in the digital space.
According to NCCIA Director General Syed Ali Nasir Rizvi, the newly established units are playing an important role in identifying anti-state propaganda, fake news, harassment of women, the promotion of obscene content, and other forms of cybercrime on social media.
NCCIA Establishes 17 Cyber Patrolling Units to Monitor Social Media
The units are tasked with monitoring online activities to identify potentially illegal content and help the agency take appropriate action. Their work covers several areas of concern, including the spread of misleading information, online harassment, and the circulation of prohibited material.
The establishment of these units is intended to make social media monitoring more effective and improve the agency’s ability to respond to cybercrime. By strengthening its online surveillance capabilities, the NCCIA aims to identify suspicious activities more efficiently and support investigations into digital offences.
Online harassment and the circulation of unlawful content have become important concerns as more people use social media for communication, information, and business. Women, in particular, can face harassment, threats, and the misuse of their personal information on digital platforms. The NCCIA’s cyber patrolling units are expected to help identify such activities and support action against those responsible.
See Also: IHC Orders PTA, Pemra and NCCIA to Explain How They Are Enforcing Online Harassment Laws
The initiative also reflects the agency’s broader efforts to strengthen its capacity to investigate cyber offences and address unlawful online activity. However, any enforcement action must follow applicable laws and legal procedures.
With 17 cyber patrolling units now in place, the NCCIA aims to improve its monitoring of social media and strengthen its response to different forms of cybercrime. The effectiveness of these units will depend on their ability to identify genuine offences, support investigations, and ensure that action against unlawful online activities remains within the boundaries of the law.
