items.title: Bolsonaro claims he is Brazil’s true leader after fleeing to US
items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
Brazil’s defeated right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro insisted Wednesday he is his country’s rightful leader after arriving in the United States to start a self-imposed exile.
Bolsonaro’s defiance on fleeing to Florida signaled continued upheaval for Brazil, where leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva won a dramatic runoff election Sunday.
“I am the elected president, and the criminals who stole Brazil’s election are part of a criminal organization that has established a tyranny,” Bolsonaro said in the statement published on his X account, slamming “electoral fraud.”
“I will lead the opposition from here,” he said. In a subsequent statement, he revised his claim, saying he is the “leader,” rather than “president.”
Bolsonaro, 45, touched down earlier Wednesday in a private jet at Opa-Locka Executive Airport near Miami.
President Donald Trump’s hard-right administration has strong links to Bolsonaro and his father Jair Bolsonaro, who is under house arrest in Brazil after attempting to overturn his own electoral loss to Lula in 2022.
Trump reiterated his stand that Brazil’s election was “very strange” but told reporters he “won’t get involved” in Flavio Bolsonaro’s claim to the presidency.
Details of how Bolsonaro, accompanied by his wife and daughters, made it to US soil are still emerging.
He is under investigation in his home country over alleged corruption and money laundering. With his current parliamentary immunity about to expire, he was ordered to surrender his passports but left anyway, reaching the United States via Argentina and Ecuador.
A police source told AFP that Bolsonaro’s Brazilian and diplomatic passports had been canceled, but the senator has also held Italian nationality since 2023, according to Italian documents seen by AFP.
The US Department of Homeland Security said in a statement that the Bolsonaro family members were inspected and cleared “with applicable immigration laws and procedures.”
The travel ban was issued by powerful Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes, who led the case against Flavio Bolsonaro’s father and is a controversial figure hated by the Brazilian right.
Flavio Bolsonaro had vowed to seek the justice’s impeachment if he were elected — which up until Lula’s comeback in the runoff had looked increasingly likely.
– ‘Shameful’ act –
Lula, who won the election with 51.8 percent of Sunday’s vote, called Flavio Bolsonaro’s departure a “shameful” act.
“A person who sneaks out of their country must have something to hide,” he said in Brasilia during his 81st birthday celebration on Tuesday.
But Brazil police issued a statement Wednesday saying that he was not considered a fugitive.
There was controversy in neighboring Argentina, where opposition lawmakers demanded to know how Bolsonaro had managed to transit through the country.
While Argentinian authorities said he was carrying valid travel documents, officials have requested chief of cabinet Diego Santilli to provide details to parliament, according to opposition lawmaker Agustin Rossi.
– Fraud cases –
The most high-profile fraud case against Flavio Bolsonaro in Brazil centers on the unreleased biopic “Dark Horse” starring US actor Jim Caviezel as Flavio’s father Jair.
In May, the outlet Intercept Brasil revealed audio recordings in which Flavio Bolsonaro negotiated approximately $24 million to finance the film with banker Daniel Vorcaro, who is jailed over one of Brazil’s biggest-ever fraud cases.
Before the leak, Flavio Bolsonaro had denied knowing Vorcaro, or that he had financed the movie.
In July, the Supreme Court ordered a probe into the financing of the film, and whether it involved corruption, money laundering or the illegal movement of currency.
Flavio Bolsonaro acknowledged Vorcaro had funded the film, but insisted it was a private business deal that was “completely legal.”
In another probe, police are investigating whether Flavio Bolsonaro laundered money and moved funds out of the country in collaboration with his close friend, the lawyer Willer Tomaz.
Flavio’s father Jair Bolsonaro also never conceded defeat after losing to Lula and left the country on the eve of his rival’s inauguration, before returning to Brazil three months later.
AFP

items.content:
By Dickson Omobola
The All Progressives Congress, APC, Wednesday, denied claims that ministers pay billions of Naira to secure appointments, saying comments made by its Presidential Campaign Council spokesperson, Alwan Hassan, referred to historical practices rather than the current administration.
Hassan had alleged that some ministers pay billions of naira to secure appointments and subsequently seek to recover the money.
Speaking during an interview on Arise TV, Hassan said: “The way Asiwaju is hands-on on the expenditure of our revenue is fantastic and I love it. A lot of ministers pay billions and billions, and, you know, to get themselves appointed. The first thing they think of is how to recoup that money.”
Reacting to the statement, which has generated backlash, National Publicity Secretary of APC, Felix Morka, questioned how ministers who allegedly paid billions to secure appointments would recover such sums within Nigeria’s budgetary framework.
Speaking on Primetime, an Arise TV programme, Morka said Hassan had explained that his remarks were not directed at the current administration but were made in a historical context.
His words: “What he was referring to was not really about this administration, but he was speaking in historical context. What he said left a lot of ambiguity, some have suggested that he was speaking about appointments. He was clear as well when he said that what he was describing predated APC. As a citizen listening to him, I thought he was simply conflating systems. When he came back and said it predated the APC, that suggested to me that his frame of thought was really located, not in the present, but really in the past.
“When you are a public commentator, sometimes you generalise without really specifically drawing those lines of distinction between moments. If I say there’s corruption in Nigeria, I’m not necessarily saying that this government is corrupt. am not here to sort of overanalyse or justify comments. I think that, in due time, he alone will have to come tell what he had in his mind. But from talking to him, what I understood, after the fact, was that he was simply speaking historically, to say that ministers generally in our country have had this really terrible record of engaging in that behaviour.
“If ministers are paying billions to get appointed, how exactly, within what we know to be Nigeria’s budgetary frame, do you recoup the billions you paid to get appointed? I don’t think that is really something that, personally, I am willing to even imagine. He made a comment in historical context, as he explained it. In other democracies, lobbying for appointments is not something unusual. In the United States, there are firms that are contracted to lobby for individuals to get appointed to office. Those are usual things that happen in the background.prior to appointments.
“I think the concern here is that when lobbying becomes monetised, where people pay money to operators or to individuals with influence to procure appointments, that I think is what is really wrong.”

‎
‎By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse
‎
‎Former Kano State Governor, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, has warned the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) that alleged irregularities in the preliminary voter register could undermine the credibility of the 2027 general elections.
‎
‎Kwankwaso raised the concern in a statement posted on his official Facebook page, following reports of suspected artificial intelligence-generated photographs and other questionable records in the register.
‎
‎He warned that failure to properly investigate the allegations could weaken public confidence in Nigeria’s electoral system ahead of the elections.
‎
‎According to him, the development raises serious questions about the integrity of the voter registration process and the measures put in place by INEC to prevent electoral manipulation.
‎
‎”With the 2027 elections approaching, INEC must provide Nigerians with clear and convincing answers,” he said.
‎
‎Kwankwaso questioned how the suspicious photographs found their way into the register, whether the individuals involved were genuinely registered and if their identities were properly verified.
‎
‎While welcoming INEC’s decision to investigate the allegations, the former governor insisted that Nigerians deserved more than assurances from the electoral body.
‎
‎He called for a thorough, transparent and independent investigation, saying the findings must be made public and anyone found responsible held accountable under the law.
‎
‎Kwankwaso also demanded a comprehensive independent audit of the preliminary voter register to identify questionable entries, duplicate registrations and possible artificial identities.
‎
‎He, however, stressed that the exercise must not deny eligible Nigerians their constitutional right to vote.
‎
‎”Our democracy cannot afford any compromise in the integrity of the voter register. Every eligible Nigerian must have the right to vote, and every vote must count,” he said.
‎
‎The former governor further warned against the use of emerging technologies, particularly artificial intelligence, to manipulate the electoral process.
‎
‎”Nobody should be allowed to exploit technology, including artificial intelligence, to undermine our electoral system,” he added.
‎
‎Kwankwaso maintained that the credibility of the 2027 general elections would depend largely on the accuracy and integrity of the voter register.
‎
‎”The credibility of the 2027 elections begins with a credible voter register, and INEC must get its act together,” he declared

By Luminous Jannamike
Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has challenged President Bola Tinubu to provide daily proof of his presence in Makkah for Umrah, alleging that the planned pilgrimage could be a smokescreen for a trip to France.
Atiku said Nigerians deserved to know the President’s actual destination, daily engagements and the purpose of the trip, raising questions about a reported $20 billion loan request involving a French business partner.
In a statement by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku said intelligence available to him suggested that Tinubu might make only a brief appearance in Makkah before proceeding to France.
He called on the Presidency to release clear, current and date-stamped photographs and videos each day showing Tinubu at the Kaaba and performing the rites of Umrah.
“Nigerians deserve verifiable proof of the President’s presence in Makkah and a transparent account of his daily activities in the Holy Land,” he said.
Atiku also questioned whether the trip was connected to the President’s health and the reported $20 billion loan request, urging the Presidency to address the concerns and disclose the full itinerary.
The former vice president said he and other Nigerians would join Tinubu in prayers for the country’s peace and progress, but warned against invoking religion without sincerity.
“No one should invoke the name of Almighty Allah in vain,” he said, insisting that a spiritual mission undertaken on behalf of the nation must be treated with seriousness and transparency.
He maintained that Nigerians were entitled to know how the trip was being funded and demanded verifiable evidence of the President’s whereabouts and activities.

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
Inter Milan returned to the Serie A summit with a nervy 2-0 win at bottom side Venezia on Wednesday, while a Samuel Mbangula hat-trick sealed a 4-2 win for Bologna at San Siro to inflict a first league defeat of the season on AC Milan.
Champions Inter drew level with Lazio on 25 points at the top ahead of a hotly anticipated Milan derby meeting with their rivals on Saturday.
Ruben Amorim’s side will go into that game on the back of losing their unbeaten streak after Alphadjo Cisse’s double was not enough to avoid a defeat that left the Rossoneri fifth on 18 points.
Fresh off a pulsating stoppage-time turnaround against Fiorentina on Sunday that marked their fifth comeback win of the season, Inter thought they would have to fight back from behind once again when Lion Lauberbach fired the rock-bottom hosts in front after 29 minutes.
The champions were handed a reprieve when it was ruled out for offside, but had goalkeeper Ivan Provedel to thank for keeping the scores level at the break as he diverted a Lauberbach effort off the bar.
Venezia have picked up just three points all season but looked the likelier to make the breakthrough as Gianluca Busio fired over unmarked from 12 yards before Akor Adams rounded Provedel to score, only for the offside flag to save Inter again.
Last season’s Serie B champions stunned Napoli with a win on new coach Davide Nicola’s debut and another shock result looked possible until they were undone in painful fashion late on.
Matias Moreno and Redouane Halhal diverted dangerous deliveries into their own net in the space of two minutes to ensure Inter returned to the top of the standings and Venezia remained rooted to the bottom.
– Mbangula magic downs Milan –
At San Siro, a lengthy injury list featuring the likes of Adrien Rabiot, Diego Moreira and Mario Gila restricted Amorim’s options for the first midweek round of the season, while the Milan coach left Christian Pulisic and Luka Modric on the bench.
Mbangula, making his full debut for Bologna, swept home the opener inside eight minutes, but the visitors were soon pegged back when an Arthur Theate error gifted Cisse a simple finish.
The Milan teenager struck again in the 27th minute, volleying home a Fikayo Tomori cross, but the game was turned on its head once again in the space of two second-half minutes to stun the San Siro crowd.
The unfortunate Davide Bartesaghi turned a free-kick into his own net before Mbangula struck again with a composed control and finish in the box just after the hour mark.
The 22-year-old then completed a memorable night four minutes from time when he beat Mike Maignan for a third time with a smart finish after Bologna robbed the ball in midfield.
Bologna sealed back-to-back wins for the first time this season to move into 11th place on 11 points.
Elsewhere, Adrian Bernabe had a penalty saved by Maduka Okoye as struggling Parma and Udinese played out a 0-0 draw.
Later on Wednesday, Juventus and Napoli travel to Genoa and Monza respectively.
AFP

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
By Johnbosco Agbakwuru
The Federal Government has put a strong defence to its proposed $21.7 billion external borrowing plan, describing it as a long-term investment in infrastructure, human capital and economic growth rather than an additional debt burden.
The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, made the clarification while briefing State House correspondents at the end of the Federal Executive Council, FEC meeting, presided over by President Bola Tinubu at the Council Chamber, presidential villa, Abuja.
He said the five-year project financing plan was designed to create productive assets whose long-term economic value would outweigh the cost of borrowing.
Presenting the highlights of the Federal Executive Council (FEC) meeting, Oyedele said the plan covered critical investments in transportation, defence and security, health, agriculture, energy, digital infrastructure, small businesses, social protection, environmental protection and education.
He disclosed that about $10.6 billion had been earmarked for transportation infrastructure, including major highway projects such as the Sokoto-Badagry and Lagos-Calabar coastal highways, as well as the Kano-Kaduna Metro Rail project.
The minister, however, clarified that the proposal was a financing plan submitted to the National Assembly and did not mean the entire amount had already been borrowed or would necessarily be drawn down in full.
According to him, the Federal Government was acting as the coordinating authority for external financing covering federal, state and other public-sector projects.
He said approximately $4.8 billion of the proposed financing was allocated to projects involving state governments, the Federal Capital Territory and other subnational entities, agencies and development finance institutions.
Oyedele said about $7.9 billion would come from multilateral and bilateral development partners, including $5 billion from the World Bank at concessional rates averaging 2.1 per cent.
He added that the indicative average interest rate on the commercial component was 7.8 per cent, which he said was below the rate on Nigeria’s November 2025 Eurobond.
The minister argued that borrowing could strengthen the country’s balance sheet if the resulting investments generated assets and economic benefits exceeding their financing costs.
Using the Dangote Refinery as an illustration, he said large-scale projects often required external financing to be completed within a reasonable period, adding that Nigeria needed to adopt a similar approach to transformative infrastructure.
On the state of the economy, Oyedele said Nigeria’s economic indicators had improved since President Bola Tinubu introduced major reforms in May 2023, although he acknowledged that significant challenges remained.
He recalled that inflation stood at 22.41 per cent when the reforms began, while the country’s net foreign reserves were estimated at $859 million, insufficient to cover a month of imports.
He also cited multiple foreign exchange rates, a premium of more than 60 per cent between official and parallel-market rates, and debt-service costs consuming about 97 per cent of government revenue as evidence of the pressures facing the economy.
According to him, the government had been forced to address structural weaknesses that threatened economic stability, arguing that failure to implement the reforms could have resulted in runaway inflation and a further collapse of the naira.
Oyedele said economic growth had risen from 2.74 per cent in 2023 to 4.43 per cent in the second quarter of 2026, while inflation declined to 14.63 per cent in September from 20.98 per cent a year earlier.
He also reported that foreign reserves had risen to more than $55 billion, with net reserves exceeding $45 billion, compared with less than $1 billion three years earlier.
The minister said the naira had stabilised within the range of N1,330 to N1,350 to the dollar, adding that the International Monetary Fund had estimated that the currency was undervalued by about 25 per cent.
He further stated that the tax-to-GDP ratio had risen from approximately seven per cent in 2023 to 12.5 per cent by the end of 2025, while the debt-service-to-revenue ratio had fallen from about 97 per cent to below 60 per cent.
Federation Account revenue, he added, increased by 44 per cent between 2024 and 2025, with the government projecting growth of at least 50 per cent in 2026.
Oyedele said international confidence had also improved, citing credit-rating upgrades and positive outlooks from rating agencies, as well as Nigeria’s exit from the Financial Action Task Force’s grey list and the European Union’s list of high-risk jurisdictions.
The minister said the government’s economic programme had also provided direct support to households, students and businesses.
He disclosed that more than N372.6 billion had been disbursed through the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) to over 1.5 million students, while more than 10 million households had received cash transfers worth over N600 billion.
The government, he said, was targeting at least 15 million beneficiary households under the cash-transfer programme.
Oyedele added that more than 800,000 micro, small and medium-sized enterprises had accessed subsidised single-digit-interest loans, largely through the Bank of Industry.
Under the tax reforms, he said, low-income earners making up to N100,000 monthly had been exempted from personal income tax, while small businesses with annual turnover of not more than N100 million had been exempted from corporate income tax, value-added tax collection and withholding-tax obligations, subject to the applicable provisions of the law.
He also cited the expansion of the Nigerian capital market, whose value he said had risen from about N30 trillion to more than N160 trillion in three years, as evidence of growing investment activity and wealth creation.
Despite the improvements, Oyedele said FEC recognised the need to address the high cost of living, particularly food prices, and agreed to intensify efforts to improve living standards.
He said the council adopted a target of reducing inflation to single digits by the end of 2027 or earlier, while prioritising food-price stability, critical infrastructure, human-capital development and job creation.
The council also endorsed the National Economic Council’s 90-day action plan aimed at easing the cost of living through coordinated action by federal, state and local governments.
On other FEC decisions, Oyedele disclosed that the council considered 10 memoranda presented by his ministry, including financing arrangements for electricity transmission, railway infrastructure, road development and customs modernisation.
He said a €155.9 million credit facility arranged through Deutsche Bank and other lenders would support five substations and associated transmission infrastructure under Phase One of the Presidential Power Initiative.
The intervention, he said, was intended to improve electricity reliability for households and businesses while helping to reduce energy costs.
The council also considered a $970 million syndicated term loan arranged by Standard Chartered and the Africa Finance Corporation for rolling stock on the Kano-Maradi railway line.
According to the minister, the railway investment was expected to reduce freight costs, facilitate regional trade and improve logistics along the northern economic corridor.
Another €76.8 million facility from the ECOWAS Bank for Investment and Development was approved for Bauchi State’s transport infrastructure development programme, including rural and urban roads and routes linking farms to markets.
Oyedele said FEC also approved investment in non-intrusive inspection scanners, alongside technical support, repairs and maintenance for the Nigeria Customs Service, to accelerate cargo clearance, combat smuggling and improve the detection of prohibited goods and dangerous weapons.
He said the government remained committed to fiscal discipline and investment in infrastructure and social development, arguing that the success of the borrowing programme would ultimately depend on the value delivered by the projects and their benefits to Nigerians.

items.content:
Two Cisco executives, who asked different questions on the same day, gave the same one-word answer. That happened at the Comtech Associates (Pakistan) booth during ITCN Asia 2026, which wrapped up its 28th edition on September 24 at Expo Center Karachi.
Comtech, a Pakistan-based enterprise networking and cybersecurity provider, ran a joint booth with Cisco for all three days. Three things stood out: the hardware on display, the sessions led by its head of solutions, and what Cisco leadership told Comtech’s CEO on camera.
One Dashboard, Every Site: Inside the Cloud Networking Session
Muhammad Irfan Ghauri, Comtech’s Head of Solutions, led a session on Cisco Meraki, Cisco’s cloud-managed networking platform. It reportedly ran past its scheduled slot as audience questions kept coming.
His slides pitched one browser-based dashboard for switches, wireless, security appliances, and cameras, from a single branch to thousands of sites. Key points were zero-touch deployment (“no truck roll, no on-site expert required”), built-in security, and new sites online in “hours instead of weeks.” These are Cisco’s own claims.
The Other Two Sessions: AI Data Centers and Webex
Meraki was one of several sessions Comtech scheduled to use the expo for technical education rather than just booth traffic. Ghauri’s other two decks, on AI data centers and Cisco Webex, follow the same habit: start from the buyer’s problem, then map it to hardware.
Powering the AI Era
This talk, “Why the world needs AI data centers,” argues that traditional facilities were not built for AI workloads. A conventional rack draws 5 to 10 kW with air cooling, while an AI rack needs 40 to 100+ kW and liquid cooling. Gartner puts 2026 data center electricity use at 565 TWh.
Cisco’s answer centers on the Silicon One G300, a 102.4 Tbps switching chip, and the systems built on it. The slides organize the portfolio around three ways AI infrastructure grows:
Dimension
Scope
Cisco layer named in the deck
Scale up
Inside one server or rack
UCS servers with NVIDIA GPUs (UCS C880A M8)
Scale out
Many servers in one data center
Silicon One G300, Nexus N9000 switches, Nexus Hyperfabric
Scale across
Multiple data centers and regions
Cisco 8000 Series routers
Cisco Webex Collaboration
The Webex talk presented an “open, AI-powered” suite that unites calling, meetings, messaging, and devices under one console, Control Hub. Its most practical idea was interoperability: Cisco devices run native Webex alongside Microsoft Teams, Zoom, and Google Meet, with no forklift upgrade, from headsets to boardroom systems.
When The Vendor’s Leadership Shows Up In Person
A senior Cisco delegation, including Mohamad Besher, who leads Cisco’s Gulf, Levant, Turkey, and CCA regions, and Kashif Ul Haque, Country General Manager for Pakistan, spent time at the booth with CEO Muhammad Farooq Zaheer. He hosted both interviews himself, so the answers below respond to a partner’s questions, not an independent press interview.
Inside the Interview With Kashif Ul Haque
Farooq Zaheer asked Kashif Ul Haque six questions, and the answers ranged from Pakistan’s technology history to what a good partner owes its customers.
How much has Pakistan’s technology market changed over his career?
Kashif has worked in the industry since around 1996 and in Pakistan since 2004. He said technology used to be a conversation held “at about 40,000 feet” and credited Gen Z for pulling it down to earth, since young people would rather use an app than visit a bank in person. In 2004, he said the security conversation “was security guards.”
What do people outside Pakistan get wrong about its technology maturity?
He pushed back on the premise. Kashif said any misconception lasts only until someone lands in Pakistan, and anyone who has worked with the country, even over Webex, already knows the technology exists. He recalled outdated assumptions from his visits in the 1990s but said he does not see much of that today.
Where are Pakistani enterprises ahead, and where are they catching up?
This was the least specific answer. Kashif said he has been connected to the industry for about 25 years and believes it is “genuinely heading in a good direction.” He acknowledged that Pakistan has “our own set of problems,” as every country does, said enterprises know what they are doing, and noted that people are stepping up on a self-reliance basis.
What is the one thing every business leader should prioritize this year?
Zaheer framed this as security or AI. Kashif’s reply became the line of the event: “I put security above AI, because AI will not work without security.” He added that “anything you touch has to deal with security,” and that ignoring it could leave a business “in trouble.”
What does a partner like Comtech need to get right?
Service quality, and he used an airline to make the point. Kashif said that as a gold member he is touched in a positive way at least three times between check-in and his seat, regardless of the cabin. Recurring customers, he said, need to feel they are getting service “unlike any other brand,” and without that there is no repeat business.
What should a Pakistani business look for in a local partner?
Service levels and technical resources. His point was that sales alone does not keep a customer: “It’s not the sales that sells.” He said business flows back to a vendor on the strength of customer feedback, and a happy customer comes back, while an unhappy one remembers the night something went down at midnight and no support arrived.
Inside the Interview With Mohamad Besher
What does his role involve day to day?
Besher leads Cisco’s business across the Gulf, Levant, Turkey, and CCA. A large part of the job, he said, is making sure partners are enabled, certified, and ready to talk to customers in a way that proposes “value rather than just products.” He said AI is changing customer behavior, and customers increasingly want a partner they can rely on.
What holds small and midsize businesses back from adopting the technology they need?
He named two obstacles. The first is people: many small businesses have no security, AI, or network specialist, just “one guy who runs the show.” A partner like Comtech fills that gap, he said, by bundling those skills into one managed service and stitching together technology from several vendors.
What do people underestimate about the SMB market?
Besher disputed the idea that enterprise gets all the attention. In his words, SMB is Cisco’s fastest-growing segment, growing faster than any other segment in the company, though that is his statement and hasn’t been independently verified here. He pointed to partner programs, specialization tracks, promotions, and a dedicated SMB portfolio and said the focus began years ago rather than recently.
What technology is moving from enterprise down to smaller businesses?
“Security, without any hesitation.” Besher said attackers don’t distinguish by company size: small, medium, enterprise, and public sector customers “are under the same kind of attacks,” so security is a priority in every segment and the one technology that spans them all.
The Bigger Picture
Pakistan’s IT exports hit a record high in the fiscal year ending June 2026, with the government targeting $10 billion by FY2029. Local enterprise and SMB buyers still need networking, security, and data center partners, which is Comtech’s space.
Booth traffic and two Cisco executives naming security as the priority don’t build a market position alone. But for a company positioning itself as a full-lifecycle infrastructure partner rather than a hardware reseller, that alignment from the vendor’s own people is solid supporting evidence.
The post Three Days, One Booth! What Comtech and Cisco Actually Showed Up With at ITCN Asia 2026 appeared first on ProPakistani.

items.content:
‎
‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru
‎
‎The Federal Government on Wednesday said it has approved the commencement of procurement for the proposed East and West Super Grids as part of efforts to strengthen the national electricity network and raise transmission capacity from about 5,000 megawatts to 19,000MW within two years.
‎
‎The Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, disclosed this while briefing State House correspondents at the end of the Federal Executive Council, FEC, meeting presided over by President Bola Tinubu, at the Council Chamber, Presidential Villa, Abuja.
‎
‎The Minister explained that the projects would improve grid resilience and enable the country to evacuate more electricity to consumers.
“The East and West Super Grids are not projects for one part of the country,” Tegbe said. “They cut across the north and south of Nigeria, strengthening the backbone that must carry power from where it is generated to where it is needed.”
The initiative is designed to address one of the sector’s central contradictions: Nigeria has more than 13,000MW of available generation capacity, but its transmission network can reliably wheel only about 5,000MW.
Tegbe said the super grids would improve resilience, reduce grid instability and allow more electricity to reach homes, businesses and industries.
“The target is simple,” he said. “We want a grid that can evacuate the power we already have, not one that leaves generation stranded while consumers remain in darkness.”
The Minister explained that the corridors would strengthen transmission links from Sokoto through Abuja and other locations into parts of southern Nigeria.
Beyond the super grids, the council approved three immediate interventions for Abuja and the Lagos axis, two of the country’s most important electricity demand centres.
The first is a 33kV double-circuit underground and overhead line connected to the Katampe Transmission Substation, a major hub serving the North-Central region.
The second covers the design, manufacture and supply of three 300MVA, 330/132/33kV transformers for the Ikeja West Transmission Substation, a critical node supplying Lagos.
The third will reconstruct and upgrade the 35.6-kilometre Itumola–Mapasin–Shagamu 132kV single-circuit line into a double-circuit line to serve rising demand along the Lagos–Shagamu corridor.
“These are not glamorous projects, but they are the projects that determine whether power actually gets to the consumer,” Tegbe said.
He added that the high-capacity transformers would have to be manufactured abroad because Nigeria does not yet have the domestic capacity to produce equipment of that specification.
“Some companies have started assembling transformers locally, but these large units require specialised manufacturing,” he said. “They can take between three and six months to produce, and global demand is rising because of artificial intelligence and data centres.”
The ministry has also begun a nationwide technical audit of electricity infrastructure, dividing the country into three major energy zones: Lagos and its industrial corridor, Abuja–Kaduna–Kano, and Enugu–Onitsha–Benin.
Tegbe said the audit, ongoing for four weeks, would identify ageing and weak assets that require replacement or rehabilitation.
“We will no longer spend money on the wrong projects,” he said. “The audit will show us exactly where the system is failing and where investment will deliver measurable impact.”
The government is prioritising the Lagos–Ogun, Benin–Edo–Port Harcourt and Abuja–Kaduna–Kano corridors, with the Lagos–Ogun corridor alone accounting for about half of national energy demand.
On sector liquidity, Tegbe disclosed that the Federal Government had paid N1.23 trillion of the N3.3 trillion owed to gas suppliers and other power-sector stakeholders.
He said the outstanding liabilities had constrained gas supply to generation companies and weakened confidence across the electricity value chain.
“We have paid N1.23 trillion, and we intend to finish the job,” Tegbe said. “But we must also stop new debts from accumulating.”
The payment was made through bonds under the Presidential Power Sector Debt Reduction Programme, which is intended to improve liquidity for generation companies, support gas supply and restore investor confidence.
Tegbe said the government was also reviewing the electricity market structure to strengthen payment discipline and reduce the risk of fresh arrears.
Stranded equipment ordered cleared
The President has also directed the Ministry of Power, Nigerian Ports Authority and Nigeria Customs Service to clear more than 300 containers of stranded electricity equipment at the nation’s ports.
Tegbe described the backlog as unacceptable, noting that some containers had reportedly remained uncleared for between 14 and 20 years.
“It is unacceptable that equipment meant to strengthen the grid has been sitting at the ports for years,” he said. “The President has directed that this must be resolved.”
He attributed the delays to previous administrations’ failure to settle outstanding charges and complete clearance processes.
After clearance, technical experts will inspect the equipment to determine what remains serviceable and can be deployed, while obsolete materials will be appropriately disposed of.
Modern control centre, solar expansion
The government has also commenced construction of a new National Control Centre in Osogbo to replace the existing facility, which Tegbe said was built 64 years ago.
“The new control centre will give us modern tools to monitor and manage the national grid,” he said.
The ministry is also energising completed transmission substations in Kano, Katsina, Bauchi and Gombe, among other locations, to bring idle infrastructure into service.
In parallel, the government is expanding solar mini-grids for institutions facing transmission constraints. Fourteen federal universities have received installed and energised mini-grids of between 1MW and 5MW, while 11 more are being supported through TETFund.
Five teaching hospitals are also benefiting from solar installations being implemented with the Federal Ministry of Health.
Tegbe said the administration would continue to prioritise grid stability, infrastructure rehabilitation, improved liquidity and renewable energy investment.
“Our goal is not just to announce projects,” he said. “It is to build a power system that Nigerians can depend on.”

items.content:
The Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation (MDPCO) has criticised President Bola Tinubu’s plan to secure fresh foreign loans totalling about $20.5 billion and €1.04 billion, warning that continued borrowing could increase Nigeria’s debt burden and constrain future generations.
In a press statement dated October 28, 2026, signed by Richard Nnanna Ihediwa, Director of Strategic Communications MDPCO, the organisation said it opposed the proposed loans, which it put at ₦27.52 trillion and ₦1.558 trillion, respectively.
The statement, signed by its Director of Strategic Communications, Richard Nnanna Ihediwa, questioned the timing of the borrowing request ahead of the 2027 general election and demanded that the President withdraw it.
The organisation also urged the National Assembly to reject the request, arguing that the government had yet to demonstrate how previous loans had translated into commensurate development or present a credible plan for repaying the country’s accumulated debt.
The MDPCO cited a public debt figure of ₦166.7 trillion, claiming that further borrowing would place additional pressure on Nigerians, particularly younger generations.
It also questioned the government’s explanations that successive loans were needed to finance infrastructure, critical projects and budget deficits, asking for greater transparency over the utilisation of borrowed funds.
To support its position, the organisation listed several loans secured or approved during the Tinubu administration.
It cited a $750 million World Bank loan obtained in June 2023 under the Power Sector Recovery Performance programme, intended to improve electricity supply, and a separate $500 million loan for institutional strengthening and women’s empowerment.
The group also referred to an $800 million loan secured in July 2023 for conditional cash transfers, followed by another $700 million in September of that year.
It further cited a $2.25 billion loan obtained in June 2024 for economic stabilisation and transformation, as well as a $1.57 billion borrowing plan in 2025 for healthcare, education and human-capital development. The organisation also mentioned a separate $500 million loan from the African Development Bank in 2025.
The MDPCO questioned the impact of the loans, particularly on electricity supply, economic stability and household welfare, arguing that Nigerians had yet to see results commensurate with the scale of borrowing.
It also referenced a borrowing plan approved by the Senate in 2025 involving $21.19 billion, €4 billion and ¥15 billion. According to the organisation, the plan included $3 billion for the Eastern Railway Corridor linking Port Harcourt to Maiduguri, which it claimed had yet to record tangible progress.
The group also cited Senate approvals in April 2026 for $6 billion to modernise the country’s ports and another $1.5 billion for early-childhood development and household prosperity.
The organisation compared Nigeria’s borrowing trajectory with Egypt under Khedive Isma’il, who ruled from 1863 to 1879. It argued that Egypt’s dependence on foreign loans and extravagant spending contributed to a debt crisis that undermined the country’s financial independence.
The MDPCO called on Tinubu to withdraw the latest borrowing request and urged the National Assembly to act in what it described as the national interest.
“Nigeria is nobody’s personal fiefdom!” the organisation declared.
It also called on Nigerians to support the Allied People’s Movement (APM) presidential candidate, Engr. Seyi Makinde, whose RESET NIGERIA Agenda it said offered an alternative approach to economic management, national self-sufficiency and sustainable development.
The organisation said its proposed administration would focus on restructuring, economic opportunities and prosperity, contrasting its stated objectives with what it described as the Tinubu administration’s debt-dependent economic policies.
The claims and criticisms contained in the statement represent the position of the MDPCO.
The post MDPCO warns against fresh $20.5bn foreign loan appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
By Efe Onodjae
Cristiano Ronaldo’s 2008 Ballon d’Or-winning campaign has been voted the best in the history of the prestigious individual football award in a public poll organised to celebrate its 70th anniversary.
The result was posted by football transfer journalist, Fabrizio Romano, in a Facebook post monitored by Vanguard.
Ronaldo’s 2008 triumph topped the Ballon d’Or of All Time (BOAT) ranking, ahead of Lionel Messi’s 2012 edition, while the Portuguese forward’s 2017 campaign came third.
Messi’s 2023 season occupied the fourth position, followed by Ronaldo’s 2016 campaign in fifth place.
The ranking featured 32 editions of the award won by 10 football legends, with supporters voting for the individual campaigns they considered the greatest.
Other editions featuring prominently in the top 10 included Ronaldo’s 2014 and 2013 victories, as well as Messi’s 2015, 2011 and 2009 campaigns.
Brazilian legend Ronaldo Nazário’s 2002 triumph was ranked 13th, while Johan Cruyff’s 1974 victory came 17th. Michel Platini’s 1984 campaign occupied the 18th position, ahead of Franz Beckenbauer’s 1976 edition.
Ronaldo won his first Ballon d’Or in 2008 while playing for Manchester United, following an outstanding season in which he scored 42 goals in all competitions and helped the English club win the Premier League and UEFA Champions League.
The Portuguese forward subsequently won the award four more times, in 2013, 2014, 2016 and 2017, taking his career tally to five.
Messi, meanwhile, holds the record for the most Ballon d’Or wins, with eight, including his 2023 triumph following Argentina’s victory at the 2022 FIFA World Cup.
The BOAT ranking recognises individual Ballon d’Or-winning campaigns rather than awarding a new official Ballon d’Or or determining which player has enjoyed the greatest career.
The result is also separate from the annual Ballon d’Or award, which is decided through a jury of specialist journalists.
The poll has renewed debate among football supporters over the achievements of Ronaldo and Messi, whose rivalry has dominated discussions about the world’s best player for more than a decade.

items.title: Tinubu departs Abuja for Makkah to pray for Nigeria
items.summary:
President Bola Tinubu will depart Abuja on Thursday for Makkah, Saudi Arabia, to perform Umrah, an Islamic pilgrimage involving prayers and other religious rites.
According to a statement issued on Wednesday by his Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, the visit will provide the President an opportunity for spiritual reflection and prayers for Nigeria’s peace, unity, stability and continued progress.
While in Makkah, Tinubu is expected to perform the religious rites associated with Umrah and seek Allah’s guidance and blessings for Nigeria and its people.
Before departing Abuja, the President will commission equipment acquired by the Nigerian Air Force at the Presidential Wing of the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport.
Tinubu is expected to return to Nigeria next week after completing the spiritual exercise. The statement was dated October 28, 2026.

items.title: LPG to Get Cheaper
items.summary:
LPG prices in Pakistan have dropped by Rs. 30 to 40 per kg over the last two days after supply from Iran temporarily resumed, and another Rs. 30 per kg cut is expected in the next two to three days.
The senior vice chairman of the LPG Distribution Association said the market rate is falling gradually, but warned that the risk of an LPG crisis this winter has not gone away.
Only Pre-October 16 Cargo Allowed In
According to the association, only LPG bowsers that were loaded at Iranian refineries and reached the Pakistan-Iran border before October 16 have been allowed to enter Pakistan.
The quantity loaded until October 16 is around 8,000 to 9,000 tonnes, which will meet the country’s demand for only three days.
The association said this temporary supply will not end the crisis, which comes after prices eased with the arrival of a new shipment earlier this week.

The quantity loaded until October 16 is around 8,000 to 9,000 tonnes, which will meet the country’s demand for only three days.
The association said this temporary supply will not end the crisis, which comes after prices eased with the arrival of a new shipment earlier this week.
Association Seeks 6-Month EIF Exemption
The All Pakistan LPG Distribution Association has proposed that the federal government grant a six-month exemption from the Electronic Import Form (EIF) requirement for LPG imports from Iran.
It has also informed the Prime Minister’s Adviser Haroon Akhtar that the old mechanism should be restored for six months to meet winter demand.
The association warned that if supply from Iran is not restored, LPG could reach Rs. 1,000 per kg in winter, after warnings that the cylinder price may exceed Rs. 10,000.

items.content:
Nigerian skincare brand, Poshglow Skincare, is marking nine years in the beauty industry, with its founder, Dr Agbeluyi Bosede Folasade, reiterating the importance of safe skincare practices and informed beauty choices.
Founded in 2017, the brand has developed a range of skincare products, including cleansers, creams, serums, toners, oils, scrubs, herbal soaps and specialised skincare kits.
Agbeluyi, also known professionally as Folasade Omotoyinbo, has consistently emphasised the need for consumers to prioritise skin health rather than follow extreme beauty trends, particularly those influenced by social media.
In a July 2025 interview, she encouraged consumers, especially young women, to adopt balanced and responsible skincare routines.
“True beauty is not about extremes. It’s about taking care of your skin in a safe, consistent, and intentional way,” she said.
According to information published on the company’s official website, Poshglow combines naturally sourced ingredients with science-based product development, with its formulations designed to address different skin types and individual skincare needs.
Reflecting on the brand’s nine-year journey, Agbeluyi said its philosophy extends beyond appearance to include personal confidence and well-being.
“Our journey over the past nine years has been about more than skincare; it has been about helping people feel confident and comfortable in their own skin. As we celebrate this milestone, our commitment remains to providing quality skincare solutions, listening to our customers and continuously improving the way we serve them,” she said.
The brand’s published profile also highlights youth empowerment, training and charitable initiatives as part of its broader community-focused activities.
As Poshglow enters its tenth year, the milestone provides an opportunity to reflect on the role of responsible skincare education, product development and consumer awareness within Nigeria’s evolving beauty industry.
The company is marking the anniversary on October 28 and 29, 2026, with activities commemorating its establishment in 2017.

items.author: Shahbaz Rana
items.content:
Poverty rose to 28.9% in 2024-25, reversing earlier gains, Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal has acknowledged, as the government considers changing its poverty measurement methodology to gauge the impact of climate shocks and barriers to opportunity, and may also release a political-constituency-wise analysis of people's wellbeing next year amid rising numbers of poor in Pakistan.
The Ministry of Planning and the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI) of the University of Oxford have discussed the possibility of revising the Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI), which is currently based on outcomes in health, education and living standards.
Government officials said OPHI has proposed including demographic pressure, climate shocks and new barriers to opportunity among the yardsticks to measure poverty.
However, adopting these measures may be politically costly ahead of the 2029 general elections for a ruling alliance that has been in power since April 2022, barring a brief eight-month caretaker setup.
A recent World Bank report said one out of every two of the poorest people living in the Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan and Pakistan were living in Pakistan. Pakistan's economic growth rate remains low and dipped further to 2% in the April-June quarter of this year, which was even lower than the 2.6% population growth rate, contributing to higher poverty and unemployment.
"The political instability, policy discontinuity, economic crises and climate shocks reversed development gains," Iqbal said while speaking at an event organised to sign a memorandum of understanding with OPHI.
The minister, who has recently started speaking against the government's number-centric economic policies, emphasised the need for restoring social investment, empowering local governments and using poverty evidence to shape national development priorities. Iqbal said political stability, sustained economic growth and continuity of national development priorities were essential to restoring poverty reduction.
A planning ministry handout stated that Iqbal said an updated national poverty measurement exercise will draw upon the ongoing Pakistan Social and Living Standards Measurement Survey 2026-27 and examine the relevance of emerging development challenges, including climate vulnerability, insecurity, youth deprivation, gender inequality, digital exclusion, early childhood development, nutrition, stunting and migration.
He emphasised that new indicators and complementary thematic studies must be supported by reliable data and sound methodology to preserve the credibility and policy relevance of the national measure.
A significant component of the renewed collaboration will involve exploring multidimensional poverty analysis at the National and Provincial Assembly constituency levels, using data from the 2023 Population and Housing Census, he added.
The officials said the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics has developed political constituency-wise poverty analysis, but the government has not yet decided to make it public because of its far-reaching implications.
The planning minister was of the view that any political constituency analysis should first be done as a pilot project and as evidence of the need for targeted public investments to improve people's wellbeing, instead of being used as a scorecard of elected representatives, they added.
Iqbal said OPHI's international experience could play an important role in helping Pakistan translate poverty measurement into practical policy interventions, particularly in development planning, resource allocation and social protection targeting and sustainable graduation from poverty. The proposed collaboration includes updating the National MPI, developing constituency-level poverty analysis, examining the relationship between monetary and multidimensional poverty using household survey data, strengthening institutional technical capacity and promoting the policy use of poverty evidence, said the planning ministry.
Commenting on rising poverty in Pakistan, the minister said poverty reduction momentum had suffered a serious setback after 2018, as political instability, discontinuity in development policies, economic crises, the COVID-19 pandemic and devastating floods undermined earlier gains and constrained the country's capacity to invest in its people. His party has been in power since early 2022, and yet poverty and unemployment are on the rise. Iqbal also recently wrote to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, urging him to reset economic policies while describing the current phase of economic stabilisation as "borrowed and stunted". He said national monetary poverty declined from 29.5% in 2013-14 to 24.3% in 2015-16, with the downward trend continuing to 21.9% in 2018-19.
But Iqbal admitted that the latest official estimates show poverty increased to 28.9% in 2024-25, reflecting a substantial reversal in Pakistan's earlier progress. In his letter to the prime minister, Iqbal had also attributed the economic downfall to current economic policies. "The greatest danger is that Pakistan may successfully stabilise at a structurally low rate of economic growth."
The minister had written that Pakistan needed sustained growth significantly above population growth simply to create sufficient jobs, absorb millions of young entrants into the labour market, reduce poverty and service its debt obligations.
If development expenditure remains at rock-bottom levels, our potential growth rate itself will be damaged, he added. Similar views were expressed by the minister this week when he stated that the federal Public Sector Development Programme (PSDP) had reached Rs1 trillion in 2017-18, accounting for approximately 19.6% of the federal budget and 2.5% of gross domestic product (GDP). In contrast, the federal PSDP allocation for 2026-27 stands at approximately Rs1 trillion, almost unchanged in nominal terms despite the substantial increase in population, prices and development requirements over the intervening years, he added.
He observed that had the 2017-18 share of the federal budget been maintained, the development programme would today exceed Rs3 trillion, illustrating the scale of development investment capacity that Pakistan has been unable to sustain. The minister warned that shrinking public investment had serious consequences for education, healthcare, water security, infrastructure, skills development and economic opportunities, particularly in disadvantaged regions.
However, the finance ministry appears to be ignoring the planning minister's warnings. Iqbal said MPI evidence subsequently helped identify Pakistan's 20 poorest districts, 11 in Balochistan, five in Sindh, three in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa and one in Punjab, providing the basis for a targeted development initiative under the federal PSDP.
The minister said more geographically disaggregated evidence could help elected representatives understand development gaps within their constituencies, strengthen public accountability and generate greater political consensus around social investment.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
The Pakistan Public Procurement Regulatory Authority (PPRA) has been directed to introduce a defect liability period of at least three-year or more for major projects, with the measure to be extended to smaller projects in phases.
Federal Minister for Economic Affairs and Establishment Division Senator Ahad Cheema issued the direction at a meeting held to discuss reforms aimed at strengthening the construction sector, improving project delivery and addressing key issues faced by the industry. The meeting discussed the proposed Construction Industry Development Authority (CIDA) Bill, with the minister emphasising that it required detailed consideration, including whether to establish a single body for the construction sector or two separate entities, one to regulate the sector and another to promote the construction industry and handle related matters.
He asked the relevant officials, Minister of State for Finance Bilal Azhar Kayani and representatives of the Constructors Association of Pakistan (CAP) to consult further on the proposed institutional structure.
The retention money deposited by contractors during the defect liability period was also discussed, and the meeting considered a proposal to place these funds in accounts that earn a return, with the principal amount and interest paid back to contractors after the stipulated period. The minister called for further consultation to develop a workable mechanism.
It also considered applying the existing Dispute Avoidance/Adjudication Board (DAAB) mechanism to government projects, under which the board would monitor project implementation and help prevent or resolve disputes as they arise. CAP proposed applying it to projects valued at Rs20 billion and above, while the minister called for the threshold to be lowered and for further consultation among stakeholders to determine an appropriate limit.
The forthcoming framework for the construction sector will also draw on the rules and standards of the International Federation of Consulting Engineers (FIDIC), which the minister underscored as a key reference.
The meeting was attended by Minister of State for Finance Bilal Azhar Kayani, Housing Secretary Captain (retd) Muhammad Mahmood, a member of the Planning Commission, the PPRA managing director, representatives of CAP and other senior officials.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Gold prices in Pakistan increased by Rs3,500 per tola on Wednesday, despite a slight decline in international market, as investors awaited the US Federal Reserve's monetary policy decision and comments from its chair for clues about the future path of rates.
In the local market, gold prices rose to Rs425,636 per tola, according to rates released by the All-Pakistan Gems and Jewellers Sarafa Association (APGJSA). Similarly, the price of 10-gram gold increased by Rs3,001 to reach Rs364,914. On Tuesday, gold prices had declined by Rs1,300 per tola, settling at Rs422,136. Wednesday's increase reversed those losses and pushed domestic bullion prices higher. In the international market, spot gold edged down 0.3% to $4,044.54 per ounce by 11:46 am EDT (1546 GMT), as per Reuters. US gold futures for December delivery fell 0.4% to $4,057.30 per ounce. Higher oil prices weighed on bullion, while concerns over supply disruptions in the Middle East added to market uncertainty. Rising energy prices can fuel inflationary pressures, potentially influencing the pace of monetary easing by major central banks.
Investors remained cautious ahead of the Federal Reserve's policy announcement, scheduled for 2 pm EDT (1800 GMT), followed by a press conference by Fed Chair Kevin Warsh.
Market participants were looking for signals on the central bank's assessment of inflation and economic conditions, as well as indications of whether interest rates could decline further.
Rate expectations are a key driver of gold prices because bullion does not pay any yield. Lower rates generally make gold more attractive relative to interest-bearing assets, while expectations of tighter monetary policy can weigh on bullion demand. Investors were also looking ahead to the US personal consumption expenditures (PCE) index, due on Thursday. The measure is closely watched by the Federal Reserve as an indicator of inflationary trends. Developments in oil markets and geopolitical tensions in the Middle East were also expected to remain important factors for investors assessing inflation risks and the outlook of monetary policy.
Silver prices in Pakistan increased by Rs61 per tola to reach Rs5,854 on Wednesday. Meanwhile, the Pakistani rupee continued its upward trajectory, gaining Rs0.03 against the US dollar to close at 276.77 in the inter-bank market. On Tuesday, the local currency had settled at 276.80 against the greenback. Internationally, the US dollar held near two-week highs ahead of central bank policy decisions, with the Federal Reserve widely expected to keep rates unchanged while signalling the possibility of a move in December.
Fed holds rate steady
Later on Wednesday, the Federal Reserve held interest rates steady, as expected, opting to delay any changes to borrowing costs until after next week's US midterm elections and awaiting further data on the path of inflation.

items.author: Shazia Tasneem Farooqi
items.content:
The State Bank of Pakistan's (SBP) decision to raise its policy rate by 50 basis points to 12% has cast a shadow over the economic recovery, with economists warning that persistent energy and food price pressures could keep monetary policy tight while higher borrowing costs weigh on private investment, employment and growth.
The Sustainable Development Policy Institute (SDPI) economist Dr Abid Qaiyum Suleri said the 50-basis-point increase reflected growing concerns over inflation, particularly rising energy and food prices. With inflation reaching 10.3% in September, the central bank wanted to prevent temporary supply shocks from turning into persistent inflationary pressures.
He expects energy prices to remain elevated in the near future amid fears of another wave of US-Israeli attacks on Iran after the US midterm elections and the possibility of Iranian retaliation against neighbouring Gulf states.
This outlook leaves limited room for monetary easing in the coming months, as persistent external tensions could prolong energy price pressures and complicate the inflation outlook. He expects monetary policy to remain tight, with rate cuts unlikely unless energy prices stabilise and inflation records a sustained decline.
The SBP projects economic growth of 3.5-4.5% in fiscal year 2027, but prolonged high borrowing costs could constrain the recovery, he said.
SDPI Deputy Executive Director and founding head of the Policy Solutions Lab Dr Sajid Amin Javed said the 50-basis-point increase was expected as double-digit inflation, a recent surge in global oil prices and fears of a prolonged US-Iran conflict worsened Pakistan's inflation and economic outlook.
He said the SBP had kept the policy rate unchanged since April 2026 despite rising headline inflation, expecting global oil prices to settle and bring inflation down. However, renewed increases in oil prices and fears of further escalation had changed the outlook, prompting the Monetary Policy Committee to raise the rate.
He considered the increase necessary amid double-digit inflation, saying it was consistent with a cautious approach of making small adjustments to signal the central bank's commitment to price stability. Although higher interest rates might not directly curb supply-side inflation, he said, the increase sent the right signal to the market.
However, he warned that if fears of conflict persisted and oil prices remained elevated, the SBP could introduce a series of gradual rate increases over the next three to four months. This could further slow an already sluggish economy, although the rate would not return to its previous peak.
He projected average headline inflation of 11-13% in fiscal year 2026-27, higher than previously anticipated, while economic growth could fall below 3.5%.
The concerns over growth were echoed by Pakistan Institute of Development Economics (PIDE) Professor of Economics and Registrar Dr Nasir Iqbal, who argued that maintaining the policy rate at 11.5% would have been a more balanced response to the prevailing inflationary risks.
Referring to PIDE's Monetary Policy Assessment for October 2026, he said price pressures were largely driven by supply-side constraints rather than excessive domestic demand. Energy prices, food prices and external shocks remained the main sources of inflation, he added. Higher interest rates cannot directly address these constraints. Instead, tighter monetary conditions raise borrowing costs for businesses, discourage private investment and increase the government's debt-servicing burden, potentially weakening an already fragile economic recovery.
With September inflation at 10.3% and growth remaining modest, he said further monetary tightening risked adding to the pressure on businesses without adequately addressing the underlying sources of inflation.
Looking ahead, he expects inflation to remain elevated and volatile if global energy prices and domestic food supply pressures persist. High borrowing costs are also likely to constrain investment, employment generation and economic activity, keeping growth moderate rather than allowing it to accelerate significantly.
He urged the SBP to avoid further rate increases unless there was clear evidence that inflation had become broad-based and persistent.
His assessment highlights the limitations of relying on monetary tightening when inflation is driven primarily by supply-side factors. While higher interest rates can restrain demand, they cannot directly lower international energy prices or resolve domestic food supply disruptions.
The three economists' assessments underline the difficult choices facing monetary policymakers. Persistent inflation and uncertainty over global energy prices could keep the policy rate elevated, but the cost of credit may restrict business investment and weigh on economic activity. The outlook will depend partly on whether geopolitical tensions ease and energy prices stabilise enough to allow inflation to decline.
While Suleri sees limited scope for rate cuts without a sustained improvement in inflation, Javed warns that prolonged oil price pressures could lead to further gradual increases. Meanwhile, the PIDE economist cautions that additional tightening could deepen the economic costs without resolving the supply-side pressures driving inflation. The challenge for the SBP will be to contain inflation while avoiding further constraints on investment, employment and the broader economic recovery.

items.title: PSX climbs 1,270 points as policy fears ease
items.summary:
The Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) put on an impressive show on Wednesday as the benchmark KSE-100 index staged a strong rally, driven by accelerating purchases in the final hours despite lingering concerns over monetary tightening and rising international oil prices.
The market opened on a steady note and quickly advanced, reaching 164,830.55, up 363.35 points, or 0.22%, within minutes of the opening bell. It touched the intra-day high of 166,100.34 and low of 164,355.83. Investors came back and buying gathered pace late in the session, which helped the KSE-100 index close with notable gains of 1,269.55 points, or 0.77%, at 165,736.76.
Similarly, Asian equities rose on optimism surrounding artificial intelligence demand and ahead of earnings announcements by major US companies. The positive tone in regional markets lent support to investor sentiment, although geopolitical risks continued to cloud the outlook. Oil prices, meanwhile, remained a major concern.
Ahmed Sheraz, equity trader
items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
The Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) put on an impressive show on Wednesday as the benchmark KSE-100 index staged a strong rally, driven by accelerating purchases in the final hours despite lingering concerns over monetary tightening and rising international oil prices.
The market opened on a steady note and quickly advanced, reaching 164,830.55, up 363.35 points, or 0.22%, within minutes of the opening bell. It touched the intra-day high of 166,100.34 and low of 164,355.83. Investors came back and buying gathered pace late in the session, which helped the KSE-100 index close with notable gains of 1,269.55 points, or 0.77%, at 165,736.76.
Similarly, Asian equities rose on optimism surrounding artificial intelligence demand and ahead of earnings announcements by major US companies. The positive tone in regional markets lent support to investor sentiment, although geopolitical risks continued to cloud the outlook. Oil prices, meanwhile, remained a major concern.
Ahmed Sheraz, equity trader at KASB KTrade, noted that the KSE-100 closed with an increase of 1,270 points (+0.77%) in a broadly positive session, with approximately 183 million shares traded. Buying interest remained widespread, led by commercial banks, fertiliser, automobile and power stocks.
Among major contributors, Fauji Fertiliser led the rally following an attractive Rs18.5/share dividend announcement and its results were broadly in line with expectations. National Bank followed by posting decent earnings, while Hub Power supported the index on the back of a Rs5-per-share payout.
Market sentiment continued to improve after the State Bank's 50-basis-point policy rate hike to 12%, which was lower than expectations. This supported banking stocks, while cyclical sectors also witnessed renewed buying interest, allowing the market to consolidate at higher levels. "However, Brent crude hovering around $115 per barrel remains a key concern, alongside geopolitical uncertainty involving Iran, Israel and the US," Sheraz added.
According to JS Global analyst Nawaz Ali, bullish activity continued at the PSX for the third consecutive session, where the benchmark KSE-100 index gained 1,270 points. Buying interest was driven by investor optimism about a potential easing of geopolitical tensions.
Meanwhile, the corporate results season remained in full swing, with earnings-driven activity also contributing to market momentum. National Bank's better-than-expected results triggered stock buying in the banking sector. "Looking ahead, any positive developments regarding the US-Iran situation that lead to a decline in crude oil prices could further improve investor confidence," Ali stated.
Topline Securities observed that the benchmark index maintained a positive trajectory throughout the session, touching the intra-day high of 1,633 points, while the downside remained limited to 111 points, reflecting sustained buying interest and improved investor sentiment. Overall trading volumes increased to 578 million shares from Tuesday's total of 402 million. The value of traded shares stood at Rs26 billion.
Shares of 496 companies were traded in the ready market. Of these, 269 stocks closed higher, 180 fell and 47 remained unchanged.
Foreign investors sold shares worth Rs624 million, the National Clearing Company reported.

items.title: IESCO Electricity Suspension Schedule for 29 October
items.summary:
The Islamabad Electric Supply Company (IESCO) has announced electricity suspensions across parts of Islamabad, Rawalpindi City and Rawalpindi Cantt on Thursday, October 29.
According to the shutdown schedule shared by IESCO, power supply will remain suspended on more than 100 11kV feeders, mostly from 9:00 AM to 2:00 PM, for annual maintenance, construction and development work, and maintenance of power transformers at grid stations.
Several feeders in Rawat will see an earlier outage from 7:00 AM to 12:00 PM, while maintenance on four 132kV transmission lines will continue until 4:00 PM. IESCO said no grid station will be affected by the transmission line work.
IESCO also announced power outages in Islamabad and Rawalpindi for October 28 for similar maintenance and development work.

items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
Meta has introduced a new AI-powered app called Waddle World, allowing users to raise a virtual pet, interact with it, and share details about their daily lives.
The app is similar to the classic Tamagotchi virtual pet games but adds artificial intelligence to make interactions more personal.
Waddle World is currently available for iOS and Android users in the Philippines. Meta has not announced when it will launch in other countries.
How Waddle World Works
Waddle World features a 16-bit pixel-style environment where users can hatch and raise their own virtual pets.
Players can feed their pets, play games with them, and interact with them throughout the day.
Unlike traditional virtual pet games, Waddle World uses AI to learn about users through their interactions. The app also allows users to share their thoughts and experiences by speaking or typing.
The virtual pet listens and turns these conversations into journal entries written from its own perspective, complete with small illustrations.
Additionally, users can play short mini-games and receive weekly emails summarizing what their virtual pet has learned about them.
Meta launches AI Tamagotchi!
Meet Waddle World, an AI-powered virtual pet that:
• Remembers your conversations
• Creates illustrated journals
• Sends personalised postcards
• Lets you feed it and play games
Currently available in the Philippines. pic.twitter.com/S8WJJFNE9R
— Matt Navarra (@MattNavarra) October 27, 2026
No Daily Tasks or Rewards to Maintain
Meta says Waddle World is designed to be a relaxing experience rather than an app that pressures users to return every day.
Unlike many mobile games, it does not require players to maintain daily login streaks or chase high scores.
Users can spend a few minutes or longer with their pets without worrying about losing progress.
Meta also describes Waddle World as a virtual pet experience rather than a traditional AI chatbot, assistant, or productivity tool.
The app is intended for adults aged 18 and older.
Meta Continues Testing New AI Apps
Waddle World is part of Meta’s ongoing efforts to explore new uses for artificial intelligence beyond traditional chatbots.
The company has previously introduced Pocket, which allows users to create games using AI, and Vibes, an app for generating AI videos.
Meta has also been developing a Tamagotchi-style physical device powered by its Muse AI technology.
The new virtual pet app could be an early experiment related to that project, although Meta has not confirmed a connection.
Availability
Waddle World is currently available for free on the Apple App Store and Google Play Store in the Philippines.
Social media consultant Matt Navarra highlighted the app on October 27, drawing attention to Meta’s latest AI experiment.
For now, it remains unclear whether Meta plans to release Waddle World worldwide.
The launch also comes as AI companion services face increasing scrutiny. Companies including Character.AI and OpenAI have faced lawsuits alleging that their products harmed teenagers.
Meta has not said whether those concerns influenced Waddle World’s design or its adults-only availability.

items.author: Business Desk
items.content:
JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman took a swipe at Defence Minister Khawaja Asif in the National Assembly on Wednesday, saying defence agreements were being negotiated in Iran while Pakistan’s defence minister was at home.
“Khawaja Asif sahib is also present here. A defence agreement is being made in Iran, and the defence minister is sitting here,” Fazlur Rehman said, before turning Asif’s own famous line against him: “Koi sharam hoti hai, koi haya hoti hai” (Have some shame, have some decency).
The remark drew laughter in the House, and a video of the exchange shared by JUI-F Senator Kamran Murtaza has since gone viral on social media.
Remark Linked to Tehran Talks
Fazlur Rehman’s comment referred to the high-level talks held in Tehran on Monday, where Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Asim Munir, Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman, and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and other senior Iranian officials.
The three envoys represented the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, the military alliance signed by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkiye in August.
It was the first meeting between representatives of the pact and Iranian leaders, and focused on regional security and preventing a fresh military escalation.
Khawaja Asif said a day later that Pakistan would defend Saudi Arabia with full force under the pact.
Asif’s Own Words Come Back to Haunt Him
“Koi sharam hoti hai, koi haya hoti hai” is one of the most quoted lines in Pakistani politics. Khawaja Asif famously used it in the National Assembly years ago to criticise PTI lawmakers, and it has since become a popular meme.
Social media users were quick to point out that this may be the first time the line has been used against Asif himself, with him sitting in the House.
During the same speech, Fazlur Rehman also called on the government and opposition to sit together and draw up a new Charter of Democracy.
