items.author: Usama Anjum
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The Senate Standing Committee on Cabinet Division has given the relevant authorities one month to review the issue of reducing taxes on imported and used mobile phones in Pakistan.
The matter was discussed during a meeting chaired by Senator Rana Mahmood-ul-Hassan on Wednesday, where lawmakers and government officials raised concerns over the existing mobile phone taxation structure.
The committee chairman questioned why older smartphones are subject to the same taxes as newer models. Referring to his own three-year-old phone, he said that the device was being taxed at the same rate as a new smartphone.
A member of the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) urged the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) to reduce mobile phone taxes and suggested calculating minimum duties based on smartphone models rather than storage capacity.
The Cabinet Division secretary, however, reminded the PTA representative that taxation policy does not fall within the authority’s jurisdiction. He also called for lower taxes on locally assembled mobile phones while supporting taxation on high-end devices.
High Mobile Taxes Could Affect 5G Adoption
Federal Minister for Information Technology and Telecommunication Shaza Fatima Khawaja informed the committee that locally assembled devices currently meet approximately 90 to 95 percent of Pakistan’s mobile phone requirements.
She explained that any decision regarding further tax relief for older smartphones would fall under the Ministry of Finance’s Tax Policy Office.
Senator Dilawar Khan also called for a reduction in mobile phone duties, arguing that affordable smartphones would encourage greater mobile phone ownership and increased data consumption.
Committee chairman Rana Mahmood-ul-Hassan referred to concerns raised by the GSMA, saying that excessive taxation could undermine the adoption of 5G services in Pakistan.
Meanwhile, Senator Abdul Qadir proposed removing taxes on iPads and tablets, highlighting their importance for employment and professional activities. He also called for additional tax relief on used smartphones.
Following the discussion, the committee directed the relevant authorities to examine the matter and provide an update within one month.
No immediate reduction in mobile phone taxes has been approved. The committee will review the issue again after receiving the relevant input from government departments.

items.title: Iran's Revolutionary Court sentences director Panahi to jail term, travel ban
items.summary:
Iran's Revolutionary Court sentenced award-winning film director Jafar ​Panahi to five years in ‌prison and the seizure of all his assets, Iran's semi-official Nournews ​reported on Wednesday, citing ​his lawyer but without mentioning the ⁠charges he faced.
The court ​also banned Panahi from leaving the ​country for two years and from any social media activity, the report ​said.
Panahi's lawyer, Mostafa Nili, could not be immediately reached for comment.
Panahi, whose film It Was Just an Accident won the Palme d'Or at the 2025 Cannes film festival, has been arrested several times in the past for his filmmaking.
Despite having been sentenced to a one-year prison sentence in absentia in 2025 for propaganda activities against the system, Panahi returned to the country in March.

items.author: APP
items.content:
Religious scholars, spiritual leaders and representatives of different faiths unanimously reaffirmed the fatwa (religious ruling) against suicide attacks, terrorism, extremism and the killing of innocent people, while fully endorsing the national narrative of Paigham-e-Pakistan.
The declaration was issued at a joint meeting organised by the National Paigham-e-Aman Committee (NPAC) on Wednesday, also referred to as the Qaumi Paigham-e-Aman Committee, and the Balochistan Paigham-e-Aman Committee at Jamia Salafia Dawat-ul-Haq in Quetta.
The declaration stated that suicide attacks are forbidden in Islam, the killing of innocent people is impermissible, and terrorism runs contrary to the fundamental teachings of Islam and other religions.
It categorically stated that no individual, group or organisation had the right to engage in bloodshed, carry out armed actions against the state or take the law into its own hands in the name of religion, sect or any ideology.
Strongly condemning the exploitation of women, children, young people and students for terrorism and suicide attacks, the participants described such acts as religiously forbidden, morally reprehensible and serious crimes against humanity.
Read More: Uniting faiths, strengthening Pakistan
The declaration warned that those who mislead the younger generation and turn them into instruments of terrorism are enemies of human life and Pakistan’s future.
The participants also expressed full support for the efforts of the Pakistan Army and national security institutions against what the declaration described as Fitna al-Khawarij and Fitna al-Hindustan. They said the nation stood alongside the armed forces in efforts to eliminate terrorism and safeguard national security and stability.
Last year, the federal government officially designated all terrorist groups operating in Balochistan as Fitna al-Hindustan, accusing India of sponsoring a proxy war through the outfits, while Fitna al-Khawarij is the state-designated term for the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP).
In the joint declaration, protecting the country's security, stability and the lives and property of its people was described as a shared national responsibility.
Emphasising the importance of peace in Balochistan, the participants resolved to stand united against terrorism, extremism and sectarian violence, stressing that no one should be allowed to undermine peace under the guise of religion or sect.
Also Read: PM Shehbaz defends emergency, governor’s rule in K-P, blames PTI for resurgence of terrorism
The meeting also pledged continued joint efforts to promote inter-sectarian and interfaith harmony, religious tolerance, national unity and peace in the province. Participants expressed their commitment to addressing issues faced by mosques and religious seminaries and strengthening cooperation with the government and relevant institutions.
The meeting further called for a coordinated effort by scholars, faith leaders, parents, teachers and prominent social figures to protect young people from extremist ideologies, hate speech and the influence of terrorist organisations.
Mosques, religious seminaries, educational institutions and religious and social centres, it said, should be used to promote peace, tolerance, unity and national cohesion.
The younger generation, they stressed, represented the country's future and must not be allowed to become fuel for terrorism.
Tribute to Field Marshal Asim Munir
Separately, the participants unanimously adopted a resolution paying tribute to Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir for his efforts towards unity in the Muslim world, cohesion within the Muslim Ummah, regional stability and global peace.
The resolution commended his diplomatic efforts to promote peace and negotiations between the United States and Iran, improve relations between Saudi Arabia and Iran, and facilitate high-level talks among Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, Turkiye and Iran in Tehran on October 26.
Read More: Pakistan condemns 'reprehensible' Houthi attacks in Makkah, Madinah regions
Describing these initiatives as significant for reducing regional tensions and strengthening cooperation among Muslim countries, the resolution said efforts towards Muslim unity and international peace were a source of pride for Pakistan and of value to the wider Muslim Ummah.
The participants appealed to all political and religious parties in Pakistan to support constructive diplomatic initiatives undertaken in the national interest.
The meeting was chaired by Pakistan Ulema Council chairman and NPAC Coordinator Hafiz Muhammad Tahir Mehmood Ashrafi and attended by Maulana Ali Muhammad Abu Turab, Dr Asif Mir, Mufti Yousaf Kashmiri, Maulana Syed Samiullah Agha, Maulana Qasim Haqqani, Allama Nasrullah Hussaini, Mufti Muhammad Jan Qasmi, Maulana Hizbullah Usmani, Maulana Samiullah Awan, Maulana Abdul Rahman, Maulana Abdullah Haqqani, Mufti Umar Farooq, Maulana Abdur Rahman Salafi, Pastor Simon Bashir, Sardar Jasbir Singh and other religious scholars and representatives of different faiths.

items.title: Bulk carrier docks at Karachi port with 51,000 metric tonnes of wheat
items.summary:
The Karachi Port Trust (KPT) on Wednesday said a vessel carrying 51,000 metric tonnes of wheat has docked at the port, with handling operations underway at Berths 16 and 17, highlighting the port’s role in ensuring the uninterrupted supply of essential commodities as well as food security.
“The geared vessel MV Gokova M, carrying a declared manifest of 51,000 metric tonnes of wheat, was allocated Berths 16 and 17 and arrived at Karachi Port at 1225 hours on October 28, 2026,” the authority said in a post on X.
It added that the bulk carrier, MV Gokova M, unloaded cargo at Karachi Gateway Terminal Multipurpose Limited (KGTML).

He said all the provincial governments were consulted before the move.
Highlighting the food security strategy, he also announced that strategic wheat reserves of up to six million metric tonnes would be maintained during the current year to ensure uninterrupted grain supply and protect the country against potential market disruptions.

items.author: Anjali Jain
items.content:
AI unicorn Sarvam AI is reportedly in talks to raise funds from Nasdaq-listed IT services company Cognizant Technology Solutions as part of a funding round that could value the startup at $3.5 Bn to $4 Bn.
The Bengaluru-based startup is seeking around $300 Mn in fresh capital, ET reported, citing sources. The proposed valuation would be more than double the $1.5 Bn valuation it secured in its previous funding round.
Cognizant could acquire a small stake in Sarvam, although discussions are ongoing, the report said. The startup has also held talks with large domestic enterprises to anchor the round.
Inc42 has reached out to Sarvam and Cognizant for comments on the development. The story will be updated on receiving a response.
The talks come four months after Sarvam raised $234 Mn in the first close of its $300 Mn Series B in June 2026, becoming a unicorn. HCLTech led the round with a $150 Mn investment, while Bessemer Venture Partners participated alongside existing investors Khosla Ventures and Peak XV Partners.
An investment by Cognizant would make it the second IT services major on Sarvam’s cap table after HCLTech.
IT companies are looking to strengthen their AI capabilities as advances in generative and agentic AI raise questions about traditional outsourcing models. AI agents are increasingly capable of automating tasks across software development, application maintenance, and back-office operations.
Cognizant has indicated that investments and acquisitions could support its shift towards a business built around platforms and customer outcomes.
During an earnings call in April, CEO Ravi Kumar said Cognizant saw acquisition opportunities aligned with its ambition to become an AI builder, focusing on platforms and delivering outcomes rather than billing based on effort.
Sarvam’s Enterprise Push
Founded in 2023 by Pratyush Kumar and Vivek Raghavan, Sarvam develops foundational AI models, computing infrastructure, and enterprise applications. Its offerings target businesses and government agencies seeking tools tailored to Indian languages, data-security requirements, and local use cases.
The startup has released several models in recent months, including Sarvam Vision 2.1, a vision-language model for processing documents and recognising text in Indian languages, and Saaras V4, its speech-to-text model. In October, it launched Bulbul V4 Flash, a text-to-speech model for generating natural speech across Indian languages.
Sarvam is also expanding its enterprise business, with customers including Life Insurance Corporation of India, SBI Life, IDFC First Bank, Tata Capital, and CRED, according to ET. It recently appointed former Google Cloud India head Sashikumar Sreedharan as president and chief business officer.
Earlier this week, Sarvam announced a memorandum of understanding with Headquarters Integrated Defence Staff under the defence ministry to establish a framework for AI projects across the Indian Army, Navy, and Air Force.

items.title: Flavio Bolsonaro lands in Miami with his family after Trump offers Brazil exit
items.summary:
Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro and his family arrived in Miami on Wednesday, where the United States government will grant them entry visas after he refused ​to comply with a Brazilian Supreme Court order to surrender his passports.
Bolsonaro, who lost ‌Sunday's presidential election to leftist incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, left Brazil under a shroud of secrecy after the court order, which relates to a money-laundering investigation in which he denies wrongdoing.
Reuters TV images showed Bolsonaro, ​his wife and two daughters disembarking from the Gulfstream G400 and heading into Miami-Opa Locka ​Executive Airport.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro and his family arrived in Miami on Wednesday, where the United States government will grant them entry visas after he refused ​to comply with a Brazilian Supreme Court order to surrender his passports.
Bolsonaro, who lost ‌Sunday's presidential election to leftist incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, left Brazil under a shroud of secrecy after the court order, which relates to a money-laundering investigation in which he denies wrongdoing.
Reuters TV images showed Bolsonaro, ​his wife and two daughters disembarking from the Gulfstream G400 and heading into Miami-Opa Locka ​Executive Airport.
Read: Brazil’s Lula wins historic fourth term, Flavio Bolsonaro refuses to concede
Breaking news: Defeated Brazilian presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro has arrived in Miami from Ecuador, after he defied a Brazilian judicial order to surrender his passports in connection with a corruption and money-laundering investigation. https://t.co/56SV6QiY0X
— The Washington Post (@washingtonpost) October 28, 2026
Their journey to the United States captured attention across the region. They ⁠entered northern Argentina late on Tuesday evening, according to the country's migration department, and then took ​a private jet to the Ecuadorean city of Guayaquil. From there, they flew to Miami.
Neither Argentina's presidency, ​Ecuadorean ministries, nor Baires Fly, the operator of the private jet, responded to requests for comment.
Fresh Brazil-US rift
Bolsonaro's departure threatens to deepen a rift between the two most populous nations in the Americas.
Lula has accused Washington of colluding ​with the Bolsonaro family to help return them to power. Ahead of Sunday's election, Reuters reported ​on a US State Department campaign to restore the Bolsonaros to office.
Trump told reporters on Wednesday that he would approve ‌of Bolsonaro coming to the United States, after his State Department said it would give them entry visas.
"Would you approve of Flávio Bolsonaro coming to the United States?"@POTUS: "I would approve. I think they're fine people. The election was really strange and I thought it was terrible... It would be okay with me." pic.twitter.com/dYTBXLGAlb
— Rapid Response 47 (@RapidResponse47) October 28, 2026
Trump has previously alleged that Flavio's father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, was a victim of judicial persecution in Brazil.
Jair Bolsonaro also travelled to the United States after refusing to concede defeat to Lula in ​2022, during Joe Biden's presidency. ​He eventually returned to ⁠Brazil but was later sentenced to 27 years in prison for plotting a coup after supporters stormed government buildings in Brasilia.
Flavio Bolsonaro had been ​widely expected to win Sunday's election but suffered a shock defeat.
Flavio Bolsonaro, who loses ​his immunity ⁠from prosecution when his Senate term ends in February, had said on Monday, after the order to hand in his passports, that he had no plans to flee.
"I have never thought about leaving the country," ⁠he ​said. "I will hand over my passports and defend myself against ​this travesty, which is a clear attempt to intimidate me."

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Google has opened registration for its Registered App Stores program, which aims to make installing third-party app stores on Android devices easier. The program will allow eligible app store developers to offer a simplified installation process, reducing the number of steps users need to follow.
Announced earlier this year, the initiative is linked to proposed changes arising from Google’s legal dispute with Epic Games. The company says the program will help third-party app stores reach more Android users while maintaining platform security.
According to Google, enrollment is now open to eligible app stores outside the United States. The new installation experience is scheduled to roll out on December 1, 2026.
Google Opens Registration for One-Tap Installation for Third-Party App Stores
Under the new program, registered app stores will be able to offer a more convenient installation process. Users will no longer need to go through additional system confirmation screens when installing these stores through the supported process.
The change is expected to simplify sideloading, which allows users to install apps or app stores from sources other than Google Play. Currently, Android may display several warnings and confirmation screens before completing such installations.
The new process will also support automatic background updates and download progress indicators. These features should make it easier for users to install and maintain third-party app stores on their devices.
However, the simplified experience will only apply to stores that complete Google’s registration process. App stores that do not enroll will continue using the existing installation process.
Android 17 QPR2 and Later Required
The Registered App Stores program will support devices running Android 17 QPR2 or later. The initial rollout will be available to users outside the United States.
Google has also confirmed that participating developers will receive documentation, onboarding assistance, and access to additional tools. These include the Android Developer ID API, which is intended to support the identification and management of app developers.
The company says the program is designed to balance easier access to third-party app stores with security measures that help protect Android users.
Registration Fees and Security Requirements
Developers who want to participate will have to pay an annual registration fee. Google says the fee will cover access to the program’s new capabilities and operational support.
Additional review fees may apply to app stores whose catalogues exceed Google’s specified malware-related threshold. This suggests that the company will continue to monitor security risks associated with participating stores.
Although registration is optional, developers may find the program useful because it offers a simpler installation process and additional support from Google.
Google Plans US Expansion
For now, the program is launching for eligible app stores outside the United States. Google has indicated that it plans to bring the initiative to the US after the court approves its proposed settlement with Epic Games.
The changes could give Android users more flexibility in choosing where they download apps. They may also help alternative app stores compete more effectively with Google Play by reducing the difficulties associated with installation.
The December 1 rollout will be an important step in Google’s effort to introduce a more streamlined sideloading experience. However, the benefits will depend on how many third-party app stores join the program and how widely the new installation process becomes available.

Samsung’s upcoming foldable smartphone, the W27, has appeared in a new set of leaked renders ahead of its expected launch in China on October 29. The images offer a closer look at the phone’s design, including its dark blue finish, gold accents, and rear camera setup.
The Samsung W27 will join the company’s China-exclusive W series. These devices typically feature premium designs based on Samsung’s flagship Galaxy Z Fold smartphones. This year’s model is expected to follow the same approach, with reports suggesting that it will share its specifications with the Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra.
Samsung W27 Design Revealed in Leaked Renders
The newly leaked renders, shared by well-known tipster Evan Blass, show the Samsung W27 from several angles. The phone features a dark blue exterior with gold details, giving it a more luxurious appearance than the standard Galaxy Z Fold series.
The rear panel includes a camera module similar to the one seen on the Galaxy Z Fold8. However, Samsung has added a gold W series logo near the bottom of the back panel to distinguish the device from its regular foldable phones.
The overall design suggests that Samsung is focusing on a premium look rather than introducing major visual changes. The W27 is expected to appeal to buyers who want a high-end foldable smartphone with an exclusive finish.
Expected Specifications and Storage Options
According to previous leaks, the Samsung W27 will offer the same hardware specifications as the Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra. However, Samsung has not officially confirmed these details.
The company may launch the W27 in a single configuration featuring 16GB of RAM and 1TB of internal storage. This would provide plenty of memory for multitasking and enough space for apps, photos, videos, and other files.
The shared hardware would also mean that the W27 is likely to deliver a similar overall experience to Samsung’s flagship book-style foldable. More details about its processor, displays, cameras, and battery are expected to become clear at launch.
Samsung W27 Price Expected to Be High
The Samsung W27 will surely carry a premium price tag. The W series already targets the high-end market. It will come with the combination of an exclusive design, 16GB of RAM, and 1TB of storage could make the new model particularly expensive.
Since the device is designed for the Chinese market, its availability in other regions remains uncertain. Samsung has yet to announce any plans for an international release.
Samsung W27 Launch Date
The company will unveil the W27 in China on October 29, 2026. The launch should confirm its final design, specifications, pricing, and availability.
Until then, the leaked renders and reported specifications provide an early look at what Samsung may offer with its next premium foldable smartphone.

items.author: Shrishti Bisht
items.content:
Naukri parent Info Edge said founder and vice chairman Sanjeev Bikhchandani will take over as executive vice chairman, MD and group CEO from December 3, 2026.
He will succeed Hitesh Oberoi, who will step down as MD and CEO at the close of business on December 2, ending nearly 27 years in a full-time executive role at the company.
Oberoi, who had joined Info Edge as a COO and director in 2000, is stepping down to “devote more time to his personal interests in education, entrepreneurship, institution building, investing and philanthropy.”
Oberoi will continue to be associated with the company as a non-executive, non-independent director from December 3, subject to shareholder approval.
Oberoi said he believed the company was ready for the transition, citing the strength of its leadership team and progress across its businesses. Naukri has developed an AI and data strategy, 99acres has strengthened its market position and become a cash-generating business, while Jeevansathi and Aisle have turned profitable.
Speaking during the company’s earnings call, Oberoi said Info Edge had made progress in translating Naukri’s AI strategy into revenue-generating products.
“We wanted to have a clearly articulated AI strategy for the company in Naukri. And I think we’ve done a fairly good job on that front. And it’s now at the back end, and now in terms of products, which are generating revenue. So I think we are sorted on that front,” he said.
Oberoi added that he remained financially and emotionally attached to Info Edge and would continue on its board, subject to shareholder approval, despite stepping away from his full-time operating role.
During Oberoi’s tenure as CEO, Info Edge’s market capitalisation increased from approximately ₹2,500 Cr to ₹80,000 Cr. It also expanded its portfolio of consumer internet businesses and emerged as a significant investor in India’s startup ecosystem.
Bikhchandani Yet To Decide On Leadership Structure
Speaking about his expanded role, Bikhchandani said Info Edge had not yet decided whether to bring in additional leaders or how to structure its top management.
“Hitesh is still there for a month. And beyond that, he is there anyway and available. And I will be taking his counsel. I will be obviously talking to the nomination and remuneration committee (NRC). And we will figure out how to evolve the leadership structure at the top going forward,” Bikhchandani said during the company’s earnings call.
“The first priority will be to give internal people an opportunity to grow,” Bikhchandani said, adding that he would consult Oberoi, the NRC and senior employees before deciding on the way forward.
Asked whether his appointment was an interim arrangement ahead of an external appointment, Bikhchandani said no such discussions had taken place at the board level.
“I’m 63 years old. So, I cannot continue for 20 years. That isn’t happening. But let me go in. Let the situation stabilise and then let’s see what happens,” he said.
Info Edge Financials Disclosure
Info Edge’s consolidated net profit rose 87% YoY to ₹649.8 Cr in Q2 FY27 from ₹347.5 Cr a year earlier. It increased 32.6% sequentially from ₹490.1 Cr in Q1 FY27.
Revenue from operations grew 12.2% YoY and 2.6% sequentially to ₹903.9 Cr. Other income surged 164.8% YoY to ₹428.4 Cr from ₹161.8 Cr, taking total income to ₹1,332.3 Cr against ₹967.2 Cr a year earlier. Total expenses increased 4.5% to ₹588.6 Cr from ₹563.5 Cr.
The board also declared an interim dividend of ₹3 per share for FY27, fixing November 6, 2026, as the record date.
Separately, Info Edge approved the sale of its entire stakes in healthtech startup MedCords and employment platform Unnati Online for approximately ₹5,000 each.

items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The government has acknowledged that the rollout of QR-code-enabled identity cards is being carried out in phases, while declining to provide an assessment of overseas Pakistanis potentially affected by travel restrictions linked to expired or invalid National Identity Cards for Overseas Pakistanis (NICOPs).
In a written reply to the National Assembly, Minister for Interior and Narcotics Control Senator Syed Mohsin Raza Naqvi stated that the question regarding the number of overseas Pakistanis affected by the new travel rules did not pertain to the National Database and Registration Authority (NADRA).
The minister, however, outlined a range of measures introduced by NADRA to facilitate overseas Pakistanis in obtaining and renewing identity documents, including the expansion of services at Pakistani missions abroad, weekend mobile registration operations and online applications through the Pak ID mobile application.
The government approved the new QR-code-based polycarbonate identity card format on February 23, 2026, followed by amendments to the National Identity Card and Pakistan Origin Card Rules, 2002, notified on February 24, 2026.
According to the reply, the new card incorporates a secure, readable QR code containing protected applicant information, including the family number, which can be accessed through the Pak ID mobile application and used for authentication without specialised card readers.
The new format is intended to overcome limitations associated with chip-based identity cards, as the establishment of nationwide chip-reader infrastructure proved difficult due to cost and interoperability considerations. The polycarbonate cards also offer enhanced durability and security, while domestic production is expected to reduce reliance on imported card material.
NADRA is introducing the new format progressively under an approved transition plan. Existing Smart CNICs, Smart NICOPs and Smart Pakistan Origin Cards (POCs) continue to be processed and issued during the transition, subject to applicable rules and the availability of card material.
To improve access to identity services abroad, NADRA has equipped 10 registration centres located at Pakistani missions with its Pak ID software application, enabling faster processing and increasing daily capacity, particularly for NICOP renewals.
Mobile Registration Operations are also being conducted on weekends through registration centres in the United Kingdom, Saudi Arabia and Dubai. The initiative is aimed at facilitating overseas Pakistanis who cannot visit NADRA offices during regular working hours.
In addition, 25 NADRA counters are operational at Pakistani missions abroad to assist overseas Pakistanis with the submission of online applications and access to identity-document services.
The Pak ID mobile application provides another channel for submitting and processing applications remotely, potentially reducing the need for overseas applicants to visit NADRA offices for routine renewals.
The minister also highlighted the facility for dematerialised identity cards, introduced under an SRO dated September 9, 2025. Eligible individuals holding valid identity cards can access their digital credentials through the Pak ID application once the physical-card application reaches the printing stage.
Subject to applicable rules, the dematerialised card carries the same legal validity, evidentiary value and enforceability as its physical counterpart, the reply stated.
The government further stated that eligible NICOP holders can continue to avail themselves of associated facilities, including visa-free travel to Pakistan.
However, the reply did not provide the requested estimate of the number of overseas Pakistanis potentially affected by the travel rules, nor did it detail a specific communication strategy to counter confusion or misinformation surrounding the requirements.

items.content:
Online astrology platform Astrotalk reported a 895% increase in its consolidated net profit to ₹222 Cr in FY26 from around ₹22 Cr in the previous fiscal year.
Its operating revenue rose 55% to ₹1,823 Cr from ₹1,176 Cr in FY25, driven by growth in consultations, international markets, and ecommerce, according to the audited consolidated financial statement.
Profit before tax nearly quadrupled to ₹296 Cr from ₹75 Cr a year earlier.
International Markets Drive Growth
Astrotalk’s international revenue rose 2.6X to ₹621 Cr in FY26 from ₹236 Cr in the previous fiscal year. Overseas markets contributed 34% of operating revenue, up from 20% in FY25.
Meanwhile, domestic revenue grew 28% to ₹1,202 Cr from ₹940 Cr in FY25.
The company said it has been investing in marketing to expand internationally. Its overall marketing spend jumped 144.2% to ₹823 Cr in FY26 from ₹337 Cr a year earlier.
Ecommerce Outpaces Consultation Growth
Consultations delivered through chat, calls, and video remained Astrotalk’s largest revenue source, generating ₹1,657 Cr in FY26, up 45% from ₹1,139 Cr a year earlier. The business accounted for about 91% of operating revenue.
Meanwhile, ecommerce revenue more than quadrupled to ₹166 Cr from ₹37 Cr in FY25. Its share of operating revenue increased to 9.1% from 3.1%.
Astrotalk Store sells spiritual products, including rudraksha, gemstones, crystals, and Vastu products, through its own platforms and third-party marketplaces such as Amazon, Flipkart, and Blinkit.
Launched in November 2024, the ecommerce business forms part of Astrotalk’s push beyond consultations. Gupta previously told Inc42 that the startup had invested ₹40 Cr in building inventory, strengthening supply chains, and adding product categories after an initial investment of ₹30 Lakh.
The startup has also outlined plans for offline stores and a separate gemstones offering.
“We set out to build a diversified, global business from India, and FY26 shows it is working. A third of our revenue now comes from outside India, and Astrotalk Store has grown into a real second business,” said Puneet Gupta, founder and CEO of Astrotalk.
He further added, “The reason we are growing rapidly is that we are able to create a positive impact in the lives of our customers.”
Cash Reserves Strengthen
Astrotalk’s cash flow from operations increased 21% YoY to ₹229 Cr in FY26.
Its year-end cash and investments rose 41.1% to ₹917 Cr from ₹650 Cr. This included cash, bank deposits, mutual funds, and bonds.
The startup said it funded its FY26 investments through internal cash flows, supporting its expansion into international markets and new business lines without relying on fresh external capital.
Founded in 2017 by Puneet Gupta and Anmol Jain, Astrotalk connects users with astrologers and charges for consultations on its platform. It has raised $34 Mn to date from investors including Left Lane Capital and Elev8 Venture Partners.
In August this year, Astrotalk joined the unicorn club following an ESOP buyback at a $1 Bn valuation.
The startup competes against the likes of InstaAstro, Astroyogi, AstroSage Kundli, among others.

items.author: Faran Khan
items.content:
As winter sets in, major public hospitals in Karachi have seen a visible spike in flu patients brought in for treatment.
Aga Khan University Hospital  (AKUH) reported around 400 cases of influenza, a more dangerous variant of the common flu, this year, with the H1N1 strain infecting residents.
Speaking to The Express Tribune, Professor Dr Faisal Mahmood, section head of Infectious Diseases at AKUH, said the H1N1 strain — also known as swine flu for its similarity with the influenza virus known for infecting pigs — was currently circulating in Karachi.
“Influenza viruses evolve over time, giving rise to new variants,” Dr Mahmood said, cautioning that the number of cases could increase further by the end of the year.
Dr Mahmood said not every patient suspected of having influenza was tested, with testing generally reserved for those who were seriously ill. He warned that influenza could lead to serious complications, including pneumonia, particularly among vulnerable individuals.
Read: Rising flu cases trigger mandatory Umrah vaccination
He stressed that vaccination was an important preventive measure and urged older people, children and those with weakened immune systems to get vaccinated against the contagious respiratory infectious disease.
Meanwhile, Civil Hospital Karachi Emergency Department Head Dr Imran Sarwar Sheikh said the number of patients reporting flu symptoms had doubled during the last few days, and the facility was receiving between 70 and 80 patients every day.
Talking to The Express Tribune, Dr Sheikh said that out of the said cases, around 10 were suspected influenza cases who were then referred to DOW Hospital for tests and further medical assessment.
At Jinnah Postgraduate Medical Centre (JPMC), Dr Irfan Siddiqui, deputy in-charge of the Emergency Department, seconded that the number of flu and suspected influenza patients had increased.
“Common symptoms of influenza include high fever, a runny nose and cough. In people with weakened immune systems, the infection can affect the respiratory system and may lead to severe complications, including pneumonia and fluid accumulation in the lungs,” Dr Siddiqui stated.
Read more: Medic urges timely flu vaccination
Advising those vulnerable or caring for the sick, the doctor said, they should wear face masks, maintain physical distance and take precautions to avoid the contagious disease.
“A vaccine specifically designed to protect against influenza is available,” Dr Siddiqui said and urged people, particularly those at higher risk of severe illness, to consult healthcare professionals about vaccination.
He further recommended a healthy, balanced diet, including soups, broths and water-rich fruits, to help maintain hydration and support recovery among infected individuals.
The rise in influenza cases has also renewed concerns over the quality and availability of vaccines in Pakistan. Experts say vaccination programmes can help reduce the spread and severity of seasonal influenza, but the public should ensure that vaccines are obtained through authorised and reliable sources.
With the flu season approaching and international travel increasing, health experts say vaccination and other preventive measures will remain important in limiting the spread of influenza, particularly among children, elderly people and other vulnerable groups.

items.author: Masudul Zarif
items.content:
State surveillance and policing of online expression have a long history in the country
Originally published on Global Voices
Photo by cottonbro studio. Used under a Pexels License.
This post is part of Global Voices’ October 2026 Spotlight series, “Big Tech and Authoritarianism.” In this Spotlight, we explore how Big Tech facilitates and hinders authoritarian governments and practices, and how these choices influence the Global South. You can support this coverage by donating here.
Bangladesh is revising its cyber law to tackle AI-generated images, and the draft has triggered a furious debate over how much the state should police speech online. The ICT Division published the draft Cyber Protection (Amendment) Act for public comment in mid-September. It is now with a five-member cabinet committee led by Posts, Telecommunications and ICT Minister Faqir Mahbub Anam. In a discussion reported on October 19, media figures, legal analysts, and civil society representatives called for the most contested clauses to be removed.
The push follows a campaign season crowded with synthetic media. Global Voices previously reported on a study that identified 72 AI-manipulated items that gained traction between December 2025 and the February 12, 2026 election. Synthetic images of political figures were the most common tactic, alongside doctored news-channel graphics. The Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), which went on to win, was the most frequent target, with 47 cases.
State surveillance and policing of online expression have a long history. Section 57 of the Information and Communication Technology (ICT) Act of 2006 punished online content seen as defamatory, hurtful to religious sentiment, or damaging to the state’s image. A 2013 amendment toughened it, with sentences of up to 14 years. Journalists and ordinary social media users were among those charged under it. After years of protest, the government promised to scrap Section 57. Yet when the Digital Security Act (DSA) was signed into law in October 2018, the same offenses reappeared in sections 25, 28, 29 and 31. By 2023, the law minister had told parliament that 7,001 cases had been filed under it. The writer Mushtaq Ahmed died in custody in 2021 after ten months in jail under the DSA, which led to protests at home and abroad.
The Awami League government replaced the DSA with the Cyber Security Act in 2023, but Amnesty International said it repackaged almost all of the DSA’s repressive features. After the July 2024 uprising, the interim government scrapped nine sections through a new Cyber Security Ordinance in 2025. Rights groups say hundreds of cases from earlier years are still pending.
Fakes in the election and beyond
Women in politics faced a particular kind of attack. A Daily Star analysis of AI content before the vote found that pro-Awami League pages targeted female leaders of the National Citizen Party (NCP) with fabricated images that hinted at moral and sexual impropriety. After the election, a Prothom Alo fact-check found AI-generated images and invented statements aimed at nominees for reserved women's seats. Tanvir Mahatab Abir of Rumor Scanner told the paper that visible women, especially in politics, are frequent targets of disinformation.
Not all of it is political. Data from the Daily Star shows that Facebook pages used deepfake videos of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and his family, including his daughter Zaima Rahman, to promote fake “Family Card” offers in exchange for likes and follows. Among 52 posts analyzed, 13 featured Zaima. One page administrator told the fact-checking outlet Dismislab that the aim was to gain followers quickly and sell the pages. In such cases, for many creators of synthetic content, monetization metrics on social platforms often serve as a primary driver alongside political motives.
A case that left no remedy
For ordinary women, the damage can last much longer. Farzana Sithi, a student activist known for her role in the historic student-led uprising in 2024, was targeted by a fake Facebook profile that Dismislab investigated in March 2025. Of 166 videos and reels posted between December 13, 2024, and March 17, 2025, 133 were AI-generated deepfakes. They placed her face on videos of two Indian content creators. The five most-viewed clips drew more than 4.1 million views, and the account was monetized through Facebook's Stars feature.
“These videos are an attempt to tarnish my character,” Sithi told Dismislab, adding that she was bullied and shamed as a result. She reported the profile to Facebook several times. IT experts she approached privately asked for USD 100 to USD 150 to remove the fake accounts and videos, which she said she could not afford. At the time of Dismislab’s report, the profile was still active. Comments under the reels included rape threats.
What the law covers, and what the draft would change
Legal experts point out that the existing legislative framework has struggled to keep pace with rapid advancements in synthetic media. The Cyber Protection Act was enacted on 10 April 2026 and amended on 30 June. Its Section 25 already covers blackmail, sexual harassment, revenge porn, child sexual abuse material, sextortion and the distribution of AI-generated or manipulated content.
According to the minister, these offenses carry up to two years in prison, or up to five if the victim is a woman or under 18. The law targets AI mainly when it is used to commit existing crimes. It does not set out a dedicated framework for synthetic media or political deepfakes.
The draft would change that. It adds defamation, humiliation and bullying to Section 25 and names AI-generated content explicitly. A prior investigation by Prothom Alo revealed that the maximum penalty would rise to five years in prison and a BDT 2 million fine (roughly USD 16,131), and to ten years and Tk 4 million if the target is a woman or a person under 18. A new Section 26A would punish publishing or spreading a “rumor” or “disinformation” with up to ten years in prison, a fine of BDT 4 million (roughly USD 32,262), or both. The draft defines a rumor as unverified information that causes or risks causing confusion, panic or social instability.
The government presents the changes as a response to harm already being done. Introducing an earlier amendment in June, the ICT minister said it would require platforms such as Meta to remove disputed content within a set time. Officials told Prothom Alo that the tougher penalties are meant to curb fake videos, audio and images made with AI.
Free speech concerns
Critics say the draft goes well beyond that aim. Transparency International Bangladesh (TIB) warned that terms such as “rumor” and “demeaning” are defined loosely enough to allow selective enforcement. A joint statement by rights groups said the draft mirrors the repealed Digital Security Act. The Committee to Protect Journalists has objected to the prospect of journalists facing criminal liability for reporting officials consider unverified. An Asia Times analysis noted that because defamation sits inside Section 25, the heavier penalty for offenses against women would apply to it as well, and not only to sexual abuse.
Numbers, gaps and local responses
What the law would address is substantial. A report by Dhaka Tribune said police's Cyber Support for Women unit had been approached by 60,808 women by September 2024, and cited a 2024 Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics–UNFPA survey in which nearly 89 percent of women social media users reported online violence at least once. Officials say the real number is likely higher because of underreporting. The published figures do not separate cases involving AI.
Researchers describe a similar pattern across the region. A study in the Journal of Online Trust and Safety drew on three workshops with 49 journalists, lawyers, fact-checkers and advocates in Sri Lanka, India and Bangladesh. It found that women are disproportionately targeted, that platform moderation often fails in South Asian languages, and that victims struggle to reach institutional help. Sithi's (a student activist known for her role in the historic student-led uprising in 2024) experience, where the cost of private help was out of reach, fits that last finding.
Digital skills are an added concern. The Asian Development Bank reports that functional digital literacy in Bangladesh stands at 49 percent and that rural users are 29 percent less likely than urban users to use mobile internet. Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics data released in April show that 56.6 percent of men use the internet, against 50.2 percent of women. Advocates argue that people with fewer digital skills may find it harder to spot manipulated media or seek redress. These surveys, however, do not measure exposure to deepfakes directly.
Outside the government, fact-checkers are trying to keep pace. FactFest 2026, held on 27–28 September, brought together around 100 fact-checkers, journalists and researchers, according to an organizer. Its 13 sessions covered AI and gendered disinformation, among other topics. In the closing roundtable, speakers said Bangladeshi fact-checkers face shrinking funding and weak coordination with mainstream newsrooms.
The cabinet committee has yet to finalize the draft, which would then go to Parliament. Constitution Watchdog, a civil society group, has urged the government to withdraw the draft in its present form and reopen public consultation for at least 30 days. It also acknowledged the government's stated aim of protecting women and children from online abuse and responding to deepfakes. Whether a narrower law can do that without the speech provisions now under attack is the question facing lawmakers.
Written by Masudul Zarif

items.author: Palak Sharma
items.content:
Automotive classifieds company CarTrade reported a consolidated net profit of ₹66 Cr in the September quarter of FY27, up 3% from ₹64.1 Cr a year earlier. Sequentially, profit rose 16.2% from ₹56.8 Cr.
Operating revenue increased 10.2% to ₹213.1 Cr from ₹193.4 Cr in Q2 FY26. Sequentially, it rose 5.9% from ₹201.2 Cr.
Including other income of ₹23.1 Cr, total income stood at ₹236.2 Cr.
Total expenses rose 6% YoY to ₹150.8 Cr but declined 0.9% from ₹152.1 Cr in the preceding quarter.
Notably, the preceding June quarter included an exceptional expense of ₹3.1 Cr linked to salary restructuring to comply with the new labour codes. CarTrade reported no exceptional expenses in Q2 FY27.
EBITDA rose 20% YoY to ₹76 Cr from ₹63.6 Cr, while EBITDA margin expanded to 36% from 33%.
“We delivered our highest-ever quarterly revenue of ₹213 Cr and profit before tax of ₹85 Cr, with EBITDA growing 20% year-on-year. OLX India continued its strong momentum, recording 26% revenue growth and 36% EBITDA growth,” CarTrade Tech chairman and founder Vinay Sanghi said.
The company operates platforms spanning vehicle buying, selling, financing, and marketing. Its brands include CarWale, BikeWale, Shriram Automall, Adroit Auto, Mobility Outlook and OLX India.
Across its platforms, CarTrade reported about 76 Mn average monthly unique visitors during the quarter, with 96% of traffic coming organically.
How The Businesses Performed
The consumer business, which includes CarWale, BikeWale and CarTrade, reported operating revenue of ₹79.5 Cr, up 4% YoY from ₹76.2 Cr and 1.8% from ₹78.1 Cr in the June quarter.
Including other income, the business’s total income rose 6% YoY to ₹90.5 Cr from ₹85.4 Cr but declined sequentially from ₹91.5 Cr. Net profit increased 13% YoY to ₹32.3 Cr.
The remarketing business, comprising Shriram Automall, CarTrade Exchange and Adroit Auto, reported operating revenue of ₹70.3 Cr, up 12% from ₹62.6 Cr a year earlier. Total income increased 14% to ₹78.1 Cr from ₹68.7 Cr, while net profit rose 47% to ₹14.5 Cr.
Meanwhile, OLX India reported operating revenue of ₹70.2 Cr, up 26% YoY from ₹55.5 Cr. Including other income, total income grew 8% to ₹74.6 Cr from ₹69 Cr.
OLX India’s EBITDA increased 36% YoY to ₹22.5 Cr. However, net profit declined 25% to ₹19.1 Cr as other income fell and tax expenses increased.
Shares of CarTrade ended today’s trading session 12.68% lower at ₹2,463 on the BSE.

items.author: Usama Anjum
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Apple has acknowledged complaints about cracks and failures affecting the inner display of some newly launched iPhone Duo units and has directed affected customers to AppleCare for replacement assistance. The response follows reports from early buyers who encountered screen problems soon after purchasing Apple’s first foldable iPhone. While Apple has confirmed that a small number of devices are affected, the company has not announced a general recall or disclosed how many units may be involved.
The distinction matters for owners as Apple’s response concerns customers experiencing the reported problem, rather than a blanket replacement of every iPhone Duo on the market.
According to reporting on Apple’s October 26 statement, users with an affected device were advised to contact AppleCare to arrange a replacement. The company has not publicly identified the cause of the display failures or announced a manufacturing change.
What Triggered Apple’s Replacement Response?
Reports of problems began appearing shortly after the iPhone Duo’s launch, with some owners describing cracks near the fold and lines appearing across the flexible inner display. Others reported resistance or an unusual sound while opening or closing the device.
Some complaints concerned damage arising during normal handling, which is different from the deliberate pressure and reverse-bending used in online durability tests.
Repair specialists have discussed a possible hinge-related mechanism that could place pressure on the flexible display, but that remains a hypothesis. Apple has not confirmed a specific root cause, and the available reports do not establish that every unit is susceptible.
The company has characterized the problem as affecting a small number of units. Individual reports and early replacement claims cannot independently establish the scale of the issue.
What Affected iPhone Duo Owners Should Do—Including in Pakistan
For customers whose inner displays have developed cracks or stopped working, the immediate step is to contact AppleCare or the relevant authorized warranty provider, describe the fault, and ask about replacement eligibility.
Owners should keep purchase and warranty documentation and photograph any visible defect. They should avoid forcing a stiff hinge or attempting repairs themselves, which could complicate the assessment.
Some international reports describe replacements being arranged for affected customers, although availability may vary. Apple has not announced a Pakistan-specific replacement program for this issue.
That makes the sales channel particularly important for Pakistani buyers. Customers who bought their phone through an authorized local distributor should ask that seller or its designated service provider how Apple’s guidance will be handled. Owners of independently imported units should verify coverage and service options with Apple Support rather than assume local replacement is guaranteed.
Until more details emerge, checking warranty terms and after-sales support may be especially important for anyone considering the premium foldable in Pakistan.

iPhone Duo Owners Report Screen Cracks Along Hinge Shortly After Launch

items.author: Tom Jackson
items.content:
Nigerian startup Lumora is building a multi-app digital ecosystem that brings chat, cloud storage, an AI assistant and study tools together under a single login.
Founded in January 2025 by Samuel Derrick, Lumora is designed to replace the handful of separate apps people typically juggle for everyday digital life.
“Lumora is essentially one platform that replaces the several separate apps people typically juggle for everyday digital life,” Derrick told Disrupt Africa. “Rather than downloading and maintaining five or six different apps, users get one login and one ecosystem.”
The platform currently houses four sub-apps – Sachat, for real-time chat; VaultX, for cloud file storage; RawAI, an AI assistant that generates text, audio and video; and Studium, a set of study tools for students.
“Most digital tools in Nigeria, and Africa broadly, solve one problem each, forcing users to juggle multiple apps that each consume separate data and storage on often-constrained devices,” said Derrick.
Lumora has shipped version 1.2 of its platform and is now building version 1.3. It is live on the web and in closed testing on the Google Play Store, and has grown to 95 registered users who have sent more than 1,000 messages.
“Growth has been entirely organic, through personal networks and direct outreach, since I don’t yet have a marketing budget,” said Derrick.
That growth came after the startup recovered from a setback that saw its active users drop from 25 to zero.
“I learned the hard way that having a working product isn’t enough. My early onboarding flow caused nearly all my first users to drop off,” he said. “That forced me to diagnose the problem and rethink the entire first-time experience.”
The startup is self-funded and has not raised any external capital. It is also pre-revenue, but has a monetisation plan in place.
“The plan is a tiered model, with a free standard tier and a paid ultimate tier, with payments processed through Flutterwave,” said Derrick. “There’s also a longer-term plan for a developer tier, where other builders can create and monetise their own apps within the Lumora ecosystem.”
Getting this far has not been easy.
“The biggest challenge has been building entirely solo – no team, no co-founder, no funding – while also being a full-time student,” Derrick said.
There have also been technical setbacks.
“I ran my own local AI training server and accidentally damaged it with water, which set back one of my in-house AI experiments,” he said.
Lumora currently operates only in Nigeria, but Derrick said the platform could travel.
“There’s no formal expansion plan yet, but the platform is built to scale to other African markets facing similar constraints around data cost and app fragmentation,” he said.

items.author: Ankush Das
items.content:
A recent debate over investors’ lack of interest in India’s hardware and deeptech bets has brought some longstanding challenges in the ecosystem back into focus. These include a lack of patient capital, pressure from limited partners (LPs) for early distributions, consensus-driven investing, and the difficulty of underwriting long development and qualification cycles.
As AI infrastructure moves beyond a pure compute race to focus on the layers that determine how efficiently systems run, India stands at the cusp of a significant opportunity. However, simply adding more computing power will not be enough for the country to establish itself as a global AI leader.
Instead, opportunities are emerging in the supporting infrastructure. Data centres, for instance, need more efficient power delivery, better cooling systems, and faster connections between processors and memory. These layers are becoming increasingly critical as they directly influence real-world performance and the total cost of ownership of AI infrastructure.
For India, the debate and the technical opportunity converge. Rather than trying to compete across the entire AI hardware stack, the country can develop specialised technologies.
To understand which of these layers offer the strongest multiplier effects and what it will take for India to own them, we spoke to VCs tracking the homegrown deeptech ecosystem. Let’s unravel what they said in this edition of The AI Shift…
The Need To Power Data Centres
A consensus among VCs pointed to power delivery as the first major opportunity. As AI systems become more power-dense, improving power efficiency becomes an increasingly important engineering challenge.
Natasha Malpani, founder and general partner of Boundless Ventures, sees an opportunity in power electronics, grid-edge systems and cooling designed for hot and humid environments. Data centres operating in Indian cities must manage local temperature and humidity conditions, potentially creating demand for technologies that can also serve other tropical markets.
“The multiplier here is integration,” she said.
Power semiconductors can serve AI data centres, electric vehicles and energy infrastructure. The opportunity, therefore, is to develop components that address multiple markets instead of relying on demand from one category.
Cooling is also closely connected to this opportunity. Liquid-cooling systems help manage the heat generated by high-density computing equipment, creating demand for coolant distribution units, heat exchangers and direct-to-chip cooling technology.
The second opportunity lies in moving data between processors and memory. Debraj Banerjee, general partner of F2A (Fundamentum Frontier Advisors), which recently closed a ₹3,000 Cr fund for deeptech, argues that India should target the interconnect and memory layer of AI chips. This includes high-speed SerDes circuits, PCIe and CXL controllers, chiplet interconnects, and memory expansion silicon.
These technologies help processors exchange data and access memory efficiently. Banerjee’s argument is that standards-based technologies can give new entrants a route into multiple chip ecosystems without requiring them to challenge established GPU platforms directly.
“India shouldn’t try to win the fab race. It should own the plumbing of AI chips, the interconnect and memory layer, because that’s where the bottleneck is moving and where one design earns on every chip shipped worldwide,” he recommended.
The multiplier here is the business model. Companies that own valuable semiconductor IP could license it to multiple manufacturers and potentially earn royalties across global shipments, rather than relying entirely on engineering fees.
Pranav Pai, managing partner of 3one4 Capital, added a third dimension: India’s established semiconductor and systems-design talent can support demand for custom embedded-system design, verification and testing.
But he argues that value capture requires moving beyond services. “The opportunity is to move deeper, into components, advanced materials, proprietary process equipment, and finally product and system IP, which is where value capture will concentrate,” Pai said.
For AI infrastructure, this means turning engineering capabilities into products that global customers repeatedly buy.
Who’s Taming The AI Infrastructure Layer
Some Indian startups are already building in these areas, although their commercial maturity and ownership of technology differ.
Bengaluru-based C2i Semiconductors developed power-management technology for AI data centres, including multiphase controllers and smart power stages. Then, German semiconductor company Infineon completed its acquisition of C2i on October 5, 2026, strengthening its power-management capabilities and expanding its research and development footprint in India. The deal demonstrates how Indian-developed technology can attract a global strategic buyer.
Ahmedabad-based KuhlTherm is addressing the thermal-management problem. It develops liquid-cooling systems for high-density computing, including rear-door heat exchangers and coolant distribution units. Its next test is to demonstrate reliability, secure customer deployments and scale beyond early stage development.
In data movement, LightSpeed Photonics is developing optical interconnect technology for AI and high-performance computing. The company raised $6.5 Mn in a funding round led by pi Ventures last year. Its work highlights an emerging opportunity in using light to transmit data, although commercial adoption will depend on integration with existing systems, manufacturing readiness and customer qualification.
Government support is also building the broader semiconductor design ecosystem. Earlier this year, 24 chip-design projects were supported under the Design Linked Incentive scheme, producing 16 tape-outs, six fabricated chips and 10 patents. The projects had engaged more than 1,000 specialised engineers and developed over 140 reusable semiconductor IP cores.
These figures show growing design activity. However, chip-design progress is not the same as a proven position in the global AI hardware supply chain.
What Comes Next?
India’s challenge is to turn early technical progress into commercially competitive products. Semiconductor development involves long design and testing cycles, while cooling and power systems must demonstrate reliability under demanding operating conditions. Global customers are unlikely to switch suppliers without evidence that new products can meet performance, safety and service requirements.
Banerjee of F2A said the biggest gaps are not necessarily engineering talent, but patient capital and a lack of willingness to work with first-time chip companies. His thesis points to a need for investors who understand hardware development timelines and can support businesses through product qualification, rather than expecting rapid commercial returns.
Access to manufacturing and advanced packaging is another constraint. India’s design ecosystem is expanding, but startups still need to establish where their IP resides, which components can be produced domestically and where they depend on overseas suppliers.
The government’s Design Linked Incentive scheme provides financial incentives and design infrastructure support, but moving from prototype to volume production is still a challenge.
The next phase should be judged by commercial milestones: customer qualification, repeat orders, manufacturing scale and licensing revenue. For instance, for power and cooling startups, the test is whether their products can deliver measurable efficiency improvements and win deployments. Similarly, for semiconductor IP companies, it is whether global manufacturers adopt their designs and generate recurring revenue.
Overall, VCs agree that Indian startups need to choose where their engineering strengths can translate into proprietary technology, then build the capital, manufacturing and customer relationships needed to commercialise that technology.
The opportunity is visible. Whether it becomes a lasting advantage will depend on how many Indian startups can move from promising designs to products that global infrastructure providers cannot easily do without.
Top Stories From India & Around The World
BioStack Raises $9.5 Mn: The AI-powered healthtech platform raised $9.5 Mn to build training datasets for medical AI, addressing the shortage of high-quality healthcare data needed to develop and improve AI models.
Protectt.ai To Acquire Bosch’s AIShield: The AI-native cybersecurity startup is acquiring a controlling stake in Bosch-incubated AIShield to expand into enterprise AI security, with plans to scale its team and build a broader security platform.
Tradl Raises $4.1 Mn: The Bengaluru-based startup raised $4.1 Mn from Nexus Venture Partners and Stellaris Venture Partners to help retail traders screen stocks, analyse markets and test trading strategies using AI-powered tools.
OpenAI Launches GPT-6.1 Terra: OpenAI introduced GPT-6.1 Terra, a model designed for faster computer use, visual reasoning and coding. The company says its standard API pricing is 50% lower than that of GPT-5.6 Terra, targeting high-volume professional workflows.
The Weekly Buzz: Anthropic Files For Blockbuster IPO
Anthropic publicly filed its S-1 registration statement with the SEC this week, setting the stage for a mid-November Nasdaq listing under the stock ticker ANT.
The prospectus revealed explosive growth, first-half 2026 revenue of roughly $16.3 Bn, up more than 1,300% YoY in the most recent quarter, alongside a net loss of $80.7 Bn for the same period and soaring cloud costs.
The filing underscores Anthropic’s unusual governance structure designed to protect its safety mission and founder control even as it courts public markets. Enterprise adoption is highlighted, with thousands of customers spending six figures or more.
Founders have also restated that Claude will remain free of advertising. The move positions Anthropic as one of the largest pure-play AI IPOs in history and puts pressure on rivals still raising private capital. Investors and regulators will now scrutinise the detailed risk factors as the offering takes shape.
Startup In The Spotlight: Creedom
Founded by Naveen Murugan, Naveen Sowriraj and Aswin Dhananjai, Bengaluru-based Creedom is building an AI growth coach to help content creators understand their performance and improve their reach on platforms such as Instagram and YouTube.
For creators, identifying that a Reel or video has underperformed is only part of the challenge. Understanding why it failed to gain traction and what to change in future content remains difficult, particularly when traditional analytics dashboards offer data without personalised guidance.
Creedom initially operated as a learning platform for creators, reaching more than 1.5 Lakh creators in India before pivoting to an AI-led product. Its platform connects with creators’ Instagram and YouTube accounts, analyses content and performance, identifies trends and recommends what they should create next.
At the heart of the platform is Cree, an AI companion that allows creators to interact with their performance data conversationally instead of navigating conventional analytics dashboards. By turning content metrics into personalised, actionable advice, the startup aims to help creators make more informed decisions about their content strategy.
With India’s creator economy reaching 4.12 Mn creators in 2025, Creedom is entering a market that includes creator analytics tools such as vidIQ and TubeBuddy, alongside native platforms such as YouTube Studio and Instagram Insights.
Prompt Of The Week
What prompts and hacks are CTOs, CEOs and cofounders using these days to streamline their work?
Here’s Manavdeep Singh Grover, cofounder & CEO of SuperLiving, with a prompt he uses to turn an A/B test result into a clear ship, kill or keep-running decision.
“You are my analytics lead, and your job is to tell me the actionables from insights, not just what happened.
The A/B experiment: [what changed, the variants, the split, the start date, and who sees it].
Before any numbers:
Check the live setup matches what I described: the split, the targeting, the pricing, and the exact wording users see in each variant. Flag any mismatch first.
Judge it on one metric: total revenue per user who saw the test, across every product, and 6 month LTV projection. Not just the product we changed.
Then read it honestly:
Count each user in the variant they first saw, never by what they bought.
Show new and existing users separately, and weight by day if the split or the traffic changed mid-test.
Show the full journey for each variant: started checkout, paid, cancelled the same day, and what they bought instead.
Give the difference with a range and the chance each variant is really ahead. If it’s too early, tell me how many more days you need.
Tell me the break-even: how many buyers the pricier option can lose and still win.
End with:
Your call in one line: ship it, kill it, or keep running, and why.
The one thing that could prove the call wrong, and the date we’ll know.
Use plain language and a table for every comparison.”
Editor’s Note: Some prompts may need to be adjusted by users for best results or may not work as intended for certain users.
[Edited by: Shishir Parasher]

items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Apple’s next budget-friendly smartphone, the iPhone 18e, has appeared in a new leak that reveals key details about its chipset, cameras, and display. The phone is expected to succeed the iPhone 17e, which Apple launched in March 2026.
iPhone 18e Leak Reveals Chipset, Camera and Display Details – Here’s What We Know
According to tipster Digital Chat Station, the upcoming device could bring improvements in processing power and selfie photography. However, its display and rear camera specifications may remain largely unchanged.
iPhone 18e May Feature a 60Hz OLED Display
The iPhone 18e is tipped to feature a 6.12-inch LTPS OLED display with a 60Hz refresh rate. If the leak proves accurate, Apple will continue to offer a standard refresh rate on its entry-level iPhone.
This means users hoping for a smoother 90Hz or 120Hz display may have to wait for a future model. Higher refresh rates can make scrolling, animations, and supported games appear smoother.
Apple A20 Chipset Could Power the iPhone 18e
The upcoming smartphone is expected to use Apple’s A20 chipset, reportedly built using a 2nm manufacturing process. The newer process could improve performance and power efficiency compared with previous generations, although actual results will depend on Apple’s final hardware and software implementation.
Analyst Ming-Chi Kuo has also previously linked the A20 chip to the iPhone 18e. An earlier report suggested that the device could include 9GB of RAM, but this specification has not been officially confirmed.
Rear Camera May Remain Unchanged
According to the latest leak, the iPhone 18e will feature a single 48MP rear camera, matching the main camera resolution of the iPhone 17e.
Apple may focus on improving the front camera instead. The new model is tipped to feature a 24MP selfie camera, compared with the 12MP front camera on its predecessor.
If accurate, this upgrade could improve the level of detail in selfies and video calls. However, the final image quality will also depend on the camera sensor, image processing, and software features.
See Also: iPhone Duo Warranty in Pakistan: What Mercantile and GNext Offer
iPhone 18e Launch Expected in Spring 2027
Apple launched the iPhone 17e in March 2026, making a spring 2027 release for the iPhone 18e a possibility. Previous reports have suggested that the device could arrive around the same time as the standard iPhone 18 and the iPhone Air 2.
Apple has not officially announced the iPhone 18e or confirmed its launch schedule, so these details should be treated as rumours for now.
A Minor Upgrade Over the iPhone 17e?
Based on the leaked specifications, the iPhone 18e appears to be a modest upgrade rather than a major redesign. The A20 chipset and a potentially improved selfie camera could be its main selling points, while the 60Hz display and 48MP rear camera may remain unchanged.
Battery capacity, battery life, pricing, and other hardware details are still unknown. These features could influence how significant the upgrade will be when compared with the iPhone 17e.
More information is expected to emerge as the device moves closer to its anticipated launch.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) has denied reports of widespread irregularities in the customs clearance of courier-imported mobile phones, telling Parliament that an inquiry into an alleged scam involving an iPhone 16 Pro Max found no similar cases elsewhere in the country.
Minister for Finance and Revenue Senator Muhammad Aurangzeb informed Parliament that the Federal Tax Ombudsman (FTO) findings related to a single mobile phone and that a detailed inquiry had been conducted by the concerned Customs Collectorate, involving Customs staff, FedEx and other parties.
FBR Finds No Other Cases in iPhone 16 Pro Max Customs Scam Inquiry
According to the minister’s written response, the inquiry found that the matter primarily involved a disagreement between two private parties over a single iPhone 16 Pro Max.
The handset had remained in FedEx’s custody, and the applicable duties and taxes had been paid.
The minister said Customs released the phone to an authorised individual whose name appeared on the verifiable airway bill, following verification of the required documents, including the original detention receipt and invoice.
He added that the complainant withdrew the complaint during proceedings before the FTO.
Responding to questions about the extent of the alleged irregularities and whether similar incidents had occurred elsewhere, Aurangzeb said the Chief Collector of Customs (Airports), Islamabad, had submitted a detailed inquiry report to the FTO. The inquiry also included an audit of important FedEx clearances to establish whether similar incidents had occurred.
“However, no cases of similar nature have been reported elsewhere,” the minister stated.
On measures to prevent unauthorised release of courier-imported consignments, the minister said Customs had established procedures requiring goods to be handed over only to authorised individuals after verification of their credentials against documents such as the air waybill.
He said Customs also strictly adhered to the requirement of checking the original detention receipt issued by the department.
See Also: FBR To Move Seized Goods to Online Auctions: Who Can Bid, What It Costs and How Prices Are Set
Following the FTO’s findings and recommendations, an internal capacity-building programme had been initiated, comprising monthly training sessions for officers and officials posted at Air Freight Units (AFUs) at international airports.
The parliamentary response comes amid questions over the integrity of courier-imported goods clearance and the safeguards in place to prevent consignments from being handed over to unauthorised recipients.
While the government maintains that the reported case was an isolated dispute between private parties, the inquiry and subsequent training measures highlight the importance of document verification and accountability in customs clearance procedures.

items.content:
Update | October 28, 19:55 IST
Shares of Jio Platforms ended their maiden trading session at ₹1,417.35 on the BSE, up 26.66% from the issue price of ₹1,119 and 4.37% from the listing price of ₹1,358. The stock hit an intraday high of ₹1,423.80, up 27.24% premium to the issue price.
Jio Platforms ended its debut session as India’s second-largest listed company by market capitalisation, behind parent Reliance Industries, with a valuation of ₹13.05 Lakh Cr (about $137.2 Bn).
On the NSE, the stock closed at ₹1,417.50, up 26.68% from the issue price and 4.38% from the listing price.
Original | October 28, 10:00 IST
Shares of Jio Platforms, the telecom and digital services arm of Reliance Industries, listed at ₹1,358 apiece on the BSE and the NSE, a 21.36% premium to the issue price of ₹1,119.
The debut gave the company a market capitalisation of ₹12.5 Lakh Cr (about $131 Bn) as against the ₹10.3 Lakh Cr (about $108 Bn) capitalisation at the issue price.
The listing follows India’s largest IPO, which was subscribed 22.19X when bidding closed on October 23. Jio Platforms had set a price band of ₹1,065-₹1,119 per share for the ₹30,213 Cr offering.
The IPO comprised a fresh issue of up to 27 Cr equity shares, with no offer-for-sale component.
Ahead of the public issue, Jio Platforms raised ₹8,109.8 Cr from anchor investors by allotting about 7.25 Cr shares at ₹1,119 apiece. Participants included HDFC Mutual Fund, ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund, SBI Mutual Fund, BlackRock, the Government of Singapore, and Abu Dhabi Investment Authority.
Jio plans to use ₹27,500 Cr from the IPO proceeds to prepay certain borrowings of its telecom subsidiary, Reliance Jio Infocomm (RJIL), with the remaining proceeds earmarked for general corporate purposes.
The debt repayment makes the offering partly a balance sheet exercise, while its growth prospects depend on expanding beyond telecom connectivity into broadband, cloud services, enterprise solutions, and AI.
RJIL had 533.3 Mn customers as of June 30, 2026, while Jio’s network carried around 60% of India’s wireless data traffic in FY26. During the quarter, Jio’s average revenue per user (ARPU) rose 3.26% to ₹215.60 compared with ₹208.80 a year earlier. Monthly data consumption also increased to 43.7 GB per customer from 37 GB.
This comes as the company has been working on extracting revenue from customers beyond its mobile connectivity offerings. Jio’s fixed broadband customer base grew from 11.2 Mn in March 2024 to 28.6 Mn in June 2026, including 14 Mn JioAirFiber customers, giving it an avenue to deepen household engagement.
On the financial front, Jio Platforms’ operating revenue rose nearly 15% YoY to ₹1.47 Lakh Cr in FY26, while net profit increased 15.1% to ₹30,049 Cr.
Earlier today, Motilal Oswal initiated coverage on Jio Platforms with a ‘BUY’ rating, setting a target price of ₹1,350 per share. The brokerage expects Jio to sustain its leadership in wireless connectivity and home broadband, while expanding its digital services business across cloud, enterprise communications, IoT and managed services.
