items.content:
Government of India (GoI) has announced the sale (re-issue) of four dated securities for a notified amount of ₹33,000 crore as per the following details:
Sr No Security Date of Repayment Notified Amount
(₹ Crore) GoI specific Notification Auction Date Settlement Date
1 6.20% GS 2029 Aug 17, 2029 9,000 F.No.4(1)-B(W&M)/2026 dated October 26, 2026 October 30, 2026
(Friday) November 02, 2026
(Monday)
2 6.57% GS 2033 Aug 17, 2033 12,000
3 7.63% GS 2056 Sep 15, 2056 9,000
4 7.50% GOI SGrB 2056 Apr 27, 2056 3,000
  Total   33,000      
2. GoI will have the option to retain additional subscription up to ₹2,000 crore against each security mentioned above.
3. The securities will be sold through Reserve Bank of India Mumbai Office, Fort, Mumbai – 400001. The sale will be subject to the terms and conditions spelt out in the ‘Specific Notification’ mentioned above and the General Notification F.No.4(2)–B(W&M)/2018, dated March 26, 2025.
4. The auction will be conducted using multiple price method. Both competitive and non-competitive bids for the auction should be submitted in electronic format on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber system) on October 30, 2026 (Friday). The non-competitive bids should be submitted between 10:30 a.m. and 11:00 a.m. and the competitive bids should be submitted between 10:30 a.m. and 11:30 a.m. The result will be announced on the same day and payment by successful bidders will have to be made on November 02, 2026 (Monday).
5. Bids for underwriting of the Additional Competitive Underwriting (ACU) portion can be submitted by ‘Primary Dealers’ from 09:00 a.m. up to 09:30 a.m. on October 30, 2026 (Friday) on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber system).
6. The securities will be eligible for “When Issued” trading for a period commencing from October 27, 2026 – October 30, 2026.
7. Operational guidelines for Government of India dated securities auction and other details are given in the Annex.
Ajit Prasad          
Deputy General Manager
(Communications)    
Press Release: 2026-2027/1390
ANNEX
Type of Auction
1. For multiple price-based auction, successful bids will get accepted at the respective quoted yield/price for the security. For uniform price-based auction, bids will get accepted at the cut off yield/price accepted in the auction.
2. The auction will be yield based for new security and price based for securities which are re-issued.
3. In case of a Floating Rate Bonds (FRB), the auction will be spread-based for new security and price based for securities which are reissued. At the time of placing bids for new FRB, the spread should be quoted in percentage terms.
Minimum Bid Size
4. The securities will be issued for a minimum amount of ₹10,000/- (nominal) and in multiples of ₹10,000/- thereafter.
Non-Competitive Segment
5. In all the auctions, Government security up to 5% of the notified amount for sale of individual security will be allotted to the eligible individuals and institutions under the Scheme for Non-competitive Bidding Facility in the Auctions of Government Securities. Individual investors can also place bids as per the non-competitive scheme through the Retail Direct portal (https://rbiretaildirect.org.in).
6. Each bank or Primary Dealer (PD) on the basis of firm orders received from their constituents will submit a single consolidated non-competitive bid for individual security on behalf of its constituents in electronic format on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber system).
7. Allotment under the non-competitive segment will be at the weighted average rate of yield/price of the successful bids that will emerge in the auction on the basis of the competitive bidding.
Submission of Bids
8. Both competitive and non-competitive bids for the auction should be submitted in electronic format on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber system).
9. Bids in physical form will not be accepted except in extraordinary circumstances.
Business Continuity Plan (BCP)-IT failure
10. Only in the event of system failure, physical bids will be accepted. Such physical bids should be submitted to the Public Debt Office, Mumbai through (email; Phone no: 022-22603456, 022-22603457, 022-22603190) in the prescribed form which can be obtained from RBI website (https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_ViewForms.aspx) before the auction timing ends.
11. In case of technical difficulties, Core Banking Operations Team should be contacted (email; Phone no: 022-69870466, 022-69870415).
12. For other auction related difficulties, IDMD auction team can be contacted (email; Phone no: 022-22702431, 022-22705125).
Multiple Bids
13. An investor can submit more than one competitive bid in electronic format on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber system).
14. The aggregate amount of bids submitted by an investor in an auction should not exceed the notified amount of auction.
Decision Making Process
15. On the basis of bids received, the Reserve Bank will determine the minimum price/maximum yield up to which tenders for purchase of Government Security will be accepted at the auctions.
16. Bids quoted at rates lower than the minimum price/higher than the maximum yield determined by the Reserve Bank of India will be rejected.
17. Reserve Bank of India will have the full discretion to accept or reject any or all bids either wholly or partially without assigning any reason.
Issue of Securities
18. Issue of securities to the successful bidders will be by credit to Subsidiary General Ledger Account (SGL) or to Constituents’ Subsidiary General Ledger Account (CSGL), maintained with Reserve Bank of India.
Periodicity of Interest Payment
19. Interest on the Government Security will generally be paid half-yearly other than in case of securities with non-standard maturities. The exact periodicity of coupon payment is invariably mentioned in the specific notification for the issue of security.
Underwriting of the Government Securities
20. The underwriting of the Government Securities under auctions by the ‘Primary Dealers’ will be as per the “Revised Scheme of Underwriting Commitment and Liquidity Support” announced by the Reserve Bank vide circular RBI/2007-08/186 dated November 14, 2007 as amended from time to time.
Eligibility for Repurchase Transactions (Repo)
21. The securities will be eligible for Repurchase Transactions (Repo) as per the conditions mentioned in Master Direction – Reserve Bank of India (Repurchase Transactions (Repo)) Directions, 2025 as amended from time to time.
Eligibility for ‘When Issued’ Trading
22. The securities will be eligible for “When Issued” trading in accordance with the guidelines on ‘When Issued transactions in Central Government Securities’ issued by the Reserve Bank of India vide circular No. RBI/2018-19/25 dated July 24, 2018 as amended from time to time.
Investment by Non-Residents
23. Investments by Non-Residents are subject to the guidelines on ‘Fully Accessible Route’ for Investment by Non-residents in Government Securities and other related guidelines as issued by the Reserve Bank from time to time.

Governor Dauda Lawal has been repositioning the healthcare sector in Zamfara state through infrastructural revitalisation, improved healthcare service delivery, institutional strengthening, the Medical Association, (NMA) has said.
The NMA Chairman, Zamfara State chapter, Dr Muhammad Murtata Salahu, revealed this at the 2026 Annual Physicians’ Week And Ordinary General Meeting of the association.
He reaffirmed the NMA’s readiness to work closely with Governor Lawal’s administration in building a healthcare system that is resilient, accessible, equitable and responsive
“A stronger medical profession means a stronger healthcare system, and a stronger healthcare system means a healthier and more prosperous Zamfara,” he said.
“On behalf of the entire NMA members in Zamfara let me express our profound appreciation to  Governor Dauda Lawal for his visionary leadership, remarkable commitment to healthcare transformation and sustained support for the medical profession.
“We acknowledge and commend the  determination of the present administration in the state to reposition the healthcare sector through infrastructural revitalisation, improved healthcare service delivery, institutional strengthening and greater attention to the welfare and professional development of healthcare personnel,” he explained.
He said. “Governor Dauda Lawal’s commitment of giving the healthcare a priority of his administration demonstrates a clear understanding that a healthy population remains the foundation of sustainable development, economic productivity and social stability.
“We particularly appreciate his administration’s responsiveness to the needs and concerns of medical professionals and its efforts towards creating a more conducive environment for effective medical practice.
“These initiatives are encouraging and represent important steps towards addressing longstanding challenges within our healthcare system.
“The commitment of the state government to healthcare development is commendable, and we assure you of the continued professional support and constructive partnership of the Nigerian Medical Association in translating the state healthcare vision into sustainable benefits for the people of Zamfara.
“We equally encourage the governor to sustain this positive momentum through continued investment in healthcare infrastructure, workforce development, improved welfare packages, recruitment and retention of medical personnel, and the strengthening of healthcare services across the state,” he explained.
The theme for this year’s Physicians’ Week is,  “Securing the Future of Medicine in Nigeria.”
Part of the activities marking the week was scientific lectures presentations on polio in Zamfara, Applications of Artificial Intelligence in healthcare, and Diphtheria Case Management.

items.author: Team Inc42
items.content:
Festive Rush Comes At A Cost
India’s ecommerce sellers are heading into the festive rush with a growing cost burden. While Amazon India and Flipkart have cut commissions to attract more sellers, higher cancellation penalties, platform fees and logistics costs are denting their margins just as festive demand peaks. Meanwhile, subdued discretionary spending and rising logistics costs are adding to their woes. But what’s really happening?
Flipkart’s Penalty Shot: Flipkart’s zero-commission push across fashion categories in July has nearly doubled seller onboarding. However, its new penalty structure charges sellers ₹30 for delayed dispatches and another ₹60 for cancelled orders, regardless of order value. This flat fee is hurting smaller sellers and low-value orders, taking the shine off its zero-commission model.
Amazon Plays Spoilsport, Too: The ecommerce giant has followed suit. It has revised its cancellation fee structure, linking charges to order value instead of slapping a flat fee. Amazon’s flat tier-based penalty for cancelled orders can go up to 10% of the order value for orders up to ₹10,000, falling to 8% for orders between ₹10,001 and ₹50,000, 5% for orders between ₹50,001 and ₹1 lakh, and 2% for orders above ₹1 lakh. An additional 18% GST applies to these charges.
Deliveries Turn Costlier: Rising logistics costs are also adding to the festive-season strain, with Amazon raising closing fees and Delhivery introducing a surcharge on D2C shipments. Flipkart is also considering a revision in seller fulfilment fees. Quick commerce is adding to the pressure, with frequent, smaller shipments increasing vehicle requirements and waiting times at distribution hubs.
Sellers In A Tight Corner: The shift to value-linked cancellation fees adds to the cost of doing business on marketplaces, particularly for those operating on thin margins. Sellers have also flagged the difficulty of contesting such charges, saying the process can be cumbersome even when they have evidence of timely dispatch.
With penalties, surcharges and logistics costs piling up, here’s how ecommerce sellers are paying the price.
From The Editor’s Desk
WeWork India Q2 Profit Jumps 219%
WeWork India’s net profit surged 219% YoY to ₹20.4 Cr in Q2 FY27, while operating revenue rose 33.6% to ₹767.8 Cr. The company added a record 11,700 desks during the quarter.
Operational capacity grew 26.9% YoY to 1,45,300 desks across 85 centres in eight cities. Its member base rose 32.5% to 1,21,700, while occupancy stood at 83.7%.
Value-added services and digital revenue grew 38% to ₹108.8 Cr, outpacing core revenue growth. WeWork India also reported a net cash position of ₹23.1 Cr, compared with net debt of ₹310.5 Cr a year earlier.
Baillie Gifford Funds Mark Down VerSe By Up To 80%
Two funds managed by Baillie Gifford slashed the value of their VerSe Innovation holdings by around 80% over different periods. One fund’s assessment implied a valuation of about $576 Mn, nearly 90% below its $5 Bn valuation in 2022.
VerSe Innovation, the parent of Dailyhunt and Josh, last raised $805 Mn in April 2022 at a reported $5 Bn valuation. The company has raised nearly $1.7 Bn from investors including Google, Microsoft and Peak XV Partners.
VerSe reported an 88% YoY rise in FY25 operating revenue to ₹1,930 Cr, while its EBITDA burn narrowed 20% to ₹738 Cr. However, the latest markdowns reflect investor concerns and do not establish a definitive company-wide valuation.
Practo Cofounder’s Cent Raises $15 Mn
Healthtech startup Cent raised $15 Mn in a Series A round led by Blume Ventures and South Park Commons. It also acquired AI-powered radiology platform Medsee to improve reporting workflows.
Founded by Practo cofounder Shashank ND and two other executives, Cent combines AI, radiology and biomarkers to screen asymptomatic patients for over 300 conditions, including cancer and cardiac disease.
Cent said it has completed 10,000 preventive whole-body scans across Bengaluru, Mumbai and Delhi NCR. It plans to use the fresh capital to expand its AI, engineering and clinical teams, and scale to 1 Cr scans by 2035.
Parsec Aerospace In Talks To Raise $10 Mn
Bengaluru-based Parsec Aerospace is in talks to raise around $10 Mn in a funding round led by Nexus Venture Partners, with participation from existing investor Lightspeed Venture Partners, sources told Inc42.
Founded by former Pixxel engineer Effy John, Parsec Aerospace is developing next-generation engines for aerospace applications. Incorporated in September 2025, the startup remains in stealth mode.
The funding talks come as Indian deeptech startups raised $290 Mn across 28 deals in Q3 2026, nearly 2.8X the $105 Mn raised in the year-ago quarter. Recent investments include aerospace propulsion startup D-Propulse Aerospace’s ₹25 Cr fundraise.
IndiaMART’s Q2 Snapshot
IndiaMART’s net profit rose 9.8% YoY to ₹90.7 Cr in Q2 FY27, while operating revenue grew 10% to ₹428.6 Cr. EBITDA fell 2% to ₹156 Cr, but margins improved 300 bps to 40%.
Customer collections increased 9% YoY to ₹443 Cr during the quarter. The B2B ecommerce platform recorded 2.7 Cr unique business enquiries, while its paying suppliers stood at 2.2 Lakh.
Annualised revenue per paying supplier rose 10% to around ₹72,000, supporting marketplace revenue growth. However, profit declined 47.3% sequentially from ₹172.2 Cr in Q1 FY27.
Inc42 Markets
Inc42 Startup Spotlight
How Protonas Is Making Hydrogen Power More Affordable
Backup power in India often means diesel generators. But these are costly to run, pollute the environment and have high upfront costs. To solve this, Protonas is redesigning PEM fuel cells to make hydrogen power viable where traditional batteries fall short.
A Cost-First Design: Founded in 2024, Protonas is building air-cooled proton exchange membrane (PEM) fuel cells. This technology converts hydrogen and oxygen into electricity, with water as the only point-of-use byproduct. Its stack architecture uses fewer components and simpler cooling systems, which the startup claims can slash manufacturing and operating costs.
Lighting Up India: Protonas is building systems for backup power, mobility and UAVs. Its 500W–2kW systems for telecom networks and critical infrastructure are designed to provide eight to 72 hours of backup during outages. The startup is also developing fuel-cell engines for three-wheelers, alongside systems aimed at extending drone flight times.
Building In India: Backed by Transition VC, Protonas now plans to build its engineering and manufacturing operations in Bengaluru. Competing with the likes of Ballard Power Systems and Plug Power, it is now focused on developing affordable prototype systems for emerging markets. So, can Protonas make hydrogen fuel cells affordable and mainstream?

items.content: Shares of Jio Platforms, the telecom and digital services arm of Mukesh Ambani-led Reliance Industries, are set to make their stock market debut today, following India's biggest-ever initial public offering (IPO). Ahead of the listing, the grey market premium (GMP) of around 22% indicates a strong start for the Rs 30,213 crore issue, which attracted record investor demand.Jio shares are commanding a grey market premium of around Rs 246-247 over the IPO price of Rs 1,119, indicating a possible listing price of Rs 1,365-1,366. This translates into potential listing gains of around Rs 2,950 for investors allotted one lot of 12 shares.The unofficial premium suggests strong buying interest ahead of the debut, although actual listing gains will depend on demand during the opening session. Grey market premiums are unofficial and can fluctuate sharply before trading begins.Jio's public issue, which opened on October 21 and closed on October 23, was subscribed 22.19 times, with qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) leading the demand. The QIB portion was subscribed 70.55 times, while non-institutional investors bid for 14 times their allotted shares. The retail category was subscribed 2.72 times.Also Read: Jio’s big-bang listing may give it stock market’s No.2 crown after Reliance IndustriesThe record subscription and the company's Rs 10.3 lakh crore IPO valuation have made Jio's listing one of the most closely watched market events of the year.What analysts expect from Jio's listingAnalysts expect Jio's market leadership, subscriber base and expanding digital businesses to support investor interest beyond its debut.Uday Patil, Executive Director at PL Capital, described the listing as a milestone for India's capital markets, citing the company's established telecom operations and opportunities in broadband, cloud computing and artificial intelligence."Jio has more than 500 million subscribers and a large telecom network, alongside broadband, enterprise technology, cloud and AI opportunities," Patil said. He believes higher average revenue per user (ARPU), home broadband adoption, enterprise services and monetisation of digital platforms could support the company's future growth."Execution will determine how much value these opportunities create," Patil said, adding that Jio offers a long-term investment opportunity.Motilal Oswal sees room for long-term growth, citing its leadership in India's telecom market, earnings growth and opportunities in emerging digital services. "Jio offers a combination of market leadership, healthy earnings growth and future opportunities in broadband, enterprise technology and AI," the broker said.It identified ARPU growth, future tariff increases and digital services monetisation as important factors to monitor.Record IPO demand puts Jio in the spotlightJio Platforms' Rs 30,213 crore IPO surpassed Hyundai Motor India's Rs 27,870 crore offering to become the largest public issue in India's capital market history. The issue was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of opening, reflecting strong early participation from institutional and retail investors.The public book attracted bids worth more than Rs 4.9 lakh crore, while the anchor allocation drew substantial interest from leading domestic and international investors. The IPO attracted more than 1.38 crore applications, according to Investoyard data, setting a new reported record for investor applications.Jio raised Rs 8,110 crore through its anchor allocation ahead of the public issue, with institutional investors including BlackRock, Fidelity and Life Insurance Corporation of India participating. At the upper end of its price band of Rs 1,065-1,119, Jio Platforms is valued at Rs 10.3 lakh crore, placing it among India's most valuable companies.The offering comprised 27 crore fresh equity shares, with no offer-for-sale component. Existing shareholders, including Reliance Industries and strategic investors, did not sell shares through the IPO.The company intends to use up to Rs 27,500 crore of the net proceeds to repay or prepay borrowings at Reliance Jio Infocomm, while the remaining funds will be used for general corporate purposes.What investors will watch after listingJio enters the market with a subscriber base of more than 53 crore and a nationwide 5G network. Its future earnings growth will depend on tariff revisions, rising data consumption, home broadband expansion and revenue from enterprise technology services.For FY26, the company reported revenue from operations of Rs 1.47 lakh crore and profit after tax of Rs 30,049 crore. Its EBITDA margin stood at 51.91%.At a listing premium of 22%, Jio's implied market cap could reach nearly Rs 12.6 lakh crore, giving it a place among India's most valuable listed companies from its first trading session.The debut will also be closely tracked for its potential impact on Reliance Industries, which will remain Jio Platforms' majority shareholder after the offering.Disclosure: This article has been written by Podishetti Akash, who is not a SEBI-registered Research Analyst or an Investment Adviser. They should not be construed as the views or recommendations of The Economic Times Digital or the journalist. items.author: Shrishti Bisht
items.content:
Bengaluru-based enterprise AI startup QwikBuild has raised $2.3 Mn (around ₹22 Cr) in a pre-seed funding round led by Japanese tech major Globalway, along with participation from Blume Ventures, DeVC, Marsshot and angel investors Lalit Keshre, founder of Groww, and Curefoods’ CEO Ankit Nagori.
The startup will use the fresh capital primarily to fuel its go-to-market (GTM) activities. This will include setting up a team in the US as well as expanding operations across South East Asia.
Besides the investment, QwikBuild also announced that it is forming a joint venture (JV) with Globalway to enter Japan’s enterprise software market. Expected to become operational by the end of 2026, the JV will take QwikBuild’s platform to Globalway’s existing and prospective enterprise customers in Japan.
Founded in 2025 by ex-slice executive Pradeep Ayyagari, QwikBuild builds enterprise software and AI agents that can bring down the software development and deployment significantly.
The startup claims to be serving more than 100 enterprises across India, Southeast Asia, the US and Dubai. It says that about 10-12% of its clients are large enterprises, while about 30% are smaller businesses that use the platform to deploy softwares without setting up dedicated technology teams.
QwikBuild’s Enterprise AI Play
QwikBuild combines custom software development with AI-driven workflow automation. Its platform allows businesses to build applications from scratch, replacing legacy systems or custom software layers on top of tools offered by giants like SAP and Salesforce.
According to Ayyagari, the SaaS startup focuses on codifying business decisions rather than automating individual tasks alone.
For instance, a financial services company may need to decide which customers to contact, what filters to apply and which scripts to use for different customer segments. While a specialised AI startup may automate the calling process here, QwikBuild will look at codifying the decisions that determine which calls should be made in the first place.
Businesses can then autonomously deploy voice agents or other tools to execute these workflows, either through QwikBuild or other providers.
“Tech has always been the enabler. But adoption of tech was always the hardest problem that I have seen,” Ayyagari said, drawing on his experience at Flipkart, Swiggy and Slice.
QwikBuild aims to address this gap by allowing business teams to build and test applications as their requirements evolve, without repeatedly relying on engineering teams.
Ayyagari cited a recent customer meeting in which a business team discussed changes to an application. “The agent understood what the context was. The feature was immediately built within the next five minutes,” he said. “Tech and business can work parallelly together,” he added.
He also pointed to the potential for enterprise AI adoption. “Hardly 1% of enterprises have adopted AI. It’s a huge market that needs to be unlocked,” he said, adding that the software needed to automate businesses over the next five years would be “at least 10X” in price when compared with what’s available today.
The startup is betting that businesses will increasingly turn to platforms combining software development, integrations and AI agents to automate operations.
This is also reflected in recent enterprise AI investment trends in the Indian startup ecosystem, For instance, enterprise AI and automation startup RapidCanvas netted $29 Mn last week. On a broader level, Indian AI startup funding surged 265% YoY to $438 Mn in Q3 2026, according to Inc42’s Indian Tech Startup Funding Report.
However, Inc42’s survey of 85+ institutional investors found that 63% saw some degree of froth in AI valuations, with about half of them expecting a correction within 18 months. Despite these concerns, investors see vertical AI as the biggest value driver over the next five years, followed by AI hardware and semiconductors and AI-led IT and business services.

items.summary:
Arsenal suffered one of the most humiliating defeats in their history as the Premier League champions were stunned by fourth-tier minnows Fleetwood in a League Cup penalty shoot-out on Tuesday.
Mikel Arteta’s side crashed out 5-3 on penalties in an incredible fourth round upset after the tie finished 1-1 in normal time.

Arsenal’s 16-year-old rising star Max Dowman was sent off for violent conduct in the closing stages.

They had moved level on points with Premier League leaders
items.author: Emmanuel Okogba
items.content:
Arsenal suffered one of the most humiliating defeats in their history as the Premier League champions were stunned by fourth-tier minnows Fleetwood in a League Cup penalty shoot-out on Tuesday.
Mikel Arteta’s side crashed out 5-3 on penalties in an incredible fourth round upset after the tie finished 1-1 in normal time.
Arsenal’s Bruno Guimaraes had his penalty saved by Jay Lynch in the shoot-out and Conor Haughey scored Fleetwood’s winner.
Aaron Loupalo-Bi’s first-half goal had put Fleetwood ahead before Viktor Gyokeres equalised after the interval.
Arsenal’s 16-year-old rising star Max Dowman was sent off for violent conduct in the closing stages.
Arteta paid the price for prioritising Sunday’s Premier League trip to Liverpool as his decision to make nine changes backfired spectacularly.
No one would have predicted Arsenal’s embarrassment regardless of Arteta’s selection gamble.
They had moved level on points with Premier League leaders Manchester City after a 2-0 victory over Everton on Saturday.
But instead of extending their run of 11 wins from their 13 previous games, Arsenal returned to north London red-faced after a loss that ranks among the darkest days in the club’s glittering history.
Referee Michael Salisbury shows a red card to Arsenal’s English midfielder #56 Max Dowman (R) during the English League Cup fourth round football match between Fleetwood Town and Arsenal at Highbury Stadium in Fleetwood, north west England, on October 27, 2026. (Photo by Darren Staples / AFP)
Arsene Wenger’s Arsenal suffered a shock League Cup loss against fourth tier Bradford on penalties in 2012.
Arteta’s team were beaten by second tier Southampton in the FA Cup last season and also lost to Nottingham Forest, then in the Championship, in the same competition in 2022.
Supporters of an older vintage will recall Arsenal’s 1969 League Cup final loss against third tier Swindon and their 1992 FA Cup exit at fourth tier Wrexham.
But even those painful defeats cannot compare to this remarkable result.
For once, Arsenal fans will not have fond memories of Highbury —  Fleetwood’s ground shares the same name as the Gunners’ ancestral home before their move to the Emirates Stadium in 2006.
Fleetwood’s tiny 5,327-capacity ground — where goals are celebrated with a burst of children’ cartoon song Captain Pugwash over the tannoy — is a far cry from the famous marble halls and dignified grandeur of Arsenal’s former stadium.
Now it will be remembered forever as the site of Arsenal’s most chastening loss in the Arteta era.
Fleetwood boss Matt Lawlor wept tears of joy as disbelieving fans flooded the pitch to celebrate their club’s astonishing victory.
– ‘Cod Army’ uprising –
Only Myles Lewis-Skelly and Viktor Gyokeres kept their places from the Everton game, with teenagers Dowman and Marli Salmon starting, while 18-year-old winger Ceadach O’Neill made his debut.
Arsenal’s Swedish striker #14 Viktor Gyokeres (C) celebrates after scoring the equalising goal during the English League Cup fourth round football match between Fleetwood Town and Arsenal at Highbury Stadium in Fleetwood, north west England, on October 27, 2026. (Photo by Darren Staples / AFP)
Languishing in 18th place in League Two, Fleetwood had lost their previous two league games against Exeter and Cheltenham, yet they showed no signs of being intimidated by their illustrious visitors.
After an eight-minute delay due to an unauthorised drone flying over the stadium, Arsenal were caught cold on a windy night by the Irish Sea.
Fleetwood are nicknamed the ‘Cod Army’ in reference to the town’s fishing industry, so it was somewhat fitting that a mistake from Salmon netted their opener in the 21st minute.
Salmon’s lack of experience was brutally exposed when Loupalo-Bi muscled his way past the 17-year-old with ease, racing into the penalty area to plant a low finish past debutant keeper Illan Meslier.
Fleetwood fans invade the pitch as they celebrate winning the English League Cup fourth round football match between Fleetwood Town and Arsenal at Highbury Stadium in Fleetwood, north west England, on October 27, 2026. Fleetwood won the match 5-3 following a penlaty shoot out. (Photo by Darren Staples / AFP)
Arsenal monopolised possession after that shock, but Arteta grew visibly agitated with their lack of cutting edge.
Arteta sent on Martin Odegaard at half-time and Gyokeres bagged Arsenal’s equaliser five minutes later.
It was a scrappy effort that left Fleetwood feeling aggrieved as Gyokeres wrestled with his marker before poking O’Neill’s ball past Lynch from close-range.
Dowman saw red in the 85th minute, dismissing for kicking out at Harrison Neal after a strong challenge from the Fleetwood midfielder.
Although it looked a harsh decision, Arteta was unimpressed with Dowman, giving him a stern word as the midfielder trudged off.
Both teams scored their first three penalties in the shoot-out, but Guimaraes was denied by Lynch and Haughey held his nerve to seal the biggest shock in League Cup history.
The post 4th-tier Fleetwood Town knock Arsenal out of Carabao Cup after penalties appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.title: Former Grand Slam winner Wawrinka ends tennis career
items.summary:
Stan Wawrinka bid farewell to tennis as he brought the curtain down on a decorated 24-year career following a first-round exit at the Basel Open on Tuesday.
The 41-year-old Swiss announced earlier in the season that his last tournament as a professional would be the ATP 500-level event in his home country and a 7-5, 7-6 (7/2) defeat by Czech Jiri Lehecka brought an end to the career of the three-time major champion.

On court in Basel, Wawrinka’s every point
items.author: Emmanuel Okogba
items.content:
Stan Wawrinka bid farewell to tennis as he brought the curtain down on a decorated 24-year career following a first-round exit at the Basel Open on Tuesday.
The 41-year-old Swiss announced earlier in the season that his last tournament as a professional would be the ATP 500-level event in his home country and a 7-5, 7-6 (7/2) defeat by Czech Jiri Lehecka brought an end to the career of the three-time major champion.
Former world number three Wawrinka, along with Andy Murray, was the only player to win multiple Grand Slams in a period dominated by Roger Federer, Rafael Nadal and Novak Djokovic.
He bested Nadal to win his first Grand Slam at the Australian Open in 2014, before beating Djokovic in the French Open final the following season and then again in the US Open title-match in 2016.
Alongside his compatriot Federer, the Lausanne native won the Davis Cup for Switzerland and claimed gold in the doubles at the 2008 Beijing Olympics.
On court in Basel, Wawrinka’s every point won, as well as several trademark booming one-handed backhands, was greeted by wild cheers from the partisan home crowd.
But Lehecka got his nose in front with a break of serve in the 11th game and sealed the opening set with an ace as he held to love.
A tight second set rumbled towards a tie-break, but it was just a step too far for Wawrinka as his 21st-ranked opponent took firm control to seal the breaker and the match.

items.title: Brazil’s Flavio Bolsonaro flees to US after election loss
items.summary:

items.content:
Defeated right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro left Brazil and is traveling to the United States despite a court order banning him from exiting the country, US media reported Tuesday.
The son of jailed ex-leader Jair Bolsonaro lost elections to incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva on Sunday and refused to concede defeat.
The right-wing senator on Monday said a Supreme Court justice had ordered him to hand over his passports. Bolsonaro is under investigation for alleged corruption and money laundering, and with his election loss is also set to lose his parliamentary immunity.
The 45-year-old was heading to Florida, CNN reported Tuesday, citing an anonymous official source. Other US media confirmed he was heading to the country.
The US State Department said Tuesday that it would issue visas to Bolsonaro and his family, without confirming his travel plans.
A police source told AFP that the senator’s Brazilian and diplomatic passports had been canceled, adding that “there is no formal record of Flavio Bolsonaro leaving the country.”
But he has held Italian nationality since 2023, according to an Italian parliamentary document seen by AFP.
Bolsonaro’s campaign manager Rogerio Marinho expressed shock over reports that the defeated candidate had fled Brazil.
“We still don’t have any news about his whereabouts,” he told reporters in Brasilia on Tuesday.
“I received a text message from him this morning, where he said he would let some time pass today and then would talk with us, and that was it,” Marinho said.
“That was the only communication we had.”
– Scare tactic –
Flavio Bolsonaro said Monday that the ban on his exit from Brazil amounted to a scare tactic.
“I never had any intention of leaving the country. I will surrender my passports and defend myself against this travesty,” he said in the video posted on Instagram.
US President Donald Trump, a close ally of Jair Bolsonaro, on Monday said Brazil’s elections were “rigged” following the defeat of Bolsonaro junior.
Flavio’s brother Eduardo, a US-based former lawmaker, maintains close ties with the White House.
Last week, he told a US podcast that Flavio Bolsonaro should leave Brazil in the event of electoral defeat, given the active probes into his activities.
In his Monday statement, Lula’s challenger also said he would lead the opposition to the leftist government.
Following Lula’s victory with 51.8 percent of the vote, Bolsonaro said he would seek to annul the result, citing the decision to extend polling hours over transportation difficulties that prevented some citizens from voting.
Lula had requested the extension, as had Bolsonaro over bad weather in parts of the country.
– In his father’s footsteps –
All bets were on a Bolsonaro win after he came out on top in the first round of elections earlier this month.
He campaigned on a pledge to liberate his father, who is under house arrest for coup-plotting after his own electoral loss to Lula in 2022.
Jair Bolsonaro never conceded defeat and left the country on the eve of his rival’s inauguration, only returning to Brazil three months later.
Separately on Tuesday, the Supreme Court ordered police to investigate alleged foreign funding of Flavio Bolsonaro’s campaign and other interference from abroad such as social media “manipulation.”
Lula’s campaign complained about interference in the election by Meta, the parent company of WhatsApp, Facebook and Instagram, claiming “algorithmic manipulation.”
Meta denies taking any actions to favor one side in the election, but previously said that some of Lula’s campaign ads had been mistakenly deactivated due to technical errors.

items.content:
A connector’s network can span the continent. Supplier eligibility still depends on the company and its records, with South Africa currently on SourceX’s published list.
Consider an illustrative Nairobi founder who knows a Cape Town software CEO, an ex-colleague running a London services firm and a former manager in Austin. Each could be a strong AI data licensing introduction. Each sits under different eligibility rules.
That is the core idea behind South Africa data licensing referrals. What matters is not where the connector lives. It is where the company being introduced is based, what its data looks like and who has authority to decide.
Get that distinction right and a cross-border network becomes an asset. Get it wrong and you promise a founder something nobody can deliver.
Do South African companies qualify?
SourceX’s current supported-company guidance lists the United States, Canada and the European Union. It also lists additional markets, including South Africa, the UK, Australia, New Zealand, India, Singapore, Latin America, the UAE and Saudi Arabia, under a language condition.
For a South African company, as for the other additional markets, that condition is that at least 90% of the data is in English. Other African countries are not on the current list, so a company in Lagos, Nairobi or Kigali should not be promised eligibility just because the connector has an international network.
A supported location is a starting condition, not acceptance. Rights, the actual dataset and the rest of the qualification criteria still need review.
Run a 60-second fit check before you pitch
Before making introductions, obtain an approved partner account and sign the SourceX Channel Partner Agreement. Check any employment, client or professional obligations, disclose your potential reward and ask the company’s permission. Approval to introduce a company never authorizes access to its records.
You do not need a single internal file to know whether a conversation is worth suggesting. Broad facts are enough:
Where is the company that would actually sign based?
Has it had at least 50 full-time employees at peak?
Has it operated for several years?
Outside the US, Canada and the EU: is at least 90% of its data in English?
Does it run support, CRM, engineering or documentation systems that hold real work history?
Check every mandatory condition rather than counting yes answers. A company outside the supported footprint does not become eligible because it has a large team or useful records. Where broad fit is plausible, approach an owner or authorized executive; never ask an employee to send internal files as proof.
Multinational structures need one extra step. If the Cape Town office belongs to a parent registered somewhere else, identify which entity actually holds the records and would sign. A convenient address is not the same as the supplier.
How does the referral reward work?
The SourceX referral program offers a standard reward of 25% of Actual Supplier Payout, excluding separately itemized taxes and expense reimbursements, with a cumulative cap of US$100,000 per referred company unless signed terms say otherwise. SourceX pays it separately, so the company’s own agreed payout is never reduced.
Actual Supplier Payout is the compensation actually paid for selected data that reaches Closing and the qualifying completed handoff. It excludes separately itemized taxes and expense reimbursements, the partner reward, SourceX’s fees and the buyer’s full transaction price. Unpaid estimates do not count; rewards accrue as supplier installments are paid.
The $100,000 cap applies cumulatively to each referred company across installments, agreements, repeat licenses and renewals; it never resets. SourceX pays the reward separately, without reducing the supplier’s agreed compensation. The signed Channel Partner Agreement’s Schedule A and agreed addenda control the rate, calculation base and cap.
A hypothetical example shows the arithmetic: a qualifying supplier payout of US$200,000 would produce a US$50,000 reward. It is not a typical payout, a promise in rand or naira, or evidence of a completed African transaction.
A lead, meeting or signed agreement alone earns no payable reward. A qualifying transaction must satisfy these conditions:
The buyer accepts the dataset.
The buyer’s payment to SourceX clears.
SourceX pays the supplier.
Finance approves the reward, required tax and payment details are complete, and payment is lawful.
The qualifying dataset handoff must also be complete. These payment conditions apply to the reward, not merely to whether the company seemed promising when introduced.
The reward deadline is 60 calendar days after the later of the buyer’s final written, unconditional acceptance and completed handoff of the complete, validated and approved dataset. Payment also requires cleared buyer funds at SourceX, supplier payment, finance approval, the partner’s required payment and tax details, and lawful payment. If a condition is outstanding at the deadline, payment follows promptly once it is met; no new 60-day period starts. The supplier’s invoice timetable is separate.
A convenient address is not the same as the supplier.
Disclose first, then ask permission
The introduction itself can fit in a WhatsApp message, something like this:
“Hi [name], quick one: your company may suit an AI data licensing program I know. If a qualifying deal ever completes, SourceX could pay me a referral reward on top of your payout, never out of it. Want an intro, or shall I drop it?”
Keep customer and employee records out of the first exchange entirely. The company decides what to discuss and controls any later data review.
Check any professional, board or employment duties before accepting a fee. Credit goes to the first valid introduction of a new company when it submits a verified application within the 90-day attribution window. SourceX checks dated introduction evidence, existing applications and prior relationships; an earlier click alone does not secure credit. Earlier leads, accounts or email correspondence can make a company a duplicate. Only one partner is credited per company.
Can a connector outside South Africa participate?
Partners can apply from most countries, subject to account approval and applicable U.S. sanctions and restricted-party checks. Check the connector’s eligibility separately from the supplier’s supported location; neither one establishes the other.
For South Africa data licensing referrals, the useful first action is small. Identify one established company whose owner you can approach naturally, check its location and broad fit, disclose the reward and ask whether a conversation would help.
A cross-border connection is valuable because it reaches the right decision-maker. It is never a way around the company’s authority over its own data.
Check the current company criteria and partner terms through the SourceX referral program. Obtain approval and sign before introducing a leader; explain both the potential reward and its conditions without promising a local payout.
About the founder
Noah Loul is a four-time founder and the founder and CEO of SourceX, which licenses business data directly from companies for AI training and evaluation. He previously founded B2B Rocket, acquired by Blackpearl Group. His work focuses on building permission-based data infrastructure for AI.

items.content:
Russian foreign minister Sergey Lavrov has dismissed insinuations that the Russian government sponsored some Nigerian youths who waved Russian flags during the 2024 #EndBadGovernance protests.
Lavrov, who spoke in Moscow on the sidelines of the Third Russia-Africa Summit, in response to a question by the News Agency of Nigeria, said Russia had no hand in the action and distanced Moscow from any attempt to undermine Nigeria’s sovereignty.
According to him, Russia and Nigeria enjoy a robust relationship dating back to the Soviet Union.
He said those who wore Russian flags did so in their personal capacity and that it did not translate into official support from Russia.
“Anyone, who donned the Russian flag, did so in his or her personal capacity. It does not mean that Russia was in support of this kind of action.
“A lot of citizens sympathetic to Palestinians wave Palestinian flags to express solidarity. It does not mean the Palestinian government is behind them,” Lavrov said.
The News Agency of Nigeria(NAN), recalls that the nationwide #EndBadGovernance protests took place from Aug. 1 to Aug. 10, 2024, with the protesters citing high cost of living and economic hardship for their action.
NAN also recalls that during the protests, some groups of protesters, mostly youths and minors in Kano, Kaduna, Zamfara and Abuja, were seen waving Russian flags and chanting slogans calling for military intervention.
The action, which the Federal Government described as treasonable and a threat to Nigeria’s sovereignty, led to the arrest of scores of protesters and some tailors who were allegedly sewing the flags.
The Russian Embassy in Abuja had, at the time, also denied any involvement.
Lavrov said the robust relationship between Nigeria and Russia had seen an increase in scholarships awarded to Nigerians, reaching a peak of 220 in 2026.
He recalled that in 2024, he met with his Nigerian counterpart in Abuja who warmly received him, and cemented the bilateral ties between the two countries.
On defence pacts with some countries in the Sahel, Lavrov said Russia was helping to eliminate security threats in the region, adding that Moscow was aware that some Western capitals were using Ukrainian mercenaries to sabotage the efforts, as they did in Libya, in a bid to undermine regional stability.
Commenting on the recent diesel supply agreement with the United States, the foreign minister said it was purely a business decision and would not affect the interest of its allies.
“The diesel agreement with the U.S. is purely a business decision by two world leaders who are concerned by the rising cost of energy,” he said.

items.author: Daily Trust
items.content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has reacted to reports of AI-Generated images on the published voters’ register.
In the preliminary register that the commission published after the outcry over alleged violation of the Electoral Act, there were entries from a polling unit in Etsako West Local Government Area of Edo State, which had photographs suspected to be generated by AI.
This has fueled speculations online, with many doubting the credibility of the process.
But in a statement on Tuesday, Mohammed Haruna, Chairman, Information and Voter Education Committee, clarified that the published list is not the final one.
“The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has noted public concerns and reports circulating on social media regarding suspected AI-generated photographs appearing in the Preliminary Register of Voters recently published on its website.”
“The Commission wishes to clarify that the register published online on 26 October 2026 is the same preliminary register physically displayed at Registration Areas (RAs) nationwide from 9th to 15th October 2026 as part of the Display, Claims and Objections exercise.
“During the physical display, a number of questionable registration records were identified and flagged for further examination. The Commission commenced the process of reviewing these records and taking appropriate corrective action in accordance with established procedures.
“The online publication represents the original preliminary register and does not reflect all ongoing data-cleanup activities. It is important to emphasize that the preliminary register is not the final certified register. The Display, Claims and Objections exercise is specifically intended to facilitate public scrutiny, identify inaccuracies and irregularities, and enable appropriate corrections before certification.
“The Commission is also examining the circumstances surrounding the suspicious photographs, including possible technical or procedural lapses, and will take appropriate action based on verified findings.
“The Commission appreciates the vigilance of citizens and stakeholders who have brought these concerns to public attention. Such scrutiny contributes to the process of improving the accuracy and integrity of the register.
“INEC remains committed to completing the necessary verification, adjudication, and data-cleanup processes ahead of the scheduled certification of the final Register of Voters on 15th December 2026. The Commission assures Nigerians that verified irregularities will be addressed through the applicable procedures and that further updates will be provided as the review progresses.”

items.author: Akinbayo Wahab
items.content:
The Sokoto State House of Assembly unanimously adopted the Sixth Alteration Bill, which seeks to provide a constitutional framework for establishing state police services in Nigeria.
The News Agency of Nigeria reports that the Deputy Majority Leader of the House, Mustapha Abdullahi (APC-Sokoto South II), moved the motionduring plenary in Sokoto on Tuesday.
Presenting the bill, Abdullahi said it sought to amend the 1999 Constitution, as altered, to establish state police services while retaining the Nigeria Police Force as the federal police service.
He said the executive transmitted the bill, the Senate considered it on June 24, the House of Representatives on July 23, andthe Sokoto Assembly on September 22.
According to him, the proposed framework will delineate the responsibilities of federal and state police services to ensure effective policing and address security challenges across the country.
He explained that the federal police would handle interstate and international crimes, terrorism, cybercrime, border security, policing of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) and protection of federal assets.
“Conversely, state police services would be responsible for law enforcement, maintenance of public order and safety, protection of lives and property, and investigation of local crimes.
“Therefore, the federal police and state police will function side-by-side in every state,” Abdullahi said.
The lawmaker added that the federal police could intervene in state policing matters at the request of a state governor or where there was a breakdown of law and order that the state police could not contain.
He said the head of a state police service would be known as the State Commander of Police and appointed by the governor on the recommendation of the National Police Council, subject to confirmation by the State House of Assembly.
Abdullahi further explained that the bill proposed the establishment of a State Police Service Commission as an executive body responsible for the appointment, promotion and discipline of state police personnel, except the State Commander.
On funding, the lawmaker said the proposed framework would provide for the State Police Service Commission to receive funds directly from the state’s Consolidated Revenue Fund to ensure financial autonomy.
He added that the Nigeria Police Force would continue to operate in every state until the state’s police service commenced operations.
Abdullahi cited Section 9(2) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, which provides that a constitutional alteration must be approved by resolutions of the houses of assembly of not less than two-thirds of all the states.
Contributing to the debate, several lawmakers supported the bill, describing state policing as a necessary measure to address the security challenges confronting states across the country.
The Speaker, Alhaji Tukur Bala, who presided over the plenary, subsequently put the motion to a voice vote and the lawmakers unanimously adopted it.

items.content:
— Insist on leadership rotation to Abia, urge massive voter turnout
By Steve Oko
The South-East Traditional Rulers Council has renewed its demand for the unconditional release of detained Indigenous People of Biafra, IPOB, leader, Mazi Nnamdi Kanu, lamenting that previous appeals to the Federal Government have failed to yield the desired outcome.
The monarchs also reaffirmed their position that the council’s leadership should rotate to Abia State, with HRM Eze Sir Dr Linus Nto Mbah assuming the chairmanship in accordance with the council’s constitution.
These resolutions were contained in a communiqué issued after the council’s quarterly delegates meeting held on October 23, 2026, at the Parliament of Ndi Eze, Owerri, Imo State.
On the political front, the traditional rulers expressed concern over the scheduled dates for the forthcoming national elections, which they said could pose challenges for the South-East.
They nevertheless urged eligible voters across the region to return to their respective registration areas and participate massively in the elections.
The council also called on traditional rulers and community leaders to suspend festivals and ceremonies during the election period to enable eligible voters to exercise their civic responsibilities.
On traditional leadership in the South, the monarchs reaffirmed their support for the rotational chairmanship of the Southern Traditional Rulers Council among the South-East, South-West and South-South geopolitical zones.
They rejected any arrangement that would confer permanent chairmanship on one zone, insisting that the position should rotate among the three zones for two-year terms, in line with the decision of the Southern Governors Forum reached in Ogun State in 2025.
The council further called for the reconstitution of the Southern Traditional Rulers Council’s leadership to reflect recognised traditional rulers from member states and conform to the leadership template of the Southern Governors Forum.
The communiqué was signed by the chairman of the South-East Traditional Rulers Council and chairman of the Abia State Council of Traditional Rulers, HRM Eze Dr Linus Nto Mbah; the Obi of Onitsha, HRM Igwe Nnaemeka Achebe; and other traditional rulers from the five South-East states.
The monarchs expressed appreciation to Imo State Governor, Senator Hope Uzodimma, for hosting the meeting, as well as the Imo State Council of Traditional Rulers and the people of the state for their hospitality.
They also acknowledged the support and encouragement of governors across the South-East.

items.content:
.Vows to hunt down anyone who threatens ad-hoc staff, corps members
.Set to hold National Election Security Confab
By Omeiza Ajayi
ABUJA: The Independent National Electoral Commission INEC has unveiled an intelligence-led security framework to curb violence ahead of the 2027 General Election, vowing to hunt down anyone who threatens its ad-hoc staff, National Youth Service Corps NYSC members or permanent personnel.
INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan SAN, disclosed this in Gombe on Tuesday while declaring open the North-East Zonal Interactive Meeting with Staff and Readiness Assessment for the 2027 General Election.
The Commission in its daily bulletin said it was shifting from reactive, election-day deployments to a framework designed to protect voters, personnel and electoral materials before any ballot paper is moved.
INEC said its collaboration with the Nigeria Police Force, the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps NSCDC, the Department of State Services DSS, the Armed Forces and other paramilitary agencies under the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security ICCES has, according to him, been fundamentally restructured.
The new framework, which the Commission terms the “ICCES Tentacle,” extends inter-agency security coordination from national and state headquarters directly down to the most remote Local Government Areas and Registration Area Centres.
Amupitan told the gathering that no election, however well planned administratively, could be deemed credible if voters, election personnel and observers operate under physical threat or fear of violence.
He explained that the framework rests on three pillars, the first being “Map and Mitigate.” Under it, the Commission will use Electoral Risk Management (ERM) tools to identify security flashpoints, seasonal threat factors and local vulnerabilities early, so that security agencies can deploy proactive measures long before ballot papers arrive.
The second pillar, “Ensure Safety,” provides a protective umbrella over all electoral personnel, technological assets, including Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) devices and server infrastructure, and, most importantly, the voter.
The third pillar, “Guarantee Access,” is aimed at ensuring that each of the 176,846 polling units nationwide remains a safe, peaceful and dignified space for the exercise of democratic rights, regardless of geographical remoteness or historical security challenges.
According to him, the collaboration among the agencies had already produced concrete results. He disclosed that joint operations led by the DSS recently uncovered a covert plot by criminal kingpins targeting the Commission’s ad-hoc staff and Youth Corps members.
Amupitan said swift, intelligence-led intervention neutralised the threat, and the principal orchestrators were arrested and are currently undergoing prosecution.
“Let me send a clear message from Gombe,” Amupitan said, warning that anyone who attempts to threaten, intimidate or harm ad-hoc staff, NYSC members or permanent personnel of the Commission would be hunted down and brought to justice under the full weight of the law.
He disclosed that the Commission would shortly convene a National Election Security Conference in Abuja, where state-specific security protocols for high-risk zones would be finalised.
Amupitan acknowledged that the North-East presents distinct operational challenges, including vast desert terrains, riverine stretches along the Benue trough, remote agrarian communities and expansive landmasses. He noted, however, that the zone had demonstrated remarkable resilience and civic determination.
The zone has 13,965,475 registered voters, representing 13.51 per cent of the national register of over 103 million. Bauchi State has the highest number with 3,012,547 voters, followed by Borno with 2,765,165, Adamawa with 2,431,146, Taraba with 2,254,380, Gombe with 1,768,566 and Yobe with 1,733,671.
The Chairman said the 2027 General Election would be a simultaneous national undertaking across 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). The Presidential and National Assembly Elections are scheduled for Saturday, 16th January 2027, while the Governorship and State Houses of Assembly Elections will hold on Saturday, 6th February 2027.
Earlier, the host Resident Electoral Commissioner REC for Gombe State, Alhaji Umar Muktar Gajiram, speaking on behalf of all North-East RECs, assured the Chairman that the zone was fully prepared, loyal and committed to ensuring that not a single voter out of the 13.96 million in the zone is disenfranchised.
Gajiram said all directives on voter register display, logistics audit and technological testing would be executed to the letter.
Amupitan assured staff and stakeholders across the North-East that INEC was not working in isolation, describing security as “the bedrock of electoral integrity.”
“Insecurity may pose a challenge, but our collective constitutional resolve is far stronger,” he said.

Authorities have suspended the Cameroon National Salvation Front (FSNC) of opposition figure Issa Tchiroma Bakary, in Gambian exile, for three months, the minister for territorial administration announced Tuesday.
Bakary, a former minister, had rallied young people seeking change during the presidential election of a year ago, won by 93-year-old Paul Biya, who has been in power since 1982.
Territorial administration minister Paul Atanga Nji suspended the party, according to a statement, on grounds of “incitement to insurrection” and “serious disturbance of public order,” saying this had occurred “before, during and after the presidential election of October 12, 2025.”
The statement warned the party could face legal challenge if it did not accept the sanction.
After declaring himself the winner of the election, Bakary repeatedly called on supporters to defend his “victory”, triggering protests in major cities that were brutally suppressed, resulting in a number of deaths with the government yet to provide a toll.
Thereafter Bakary went into exile in Gambia.
The temporary suspension of the party, which has two members of parliament, comes ahead of local and parliamentary elections, scheduled for early 2027 after multiple postponements.

items.author: Emmanuel Okogba
items.content:
By Favour Ulebor, Abuja
Diplomats from MIKTA member countries and the Federal government have called for improved access to climate finance, stronger international partnerships and increased investment in practical solutions to help developing countries address climate change.
The call was made at a MIKTA roundtable on Climate Finance and Implementation Partnerships in Africa, held on Tuesday in Abuja, ahead of the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference, COP31, scheduled to hold in Antalya, Türkiye, from November 9 to 20.
The discussions brought together representatives of Australia, Türkiye, Indonesia, the Republic of Korea, Mexico, Ethiopia and relevant stakeholders from the climate change sector to examine ways of translating climate commitments into projects that support economic growth, energy access, agriculture and community resilience.
Speaking at the meeting, the Australian High Commissioner to Nigeria, Ms Leilani Bin-Juda PSM, said climate action must deliver practical outcomes, particularly for developing countries and communities most vulnerable to its effects.
Bin-Juda said many developing countries continued to face difficulties accessing climate finance because of complex applications, fragmented funding systems, reporting requirements and delays.
She said Australia was working with Türkiye towards COP31 and with Pacific partners to ensure their priorities were reflected in the global climate discussions.
The High Commissioner also highlighted a Pacific-led Action Plan on access to climate finance for Small Island Developing States and Least Developed Countries, launched at Pre-COP in Fiji on October 8.
She said the initiative sought to simplify funding applications, approvals and disbursement, mobilise private investment and strengthen countries’ capacity to develop investment-ready projects.
Bin-Juda urged Nigeria to support the initiative, noting that broader international backing would strengthen efforts to make climate finance more accessible and responsive to the needs of vulnerable countries.
“For Australia, COP31 is about turning climate ambition into practical outcomes,” she said.
The Turkish Ambassador to Nigeria, Mehmet Poroy, said COP31 should focus on implementing existing commitments and ensuring that climate ambitions translated into measurable results.
Poroy said African countries needed adequate financial resources, technology, institutional capacity and support for project preparation to implement their national climate plans.
He said climate finance should also support development priorities, including energy systems, sustainable agriculture, food security, green industries and climate-resilient cities.
The ambassador highlighted Türkiye’s Climate Implementation Bridge initiative, being developed with the United Nations Development Programme, to help developing countries bridge the gap between climate commitments and investment-ready projects.
He explained that the initiative was not designed to establish a new fund or replace existing climate finance mechanisms, but to help countries connect their climate priorities with appropriate financing and private capital.
Poroy said cooperation between MIKTA countries and African partners could help strengthen implementation as the international community prepares for COP31 and COP32, expected to be hosted by Ethiopia in 2027.
Meanwhile, the Indonesian Ambassador to Nigeria, Bambang Suharto, said the scale of investment required to achieve climate targets in developing countries highlighted the need to combine public resources, private investment and international support.
He said Indonesia estimated that it would require about $472.6bn to achieve its climate targets, with annual financing needs of approximately $14.5bn through 2030, compared with an annual state budget allocation of about $4.42bn.
Suharto said Indonesia was exploring different financing instruments, including green sukuk, blended finance, thematic bonds and concessional funding, to support climate action.
He called for existing international climate finance commitments to be delivered and for greater support for project preparation to help countries develop proposals capable of attracting investment.
The envoy also highlighted the importance of ocean conservation and coastal resilience, including mangrove restoration, early-warning systems and sustainable fisheries.
He expressed Indonesia’s readiness to consult with Nigeria and interested partners on a possible Indonesia-Nigeria Climate Finance and Resilience Partnership, with potential areas of cooperation including climate-resilient agriculture, land restoration, coastal protection, clean energy and green industrialisation.
Similarly, South Korea’s Ambassador to Nigeria, Jeong Yoan, outlined opportunities to deepen climate cooperation with Nigeria through renewable energy, agricultural technology, infrastructure and green investment.
Jeong said South Korea was committed to achieving carbon neutrality by 2050 and had set a 2035 target to reduce net greenhouse gas emissions by 53 to 61 per cent compared with 2018 levels.
He said Korea’s cooperation with Nigeria included a planned 2026 to 2030 project involving the Korea International Cooperation Agency, KOICA, and the Food and Agriculture Organisation, FAO, aimed at creating green jobs for young people in agriculture and food systems.
According to him, the project is expected to support practical training in climate-smart agriculture and digital technology, with the broader objective of improving food security and strengthening resilience.
Jeong also identified private investment and a stable investment environment as important factors in mobilising climate finance, noting that clear regulations, transparent procedures and reliable infrastructure could encourage long-term investment.
He noted, Nigeria estimated that it would require about $337bn between 2026 and 2035 to meet its climate commitments, underscoring the need for domestic resources, international financing and private-sector participation.
The Mexican Charge d’Affaires in Nigeria, Jose Manuel Briseno Flores, also stressed the need to ensure that climate resources translated into practical outcomes, including renewable energy products.
He said climate finance should support solutions that could be deployed to address the needs of communities while advancing the transition towards cleaner energy.
In her remarks, the Director-General of the National Council on Climate Change, NCCC, Mrs Omotenioye Majekodunmi, said the country was committed to moving from climate pledges to implementation.
Majekodunmi who was represented by the council’s Department of Energy, Transportation and Infrastructure, NCCC, Mrs Jummai Vandu said Nigeria supported efforts to turn its Nationally Determined Contributions into bankable, investment-ready projects that could attract financing and deliver measurable results.
She identified adaptation finance, decentralised climate action, gender inclusion and a just transition as key priorities for the country.
According to her, climate finance must be predictable and accessible to communities facing environmental challenges, while international partnerships should create pathways for states, cities and local governments to implement projects at the subnational level.
She also said women and young people should be empowered as decision-makers and direct beneficiaries of climate investments, adding that the transition to clean energy must protect energy security, job creation and economic equity.
Majekodunmi said Nigeria was ready to work with MIKTA, the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change and other international partners to ensure that COP31 produced practical outcomes.
Also speaking, the Ambassador of Ethiopia to Nigeria, Legesse Geremew Haile, said Africa faced disproportionate climate vulnerabilities despite contributing marginally to global emissions.
He called for direct access to predictable, grant-based financing and technology transfers, noting that African countries needed support to implement their climate priorities.
The Ethiopian envoy highlighted his country’s Climate Resilient Green Economy Strategy and Green Legacy Initiative as examples of efforts to combine environmental protection, employment and sustainable development.
He said Ethiopia was looking forward to hosting COP32 in 2027, adding that the conference would provide an opportunity to place African development priorities, just energy transitions and loss-and-damage delivery at the centre of the global climate agenda.
MIKTA is a cross-regional partnership comprising Mexico, Indonesia, the Republic of Korea, Türkiye and Australia.

items.author: Emmanuel Okogba
items.content:
By Clare Nnabuike, Minna
Five person, four male students and a young lady have died in a fatal accident involving the Niger state governor Mohammed Umaru Bago’s convoy in Minna, the state capital.
The incident happened on Monday at Gidan Mangoro community along the Minna–Bida Road. It followed a head-on collision between a high speeding Hilux van in the convoy of Bago, and a private Peugeot 206 car.
The lady identified as Mrs Nafisa was driving the car and died at the spot of the accident. She was said to be a staff of an NGO, and Programme Manager at Labspace, and the Founder of Wosh Mart Service Ltd.
A resident of Gidan Mangoro, Abdullahi Musa, told Vanguard that the accident occurred at about 11:35am when the governor was returning from Bida. He and his team paid a condolence visit on the Etsu Nupe and chairman of the Niger state council of traditional rulers Alhaji Yahaya Abubakar over the passage of the Sagi Nupe Hajia Aisha.
He said the occupants of the private car driven by Nafisa were suspected to be postgraduate students of the Federal University of Technology, Minna.
His words, “The people in the private car died instantly, while those in the government Hilux sustained serious injuries with the driver dying on the spot.
Nafisa
“The accident was caused by wrongful overtaking by the Hilux in the governor’s convoy. The other car was in its lane when the Hilux rammed into it.”
A member of staff of Minna General Hospital, where the victims were rushed to told Vanguard that three people died on the spot while two other people died due to high level of injuries sustain from the crash.
“Some of the injured victims were subsequently referred to IBB Specialist Hospital for advanced medical care,” he said.
Vanguard gathered that one of the occupants of the Hilux van was a former Niger state local government council chairman who sustained fractures to his legs but was still alive at the time of this report.
The Niger State Sector Commander of the Federal Road Safety Corps, FRSC Aishat Sa’adu, confirmed the road crash but said that by the time her officers arrived at the scene, the victims had already been evacuated to the hospital.
The Police Public Relations Officer of the Niger state command Superintendent of Police Wasiu Abiodun confirmed the incident and said the accident was under investigation. He did not however give the names or numbers of the deceased.
“The accident occured this morning and we are investigating it,” Abiodun said.

items.content:
…19-month health workers’ arrears
By Victor Ahiuma-Young
The Federal Government and the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) have reached an agreement on a series of measures aimed at easing the economic difficulties facing workers, including a ₦70,000 transport intervention and the payment of 19 months’ arrears owed to health workers.
The resolutions were reached at a conciliation meeting held at the Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment on Tuesday, 27 October 2026, following an earlier meeting convened on 22 October.
The meetings were organised to address concerns raised by the NLC over the rising cost of living, the implementation of the National Minimum Wage, petroleum pump prices, workers’ welfare and outstanding allowances.
Under the agreement, the Federal Government will provide a transport intervention of ₦70,000 across all levels for six months, beginning in November 2026.
The government also approved the peculiar allowance with effect from 1 May 2026. Payment of the arrears is expected to begin in November and will be made in three equal monthly instalments.
In addition, the 19 months’ outstanding allowances owed to health workers will be paid within three months, beginning in December 2026.
The meeting also agreed that the Minimum Wage Negotiation Committee would be constituted and commence work immediately. However, the parties remained divided over the effective date for implementing the new minimum wage.
On the issue of tax relief for workers, the meeting resolved that the matter would be referred to the National Executive Council, as taxation is a statutory issue.
The Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security has submitted the list of beneficiaries and the cost implications of the proposed hazard allowance for agricultural officers to the National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission for verification.
The verification is expected to be completed within two weeks, after which the commission will issue an implementation template.
Similarly, the NSIWC is expected to complete an updated assessment of the cost implications of the proposed CONHESS adjustment within three weeks. The assessment will enable the Presidential Committee on Salaries to take a decision on the matter.
The Federal Government and the NLC urged state and local governments to participate in the intervention process and implement the agreed measures.
The parties also agreed to reconvene after one month to review the level of implementation of the resolutions.
The agreement was signed on behalf of the federal government by Dr. Muhammad Maigari Dingyadi, Honourable Minister of Labour and Employment, Timi Yakubu, Director-General, Budget, Dr. Garba Abdul S. U., Permanent Secretary (SWO), Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation.
