Sustained Earnings Momentum Reinforces BOP’s Financial Strength
The Bank of Punjab continued its upward earnings trajectory during the nine months endedSeptember 30, 2026, demonstrating the strength of its core banking franchise and the effectiveness of its business strategy. Operating Profit (before provisions and gains) climbed to Rs. 34.42 billion, marking an impressive 34% year-on-year increase. The Bank’s revenue performance remained equally encouraging, with Net Interest Income reaching Rs. 69.40 billion, up 19%, while Non-Markup Income (excluding gains) advanced to Rs. 18.04 billion, recording 47% growth. These results highlight the Bank’s ability to generate sustainable earnings through strategic balance sheet management, strengthening non-funded income streams, and a diversified revenue base.
The sustained strength in core earnings, complemented by disciplined expense management, continued to support the Bank’s overall profitability. Profit Before Tax rose to Rs. 30.46 billion, representing 15% year-on-year growth, while Profit After Tax increased to Rs. 14.53 billion, reflecting a 22% improvement over the corresponding period last year. The Bank’s continued focus on productivity, cost optimization, and operational discipline contributed to improved efficiency, with the Cost-to-Income Ratio (excluding gains) improving by 3.03%. This combination of revenue growth, profitability, and enhanced operating efficiency reflects BOP’s progress towards building a stronger, more competitive, and financially resilient banking institution.
Robust Advances Growth & Improved Deposit Mix
The Bank also demonstrated sustained business momentum during the nine months ended September 30, 2026, with gross advances registering an impressive 28% year-on-year growth, reflecting the Bank’s expanding lending footprint and continued support for economic activity. Despite a broadly stable overall balance sheet, the Bank made significant strides in strengthening its core deposit franchise, with current deposits growing by 16% year-on-year, while average current deposits recorded a remarkable 25% increase over the corresponding period last year.
This strong growth in low-cost deposits underscores the Bank’s continued focus on improving its funding mix, enhancing funding efficiency, and building a more sustainable foundation for long-term profitability. Total assets and deposits stood at Rs. 2,456 billion and Rs. 1,928 billion, respectively, while gross advances reached Rs. 1,073 billion, highlighting the Bank’s continued emphasis on productive asset deployment and strengthening its core banking business.
Strengthened Capital Base & Regulatory Compliance
The Bank further reinforced its capital position, supported by strong financial performance and continued equity support from the Government of Punjab. During the period, the Bank received Rs. 15.6 billion from the Government of Punjab under the equity injection arrangements, representing a significant step towards strengthening its capital base.
As of September 30, 2026, the Bank’s Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR) stood at 13.94%, while its Leverage Ratio reached 4.07%, both comfortably above the regulatory requirements prescribed by the State Bank of Pakistan. The Bank also maintained full compliance with applicable IFRS 9 provisioning requirements, reaffirming its commitment to prudent financial management, regulatory discipline, and long-term financial resilience.
Strategic Milestones & Growing Institutional Recognition
The year 2026 marked significant strategic achievements for The Bank of Punjab, further strengthening its institutional standing and growth prospects. The Bank’s long-term credit rating was upgraded by PACRA to the highest AAA category with a Stable Outlook, reflecting its strengthened financial profile and institutional resilience.
Expanding its international footprint, BOP also secured in-principle approval from the State Bank of Pakistan to establish an Overseas Wholesale Banking Unit in the Kingdom of Bahrain, opening new avenues for cross-border business and regional connectivity. Complementing these milestones, the Bank continued to earn prestigious national recognition, securing three accolades at the Pakistan Banking Awards 2026 for Agriculture Inclusion, SME Banking, and Women’s Inclusion. These achievements extend BOP’s remarkable track record of consecutive awards across key banking segments, reinforcing its growing market standing, commitment to financial inclusion, and pursuit of sustainable long-term growth.
Building a Future-Ready Bank | Strategic Outlook
The Bank of Punjab continues to strengthen its position as a dynamic and increasingly competitive financial institution, combining its established public-sector relationships with a growing commercial banking franchise. Beyond its traditional role as a key financial partner to the Government of Punjab, BOP is progressively broadening its business horizons through deeper customer engagement, diversification of banking services, and a sharper focus on sustainable, relationship-driven growth.
The Bank remains committed to leveraging technology, digital innovation, and operational excellence to enhance customer experience, improve service delivery, and build a more efficient and agile banking model. With a clear emphasis on strengthening core banking capabilities, maintaining prudent risk management, and capitalizing on emerging domestic and international opportunities, BOP aims to translate its institutional progress into enduring financial performance. Looking ahead, the Bank’s strategic direction remains firmly anchored in profitable growth, customer-centric innovation, financial inclusion, and sustainable stakeholder value, while continuing to play a meaningful role in Pakistan’s economic development.

items.content:
Pakistan has paid around $16 billion in interest on its foreign loans over the past four years, an average of about $4 billion a year, State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) Governor Jameel Ahmed has said.
Speaking at his post-monetary policy press conference on Monday, the governor said the country’s total external debt now stands at around $107 billion. It was already above $100 billion in 2022.
He said that if Pakistan had not borrowed at all, its external debt would have been around $116 billion today because of the interest it paid.
Interest Paid Without New Loans
About $10 to 11 billion of this interest was paid with dollars the SBP bought from the market, not with fresh loans.
The central bank has bought over $30 billion from the market in this period. This also helped lift reserves from about $3 billion in early 2023, when they covered only two weeks of imports, to around $21.5 billion now.
SBP Governor said external debt grew by only $5 to 6 billion in the last four years, or about $1 to 1.25 billion a year. Between 2015 and 2022, it rose by around $6.5 billion every year.
Interest Bill to Fall Below $3 Billion
The governor said the quality of Pakistan’s debt has also improved. About 80 percent of external debt now comes from multilateral and bilateral lenders, such as the World Bank and the Asian Development Bank, up from 55 percent in early 2023.
He expects annual interest payments to fall below $3 billion next year.
Governor said SBP aims to raise forex reserves to $23 billion by December and $25 billion by June 2027.
The remarks came after the SBP raised the policy rate by 50 basis points to 12 percent. Earlier this year, Pakistan’s foreign debt interest bill was reported to have jumped sharply.

items.content:
The National Assembly was informed on Monday that tax exemptions worth Rs11.047 trillion were granted over the last five years, while the government was preparing a new policy to provide relief to low-income households facing high liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) prices.
According to the Finance Ministry, the exemptions were granted between fiscal years 2020-21 and 2024-25. They included Rs580 billion in income tax, Rs1.274 trillion in sales tax and Rs499 billion in customs duty, while the overall figure covered tax exemptions across the period.
Responding to a Calling Attention Notice on rising LPG prices, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik said that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had held two to three meetings to address the LPG price issue.
He said the government was working on a comprehensive policy to improve supplies and provide relief to deserving consumers, which would be finalised within one to two days.
"The prime minister is fully aware of the difficulties faced by the consumers," Malik said, adding that progress would be visible soon. He said the proposed policy would seek to ensure fair competition in the market while providing subsidised fuel to vulnerable households.
The minister said the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority's (OGRA) notified rate of Rs280 applied to locally produced LPG, while no policy was currently in place for imported supplies. He added that the price of locally produced LPG was also linked to the international contract price set by Saudi Aramco.
The international benchmark had risen to $705 per tonne, contributing to changes in notified prices, Malik said. The proposed policy would consider supply difficulties through land borders and explore arrangements to import alternative supplies from Oman and Saudi Arabia.
He said the government was examining additional costs associated with LPG supplies, as no adequate mechanism was available to cover them. Since locally produced and imported LPG could not be treated differently in the market, enforcement action by OGRA could create further complications, he added.
Malik said that Pakistan's gas supply had been affected by the suspension of around 900 million cubic feet per day of gas supplies from Qatar due to the war, forcing the government to ration available supplies. He acknowledged that demand for alternative fuels would increase as winter approached.
The government also presented details of youth financing and training initiatives. According to the Planning Ministry, 518,000 young people had received loans under the Prime Minister's Youth Business and Agriculture Loan Programme, while a target had been set to train 230,000 young people.
The Higher Education Commission (HEC) informed the house that undergraduate degree programmes required internships or field experience worth at least three credit hours. The commission had also revised the national curricula for 47 disciplines.

items.title: FBR Orders Textile Mills to Install Cameras
items.summary:
The Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) has directed all registered textile spinning units to install video surveillance cameras by November 15, 2026, to monitor the processing of cotton and other natural, man made and blended fibers.
Under Sales Tax General Order No. 30 of 2026, issued on Monday, FBR has expanded electronic production monitoring requirements to cover loose, opened and other non bale forms of fiber, including cotton, polyester, viscose, wool and acrylic.
The new requirements supplement an earlier order issued on November 20, 2025.
FBR Specifies Camera Installation Points
The order requires cameras at key points across textile spinning operations, including hopper bale openers and hopper feeders where loose fiber is fed manually, as well as weighing hopper feeders and blending feeders used to mix natural and man made fibers.
Surveillance is also required on blow room lines dedicated to man-made fibers, including polyester and viscose, as well as acrylic processing lines.

items.author: Muhammad Bilal
items.content:
The Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) has directed all registered textile spinning units to install video surveillance cameras by November 15, 2026, to monitor the processing of cotton and other natural, man made and blended fibers.
Under Sales Tax General Order No. 30 of 2026, issued on Monday, FBR has expanded electronic production monitoring requirements to cover loose, opened and other non bale forms of fiber, including cotton, polyester, viscose, wool and acrylic.
The new requirements supplement an earlier order issued on November 20, 2025.
FBR Specifies Camera Installation Points
The order requires cameras at key points across textile spinning operations, including hopper bale openers and hopper feeders where loose fiber is fed manually, as well as weighing hopper feeders and blending feeders used to mix natural and man made fibers.
Surveillance is also required on blow room lines dedicated to man-made fibers, including polyester and viscose, as well as acrylic processing lines.
Waste openers, recycling lines handling soft waste, comber noil and card flat strips, and mixing or laydown areas where loose fibers are stacked or mixed must also be monitored.
Video Analytics Must Track Production in Real Time
The FBR has directed vendors authorized under Chapter XIV BA of the Sales Tax Rules, 2006, to ensure their video analytics systems are integrated with the installed cameras and can detect, count and quantify fibers fed into production in loose, open, or other non-bale forms.
The systems must capture production processes in real time, collect production data through object detection and counting, and transmit data to the FBR’s Central Control Unit in real time. They must also store and archive data, detect unexpected production stoppages, analyze production quantities and support data analysis for required legal action.
The FBR issued the new order under Section 40C(2) of the Sales Tax Act, 1990, and Rules 150ZQR and 150ZQT of the Sales Tax Rules, 2006.
The board said Sales Tax General Order No. 08 of 2025, dated November 20, 2025, will remain in force. The latest order adds monitoring requirements for loose, opened and other non bale fiber processing to the existing system for monitoring cotton bales.

Logistics company LEAP India reported a net profit of ₹17.8 Cr in Q2 FY27, up 62% from nearly ₹11 Cr in the year-ago period. Sequentially, the company’s profit dipped 28% from ₹24.7 Cr in Q1 FY27.

The company also announced two strategic acquisitions. Through its wholly owned subsidiaries, LEAP signed agreements to acquire the businesses of Vimprotech and Total International Packaging Solutions (TIPS) for a combined consideration of ₹142 Cr. The businesses generated ₹65 Cr in revenue in FY26 and serve more than 200 customers across sectors including electronics, white goods, pharmaceuticals, agriculture, automotive and food and beverages.
Vimprotech brings in-house plastics design, mould-making and manufacturing capabilities across facilities in Puducherry and Tamil Nadu. TIPS adds an automotive container-pooling business with four warehouses across Bengaluru, Nashik and Tirunelveli. The acquisitions are expected to strengthen backward integration, reduce reliance on external suppliers and create cross-selling opportunities for pallets, crates, containers and MHE.
Founded in 2013 by Sunu Mathew, LEAP India provides supply chain solutions spanning equipment pooling, inventory management, transportation, and repair and maintenance. It serves customers across sectors such as FMCG, beverages, ecommerce, automotive and retail.
Asset pooling remained the core growth driver. Income from asset pooling increased 19% YoY in Q2 FY27, while material handling equipment (MHE) income rose 52%. LEAP operates a pool of 15.5 Mn assets valued at over ₹1,820 Cr, serving more than 1,100 customers across 11,000-plus touchpoints and 27 fulfilment centres. Customer churn remained below 0.5%.
Asset utilisation stood at 89.3% for pallets and 82.3% for MHE as of September 2026, while container utilisation improved to 73.7%. LEAP estimates that it commands around 90% of India’s organised pallet-pooling market, which it expects to expand as organised warehousing, supply-chain automation and modern retail drive demand.
LEAP’s balance sheet also strengthened. Net debt nearly halved to ₹433.7 Cr from ₹801 Cr a year earlier, while the debt-to-equity ratio improved to 0.48x from 0.96x. Net debt-to-EBITDA declined to around 1.9x from 4.4x.
“Strong growth, continued improvements in cost efficiency and rising profitability position us well to sustain this momentum. With a scalable business model, disciplined execution and a clear focus on operational excellence, we remain confident in our ability to deliver long-term value and strengthen the trust our shareholders have placed in us,” Mathew said.
Shares of LEAP India ended today’s trading session 3.06% higher at ₹126.35 apiece on the BSE.

items.author: Business Desk
items.content:
Pakistan’s Directorate General of Customs Valuation Karachi has set new customs values for three types of imported firearms, including 9mm pistols and rifles, under Valuation Ruling No. 2121/2026.
Under the ruling, the customs value of a Norinco CF98 pistol, caliber 9mm, has been fixed at $140 per piece, while another CF98 pistol, caliber 9mm, has been valued at $134 per piece.
The customs value of a Norinco CQ A5 rifle, caliber .223 Rem, has been set at $205 per piece. The revised values apply to imports from all origins.
New Ruling Replaces Previous Valuation
Issued under Section 25A of the Customs Act, 1969, the ruling supersedes the relevant values established under Valuation Ruling dated May 17, 2023, and its addendum dated September 23, 2024, for the items covered by the latest determination.
The directorate initiated the reassessment after receiving requests from stakeholders to review customs values for certain items covered by the previous ruling. Proceedings under Section 25D of the Customs Act, 1969, were also initiated to amend the earlier valuation.
The process followed Order in Revision No. 14/2026, dated May 25, 2026, which directed the directorate to conduct a fresh valuation exercise for arms and ammunition.
The directorate subsequently held a meeting with relevant stakeholders, who presented their views on the existing customs values. Representatives were given an opportunity to submit supporting documents for their claims.
Market Research Used to Determine Values
The directorate reviewed stakeholder submissions, available import data, previous valuation records, market information and other relevant material. It also conducted market inquiries to determine prevailing prices before finalizing the revised customs values.
According to the ruling, the valuation methods prescribed under Section 25 of the Customs Act, 1969, were considered in sequence.
However, the transaction value method under Section 25(1) could not be applied because the information required under Section 25(2) was unavailable.
The directorate also examined the identical goods method under Section 25(5) and the similar goods method under Section 25(6).
Both methods were found unsuitable because of differences in brands, models, specifications, declared values and other transaction-related factors.
Consequently, the customs values were determined through market inquiry under Section 25(7) of the Customs Act, 1969.

items.author: ZAFAR BHUTTA
items.content:
Pakistan's economic managers have tasked the Ministry of Industries' secretary with immediately selling 21 properties valuing at Rs12 billion. The Economic Coordination Committee (ECC), in a recent meeting, directed the secretary to ensure a smooth disposal of the immovable property of Utility Stores Corporation (USC) without delay. USC owns 21 properties worth Rs12.045 billion.
The Ministry of Industries and Production informed the meeting that Rs23.20 billion had been allocated during financial year 2026-27 and accordingly it requested the Finance Division to release the amount, as earmarked in the federal budget. In response, the Finance Division advised USC to expedite the realisation of proceeds from the disposal of properties and assets, and submit a case for approval of a technical supplementary grant of Rs11.98 billion.
For the sale of USC properties, the ministry has already taken up the matter with the Privatisation Commission in accordance with its mandate under the Privatisation Commission Ordinance, 2000. However, their disposal still awaited the approval of the Privatisation Commission and the Cabinet Committee on Privatisation (CCOP). The CCOP constituted a committee, headed by the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan, to examine the matter and recommend the future course of action.
The Ministry of Industries pointed out that as the process for liquidation of USC assets was still pending, the corporation required immediate funding to discharge its outstanding financial obligations arising from its closure. The ECC was requested to approve Rs11.329 billion as a technical supplementary grant for USC to meet its immediate financing requirements and facilitate completion of the closure process. The remaining requirement of Rs21.529 billion would be taken up separately with the Finance Division.
During discussions, the ECC expressed its satisfaction over the efforts made by the Ministry of Industries to shut down the utility stores. It considered a summary titled "Request for Approval of Technical Supplementary Grant and Funding Requirements for Completion of Closure Process of Utility Stores Corporation during financial year 2026-27" and approved the proposal with the directive that the industries secretary, under guidance of the adviser to PM on industries, would ensure a smooth disposal of the immovable property of USC.
The ministry briefed the ECC that pursuant to directives of the prime minister and the federal cabinet decision, the operations of USC were closed across Pakistan with effect from July 31, 2025. The ECC had approved a supplementary grant of Rs30.216 billion to pay off the employees' severance package and other dues, clear the outstanding liabilities of suppliers and meet expenditures pertaining to the continuation of operations till the eventual privatisation of USC. The decision was subsequently ratified by the federal cabinet.
As per the cash flow plan approved by the cabinet, the total funds required for the USC closure were estimated at Rs40.151 billion, of which Rs13.822 billion was projected to be generated through the disposal of USC assets, resulting in a net federal government liability of Rs26.329 billion. Of this, Rs15 billion had been released during FY2025-26, which was fully utilised.
The Ministry of Industries apprised the ECC that USC had implemented the closure plan and achieved significant progress. In that regard, 11,083 employees were laid off and a severance package amounting to Rs8.146 billion was disbursed to 9,119 employees after third-party validation. In addition, widow compensation worth Rs683 million and house ceiling payment of Rs147 million were also released.
A voluntary settlement agreement with the workers' union, vetted by the Ministry of Law, was successfully concluded. Furthermore, during FY2025-26, payments of Rs3.381 billion were made to suppliers after third-party validation. Also, branded stocks valuing at Rs3.074 billion, out of the total of Rs3.650 billion, were returned to suppliers without additional cost, resulting in an exceptionally high stock return ratio of 85%.
USC also liquidated perishable stocks (rice, pulses, condiments, etc) through an auction and realised net proceeds of Rs214.60 million (excluding taxes) against the projected sale price of Rs208.89 million, and compared to the approved cash flow projection of Rs50 million.
Owing to obsolete stock, the USC board approved a total write-off amounting to Rs204.58 million. Moreover, assets such as steel racks were disposed of through an auction, generating around Rs8.40 million against the target of Rs350 million.
The Ministry of Industries told the ECC that USC had cleared a three-year backlog of statutory audits, updated audited accounts up to FY2024-25 and settled 1,003 internal audit observations. Owing to the closure of retail operations, workforce rationalisation and reduction in operational expenditures, USC made savings of Rs13 billion.
In order to complete the essential residual functions, the USC board, during its 203rd meeting held on June 11, 2026, approved the retention of 326 essential staff till the completion of residual tasks. For meeting the remaining obligations arising from implementation of the closure plan, the board, in its 205th meeting on August 20, 2026, approved the budgetary requirement of Rs32.858 billion for FY2026-27, covering employee compensation, terminal dues, vendor payments, TCP liability, administrative expenses and other obligations.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Bulls returned to the Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) on Monday as buying re-emerged in index-heavy sectors in the latter half of trading, reversing the early fall amid anxiety ahead of the State Bank of Pakistan's (SBP) policy rate decision.
In the morning, trading started on a weak note as the KSE-100 index fell to 162,347.31, down 27.56 points. Sentiment remained subdued over the lack of positive triggers while the Monetary Policy Committee's (MPC) decision later in the day also weighed on market mood. The benchmark index posted a gain of 663.59 points, or 0.41%, to close at 163,038.47.
The market remained under pressure earlier in the session, with the index touching the intra-day low of 161,250.07. However, upward momentum in the latter half took it to the high of 163,477.09. In the afternoon, the SBP raised its policy rate by 50 basis points to 12%, a move that would increase borrowing costs for businesses.
Meanwhile, international oil prices fell after surging last week but remained near six-month highs amid expectations of easing hostilities between the US and Iran. Persistent attacks on key oil producer Saudi Arabia, however, kept investors wary and continued to cloud the outlook for global energy supplies.
According to KASB KTrade equity trader Ahmed Sheraz, the KSE-100 index closed up 664 points (+0.41%), recovering from the intra-day low of 161,250 to the high of 163,477. Trading remained volatile amid earlier concerns over a potential 100-basis-point rate hike, while buying interest emerged later, particularly in cement, which helped the index recover to close in positive territory. Sector-wise, performance was mixed, where cement firms, investment banks and oil & gas companies contributed positively. UBL, Engro Holdings and Lucky Cement supported the upside, while Meezan Bank closed in the red.
Meanwhile, Brent crude hovering near $115 per barrel continued to fuel inflationary concerns. Pakistan, alongside Saudi Arabia and Turkey, was pursuing mediation efforts with Iran as a delegation visited Tehran on Monday. Despite the positive close, investor sentiment may remain cautious amid elevated oil prices, regional mediation efforts, Israeli elections and the upcoming US midterm polls, Sheraz said.
"The market traded in both directions amid cautious investor sentiment ahead of the SBP's MPC announcement, with market participants largely anticipating a 50-basis-point hike in the policy rate," Arif Habib Limited Deputy Head of Trading Ali Najib commented.
Later, the central bank raised the policy rate by 50 basis points to 12%, in line with market expectations. The decision reflected heightened geopolitical risks stemming from the US-Iran conflict, which drove international oil and commodity prices higher, raising concerns over domestic inflationary pressures. On the geopolitical front, Pakistan's Chief of Defence Forces arrived in Tehran for high-level talks involving Iran, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye amid escalating regional tensions following Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.
UBL, Engro Holdings, Lucky Cement and OGDC contributed 719 points to the index, while Meezan Bank, Engro Fertilisers, Fauji Fertiliser, Pakistan Services and HBL erased 367 points.

The Central Development Working Party (CDWP) has recommended three projects worth Rs172.25 billion to the Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (ECNEC) while approving 10 smaller schemes valued at Rs40.915 billion, at a meeting chaired by Federal Minister for Planning, Development and Special Initiatives and Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission Ahsan Iqbal.
Two of the three referrals are climate-resilient irrigation schemes co-financed by the Asian Development Bank (ADB), which together account for Rs129.19 billion of the referred total, according to a statement issued on Monday.
The Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Resilient Irrigated Agriculture Livelihoods Development Project, valued at Rs69,893 million, will be financed by the ADB with Rs56,132.50 million and the Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa government with Rs11,691.90 million, with land acquisition funded through a separate planning commission proforma (PC-I). It will rehabilitate the Pehur Main Canal, construct the Mulkhow Irrigation Distribution System and extend the Pehur High Level Canal.
The Integrated Hill Torrent Management (Chachar-Mithawan) project in Dera Ghazi Khan and Rajanpur, worth Rs85,342.110 million, will be co-financed by the ADB with Rs73,060 million and the Punjab government with Rs12,282.11 million, implementing spate irrigation, flood protection channels, telemetry and centralised SCADA monitoring.
The third referral is the Prime Minister's Solar Scheme for Newly Merged Districts, valued at Rs13,323 million, approved in principle to provide off-grid solar energy solutions to households.
Of the 10 approved projects, the CDWP cleared Daanish Schools across Azad Jammu and Kashmir, Gilgit-Baltistan, Balochistan, Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa and Sindh at Rs122.400 million, with instructions to rationalise costs, along with a Daanish School in Kuri, Islamabad, at Rs7,357.233 million and another in Qila Saifullah, Balochistan, at Rs4,527.838 million.
Higher education schemes approved in principle include the Prime Minister's Youth Development Centres at Rs4,144.854 million, the Talent Hunt Youth Sports League (Phase-I) at Rs3,988.056 million, the National Innovation Award at Rs1,970 million and sports academies with the Youth Olympics at Rs2,955.927 million. The party also approved in principle revamping Pakistan Television Corporation (PTVC) at Rs3,962.250 million and a pilot Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) at the 220kV Jhimpir-I grid station at Rs4,394.720 million.
It approved an eight-lane overhead bridge at Imamia Colony Railway Crossing, Shahdara, at Rs7,492.050 million, and recommended widening of National Highway N-45 from Chakdara to Timergara, 39 kilometres, at Rs17,012.323 million to ECNEC, to be financed through Exim Bank.

items.author: SHAHRAM HAQ
items.content:
Economic, trade and investment policy uncertainty eased in Pakistan during September 2026, led by a sharp decline in policy concerns after the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) kept its policy rate unchanged, foreign exchange reserves increased and tax collection hit the first-quarter target, according to the Lahore School of Economics (LSE).
The LSE Policy Uncertainty Index dropped 24.21% month-on-month to 162.46 in September. The decline indicates that businesses and investors saw a more stable policy environment during the month, although concerns over fuel prices, subsidies and delayed talks with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) continued to weigh on sentiment.
The central bank left the policy rate on hold at 11.5% in September, providing some clarity to markets about borrowing costs. Meanwhile, Pakistan's foreign exchange reserves rose to $26.8 billion, improving confidence in the country's external financial position. On Monday, however, the SBP raised the rate by 50 basis points to 12%.
The Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) met its overall revenue target for the first quarter of fiscal year 2026-27. However, income tax collection missed the target, showing that pressure on government finances had not fully eased. Policy uncertainty remained high in areas linked to energy pricing. The government continued with daily fuel price adjustments and kept petroleum levy at a high level. It also introduced a fuel subsidy scheme, which raised concerns at the IMF.
Talks with the IMF on its review programme remained stalled over issues including fuel subsidies, gas-sector receivables and the circular debt. These unresolved matters could limit the improvement in economic confidence if these are not addressed.
Trade policy uncertainty came down, but still it stood at a relatively higher level. The Lahore School Trade Policy Uncertainty Index declined 22.1% month-on-month to 192.89 in September. The drop came as trade deficit narrowed in August and exports during July and August rose 7% compared with the same period a year earlier. The improvement in exports and a smaller deficit offered some relief for the external sector.
The government also continued its tariff rationalisation programme. Duties on imported mobile phones were reduced, signalling that the authorities were moving ahead with planned trade reforms. However, trade-related concerns persisted because the Auto Industry Development and Export Policy for 2026-31 had not been finalised. The proposed policy was under IMF review, leaving automakers and investors without clarity about future rules for the sector. Disruption to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz added another risk. The route remained affected during the month, while Brent crude oil prices moved above $100 per barrel. Higher oil prices and shipping disruptions could increase Pakistan's import bill and put renewed pressure on inflation.
Investment policy uncertainty recorded a smaller decline. The Lahore School Investment Policy Uncertainty Index fell 6.45% month-on-month to 145, supported by progress on power-sector reforms and Pakistan's successful return to international debt markets.
Regulatory uncertainty eased as the privatisation process for electricity distribution companies moved forward. A revised draft of the telecom bill was also prepared, although concerns raised in the Senate showed that regulatory changes may still face political and institutional hurdles. Financial uncertainty declined after Pakistan raised a record $3 billion through a Eurobond issue. The transaction reduced immediate financing concerns and signalled improved investor access to international markets.

items.author: Business Desk
items.content:
Pakistan’s textile exporters say the country is making it harder for them to compete globally, as high production costs and expensive industrial loans put local manufacturers at a disadvantage against rivals in India, Vietnam and China.
The Pakistan Textile Exporters Association (PTEA) has criticized the State Bank of Pakistan for raising its policy rate by 50 basis points to 12 percent because higher borrowing costs will add to the pressure on an industry already struggling with expensive energy and raw materials.
PTEA Chairman Rehan Naseem Bharara said the rate increase would make working capital more expensive, discourage investment and weaken exporters’ ability to compete in international markets.
He added that the actual cost of borrowing for Pakistani businesses rises further once banks’ spreads are included.
He said industrial term loans in India carry annual rates of around 9.25 to 9.6 percent, while machinery and small and medium-sized enterprise (SME) loans range from 8.5 to 12.5 percent.
In Vietnam, SMEs in supporting industries can borrow at rates of 8 to 10 percent.
China offers even cheaper financing, with the average lending rate for general business loans at 3.04 percent.
Loans for technological upgrades carry rates of around 2.7 percent, which can fall to an effective 0.85 percent after government interest subsidies, he said.
Bharara argued that Pakistani exporters are being forced to compete with businesses in China and Vietnam that have access to substantially cheaper capital. He called for coordinated steps to reduce production costs and support export-led growth.
Exporters Warn of More Pressure
PTEA Vice Chairman Haris Yousaf said exporters were already struggling to finance daily operations, purchase raw materials and cover other expenses.
Higher interest rates would make these challenges worse and could undermine the government’s export-led growth plans.
Yousaf also warned that a prolonged decline in exports could slow economic growth, reduce funds available for development spending and weaken Pakistan’s ability to meet its external debt obligations.
Shipping costs have also increased by nearly 200 percent, he added.
Yousaf said SMEs, which contribute around 45 percent of Pakistan’s gross domestic product, need easier access to financing to expand and remain sustainable.
More expensive loans could discourage investment and further constrain business activity.
PTEA called for an export-focused policy framework that treats the textile value chain as an interconnected industry rather than targeting its different parts through separate taxation measures.

items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
Apple’s first foldable smartphone, the iPhone Duo, has undergone a teardown by repair specialists at iFixit, revealing a complicated hinge mechanism that could be linked to recent reports of display damage.
The teardown also found that the iPhone Duo is relatively easy to repair compared with competing foldable smartphones, earning a repairability score of 5 out of 10.
For comparison, Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold8 received a score of 4 out of 10, while the older Galaxy Z Fold7 scored 3 out of 10.
Easier Repairs Than Other Foldables
According to iFixit, several internal components of the iPhone Duo can be removed without dismantling most of the device.
The external display, for example, can be detached using a suction clamp and a prying tool. The process appears at approximately 4:20 in iFixit’s teardown video.
The phone also features two batteries that can be removed using Apple’s electrically assisted adhesive-release system, known as anodic delamination.
This method involves connecting a low-voltage power source, such as a 9V battery, to silver tabs on the battery cells. The electrical current releases the adhesive holding the batteries in place.
The battery removal process is demonstrated at around 5:50 in the teardown video.
&&&&&&&
How Apple Hides the Display Crease
The teardown also provides a closer look at the technology Apple uses to make the foldable display’s crease less noticeable.
At approximately 3:00 in the video, iFixit examines the inner screen’s matte nano-texture protective layer under a microscope.
The surface contains thousands of microscopic bumps that scatter reflected light, making the crease harder to see.
Apple also uses a modified arrangement of RGB subpixels inside the OLED panel. These subpixels sit at different angles to further reduce the visibility of the fold.
Together, these technologies help conceal the crease without removing the physical fold in the display.
Complicated Hinge Raises Concerns
Despite its relatively good repairability score, the iPhone Duo’s hinge mechanism has raised concerns following complaints from early buyers.
Several owners have reported that the hinge becomes unusually stiff while unfolding the device.
When users apply additional force, they reportedly hear a popping or cracking sound, followed by permanent damage to the inner screen.
The affected displays typically develop a vertical line through the center and a horizontal line extending toward the right side.
iFixit’s teardown reveals a complicated hinge design that could help explain the reported failures.
One possible explanation is that certain components inside the hinge are not moving downward correctly, causing the mechanism to become stuck.
Another potential cause is the accordion-like flexible cable running through the hinge, which could interfere with the folding mechanism.
However, neither explanation has been confirmed, and the exact cause of the reported display failures remains unknown.

items.author: Akshit Pushkarna
items.content:
Fintech major Paytm’s profit for the September quarter surged to ₹225 Cr, 10.7X from ₹21 Cr in the year-ago quarter.
The company’s profit for the period was also ₹5 Cr higher than the ₹220 Cr net profit raked in the June quarter. Meanwhile, its EBITDA surged 90% YoY to ₹270 Cr
Operating revenue for the quarter surged 28% YoY and 8% QoQ to ₹2,648 Cr. Including other income of ₹182 Cr, Paytm’s total income for the quarter stood at ₹2,830 Cr.
Meanwhile, total expenses for the quarter also increased 23% YoY to ₹2,531 Cr. Payment processing charges continued to be the biggest expense during the quarter under review and increased 28% YoY to ₹805 Cr.
The company said that its indirect expenses increased 14% YoY to ₹1,209 Cr, but declined to 46% of revenue from 52% a year earlier.
Software, cloud and data centre expenses rose 59% YoY to ₹211 Cr, reflecting higher AI usage, which Paytm expects to continue for another quarter. It attributed the improvement in operating leverage to AI-led efficiencies and slower growth in platform-building costs relative to revenue.
The company also incorporated ₹3 Cr share of loss from a joint venture during the quarter under review and a ₹4 Cr exceptional item charge which came at the behest of “written-off obsolete capital work-in-progress”.
Besides its financial statements, Paytm’s board also approved the following:
An additional ₹500 Cr investment in subsidiary Paytm Cloud Technologies Ltd (PCTL) in one or more tranches over the next twelve months. Subsequently, PCTL’s board has also approved an investment of ₹500 Cr in its subsidiary Paytm Singapore to support future requirements of working capital, investments and business expansion.
On NPCI’s recent decision to extend UPI MDR implementation to post Diwali, Paytm said that it expects an indicative uplift of about 2.5 bps in overall Payments Processing Margin. “We expect the actual outcome may stabilise in 2–3 quarters post implementation,” the company added.
The fintech major revised its default loss guarantees (DLG) for lending partner Piramal and KSF to ₹150 Cr from ₹90 Cr, up to ₹100 Cr for Vivriti and Ugro, where it had disclosed DLG of up to ₹350 Cr and Muthoot Fincorp Limited of up to ₹90 Cr.
With that, here’s a look at some of the key operational updates for Paytm in the September quarter.
Paytm Q2 Operational Updates
The fintech company continued to expand its payments and financial services distribution business in Q2 FY27 and reported gains in payment processing margins as well as continued its AI investment spree to enhance consumer engagement.
Merchant payments has continued to be the key business growth driver. Paytm’s merchant gross merchandise value (GMV) grew 26% YoY to ₹7.1 Lakh Cr in the September quarter while subscription-paying merchant base grew by 27 Lakh YoY to 1.64 Cr. The company said high merchant retention and subsequent loan distribution were contributing to higher revenue per merchant.
Net payment revenue, excluding the Payment Infrastructure Development Fund (PIDF) incentive, rose 21% YoY to ₹644 Cr on a comparable basis, while reported growth stood at 8%.
The company said that it received a PIDF incentive of ₹12 Cr in the quarter as against ₹74 Cr in the year-ago quarter. Therefore, its operating revenue, minus the PIDF incentive, grew 33% YoY to ₹2,636 Cr, it claimed.
Meanwhile, Paytm’s payment processing margins expanded by more than four basis points due to a higher share of merchant transactions through credit cards on UPI and Paytm Postpaid, market share gains and pricing discipline.
Paytm Postpaid, its credit line on UPI product, recorded higher sign-ups, increased spending per customer, improved portfolio performance and better profitability following its relaunch. The company expects the product to contribute meaningfully to revenue and EBITDA from FY28 onwards. It also reported improved monetisation through margin trading funding (MTF) and Paytm Gold.
Besides, Paytm’s financial services distribution also expanded. Revenue from the business increased 49% YoY to ₹912 Cr. The number of key financial services customers rose by 2.3 Lakh, or 35%, to 8.8 Lakh. More than half of merchant loan disbursements went to repeat borrowers, reflecting continued engagement and demand among existing customers.
Its merchant loan distribution is also benefiting from a wider pool of eligible borrowers, increased disbursements by lending partners and stable portfolio performance. It is also expanding into higher-ticket loans for merchants using electronic data capture (EDC) devices.
Paytm also continued to gain share in consumer payments. Its monthly transacting users (MTUs) increased by 1 Cr YoY to 8.5 Cr, highest YoY jump in nearly three years. The company’s UPI gross transaction value grew 42% YoY, compared with 19% growth for the industry, marking its sixth consecutive quarter of consumer payment market share gains.
This growth gives it a substantial base for the gains it could potentially realise from the UPI MDR. However, it said that its core business moat doesn’t rely on the discount rate.
“Our business model is to acquire customers through payments and monetise through financial services and technology services. We do not depend on UPI MDR for profitable growth; any MDR on UPI would be an upside, not its foundation,” the company noted.
Shares of Paytm ended today’s trading session 2.67% higher at ₹1,655 apiece on the BSE.
The post Paytm Q2 Profit Skyrockets Over 10X YoY To ₹225 Cr, Revenue Up 28% appeared first on Inc42 Media.

items.author: Debarghya Sil
items.content:
Fintech startup axiTrust is in talks to raise around $5 Mn in fresh capital in its Series A funding round, people aware of the matter told Inc42 on the condition of anonymity.
The fresh round is likely to be led by Singapore based Argor.vc, and will see participation from axiTrust’s existing investor General Catalyst.
Questions sent to axiTrust didn’t elicit any response at the time of publishing the story.
The fresh round has come almost a year after the startup raised $2.6 Mn in its seed funding round led by General Catalyst. Other investors including Atrium Angels, YAN Network and Supermorpheous are also on the fintech startup’s cap table.
The fresh capital will help the startup build digital infrastructure to accelerate adoption of its surety bonds offering.
For context, surety bonds are insurance-backed guarantees that assure a buyer or project owner that a business will fulfil its contractual obligations. Instead of blocking the capital as collateral, they allow the buyers to pay a premium to secure the guarantee, helping free up working capital and reduce financial strain.
Founded in 2024 by Aditya Tulsian (CEO), Rajeev Chari (COO), and Mukund Daga (CRO), axiTrust issues, underwrites and manages digital surety bonds, providing an alternative to traditional, collateral-heavy bank guarantees.
As per the startup, more than ₹15 Lakh Cr of MSME working capital is locked up as collateral for bank guarantees, and replacing these traditional guarantees with insurance-backed digital surety bonds can free that capital, expand credit access, and improve trust in business transactions.
From digital underwriting and AI-based risk assessment to cashflow-based lending and embedded finance, they are filling long-standing gaps that traditional banks could not address efficiently. These solutions are helping businesses and consumers access credit with fewer delays, lighter paperwork, and better transparency.
Investors are actively backing such startups because the lending market in India is massive, still underserved, and primed for digital disruption offering both strong growth potential and meaningful financial inclusion.
As per Inc42’s Indian Tech Startup Funding Report Q3 2026, the fintech sector saw funding of $243 Mn across 13 deals. Of these, the heavy lifting was done by lendingtech startup Centricity ₹280 Cr round and Navi’s $100 Mn pre-IPO funding.

items.author: Debarghya Sil
items.content:
Bengaluru-based AI-powered trading platform Tradl has raised $4.1 Mn (about ₹40 Cr) in a seed funding round from Nexus Venture Partners and Stellaris Venture Partners, sources told Inc42.
The funding round also saw participation from a few angel investors, the sources added.
The startup’s MCA filing further confirmed the fundraise.
Questions sent to Tradl, Stellaris Venture Partners, and Nexus Venture Partners didn’t elicit any response till the time of publishing this story.
Founded in 2025 by Shubham Bansal and Nilesh Raj, Tradl combines AI with quantitative analysis to help retail traders identify opportunities, analyse stocks, and test trading strategies.
The cofounders are IIT Guwahati graduates. Bansal previously spent around five years at Goldman Sachs, while Raj worked at fintech startup Stable Money.
Bringing AI To Trading
Tradl’s toolkit includes an AI-powered stock screener, technical charts, and backtesting tools that allow users to test trading strategies against historical market data. It also helps traders track sector rotation and monitor corporate events that could influence stock prices.
The startup lists chart pattern alerts, broader market insights, and personalised option chains among its other tools, although these are marked as available through private access on its website.
According to Tradl, its AI interprets natural-language queries and translates them into instructions for its quantitative engine. The engine then processes market data using fixed rules to generate consistent results for the same query and dataset.
The startup’s stated aim is to give retail traders access to the depth of analysis typically available to institutional trading desks. It lists the NSE, the BSE, and the MCX as exchange partners, and CMOTS as a data partner on its website.
Tradl’s fundraise comes amid growing investment in Indian AI startups. The segment attracted $438 Mn across 35 deals in Q3 2026, up 265% YoY, making it the most-funded sector during the quarter.
AI is also becoming a feature of platforms serving retail investors and traders. Investment and stock broking platform Trackk raised $3.7 Mn in a seed round led by Lightspeed, with participation from Info Edge Ventures, earlier this year. The startup offers AI-led stock discovery alongside broking, derivatives trading, and portfolio tracking tools.
More recently, IPO-bound investment advisory platform StockGro raised ₹110 Cr from existing backers as part of its ongoing Series B round. StockGro combines investment research and trading insights with AI-powered research tools.

items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
Defence Minister Khawaja Asif on Monday hinted at the possibility of "progress" in a meeting of the Makkah Defence Alliance members with Iran, stating that the participants had likely arrived at a "conclusion" to end Saudi Arabia's conflict with the Houthis.
Members of the Makkah Defence Alliance and Iran agreed to continue further dialogue in an effort to ramp up cooperation for regional peace and security after a high-level meeting in Tehran.
Attacks by Yemen's Houthis have spiralled in recent weeks, and rhetoric between Washington and Tehran has grown more heated. Both countries have also drawn up plans to restart the wider war, possibly after the US midterm elections on November ​3.
Read: Makkah alliance, Iran agree to continue dialogue for bolstering cooperation in regional peace, security
Speaking on a private news channel, Asif said it seemed that "some progress" had transpired in the Tehran meeting, given how Iran had issued a joint statement after the meeting about deciding to launch joint efforts towards peace along with regional countries.
Questioned whether the meeting was more about the US-Iran war or the Saudi-Houthi conflict, he said the talks in Tehran were directed as “more of an effort for what is happening in Saudi Arabia”, further adding that while the US-Iran aspect would have been discussed, the presence of the Saudi defence minister and the Turkish intelligence chief were also significant.
“The joint statement from Iran has come at the highest level of the country’s hierarchy. I think we have arrived at some sort of a conclusion that will help close out this war."
He added: "Let us hope that after Iran’s joint statement, there are some steps taken towards peace."
The minister underscored that it remained binding on Pakistan to safeguard Saudi Arabia, especially given how the Houthis were targeting Riyadh airport and the holy sites.
“We will defend Saudi Arabia with all of our might and capability.
"Just as Pakistan’s defence is indispensable for us, in the same manner, the defence of Saudi Arabia is also compulsory for us. Under the agreement, the three countries are committed through an arrangement to collectively deal with threats," he said.
Responding to a question of whether Iran would bring Houthis to the negotiating table or make them stop attacks on the kingdom, Asif stated that elements such as the Houthis operated as independent actors and did not necessarily require patronage.
“Once you have a setup in a country where there is no state structure, then it is possible for groups like this to operate in this manner”.
Asif further noted that Saudi Arabia's war with Yemen started in March 2014, and it had been Pakistan’s commitment ever since to defend the kingdom. "Now three countries are bound by the agreement that we will defend each other's territory against any foreign aggression."
The defence minister stated that Pakistan’s peace initiatives, led by Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, had positive effects.
Commenting on elections in Israel and the United States, Asif said it was unfair to create and continue conflicts for political reasons.
"In my view, for limited political objectives, wars should not be started."
Tensions rising
Saudi Arabia intercepted another wave of missiles and ​drones on Sunday as fighting with the Houthis ​continued unabated.
Ministers from the Makkah pact countries ⁠held an emergency meeting in Riyadh earlier this month and agreed to ensure the "rapid deployment" of military forces and capabilities in Saudi Arabia.
The Houthi attacks have become an increasingly destabilising element in the US-Israeli conflict with Iran, turning US ally Saudi Arabia into a pressure point in the wider ​war.
Read More: Saudi-led coalition intercepts 3 drones over Riyadh, southern Saudi Arabia
Tensions between Washington and Tehran have sharpened in recent days. President Donald Trump said on Friday the US may carry out another ​military operation against Iran and ⁠Iran's leaders have said that a renewed US military campaign would be met with a stronger response than before.
Iranian security officials have told Reuters that Tehran has drawn up detailed plans to hit Gulf undersea cables if the United States and Israel attack again. A US intelligence memo this week warned that Iranian plots against American personnel had reached "advanced stages".
The war, now nearly eight months old, has weighed ⁠on US President Donald ​Trump's approval ratings ahead of the midterms.
The Makkah agreement's first article says the parties shall use "all necessary means" to ​eliminate threats to one another's territorial integrity, sovereignty or internationally recognised borders, according to a text seen by Reuters.
Efforts by Turkiye’s parliament to ratify the agreement began last week and are still underway, while Pakistan approved the pact last ​week.

items.content:
The federal government on Monday increased the price of petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs1.54 and Rs2.16 per litre, respectively, for October 27.
According to a notification issued by the Petroleum Division, the price of petrol was fixed at Rs379.25 per litre, while HSD would cost Rs395.82 per litre for Tuesday.
The latest revision comes after the government increased the price of HSD by Rs1.91 per litre while keeping the price of petrol unchanged from October 24 to October 26.
Read: Govt increases diesel by Rs1.91, keeps petrol unchanged till Oct 26
On July 17, the government announced a new pricing mechanism under which petroleum product prices would be reviewed and notified daily, replacing the weekly pricing mechanism, as renewed tensions between the United States and Iran continued to drive volatility in global oil markets and raise concerns over fuel supplies.
On September 13, PM Shehbaz announced a special relief scheme offering Rs100 per litre off petrol for motorcycles, three-wheeler rickshaws and cars with engines up to 800cc, in an attempt to shield lower-income consumers from the impact of rising petroleum prices.
Under the proposal, an estimated 11.8 million beneficiaries would be covered. Around 10 million two-wheeler users and 800,000 three-wheeler users would be entitled to relief on 20 litres of fuel per month, translating into a maximum monthly benefit of Rs2,000 per beneficiary.
Another one million users of cars up to 800cc would receive relief on 30 litres per month, providing them with a maximum benefit of Rs3,000 each.
On Sept 17, the government reintroduced austerity and fuel conservation measures amid rising fuel prices, tightening business operating hours and restricting public events.
Under the measures, notified with immediate effect, shops, markets, shopping malls, bazaars, departmental stores, grocery stores, general stores and kiryana shops would close by 9pm throughout the week, according to a notification issued by the Cabinet Division.
Marriage halls, marquees and other commercial venues hosting festive events would close by 10pm, while restaurants, cafes, eateries, food outlets and standalone fruit and vegetable shops would be allowed to operate until 11pm. Takeaway and home delivery services would remain exempt from the timing restrictions.
Global geopolitical developments continue to pose significant risks. International oil prices are influenced by decisions taken by OPEC+, conflicts in the Middle East, sanctions on oil-producing nations, and disruptions in critical shipping routes such as the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea. Any interruption in these supply chains can immediately increase crude oil prices and freight costs. Since Pakistan imports the majority of its petroleum requirements, these developments quickly translate into higher domestic fuel prices.
Oil prices inched higher after falling more than $2 a ‌barrel on Monday, as persistent attacks on key producer Saudi Arabia kept investors wary and prices near six-month highs, even as diplomatic efforts to resolve the conflict in the Middle East resumed.
Brent crude futures rose 49 cents, or 0.4%, to $117.21 at 12:51 pm ET (1637 GMT), while US West Texas Intermediate crude futures were down 35 cents, or 0.34%, at $102.92 per barrel.
Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan also held talks with Iranian officials in Tehran on Monday as part of efforts to prevent further escalation in the region.
"With the jeopardy doubled by Houthi attacks into ​Saudi, any Brent price dips back to the lows of last week will find grateful buyers," PVM Oil Associates analyst John Evans said.

items.author: Aftab Khan
items.content:
Once familiar visitors to Pakistan’s sandy shores, Olive Ridley sea turtles have all but vanished from the country’s recorded nesting grounds. Now, the discovery of a dead turtle on Clifton Beach has brought an old ecological mystery into focus: if these turtles still inhabit the Arabian Sea, where have the breeding females gone?
The turtle’s death has no confirmed explanation. It may have become entangled in a fishing net, collided with a vessel or fallen victim to marine pollution. But its appearance on Karachi’s shoreline has renewed concern over a far bigger disappearance - the collapse of Olive Ridley nesting along Pakistan’s coast.
According to WWF-Pakistan technical adviser Muhammad Moazzam Khan, these turtles were once found in significant numbers at Sandspit, Hawke’s Bay, Manora, Sonmiani Beach and other coastal locations. Historical research cited by experts recorded more than 500 Olive Ridley nests along Karachi’s beaches during the 1980s and 1990s. By 1996-97, that number had reportedly plummeted to just two.
In the years that followed, researchers failed to establish reliable evidence of regular nesting by the species on Pakistan’s shores. The turtles, however, have not disappeared entirely from regional waters. Olive Ridleys continue to inhabit the Arabian Sea, leaving scientists with a crucial unanswered question: have Pakistan’s breeding females shifted to distant shores, or are other factors disrupting their nesting cycle?
 
Khan believes satellite tracking could help unravel the mystery. He cited a study in a neighbouring country in which an Olive Ridley fitted with a GPS tag crossed the Arabian Sea and reached Oman to breed. Similar research in Pakistan could identify migration routes, locate breeding grounds and reveal the dangers turtles encounter in their journeys across the sea.
The need for such research is underscored by recent encounters along Pakistan’s coastline. Two Olive Ridley turtles caught in fishermen’s nets near Jiwani, Balochistan, were recently rescued and released. Their presence offers evidence that the species continues to frequent Pakistani waters, even as its nesting history remains largely unaccounted for.
The dead turtle at Clifton is not an isolated reminder of the pressures facing marine life. Several dead green turtles have previously been found at Hawke’s Bay and Sandspit, raising wider concerns about the hazards confronting sea turtles along Karachi’s increasingly busy coastline.
Fishermen Sajag Forum Chairman Muhammad Bakhsh Jat warned that plastic bags, discarded plastic waste and marine pollution posed serious threats to marine life. Damage to the marine ecosystem, he said, also threatens the livelihoods of fishing communities that depend on healthy coastal waters.
Experts identify entanglement in fishing nets, intensive human activity, pollution and changes to natural nesting habitats among the principal dangers facing sea turtles. Yet the precise reasons behind the collapse of Olive Ridley nesting on Pakistan’s beaches remain uncertain, and specialists caution that more scientific investigation is needed before definitive conclusions can be drawn.
Olive Ridleys are capable of travelling thousands of miles between feeding and breeding areas. Tracking their movements could therefore help determine whether turtles frequenting Pakistani waters are nesting elsewhere and, if so, where their breeding grounds lie. It could also provide the scientific basis for regional cooperation to protect their migration routes and habitats.
For now, the dead turtle on Clifton Beach is both a troubling sight and a reminder of how much remains unknown beneath the Arabian Sea’s surface. The species may still be passing through these waters, but until its movements are tracked and its breeding destinations identified, the silence of Pakistan’s once-recorded nesting grounds will remain an ecological mystery.

items.author: Fact Check By iVerify
items.content:
Several people have been sharing a video on social media platform X since October 23, 2026, allegedly showing a new railway route connecting Iran to Afghanistan via China. However, the video is from October 2024 and shows the resumption of direct freight train services between China and Afghanistan.
Chinese and Afghan media reported on Oct 23, 2026, that a dedicated freight train carrying commercial goods departed Shandong Province for Hairatan port in northern Afghanistan, with the journey expected to take about 20 days.
The train marked the first dedicated freight service from Shandong to Hairatan, a key trade and transport hub in Afghanistan’s Balkh Province. It was expected to travel through Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan before entering Afghanistan via the Termez border crossing.
How it started
An X account identified as an Afghan propaganda account based on its past posts shared a video of a Chinese train with the following caption on Oct 23: “China has launched its first freight train from Shandong to Hairatan, Afghanistan, carrying goods worth 8 million yuan. Transit Route: Kazakhstan → Uzbekistan → Afghanistan. The train is expected to reach Afghanistan in approximately 20 days, opening another route for trade between China and Afghanistan.”
The post garnered 43,805 views.
On Oct 25, a pro-Iran user on X, based on its past posts and profile picture, shared a video of a Chinese train with the following caption: “Afghanistan now has a railway connection to China with the help of Iranian engineering firms. Iranian companies have made significant efforts to revive Afghanistan’s rail network, and more tracks are under construction. Iran now has a new rail route option to China via Afghanistan.”
The post garnered 234,425 views.
The same video was also shared on the same day by another X user with the caption: “Afghanistan now has a railway connection to China with the help of Iranian engineering firms. Oil: Iran - Afghanistan - China. Pakistan will be sidelined. No way Afghanistan will allow a drop of Iranian oil /LPG into Pakistan.”
The post garnered 12,106 views.
The same video was shared by multiple other users on X, as can be seen here, here, here, here and here.
Methodology
A fact-check was initiated to verify the viral claim due to its high virality and keen public interest amid tense regional relations.
A keyword search was conducted to verify whether the video was covered by any credible Iranian, Chinese, Afghan or international media outlets in the context of the Shandong-Hairatan freight train’s launch but yielded no results.
A reverse image search was conducted to trace the source of the video, which yielded the same visual being shared by Arezo News, an Afghan news channel on Oct 31, 2024.
How it started
An X account identified as an Afghan propaganda account based on its past posts shared a video of a Chinese train with the following caption on Oct 23: “China has launched its first freight train from Shandong to Hairatan, Afghanistan, carrying goods worth 8 million yuan. Transit Route: Kazakhstan → Uzbekistan → Afghanistan. The train is expected to reach Afghanistan in approximately 20 days, opening another route for trade between China and Afghanistan.”
The post garnered 43,805 views.
On October 25, a pro-Iran user on X, based on its past posts and profile picture, shared a video of a Chinese train with the following caption: “Afghanistan now has a railway connection to China with the help of Iranian engineering firms. Iranian companies have made significant efforts to revive Afghanistan’s rail network, and more tracks are under construction. Iran now has a new rail route option to China via Afghanistan.”
The post garnered 234,425 views.
The same video was also shared on the same day by another X user with the caption: “Afghanistan now has a railway connection to China with the help of Iranian engineering firms. Oil: Iran - Afghanistan - China. Pakistan will be sidelined. No way Afghanistan will allow a drop of Iranian oil /LPG into Pakistan.”
The post garnered 12,106 views.
The same video was shared by multiple other users on X, as can be seen here, here, here, here and here.
Methodology
A fact-check was initiated to verify the viral claim due to its high virality and keen public interest amid tense regional relations.
A keyword search was conducted to verify whether the video was covered by any credible Iranian, Chinese, Afghan or international media outlets in the context of the Shandong-Hairatan freight train’s launch but yielded no results.
A reverse image search was conducted to trace the source of the video, which yielded the same visual being shared by Arezo News, an Afghan news channel on Oct 31, 2024.
The video’s caption stated the following: “The Afghan Embassy in China has announced the opening of a railway to transport goods between China and Afghanistan. The first train loaded with 50 containers of electrical appliances, clothes and other goods will leave the Chinese city of Nantong and arrive in Hairatan port in northern Afghanistan in 20 days, the Afghan embassy in China said in a statement.”
A keyword search yielded a report by Afghan outlet Kabul Now, published on October 31, 2024, titled “China and Afghanistan resumes direct freight train services”.
The report stated that Chinese and Taliban officials had announced the resumption of direct freight train services between China and Afghanistan. China’s Special Envoy for Afghanistan, Yue Xiaoyong, confirmed that a freight train carrying 55 wagons had departed from Nantong, Jiangsu Province, bound for Afghanistan, marking a step toward strengthening bilateral trade relations.
Another report by Afghanistan International, published on October 31, 2024, titled “Taliban announces launch of direct freight railway line Between China & Afghanistan,” also reported on the development.
The reports focused on the resumption of direct freight train services between China and Afghanistan in October 2024.
Fact-check status: misleading
The claim that a viral video shows a newly launched freight train from China to Afghanistan is misleading.
The video dates back to October 2024 and relates to the launch of a direct freight railway line from China’s Nantong to Afghanistan’s Hairatan port.
This fact check was originally published by iVerify Pakistan— a project of CEJ-IBA and UNDP.

items.content:
Pune Police has written to Google and Apple seeking the removal of Rapido’s app from their respective app stores over its alleged unauthorised bike taxi operations in the city.
Pune Police Commissioner Amitesh Kumar told the Times of India that communications had been sent to the two companies requesting the app’s removal.
Inc42 has reached out to Rapido for comment. The story will be updated on receiving a response.
The move follows an FIR against Rapido’s parent entity, Roppen Transportation Services Pvt Ltd, for allegedly operating bike taxi services without the required licence and regulatory approvals. The FIR was registered at Vishrantwadi police station following an enforcement drive by the Pune Regional Transport Office (RTO).
Earlier, Pune district collector and Regional Transport Authority (RTA) chairperson Jitendra Dudi had directed Rapido to suspend its bike taxi operations across Pune district until it secured an ebike taxi aggregator licence.
According to TOI, Rapido’s application for permission to operate bike taxis remains pending with the transport department.
The FIR alleges that Rapido facilitated paid passenger rides on two-wheelers registered as non-transport vehicles. The alleged violation came to light when Pune RTO motor vehicle inspector Prasad Govardhan Surwase booked a ride through the app during the enforcement drive.
It also refers to an October 15 notice warning the platform against unauthorised operations and an earlier notice issued by the Transport Commissioner’s Office on April 29, 2025.
According to the FIR, Rapido applied for an aggregator licence with the Transport Commissioner’s Office in Mumbai on August 11, 2026, but the application remained pending at the time of the alleged violation.
The complaint also alleges inadequate driver background checks, raising concerns about passenger safety, particularly for women.
Wider Scrutiny Of Aggregators
Separately, Dudi directed cab aggregators to submit monthly fare data to the district administration and display RTA-approved fares separately on their apps, following complaints from autorickshaw and cab drivers about alleged fare violations.
According to Dudi, drivers must receive 80% of the RTA base fare, while passenger fares can range from 50% below the base fare to 1.5 times that amount. Complaints about driver underpayment and passengers being charged beyond the permitted range prompted the monthly reporting requirement.
The directions followed a meeting with representatives of driver unions and aggregators. Dudi warned of legal action over continued unauthorised bike taxi operations and said Rapido could not resume the service without a licence.
Rapido’s efforts to secure permission to operate in Pune date back to 2022, when its licence application was rejected, triggering proceedings before the Bombay High Court and the Supreme Court.
In January 2023, the Bombay High Court directed Rapido to stop operating its app. The following month, the SC disposed of the related petitions, allowing the platform to approach the High Court to challenge Maharashtra’s January 2023 notification prohibiting the aggregation and pooling of rides using non-transport vehicles.

Contract manufacturing company Aequs reported a consolidated net loss of ₹52.4 Cr in the September quarter of FY27, widening 154.4% from ₹20.6 Cr in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal year.
Operating revenue climbed 45.3% to ₹409.1 Cr from ₹281.6 Cr.
Sequentially, revenue increased 3.4% from ₹395.5 Cr, while net loss narrowed marginally from ₹53.2 Cr in Q1 FY27.
Including other income of ₹10.6 Cr, Aequs’ total income stood at ₹419.7 Cr during the quarter under review.
However, expenses excluding finance costs, depreciation, and amortisation rose faster than revenue, increasing 56.2% to ₹395.2 Cr from ₹253.1 Cr a year earlier.

The company said that its aerospace order book reached $1.1 Bn, growing 9% QoQ. During said that the Safran A320 wheels agreement marks Aequs’ first serial-production contract
Meanwhile, consumer business revenue increased 52% to ₹57.7 Cr from ₹37.9 Cr.
Executive chairman and CEO Aravind Melligeri highlighted a slow down in Q2 volume ramp in the consumer business due to extended qualification timelines and supply chain constraints.
“We view this as a timing-related shift rather than a change in the underlying opportunity, with customer programs continuing to progress. Given these factors, we are recalibrating the path to consumer EBITDA breakeven, with our near-term focus on improving utilisation and translating installed capacity into profitable growth,” he added.
During the quarter, the company signed new long-term supply agreements, expanding its relationships to six Safran entities and broadening its manufacturing scope across critical aerospace components. It is currently leveraging Belagavi manufacturing and working on completion of its upcoming Hosur manufacturing ecosystem.
For this, the company’s promoter group recently infused ₹650 Cr by subscribing to preferential warrants to fuel its next phase of capacity expansion, bolster strategic JV investments and cater to certain working capital requirements.
“To support this next phase of growth, we continue to invest in our manufacturing capabilities. H1 FY27 capital expenditure stood at ₹159.7 Cr, and the ₹650 Cr promoter warrant is intended to support the next phase of expansion, including Hosur. Following quarter-end, new Safran agreements expanded our relationships to six entities. As these capabilities and partnerships grow, our focus remains on disciplined execution and stronger returns,” Melligeri added.
Shares of Aequs ended today’s trading session 2.74% higher at ₹242.10 apiece on the BSE.
