items.content:
India’s D2C ecosystem has no shortage of new brands. But as competition intensifies, identifying the businesses delivering strong revenue growth, beyond the attention generated by funding announcements, product launches and marketing campaigns, is becoming increasingly important.
This is the premise behind FAST42, Inc42’s annual ranking of India’s fastest-growing D2C brands. Now in its sixth edition, FAST42 2027 invites applications from emerging consumer brands to identify and rank 42 businesses by verified revenue growth between FY24 and FY26.
Since 2022, FAST42 has been part of Inc42’s broader effort to identify, track and recognise emerging consumer businesses. Backed by more than a decade of startup ecosystem coverage, sector research and engagement with D2C founders, the initiative has consistently focused on a measurable indicator of business growth: revenue.
The numbers from previous editions illustrate the scale of businesses featured in the ranking. The FAST42 2026 cohort, selected from over 250 applications, comprised 42 brands that collectively generated ₹2,154 Cr in annual revenue and employed more than 6,700 people.
Over the years, FAST42 has recognised brands such as Pilgrim, The Sleep Company, Snitch, Sweet Karam Coffee, Beco, Perfora, XYXX, Innovist, Fix My Curls and The Pant Project, among others.
These brands represent a cross-section of India’s consumer economy, spanning established categories, emerging niches and different approaches to building and scaling a business.
With FAST42 2027, Inc42 is looking to identify the next set of emerging brands demonstrating exceptional revenue growth.
Presented by Inc42 and Shadowfax, and co-presented by PhonePe Payment Gateway, the sixth edition will culminate in the unveiling of India’s 42 fastest-growing eligible D2C brands in February 2027.
Apply For FAST42 2027
India’s D2C Market Is Growing. So Is The Competition.
India’s D2C market is entering a period of significant expansion. According to Inc42’s D2C 3.0: The Next Big Wave In Indian Ecommerce Report 2026, India’s D2C gross merchandise value (GMV) is projected to grow from $65 Bn in 2026 to $310 Bn by 2031, clocking a CAGR of approximately 37%.
This compares with a projected 22% CAGR for the broader ecommerce market. D2C channels are also expected to account for nearly 86% of the incremental GMV added by India’s ecommerce sector over the next five years.
However, the changing retail landscape is also making growth more complex.
Performance marketing and online marketplaces, which powered India’s first wave of digital-first brands, are increasingly being complemented by quick commerce and offline retail. Brands now have more ways to reach consumers, but must also manage competition across channels, customer acquisition costs, repeat purchases and distribution economics.
As India’s D2C ecosystem moves into this next phase, the distinction between building brand visibility and translating consumer demand into revenue growth becomes more relevant.
FAST42 2027 will spotlight brands that have demonstrated this growth, regardless of the categories they operate in or the combination of channels driving their sales.
How Will FAST42 2027 Identify The Fastest-Growing Brands?
FAST42 is a data-led ranking, with growth determined by financial performance rather than funding, valuations or brand popularity.
For its 2027 edition, Inc42 will rank 42 eligible D2C brands on their compound annual revenue growth rate (CAGR) between FY24 and FY26.
Inc42’s team of editors, reporters and analysts will review applications and verify the financial information provided by shortlisted brands before determining the final ranking.
The ranking will also document the selected brands’ business journeys, offering insights into the categories, strategies, and markets driving their expansion.
Apply For FAST42 2027
What Does Making The FAST42 List Mean For Brands?
Beyond the ranking itself, FAST42 provides emerging consumer brands with a platform to bring their growth stories to a wider audience.
Previous editions have featured businesses across food and beverages, fashion, beauty and personal care, wellness, home products and other consumer categories, highlighting the breadth of brands gaining scale in India.
For brands selected in FAST42 2027, the initiative offers:
Recognition For Verified Growth: A place among India’s 42 fastest-growing eligible D2C brands, determined through a consistent, revenue-based ranking methodology.
Visibility Across Inc42’s Platforms: A feature in FAST42’s interactive online ranking and an exclusive coffee table book documenting the selected businesses.
A Platform For Their Growth Stories: Opportunities for Inc42’s editorial team to examine the founders, business models and strategies behind standout brands.
Access To The Wider Ecosystem: Recognition at the FAST42 Conclave and visibility among investors, business partners, industry leaders and prospective talent.
For emerging brands navigating their next stage of expansion, FAST42 offers an independent distinction based on their financial performance and an opportunity to bring their businesses to the attention of a larger industry audience.
FAST42 2027 Applications Close On 10 December
Applications for FAST42 2027 are open until 10 December 2026.
The final ranking will be unveiled at the FAST42 Conclave in Delhi NCR in February 2027, bringing together the selected brands, D2C founders, investors and other stakeholders from India’s consumer ecosystem.
The 42 ranked brands will also be featured on Inc42’s website and in the FAST42 coffee table book.
As India’s D2C market continues to expand, FAST42 2027 aims to identify the emerging brands turning that market opportunity into measurable growth.
If your brand has demonstrated exceptional revenue growth between FY24 and FY26, applications for FAST42 2027 are now open.
Applicants must be able to substantiate their revenue figures with supporting financial documents. With no jury selections or paid placements, every position on the FAST42 list is earned through verified revenue growth.
Apply For FAST42 2027

PKR 100,000 is a serious budget, and buyers have every right to expect a lot for it. Before you choose, four things are worth comparing: battery life, performance, design and display. Here is what to look for in each, and how the TECNO POVA Curve 2 5G, available in Pakistan at PKR 99,999, answers them.
Battery life: look past the capacity
A big number on the box is a start, but also check how fast the phone charges and how long the battery will last over the years. The POVA Curve 2 5G has an 8000mAh battery, enough for charging only every two days. 45W fast charging takes it to 30% in 21 minutes and 50% in 36 minutes, with a full charge in 82 minutes, and 10W reverse charging lets it power other devices. The battery is built for 2,000 cycles, which TECNO describes as six years of safe use.
Performance: ask how long it stays fast
A phone that is quick on day one but slow in year two is a poor deal. Look at the processor, the memory, how the phone handles heat, and how long the software is supported. The POVA Curve 2 5G runs on the MediaTek Dimensity 7100 5G with 8GB of RAM and 256GB of storage, and Ice Cooling 3.0 helps it stay cool under load. It is TÜV Rheinland certified to stay lag-free for six years, with 2 Android version updates and 3 years of security patches, and support for 20 5G bands keeps you connected.
Design: judge it in your hand and pocket
Looks matter, but so does how a phone feels over a full day. At 7.42mm and 195g, the POVA Curve 2 5G is the slimmest phone among those with an 8000mAh battery, so it slips into a pocket without the bulk of a big battery. Its bold, flowing lines are inspired by interstellar spaceships, and it comes in Melting Silver, Mystic Purple and Storm Titanium. Corning Gorilla Glass 7i and SGS-certified 1.5m drop resistance cover everyday knocks.
Display: check smoothness, brightness and touch
Refresh rate, peak brightness and touch response decide how a screen feels every day. The 6.78-inch curved AMOLED display on the POVA Curve 2 5G runs at 144Hz for smooth scrolling and gaming, reaches up to 4,500 nits for outdoor viewing, and has a 2160Hz touch sampling rate with anti-mistouch for wet or oily hands.
Don’t skip the extras
The camera setup is a 50MP primary, a 2MP macro and a 13MP front camera, with AI tools such as AI Eraser 2.0. FreeLink 2.0 keeps calls and messages going between phones within 1.5km without network coverage.
Price and availability
The TECNO POVA Curve 2 5G is available across Pakistan in 8GB RAM + 256GB ROM at PKR 99,999. Buyers get PKR 5,000 off through PalmPay’s instalment service, and PKR 5,000 off on Daraz with TECNO Fans discount vouchers.
For buyers weighing PKR 100,000, the POVA Curve 2 5G is built to tick all four boxes.

Edtech startup Imarticus Learning plans to file its DRHP with SEBI through the confidential route within the next two to three months for a ₹1,000 Cr IPO, sources told Inc42.
The proposed issue size has increased from the ₹750 Cr planned earlier, which was to comprise a mix of fresh issue and an offer for sale (OFS).
Imarticus intends to use proceeds from the IPO to expand its existing business and pursue acquisitions, the sources added.
Its organic expansion could include setting up more Centres of Excellence (CoEs), expanding offerings at the Imarticus School of Finance and Business (ISFB), and strengthening its B2B business, they said.
Inc42 has reached out to Imarticus for comment on its IPO plans. The story will be updated on receiving a response.
Expanding Ahead Of IPO
The IPO preparations follow Imarticus’ recent ₹800 Cr acquisition of Singapore’s BELLS Institute of Higher Learning, aimed at expanding its presence in Singapore and Southeast Asia.
The acquisition also strengthened its capabilities in enterprise learning, AI, data analytics, technology, and workforce development. Imarticus plans to launch the BELLS School of AI, offering courses in machine learning, AI applications in finance and fintech, and business transformation.
The startup also inaugurated a Centre of Excellence for the Indian capital market in August. This followed the launch of ISFB last year, with an inaugural undergraduate cohort of 50 students.
Founded in 2012 by Nikhil Barshikar and Sonya Hooja, Mumbai-based Imarticus offers professional education and upskilling programmes across finance, banking, analytics, technology, marketing, and management.
Its business spans B2C programmes for students and working professionals, alongside enterprise training, e-learning, and workforce development solutions.
Last year, the startup acquired edtech platform MyCaptain in a ₹50 Cr cash and stock deal to broaden its course offerings, drawing on the latter’s expertise in digital marketing.
The planned offering follows PhysicsWallah’s ₹3,480 Cr IPO in November 2025. Meanwhile, Fusion Klassroom Edutech listed on the BSE SME platform in August 2026 following its ₹39.04 Cr IPO.
Imarticus’ IPO preparations come amid a prolonged funding slowdown and consolidation in the edtech sector. Last month, upGrad completed its acquisition of Unacademy in a deal valuing the latter at just over $200 Mn, down more than 90% from its peak valuation of $3.5 Bn.

items.content:
Serbia woke to a new era on Monday after a student-backed protest movement unseated longtime leader Aleksandar Vucic in a historic landslide election that sparked nationwide celebrations, although few had an idea of how they would govern.
Tens of thousands took to the streets of Belgrade and other cities and towns across Serbia after Vucic conceded defeat late on Sunday, capping two years of peaceful anti-government protests calling for the populist ruler to step down.
With almost 99% of votes counted, the students' candidates had secured a commanding 52.7% of the vote, according to the State Election Commission, versus 39.2% for Vucic's Serbia Progressive Party (SNS)-led alliance.
That gives the students 139 seats in the 250-seat parliament, leaving the SNS alliance with 97, and the remainder held by minority parties. The constitution allows up to 90 days for the creation of a government, once the parliament is convened after the announcement of final results by the State Election Commission.
"I thought it was unbelievable, I still do not believe it. It was too long, and (Vucic) was pressuring us for a long, long time," said university administrator Marijana Radovanovic Pajovic.
Vucic dominated Serbian politics as prime minister or president from 2014. But he was swept from power by a list of student-backed candidates born out of anti-corruption protests following the deaths of 16 people in the collapse of a train station canopy in the city of Novi Sad.
Profound political shift 
The students' win marks a profound political shift in the country of some 6 million people and is reminiscent of the defeat of Hungary's Viktor Orban in April. It may also offer inspiration to other student movements that have cropped up across Europe in recent weeks demanding better education standards and prospects.
Read More: Lula says bus cuts hinder voters in Brazil
While the students' candidates include university professors, actors and farmers, the movement is without a leader - a strategy employed during protests to avoid any smear attempts by the government. It is unclear who will become prime minister and assume other key positions in order to enact the students' domestic agenda, which aims to root out graft and improve schooling, and manage the country's place on the international stage.
"This corruption that has entered into all pores of our lives...of course it will change, we are hoping we will slowly go into that direction of a normal community," said 60-year-old insurance worker Svetlana Karagkozidou.
Prominent figures include the head of the students' candidate list, cardiologist Ilija Srdanovic, former central bank governor Dejan Soskic and Radomir Sajcic, a professor at Belgrade University, who spoke on behalf of the students following their victory.
However, not everyone welcomed the change.
"Changing the country like that so suddenly and all at once, I don't like it. I don't even know who is standing behind, who those people are, who will be leading the country," said 60-year-old civil worker Senka Radakovic.
Meanwhile, supporters of the student movement set about cleaning up a park near the parliament building in Belgrade that had long been used as a camp by Vucic's supporters. They removed metal barricades and tents and cleaned stickers off children's play equipment.
"I think it is one of Belgrade's most beautiful parks, that they took from us for a year or a year-and-a-half, and this is the least we can do right now," said one of the cleaning volunteers, Filip Beselinovic.
Vucic and the SNS repeatedly denied accusations of repression and corruption.

Minister for Petroleum Ali Pervaiz Malik on Monday held a meeting with United States Chargé d’Affaires (Cd'A) Natalie Baker to discuss avenues for strengthening bilateral cooperation in the energy sector.
During the meeting, Malik briefed Natalie on the measures taken by Pakistan to ensure energy security amid the evolving geopolitical situation.
He highlighted that the ongoing conflict in the Middle East had created challenges for fuel availability, requiring proactive measures to maintain uninterrupted supplies.
Read: Pakistan, US agree to deepen energy ties
Natalie congratulated Pakistan on efficiently managing the fuel supply situation, noting that the country had not experienced a fuel shortage despite the challenging regional circumstances.
Federal Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik met US CDA H.E. Natalie A. Baker to discuss enhanced energy cooperation. Both sides explored opportunities in LNG supplies, refinery upgradation and long-term energy contracts to strengthen Pakistan’s energy security and attract US investment. pic.twitter.com/TBjxCBu4CH
— Petroleum Division, Ministry of Energy (@Official_PetDiv) October 26, 2026
The minister underscored Pakistan’s commitment to securing its energy needs and highlighted the ongoing engagement between the teams of both countries to explore opportunities for cooperation.
He further noted that Pakistan’s refinery upgradation programme could offer investment opportunities for US financial institutions.
Cd'A Baker expressed the desire to work closely with Pakistan to address its energy needs.
She emphasised the importance of creating opportunities for US companies in Pakistan and expressed optimism about establishing long-term energy supply contracts, noting that such arrangements would be mutually beneficial and create opportunities for American businesses.
The managing directors of Pakistan State Oil and Pakistan LNG Limited briefed the participants on the interest shown by US companies in LNG supply to Pakistan.
Malik invited US companies to participate in the upcoming Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum, highlighting the investment opportunities available in Pakistan.
Read More: US eyes investment in IT, mining, energy
He also expressed deep appreciation for US support and emphasised that enhanced bilateral engagement would help strengthen energy cooperation and contribute to Pakistan’s long-term energy security.
On October 25, Gilgit-Baltistan Chief Minister Advocate Amjad Hussain Azar said that the US had shown interest in investing in the region's energy sector, and that a public-private partnership unit had been established for that purpose.
On September 2, Oil and Gas Development Company Limited (OGDCL) signed a contract with Baker Hughes, a US energy technology company, to deploy Mature Assets Solutions aimed at revitalising ageing oil and gas wells and increasing Pakistan's indigenous hydrocarbon production.
Also Read: OGDC turns to US firm to boost oil output
Mature Assets Solutions was designed to unlock greater value from established fields experiencing natural production decline. Baker Hughes would bring technical expertise, advanced technologies and integrated capabilities to support OGDCL in identifying production opportunities across mature assets. The partnership was part of OGDCL's comprehensive Production Optimisation Drive.
Natalie, who attended the signing ceremony, described the agreement as a milestone in the US-Pakistan energy partnership, saying energy was a foundation of economic security and that collaboration would advance the shared goal of strengthening Pakistan's energy security.
On February 22, in a meeting between Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb and US Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick in Washington, the US expressed interest in investing in Pakistan's IT, mining, minerals and energy sectors.

items.content:
Dictionary.com named “maxxing” its 2026 Word of the Year, highlighting a growing internet-driven culture focused on optimising different aspects of life, the Guardian reported on Monday.
“Maxxing,” sometimes written as “-maxxing,” is short for “maximising” and refers to doing something to the fullest or optimising it as much as possible, according to the online dictionary.
The term gained popularity among Gen Z and Gen Alpha and has evolved into a flexible slang expression that can function as a noun, verb, adjective, or adverb.
Examples include “gymmaxxing” for optimising workout routines, “healthmaxxing” for maximising health and wellness practices, “sleepmaxxing” for optimising sleep and “tokenmaxxing” for deliberately maximising the use of artificial intelligence tools.
“Maxxing really stood out this year because not only was it everywhere, in all types of articles, but it crossed a lot of different domains,” Steve Johnson, director of lexicography for Dictionary Media Group, which operates Dictionary.com, told CBS News.
The term has also appeared in political messaging, including the use of “homelandmaxxing,” while “cozymaxxing” has been used to describe efforts to optimise leisure and comfort.
Dictionary.com said its selection was based on an analysis of search data, social media trends and news coverage, as well as the word's cultural significance.
Johnson said the dictionary's lexicographers maintain a list of words to monitor throughout the year, examining their frequency and how they reflect broader cultural developments.
The choice marks a contrast with Dictionary.com's 2025 Word of the Year, “67,” a viral expression whose meaning often remained unclear to users.
Other 2026 Finalists
Dictionary.com selected finalists from internet culture, politics, technology and wider media trends.
They included “affordability,” reflecting concerns over housing, groceries, childcare and other rising costs; “data centre,” amid the expansion of infrastructure supporting artificial intelligence; “unc,” a Gen Z and Gen Alpha slang term for an older person perceived as uncool or out of touch; and “odyssey,” referring to a long and eventful journey that gained renewed cultural attention following Christopher Nolan's 2026 film adaptation of Homer's epic.

items.author: Usama Anjum
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
An advertisement appearing on your smartphone may seem harmless, but Pakistan’s National Computer Emergency Response Team (National CERT) has warned that sophisticated spyware can potentially exploit online advertising systems to target mobile devices without users clicking anything.
The warning concerns a technique known as AdFection, which uses digital advertising infrastructure to identify potential targets and, under certain conditions, deliver malicious code to their devices.
Unlike familiar online scams that trick users into opening suspicious links or downloading attachments, this technique may not require any action from the victim. Simply avoiding unknown links may therefore not be enough to protect against such targeted attacks.
The advisory follows research published by Citizen Lab on October 15, 2026. Researchers reported with high confidence that devices associated with Al Jazeera had been targeted and infected with Candiru spyware through this method.
However, National CERT stressed an important distinction: seeing an advertisement does not mean your phone has been hacked. The attack requires additional steps, including successful exploitation of a security vulnerability.
How Can Spyware Reach a Phone Without a Click?
The technique takes advantage of the complex systems used to deliver advertisements across websites and mobile applications.
When someone opens a website or application containing advertisements, advertising networks may process information about the device and select which advertisement to display. This process can involve real-time bidding, where advertisers compete to show their ads to particular audiences.
According to National CERT, attackers could exploit parts of this infrastructure to profile devices, identify specific individuals, and attempt to deliver malicious code.
A potential attack could begin with device profiling and target selection, followed by advertisement delivery and an attempt to exploit a vulnerability in the operating system, browser, or application.
If the exploitation succeeds, spyware may gain access to sensitive information stored on the device. Depending on its capabilities and privileges, such spyware could potentially expose private messages, contacts, photographs, documents, account information, and other confidential data.
The threat is particularly concerning for journalists, government officials, researchers, corporate executives, and organizations dealing with sensitive information.
However, National CERT has not suggested that every online advertisement poses such a threat. The advisory concerns sophisticated, targeted exploitation rather than ordinary advertising activity.
Another challenge is detection. Unlike conventional phishing attempts, these attacks may not leave obvious warning signs such as suspicious links, unusual downloads, or messages from unknown senders.
National CERT Shares Precautions for Mobile Users and Organizations
National CERT has urged smartphone users and organizations to strengthen their security practices, particularly where sensitive information is involved.
The most important recommendation is to keep mobile operating systems, browsers and applications updated. Security updates can address vulnerabilities that attackers may attempt to exploit.
Users should also prefer devices that continue receiving regular security patches, install applications only from trusted sources, and review application permissions periodically.
Reputable ad-blocking tools and browser-level protections may help reduce exposure to potentially malicious advertising infrastructure. However, National CERT cautioned that these measures cannot guarantee protection against advanced spyware attacks.
The advisory also recommends using strong, unique passwords and multifactor authentication, along with regularly reviewing connected devices, active account sessions, and recovery settings.
For organizations, the warning goes further. National CERT has advised maintaining proper mobile-device inventories, using suitable device-management and endpoint-security controls, and preserving historical DNS, firewall, proxy and other security logs that could help investigate suspected attacks.
Organizations handling particularly sensitive information should also consider separating confidential activities from routine web browsing wherever practical.
The agency cautioned users against assuming their phones have been compromised simply because a device becomes hot, consumes more battery, or starts performing slowly. These symptoms can have many explanations and are not reliable proof of spyware infection.
At the same time, a normal antivirus scan or the absence of security alerts does not necessarily mean a device is free from sophisticated surveillance software.
If there are credible indications of compromise, National CERT recommends seeking specialist cybersecurity or digital forensics assistance. Resetting a phone or deleting applications before evidence is preserved could make an investigation more difficult.
Users who receive targeted threat notifications from Apple, Google or other technology providers should verify those warnings through official account or support channels rather than clicking links in unsolicited messages.
The latest advisory highlights a changing reality of smartphone security. While phishing messages and suspicious downloads remain important threats, advanced attackers may increasingly attempt to exploit the technologies that operate quietly in the background of everyday internet use.
For ordinary users, regular security updates and careful device management remain essential. For organisations dealing with sensitive information, the warning is a reminder that cybersecurity planning must also account for targeted attacks that require no interaction from the victim.
Also read:
NCERT Issues High-Risk WhatsApp Web Cyberattack Alert for Government Officials and Sensitive Staff
The post Your Phone Could Be Targeted by Spyware Through Online Ads Without a Single Click, NCERT Warns appeared first on PhoneWorld.

items.content:
China's Communist Party ​began a meeting of senior cadres on Monday aimed at tightening discipline and pressing officials to implement Beijing's orders, ‌paving the way for a leadership reshuffle next year expected to extend President Xi Jinping's rule for another five years.
Xi briefed the party's four-day Central Committee meeting on a draft document centred on "full and rigorous party self-governance" that state news agency Xinhua said addressed the challenges the party faced, including ​growing its governing capacity, as well as guarding against complacency and combating corruption, the president's signature campaign.
The implementation of ​major decisions and plans of the Central Committee, the largest of its top decision-making bodies, must not ⁠be empty rhetoric, the Xinhua commentary read.
The Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee on Monday started a four-day plenary session in Beijing, which focuses on strengthening Party self-governance. This marks the latest move by the Party Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core to strengthen the Party… pic.twitter.com/ZOTQsQJk3k
— China Xinhua News (@XHNews) October 26, 2026
"It is essential to both refine institutional rules and regulations to close loopholes and strengthen ​safeguards, and ensure their effective implementation," it said.
Read: China's Communist Party ousts former ministers from Central Committee
The Central Committee will convene in a closed-door meeting from Monday to Thursday, the fifth ​such gathering since the current cohort was formed in 2022 and therefore known as the "fifth plenum".
Analysts say this could be the last major party gathering before its 2027 leadership reshuffle, when Xi is expected to hold on to the top job for a fourth term.
"The plenum will present Xi as ​in control, and able to continue his command," said Kerry Brown, director of King's College London's Lau China Institute. "It is likely ​everything will be centred on him, to dispel any rumours or doubts about his physical fitness and ability to continue in his role."
China’s Communist Party is gathering for its most important meeting of the year: the fifth plenum. Xi Jinping’s leadership purges and efforts to tighten party control are set to take center stage. Here’s what to watch for. https://t.co/TasreYLghF
— Bloomberg (@business) October 25, 2026
With substantive ‌policy issues ⁠already largely set in previous gatherings, "this will be a plenum where appearances will matter as much, if not more, than substance," Brown added.
Rooting out corruption for market predictability
Xi has overseen a vast anti-corruption campaign in recent years which has led to the purge of hundreds of senior officials and top generals, even the president's one-time allies.
Read More: China purges third Politburo member in deepening anti-graft drive
While some say the purges, particularly those targeting the highest ranks of ​the armed forces, are destabilising and ​undermine combat readiness, the party ⁠has portrayed the campaign as both necessary and regenerative, saying the military must undergo a phoenix-like rebirth and "bathe in flames and be forged anew".
The Xinhua commentary presented the anti-corruption drive as a ​demonstration of "sustained and systemic" self-governance to "ensure officials dare not, cannot and do not want to commit ​corruption".
"For global investors ⁠and policymakers, this signals greater predictability," it said, arguing that China was also creating a more transparent environment for international cooperation as merit and the rule of law prevail over connections and bribery.
Typically, seven plenums, each usually associated with a particular agenda, are held between ⁠major party ​congresses, which convene twice a decade. The party's constitution requires at least one ​plenum to be held every year.
The fifth plenum usually deliberates the country's strategic blueprint, the five-year plan, but an unusually late third plenum, delayed for more than half a year ​until mid-2024, has disrupted the conventional scheduling.

US singer Chris Brown was ​spared an immediate prison sentence in Britain on Monday for attacking a music producer with a tequila bottle ‌in a London nightclub in 2023, with his fans cheering as the musician walked free from court.
Brown, 37, was given an eight-month suspended sentence at London's Southwark Crown Court over the attack on Abraham Diaw at the Tape nightclub in February 2023 that lasted around 20 seconds.
Diaw was hit twice in the head ​with a bottle, which was then swung twice more at him in what prosecutors described as "a vicious and unprovoked attack".
The ​R&B star and his vocal coach Omololu Akinlolu, 40, pleaded guilty to a charge of affray in July, ⁠having denied more serious charges of attempting to inflict grievous bodily harm and assault causing actual bodily harm.
No speical treatment
Judge Tony Baumgartner said: "This was ​serious, public violence. In your case, Brown, it involved the repeated use ... of a bottle, including twice striking Diaw to his head."
The judge told ​Brown: "Your fame, commercial success and professional standing do not entitle you to special treatment – the law applies equally to everyone."
But Baumgartner said he could suspend Brown's sentence for 12 months, meaning he will not go to prison unless he commits another offence in that period. Akinlolu was also spared an immediate jail ​sentence.
"Violence will not be accepted on the streets of London," Detective Chief Superintendent Christina Jessah from the Metropolitan Police said in a ​statement. "Regardless of an individual's profile or status, we will pursue those responsible and work tirelessly to bring them before the courts."
US singer Chris Brown arrives at Southwark Crown Court where he is due to be sentenced after pleading guilty to affray over an incident in which prosecutors said he attacked a music producer with a bottle in a London nightclub in 2023, in London, Britain, October 26, 2026. PHOTO: Reuters
Brown's fan cheer suspended sentence
Brown, ‌winner of ⁠Grammy awards for best R&B album in 2011 and 2025, has previously admitted other violent offences in the US, having been charged with assaulting his then-partner, singer Rihanna, in 2009, with a photo of her bruised face making headlines around the world.
Prosecutor Heidi Stonecliffe said Brown pleaded guilty to the 2009 assault of Rihanna and was sentenced to five years' probation. He also admitted a 2013 assault on a fan he ​was accused of punching when he ​asked for a photograph.
Brown remains ⁠hugely popular and has sold tens of millions of records worldwide, with dozens of fans queuing outside court from around 0700 GMT, about an hour before the building opened.
His lawyer Sallie Bennett-Jenkins said Brown ​was profoundly sorry for the incident and described him as "a dedicated, loving and loyal father to four ​children".
"This was an ⁠ugly and unattractive incident, we would be the first to accept," she added. "It was, however, an incident that was very short-lived."
Brown thanked the judge before leaving the dock and nodding towards about two dozen of his supporters in the public gallery.
Other fans who gathered outside the building cheered ⁠as Brown ​left and went into a waiting car.
Brown was arrested in May 2025 having ​returned to Britain for the first time since the attack and was initially denied bail, throwing his worldwide "Breezy Bowl XX" tour into doubt.
But Brown was eventually released after promising to pay ​a £5 million ($6.7 million) security fee, allowing the tour to go ahead.

items.author: Akshit Pushkarna
items.content:
Ahead of listing on the mainboard, BSE SME-listed fintech SaaS company Veefin Solutions reported a 127% rise in its consolidated net profit to ₹24.9 Cr in H1 FY27 from ₹11 Cr in the corresponding period of the previous fiscal year. The company’s net profit also increased 9% from ₹22.8 Cr in the preceding six months.
Operating revenue more than doubled to ₹238.8 Cr in the first half of FY27 from ₹110.4 Cr a year earlier. This was also 3% higher than the ₹232.7 Cr recorded in H2 FY26.
Including other income of ₹1.8 Cr, Veefin’s total income stood at ₹240.6 Cr in H1 FY27, compared with ₹112.1 Cr a year earlier.
Total expenses increased 109% to ₹205.3 Cr from ₹98 Cr.
For Q2 FY27, Veefin’s net profit rose 61% to ₹15.3 Cr from ₹9.5 Cr in the preceding quarter. Operating revenue increased 9% QoQ to ₹124.7 Cr from ₹114.2 Cr, while total income stood at ₹125.7 Cr.
The company’s consolidated EBITDA, or earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation, rose 160% to ₹60.8 Cr in H1 FY27 from ₹23.4 Cr in the year-ago period. Its EBITDA margin expanded to 25.5% from 21.2%, an improvement of 424 basis points. The consolidated profit margin also increased to 10.4% from 9.9%.
On a standalone basis, Veefin reported operating revenue of ₹49.2 Cr in H1 FY27, up 83.6% from ₹26.8 Cr a year earlier. Standalone EBITDA more than doubled to ₹27.2 Cr from ₹13.1 Cr, while net profit rose 79.4% to ₹14 Cr from ₹7.8 Cr.
Important to highlight that the SME company secured an in-principle approval from the BSE’s Internal Regulatory Oversight and Review Group (IRORG) to migrate its shares from the exchange’s SME Platform to the mainboard. It is yet to receive a go-ahead from the NSE for the migration.
Veefin’s Growing Business Pipeline
Beyond its financial performance, Veefin reported an open business pipeline of ₹920 Cr at the end of the September quarter, up from ₹760 Cr at the end of the preceding quarter. The company added ₹240 Cr in new opportunities during the quarter, while ₹46 Cr was converted into contracted business. Other movements reduced the pipeline by a net ₹35 Cr.
The pipeline comprises 77 deals across 16 countries in five regions. According to the investor presentation, 75% of the pipeline is qualified, while 11% is under negotiation. The company also reported recent wins involving a leading finance company and two public sector banks (PSBs) in India.
Supply chain finance (SCF) accounts for 35% of the pipeline value, followed by digital lending at 23%, trade and cash management at 18%, and digital banking at 16%. Fraud and risk management contributes 3%, while other products account for the remaining 5%.
The company has expanded beyond its bread and butter SCF, with 65% of the open pipeline value coming from offering beyond SCF. Further, 38 of the 77 deals involve customers evaluating more than one product, indicating opportunities to sell multiple solutions to the same customer.’
Veefin’s broader product portfolio includes supply chain finance, trade finance, cash and liquidity management, loan origination and management, debt collections, corporate and retail internet banking, mobile banking, fraud management, risk analytics and financing infrastructure. The latter includes its PSB Xchange Marketplace, guarantee management and TReDS technology.
International markets account for 84% of the pipeline value. Southeast Asia contributes 56%, followed by India at 16%, the rest of South Asia at 12%, the Middle East at 11%, Africa at 3% and Europe at 2%. India accounts for the largest number of deals, at 32%, followed by Southeast Asia at 29%.
Existing customers contributed 73.9% of standalone revenue during the first half, with new customers accounting for the remaining 26.1%. In Q2 FY27, the corresponding shares were 69.9% and 30.1%, respectively.
Shares of Veefin ended today’s trading session 14.89% higher at ₹245.30 apiece on the BSE.

items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Reinforcing their commitment to digital innovation and operational excellence in Pakistan’s capital market, Central Depository Company of Pakistan Limited (CDC) and EClear Services Limited are expanding their collaboration to introduce advanced digital payment and investor verification services under CDC’s Raast Aggregator framework.
The collaboration builds on the successful implementation of Raast Person-to-Person (P2P) and Static QR Code services by CDC, which enables customers of capital market entities to conveniently transfer funds for trading, investment or any other purpose. Building on the successful implementation of the P2P mechanism, CDC has now taken another pioneering step by becoming the first institution to extend Raast Person-to-Merchant (P2M) payment solutions and Raast-based IBAN-CNIC Validation services to Pakistan’s capital market.
Demonstrating its commitment to embracing next-generation financial technology, EClear Services is set to become the first institution in Pakistan’s stock market to adopt Raast P2M Request to Pay Later (RTPL) and Dynamic QR Code use cases. These solutions will introduce more convenient and efficient ways to initiate, manage, and collect payments, with potential applications across a range of broker operations. One such application is the automation of debit and margin calls by EClear’s connected TO brokers, offering a more streamlined alternative to conventional payment collection processes.
This initiative highlights how the integration of digital payments and verification services can translate into tangible operational benefits for capital market participants. By adopting these capabilities, institutions can improve payment collection workflows, reduce manual intervention, and deliver a more seamless experience for investors.
Speaking on the occasion, Mr. Badiuddin Akber, Chief Executive Officer, CDC, stated:
“CDC was the first capital market institution to connect with the State Bank of Pakistan’s Raast system, successfully implementing RAAST 1st use case of bulk payments mechanism for its eDividend initiative in 2021. Since then, we have continued to adopt the latest payment solutions under the Raast framework and extend their benefits to capital market participants, including mutual fund companies, stockbrokers, and insurance companies. Our expanded collaboration with EClear Services further reinforces our commitment to driving digital innovation and efficiency across Pakistan’s capital market.”
Through its Raast Aggregator framework, CDC continues to expand the digital capabilities available to Pakistan’s capital market, leveraging the State Bank of Pakistan’s Raast infrastructure to facilitate innovative payment solutions and streamlined financial processes. By enabling market participants to access and integrate these services, CDC is helping create the foundation for a more connected, efficient, and digitally enabled investment ecosystem.

items.content:
More than half of research participants in Switzerland consider disinformation a "major" social problem, expressing concern over misinformation, according to a study released Monday.
The findings were published in the University of Zurich's Research Centre for the Public Sphere and Society 2026 Quality of the Media Yearbook, Swissinfo reported.
Some 56.5% of the participants view "fake news as a major social problem," the report noted.
The latest percentage represents a "significant" increase compared with five years ago, it added.
The study found that more than half of respondents regularly encounter misleading information, particularly through social media, video-sharing platforms, and artificial intelligence chatbots.
Some 42% were classified as "news-deprived," referring to people who rarely follow current affairs or rely on fragmented information from social media, making them more vulnerable to conspiracy theories.
Read More: Meta to raise up to $95 billion in equity to fund costly AI expansion
Researchers found that relying exclusively on platforms such as TikTok and Instagram offered no greater protection against conspiracy theories than avoiding news altogether.
While overall news quality remained stable in 2025, media diversity declined, with 44.7% of national political coverage appearing across multiple German-language publications.
The study also found that 57.7% of respondents considered public broadcasting important or very important.
Meanwhile, technology platforms captured up to 2.5 billion Swiss francs ($3 billion) in annual advertising revenue, while domestic media revenues fell to 1.94 billion francs ($2.3 billion).
The researchers called for countermeasures, such as media vouchers for young adults.

items.content:
Consumer-focused investment firm L Catterton has made a strategic investment in InMobi-backed AI shopping platform Glance to support its expansion, with a particular focus on the US.
The companies did not disclose the investment amount or other transaction terms. Sources told Inc42 that the investment was a fresh equity infusion
L Catterton said it will use its consumer and category expertise, operating capabilities, and global network to support Glance’s growth.
Glance uses agentic AI to understand consumers’ interests and preferences and recommend products across smartphones, connected TVs, and other digital platforms. It aims to help users move from product discovery to purchase on devices they already use.
Through partnerships with Samsung, Motorola, and DIRECTV, the platform is already available on millions of devices across the US.
Glance founder and CEO Naveen Tewari said the investment validates the company’s approach to shopping, which aims to move commerce beyond search towards agentic shopping.
L Catterton global CEO Scott Dahnke said Glance combines a differentiated shopping proposition with broad distribution across the screens consumers use throughout the day.
From Content To Commerce
Founded in 2019 by InMobi’s four cofounders — Naveen Tewari, Piyush Shah, Abhay Singhal, and Mohit Saxena — Glance initially curated content on smartphone lock screens.
Its original offering had built a user base of 300-400 Mn as of May 2025 without a separate app and attracted around $500 Mn from investors, including Google, Mithril Capital, and Jio Platforms.
Its move into AI shopping took shape publicly in April 2025, when president and COO Piyush Shah previewed the offering at Inc42’s ‘The GenAI Summit’. Shah demonstrated how users could upload a selfie to generate images of themselves wearing different outfits.
Glance subsequently launched its generative AI shopping app in India in May 2025, following a soft launch in the US. Users could visualise themselves in suggested outfits, save the images as wallpapers, or proceed to purchase.
At the time, Glance described three technology layers: a commerce model for discovery and recommendations, a generative AI model for visual experiences, and a transaction model to enable purchases. It had also partnered with Myntra in India and brands in the US to facilitate shopping.

items.content:
Egypt's parliament authorised the military on Monday to provide support to help defend Saudi Arabia, parliamentarians said, and local media reported, a move that could push Cairo directly into the regional conflict ​that has expanded with intensified attacks by Yemen's Iran-allied Houthis on the Gulf kingdom.
President ‌Abdel Fattah al-Sisi had asked parliament last week to approve defending its Gulf Arab ally and the world's biggest oil exporter if Riyadh requests help against the Houthis, whose advances also threaten the strategic Bab el-Mandeb Strait — a gateway to Egypt's Suez ​Canal.
Egypt has frequently condemned Iranian and Iranian-backed attacks on Gulf countries but has not publicly ​engaged in direct combat or joined the Makkah mutual defence pact between Saudi Arabia, ⁠Pakistan and Turkiye that was signed in August.
The approval followed closed-door discussions on authorising military support to the kingdom, including the possible deployment of troops, amid escalating regional tensions.
Parliament said the two-thirds-majority authorisation allows Sisi to take measures, in coordination with Saudi Arabia, to defend the kingdom’s territory, sovereignty and holy sites.
The decision followed closed-door sessions held on Oct 18, 19 and 26 at the president’s request, the statement said.
Lawmakers discussed regional developments and their implications for Egyptian and Arab national security, with representatives from different political parties and independent lawmakers participating, it added.
Parliament said the authorisation was consistent with decisions taken by Egypt’s National Defence Council at its Oct 18 meeting.
The statement did not specify the measures to be taken or explicitly announce a deployment of Egyptian troops.
Earlier today, lawmakers resumed deliberations in a third closed-door session chaired by Parliament Speaker Hisham Badawi, following two meetings held last week at Sisi’s request.

Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty said this month that Egyptian membership in ​the pact remained "under serious consideration".
Read: Egypt's Sisi seeks parliament's backing to help defend Saudi Arabia if asked
Egypt, the Arab world's most populous state with one of the region's largest ​militaries, joined the Saudi-led coalition in an earlier phase of Yemen's war in March 2015 mainly as a naval partner, sending warships to secure Red Sea shipping lanes while pledging air support. It also deployed around 800 ground troops but ​played only a limited combat role.
Egypt was involved in a costly military intervention in Yemen in the ​1960s and has not undertaken a large-scale foreign ground deployment since the 1991 Gulf War.
Saudi Arabia is a major ‌political and ⁠financial partner of Cairo, providing billions of dollars in aid, deposits at the central bank and energy supplies under Sisi.
Fighting between the Saudi-led coalition backing Yemen's internationally recognised government and the Houthi militia, which controls the capital Sanaa, has escalated in recent weeks, becoming a volatile front in the US-Israeli war on Iran.
The ​Houthis have attacked Riyadh's international ​airport and the state ⁠oil giant Saudi Aramco, disrupting flights and oil exports, while aid agencies have warned of worsening conditions in Yemen, already suffering one of the world's worst humanitarian ​crises.
Abdelatty and Egyptian intelligence chief Hassan Rashad travelled to Riyadh on Wednesday ​to deliver a ⁠letter to Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman from Sisi, who said Egypt's support would be limited to defending Saudi territory and borders rather than attacking Yemen. Abdelatty said after that visit that Cairo advocates exploring "every ⁠opportunity" to ​resolve the Yemen conflict diplomatically.
Read More: Egypt's Sisi says Saudi defence role would not include attack on Yemen
The Saudi crown prince visited Sisi in ​Cairo on September 15 to discuss security and navigation in the Red Sea after the fighting in Yemen reignited.

items.title: Vote young yet govern much later: West African youth’s struggle for power
items.summary:
In all of West Africa, te voting age is 18, but presidential eligibility ages vary widely
Originally published on Global Voices
Youth mobilized in Africa. Screenshot from DW Africa's YouTube channel
In West Africa, young people can vote for the first time at 18. In some states, they are eligible to serve in parliament by age 25. However, depending on the country, they must wait until they are 35, 40, or even 50 years old before being eligible to run for the highest office. Although these age limits are beginning to shift, the real challenges often lie deeper in the electoral structure.
Young people are deemed mature enough to elect their leaders, yet not to replace them. They drive political movements forward by voting, advocating, campaigning, and protesting, yet cannot run for office themselves. The question is, can democracy really be called inclusive when it gives young people the right to elect but not to be elected?
Age: A shifting barrier
Across the region, the voting age is 18.
items.author: Laura
items.content:
In all of West Africa, te voting age is 18, but presidential eligibility ages vary widely
Originally published on Global Voices
Youth mobilized in Africa. Screenshot from DW Africa's YouTube channel
In West Africa, young people can vote for the first time at 18. In some states, they are eligible to serve in parliament by age 25. However, depending on the country, they must wait until they are 35, 40, or even 50 years old before being eligible to run for the highest office. Although these age limits are beginning to shift, the real challenges often lie deeper in the electoral structure.
Young people are deemed mature enough to elect their leaders, yet not to replace them. They drive political movements forward by voting, advocating, campaigning, and protesting, yet cannot run for office themselves. The question is, can democracy really be called inclusive when it gives young people the right to elect but not to be elected?
Age: A shifting barrier
Across the region, the voting age is 18. However, presidential eligibility ages vary widely. In Gambia, it’s 30; in Senegal, Nigeria, and Côte d’Ivoire, it’s 35; and in Benin, Ghana, and Guinea, it’s 40. In the legislative assemblies, the bar is even lower. In Togo, Benin, Senegal, and Nigeria’s House of Representatives, it’s 25, while in Ghana it’s 21.
The situation in Togo requires closer inspection. On May 6, 2024, the country legally became a parliamentary republic. Under the 2024 Constitution, the eligibility age for President of the Republic is 50. Parliament also now elects the president, whose powers are limited. Authority now rests with the President of the Council of Ministers, who must be at least 40 and is not elected in public presidential elections. Faure Gnassingbé has held this position since May 3, 2025, the day parliament also elected the country’s oldest-ever incoming president of the Republic, Jean-Lucien Savi de Tové, 86.
However, the country’s legal age limit is hardly set in stone. In 2002, the National Assembly lowered it from 45 to 35 — a reform the opposition called tailor-made for Faure Gnassingbé.
More recently, in Ghana’s capital, Accra, on July 30, 2026, the Ghanaian government agreed in principle to lower the minimum presidential eligibility age from 40 to 35, defying the Constitutional Review Committee’s recommendation of 30. This legislation will ultimately go to a referendum, requiring a 40 percent turnout and a 75 percent approval.
In 2018, Nigeria set a regional precedent. Under pressure from the youth-led Not Too Young To Run campaign, the law lowered the presidential eligibility age from 40 to 35 and the House of Representatives’ eligibility age from 30 to 25.
According to data from the Inter-Parliamentary Union, lowering the minimum presidential age leads to younger parliaments. However, Côte d’Ivoire tells a very different story. In 2016, after removing the maximum age limit of 75 to run for office, incumbent President Alassane Ouattara, 83, ran for another term in 2025. The law rarely protects younger generations.
Youths particularly active in street movements
Even though young people have the right to vote across the continent, that does not mean all young people exercise that right. In August 2025, an Afrobarometer survey found that those aged 18 to 35 were less active than their elders in almost all traditional means of political participation. Overall across the continent, they trailed by 18 percentage points in voting, but by a record 29 points in Senegal. Protests were the only exception.
In Togo’s capital of Lomé, the June 6 Movement, sparked by the rapper Aamron’s arrest, brought thousands of people onto the streets. According to the Media Foundation for West Africa, the subsequent crackdown, for which the International Federation for Human Rights (FIDH) blamed government-backed militiamen, left seven dead.
Similarly, in Madagascar, the September 2025 protests toppled President Andry Rajoelina’s government, resulting in a military takeover. According to the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS), the overthrown president himself came to power in 2019 on the back of a protest, at just 34 years old.
Comparably, in Kenya, street protests forced the withdrawal of the 2024 Finance Bill. Meanwhile, in Morocco, youth-led protests prompted the authorities to announce youth candidacy incentives and prosecute specific ringleaders.
Although leaderless movements wrest concessions, they rarely last without political parties or trade unions to sustain them.
The gap between participation and representation
The Inter-Parliamentary Report, published on April 9, 2026, found that elected officials aged 30 and under account for just 2.8 percent of all parliamentarians worldwide. Since 2023, progress has stalled for the first time since 2014. More than a third (37.1 percent) of legislative houses have no parliamentarians in this age group.
The lack of youth representation and participation is a significant challenge considering young people under 35 account for roughly 70 percent of West Africa’s population, according to the West Africa Youth Democracy Conference.
According to data from the Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU), at the start of Ghana’s 2025 parliamentary term, despite the legal minimum age of 21, no parliamentarians were aged 30 or under. What’s more, those aged 31 to 40 held just 46 of the 269 parliamentary seats, or 17.1 percent. After Senegal’s 2024 legislative elections, the National Assembly had only five members under 30, accounting for just 3 percent. Although almost 38 percent of registered voters were aged 18 to 35, the Assembly’s average age was 47. Elected at just 44, the country’s youngest-ever president, Bassirou Diomaye Faye, only became an official candidate after his mentor, Ousmane Sonko, was disqualified.
In Nigeria, International IDEA, an intergovernmental organization that supports sustainable democracy worldwide, reported that in 2015, only three of the 360 members of the House of Representatives were between the ages of 18–25, rising to 14 in 2019 — a positive but modest development.
In Dakar, the head of Yiaga Africa, the organization behind the Not Too Young to Run campaign, summed up the situation, stating that the political arena is more open on paper than in reality.
However, Afrobarometer has identified a paradox. While young people do vote less than their elders, they are also excluded from seats of power and the polls. This representation gap is anything but passive; it breeds disengagement. The IPU warns that young people’s absence from parliamentary assemblies undermines institutional legitimacy and jeopardizes trust in democracy. Senegal, listed in the 2026 IPU report as one of the countries where parliament grew younger in the most recent elections, shows that rejuvenation is possible when a political agenda empowers a generation.
Rewriting the deal: money, parties, obstacles
High age limit proponents demand experience. Across the 34 countries that Afrobarometer surveyed, citizens favor an average leadership age of 39. Those calling for a lower age limit seek proven engagement measures, such as lowering the eligibility age, quotas, and forums for young parliamentarians. However, as Nigeria shows, often, the main obstacle is financial.
Nigeria’s ruling party, the All Progressives Congress (APC), has set the total cost of its 2027 presidential nomination and expression-of-interest forms at NGN 100 million (USD 75,000), NGN 30 million (USD 22,521) for the expression of interest, and NGN 70 million (USD 52,550) for the nomination. The Senate will cost NGN 20 million (USD 15,014) and the House of Representatives NGN 10 million (USD 7,507).
Young people will receive a 50 percent discount only on nomination fees, leaving the presidential bill at NGN 65 million (USD 48,789). A Nigerian civil society group calculated that workers earning the minimum wage, NGN 70,000 (USD 52) per month, would have to work for more than a century to buy some of these forms.
The Electoral Act, 2026, signed on February 18, also doubled the presidential candidate’s campaign spending limit to NGN 10 billion (USD 7.5 million) and tripled that of governorship candidates to NGN 3 billion (USD 2.2 million).
At the initiative of ECOWAS and the youth-led advocacy organization Legis360, delegates from 12 countries gathered in Dakar to bring these obstacles to the forefront. In their communiqué, they launched the West Africa Youth Observer Network (WAYON) and called for youth quotas, reduced candidate fees, and spending limits. ECOWAS later announced it would deploy youth-only election observers for Nigeria’s upcoming presidential election on January 16, 2027.
Other countries exemplify how laws can directly impact nominations. According to the IPU, Ecuador owes much of its progress to a 2022 law, which required 25 percent of its candidates to be young adults. Countries with term limits also have considerably more young parliamentarians than the global average. In 2023, the IPU also noted that limited youth funding and a lack of spending limits contributed to aging parliamentary assemblies.
Elsewhere, the obstacles are political. Take, for example, Benin. After disqualifying the main opposition candidate (Les Démocrates) for failing to meet election requirements, current President Romuald Wadagni faced only one opponent (Paul Hounkpe). On April 12, 2026, Wadagni subsequently won the presidential election with 94.27 percent of the vote. In 2024, a constitutional reform that extended the presidential term from five to seven years also raised the minimum vote threshold for securing seats in the National Assembly from 10 percent of parliamentary election votes to 20 percent. This regulation far outweighs a candidate’s date of birth when they have no party machine behind them.
Another example is Burkina Faso. In January 2026, the military junta dissolved all political parties. Meanwhile, in The Gambia, President Barrow will run for a third term in the December 5 presidential election.
Inclusive voting, but flawed representation
Is a system that gives young people the right to elect their leader but impedes their ability to become one themselves fully inclusive? The findings speak for themselves. Although Nigeria has lowered its age limits and Ghana has committed to doing the same, these limits are more a symptom than a cause. Age is not the sole contributing factor.
Critics argue that lowering age limits without also addressing nomination costs, party regulations, and the openness of the political arena would only be the first step on a seemingly endless staircase. What stands between young people and decision-making positions are exceedingly high costs, restrictive nomination practices, candidate exclusions, and even the lack of parties.
Until street movements have credible institutional representatives, they will continue to wrest temporary concessions or, as seen in Madagascar, give way to powers other than those they had hoped for. The primary challenge of the West African Democratic Pact is making young people not only the promised future of politics, but also an active part of today’s representation.

items.author: Rizwana Omer
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The National Cyber Emergency Response Team (NCERT) has issued a high-severity WhatsApp Web cyberattack alert, warning of targeted phishing and malware attacks that arrive through WhatsApp Web, the WhatsApp desktop app and email.
Government officials and people who handle sensitive information are the main targets, according to the advisory. NCERT has rated the threat level as high.
How the attack works
The advisory says attackers pose as government officials and departments, then send harmful files to their targets. A file sent under the name of an official document can infect a Windows system when opened.
Phishing means tricking a person into opening a link or file, or giving up information, by pretending to be someone trustworthy. Malware is software designed to harm a device or steal from it.
If a system is compromised, NCERT says the risks include remote control of the device, password theft and data theft.
Why a message from a known number is not proof
The advisory raises a second risk, which is session hijacking. A WhatsApp Web session lets a computer use an account already logged in on a phone. If an attacker takes over that session, they could commit fraud from the victim’s own number.
For that reason, NCERT says an unexpected message or file from a number the recipient knows can itself be a sign of targeting. Another warning sign is an unfamiliar device in the “Linked Devices” list in WhatsApp.
What NCERT recommends
The advisory advises officers who hold sensitive information not to use WhatsApp Web or the desktop app on Windows. It also recommends that WhatsApp files not be moved onto official Windows computers.
For everyone, the recommendations are:
End any suspicious WhatsApp Web sessions immediately.
Do not open unverified links, files or messages. Confirm through a separate channel first.
Never share passwords, one-time passwords (OTPs) or verification codes.
Keep Windows, browsers and other software updated.
Turn on two-factor authentication and WhatsApp’s two-step verification.
If a compromise is suspected, the device should be disconnected from the network and the internet at once. Messages and logs should be saved as evidence and not reopened.
Users can check their own account in WhatsApp under Settings, then Linked Devices. Any device they do not recognise should be removed.
Bottom Line
The advisory’s most notable instruction is also its most restrictive: officers with sensitive information should avoid WhatsApp Web and the desktop app on Windows altogether. That is a stronger step than the usual advice to be careful with links, and it suggests NCERT sees the risk as built into the setup and not just a matter of user mistakes.
WhatsApp is widely used for day-to-day work communication, including in offices. Messaging apps tend to feel informal, which lowers people’s guard, and a message from a familiar name carries a trust that email does not. Attackers who copy official names are using exactly that habit.
The practical test of the advisory will be whether departments turn it into written rules about which channels officials may use for official files. Warnings reach individuals, but only policy changes what a whole office does by default.

items.title: [Update] IRDAI Extends Feedback Deadline For Insurance Distribution Reforms To Oct 31
items.summary:
Update | October 26, 12:52 IST
The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) has extended the deadline for stakeholders to submit feedback on its proposed insurance distribution reforms to October 31 from October 25, following an “encouraging response” to the consultation paper.
The insurance regulator said it has received more than 650 comments on its consultation paper, titled ‘Recalibrating Economics of Insurance Distribution’, released on September 23. The paper proposes changes to commission structures for insurance distributors and expense limits for insurers.
“In view of the significant interest and to facilitate wider participation, the last date for submission of comments has been extended till 31st October 2026,” IRDAI said.
The extension comes amid opposition from insurance brokers over the proposed changes, with the Insurance Brokers Association of India (IBAI) previously seeking an extension of the feedback deadline until December 31, 2026.
Original |
items.author: Gaurav Bagur
items.content:
Update | October 26, 12:52 IST
The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) has extended the deadline for stakeholders to submit feedback on its proposed insurance distribution reforms to October 31 from October 25, following an “encouraging response” to the consultation paper.
The insurance regulator said it has received more than 650 comments on its consultation paper, titled ‘Recalibrating Economics of Insurance Distribution’, released on September 23. The paper proposes changes to commission structures for insurance distributors and expense limits for insurers.
“In view of the significant interest and to facilitate wider participation, the last date for submission of comments has been extended till 31st October 2026,” IRDAI said.
The extension comes amid opposition from insurance brokers over the proposed changes, with the Insurance Brokers Association of India (IBAI) previously seeking an extension of the feedback deadline until December 31, 2026.
Original | October 7, 12:14 IST
The Insurance Brokers Association of India (IBAI) has said that the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India’s (IRDAI) recently proposed norms could trigger a 60-70% revenue collapse across the insurance broking sector.
Addressing a press briefing, the industry body representatives also said that the insurance distribution sector, which employs over 83 Lakh people, could see the loss of up to 10 Lakh jobs lost as a result of the economic impact of the proposed policies.
This comes days after IRDAI proposed reintroducing product-wise commission caps for insurance distributors. The regulator also proposed tighter limits on insurers’ overall expenses over concerns related to disproportionate increases in commissions paid to distributors.
The industry body has also sought an extension of the deadline to submit feedback on the proposed norms to December-end from October 25 currently.
While noting that the association supports the regulator’s goal of making insurance more affordable and accessible, the IBAI representatives noted that the proposed sweeping changes threaten small businesses and MSMEs.
The resulting job losses could impact insurance awareness, policy renewals, assistance to policyholders, and penetration of insurance among underserved communities, the representatives added.
The brokers also countered IRDAI’s data that showed that general insurance premiums sourced through brokers had risen 37% whereas commission payouts zoomed 173% between FY23 and FY27. The industry body argued that the rise in commissions since FY23 largely reflected the reclassification of off-book marketing expenses following regularisation, and did not reflect inflationary pressures on insurance consumers.
The IBAI also claimed that the entire general insurance industry’s operating expenses averaged around 26.5% of gross premiums as against the mandated limit of 30%. Making its point, the representatives also claimed that policyholders received back ₹84.4 in non-life insurance claim payouts for every ₹100 of premium paid over a five-year period.
This is more than the global average of 72-75%, demonstrating the efficiency of the market in delivering value, the body’s representatives claimed.
The industry body said it was ready to work with IRDAI to address specific market anomalies, such as misselling or disproportionate remuneration. It has also submitted formal letters to the Prime Minister’s Office and the Finance Ministry on the matter.
Notably, the pushback comes as insurtech platforms continue to be up in arms against the proposed norms. Last week, Sanjib Jha, founder of insurtech startup Coverfox, said that the proposal could impact the viability of distributing insurance to rural and low-income borrowers.
Pune-based insurance broker Quickinsure has also trimmed more than 100 jobs in response to the proposal as its founder Anand Shrikhande projected that the industry would see more than 1 Lakh jobs affected due to the changing economics.
The news has also triggered a major sell-off in listed insurtech majors PB Fintech, which operates Policybazaar, and Turtlemint over fears that the IRDAI’s new policies would dent their core businesses.

items.author: Press Release
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
vivo today officially introduces the vivo Y32 in Pakistan, a highly anticipated smartphone designed for users with long, demanding days. Designed for young professionals, mobile workers, and anyone who needs a device that can keep going, the Y32 debuts with a clear and powerful promise: to deliver all-day power without compromise. By combining a massive 8000 mAh All-Day Battery with an expressive design and practical durability, the newest addition to the Y series is engineered to be a reliable partner for work and life, ready to help users power through their day.
Power that Lasts, Today and for Years to Come
At the heart of the vivo Y32 story is its extraordinary battery endurance, built to eliminate power anxiety from morning until night. For a delivery rider navigating the city, a contractor at a job site, or a professional moving between meetings, a dead battery means a disruption to their work. The vivo Y32 solves this with its massive 8000 mAh All-Day Battery, a power cell designed to support the most demanding schedules with fewer charging interruptions. Users can finally enjoy the freedom to use navigation for hours, stay in constant communication with clients, and still have enough power for entertainment on the commute home. It is truly a ‘’Business Never Stops’’ experience.
To put this capacity into perspective, a single charge can comfortably support an uninterrupted daily routine. Imagine waking up at dawn, running GPS turn-by-turn navigation, handling continuous client correspondence, taking real-time product photos, and streaming music in the background; all these can be done without battery anxiety. In a 12-hour mixed-use scenario, the Y32 finished with 20% battery remaining, leaving power for whatever comes next.
But true power is not just about a single day’s charge; it is about long-term reliability. The Y32 is built for the long run with its 6-Year Battery Health. Under vivo’s laboratory testing, the battery is engineered to retain at least 80% of its health after 1,500 complete charging cycles. Based on a full charge every 1.5 days, this is equivalent to approximately six years of reliable performance, ensuring the phone feels as dependable on day one as it does years later. The powerful battery can deliver stable performance even under extreme temperature conditions. Rigorous lab tests also show that Y32 can stand by for 4 hours at -20°C and can maintain storage function for 24 hours at -40°C, helping users brave through temperature challenges.
This long-term reliability is supported by a Smart Charging Engine that learns user habits to reduce unnecessary battery wear, and Overnight Charging Protection that intelligently completes charging before wake-up time. For those moments when a quick top-up is needed, 44W FlashCharge offers a fast and practical way to recharge during a short break, getting you back to your day without long delays.
A Design that Stands Out and Is Ready for Business
The Y32’s design ensures it remains a sophisticated and highly professional companion for any setting. The device moves beyond mere utility, presenting an expressive and sleek physical identity that serves as an elegant social business card for client meetings and formal occasions alike.
This premium look and feel is anchored by the Premium Metallic Camera Design, which provides a strong, modern visual signature for the rear of the phone. Rather than treating the camera as a purely functional element, vivo has elevated the module with a meticulously crafted metallic grain texture and precise detailing, transforming the camera area into a focal point of refined craftsmanship. This structural sophistication is further enhanced by Dynamic Light, which balances the entire camera design. It not only provides real-time, at-a-glance notifications for calls, messages, and key alerts, but also offers different colored light flashes with dynamic effects, bringing the phone to life and reflecting consumers’ style and mood.
Durability Built for the Unexpected Moments
The vivo Y32 is built to handle the realities of a busy workday. It features IP68 & IP69 Dust and Water Resistance, providing extra protection against demanding environments. Whether you are caught in a sudden downpour on your commute or working in a dusty outdoor environment, you can have confidence that your device is built to brave the elements.
This is reinforced with Anti-Drop Armor Design, which provides another layer of protection against the accidental bumps, knocks, and drops that can happen in real life. Backed by an SGS 5-Star Premium Performance Mark for Overall Unit Drop Resistance, the Y32 is designed to be resilient without the bulky look of a rugged phone. It is a device that looks expressive and fashionable while being better prepared for the small accidents of a demanding day.
Availability
The vivo Y32 will soon be officially available for purchase in Pakistan soon. The device will be offered in three colors: Twilight Red, Sunset Orange and Meteor White. To suit different storage and multitasking needs, the Y32 comes in (6GB+128GB) and (6GB+256GB) memory variants, priced at PKR 82,999 and PKR 99,999, respectively. Reddit user u/leftyhyzer16 on the subreddit r/iPhoneDuo posted a picture of his new iPhone Duo, which had developed a crack on its foldable screen right in the middle of the display, where the crease is. Along with the crack, the display of his unit has seemingly also developed a green line of pixels running vertically and another band running horizontally. iFixit, in his iPhone Duo teardown video and blog post, called Apple’s foldable the most repairable foldable, while highlighting that it has a “huge screen problem”. iFixit writes that the issue could possibly be because the support bar in the middle failed to retract properly in specific cases, which put pressure on the flexible screen of the iPhone Duo, causing the cracks. The second theory says that the curved rails of the hinge could be causing the screen to break.

items.title: What Silicon Valley playbooks get wrong about African markets
items.summary:
