items.author: Shakeel Ahmad Ramay
items.content:
Europe is once again experiencing a series of protests. Several countries are already seeing them, including France, Portugal, Italy and Spain. France is experiencing the worst of the current wave. Protesters are burning property and looting shops, malls and anything in their path. They are confronting police and law enforcement agencies. France has had to deploy the army in major cities to control the unrest.
Italian protesters are following suit and have started looting shops and malls. The circle is expanding, with Belgium now also affected, and there is fear other countries could follow. The question is why countries are falling into protests one after another, and what drives them. A common reason is the rising, unbearable cost of living and the weakening of public welfare and service institutions. In France, protests began with students unhappy with the education system. They complained about school facilities, teacher availability and university fee structures. Other groups joined them, citing the rising cost of living. People in Spain are agitating over rising housing prices and other essentials. Italians are protesting over similar issues. The causes are the same across Europe.
Cost-of-living issues and the delivery of services such as education are rooted in Europe's economic and social system. It is unfortunate that poverty and social exclusion have worsened over the years. Let us try to understand this using European Union (EU) data. Figures for 2025 show that almost 21% of the EU population is at risk of poverty or social exclusion. This means 92.7 million people are at risk. The worst part is that 19.3 million children are at risk, which puts the EU's future at stake.
It is shocking that major economies also have high poverty risk, including Spain at 25.7%, Germany at 21.2%, Italy at 22.6% and France at 20.8%. Some experts believe the data is manipulated and the actual numbers may be higher. Ongoing violent protests and rising numbers point to this dimension. Inequality is another problem that haunts the EU over time. These indicators are disturbing, especially when the EU claims the best governance, political and economic system in the world. It claims that the economic model, capitalism, has helped the West achieve high economic growth and development. A thorough look at the history of rapid growth highlights two disturbing facts.
First, the system presented and advocated as the best in human history is responsible for the current mess. A deep dive into the liberal economic model indicates certain flaws. One, it recognises that it will create losers and winners. Losers would be compensated and winners would pay to compensate them. Thus the state, with experts, devised tools such as taxes and built institutions to implement them. This would not be possible without a strong state role. Unfortunately, the role of the state was weakened over time in the name of the free market. Powerful business groups acquired more space in decision-making and in setting the rules. They also exploited liberal democracy to occupy the driving seat by funding candidates and parties. As a result, the state continued to lower taxes for corporations and raise them on ordinary citizens.
Two, Riba is the main reason for the failure of the liberal economic model. It favours the winners and undermines the losers. It discourages investment in productive sectors and encourages wealth accumulation. The capitalist financial system offers lucrative opportunities to accumulate money, and seems attractive because wealth can be created with little effort. This creates many problems. For example, less investment in productive sectors leads to fewer jobs, which increases unemployment, poverty and suffering. Three, there is no system for redistributing wealth and resources. Tax or corporate social responsibility systems contribute little to compensating the losers. This creates the illusion of competition without building mechanisms to protect the losers.
Second, the current situation dispels the myth that the liberal economic system ensures rapid growth and development. It has revived debate about colonisation's role in Europe's growth, including how European countries exploited weak but resource-rich countries. Europe did not hesitate to commit crimes against humanity and genocide to fulfil its economic agenda. After the old colonial system collapsed, Europe, with the United States, invented the Bretton Woods institutions to continue exploitation. However, the new system is also in decay. Therefore, Europe cannot solve its problems.
In this context, Europe needs a new economic system if it wants to solve its problems and end agitation. Europe can explore two options. First, the Islamic economic system offers answers to all of Europe's questions and problems. It has a sophisticated system to ensure wealth redistribution through Zakat. It encourages investment in productive means by forbidding Riba. The whole system revolves around people's welfare and the betterment of society. It prohibits exploitative profits and keeps people's needs first. However, Europe does not believe in Islam. Moreover, the Islamic model is unfortunately not in practice anywhere in the world. So Europe can pursue a second option.
The second option is the Chinese economic model. It centres on people's welfare. It has all the ingredients of modern economies, including a free market, openness and competition. However, the state does not leave the economy to the invisible hand. Rather, the state plays a prominent role in protecting common people's interests without compromising growth goals. As a result, China has grown exponentially, eliminated poverty and ensured the welfare of its people.
Unfortunately, instead of learning from the Chinese model, the EU declared China an ideological rival and is doing everything it can to undermine it. However, it is encouraging that many European experts and ordinary citizens are discussing the Chinese model and want to learn from it to tackle European problems. Therefore, many people think now may be the time for the Red Star to shine over Europe. However, we have to wait for the final conclusion, as the liberal order's actors and beneficiaries will fight back to sustain this order and keep extracting benefits. They need to understand that no system can sustain itself without meeting people's basic needs. Thus, if they want to sustain it and revive its glory, they must listen to and care for people's needs. Otherwise, nothing can help them, and the system will continue to decay, leading to its collapse.
THE WRITER IS A POLITICAL ECONOMIST AND A VISITING RESEARCH FELLOW AT HEBEI UNIVERSITY, CHINA

items.author: AAH Soomro
items.content:
Ask Pakistan's business community about the economy and relief often outweighs confidence. Memories of punishing inflation and currency instability remain fresh, while global wars, energy shocks and domestic political uncertainty cloud investment decisions. Against this backdrop, the push for affordable housing offers a welcome bright spot: an opportunity to generate employment, revive industry and help families acquire their first meaningful asset.
Housing combines economic opportunity with a basic human need. The State Bank cites an estimated shortage of 10 million homes, concentrated among lower- and middle-income households. At an October planning review, annual demand was estimated at 700,000 units against supply of approximately 250,000. These estimates are imperfect, but the direction is unmistakable: Pakistan continues to add to an already substantial housing deficit. For a working family, home ownership can offer protection from rising rents, greater financial security and an asset to pass to the next generation. Its social value extends to children's stability, privacy and dignity. Affordable housing policy therefore deserves to be judged by how widely it distributes these benefits.
The federal government's Apna Ghar programme provides financing of up to Rs10 million at a fixed customer rate of 5% for the first 10 years with Rs66,000 monthly installment only. The advertised repayment period extends to 30 years, with market-linked pricing after 10 years. Eligible properties include houses up to 10 marla (2,700 square feet) and flats up to 1,500 square feet. This represents meaningful support for households otherwise priced out of mortgage finance.
Demand is encouraging. The programme's dashboard reported approximately 191,900 applications and 75,200 approvals as of October 9. An earlier October review reported Rs426 billion in approvals and Rs76 billion in disbursements, alongside a Rs700 billion financing target covering 125,000 homes. The gap matters: only about 18% of the approved amount had reached borrowers. Converting approvals into completed transactions is now the critical delivery challenge.
Punjab offers a complementary approach through Apni Chhat Apna Ghar. Its construction loan component provides up to Rs1.5 million interest-free, with the provincial government requiring repayment over nine years at approximately Rs14,000 monthly. It serves eligible owners of small plots – up to five marla in urban areas and 10 marla in rural areas – who need financing to build. This can reach households requiring a modest construction loan, although families without land still need a separate solution.
The economic benefits extend well beyond property transactions. The Pakistan Economic Survey 2025-26 estimated construction's direct contribution at 2.35% of GDP, with growth of 5.73%. Large-scale manufacturing, separately accounting for 8.17% of GDP, grew 6.11%. Construction creates demand across several manufacturing industries; their contribution should not be confused with, or mechanically added to, construction's direct share. Some cite 19% YoY growth in construction sector in Q1 of FY27.
Demand travels through the economy in stages: cement, steel and aggregates first; cables, pipes, glass and tiles next; paints, furniture and appliances as homes approach completion. Alongside factories, masons, electricians, plumbers, transporters and small retailers benefit. The finance ministry reported that domestic cement dispatches increased 7-8% during 1QFY27. This indicates improving construction demand, although the increase cannot be attributed entirely to subsidised mortgages.
The fiscal connection is also substantial. FBR recorded approximately Rs108.7 billion in domestic sales tax collection from cement alone in FY2025, excluding its other tax contributions. Higher formal production can expand sales, excise and income tax receipts across the supply chain. However, additional revenues must be weighed against subsidy costs; housing finance should not be assumed to pay for itself automatically. International experience provides useful lessons. India's PMAY-U 2.0 combines construction assistance, affordable rental housing and interest subsidies; eligible borrowers receive a 4% subsidy on the first INR800,000 of their loan, subject to programme limits. Indonesia's FLPP offers subsidised mortgages at 5%, with down payments starting at 1%, and explicitly includes informal-income workers. The lesson is to combine affordable credit with housing supply and inclusive eligibility.
Pakistan's central challenge is access. A salaried employee can produce payslips; a tailor, driver or electrician with comparable earnings may struggle to prove repayment capacity. SBP's August regulations already require banks to use applicable informal-income assessment models and recognise evidence such as rent payments and utility bills. They also permit general mortgage tenors of up to 30 years and a debt burden ceiling of 65%. These broader limits should not be mistaken for automatic scheme eligibility, or comfortable household affordability.
The next phase should therefore prioritise implementation and fairness. Banks should assess verified cash flows, rent payment histories and digital receipts, allow suitable co-borrowers and offer repayment schedules matching irregular earnings. Carefully capped guarantees can support deserving borrowers, while grants, incremental construction and affordable rentals are needed for families unable to sustain a mortgage.
Supply must expand alongside credit. Faster approvals, reliable land titles, serviced plots and affordable apartments near employment centres would help prevent subsidies from being absorbed into higher selling prices. Financing an existing home changes ownership; financing additional construction creates new housing supply and a stronger industrial stimulus.
Borrowers also need transparent legal, valuation and insurance charges, enforceable processing deadlines and effective complaint channels. Affordability assessments should preserve money for food, education and healthcare and explain potential instalment increases after the subsidy expires. Recovery must follow lawful procedures, with restructuring options for genuine hardship. Finally, publish outcomes by income, gender, district and employment type, alongside disbursements, completed homes, defaults and subsidy costs. Any increase in loan limits should follow evidence that lower-income applicants are being served adequately. Perhaps it is time for assisting with the down payments also at a slightly higher mark-up as "Help to Buy" scheme in the UK.
Amid global conflict and economic uncertainty, housing finance is a promising policy success taking shape. Its lasting achievement should be measured in secure homes, productive jobs and broader ownership of wealth. The strongest endorsement will come when workers building Pakistan's homes can afford homes of their own.
The writer is an independent economic analyst

items.author: Liam Anderson
items.content:
Being Mozambican is a matter of belonging — regardless of one’s origin, appearance, or surname
Originally published on Global Voices
Indians in Mozambique celebrating the Hindu festival of Navratri. Image by Kash_if via Flickr. CC BY 2.0.
In Mozambique, the word monhé has a much deeper history than its everyday use might suggest. Depending on who says it and the context, it can simply be a reference to the population of Indian origin, an identity marker, or a prejudiced remark. But behind the word there is a history of migration, trade, colonialism, independence, displacement, and, above all, belonging.
The question of who is Mozambican gets particularly interesting when we look at the communities of Indian origin, who have lived in the country for several generations. Are they Mozambicans? Indians? Foreigners? Or, in some cases, stateless persons? The answer cannot be found in appearance, surname, religion, or family origin alone. It is found in the country’s history and, particularly, in its nationality law.
A presence older than modern borders
The presence of people originating from the Indian subcontinent in the lands we now call Mozambique predates the country’s independence and, in many instances, predates the demarcation of the current political borders. The Indian Ocean’s trade networks connected the East African coast to South Asia long before 1975, the year Mozambique gained its independence. Over time, merchants, families, and whole communities settled in different parts of the country.
During the Portuguese colonial period, this took place within a political structure that gave people nationalities and legal statuses according to the rules of the empire. As such, “being of Indian origin” never meant automatically “being an Indian citizen.” A person can have Indian ancestry and at the same time hold Portuguese, Indian, Pakistani, or any other nationality, which could leave people in a complex bureaucratic situation. This distinction became especially important when the empire came to an end.
1975: When the question “Whose country is this?” took on a new meaning
Mozambique’s independence, made official on June 25th, 1975, did not just mean a transfer of political power. It also implied the need to define who would legally receive the new state, which was known as the New State. The Nationality Law of 1975 was key to answering that question. Among its provisions were rules that recognized as Mozambicans certain people born in the territory and resident in Mozambique at the time of independence, as well as other criteria related to birth, family links, and residence. The legislation would thus transform a heterogeneous imperial population into a national political community.
For many families of Indian origin who lived in Mozambique for decades or generations, this transformation would mean a fundamental change: no longer being legally associated with a colonial power or a foreign nationality and becoming part of the new Mozambican nation. But the experience of this transition was not the same for everybody.
When identity doesn’t fit neatly into a passport
Decolonization created situations where identity, origin, and nationality did not match. Imagine a family history across three generations: the grandparents born in India, the parents born in Mozambique during the colonial period, and the children born after independence. Which nationality should each generation have? The answer may depend on specific legal circumstances: place of birth, the parents’ nationality, residence in Mozambique at its independence, existing documentation, and any decisions to opt for or relinquish nationality.
Here, the issue of statelessness arises. A stateless person is somebody who is not considered a national by any state’s legislation. It is not an ambiguous cultural identity or feeling divided between two countries, but a legal status.
After decolonization, some people in former colonial territories, such as Angola and Mozambique, faced this problem: some were no longer recognized as nationals by the former colonial power without any other nationalities automatically being granted. This does not mean, though, that the whole Indian community in Mozambique became stateless. This generalization would be historically and legally incorrect.
‘Monhé’ is not a nationality
This may be where everyday language misleads us. The term “Monhé” may be used as an identity category, but it is not a legal category. Somebody called a monhé can be as Mozambican as anybody else born or naturalized in the country. They may have been born in Maputo, Nampula, Beira, or Quelimane, speak Portuguese or another Mozambican language, have had family in Mozambique for several generations, and never have lived in India. Your ancestry does not disqualify your citizenship.
Likewise, a person of Indian origin living in Mozambique can be a citizen of another country. And, in certain cases, they may have difficulties in proving or acquiring a nationality. As such, it is important to distinguish three concepts that are often confused: origin, nationality, and citizenship. A person’s origin may be Indian. Their identity can be simultaneously Mozambican and Indian. Nationality, though, is a legal relationship between an individual and a state.
A community across oceans
The history of so-called monhés in Mozambican identity also challenges an overly simplistic view of nationality.
Mozambique has always been a space where people cross paths. Africans, Arabs, Indians, Portuguese, and other peoples participated, at different moments, in the country’s social, economic, and cultural development. The Mozambican coast, in particular, cannot be understood without movements across the Indian Ocean.
This is why it may be inappropriate to think of the Indian diaspora as forever an “outsider” population. For many of these families, Mozambique is not simply the country where they live. It is the country where they were born, where their parents were born, where their ancestors are buried, and where they built their lives. India may be their family origin. Mozambique is, for many, a homeland.
The ongoing question
Around half a century after independence, the question of nationality continues to be more than a matter of just documents. It is a question of recognition. Who has the right to say “I am Mozambican”? Is it enough to have been born in the country? Have Mozambican parents? Have lived in the country for decades? Participate in society? Speak its languages? Share a collective memory? Or will some people continue to be seen as foreigners by many, despite legally being citizens? It is in this space between the law and general perception that many identities exist.
This evokes the concept of a “bridge” — Mozambique’s Indian-origin community historically finds itself between different spaces: Africa and Asia, family tradition and national identity, migratory memory and territorial belonging. But being between two shores does not necessarily mean not belonging to either. Sometimes it means belonging to both. And, for some, it means discovering that their family history crossed oceans long before modern passports decided which country a person belonged to.
The history of Mozambique’s monhés is thus also a history about the very meaning of being Mozambican. Not a story of people who simply “came from outside,” but a story of people who, over generations, helped build the country, while continuing to negotiate, within their families and wider society the fundamental question that follows all those who migrate: where, in the end, is home?
Written (Português) by Tirso Sitoe

Pakistan plans to set up around 3,000 public electric vehicle (EV) charging stations across the country by 2030, the Ministry of Industries and Production has said.
The ministry shared the target in a written reply to the National Assembly. It was responding to a question from lawmaker Malik Shakir Bashir Awan.
Fast Chargers on Motorways First
According to the ministry, the New Energy Vehicle (NEV) Policy 2025-30 envisions an initial phase of 40 fast-charging stations. These will be installed along motorways and selected sections of the National Highway (N-5).
Charging points are planned at intervals of about 50 kilometers on major highways to support the growth of electric transport. Some of this work is already visible, as a major motorway recently got ultrafast EV charging stations.
Fuel Stations and Battery Swapping
Under the policy, fuel stations will be encouraged to install EV charging units. The government also plans to expand fast-charging, Level 2, and Level 1 facilities.
Battery-swapping stations are also planned for electric two-wheelers and three-wheelers.
Incentives for Private Investors
To attract private investment, the government is offering a dedicated commercial electricity tariff for charging stations and faster electricity connections.
Public-private partnerships, including viability gap funding arrangements, are also part of the plan. Last year, 3,800 investors showed interest in setting up EV charging stations across Pakistan.
Recycling Old EV Batteries
The policy also covers the collection, transportation, reuse, dismantling, and recycling of end-of-life EV batteries, particularly lithium-ion batteries.
The ministry said work is underway on a regulatory framework and a nationwide network of battery collection and recycling facilities.
Source: ARY News

items.content:
Punjab’s first modern film city will be inaugurated on December 15, as preparations for its launch have been completed.
The update came on Sunday during the first meeting of the Punjab Film Authority, chaired by Senior Minister Marriyum Aurangzeb. The meeting approved several key decisions aimed at reviving the local film industry, promoting modern filmmaking, and restoring Lahore’s position as the country’s cinematic hub.
First Royalty Law for Artists
Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz has approved the drafting of Pakistan’s first royalty law for artists. She directed that the proposed legislation be presented at the next meeting of the Film Authority.
The meeting also approved the setting up of a film and music school, a film trading house, a post-production facility, and a studio complex with modern soundstages. Pakistan’s largest convention center will also be built in Punjab.
The film city was first announced by Maryam Nawaz in April as an integrated media production hub in Lahore.
Rebate Framework and Online Platform
Marriyum Aurangzeb directed officials to present a film rebate framework at next week’s meeting. She said the rebate policy would give financial support to filmmakers and help improve production quality.
A single-window online platform will also be launched to help filmmakers choose suitable shooting locations.
Budget and Hiring
A proposed budget of Rs. 589 million for the Film City Authority was sent to the finance committee for review.
The authority also approved hiring 26 people against 53 vacant posts in the first phase. The board will hold hiring and firing powers within the Film City Authority.
The meeting also reviewed progress on forming the Punjab Film Fund Committee and setting up six specialized sub-committees.
Old Cinemas to Be Restored
The meeting approved plans to restore old cinema halls, equip them with solar power systems, and introduce online ticketing. Capacity-building training programs for young filmmakers, conducted by international experts, will also be launched.
The move follows the Punjab government’s plan to launch a one dollar cinema project.
Marriyum Aurangzeb said Maryam Nawaz aims to turn Punjab into an international hub for screen tourism within five years. She added that the initiative would showcase the province’s rich culture and heritage on the global stage.
Source: ARY News

items.content:
An audit has found irregularities and losses worth Rs. 18.46 billion in the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Economic Zones Development and Management Company (KPEZDMC) during the fiscal year 2024-25.
According to the Auditor General of Pakistan’s report, the losses to the public exchequer were caused by poor planning, weak management, and financial irregularities at the company.
Lease Money Not Recovered Despite Court Orders
The report said the company failed to recover Rs. 2.08 billion in lease payments from industrial owners for allotted land, even though court orders were in place.
It also failed to renew agreements for commercial land, which caused a loss of Rs. 629.8 million to the exchequer.
Land Issues in Buner, Mohmand, Jalozai, and Haripur
The auditors found that the company did not get land vacated in Buner, Mohmand, and Jalozai, resulting in a loss of Rs. 1.08 billion. Another Rs. 174.1 million was lost because commercial land was illegally allotted for industrial use.
In Haripur, plots 185, 186, 187, and 190, spread over 10 acres, were allotted to Al-Hadeed Engineering. However, the payment was not collected, which caused a loss of Rs. 497.8 million.
The findings come days after another audit found Rs. 16.94 billion in irregularities in the KP Minerals Department.
Liabilities Threaten Company’s Future
According to the report, the company’s contingent liabilities have reached Rs. 14 billion, which poses a serious risk to the continuity of its business operations.
The report raised questions about the company’s governance, land allotments, recovery of dues, and financial affairs. It said poor administrative decisions and alleged steps to benefit favored individuals caused serious damage to public resources.
KPEZDMC manages the province’s economic zones, including the Rashakai Economic Zone.

items.title: Japan to simulate cyberattacks as PHP flaws roil global internet
items.summary:
Japan said on Friday ​it would set up a team to simulate cyberattacks using AI to identify weaknesses in technology systems as ‌organisations scramble to curtail risks from flaws in the PHP programming language that underpins much of the internet.
Government and company websites across the world went offline this week after the disclosure of critical vulnerabilities in the widely used programming language prompted millions of hacking attempts, forcing website operators to rush to protect ​or temporarily shut down their systems.
Highlighting the extent of the disruption, Japan's third-largest mobile carrier, SoftBank, said on Friday ​it was suspending its emergency alert system for mobile users.

Japan said on Friday ​it would set up a team to simulate cyberattacks using AI to identify weaknesses in technology systems as ‌organisations scramble to curtail risks from flaws in the PHP programming language that underpins much of the internet.
Government and company websites across the world went offline this week after the disclosure of critical vulnerabilities in the widely used programming language prompted millions of hacking attempts, forcing website operators to rush to protect ​or temporarily shut down their systems.
Highlighting the extent of the disruption, Japan's third-largest mobile carrier, SoftBank, said on Friday ​it was suspending its emergency alert system for mobile users.
Read: Data of over 10M customers exposed in cyberattacks on Japanese firms
Japan is setting up a team to simulate cyberattacks as it scrambles to identify security weaknesses in systems that rely on PHP. https://t.co/9fkwdtPbH3
— The Japan Times (@japantimes) October 24, 2026
That means customers would not receive early warnings ⁠for earthquakes, tsunami alerts or disaster and evacuation information as the system undergoes maintenance to address a PHP vulnerability, SoftBank said.
Japan ​is regularly affected by natural disasters and is one of the world's most earthquake-prone countries, with typhoon Champi currently approaching the southernmost prefecture ​of Okinawa.
SoftBank, which has more than 30 million smartphone customers, said users could still receive earthquake warnings through services such as an app from its Yahoo business.
"An attack can succeed by getting through just one hole ... for that reason it's important we shift our mindset and think from the perspective of ​the attacker," Japanese industry minister Ryosei Akazawa said on Friday.
"Defenders also need to make use of AI and respond proactively, staying ​one step ahead."
Nobuo Miwa, president of Tokyo-based cybersecurity firm S&J Corp, said the government response was too slow.
"This is like trying to take on a ‌bomber ⁠with a bamboo spear," he said.
Emergency shutdowns this week from Tokyo to Helsinki of banking, airline, rail, tax and government services marked one of the most dramatic tests of the decades-old programming tools that keep the web running.
Companies including brokerage Nomura, lender Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group, airline ANA and East Japan Railway (JR East) temporarily suspended some internet services as part of emergency measures.
Japan's Ministry of Finance, National Tax ​Agency and Meteorological Agency also ​suspended some online services.
On Friday, ⁠JR East said some group services had resumed while others would be restored once confirmed safe. Nippon Paint said it had applied a security patch as a precaution and its website is back ​online.
Attackers are likely targeting Japanese businesses for their thorough records, which are no longer protected by ​a language barrier ⁠because of AI, said Eva Chen, CEO of Trend Micro.
Read More: Japan passes 'Active cyber defense' taking effect from 2027
Japan has been too comfortable with its existing infrastructure, which it felt was safe enough, she said.
Cybersecurity experts have said AI is helping attackers automate tasks from scanning for software vulnerabilities to crafting phishing campaigns, making cybercrime faster, ⁠cheaper, and ​harder to detect.
The developers of PHP released fixes on Wednesday for vulnerabilities that had ​lurked in the software for years until they were uncovered using AI. They urged users to "update immediately".

items.content:
The discovery of two ​serious flaws in PHP this week set off a global scramble to ‌keep websites safe from hackers, showing just how critical the three-decade-old open-source programming language is to the internet.
Yet the nonprofit foundation that supports PHP, which may underpin up to 70% of sites globally, operates on ​a shoestring budget.
“We have one full-time staff member (that's me) and 14 mostly ​part-time contractors,” Executive Director Elizabeth Barron of the PHP Foundation said via ⁠email in an interview on Friday. Board members are unpaid volunteers, and funding ​comes from donations and grants.
Read: Millions of hacking attempts as companies, governments rush to patch PHP flaws
The foundation works with outside researchers and companies, including OpenAI ​and cybersecurity firms Wiz and Calif, to investigate security flaws and coordinate fixes, including Wednesday's patches.
While Web security company Cloudflare has reported millions of hacking attempts, Barron said the foundation had no ​evidence hackers were able to exploit the vulnerabilities before they were disclosed, or ​on sites that have been patched.
"We received no further indication from OpenAI, Wiz or Calif, with ‌whom ⁠we're working closely on this issue, regarding any issues on patched systems,” she said.
Artificial intelligence has proved both a help and a burden to the foundation. It helped researchers find the flaws, which had been present for a decade, and Barron ​said it made programmers ​more efficient.
However, it ⁠is also increasing maintainers' workloads. The PHP project is receiving nearly twice as many proposed code changes as a year ago, “yet ​the number of contributors hasn't doubled,” she said. Reviewing contributions ​and bug ⁠reports requires “a massive amount of human input and experience.”
Read More: Government websites in Europe, elsewhere go dark as software flaw sparks security scramble
Recent events have shown how heavily companies and governments rely on PHP, Barron said.
“Given that reliance, it is clear that PHP ⁠is incredibly underfunded.”

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
US stock investors face a pivotal week, with corporate earnings reports led by major AI players and a ​Federal Reserve meeting posing critical tests for a suddenly shaky market rally.
Weakness in technology shares left investors on edge about the state of the AI trade that ‌has driven the US equity bull market that just marked its fourth anniversary.
The Nasdaq Composite posted a slim loss on Friday, a day after the tech-heavy index suffered its biggest daily drop since June. Investors were disappointed by quarterly reports from Meta and Lam Research. Meta is one of the hyperscalers spending massively to build out data centres, while Lam is a high-flying semiconductor company, one of a group that has been among the biggest ​AI stock winners.
Read: Among AI crowd, some investors position for slower hyperscaler spending growth
Three other hyperscalers, Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon, headline a packed week of quarterly results, including about one-third of S&P 500 companies. The Fed's interest rate policy meeting ​on Wednesday also could rattle markets.
"There are a lot of balls in the air," said Nick Giorgi, chief equity strategist at Alpine Macro.
"Next week, ⁠you have a lot more tech earnings, and right now the market is taking a discerning eye as it relates to all the spending that goes along with artificial intelligence," Giorgi ​said. "The market's just not giving the benefit of the doubt to companies that are spending a ton of money on building this all out, which to us is actually very healthy, but still ​does augur for some short-term pain."
Investors also have their focus trained on the US midterm elections on November 3, with growing bets that the Democrats will wrest control of the US Congress away from President Donald Trump's Republican party. The series of market catalysts could ratchet up volatility over the next couple of weeks and challenge optimism that has helped lift the benchmark S&P 500 index up 11% in 2026.
Hyperscalers on the hot seat
Robust US ​profit growth has underpinned the stock market's gains this year in the face of headwinds including spiking Treasury yields and rising energy costs stemming from the Middle East conflict.
With more than ​100 companies having posted results so far, third-quarter S&P 500 earnings are on pace to have climbed more than 32% from a year ago, according to LSEG IBES data. Next week is the busiest of the ‌reporting season.
"I ⁠think earnings will determine whether this ... tech pullback is a buying opportunity, or is there a deeper correction ahead," said King Lip, chief strategist at BakerAvenue Wealth Management. "What we need is just another round of really strong earnings."
Alphabet and Microsoft report on Wednesday. Amazon's results are due on Thursday. Focus will be on the guidance the companies give on capital spending plans and whether they are seeing returns on the massive outlays.
Capital spending from hyperscalers, expected to be around $800 billion this year, is boosting the bottom lines for a wide swath of companies involved in the AI buildout. But ​investors are wary of the sustainability of such ​spending amid mounting financing costs.
"Earnings are critical ⁠to the overall confidence level of the AI trade and how much longer the spend will continue," said Kevin Mahn, president and chief investment officer at Hennion & Walsh Asset Management.
Fed expected to pause on rates, for now
Quarterly reports next week from chip companies Intel and Sandisk also could influence ​the AI trade.
Elsewhere, other high-profile companies set to report next week include drugmaker Eli Lilly, oil majors Exxon and Chevron and industrial equipment ​giant Caterpillar.
The prospect for ⁠more interest rate hikes also comes into focus with the Fed meeting. The Fed raised rates in September for the first time since 2023, in an effort to control above-target inflation, but Fed funds futures late on Friday suggested a less-than-10 % chance the Fed will hike again when it gives its policy statement on Wednesday, according to LSEG data.
One factor: Investors are dubious that the Fed will want to ⁠increase rates ​just a week before the midterm elections.
However, markets are leaning toward a hike at the next meeting in December, ​with futures suggesting a roughly 80% probability of such a move then.
Walter Todd, chief investment officer at Greenwood Capital, said he will be watching for any hints about the rate path at Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's press conference following the decision.
"Does he ​say something to give an idea about December, because right now the expectation is there is going to be a hike," Todd said.

items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Mobile users in Pakistan sometimes notice unexpected deductions from their prepaid balance without making calls or sending messages. These balance deductions may occur because of Value Added Services (VAS) subscriptions that charge users for additional mobile services.
The Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) has shared awareness guidelines to help subscribers check their active VAS subscriptions and deactivate services they no longer need. The regulator has also provided USSD codes for customers of Jazz, Zong, Ufone, and Telenor.
What Are VAS Services? How to Stop Unwanted Mobile Balance Deductions
Value Added Services, commonly known as VAS, are additional services offered by mobile operators beyond standard calls, SMS, and internet packages. These services may include news alerts, entertainment content, caller tunes, games, and other subscription-based offerings.
Some VAS services charge users daily, weekly, or monthly. As a result, customers may continue to lose mobile balance while a subscription remains active.
Users may activate these services intentionally or subscribe to them accidentally while browsing websites, clicking promotional links, or responding to service messages. Checking active subscriptions regularly can help prevent unnecessary charges.
PTA has shared the following USSD codes to help mobile subscribers manage their VAS subscriptions.
Mobile Network
USSD Code
Jazz
*6611#
Zong
*6611#
Ufone
*6869#
Telenor
*4444#
To get started, dial the relevant code from the SIM on which you are experiencing balance deductions. Follow the instructions displayed on your phone to check or deactivate unwanted services.
The available options may vary by operator and service. If a code does not work or does not show the subscription you want to cancel, contact your mobile operator’s helpline and ask for details of your active VAS services.
How to Complain About Unwanted Balance Deductions
If your mobile balance continues to decrease after you deactivate unwanted services, you can contact your network operator and register a complaint.
Ask the operator to identify the service responsible for the deductions and confirm whether the subscription has been cancelled. Keep the complaint reference number for future follow-ups.
If the operator fails to resolve the issue within the specified period, you can escalate the complaint through the PTA’s Complaint Management System (CMS).
Tips to Avoid Unnecessary Mobile Charges
Mobile users should regularly check their active subscriptions and cancel services they no longer use. They should also read promotional messages carefully and avoid clicking unfamiliar links that may lead to paid subscriptions.
Before activating any additional service, check its charges and renewal terms. If you notice unexpected deductions, contact your operator promptly to identify the reason.
By checking VAS subscriptions and using the available complaint channels, mobile users can better manage their balance and avoid paying for services they do not need.

The disagreement has slowed progress on the policy, which aims to establish a framework for the country’s automotive sector for the next five years. The two ministries have held several meetings to resolve their differences, but they have yet to reach an agreement.
Pakistan’s Auto Policy 2026-31 Faces Further Delay Over Import Duties
The main issue is the proposed tax structure for imported vehicle parts and its potential impact on local manufacturers. Both ministries have differing views on the tariff rates that should apply, making it difficult to finalise the policy.

Pakistan’s proposed Auto Policy 2026-31 has faced another delay as the Ministries of Commerce and Industries remain divided over import duties on locally assembled vehicles, auto parts, and New Energy Vehicles (NEVs).
The disagreement has slowed progress on the policy, which aims to establish a framework for the country’s automotive sector for the next five years. The two ministries have held several meetings to resolve their differences, but they have yet to reach an agreement.
Pakistan’s Auto Policy 2026-31 Faces Further Delay Over Import Duties
The main issue is the proposed tax structure for imported vehicle parts and its potential impact on local manufacturers. Both ministries have differing views on the tariff rates that should apply, making it difficult to finalise the policy.
The matter is now expected to be referred to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif for a final decision. His intervention could help resolve the dispute and allow the government to move forward with the proposed policy.
The new auto policy will set the direction for Pakistan’s automotive industry from 2026 to 2031. Its proposed measures cover locally assembled vehicles, imported components, and NEVs, a category that includes electric vehicles and other vehicles using alternative energy technologies.
Import duties are an important part of the policy because they can influence production costs, vehicle prices, and the competitiveness of local manufacturers. Changes in tariffs on imported parts could affect how much companies spend on assembling vehicles in Pakistan. The final structure will therefore be important for both automakers and consumers.
However, the government has not finalised the policy yet. It remains in draft form, and the proposed changes to import duties have not been implemented.
Until the ministries reach an agreement and the government approves the policy, the existing tariff arrangements will remain unaffected by the draft proposals. Further progress will depend on resolving the disagreement and finalising the government’s approach to duties on vehicles and automotive components.

items.author: APP
items.content:
The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) proposed 12 amendments to the 2023 codes of conduct for political parties, media organisations and election observers to curb the misuse of artificial intelligence (AI) during elections.
According to sources in the ECP, the draft amendments proposed five changes to the code of conduct for media organisations, five for political parties and candidates, and three for election observers.
The commission has sought public and stakeholder feedback on the proposed amendments by Nov 20, with the measures aimed at regulating AI-generated content, prohibiting deceptive deepfakes and ensuring transparency in election-related communication.
Read: AI able to manipulate elections worldwide, expert says
Under the proposed rules for media, outlets would be required to clearly disclose when content generated or modified through AI is broadcast, published or released.
The draft strictly prohibits the use of deepfake technology to create fabricated images, voices or statements of political party leaders, candidates, election officials, members of the judiciary, armed forces personnel and other state officials if the content is false, defamatory or intended to ridicule them.
Media organisations would be permitted to use AI tools for preparing, translating, presenting or analysing election-related content, provided they disclose such use to their audiences and remain responsible for the authenticity and accuracy of the material.
The Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority (PEMRA), the Social Media Protection and Regulatory Authority, and the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency would monitor undisclosed or unlabeled AI-generated media content and report violations to the ECP, with appropriate action to be taken in cases of non-compliance.
The proposed amendments also require media houses to promptly remove misleading or undisclosed AI-generated content from their platforms, or correctly relabel it, when directed by a regulatory body or the ECP.
For election observers, three amendments have been proposed, requiring them to remain vigilant for AI-related manipulation during the observation process and immediately report any such instances to the ECP.
The draft also bars observers from using AI to generate, alter or enhance their observations, factual findings, photographs, videos or reports submitted to the commission.
Five amendments have been proposed for political parties and candidates to regulate their use of AI-generated material during election campaigns.
Under the proposed provisions, political parties and candidates would not be allowed to create, publish, broadcast or distribute AI-generated or manipulated content, including deepfake images, videos and audio clips, without clearly labelling it as AI-generated.
The draft prohibits the use of AI-generated material intended to deceive voters by falsely portraying a person’s image, words or actions.
It also bars the creation of fabricated, ridiculing or defamatory images, voices or statements of political leaders, candidates, election officials, members of the judiciary, armed forces personnel and other state officials through deepfake technology.
Political parties and candidates would be required to preserve all AI-generated content produced during the election process.
The proposed rules further prohibit the use of AI-powered bots, automated accounts and similar tools to manipulate online engagement or create fake trends.
The use of AI for voter outreach through robocalls or voice-cloned messages would also be regulated, with a clear disclosure at the beginning of each call or message that the content has been generated through AI.
The proposed amendments aim to strengthen transparency and accountability in election campaigning and media coverage while addressing the risks posed by fabricated digital content and AI-driven voter manipulation.

items.title: Putin says accusations of Russia provoking European protests are ‘clear overkill’
items.author: Anadolu Agency
items.content:
Russian President Vladimir Putin called accusations that Russia was provoking mass protests in major European cities a “clear overkill.”
Speaking in an interview with the VGTRK broadcasting company published on Sunday, Putin said he was surprised that the initial reaction in Europe was not anti-Russian but anti-American.
“Claims immediately began to be thrown out that the events taking place in Europe are the result of the activities of the current American administration and its support for right-wing parties and movements,” he said.
Read: Kremlin dismisses allegations of Russia's involvement in Europe unrest
Putin said that was “strange and completely unexpected” to him, as he did not expect European leaders to attack “their main ally and protector, so to speak, in the military sense of the word, across the ocean.”
“But they quickly came to their senses and switched to their traditional accusations against the Russian Federation,” he said.
Blaming Russia for all mortal sins as is happening now, amidst the mass unrest in European countries, has become a standard practice for the West, Vladimir Putin told Vesti reporter Pavel Zarubin:https://t.co/zJnAK3SlsY pic.twitter.com/BkPionkaiz
— TASS (@tassagency_en) October 25, 2026
The president added: “There is nothing unexpected here. As is known, Russia has always been accused of all mortal sins. But now I am ready to respond.”
Putin said claims that Moscow was provoking mass demonstrations in major European cities are an obvious exaggeration even to ordinary citizens of European countries.
“My first reaction when I saw this was surprise, because to say that we are provoking mass protests in major European cities is a clear overkill, which, in my opinion, is obvious to ordinary citizens of European countries,” he noted.
“Nevertheless, they have now taken this well-trodden and worn-out path, and we see some accusations against Russia,” he added.
Putin said this points to “the weakness and inability of some leaders in European countries to take responsibility for what is happening.”
“This is bad. Why? Because it means they do not analyse the events, do not look for the causes of what is happening, but simply shift the blame onto someone, first the US, now Russia,” he said.
Nationwide student protests have been underway in France for several weeks.
Read More: France deploys 70,000 police to try to contain nationwide protests
French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot, speaking at an OECD-hosted conference on October 21, accused protesters of using “hostile narratives” from Russia, China, Iran and the MAGA community.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on October 19 that nobody takes such “absurd accusations” seriously. US President Donald Trump had blamed the unrest on mass migration.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Apple’s first foldable smartphone, the iPhone Duo, is facing early durability concerns after some buyers reported screen cracks along the hinge just hours after its public launch. Users have shared images online showing screen cracks and lines of dead pixels along the device’s folding area.
The reports have raised questions about the durability of Apple’s hinge mechanism and the long-term reliability of its first foldable phone. However, the number of reported cases remains unclear, and Apple has not issued an official statement about the problem.
iPhone Duo Owners Report Screen Cracks Along Hinge Shortly After Launch
According to complaints shared online, some iPhone Duo owners experienced screen damage after only a short period of use. One buyer in Australia claimed that the display broke after around six hours, despite opening the phone fewer than 20 times.
The user reportedly noticed an unusual movement beneath the screen while unfolding the device. A loud snapping sound followed, and the display developed a split along the crease. The owner said the phone showed no other visible signs of damage that would suggest a drop or physical misuse.
Similar images have also appeared online from users in China. However, it remains uncertain whether all the affected devices were purchased by customers or included store display units that may have experienced heavy handling.
The reported damage mainly appears around the central fold, with some images showing visible cracks while others display thick lines of dead pixels.
Apple Has Yet to Comment on the Reports
Early reviewers did not report similar screen failures during their initial testing. However, the limited number of review devices means these experiences may not reflect how the phone performs across a wider group of users.
Apple has not publicly addressed the complaints or confirmed whether the reported cases point to a manufacturing or design issue.
Some customers who took their damaged phones to Apple retail stores reportedly received replacement devices. The company may also examine returned units to identify the cause of the failures.
If further investigation reveals a widespread hardware defect, Apple could need to review its manufacturing process or make changes to the device’s design.
Screen Repairs Could Cost $999
The reported failures have also drawn attention to the potential cost of repairing the iPhone Duo’s foldable display. According to the report, replacing the internal screen outside the standard warranty could cost $999.
For buyers investing in Apple’s first foldable phone, such a high repair cost makes screen durability an important consideration.
The report states that early screen failures are covered by the standard iPhone warranty. Customers also have a 14-day return window if they decide the device does not meet their expectations, although applicable terms may vary by market.
Owners experiencing unusual sounds or visible changes around the hinge should contact Apple support or visit an authorised service provider rather than continuing to fold the device.
See Also: iPhone Duo Warranty in Pakistan: What Mercantile and GNext Offer
Early Durability Concerns Could Affect Apple’s Foldable Phone
Foldable smartphones place additional stress on their displays and hinges because users repeatedly open and close the devices. Manufacturers have faced durability challenges with these designs, particularly around the folding area.
The latest reports suggest that Apple could face similar challenges with its first foldable smartphone. However, it is too early to determine whether the reported failures are isolated incidents or signs of a broader problem.
How Apple investigates the damaged units and responds to affected customers could play an important role in building confidence in its foldable technology.
For now, prospective buyers may want to monitor further reports and wait for more information about the screen failures before making a purchase decision.

items.author: AFP
items.content:
Indian protesters angry over a proposed Himalayan mega-dam, intended to counter an upstream Chinese hydropower project, have clashed with police and torched buildings, officials said.
The violence in northeastern Arunachal Pradesh state erupted late on Friday during protests against the proposed 11,200-megawatt Siang Upper Multipurpose Project of state-run hydropower company NHPC, Chief Minister Pema Khandu told reporters on Saturday.
“The mob destroyed a lot of properties, police station, the NHPC office was vandalised, several elected representatives’ homes were ransacked,” Khandu told reporters.
Around 40 police personnel were injured by stones thrown by protesters, who also vandalised the NHPC’s offices. Police fired tear gas canisters to disperse the crowd.
Read: UN experts urge Indian authorities to cease 'use of excessive force' to curb protests
Khandu urged opponents of the project to engage with the government. “Question us, have dialogue with us, instead of violence,” Khandu said.
India says the proposed dam is needed to counter China’s $167-billion Yaxia project, a likely record-breaking hydropower scheme upstream in Tibet.
New Delhi fears the Chinese project could affect water flows downstream, and says the proposed Indian dam would create a vast reservoir to store water and help maintain flows into the Brahmaputra river. Beijing has said its project will have no “negative impact” downstream.
China claims Arunachal Pradesh as part of southern Tibet. India says the state is an integral part of its territory.
India’s proposed dam, which would be by far its largest hydropower project, has drawn fierce opposition from local communities who fear the loss of their homes and land.
Read More: Injuries in China's Tibet rise to 76 after earthquake, death toll remains at 16
The project underscores tensions between the two most populous countries, which share a disputed Himalayan border patrolled by tens of thousands of troops.
India’s foreign ministry said on Friday the two sides remained in regular contact to manage border tensions, after a top Indian border police official Shatrujeet Kapur reported “face offs” between Indian and Chinese forces.
“The situation in the India-China border areas gets disturbed from time to time when Chinese forces diverge from established patrolling patterns,” foreign ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal told reporters in New Delhi. “Both sides continue to use existing diplomatic and military mechanisms to resolve outstanding issues and avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation.”

items.author: Life And Style Desk
items.content:
The trial in the knife attack on Bollywood actor Saif Ali Khan began in Mumbai, with the first witness telling the court that the intruder had demanded INR10 million during a break-in at the actor’s Bandra residence in January 2025.
The nurse, who cared for Khan and Kareena Kapoor Khan’s younger son, Jeh, identified the accused, 31-year-old Mohammad Shariful Islam, during her testimony on Friday, according to Gulf News.
The nurse, who is the complainant in the case, has worked with the family for more than five years and was the first witness called to testify, the report said.
According to the The Indian Express, the nurse told the court a noise had woken her at around 2am on January 16, 2025. She initially noticed that the bathroom light was on and assumed Kareena was inside.
After waking again, she saw a man wearing a cap moving towards Jeh’s bed. The child was four years old at the time.
The nurse said she rushed towards the bed and attempted to pick up the child when the intruder attacked her with a hacksaw blade and told her to remain silent. When she asked what he wanted, the man allegedly demanded INR10 million.
The commotion alerted another nanny, who raised the alarm. Khan and Kapoor Khan then emerged from their rooms, and the actor confronted the intruder, asking who he was and what he wanted.
According to the witness, the man subsequently attacked Khan and another member of the household staff. Khan managed to overpower the intruder, while others took refuge in a room and locked themselves inside.
The accused had fled by the time additional staff members arrived, according to Gulf News. The nurse sustained cuts to two fingers during the incident.
Khan was taken to Mumbai’s Lilavati Hospital following the attack, where he underwent emergency surgery for multiple injuries. Doctors reported six wounds, including two deep injuries to his left hand and neck. A fragment of a knife was lodged near his spine, and surgeons removed a piece of the blade measuring approximately 2.5 inches.
The actor was discharged from hospital several days later.
Mumbai Police arrested the accused near Hiranandani Estate in Thane on January 19, 2025, three days after the incident. Police said he had used several aliases, including Vijay Das and Bijoy Das, according to Gulf News.
Described in the report as a Bangladeshi national, the accused remains in judicial custody. He faces charges under India’s Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, including robbery with a deadly weapon, causing grievous hurt and house trespass. He has also been charged under the Foreigners Act and the Passport (Entry into India) Rules.
The trial followed two unsuccessful attempts by the accused to plead guilty. According to Gulf News, his lawyer, Vipul Dushing, submitted an application in late August stating that his client was willing to plead guilty and seeking leniency. The court rejected the request on September 11 and ordered the trial to proceed.
The accused again indicated on October 8 that he intended to plead guilty to all charges. Hindustan Times reported that the court rejected this second attempt as well, paving the way for witness testimony to begin.
Khan has previously spoken about the ordeal in an interview with journalist Barkha Dutt on Mojo Story, recalling that he feared he might die as he lay injured on the floor.
The actor also said he had considered forgiving the intruder, although he struggled to move past the possibility that the man had tried to kill him. 
As proceedings continue, the defence is expected to cross-examine the nurse. Other members of the household staff are also expected to testify, while Khan himself could be called as a witness.
The report did not specify a date for the next hearing.

items.author: Anadolu Agency
items.content:
An Istanbul court ordered prosecutors to investigate Turkish nationals allegedly involved in the mistreatment of participants in the Gaza-bound Global Sumud Flotilla while they were held in Israel, during the first hearing of a case against 35 defendants, including Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
The Istanbul 11th High Criminal Court ruled that individuals identified by complainants as Turkish citizens who participated in alleged abuses against them in Israeli custody should be identified and referred to prosecutors for necessary legal action.
The court also ordered that existing arrest warrants and Interpol Red Notice requests against all 35 defendants remain in effect.
The case concerns Israel's armed interception of the Global Sumud Flotilla, which was carrying humanitarian aid to the Gaza Strip.
Flotilla participants describe alleged mistreatment
During the hearing, complainant Osman Cetinkaya said he had joined the flotilla as a doctor to deliver medical supplies to Palestinians in Gaza. He said Israeli soldiers confiscated five or six boxes of medical supplies from their vessel and that participants were subjected to mistreatment at Israel's Ashdod port.
Cetinkaya said he wished to pursue his complaint against the defendants.
Another complainant, Zeynep Tekocak, said she had been subjected to two strip searches and had an altercation with Israeli soldiers after refusing to remove her headscarf. "They recorded me wearing the clothes they gave me instead of my headscarf and mocked me," she told the court.
Read: Three years of genocide: Israel’s traditional Asian allies shift stance on Gaza
Tekocak said one of the soldiers who detained her had told her he was from Turkiye's central province of Yozgat. "They took our personal belongings, and I have not been able to recover any of them. Our privacy was seriously violated. I am filing a complaint," she said.
Turkish lawmaker Sema Silkin Un also testified, saying she and approximately 80 other participants were held in a poorly ventilated room after being detained. She said that an Israeli soldier insulted Islam while they were reading the Quran.
Un said detainees were not allowed to sleep and were subjected to verbal abuse and psychological mistreatment. "We were not even allowed to close our eyes where we were held. Sleeping was forbidden," she said.
She added that police officers who arrived the following day insulted Turkiye and the detainees in Hebrew.
Lawyers call for broader investigation into Gaza
Riza Saka, president of the Istanbul No 2 Bar Association, described the proceedings as historic and called for further international evidence to be included in the case. He referred to provisional measures ordered by the International Court of Justice (ICJ) in proceedings concerning allegations of genocide in Gaza.
Saka requested copies of relevant ICJ documents and a UN report concerning allegations of genocide in Gaza. He also referred to the arrest warrants and Red Notice requests issued against Netanyahu and the other defendants.
Lawyer Yasin Samli argued that the case involved allegations of genocide, crimes against humanity and attacks against civilians. Samli said lawyers had submitted eight volumes of evidence, including five concerning alleged crimes against women and children in Gaza.
Court seeks separate indictment over alleged crimes against Gaza civilians
In its interim ruling, the court noted that the existing indictment primarily described actions taken against the Global Sumud Flotilla, while allegations concerning crimes committed against civilians in Gaza were presented only indirectly and in general terms.
The panel said investigations into genocide and crimes against humanity could be conducted upon a request from Turkiye's justice minister.
Read More: Israel committed 'brutal violations' against aid flotilla activists: ICBSG
Taking into account the principle that courts are bound by the factual allegations set out in an indictment, the panel ordered a formal request to prosecutors concerning a possible new indictment.
The request calls for alleged crimes against civilians in Gaza, separate from the actions involving the flotilla, to be described in concrete terms and linked to supporting evidence.
The court said evidence submitted by the Istanbul No 2 Bar Association and the International Jurists Union should be considered in that process.
Court orders asset inquiries, requests ICC documents
The panel also ordered inquiries into whether any of the 35 defendants hold movable or immovable assets in Turkiye.
It directed that a request be sent through the Justice Ministry for documents from proceedings involving the defendants before the International Criminal Court (ICC). The court additionally ordered that a UN report submitted concerning allegations of genocide in Gaza be requested through the Justice Ministry.
The panel accepted applications to participate in the proceedings from complainants and several organisations, including the Istanbul No 2 Bar Association, MAZLUMDER, the International Jurists Union and the Association of Lawyers of the Earth.
The hearing was adjourned until March 30, 2027.

items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
Apple’s first foldable iPhone is facing early durability concerns after owners reported cracks in the inner display near the hinge, in some cases within hours of purchase.
Photographs shared on Reddit and technology forums show cracks along the screen’s central fold, with some damaged displays developing bright lines of pixels. However, the cause remains unclear, and the reports do not establish how widespread the problem is.
One Australian customer said their iPhone Duo’s display cracked after approximately six hours of ownership and fewer than 20 openings.
According to MacRumors, the owner felt something beneath the screen near the hinge while opening the phone to show a friend, followed by an audible crack. The customer reported no visible external damage.
Apple initially offered an express replacement, but the owner instead visited an Apple Store and received a replacement device on the spot.
Similar images have circulated online, with Tom’s Guide and Digital Trends reporting complaints involving devices in several markets. However, social media posts alone cannot establish a failure rate or confirm that all reported cases share the same cause.
The complaints have also drawn attention to the phone’s hinge mechanism and dust resistance.
Tom’s Guide covered a durability test by YouTuber JerryRigEverything, which reportedly found dust entering the hinge area. During a subsequent bend test, a green line appeared on the inner display before it stopped responding.
The test involved deliberate physical stress and does not establish that the same damage occurs during normal use.
The location of the reported cracks has prompted speculation about possible pressure from internal hinge components, manufacturing tolerances or trapped debris. None of these explanations has been confirmed.
Users have also taken to X to share their concerns about the device’s durability.
In a post on Saturday, Sam Kohl warned against taking the iPhone Duo to the beach, highlighting concerns about the device’s potential vulnerability to environmental elements. The post can be viewed here.
Another user, fenibook, reported on Friday that two cases of inner-display failure had already emerged on the phone’s launch day, adding that further reports over the following days would help establish whether the problem was more widespread. The post is available here.
Apple had not publicly identified a cause for the reported failures in the coverage reviewed.
The complaints have emerged as the iPhone Duo attracts strong interest following its launch. A separate report highlighted strong demand during the phone’s initial sales period, while another noted limited store availability at launch.
Supply constraints could complicate replacement arrangements for affected buyers, although there is no evidence linking limited availability to the reported screen damage.
For now, the reported failures remain a developing story rather than proof of a widespread defect. More verified cases, technical inspections and an official response from Apple will be needed to determine whether the incidents point to a broader reliability problem.

items.title: Flipkart’s Summer Of Discontent
items.summary:
