“Our government went away while we kept negotiating with the government,” he said, referring to the opposition’s attempts to pursue political dialogue.
Gohar also questioned the criteria used to assess political leaders’ loyalty to the state, saying that despite nearly three years of the current parliament, he still did not understand the formula used to determine such allegiance. &ldquo
items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
Opposition leaders Mahmood Khan Achakzai and Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan on Thursday criticised the government over stalled political negotiations and restrictions on parliamentarians, calling for meaningful dialogue and the protection of elected representatives’ rights.
Speaking at a press conference outside Parliament House alongside opposition leaders, Gohar said the opposition had repeatedly engaged in negotiations with the government in good faith and without preconditions, but the process had failed to produce the desired results.
“Our government went away while we kept negotiating with the government,” he said, referring to the opposition’s attempts to pursue political dialogue.
Gohar also questioned the criteria used to assess political leaders’ loyalty to the state, saying that despite nearly three years of the current parliament, he still did not understand the formula used to determine such allegiance. “We have always said that Pakistan comes first and the state comes first,” he said.
“We are treated as though we are not loyal to the state. This perception must end,” he added, calling for an end to questions about opposition politicians’ commitment to Pakistan.
He also called for parliamentarians to be protected so they could represent their constituents freely and without fear. Recalling an incident in September 2024, when opposition lawmakers were allegedly picked up, Gohar said the opposition leader had moved a resolution in the National Assembly in response.
He added that a special committee had also been constituted to address the issue of parliamentarians’ protection.
Achakzai calls for complete recording of parliamentary speeches
Speaking at the same press conference, Opposition Leader in the National Assembly Mahmood Khan Achakzai stressed that parliamentary speeches should be recorded in their entirety, arguing that the official record was essential to preserving the country’s political history and allowing the public to assess the statements of elected representatives.
“The complete speech of a member speaking in the National Assembly being recorded is a constitutional requirement,” he said.
Achakzai said parliamentarians had to struggle even for rights that should ordinarily be guaranteed under parliamentary rules. He maintained that the speaker’s authority should be exercised in accordance with the rules and regulations governing the assembly.
Referring to his speech in the National Assembly a day earlier, he said he had made no inappropriate remarks. He alleged that his four-and-a-half-minute speech had been presented as a nine-minute address.
He also rejected suggestions that his remarks had been directed against the country, saying not a single word in his speech had been against Pakistan.
The opposition leader said the time allotted to opposition lawmakers to speak in parliament had been curtailed, describing the restriction as another obstacle to democratic debate.
Achakzai questioned what he described as the inconsistent issuance of production orders for lawmakers, saying such orders had been issued for some members but not others. He argued that parliamentary proceedings and the rights of elected representatives should be protected without discrimination.
He also criticised the government’s approach to political negotiations, questioning how the opposition could trust a process that, in his view, had been ridiculed by those in power.
He said political dialogue required a meeting with PTI founder Imran Khan. He also recalled that Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman had met the prime minister in connection with the issue.
The opposition had asked the government to ensure that the prime minister personally extended an invitation for negotiations, he said. “Negotiations cannot take place in an atmosphere where the process itself is being mocked,” he said.
Achakzai called for a committee to investigate allegations of corruption against the incumbent government, proposing that Defence Minister Khawaja Asif head it.
He maintained that the opposition would resist what it considered an undemocratic system through democratic means. “It is the duty of every citizen who wants to save Pakistan to stand up for democracy,” he said, adding that the country needed a strong parliament and state institutions operating within their respective constitutional jurisdictions.
“We will not hand Pakistan over to an undemocratic system,” he said, warning that such an order could threaten the country’s unity.
Raja Nasir Abbas calls for rule of law, constitutional supremacy
Also speaking at the press conference, Majlis Wahdat-e-Muslimeen chief Allama Raja Nasir Abbas stressed that the rule of law, justice and respect for the Constitution were essential for Pakistan’s progress, saying the country’s political and economic crises could not be resolved without the supremacy of law.
He said the rule of law and access to justice were fundamental to national development. Pakistan could not overcome its ongoing political crisis unless the Constitution was upheld and the rule of law firmly established, he added.
Addressing the country’s economic challenges, Abbas said the economic crisis, too, could not be resolved without ensuring the supremacy of law. He added that justice was necessary to restore public confidence in state institutions and the wider system.
He expressed concern that the trust deficit between the rulers and the people had reached its highest level in the country’s history. He also criticised the continued registration of fabricated cases and first information reports (FIRs), saying such practices further undermined public trust.
Referring to the February 8, 2024, general elections, Abbas alleged that the people’s mandate had been stolen. He said depriving citizens of their right to vote and undermining their electoral choices constituted serious injustices.
He further said tampering with votes amounted to an attack on the Constitution and the rule of law, stressing that protecting the sanctity of the vote was essential to upholding democratic principles and restoring public confidence in the political system.
Abbas reiterated that Pakistan’s sustainable progress, political stability and economic recovery depended on constitutional supremacy, the rule of law and justice for all citizens.
Gohar denies reports of differences within PTI
Meanwhile, Gohar addressed reports concerning internal party affairs, PTI lawmakers in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) and the provincial organisation, urging party members to verify information before reacting to reports.
He said the news that had prompted a social media post by the party’s secretary general was incorrect and that he had spoken to the relevant leaders and lawmakers.
Describing PTI’s lawmakers from K-P as a valuable asset, Gohar praised their role in supporting Imran over the past two years. He said they had remained steadfast despite difficult circumstances and continued to play a leading role in rallies, public meetings and protest marches.
“All these members are standing even more firmly with Imran Khan, his ideology and his struggle,” he said, adding that they enjoyed the PTI founder’s full confidence.
Gohar said no party lawmaker would consider disregarding Imran’s instructions and assured the provincial leadership that it would be consulted on important party decisions.
On the provincial party presidency, he clarified that Junaid Akbar had been appointed by Imran himself and that he had issued the notification in accordance with the PTI founder’s instructions. Junaid would continue to serve as provincial president, he said.
In Junaid’s absence, senior vice-president Noorul Haq Qadri would chair meetings of the provincial organisation under the party constitution, while provincial secretary general Ali Asghar Khan would oversee other organisational matters.
Gohar said discussions had taken place with the relevant office-bearers and that the provincial organisation had expressed the same preference during its meeting. A formal notification was expected to be issued on the matter.
He added that no changes would be made to the provincial organisation or its existing cabinet until Junaid returned.
Emphasising party unity, the PTI chairman said the party’s focus should remain on Imran’s position, political narrative and struggle rather than internal disagreements or unnecessary public statements.
He reiterated that the party remained united under Imran’s leadership and that his decisions and instructions were final.
Gohar also reaffirmed PTI’s position on the K-P chief minister, saying Sohail Afridi remained the party’s choice and that there was no question of considering anyone else for the position, as the decision rested with Imran.
Salman Akram Raja rejects claims Sohail Afridi derailed talks with govt
Separately, PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja has rejected claims that non-functional K-P Chief Minister Sohail Afridi was responsible for the breakdown of negotiations with the federal government, saying the talks collapsed over the denial of access to PTI founder Imran Khan’s personal physicians and concerns over provincial autonomy.
In an interview with a private television channel on Thursday, he said the refusal to allow Khan’s personal doctors to examine him was one of the two principal reasons behind the failure of the negotiations.
He said PTI could not grant the federal government unrestricted authority to intervene in the affairs of K-P. “These were the two principal reasons why the talks collapsed,” Raja said, alleging that the government had deliberately undermined the negotiations.
The PTI leader also described the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in the province as unconstitutional, alleging that the government had introduced the measures to take control of the provincial administration. “They just wanted to take over the province,” he said.
Raja said an all-parties conference (APC) was being planned within the next 10 days, or earlier, to discuss the prevailing political situation. “This is a political issue and therefore all political parties must play their role,” he said.
He disclosed that several political parties were in contact with him over the situation, including Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman.
Asked about the role of Pashtunkhwa Milli Awami Party chairman Mehmood Khan Achakzai, Raja said the final decision rested with the PTI founder. He described Achakzai and Majlis Wahdat-e-Muslimeen chief Allama Nasir Abbas as a shield for the party, adding that PTI would continue to seek their political advice and support.
Raja also maintained that PTI’s long march had not ended, signalling that the party’s political campaign would continue.
Meanwhile, PTI leader and Senator Syed Ali Zafar denied that negotiations with the government were imminent, saying decisions concerning the party would be made by its parliamentary party.
“We are yet to determine the terms of reference,” Zafar said while speaking to a journalist from the same television channel. He further alleged that the government had decided to impose governor’s rule around one-and-a-half months earlier.
Yousafzai distances party from YouTubers campaigning against state institutions
PTI's K-P information secretary Shaukat Ali Yousafzai on Thursday distanced the party from YouTubers campaigning against state institutions, saying they had no links with PTI and that such campaigns had negatively affected the party.
Speaking in an interview with a private television channel, Yousafzai said PTI founder Imran Khan had always referred to the armed forces as his own institution, adding that no other viewpoint would be entertained on the matter.
He said PTI had always condemned terrorism and described it as unjustified to label the party’s leaders or workers as facilitators of terrorists. He also alleged that the government had used concerns over peace and security as a pretext to impose emergency and governor’s rule in K-P, calling the move unjustified.
He expressed confidence in Barrister Gohar Ali Khan and Salman Akram Raja, adding that he would not be “intimidated by a YouTuber” based overseas.
Deadlock on emergency and governor’s rule in K-P
The debate over emergency and governor’s rule in K-P intensified in late September amid worsening security concerns and growing political tensions between the federal government and the PTI-led provincial administration.
Federal ministers accused the provincial government of failing to address terrorism and governance challenges, while PTI considered the possibility of an in-house change or dissolution of the provincial assembly.
The federal government subsequently stepped up its warnings, with Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar and other officials arguing that constitutional provisions allowed the Centre to intervene if circumstances warranted extraordinary measures. The government cited the deteriorating law and order situation and the provincial administration’s handling of security challenges as precursors for governor’s rule and emergency.
Later, on October 11, President Asif Ali Zardari approved the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in the province on the advice of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, following approval by the federal cabinet. The government cited escalating terrorist attacks, threats to lives and property, and what it described as a breakdown of the constitutional system in the province.
The measures invoked Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution, while the federal government also authorised the deployment of the army to assist the civil administration.
Read More: PHC takes up challenge to emergency today
The move transferred executive authority from the elected provincial government to Governor Faisal Karim Kundi and affected 12 districts under the emergency proclamation. PTI rejected the decision, arguing that it undermined provincial autonomy and the party’s electoral mandate.
The intervention also marked the fourth spell of governor’s rule in the province, following earlier instances in 1975, 1994 and 1999.
The issue subsequently moved to Parliament and the courts.
On October 12, a petition challenging the imposition of emergency measures and governor’s rule in K-P was filed in the Peshawar High Court by PTI, a day after President Asif Ali Zardari approved the federal government’s decision on the advice of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif. The opposition argued that the constitutional requirements had not been fulfilled and that the intervention violated provincial autonomy.
Three days later, on October 15, a joint sitting of Parliament approved separate resolutions endorsing the emergency and governor’s rule for two months, despite severe protests from the opposition parties.
So far, the government and the opposition remain at loggerheads regarding the governance of the province.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
WhatsApp is rolling out a scheduled messages feature to its iOS app, allowing users to send messages automatically at a selected date and time. The feature is designed to help users plan their messages in advance without having to open the app when the scheduled time arrives.
According to WABetaInfo, the feature is available to some beta testers through WhatsApp beta for iOS version 26.42.10.19, distributed through TestFlight. The company is gradually expanding access, and more beta testers are expected to receive it over the coming weeks.
WhatsApp Rolls Out Scheduled Messages Feature on iOS Beta – Here’s How to Do it
Users can schedule a message directly from an individual or group chat. After typing a message, they need to tap and hold the send button to open the scheduling screen. They can then select the desired date and time using the available controls.
The screen displays the exact delivery time before users confirm their selection. Once the message is scheduled, WhatsApp shows a confirmation in the chat. However, this confirmation is visible only to the person who scheduled the message.
The feature allows users to schedule messages at least 10 minutes in advance and up to two weeks ahead. This gives them enough flexibility to prepare birthday wishes, important announcements, reminders, and other messages without worrying about sending them manually at the right time.
Support for Photos, Videos, and Links
WhatsApp’s scheduled messaging feature supports more than just text. Users can also schedule photos, videos, and links for later delivery.
To schedule a photo or video, users can tap and hold the send button from the drawing editor screen. However, the feature does not currently allow users to schedule multiple items together. They must create a separate scheduled message for each photo or video they want to send.
The feature also supports end-to-end encryption, helping protect scheduled messages in the same way as other WhatsApp communications.
See Also: WhatsApp Tests New Location Request Feature
Users Can Manage Scheduled Messages
WhatsApp has added a dedicated section for scheduled messages in the chat information screen. In group conversations, users can access this section through the group information screen.
This section allows users to review messages before WhatsApp sends them. If they change their mind or need to make adjustments, they can delete a scheduled message at any time before its delivery.
WhatsApp does not notify recipients when a sender deletes a scheduled message before it is sent. This gives users more control over messages they have planned in advance.
Scheduled Messages Also Work in Group Chats
The feature supports both individual and group conversations. However, WhatsApp applies a specific rule to scheduled messages in groups.
A scheduled message will reach only the members who were part of the group when the sender scheduled it. Anyone who joins the group afterward will not receive that message. This approach ensures that the message does not reach people who were not members of the group when it was originally scheduled.
When Will the Feature Be Available to Everyone?
WhatsApp is currently rolling out scheduled messages to a limited number of iOS beta testers. Users running the compatible beta version may not see the feature immediately because availability depends on the gradual rollout.
More beta testers are expected to receive access over the coming weeks. However, WhatsApp has not announced an official release date for the stable version.
The arrival of scheduled messages on iOS follows the feature’s introduction in the Android beta. Once widely available, it could make WhatsApp more convenient for users who want to plan personal messages, group announcements, and important reminders in advance.

items.author: Life And Style Desk
items.content:
Actor Zoya Nasir questioned the excitement surrounding Hollywood comedian Sacha Baron Cohen’s recent shoutout to Pakistan, arguing that his history of comedy involving racial and religious stereotypes warranted a closer look at the interaction.
The Bas Tera Saath Ho actor shared her views on Instagram Stories after a video of Cohen’s brief interaction with Pakistani actor Haris Waheed began circulating online.
Waheed, who shared the clip earlier this week, can be seen meeting Cohen, expressing his admiration for the comedian and telling him that he is from Pakistan. Cohen, dressed as his character for the upcoming film Ali G: Who Iz I, responds, “Yo, big up the Pakistan, man,” prompting cheers from people nearby.
The exchange received a warm response on social media, with users appreciating the British star’s acknowledgement of Pakistan. Nasir, however, questioned whether the moment deserved the positive reaction it received.
“I’m sorry but the sheer lack of awareness is staggering. Sacha Baron Cohen has been openly hostile towards Muslims. Majority of his movies back that up,” she wrote.
Criticising the comedian’s approach to comedy, Nasir described his demeanour as marked by “smug, dripping sarcasm” and a “theatrical sense of superiority”.
She challenged the enthusiasm surrounding the exchange, asking: “This was not a positive interaction in anyway, shape or form. Why are we excited about that again?”
Screengrab: zoyanasir/Instagram
 
Cohen is known for creating characters that use exaggerated accents, cultural appropriation and provocative humour to explore prejudice and social attitudes. However, his work has also attracted criticism over whether it challenges stereotypes or risks reinforcing them.
His Borat character, for instance, has sparked debate over the use of ethnic and cultural caricatures, while The Dictator has faced scrutiny over its portrayal of authoritarianism and people from the Middle East. His Ali G persona, meanwhile, has been criticised for appropriating elements of Black culture.
Cohen has consistently defended his work as satire intended to expose ignorance and prejudice rather than endorse them.
In an interview published by Time on October 20, the comedian addressed criticism of Ali G, explaining that the character was designed to expose cultural bias and reveal how readily people in positions of power took him seriously.
“I’ve always designed my characters and comedy as vehicles to expose prejudice, bias and stupidity, though I realise not everyone sees them that way,” he said.
He further described Ali G as a white character who imitates the fashion and lyrics of gangsta rap and dancehall artists, adding that the joke was directed at the character himself and the predominantly white, male establishment that believed him.
Nasir’s comments highlight the divide in how Cohen’s comedy is received, particularly when an interaction involving one of his characters is interpreted as a gesture of goodwill towards a country or community.

items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
The federal government has directed all ministries and divisions to submit consolidated details of civil servants’ declarations regarding foreign nationality, travel documents and dependants’ nationality status, according to an official notification issued by the Establishment Division dated October 21.
The notification referred to the Civil Servants (Disclosure and Regulation of Foreign Nationality) Rules, 2026, under which all civil servants were required to submit declarations regarding their own and their dependants’ nationality status within 90 days of the rules’ publication in the official gazette.
Under Rule 3(3), civil servants must declare whether they hold the nationality of any foreign country, possess foreign travel documents or are married to a foreign national. They must also disclose the relevant nationality and travel-document status of their dependants.
The Establishment Division said failure to submit the required declaration or providing false information would constitute misconduct under the Civil Servants (Efficiency and Discipline) Rules, 2020, in accordance with Rule 3(4) of the 2026 rules.
The notification directed all ministries and divisions to provide the information in a consolidated format for officers under their administrative control, excluding those belonging to the Pakistan Administrative Service (PAS), Police Service of Pakistan (PSP), Secretariat Group (SG) and Office Management Group (OMG).
The prescribed format requires the name, designation and basic pay scale of each officer, confirmation of whether a declaration has been submitted under Rule 3(3), and details of the foreign nationality or travel-document status of both the officer and their dependants.
Earlier this month, the government decided to enforce the Foreign Citizenship Rules 2026, directing civil servants to submit declarations detailing any foreign citizenship held by themselves or their dependants within one week.
The Establishment Division, through an office memorandum, directed civil servants to provide details of foreign citizenship, foreign travel documents and marriages to foreign nationals. The directive applies to officers holding dual nationality and requires them to furnish the relevant information within the stipulated one-week deadline.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Chinese ​AI startup DeepSeek has raised about 100 billion yuan ($14.98 billion) in its latest funding round from investors including chipmaker ‌GigaDevice, food delivery company Meituan and automaker Geely, according to four people with knowledge of the matter.
Battery maker Contemporary Amperex Technology (CATL) and WeChat operator Tencent Holdings, both existing shareholders, were among the biggest investors in the round, said two of the people.
Home appliances maker Midea and existing shareholder NetEase also participated, the people ​said.
Other investors include Boyu Capital, CPE and Legend Capital, as well as existing shareholder IDG Capital, three of the people said.
The ​total number of investors in the funding round exceeded 15, one of the people said.
Read: Trump says companies should pay 'dividend' to communities to make data centres popular
DeepSeek, which sources have ⁠said is valued at 500 billion yuan before new capital is injected, will have doubled its original fundraising target of 50 billion ​yuan. The rise underscores strong interest from investors - many backed by the state and big corporations - as China aims to stay competitive in ​the AI race against the US.
"It's encouraging to see such a high valuation for DeepSeek, showing the confidence from investors on the future of its open-source strategies," said Lian Jye Su, chief analyst at research firm Omdia.
"Given that they (the investors) are all Chinese and critical component supply chain vendors, I can see ​DeepSeek itself becoming a key part of these domestic tech supply chains," Su said.
The fundraising is set to be complete in the coming ​days, but financial details and the investor lineup are not ironclad and could still change, a second person said.
DeepSeek could not be immediately reached for comment. ‌Geely declined ⁠to comment. The other firms mentioned in this article did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
On Thursday, Bloomberg first reported, citing sources, that DeepSeek had raised $15 billion in the latest funding round, with CATL and Tencent as its main backers.
DeepSeek's fundraising outcome comes amid growing concerns over massive AI spending that triggered a new selloff in global tech stocks this month.
Read More: China's DeepSeek developing its own AI chip, sources say
The soured sentiment has led to delays or withdrawals ​of data centre IPOs and poor market ​debuts of AI-related companies in South ⁠Korea and Hong Kong, Reuters has reported.
Shares of Z.AI and MiniMax, two large language model developers listed in Hong Kong since January, have fallen sharply from their peaks earlier this year.
After the fundraising, DeepSeek ​is getting closer to tapping public markets. In September, Reuters reported that the company aimed to kick ​off its IPO ⁠process this year and had hired CITIC Securities to prepare for the potential STAR Market float.
Last month, the company released its latest model, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, which it said was designed for greater capability, faster inference, higher throughput and scaling to larger models.
The Hangzhou-based firm raised $7.4 billion from its inaugural external funding round ⁠in June, ​Reuters has reported.
Filings by two Chinese investors in July suggested DeepSeek was valued at ​350.88 billion yuan, or around $52 billion, in the June fundraising.

items.author: AFP
items.content:
Max Verstappen is set to be a party-pooper this weekend as he seeks to delay Kimi Antonelli's title celebrations by notching a third consecutive win with another triumph at the United States Grand Prix.
Red Bull's four-time world champion won both the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia and then the Singapore Grand Prix to emerge as a leading contender for more success just when Mercedes' precocious 20-year-old Italian moved within reach of the title.
The 29-year-old Dutchman, who has acknowledged Antonelli's generational talent, won from pole at the Circuit of the Americas last year and is chasing a fifth win at the Texan track where Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton was won five times.
But Verstappen has been reluctant to claim that Red Bull's recovery in form and results will automatically translate to more success. "It's difficult to say – I don't want to say now that I will be in the fight in Austin," he said after his Singapore win.
"But the last few weekends have been great. I just take it race by race and we'll see how it goes there. It's another very different kind of track."
After a run of seven podium finishes in his last eight races, including two wins and three second places, Verstappen, 119 points adrift in fourth, may well scupper hopes that Antonelli can win and, with the stars aligning, become Italy's first champion since 1953 and the youngest in F1 history.
- Title within reach -
To seize the title in Texas, the Italian, who leads Mercedes team-mate George Russell by 102 points, needs to win the race and see Russell fail to finish in the top nine and Hamilton outside the top four.
Antonelli was only four years old when Sebastian Vettel took the record as youngest champion, with Red Bull, in 2010, and he knows he must stay focused and race to win, as he always does.
"I know it's very close and I know it's there, but I need to make sure I keep doing my best and go out and win and perform in my best way," he said. Italy's last champion was Alberto Ascari for Ferrari.
McLaren's deputy team principal Bradley Lord drew upon tennis when he described Antonelli's position by saying: "We're in that uncomfortable phase where you have to navigate the media with everyone saying 'you can do it – you've got first match point."
Russell's hopes of reining in Antonelli may be aided by Verstappen while Hamilton could also be a threat as he returns to one of his favourite circuits seeking a record sixth win and seventh in the United States GP.
Both Mercedes drivers will run the team's latest updates package as they go into a decisive triple-header of races in Texas, Mexico and Brazil, but it may be that Ferrari and Red Bull can steal the initiative.
These races may be run on bumpy tracks and in hot conditions that deliver unexpected results, a prospect that Verstappen has anticipated.
"From what I saw in the world endurance championship race in Austin, the track is incredibly bumpy and I will probably need to order a new spine after the weekend – or become like Robocop. It's crazy.

items.author: Shrishti Bisht
items.content:
Anthropic has unveiled Claude Duet, a proactive AI agent designed to monitor connected apps, prioritise tasks, and carry out work in the background, including when users switch off their devices.
The offering targets professionals and small business owners. Powered by Claude Opus 5.5, it is available as a research preview through a waitlist for Claude Pro and Max subscribers in the US.
Users can access Claude Duet through standalone iOS and Android apps or on Claude’s website. It is included in existing Pro and Max subscriptions but shares usage limits with other Claude products. Background checks count towards these limits, while complex assignments consume more usage, Anthropic said.
Unlike conventional AI chatbots, Claude Duet is designed to identify work that needs attention without waiting for a prompt. It sends users a daily briefing covering important items across connected apps, including emails and calendars, and provides updates when tasks are completed or require a decision.
Users can assign tasks through text or voice messages, ranging from scheduling meetings and drafting email replies to building dashboards, financial forecasts and web applications. The agent can also search past conversations and use existing Claude memories, skills and connected apps.
Claude Duet connects with more than 6,000 tools and plugins available through the Claude Marketplace, including Gmail, Slack, QuickBooks, Stripe, Gusto, LinkedIn, DocuSign, HubSpot and Shopify.
For instance, it can identify unpaid invoices through QuickBooks or Stripe and draft payment reminders. It can also prepare payroll information, draft job postings, create follow-up emails using customer and deal histories, and help businesses set up and manage online stores.
The agent runs on its own cloud-based virtual machine with a browser, allowing it to continue working even when users close the app or switch off their devices. Anthropic said it checks connected accounts every few hours rather than continuously, partly to limit subscription usage.
Claude Duet can also help users make business purchases through Link, Stripe’s digital wallet, and Shop Pay. Payments require user approval, while Link uses a virtual card to avoid sharing the user’s actual card number. Integration with 1Password for accessing saved website logins is also planned.
Anthropic said the agent requires approval before sending messages, making payments, signing documents or deleting information. Trading securities and transferring money between accounts remain prohibited, even with user approval. Users can disconnect apps, and only they can mark tasks as finished.
Safeguards And Early Limitations
Anthropic said Claude Duet includes safeguards designed to prevent unauthorised actions, prompt injection, and sensitive data leaks. Prompt injection involves malicious instructions hidden in content an agent encounters, such as emails or websites.
The protections include an automated system that assesses proposed actions and controls designed to keep passwords and sign-in tokens out of the agent’s direct view.
A separate message-checking system is designed to block requests to share highly sensitive information, including credit card numbers and government identification. Other sensitive information, such as health and personal finance details, can be shared only on explicit user instructions, Anthropic said.
The company said Claude Duet has undergone adversarial testing and external penetration testing, and is covered by its public bug bounty programme.
However, Anthropic acknowledged that the early version may misinterpret conversations, misjudge urgency, or miss information arriving between checks. It is currently better suited to work assignments than personal errands, such as booking tickets, and users cannot yet view its browser.
The launch adds to the growing competition in always-on AI agents that work across apps with limited human intervention. OpenAI’s Dots and Meta’s Muse target similar use cases, while Bengaluru-based Emergent’s Wingman handles tasks across email, calendars, and workplace software through WhatsApp and Telegram.
As agents gain access to more business systems, their permissions and accountability are also coming under scrutiny. Recently, CERT-In warned about unauthorised AI agent access to Indian organisations’ systems, highlighting the risks associated with deploying increasingly autonomous tools.
Anthropic said feedback from early users will inform further development. The research preview does not currently include Team and Enterprise subscribers.

items.author: Tom Jackson
items.content:
Nigerian startup ECS Network is looking to bring long-term structure to competitive gaming in Africa, offering a league system with divisions, promotion and relegation, player statistics and team rankings.
Launched just over a year ago, ECS Network started out as competitive Call of Duty: Mobile (CODM) “scrims” – or practice games – before evolving into a broader e-sports organisation covering multiple games.
“A lot of competitive gaming activity was centred around standalone tournaments, where everything essentially started and ended with one event. We wanted to build something with continuity, where teams and players could compete consistently and have their performances tracked over time,” CEO Larry Channel told Disrupt Africa.
That led the startup to develop a structured league system featuring multiple divisions, promotion and relegation, player statistics, team rankings, MVP recognition and competitive integrity systems.
ECS now has more than 50 staff working across its different titles and operational areas, including event management, competitive integrity, verification, rankings, community management and media.
Channel said there were several tournament organisers and esports communities operating across Africa, but most were primarily focused on individual tournaments or events.
“Our main difference is the long-term structure. ECS is built around an ongoing competitive system where teams can progress through divisions, players can build statistics and rankings, and performances continue to matter beyond a single tournament,” he said.
The approach is resonating. ECS has grown to more than 43,000 players and over 5,000 registered teams across 10 titles, while more than 1,600 teams and 15,000 players have competed in CODM alone since launch. Having started with CODM, the platform has expanded to include Free Fire, PUBG Mobile, eFootball, FC Mobile, Blood Strike, Mobile Legends and Valorant, among others.
“The response has been very strong,” said Channel.
Though its core competitive base is in Africa, ECS has also built an audience in Europe, North America and the Middle East. The startup plans to continue expanding across more games and to strengthen its position as a wider African esports ecosystem.
ECS is self-funded by its management team, and has so far awarded more than NGN75 million (US$56,000) in prize money across its events. It generates revenue primarily through sponsorship and commercial partnerships.
“At this stage, revenue is largely reinvested into the operation and development of the league, including events, prize pools, staffing, infrastructure and community development, rather than being taken as profit,” Channel said.
The journey has not been without its challenges, chief among them changing how players view competitive gaming.
“One of the biggest challenges was changing the mindset around competitive gaming from viewing each tournament as a standalone event to seeing it as part of a longer competitive journey. Building that trust and getting teams and players to buy into a structured system took time, but we’ve seen that improve significantly,” he said.
Sponsorship remains a hurdle too.
“African e-sports is still developing commercially, so securing long-term sponsorship support remains something we’re actively working on,” said Channel.

items.author: Team Inc42
items.content:
Omnichannel furniture and home furnishings brand Chapter Homes has raised ₹63 Cr ($6.6 Mn) in a strategic funding round through a mix of debt and equity. The fundraise valued the startup at nearly ₹1,000 Cr (around $106 Mn).
The round saw participation from Bessemer Venture Partners, Stride Ventures, comedian Tanmay Bhat and a clutch of family offices. The brand claims to have also received further commitments from undisclosed backers for a future fundraise.
In a statement, the startup said that it plans to utilise the fresh capital to strengthen product development, expand into newer categories and invest in technology and brand building. A chunk of the capital will also be used to scale its omnichannel distribution network and set up its initial offline footprint.
“… Consumers are increasingly looking for better-designed products, trusted quality, strong functionality and a superior overall experience – online and in store – and we see a meaningful opportunity to build for those needs. That is why we are building focused brands for each category across home and kitchen,” said Chapter Homes cofounder Nitin Chugh.
Founded in 2025 by former PharmEasy executives Chugh, Akarsh Bharadwaj, Shrey Mittal, Dhiraj Jain and Dheeraj Goyal, Chapter Homes claims to be building multiple consumer brands across categories for home and kitchen needs of Indian consumers. It has already launched a home furnishing brand under HOKIPO.
Going forward, it plans to leverage synergies across supply chain, content, technology and distribution to expand into adjacent categories such as cookware, home décor and small kitchen appliances. The startup also said that it plans to leverage AI across cataloguing and demand forecasting to product assortment and customer retention to launch faster and rein in costs.
Notably, Chapter Homes is not the first home improvement startup to emerge from the PharmEasy stable. Earlier this year, AllHome, founded by PharmEasy cofounders, raised ₹200 Cr in its Series B round led by Bessemer Venture Partners.
The fundraise comes amid continued investor interest in the home improvement and home decor segment. In August, home decor marketplace Vaaree raised ₹65 Cr in its Series A round co-led by Hero Enterprise and Cap Alpha Ventures. Prior to this, D2C homeware startup HomeEssentials also raised ₹70 Cr in its pre-Series B round led by 360 ONE Asset.
Even the adjacent kitchen tech segment is seeing healthy adoption among masses due to LPG shortages. Many Indians are now buying induction cooktops, AI-powered smart appliances and electric rice cookers and air fryers. It is this segment that Chapter Homes plans to target going forward.
But for now, Chapter Homes is eyeing a piece of the Indian home furnishing and decor market, which is projected to become a $45.5 Bn opportunity by 2031.

Apple has warned customers that the new iPhone Duo may be difficult to buy in stores on launch day due to limited stock and strong demand. The foldable smartphone will go on sale on Friday, October 23, 2026, but customers planning to purchase it without a pre-order may face difficulties.
According to Apple, demand for the iPhone Duo has been extraordinary since pre-orders opened last week. The company expects the limited stock available for walk-in customers to sell out quickly.
The warning means buyers who have not secured a pre-order may need to reserve a device online or wait for additional stock.
Apple Confirms Limited Walk-In Availability for iPhone Duo
Apple will offer limited walk-in stock in the United States, Australia, Austria, Belgium, Canada, Mexico, Germany, the Netherlands, Singapore, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Türkiye, and the United Kingdom.
Some Apple Stores in Italy will also offer the device to walk-in customers, although the company has not identified the locations. In Macao, walk-in purchases will be available only on launch day, with limited inventory.
However, customers in France, China, Hong Kong, India, Japan, Malaysia, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand, and the United Arab Emirates will not be able to purchase the iPhone Duo as walk-in buyers on launch day.
Instead, customers in these markets will need to book a pickup time through Apple’s online store. The store has currently advised customers to check again on Saturday, October 24, leaving some uncertainty about whether pickup reservations will become available on launch day itself.
Apple Takes Steps to Control Demand
Apple’s restrictions appear aimed at managing crowds and limiting purchases by resellers who may try to buy devices in large quantities and sell them at higher prices.
The company has also limited iPhone Duo purchases to two units per customer. This measure is intended to give more buyers a chance to purchase the foldable phone rather than allowing a small number of customers to acquire large quantities.
There is some positive news for customers who have already placed pre-orders. Apple has moved up estimated shipping dates for many buyers after delivery estimates previously extended as far as January 2027.
The change suggests that some customers may receive their devices sooner than initially expected, although availability will depend on their individual orders.
iPhone Duo Specifications and Features
The iPhone Duo is Apple’s new foldable smartphone and comes with two LTPO OLED displays. Its inner screen measures 7.6 inches and offers a resolution of 1,878 x 2,670 pixels, while the 5.4-inch cover display has a resolution of 1,398 x 2,034 pixels. Both screens support a 120Hz refresh rate.
The device runs on Apple’s A20 Pro chipset and includes 12GB of RAM. Buyers can choose configurations with up to 2TB of internal storage.
For photography, the phone features a 48MP main camera with sensor-shift optical image stabilisation and a 48MP ultrawide camera. It also includes a 12MP selfie camera on the cover display and a 4MP under-display camera on the inner screen.
The iPhone Duo packs a 4,883mAh battery and supports 25W MagSafe and Qi2 wireless charging. Other features include an IP68 rating for dust and water resistance and Apple’s iOS 27.1 software.
iPhone Duo Price
The iPhone Duo starts at $1,999 in the United States. Its starting price is €2,299 in Germany and £1,999 in the United Kingdom.
With strong demand and limited walk-in availability, customers who want the foldable iPhone may need to act quickly. Those who have not placed a pre-order should check Apple’s online store for pickup reservations and future stock updates before visiting a retail location.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
North Korean hacking group Lazarus is using post-quantum cryptography to deliver malware in a new cyberattack campaign targeting South Korean organizations. The operation combines older malware tools with new techniques designed to make attacks harder to detect.
Cybersecurity researchers at Kaspersky have named the campaign FlashHole. Their investigation found that the hackers use a standardized post-quantum encryption mechanism to secure communication between infected systems and their command-and-control (C2) servers.
Lazarus Hackers Use Post-Quantum Cryptography to Deliver Malware
The attacks reportedly began in July 2025. Researchers identified at least three affected companies operating in the software, construction, and wired communication equipment manufacturing sectors in South Korea. However, they believe the campaign may have targeted more organizations.
How the FlashHole Campaign Works
The attackers use phishing pages to direct victims to specially designed GitHub pages. These pages load JavaScript code from external domains, starting a complex infection process that allows the hackers to install malware on targeted systems.
The attack chain also abuses INISAFE CrossWeb EX, a security tool commonly used in South Korea. The tool’s process launches a legitimate Windows executable called fsquirt.exe, which the attackers use to execute malicious code.
This process installs TechHub, a downloader that retrieves additional malware from private GitHub repositories.
The campaign also uses ClientHub, a malware loader that supports communication through Dropbox and direct data exchange with LPEClient. This helps the attackers deliver additional malicious components to compromised systems.
Multiple Malware Tools Used in Attacks
LPEClient plays a central role in the campaign. The malware collects information about infected systems, receives encrypted payloads, and helps the attackers avoid security monitoring.
Another tool, called Cubridge, is a modular backdoor that gives attackers several ways to control compromised computers. It supports file management, command execution, system reconnaissance, screenshot capturing, and the installation of additional malware.
Kaspersky also identified tools designed to steal sensitive information from Chromium-based browsers. These tools can target account credentials, cookies, and browsing history.
Researchers noted that much of the malicious code runs directly in system memory instead of being stored as files on the device. This technique can make detection more difficult because security tools may have fewer files to examine. However, some components still leave files on infected systems to maintain access.
Why Post-Quantum Cryptography Matters
One of the most notable features of FlashHole is its use of ML-KEM-1024, a standardized post-quantum key encapsulation mechanism approved by the US National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST).
Post-quantum cryptography is designed to protect communications against attacks from future quantum computers. It can also help address the risk of attackers collecting encrypted information today and attempting to decrypt it later when more powerful technology becomes available.
In the FlashHole campaign, Lazarus uses ML-KEM to establish shared cryptographic keys between its malware and command-and-control infrastructure.
According to Kaspersky, LPEClient receives data containing four ML-KEM-1024 public keys from the C2 server. It then generates four separate pairs of shared keys and ciphertexts. The malware encrypts the ciphertexts using the GOST algorithm and sends them back to the server through ClientHub.
The resulting shared secrets provide key material for the Threefish encryption algorithm. This allows LPEClient to decrypt the server’s response, which contains configuration information and an executable payload.
The final payload is Cubridge, which LPEClient loads directly into the system’s memory.
Kaspersky believes this combination of post-quantum cryptography and in-memory execution helps Lazarus conceal its subsequent payloads and reduce the chances of detection.
Links to Earlier Lazarus Operations
Researchers have placed FlashHole within the broader Cascade Hole activity and linked it to the earlier Operation SyncHole campaign with medium-to-high confidence.
The findings highlight how advanced hacking groups are combining established malware with newer cryptographic methods to improve their attacks. While post-quantum encryption is being developed to strengthen cybersecurity, its use in this campaign shows that malicious actors can also adopt modern security technologies to protect their own communications and conceal malware delivery.
The discovery reinforces the need for organizations to strengthen phishing defenses, monitor suspicious application behavior, and investigate unusual activity involving trusted software and online services.

items.author: Rizwana Omer
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
OnePlus is putting a fan inside a phone. The company has confirmed that the OnePlus Ace 7 Pro and Ace 7 launch in China on October 29 at 7 PM local time, which is 4:00 PM in Pakistan.
OnePlus calls the Ace 7 Pro its “most powerful Ace ever” and the first OnePlus phone with an active cooling fan.
What OnePlus has confirmed
The Ace 7 Pro runs on the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5, a 3 nm chip with an Adreno 840 GPU. The fan is the headline feature, with two air paths: one cools the chip, and the other cools the back panel.
The company says the design lowers temperature by up to 10°C in long gaming sessions. The air intake sits away from where fingers rest, and hot air leaves through the top of the phone.
OnePlus also claims maximum frame rates at maximum graphics in all games. In one example, it says the Ace 7 Pro beats rival phones with the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 in Delta Force at 185 fps.
These are company claims, not independent tests. Earlier leaker posts described the rival in that test only as an unnamed 2nm flagship, which hit 165 fps, so the exact comparison phone is unclear.
What is still a leak?
OnePlus has not confirmed the rest of the specifications.
Detail
Status
Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5, Adreno 840, two-path fan
Confirmed by OnePlus
6.78-inch 1.5K OLED flat display, 185 Hz
Leaked
200MP Samsung HP5 main camera
Leaked
50MP 3.5x periscope telephoto (Pro)
Leaked
About a 9,000 mAh battery
Leaked
120W wired charging
Leaked
Ace 7 with the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 V Series variant
Leaked
Leaks also say the main camera will use OPPO’s flagship camera processing. Pricing has not been announced. Whether the standard Ace 7 gets a fan is also unclear. There is no certainty yet that it will have the cooling fan found on the Pro.
Why a fan matters
Most phones slow down in long gaming sessions as the chip heats up. This is called thermal throttling, where the processor cuts speed to protect itself. Vapour chambers and heat spreaders delay the effect. A fan pushes heat out of the body, which is a more direct fix.
The trade-off is physical. A fan needs openings, which raises questions about dust, water resistance, noise and long-term durability. OnePlus has said none of this so far.
Editorial view
A cooling fan is a clear selling point, but the evidence offered so far is thin. OnePlus’s Delta Force result is a single game, and “max frame rates in all games” is a marketing line, not a measurement.
If the claims hold, the Ace 7 Pro could set a template for mid-priced performance phones. If the fan proves noisy or fragile, it will stay a niche feature. Price will decide how many people ever find out.

1. For multiple price-based auction, successful bids will get accepted at the respective quoted yield/price for the security. For uniform price-based auction, bids will get accepted at the cut off yield/price accepted in the auction.
2. The auction will be yield based for new security and price based for securities which are re-issued.
3. In case of a Floating Rate Bonds (FRB), the auction will be spread-based for new security and price based for securities which are reissued. At the time of placing bids for new FRB, the spread should be quoted in percentage terms.
Minimum Bid Size
4. The securities will be issued for a minimum amount of ₹10,000/- (nominal) and in multiples of ₹10,000/- thereafter.
Non-Competitive Segment
5. In all the auctions, Government security up to 5% of the notified amount for sale of individual security will be allotted to the eligible individuals and institutions under the Scheme for Non-competitive Bidding Facility in the Auctions of Government Securities. Individual investors can also place bids as per the non-competitive scheme through the Retail Direct portal (https://rbiretaildirect.org.in).
6. Each bank or Primary Dealer (PD) on the basis of firm orders received from their constituents will submit a single consolidated non-competitive bid for individual security on behalf of its constituents in electronic format on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber system).
7. Allotment under the non-competitive segment will be at the weighted average rate of yield/price of the successful bids that will emerge in the auction on the basis of the competitive bidding.
Submission of Bids
8. Both competitive and non-competitive bids for the auction should be submitted in electronic format on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber system).
9. Bids in physical form will not be accepted except in extraordinary circumstances.
Business Continuity Plan (BCP)-IT failure
10. Only in the event of system failure, physical bids will be accepted. Such physical bids should be submitted to the Public Debt Office, Mumbai through (email; Phone no: 022-22603456, 022-22603457, 022-22603190) in the prescribed form which can be obtained from RBI website (https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_ViewForms.aspx) before the auction timing ends.
11. In case of technical difficulties, Core Banking Operations Team should be contacted (email; Phone no: 022-69870466, 022-69870415).
12. For other auction related difficulties, IDMD auction team can be contacted (email; Phone no: 022-22702431, 022-22705125).
Multiple Bids
13. An investor can submit more than one competitive bid in electronic format on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber system).
14. The aggregate amount of bids submitted by an investor in an auction should not exceed the notified amount of auction.
Decision Making Process
15. On the basis of bids received, the Reserve Bank will determine the minimum price/maximum yield up to which tenders for purchase of Government Security will be accepted at the auctions.
16. Bids quoted at rates lower than the minimum price/higher than the maximum yield determined by the Reserve Bank of India will be rejected.
17. Reserve Bank of India will have the full discretion to accept or reject any or all bids either wholly or partially without assigning any reason.
Issue of Securities
18. Issue of securities to the successful bidders will be by credit to Subsidiary General Ledger Account (SGL) or to Constituents’ Subsidiary General Ledger Account (CSGL), maintained with Reserve Bank of India.
Periodicity of Interest Payment
19. Interest on the Government Security will generally be paid half-yearly other than in case of securities with non-standard maturities. The exact periodicity of coupon payment is invariably mentioned in the specific notification for the issue of security.
Underwriting of the Government Securities
20. The underwriting of the Government Securities under auctions by the ‘Primary Dealers’ will be as per the “Revised Scheme of Underwriting Commitment and Liquidity Support” announced by the Reserve Bank vide circular RBI/2007-08/186 dated November 14, 2007 as amended from time to time.
Eligibility for Repurchase Transactions (Repo)
21. The securities will be eligible for Repurchase Transactions (Repo) as per the conditions mentioned in Master Direction – Reserve Bank of India (Repurchase Transactions (Repo)) Directions, 2025 as amended from time to time.
Eligibility for ‘When Issued’ Trading
22. The securities will be eligible for “When Issued” trading in accordance with the guidelines on ‘When Issued transactions in Central Government Securities’ issued by the Reserve Bank of India vide circular No. RBI/2018-19/25 dated July 24, 2018 as amended from time to time.
Investment by Non-Residents
23. Investments by Non-Residents are subject to the guidelines on ‘Fully Accessible Route’ for Investment by Non-residents in Government Securities and other related guidelines as issued by the Reserve Bank from time to time.

items.content: Mumbai: In just about six weeks, the Reserve Bank of India has drained banking system liquidity from a peak surplus of ₹11 lakh crore to ₹48,303 crore. How did the central bank withdraw this liquidity and what was the market impact of this? ET explains.Why was there a sudden gush in system liquidity?The banking system was suddenly flushed with liquidity after banks attracted $133 billion dollars from overseas Indians under the FCNR(B) scheme. Banks exchanged these dollars with the RBI through a swap facility, receiving rupee funds in return. Thus, system liquidity, which stood at a surplus of about ₹3.5 lakh crore in August, went up to over ₹11 lakh crore in September.What was the impact of this sudden liquidity surplus?The overnight rates, the weighted average call rate (WACR), went as low as 4.93% in mid September, or 30 bps below the repo rate. The WACR is supposed to be closely aligned with the RBI repo rate. However, crude oil prices were also beginning to rise, fuelling expectations of a rate hike by the RBI to contain inflationary pressures. But for a rate hike to translate into tighter monetary conditions, liquidity would ideally need to be neutral or in deficit, with WACR at the repo rate. The banking system, however, was flush with surplus funds, kept overnight rates below the repo rate and potentially diluting the impact of monetary tightening.Read more: Sundaram Mutual Fund announces launch of Equity Ex-Top 100 Long Short Fund through its SIF platform SelectWhat measures did the RBI take to absorb liquidity?The Reserve Bank of India was draining liquidity via temporary variable rate reverse repo (VRRR) auctions. But the WACR was still lower than the repo rate. The central bank also conducted sell-buy swaps of at least $10 billion in September in an effort to drain the excess cash.Lastly, the RBI increased banks daily cash reserve ratio (CRR) to 99%, from 90%. Raising the daily minimum to 99% reduced banks' flexibility to use those funds, helping Reserve Bank of India absorb surplus liquidity and keep overnight rates closer to its intended policy rate.With the RBI maintaining a calibrated tightening stance, the persistently large liquidity surplus and overnight rates trading below the repo rate were at odds with its policy stance. The central bank therefore needed to absorb excess liquidity to align money-market conditions more closely with its tightening stance.Read more: Jio Platforms' IPO-linked inflows boost rupee; elevated oil prices spur cautionAfter withdrawing a substantial amount of surplus liquidity, why did the RBI announce a variable rate repo (VRR) operation to inject funds ?The liquidity drain had pushed the WACR higher, with the rate rising to 5.75% last Friday, 25 basis points above the 5.50% repo rate on Friday. The WACR remains elevated at around 5.65% on Wednesday.To prevent overnight rates from rising too sharply as liquidity tightens, the RBI has temporarily infused funds through VRR operations. It conducted a ₹1 lakh crore VRR auction on Monday and a ₹50,000 crore operation on Friday.

The Sensex and Nifty, which ended around 0.5% lower each on Wednesday, have declined nearly 15% so far in 2026.Although there is no universally accepted definition of a market correction, a decline of 10% or more, but less than 20%, from a recent high is generally considered one.135103453Many smaller stocks have broadly withstood the weak sentiment in the market and sharp declines in blue chips over the past two years thanks to a flood of retail money through equity mutual funds and directly. But concerns over elevated valuations are beginning to catch up as investors evaluate whether the broader risk-off sentiment could impact future returns.Over the past two years, the midcap and smallcap indices have each entered correction territory three times. The midcap index fell nearly 19% from its January 2025 high to its February low. The smallcap index fell nearly 26% in this period, entering bear market territory but subsequently recovered.Read more: Sundaram Mutual Fund announces launch of Equity Ex-Top 100 Long Short Fund through its SIF platform SelectAnand Radhakrishnan, managing director of Sundaram Mutual, said some domestic investors had shifted money from large-cap stocks to mid-cap and smallcaps, viewing them as safe amid foreign investors' selling. This perception could be slowly shifting with valuations rising."What is perceived as a safe space can gradually become unsafe as valuations go up. We are seeing corrections even in midcap and smallcap stocks, although this may not yet be visible at the index level," he said.Read more: Jio IPO Day 1: Issue subscribed 3 times on strong QIB push; retail portion booked 68%. Check GMPOf the 97 stocks in the midcap index that have hit 52-week highs so far in 2026, two have fallen 40-45% from their peaks, 18 have declined 30-40%, 35 have lost 20-30%, and 42 are down 1-20%.In the smallcap segment, 172 stocks have hit 52-week highs so far this year. Of these, nine have declined 40-45% from their peaks, 32 have fallen 30-40%, 54 have lost 20-30%, and 77 are down 1-20%.In the microcap segment, 165 stocks have hit 52-week highs this year. Of these, seven have fallen 40-50%, 23 have declined 30-40%, 64 have lost 20-30%, and 70 are down 1-20%.Even after the recent declines, valuations are still at a premium over large-caps. The mid-cap index is currently trading at a 42% premium to the Nifty, compared with its five-year average of 40%. The small-cap index is trading at a 45% premium, below its five-year average of 75%, analysts said."Small and mid-cap valuations have come off from very high levels but remain on the higher side," said Atul Bhole, executive vice-president and fund manager at Kotak Mahindra AMC. "That said, the aggregate earnings outlook is holding up very well, with 16-20% earnings growth projected for the midcap and smallcap universe. Any improvement in news flows on the war, crude prices and yields could cause a relief rally."

items.author: Shrishti Bisht
items.content:
Agentic AI startup Karta AI has raised $3 Mn (around ₹28 Cr) in a seed funding round led by PeerCapital and Cedar Hill Capital. The round also saw participation from Wyser VC, CDM Capital and Seedstars.
The startup intends to use the fresh capital to expand its go-to-market (GTM) strategy and distribution over the next two years. A portion will also help it expand its product development, particularly capabilities around emerging AI technologies such as self learning, cofounder and CEO Vijaypal Singh told Inc42.
Founded in 2024 by former Razorpay executives Vijaypal Singh and Abhishek Kushwaha, Karta AI offers an omnichannel customer communication platform spanning voice, chat, email and WhatsApp.
The startup focuses primarily on voice-based interactions, targeting complex inbound queries that require coordination across multiple enterprise systems rather than routine frequently asked questions.
It claims to handle around 2 Mn customer conversations a month across more than 25 languages. According to Singh, it has 10-12 paying customers, including PhonePe, Pine Labs, Bajaj and Aavas.
Karta AI deploys its AI agents across customer servicing and retention workflows at financial institutions.
The startup claims its agent resolves around 70% of borrower queries end to end without human intervention, reducing the cost per query by approximately 50%. These queries include requests for loan disbursal updates, statements of account, foreclosure statements and the release of property documents.
It focuses on inbound interactions, where customers contact businesses to resolve issues such as failed payments, blocked cards, loan-related queries and insurance claims. Unlike outbound calls, which businesses typically initiate for a specific purpose, inbound conversations can involve multiple queries and require AI agents to retrieve information and execute actions across several systems.
Singh said he and Kushwaha began working on Karta AI after leaving fintech major Razorpay, where they had worked on internal AI automation. The startup initially focused on chat-based automation before expanding into voice in August 2025.
Karta AI targets level 2 (L2) and level 3 (L3) queries, which require AI agents to interpret multiple customer intents, retrieve information from different systems and execute workflows. This differs from level 1 (L1) queries, such as basic FAQs or requests that can be resolved through a single API call.
For instance, a borrower may call a lender to check loan disbursal status and request a foreclosure statement in the same conversation. The agent must identify both intents, retrieve the relevant information and initiate the required workflows.
Singh said Karta AI has achieved 70-80% end-to-end automation in its inbound proof-of-concept (PoC) deployments and has won all such PoCs so far.
The focus on complex queries reflects their disproportionate cost. According to Singh, L1 queries account for 30-40% of customer service volumes but only around 10% of costs. L2 queries contribute another 30-40% of volumes, while L3 queries make up the remaining 10-20%. Together, he estimates, L2 and L3 queries account for around 80% of customer service costs.
The platform does not automate every interaction. Queries involving fraud or other high-risk matters, along with processes lacking clearly defined standard operating procedures (SOPs), are routed to human agents. Customers can also request a human representative.
How Karta AI’s AI Tech Works
Karta AI’s proprietary context engine is designed to help its agents manage multi-intent conversations. While conventional voice AI systems typically convert speech to text, process the query through a large language model (LLM) and generate a spoken response, Karta AI adds a layer that identifies customer intent and retrieves relevant enterprise data before generating an answer.
The engine draws on SOPs, knowledge bases, previous conversations and API data. This allows an agent to handle follow-up requests within the same call without treating each query in isolation.
Karta AI integrates with enterprise systems to execute customer-facing and back-office workflows. It uses models from OpenAI and Google’s Gemini family, alongside open-source models such as Kimi and Gemma, Singh said.
Its voice platform supports around 25 Indian languages, while its chat offering supports more than 200 languages. The voice system is designed to accommodate Hindi-English code-switching, regional accents and dialects, though performance varies across languages.
Given its focus on financial services, the startup has built compliance measures and guardrails into the platform. Singh said agents are tested by Karta AI’s team, customers and AI-based testing systems before deployment.
Karta AI primarily serves Indian businesses in banking, financial services and insurance (BFSI), where high customer interaction volumes and complex back-office processes offer opportunities for automation. It plans to develop reusable, industry-specific capabilities before expanding into international markets.
 
The post Karta AI Raises $3 Mn To Automate Inbound Calls For BFSI Players appeared first on Inc42 Media.

items.author: Gaurav Bagur
items.content:
Healthtech startup CureBay raised around ₹100 Cr ($10.6 Mn) in a pre-Series C funding round, comprising over ₹69 Cr in equity led by IvyCap Ventures alongside existing investors and around ₹30 Cr in debt from Trifecta Capital, Alteria Capital and VentureSoul Partners.
CureBay cofounder and CEO Priyadarshi Mohapatra told Inc42 that the round came amid strong investor interest. The startup will use the proceeds to expand geographically, strengthen its delivery network and invest in its AI and technology capabilities.
The healthtech startup, which currently operates in Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Bihar, plans to enter Telangana and Andhra Pradesh markets next. It aims to grow its network of rural clinics from 250 to 800 over the next two to three years.
CureBay connects patients in underserved areas with healthcare providers through a combination of rural clinics, local community health workers and a digital platform linking patients to doctors, hospitals, diagnostic laboratories and pharmacies. It also uses AI-assisted screening and care coordination to support patient care.
The startup is also investing in GPUs and training AI models to screen patients and assess health risks. Its existing AI products cover areas such as skin conditions, dental health and haemoglobin screening, with plans to expand these capabilities.
“We have a full suite of AI products for areas like skin, dental, and haemoglobin. We will keep adding more products and continue investing in width as well as depth,” Mohapatra said.
CureBay also runs Kavach, a subscription programme designed to encourage preventive care by offering consultations and support for medicines, diagnostics and certain hospitalisation-related costs.
The startup claims to have served over 12 Lakh patients and connected more than 270 doctors and 1,000 healthcare professionals across 4,500 pincodes.
Prior to this round, CureBay had raised over $34.6 Mn from investors including Bertelsmann India Investments, British International Investment and Elevar Equity.
While the startup is yet to file its audited FY26 financial statements, Mohapatra said it closed the fiscal year with an annual recurring revenue (ARR) of nearly ₹170 Cr. It aims to double this figure by the end of FY27.
“We broke even at an operating EBITDA level in FY26. Currently, our monthly run rate is about ₹20 Cr, and we expect the number to grow almost 50% from now till March,” he told Inc42.
Mohapatra attributed the growth to customers spending more on CureBay as they increasingly view it as a trusted healthcare partner, alongside the expansion into new markets.
However, the startup remains loss-making at the company level. Mohapatra said entering new markets entails fresh expenditure, while profitability would depend on reaching a more stable operating scale.
“When we stop expanding and we reach a stable state, we will be net positive at a company level. So the important metric for us to track is operating EBITDA,” he said.

items.title: Protest as a pillar of democracy
items.summary:
Protest helps close the gap between the promise of democracy and the formal structures we actually have
Originally published on Global Voices
Image via Canva Pro.
This piece is part of Global Voices’ September 2026 Spotlight series, “Protest in Democracy.” With this Spotlight, we seek to explore the many forms of protest, the tactics states use to delegitimize and suppress them, and the complex relationship between protest and democracy. You can support this coverage by donating here.
Democracy is often presented as an orderly, structured system of representation and deliberation, colorless and linear like an organizational version of the faux-classical architecture so many democratic countries adopt for their government buildings. Voting leads to representatives, debates lead to votes on laws, participation leads to action, like columns leading to a pediment.
But democracy is not actually about cushy debating chambers or political speeches — or not only about that. Democracy means rul
items.author: Malka Older
items.content:
Protest helps close the gap between the promise of democracy and the formal structures we actually have
Originally published on Global Voices
Image via Canva Pro.
This piece is part of Global Voices’ September 2026 Spotlight series, “Protest in Democracy.” With this Spotlight, we seek to explore the many forms of protest, the tactics states use to delegitimize and suppress them, and the complex relationship between protest and democracy. You can support this coverage by donating here.
Democracy is often presented as an orderly, structured system of representation and deliberation, colorless and linear like an organizational version of the faux-classical architecture so many democratic countries adopt for their government buildings. Voting leads to representatives, debates lead to votes on laws, participation leads to action, like columns leading to a pediment.
But democracy is not actually about cushy debating chambers or political speeches — or not only about that. Democracy means rule by the people, and in most of the systems we call democracies today, the people’s role is for the most part narrowed to voting, and often a curtailed, difficult, limited vote that does little for accountability or expressing preferences on specific issues.
Protest is one of the ways we close the gap between the promise of democracy and the formal structures we have. With protest, the people can express general emotional responses or very specific policy proposals; we can punctuate the long intervals of electoral cycles to influence government outside of the voting booth; and perhaps most importantly, we build coalitions and solidarity, forming a collective consciousness of our democratic responsibilities.
Voting is a single, standardized, and fairly isolated action. Protest, on the other hand, unfolds in dozens, if not hundreds, of permutations, letting us — the people — express our creativity along with our civic engagement. One of the wonderful things about this spotlight has been seeing the sheer range of capacity and ingenuity as people use protest to inspire others, express anger or determination, and pressure governments and other decision-makers.
Maybe the most obvious example of this in the spotlight is the collaborative article on protest music, with its examples of not just different songs, but different styles and approaches and even understanding of what it means to use music for advocacy. In Japan, young people are finding new paths into activism, like handing out placards, while the Cockroach Janta Party in India has used memes and online jokes to mobilize young people right from the start of the movement.
Severe oppression requires more creativity, as this article about the evolution of street art in Russia points out. Similarly, Russians — many of them in exile — used allusion and wordplay in online videos to get their messages across.
That raises the question, ably explored in this piece, about whether online and offline protest are equally effective, and what their different strengths and weaknesses are. And, if the digital world has enabled new forms of protest, it has also activated new means of repression. Our friends at Ranking Digital Rights contributed this well-researched article about the complicity of telecoms in internet shutdowns in Africa. This piece, from AlgorithmWatch, details the Russian surveillance software being used against protesters in Georgia. And the virtual world can be used to hijack, undermine, or redirect protest energy, as this case study from Funky Citizens in Romania details.
As vibrant as protests are in the moment, though, it’s also important to ask about the long-term impact, the consequences, both good and bad. The protests in Bangladesh two years ago were successful in the sense that they led to a change of government; this article asks whether that change of government led to a meaningful difference in democratic accountability. And this powerful piece from Nepal follows up with those involved in the Gen Z protests there last year, tracking the long-term impacts of injuries and trauma.
As with all our monthly spotlights, this one is in many ways about showing the common threads that link all of our countries, as well as the exceptions that can open us to new ideas or inspire us to a different kind of action. This spotlight is, then, a form of protest in its own right: a way of reasserting that protest is legitimate, important for democracy, and everywhere.
Written by Malka Older
