items.content:
The Chair the Local Organising Committee of the flag off of All Progressives Congress(APC) 2027 Presidential Campaign and the Deputy Governor of Kaduna State, Dr Hadiza Balarabe, has said that Kaduna is set to receive President Bola Tinubu on Saturday.
Dr Balarabe disclosed this to journalists after, she and members of her team inspected facilities at the Kaduna Township Stadium, the venue of the flag off, on Wednesday evening.
‘’I’m comfortable with what has been done so far; we have the holding area, the conveniences are ready, the pavilions are ready. What remains is the markings for the different states,’’ she added.
The Deputy Governor said that the LOC has deliberated extensively about security before, during and after the presidential rally, with seasoned security professionals at both state and federal levels.
Dr Balarabe said that people will be screened before gaining access into the stadium and she assured everyone of their safety in the arena.
According to her, the LOC envisages a large turnout of party members and supporters from across the country because the North West is an APC stronghold.
Also speaking, the Commissioner of Information and Culture, Malam Ahmed Maiyaki disclosed that mobilisation is still ongoing, adding that hotels and service apartments have been fully booked within Kaduna metropolis.
The Commissioner said that Kaduna State is privileged and honoured to host the flag off of the Presidential Campaign and its citizens are eager to welcome President Tinubu.
Maiyaki pointed out that hosting the maiden campaign rally in Kaduna is an opportunity for the people of the state to demonstrate their support for the president and APC.
He said that in the last three and half years, Kaduna State has benefitted from the APC-led administration in terms of projects and appointment of its citizens at the federal level.
He listed the conversion of Federal College of Education Zaria to a university, the recent conversion of Kaduna Polytechnic to a Federal University of Technology and the 122km Mando-Birnin Gwari road and proposed Kaduna Light Rail Project.

items.author: Gaurav Bagur
items.content:
Serial entrepreneur Ajeet Singh, who previously cofounded unicorns such as Nutanix and ThoughtSpot, has announced the launch of his third venture, called Different.
Emerging out of stealth mode, the AI-powered martech startup has now raised $48 Mn (nearly ₹453 Cr) in its seed funding round led by General Catalyst. The round also saw participation from Lightspeed Venture Partners.
Meanwhile, former Asana executive Abhishek Pani and former chief technology and product officer (CTPO) at PharmEasy, Abhinav Yajurvedi, have also joined Singh as cofounders at Different.
“Different is an AI marketing system that runs demand generation end-to-end for lean B2B marketing teams,” Singh said in a post on LinkedIn. The startup has teams in San Francisco and Bengaluru, per its website.
Different aims to address enterprise bottlenecks such as hiring specialised talent, engaging multiple external agencies and managing disparate software tools. The startup’s AI platform plans, creates, executes and scales personalised content across channels in accordance with the business context, strategy, audience, and other parameters specified by the user.
It also learns from the results and adjusts accordingly to optimise performance. Prior to its public launch, Different tested its services with early corporate customers, including software firms Descope and Motif.
An alumnus of IIT Kanpur and IIM Calcutta, Singh has previously worked at companies like Oracle, Honeywell and PwC. Notably, this is not the first time that Singh is setting up his own business.
He previously also cofounded Nutanix in 2009, a hybrid cloud unicorn that went on to list on the Nasdaq in 2016. Singh stepped down from the company in 2012 to launch AI-powered analytics platform ThoughtSpot that same year. ThoughtSpot has raised over $670 Mn to date and was last pegged at nearly $4.5 Bn.
The development comes at a time when a growing number of founders are starting new ventures. Last month, Livspace founder Saurabh Jain and former executive Lalit Mittal banded together to launch a new venture, Gravity.
In May, Zeta founder Bhavin Turakhia launched a new AI startup, Neo, with a personal investment of $30 Mn. Prior to this, Healthians founder Deepak Sahni also said that he was building a new healthtech venture UN:BLOC.
Earlier this year in April, Inc42 reported exclusively that BharatPe cofounder Shashvat Nakrani was set to join Dubai-based luxury ecommerce platform Luxury For You as its cofounder and CEO.
The post Nutanix Founder Ajeet Singh Floats New AI Martech Startup Different appeared first on Inc42 Media.

Hon. Bashir Saidu, former Chief of Staff to Governor Nasiru El-Rufai, has denied betraying the former governor who is currently in detention.
Saidu, who was among the former allies of El-Rufai that announced that they had parted ways with him, spoke in an interview with RFI Hausa.
Daily Trust had reported how El-Rufai recently said some people he stood by during difficult times had abandoned him, a comment which sparked further controversies.
But in the latest interview, the former Chief of Staff said he and El-Rufa’i jointly formed the structure through which the former governor attained power, at the heyday of their political activities.

He said, “We were the first to suffer before him. I was taken to prison on New year eve. I spent 50 days there. I was moved from one court to another, until the judge who agreed to attend the trial revoked my bail. I was taken back to prison again where I spent 54 days. Is there any night I have not seen?
“I also spent the last Eid-Adha in prison. It is an outright lie to say we abandoned him. We only left when the betrayal became apparent. We learnt the person we submitted to did not value us. We moved where we are valued.
“Those making the noise are not familiar with my relationship with Mallam. It has graduated to family level.”
Saidu argued that he was among those who brought El-Rufai into politics.
“We begged him to join politics. We have been in politics since the time of Abiola in the SDP. Professor Ango Abdullahi, Madakin Zazzau, San Turaki Babba are alive. Our first chairman, Ibrahim Yaro Tela, Ibrahim Zailani have passed away.”
The former Chief of Staff argued that the presumed El-Rufai’s political structure is overrated, adding the former governor still owed them.
On alleged betrayal, Saidu said they were pushing for Malam Jaafaru to emerge as their candidate in Kaduna unaware that El-Rufai’s had already anointed a candidate.

items.author: Guest Contributor
items.content:
Emerging technologies have become central to systems of coercion and control
Originally published on Global Voices
An aerial view showing destruction in Rafah, Gaza Strip, on January 21, 2025. Photo by Ashraf Amra on Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO).
By Jalal Abukhater
This post is part of Global Voices’ October 2026 Spotlight series, “Big Tech and Authoritarianism.” In this Spotlight, we explore how Big Tech facilitates and hinders authoritarian governments and practices, and how these choices influence the Global South. You can support this coverage by donating here.
For Palestinians, the relationship between technology and authoritarianism is a lived reality, rather than predictions or science fiction. Israel’s settler-colonial regime has long fused military force with legal, economic and technological mechanisms to dominate Palestinian life.
Surveillance, data harvesting, facial recognition, telecommunications blackouts, digital censorship and algorithmic systems are now woven into this architecture of control. The genocidal war on Gaza has exposed the consequences with devastating clarity, where technologies built to collect, process and classify information have been absorbed into systems that surveil, target and kill Palestinians.
But Palestine is also a warning about what comes next. Technologies developed, tested and refined under occupation do not stay there. They become products, expertise and business models that circulate globally. What emerges is a political economy in which military and intelligence institutions, technology companies, investors and governments converge around the extraction and processing of data as a means of exercising power.
This is one of the central arguments of Digital Domination, a publication of The Arab Center for the Advancement of Social Media’s Maryam Abu Daqqa Fellowship, which brings together five studies on artificial intelligence, surveillance, data extraction and corporate power in Palestine and beyond. The fellowship is named after Maryam Abu Daqqa, a Palestinian journalist murdered by Israel in Gaza in August 2025 while documenting life under siege. Across different cases, the research points to the same transformation, showing how emerging technologies have become central to systems of coercion and control. It is becoming their infrastructure.
Intimate ties
Israel’s surveillance industry shows this plainly. It operates through intimate ties between military and intelligence institutions, private companies, venture capital and international markets. Tools tested on Palestinians are refined, repackaged as commercial products and exported to the world as security solutions. This is no accident of a thriving tech sector. It is a political and economic system in which security technologies gain value precisely because of their capacity to monitor, classify and control populations.
The violence these systems enable is increasingly literal. Investigations into Israel’s AI-assisted targeting systems, including Lavender, The Gospel and Where’s Daddy, have documented how machine-learning systems and mass surveillance data have been folded into the identification and targeting of Palestinians in Gaza.
A new film, NAZA, produced by The Guardian and built on testimony from 24 Israeli military and intelligence insiders, details the secret systems used to select people for bombing in their homes at night, in the knowledge that their families would be killed, too. At a military conference in London in late June, an executive from the Israeli arms manufacturer Elbit Systems presented a slide crediting its digital command system with 850,000 “real-time intel targets” across Gaza and Lebanon between October 2023 and the end of 2025. The company has since tried to recast the figure as aggregate system activity, a claim that sits uneasily with the slide itself.
The significance is not that an algorithm has replaced human violence. It is that these systems increase the scale, speed and bureaucratic distance at which violence is organised, while cloaking life-and-death decisions in the appearance of technical objectivity. In June, Amnesty International and more than 100 other signatories warned that systems such as Lavender, Gospel and Where’s Daddy dilute human responsibility and obscure international crimes behind a veneer of algorithmic objectivity.
Digital erasure
The same architecture extends beyond weapons. At 7amleh, we have documented how platforms suppress Palestinian speech, how state-linked actors use commercial platforms to shape information environments, and how Meta profits from content and accounts tied to illegal settlement expansion and violent rhetoric against Palestinians.
Two studies in Digital Domination make the point from different angles. One examines the Israeli government’s use of Google advertising to place its preferred narratives in front of people searching for information. Another examines algorithmic voice surveillance, showing how Palestinian speech itself is captured as data for systems of control.
This is where digital erasure becomes inseparable from physical violence. The destruction of Gaza also threatens the evidence and memory through which Palestinians can establish what was done to them. Platforms have removed or restricted documentation of Israeli violence, while physical archives, cultural records, cemeteries and the evidence beneath Gaza’s rubble have been destroyed or put at risk.
The UN refugee agency UNRWA ran a covert 10-month operation to smuggle millions of documents out of Gaza and East Jerusalem, amid fears that the originals, and even their digital copies, could be seized or destroyed. This September, the UN Special Rapporteur on the occupied Palestinian territory, Francesca Albanese, warned that Israel’s clearance of Gaza’s rubble could destroy evidence of atrocity crimes, and called it unacceptable that Gaza’s reconstruction be conditioned on the erasure of its past and the evidence needed to secure justice for its victims.
The problem, therefore, goes far beyond whether a post stays online. It concerns who retains the power to document reality, preserve history and establish evidence after violence has taken place. We have described this wider process as platformicide: the destruction and denial of the digital spaces through which Palestinians communicate, organise, document and preserve collective memory.
Epistemic power
Now the same problem is entering the systems through which people increasingly access knowledge.
Large language models and AI agents are becoming intermediaries between people and information, yet they are acutely vulnerable to manipulation. Microsoft’s security researchers have documented “AI recommendation poisoning,” in which companies embed hidden instructions that plant persistent biases in AI assistants’ memory, with 31 companies across 14 industries identified.
Salesforce researchers found that web-search agents fed authoritative-looking false content will reproduce it as fact: in controlled tests, around 80 percent of queries returned the attacker’s preferred answer, and in more realistic conditions, with poisoned documents buried among more than 100,000 clean ones, nearly one in four did.
For Palestine, this is not hypothetical. Drop Site News reported that Israel awarded a USD 46.5 million contract to Brad Parscale’s firm Clock Tower X to build networks of websites and blog posts aimed at shaping what chatbots tell users about Gaza, content written for machines rather than readers. Journalists have since put leading chatbots to the test to see how far the campaign has reached.
A society already subjected to censorship, propaganda, data extraction and the destruction of evidence is now entering an information environment in which people increasingly depend on AI systems to tell them what is true, what happened and what matters, and in which the party responsible for the violence is paying to shape those answers.
The danger is not only inaccurate information. It is the concentration of epistemic power in systems whose training data, retrieval mechanisms and decision-making processes remain largely opaque. Information manipulation can move from suppressing a Palestinian post to shaping what an AI system retrieves, remembers, or presents as knowledge.
A warning to heed
Meanwhile, the technologies and companies enabling these systems are becoming embedded in public life elsewhere. In the UK, Palantir’s GBP 330 million National Health Service (NHS) contract led a parliamentary committee to call the company’s growing public-sector role “an unacceptable point of weakness”, and the government is now reviewing the contract amid pressure to use a break clause in 2027. In the United States, Amnesty International has documented how technology from Palantir and Babel Street is used to monitor and target migrants and people speaking out for Palestinian rights.
These developments should be understood as part of a wider transformation in how power is organised. Palestine shows what happens when data, surveillance infrastructure, artificial intelligence and corporate power are integrated into systems of domination. It also shows how quickly technologies developed in one context travel into another, stripped of the political conditions of their making and repackaged as innovation, efficiency, security or digital transformation.
The authoritarianism of the digital age does not require every state to build its own surveillance apparatus. It can purchase one. It does not require governments to control every source of information. It can outsource the infrastructure through which information is filtered, ranked and delivered. It does not require violence to disappear from public view. It can make violence more scalable, more automated and harder to attribute.
Palestinians are already living with the consequences. The rest of the world should heed the warning before these systems become too deeply embedded in its own institutions to challenge.
Jalal Abukhater is a human rights advocate based in Jerusalem and Policy Manager at 7amleh, The Arab Center for the Advancement of Social Media.

items.content:
Five Imams from Dorowa-Babuje, Luggere and Jol communities in Barkin Ladi Local Government Area of Plateau State have raised concerns over what they described as “security threats” affecting their areas in recent times.
The Islamic clerics are from the five Juma’at Mosques in the communities.
This development comes amid heightened tensions in Barikin Ladi, Mangu, Bokkos and Riyom LGAs where the state government has imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew to restore order following killings and attacks in the area.
Worried by the security situation in their areas, the clerics, including Imam Bashir Khamis, Imam Salihu Muhammad, Imam Idris Usman, Imam Aliyu Mahmud and Imam Yahaya, called on the government to take action to address the problems before they get out of hand.
Gov. Yusuf celebrates Kwankwaso at 70
‎Alert Group wins Fastest-Growing financial services group of the year at 2026 BAFI awards
They said the current situation was a source of concern, hence the need to draw the attention of the state and federal governments to threats capable of disrupting peace in the region.
Speaking during a visit to the Daily Trust office in Jos on Tuesday, the Imams led by Imam Yahaya of the Juma’a Mosque in Luggere, said the current situation in the area is alarming.
He said, “We are in difficult times in these communities. Unlawful arrest of our members without any cogent reason is the order of the day. Our social media team who help to share what we are going through with the world are being arrested and some threatened. Destruction of property by security personnel and rampant killing of both humans and animals are a daily occurrence. Communities are attacked and houses burned without any reason.”
According to the Imams, they are not opposed to any lawful investigation or to security agencies carrying out their duties, but they said the agencies should be impartial and treat them equally with their neighbours.
He said, “We appeal to be treated equally with our Christian neighbours and that no one should be spared if found guilty, irrespective of their ethno-religious background. We also appeal that security personnel should stop vandalising our properties and burning our houses. We also need security in our communities and in our places of worship during Juma’at prayers, and security agencies should allow cattle to graze.”

items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
Anthropic recorded a net loss of $80.7 billion in the first half of 2026, sharply wider than its $13 billion loss during the same period last year, according to a draft IPO prospectus reviewed by Reuters.
Most of the loss did not come from Anthropic’s day-to-day operations. The figure included a $72 billion accounting charge caused by an increase in the estimated value of bonds that can eventually convert into Anthropic shares.
Anthropic is expected to go public in November, while some investors are now considering a lower valuation of around $1.5 trillion following its latest financial disclosures, Reuters reported last week.
Computing Spending Nearly Quadrupled
Anthropic’s infrastructure costs also increased significantly as it continued investing heavily in AI development.
The company spent nearly $9 billion on computing capacity and infrastructure during the first half, compared with $2.3 billion during the same period last year, according to the S-1 filing.
Anthropic has committed to spending at least $518 billion over 10 years on cloud services, computing and infrastructure.
The figures highlight the enormous cost of developing advanced AI systems as investors increasingly question whether spending on chips, data centers and computing infrastructure will generate sufficient returns.
Anthropic did not respond to Reuters’ request for comment.
Revenue Reached $16.8 Billion in Third Quarter
Anthropic told prospective IPO investors at an October 14 meeting that its third-quarter revenue reached $16.8 billion, up 45% from the previous quarter, Reuters reported, citing people familiar with the matter.
The growth eased some concerns about the company’s rising expenses, but some investors were disappointed by the slower sequential growth.
Anthropic’s revenue had more than doubled between the first and second quarters, reaching $11.6 billion in Q2.
A weaker-than-expected reception for Anthropic’s IPO could also affect sentiment across the wider AI market, with investors closely watching the offering ahead of rival OpenAI’s potential listing next year.
Anthropic Lost $42 Billion in 2025
Reuters previously reported that Anthropic posted a $42 billion net loss in 2025, with most of that figure also resulting from an accounting charge linked to convertible notes.
As Anthropic’s valuation increased, the estimated fair value of those notes tripled compared with the previous year.
Excluding that charge, Anthropic reported an operating loss of around $8.1 billion on $4.6 billion in revenue in 2025.
The company has benefited from growing demand for Claude Code, its coding assistant used by developers to write software and build applications.
The latest figures show that Anthropic’s revenue is growing rapidly, but its computing, infrastructure, and financing-related costs remain extremely high as it prepares for one of the most closely watched AI IPOs.

items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
Meta has suspended the conversation-sharing feature in Muse AI after security researchers found that public DNS records could expose thousands of shared chat links.
Security researchers at Claroc discovered the issue over the weekend. Ars Technica first reported on the findings, while Meta later confirmed to Benzinga that it had paused the feature while reviewing the report.
Researchers Found Around 6,800 Shared Chats
Claroc said Muse created shared conversation URLs using a predictable structure that included the title of each conversation.
Those addresses were also written into public domain name system records. As a result, researchers could use passive DNS searches, which examine archived DNS activity, to discover shared conversations.
Claroc said one such search returned thousands of links and identified approximately 6,800 shared Muse conversations.
Researchers accessed some of those chats and found sensitive information, including meeting details involving a major AI lab, a small-business loan application, a bank fraud alert containing partial account information, a company vacation calendar and internal business documents.
Meta Suspends Muse Sharing
Meta said the Muse bug bounty program was created so security researchers could identify issues and help improve the product.
The company noted that when users shared a Muse conversation, the feature generated a webpage that anyone with the link could access.
However, Meta said it had now paused the sharing functionality while reviewing Claroc’s findings and considering changes to how those links can be discovered.
Following Meta’s update, Claroc said researchers could no longer access a sample of the previously available links.
“We are glad to see it closed this quickly,” Claroc said.
Muse Has Faced Previous Privacy Concerns
The incident follows another privacy-related controversy involving Muse.
In September, Inc. technology columnist Jason Aten alleged that Muse accessed private messages on his Mac even though he had not enabled the system’s “Full Disk Access” permission.
Meta spokesperson Andy Stone rejected the claim at the time, saying Muse can access Apple’s Messages app only when users explicitly opt in.
Meta Is Betting on Muse as a Major AI Product
The issue comes just before Meta is scheduled to report its third-quarter financial results after the market closes on Wednesday.
Analysts expect revenue of $63.36 billion, up from $51.24 billion a year earlier. Meta has beaten revenue estimates for more than 10 consecutive quarters.
Tech analyst Dan Ives expects Meta to monetize its roughly 3.5 billion-user base through the Muse AI agent, including through Facebook and Instagram.
Truist, according to market strategist Shay Boloor, estimates that Muse could generate around $29 billion in revenue by 2030, including approximately $11 billion from subscriptions.
Meta shares closed Tuesday at $694.25, down 1.59%, before rising 0.11% to $695 in after-hours trading.

The committee also expressed concern over the PMDC's practice of collecting question booklets from candidates after the examination and not allowing them to retain copies. Members questioned why the paper had not been made public, stressing that transparency in the question bank and examination process was essential to safeguarding merit.
PMDC officials said the question booklets were collected to protect the question bank and prevent candidates appearing in subsequent years from gaining an unfair advantage. The committee, however, rejected the justification.
The committee also questioned the PMDC's recently introduced policy requiring students intending to pursue medical education abroad to take the MDCAT, which was subsequently withdrawn following the committee's intervention.
Expressing dissatisfaction with the inquiry report, the committee directed the Ministry of National Health Services to conduct a fresh inquiry into the complaints within one week and submit its findings to the committee.

items.author: Shraddha Goled
items.content:
A private key meant to vouch for the security of websites around the world turned out to be the number 4.
That was one of the weaknesses researchers found in eight intermediate certificate authority (CA) certificates issued by Bengaluru-based eMudhra.
The discovery prompted Google, Mozilla, Apple, and Microsoft to block the affected certificates, triggering a wider effort to protect browsers, applications, and enterprise systems. The incident also rattled investors and eMudhra shares hit their 20% lower circuit at ₹431.55 on the BSE today.
The immediate concern is whether software still trusting the compromised keys could accept fraudulent certificates. A related challenge is replacing legitimate certificates affected by browser makers’ decision to withdraw trust in a parent certificate.
A digital certificate acts as a digital identity that allows a browser to verify a website’s authenticity. Certificate authorities issue these certificates and vouch for their authenticity. eMudhra is among the certifying authorities licensed by India’s Controller of Certifying Authorities (CCA).
The incident goes beyond one company. It shows how much of the internet’s security rests on a chain of trust that one weak link can undermine, raising questions about how India oversees companies that participate in this global infrastructure.
What Happened
On October 17, a researcher named Wayne notified the Chrome Root Program, which forwarded the report to Mozilla, and also contacted eMudhra and the Apple and Microsoft root programmes, reporting that he had obtained the private keys corresponding to eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates. He demonstrated control of each key by signing a message with it “We have a problem here – Wayne”.
The full details of how the flaw was discovered and fixed have now been published by Dennis Jackson, a cryptographic engineer at Mozilla.
Intermediate CAs can issue certificates that websites use to establish their identity. Anyone holding the corresponding private keys could potentially issue fraudulent certificates for websites they did not control, allowing affected clients that still trusted those CAs to accept the certificates.
The keys were not stolen, but the researcher found that they had been generated with insufficient randomness, making them easy to reconstruct from the public certificates.
Six of the eight intermediates were intended for website security through TLS, while two were intended for software signing. Chrome, Apple, Microsoft, and Firefox blocked the affected TLS intermediates.
What eMudhra Says
In a statement on its website, eMudhra said it was investigating the incident and reviewing its security controls and operating procedures. The company said the eight intermediate CAs were created during a key generation ceremony on April 30, 2025, and the hierarchy entered browser trust lists in mid-2025. It said its roots and issuing CAs had undergone independent audits in each of the previous two years, but did not identify the auditors or disclose the scope of those audits.
eMudhra said only one of the eight affected intermediates had been deployed in production and that none had issued end-entity certificates. It said it revoked all eight intermediates and was working with affected customers and root programmes to address the incident.
The company also said the incident did not affect its Indian Digital Signature Certificate (DSC) and eSign businesses, which operate on infrastructure separate from its global TLS business. On October 21, eMudhra said the affected global TLS business accounted for around 1% of its revenue.
India faced a similar trust-related incident in 2014, following the misissuance of certificates for Google domains by the National Informatics Centre. At the time, Google restricted the India CCA root certificate in Chrome to a limited set of domains, including gov.in and nic.in.
eMudhra has been a licensed certifying authority under India’s IT Act since 2008. The company has also worked with public- and private-sector organisations, including banks and government agencies.
The company provides digital identity, authentication and security solutions to businesses, financial institutions and governments. Its services include digital signature certificates (DSCs), electronic signatures and tools that help organisations secure digital transactions and manage identities.
In India, its DSCs are used for activities such as filing documents with government portals, including GST, the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, and income tax systems. Its eSign services also support paperless digital workflows.
Many critical government websites, including the Aadhaar issuer UIDAI as well as websites of the Indian postal services and the income tax filing portal, use eMudhra certificates or other technology developed by the company.
Why It Matters Beyond eMudhra
Browsers and operating systems rely on lists of trusted certificate authorities. A compromised intermediate CA can therefore threaten trust beyond the authority’s direct customers.
With the compromised keys, an attacker could potentially issue fraudulent website certificates to impersonate legitimate sites and intercept traffic, provided the affected systems still trusted those certificates and the attacker’s other technical requirements were met. The two code-signing intermediates also raised concerns about malicious software being presented as coming from a trusted publisher on systems that accepted their signatures.
“When news like this comes out about a company that supports our PKI infrastructure, it raises concerns about both the company’s reputation and the country’s reputation. Even a relatively small mistake or a gap in the validation process can affect confidence in the wider industry. People may start to question whether PKI infrastructure provided by Indian companies can be trusted,” said Abhijeet Zilpelwar, cofounder and chief technology officer at pi-labs.
The Long Tail: Software And Devices
Updated browsers received protections quickly. The harder problem is software and devices that do not receive the same updates or reliably check certificate revocation.
Applications, programming languages, package managers and build pipelines can use their own certificate bundles or the operating system’s trust store. Some do not reliably check revocation status, meaning they may continue to accept certificates unless their trust configuration or software is updated.
Embedded devices can be harder to update. Routers, cameras, payment terminals and industrial controllers running old firmware may continue to trust affected certificate chains if their software does not receive the relevant protections.
For Indian enterprises, exposure does not depend solely on whether they bought certificates directly from eMudhra. The company says none of the eight affected intermediates issued certificates to end users, and Google found no certificates chaining to the six website-security intermediates in public Certificate Transparency logs before blocking them.
However, systems that continue to trust the affected intermediates may remain exposed if they lack effective revocation checks or have not received relevant security updates.
Potentially affected systems include backend applications, servers and devices running outdated software, including those operated by organisations that use another certificate provider. Banking, fintech, e-governance and other businesses relying on certificate-based authentication should assess their exposure, though the incident does not establish that these sectors have been disproportionately affected.
“Mid-sized organisations, SaaS providers and those with lots of vendor-managed systems are most exposed as they often do not keep track of their certificates,” said Rajesh Chhabra, general manager for India and South Asia at global cybersecurity giant Acronis.
The Ministry of Electronics and IT has issued a statement saying that the impact of this incident on Indian websites and applications have been very limited and for a very short interval. Additionally, the department has also formed a special team to investigate the matter and is engaging with relevant stakeholders.
According to CERT-In’s advisory issued on October 21, organisations should update browsers, operating systems and applications, ensure servers and devices receive current trust lists and revocation information, identify affected certificates and services, and replace them where necessary. CERT-In also advised organisations to verify certificate details and not bypass certificate warnings or disable certificate checks.
Venkata Satish Guttula, former director of security at Rediff.com India, said the eMudhra incident raised wider concerns about security audits. “Titles keep getting bigger while the people holding them get more junior. Audits look clean on paper, but the skill behind them is thin,” he posted on X, describing what he called an “illusion of competence” in security audits.
The post eMudhra Weak Link Tests India’s Chain Of Digital Trust appeared first on Inc42 Media.

The result will cover students who appeared in the first-year examinations in FA, FSc Pre-Medical, FSc Pre-Engineering, ICS, I.Com, and other intermediate study groups.
Candidates should keep their examination roll numbers ready before the announcement. Students can also visit the official BISE Sahiwal website for result updates and examination-related information.

1. Check BISE Sahiwal Board 11th Class Result 2026 Online by Roll Number
Students can check the BISE Sahiwal HSSC Part-I Result 2026 through the board’s official website. The online method allows candidates to view their first-year examination results without visiting the board office or their colleges.
Follow these steps to check the Sahiwal Board 11th Class Result 2026 online:
Visit the official BISE Sahiwal website.
Open the Online Results section on the homepage.
Select HSSC Part-I or 11th Class First Annual Examination 2026 when the relevant option becomes available.
Enter your examination roll number in the required field.
Select the correct examination year and session.
Complete the verification process if the website requests it.
Click the Submit or Search button to view your result.
Check your subject-wise marks and examination details, then save or print the result for reference.
Students should enter their roll numbers exactly as printed on their examination slips. They should also confirm that they have selected HSSC Part-I rather than HSSC Part-II before submitting their details.
The result portal may load slowly immediately after 10:00 AM because many candidates will try to access their results simultaneously. Students can wait a few minutes and try again if the website becomes temporarily unavailable.
2. Check Sahiwal Board 11th Class Result 2026 by SMS
Students who cannot access the internet can use the SMS method to check their BISE Sahiwal Board 1st Year Result 2026. The method requires a mobile phone and the candidate’s examination roll number.
The commonly listed SMS code for the Sahiwal Board is 800292. Students can use this service to request their available result information without opening the board’s website.
Follow these steps to check the result by SMS:
Open the messaging application on your mobile phone.
Create a new text message.
Type your examination roll number.
Send the message to 800292.
Wait for the reply containing the available result information.
Students should enter their roll numbers correctly and avoid adding their names, class details, or other unnecessary words. Standard mobile network charges may apply.
The SMS method provides an alternative for students who experience internet connectivity problems. If a reply does not arrive, candidates should check the official BISE Sahiwal website for updates and confirm that the SMS service is available for the 2026 examination.
3. Check BISE Sahiwal 11th Class Result Gazette 2026
The BISE Sahiwal 11th Class Result Gazette 2026 will provide another way to search for examination results after the board releases the document. The gazette contains records for multiple candidates and helps students, teachers, and educational institutions review examination results.
Students can use the gazette to search for their results by roll number. They can also search by name if the published PDF contains searchable candidate information.
BISE Sahiwal 11th Class Passing Marks 2026
The Inter Boards Coordination Commission (IBCC) has introduced a revised grading system for SSC and HSSC examinations. The new system applies to Class 11 examinations from the First Annual Examination 2026.
Under the revised policy, students must secure at least 40% marks in each subject to meet the minimum passing threshold. Candidates who score below 40% fall under the ungraded category for the relevant subject.

Internals and Software
The Poco X8s is powered by the Snapdragon 7 Gen 4 chipset.
It comes with either 8GB or 12GB of LPDDR5X RAM and 256GB or 512GB of UFS 4.0 storage.

Connectivity options reportedly include 5G, Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 5.4, NFC, USB Type-C, and an infrared blaster.
Cameras
The rear camera system includes a 50MP primary camera and an 8MP ultrawide camera.
However, the main camera configuration has not been consistently reported across different sources.

The Poco X8s packs a 6,330mAh battery with 100W wired charging, 100W PPS charging, and 22.5W wired reverse charging.

items.author: Gaurav Bagur
items.content:
San Francisco-based AI code testing startup Blacksmith has raised $66 Mn in a Series C funding round led by Sequoia Capital, bringing its total funding raised till date to $125 Mn. Premji Invest and existing investors Peak XV Partners, Google Ventures, and Y Combinator also participated in the round.
The startup raised the fresh capital at an unicorn valuation of $1 Bn, doubling in just over two months. It was valued at $550 Mn when Peak XV led its $45 Mn Series B funding round in August.
In a statement, the startup shared plans to bolster its compute infrastructure and expand its technical engineering team. It says that it currently manages nearly 10 MW of compute footprint across data centers in the United States and Europe.
It shared plans to expand its total capacity by 5X in 2027 to meet growing enterprise demand.
“Even at the start of this year, we underestimated how much code people would be shipping. We expect that volume to only keep increasing as models get better and more engineers embrace AI codegen tools. We’re building Blacksmith to help developers merge code faster and feel confident about what they’re shipping,” Aditya Jayaprakash, Blacksmith’s cofounder and CEO, wrote in a post on LinkedIn.
Founded in 2024 by Jayaprakash, Aayush Shah and Aditya Maru, Blacksmith operates a specialised cloud platform designed for automatically building and testing software code. It claims to serve more than 10,000 corporate customers worldwide, including high-growth tech firms such as Mercury, Granola, Supabase, and LangChain.
As AI agents accelerate the speed at which code is written, the bottleneck for shipping software is moving from writing the code, to validating and testing code before deploying it – a step known as continuous integration (CI).
Blacksmith claims its platform is tailor-made to absorb the spiky nature of CI demand with zero operational overhead, compared to general-purpose cloud infrastructure.
According to the company’s blog post announcing the latest funding round, weekly CI jobs processed on Blacksmith jumped to over 90 Mn from 5 Mn back in January, driving a 17X jump in ARR over the same period.

items.title: 10% inflation splits rate call predictions

items.author: Shazia Tasneem Farooqi
items.content:
Pakistan's headline inflation is expected to rise to 10% in October 2026, driven by higher electricity charges, petrol prices and food costs, while persistent inflationary pressures could prompt the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) to raise its policy rate by 50-100 basis points at its October 26 meeting, according to a Growth Securities report authored by Nasheed Malik, which projects the National Consumer Price Index (NCPI) increasing by 1.5% month-on-month (MoM), compared with 6.2% year-on-year (YoY) and 1.7% MoM in October 2025.
Average inflation during the first four months of FY27 is expected to reach 10.2%, compared with 4.8% in the corresponding period of FY26, and the October projection is above the government's expected average of 8.9% for FY27, the report said.
The transport index is expected to rise by 0.15% to 0.20% MoM following a 5.5% monthly increase in the average petrol price to Rs396.06 per litre, up 48.3% YoY, while the housing index is also expected to increase on a monthly basis due to higher electricity charges and liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) prices, which are projected to rise by 6.2% MoM.
The food index is forecast to increase by around 0.25% to 0.30% MoM, mainly due to price increases of 10% in wheat, 14% in chicken, 11% in pulse gram and 5% in garlic, according to the report.
Malik said real interest rates returned to positive territory in June 2026 and are projected to reach 1.5% in October, compared with 1.2% in September, and he expects inflation to remain in the 9% to 10% range until March 2027 if average fuel prices stay between Rs390 and Rs400 per litre, with average inflation for FY27 projected at 9% to 9.5%. He expects the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) to raise the policy rate by 50-100 basis points at its October 26, 2026 meeting if fuel prices remain elevated.
A separate assessment by AKD Securities Director Research Mohammed Awais Ashraf holds that Pakistan's improved external and fiscal position is strengthening the case for holding rates steady, with robust remittances, improving exports, record-high foreign exchange reserves and a contained current account position improving macroeconomic buffers and giving the SBP room to hold at its upcoming MPC meeting.
The successful issuance of a $3 billion Eurobond at record-low spreads had further supported external stability, and Ashraf wrote that a slowdown in large-scale manufacturing (LSM), coupled with a decline in fuel prices since the previous MPC meeting, was also expected to support a status quo decision.
He raised his FY27 inflation forecast to 9.1% from an earlier projection, reflecting a higher oil-price assumption of $96.3 per barrel compared with $72.5 previously, maintained the FY28 forecast at 6%, and pushed back the assumed start of monetary easing to April 2027 from October 2026, citing prolonged higher oil prices and a larger-than-expected rise in wheat prices.
Dubai crude declined 15.5% since the previous MPC meeting, from $127 to $107 per barrel, reflecting improved flows through the Strait of Hormuz and the end of seasonal refinery maintenance, though renewed Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure, Red Sea disruption and declining US oil inventories continue to underpin prices.
Real interest rates are expected to average 3.4% over the next 12 months, assuming normal rupee depreciation and gradual normalisation of oil prices through February 2028, with fiscal discipline improving further.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Pakistan is building Buraq, its own large language model trained on Urdu and regional languages, and procuring sovereign compute capacity so that Pakistani data is processed within Pakistan, Federal Minister for IT and Telecom said at the Global AI and Digital Summit 2026 in Seoul.
The minister told a World Bank panel on digital government service delivery that the model, and the public compute capacity behind it, form the AI layer of a programme built on four foundations, according to a statement issued by the Ministry of IT on Wednesday.
On digital identity, the National Database and Registration Authority provides verified identity to more than 100 million Pakistanis, now extended into a digital identity that authenticates citizens online and records and enforces consent. On payments, the State Bank's Raast instant payment rail turns an AI model's identification of a qualifying household into delivery.
On data, WASL, the national exchange layer of the Digital Public Infrastructure stack built under the World Bank-supported Digital Economy Enhancement Project, lets institutions share data with every transaction authenticated, encrypted and logged. A citizen Super App and the National Open Data Ecosystem sit on top. On safeguards, the National Data Governance Policy sets a single rulebook for classifying, sharing, protecting and publishing public data.
Governments that skip the foundations get pilots that never scale and systems citizens do not trust, she said. AI is the last layer, not the first.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) rebounded on Wednesday as institutional investors returned to buy select stocks following recent weakness, while expectations of progress in diplomatic efforts to ease US-Iran tensions helped improve sentiment.
The session commenced on a relatively healthy note and the KSE-100 index hit 165,845.69, up 694 points by 9.33 am. Adding to the positive tone, a committee reviewing Pakistan's Automotive and Auto Parts Manufacturing Policy 2026-31 proposed a broad set of reforms to boost exports, including preferential sales tax rates for new energy vehicles (NEVs), covering both locally assembled and imported cars.
The bourse touched the intra-day high of 166,242.43 and low of 164,731.91 while mostly trading in the green. At close, the benchmark KSE-100 index posted gains of 779.34 points, or 0.47%, and settled at 165,930.99.
According to KTrade Securities, the KSE-100 rose 779 points (+0.5%), a partial recovery with subdued trading volumes of 130 million shares. Activity remained concentrated in refinery, investment companies and securities, and technology and communication sectors, while selective buying in power generation, commercial banks and oil and gas exploration stocks provided support.
Sector-specific performance was positive, where commercial banks, power, cement and autos contributed to the index's gains. However, weakness in Attock Refinery, Fatima Fertiliser, Engro Holdings, Fauji Cement and Millat Tractors partially offset the advance. Meanwhile, Brent crude remained elevated at $110/barrel, causing macroeconomic uncertainty and tempering the risk appetite.
"We expect the market to remain range bound amid cautious investor sentiment, with near-term direction driven by oil-price movements, geopolitical developments and corporate earnings," KTrade wrote.
"The market gained momentum amid renewed institutional buying, driven by optimism over intensified diplomatic efforts to resolve the US-Iran conflict and expectations of easing geopolitical tensions. Additionally, the prime minister's approval of the draft auto policy for 2026-31 brought auto stocks back into investors' focus," Arif Habib Limited Deputy Head of Trading Ali Najib wrote. The proposed auto policy aims to boost automotive exports to $6 billion through tariff rationalisation, localisation and EV incentives. The draft also envisages export-linked incentives and stricter safety standards, subject to requisite approvals. Hub Power, Habib Bank, UBL, OGDC, Mari Energies, PPL, Fauji Fertiliser, Sazgar Engineering, Lucky Cement and NCPL were the major contributors, adding 711 points to the index.
Overall trading volumes decreased to 379.9 million shares from 446.8 million a day ago. The value of traded shares stood at Rs21.3 billion.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Verifiable sales records and digital cash flows could help Pakistani small businesses overcome a major barrier to bank financing: their inability to demonstrate reliable financial performance, as digital banking platforms seek to bring undocumented businesses into the formal financial system.
A large number of Pakistan's micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) operate without formal registration or digitised accounts, making it difficult for banks to assess their creditworthiness. Consequently, lenders often demand collateral, which many small businesses cannot provide. Speaking at the launch of NEO BIZ, a digital banking service for SMEs, Mashreq Bank Pakistan CEO Muhammad Hamayun Sajjad said businesses often maintained bookkeeping records that banks did not consider reliable enough for lending decisions.
Pakistan has approximately 7.14 million MSMEs, contributing nearly 40% to gross domestic product (GDP), 30% to exports and employing more than 80% of the non-agricultural workforce. However, outstanding SME financing stood at around Rs882 billion as of December 2025, according to figures cited at the event.
Digital-first banking models could help bridge this gap by creating verifiable records of business transactions, including sales, payments and collections. Banks could use these records to assess turnover, analyse cash-flow patterns and evaluate repayment capacity, potentially enabling creditworthy businesses without conventional financial statements to access loans.
However, digital records alone would not guarantee financing, as lenders would still need to assess profitability, liabilities and business risks. NEO BIZ like services offer digital business account opening and management, payments and collections. Its broader roadmap includes transaction analytics, invoicing, bookkeeping, payroll solutions and business debit and virtual cards.
The planned development also includes cash-flow-based financing, tax facilitation and supply-chain services. Whether these features translate into increased lending will depend on their implementation and banks' credit policies. "Pakistan's SME sector is both dynamic and under-served, with significant gaps in access, awareness and digital capability," Sajjad said, adding that the platform was intended to simplify banking and reduce reliance on physical channels.
The initiative comes amid a longstanding debate over whether banks' substantial exposure to government borrowing crowds out private-sector lending. Banks have argued that the relationship is not straightforward, maintaining that they can obtain liquidity through the State Bank of Pakistan open market operations (OMOs) while holding government securities and extending credit to businesses.

items.author: Anadolu Agency
items.content:
Electronic Arts (EA) plans to lay off 400 employees, close its BioWare studio and cancel the next "Mass Effect" game, Bloomberg reported on Wednesday.
The layoffs will affect 3% of the US video game publisher’s workforce, including 50 employees at BioWare, the studio behind the popular "Mass Effect" and "Dragon Age" franchises.
In an internal letter, EA executives said the company reviewed its operations and decided to cancel several projects to reduce costs.
Read: Saudi-led consortium finalises $55b acquisition of gaming giant EA
“Across our portfolio, we’re making deliberate choices to align talent and investments where we see the greatest opportunities for players and long-term growth,” they wrote.
EA will also cancel a planned game in "The Sims" franchise, code-named "Project Lotus", while reducing the team developing the skateboarding game “skate”.
The company said it would continue investing in its sports games, “Apex Legends”, “Battlefield” and upcoming “Star Wars” and Marvel titles.
Founded in 1995 and acquired by EA in 2007, BioWare struggled in recent years with disappointing game releases and declining sales.
The restructuring follows EA’s $55 billion Saudi-led buyout in August, which took the company private and added $18 billion in debt.

items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
Punjab Information Minister Azma Bokhari on Wednesday rejected the criticism surrounding the alleged police encounter in which a man accused of killing a 15-year-old boy was himself killed, categorically denying that Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz had ordered the Punjab Crime Control Department (CCD) to carry out encounters and asserting that the provincial government stood with the oppressed, not the oppressors.
The suspect, Tauqeer Nazir, had allegedly chased Waseem Abbas in his car after a dispute over work and run him over in a private housing society in Multan on Monday. He was arrested and handed over to police on a four-day physical remand by a judicial magistrate the following day. Earlier today, police said the suspect fled custody and was then killed by his accomplices when a police party tried to re-arrest him.
Hours before the incident, the prime suspect in the case involving the death by suicide of former International Islamic University Islamabad student Laiba Ejaz also died after being wounded by gunfire allegedly by his accomplices during an attack on a police team in Islamabad. The developments were met with criticism, with calls for justice through the legal route and the courts.
Read: HRCP calls for independent probe into Waseem Abbas case, expresses concern over alleged extrajudicial killing of prime suspect
In an interview on local television programme Aaj Shahzeb Khanzada Kay Sath about the killing of Multan incident's primary suspect, the minister was asked about hundreds of alleged extrajudicial killings by the CCD, in which the main suspect was reportedly killed while accomplices escaped, rejecting the suggestion that this pattern occurred in every case.
She said that even when a suspect was killed, the remaining suspects were subsequently traced, arrested and brought before the police.
“When a suspect is killed, the investigation slows down a little. When suspects flee, it takes some time to trace them. But this does not mean that this happens in every incident,” she said.
Asked whether the chief minister had directly ordered the CCD to carry out encounters against such suspects, the minister categorically denied it.
“Why would the chief minister order an encounter? It is not as if she has foreknowledge of such incidents,” she said.
“The state has a responsibility to stand with the oppressed. You may consider this a mistake on the part of the state or an allegation against it; you may call it whatever you like, but the Punjab government does not stand with the oppressor. It stands with the oppressed,” she said.
She added that there was no backdoor for the powerful in the province to evade the law or avoid facing legal proceedings.
Also Read: Man accused of running over Multan teenager killed in CCD encounter
Bokhari said an investigation had revealed that the Multan incident suspect was short-tempered and ill-mannered and had treated Abbas harshly. She said the boy had tried to flee three times but was caught each time.
She said the suspect’s actions demonstrated his mindset, alleging that he chased the teenager and killed him while the latter was attempting to escape through a gate. The minister added that the brutality was such that the victim’s face had become unrecognisable.
Bokhari further alleged that Nazir was a violent person who did not treat his own children properly and subjected them to violence as well.
The minister acknowledged that he had no previous criminal record and that, given the evidence against him, including CCTV footage, a court could have sentenced him. However, she said, he chose to flee rather than face trial.
“These are criminal-minded people. He could have been punished by a court, but if someone tries to escape from the court, or his accomplices help him flee, what can the police do?” she said.
Read: Primary suspect in Laiba Ejaz suicide case dies after being shot by accomplices: police
When asked about a post on X by PML-N MPA and Punjab government official Hina Pervez Butt that was later deleted, Bokhari questioned the seriousness of the former’s statements.
“I do not want to talk about her, but she has posted such things before, perhaps out of a lack of seriousness. She has also made statements that created problems for her and caused embarrassment for the government,” she said.
Earlier in the day, Hina had shared screenshots of a television report about the Multan encounter on X, drawing criticism for her supportive remarks.
“This is Maryam Nawaz sahiba’s government; justice is served immediately here,” she wrote in a post that was later deleted amid criticism over its perceived endorsement of an extrajudicial killing under the provincial government’s watch.
Bokhari said cases involving organised crime were referred to the CCD rather than the regular police to ensure more effective investigation and prosecution and to meet all legal requirements for delivering justice.
She said the CCD had arrested hundreds, possibly thousands, of criminals, adding that public discussion should also focus on those who had been prosecuted and punished rather than only on the few hundred suspects who had allegedly tried to flee.
The minister reiterated that the chief minister had not ordered any encounter, adding that the government stood with the oppressed rather than the oppressors.
On judicial reforms, Bokhari said Pakistan was among the few countries with a large number of judicial laws, but the key issue was their implementation.
She added that the chief minister was also working to revamp the prosecution system and that considerable progress had been made in this regard.
Allegations of extrajudicial killings and increasingly unlawful conduct by Punjab’s CCD have long been a source of concern for human rights organisations, which have repeatedly raised the issue.
According to figures released by the Human Rights Commission of Pakistan in June, the organisation had documented 808 police ‘encounters’ since the CCD was established in April 2025, in which at least 1,100 suspects were killed.
Earlier today, it expressed concern over Abbas's killing and the subsequent death of the primary suspect in an alleged police encounter, calling for an independent and transparent investigation into the case.
The commission said extrajudicial killings violated the right to due process and deprived victims and their families of the opportunity to establish the truth and seek justice.
It added that the perception that such killings were an acceptable means of controlling crime suggested that vengeance without accountability was being prioritised over justice.
The HRCP called for an independent and transparent investigation into the case and urged the authorities to bring an end to extrajudicial killings in all forms.

items.title: eMudhra security breach: What it means for smartphone, internet users
items.summary: Researchers found that eight digital certificates issued by eMudhra had weak secret keys that could be easily exploited. Browser companies like Google, Apple, Microsoft, and Mozilla responded by blocking these certificates rapidly. eMudhra explained that a flaw during the creation process led to the publication of the weak keys. Importantly, no evidence suggests these weak keys were used in actual attacks so far.

items.author: APP
items.content:
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Wednesday handed Rs5 million to the family of late student Laiba Ejaz during a visit to her residence to offer condolences and brief the family on progress in the case.
Laiba, who had aspired to study at a top US university, was found hanging from a tree near a road in Islamabad on October 9, after her family allegedly lost around Rs7 million to a consultant who had promised to secure her admission and a scholarship.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif took notice of the incident and directed the inspector general of Islamabad police and the chief commissioner to take immediate action against the suspect. Naqvi also vowed to look into the case personally. The primary suspect in the case died after being wounded by gunfire from his own accomplices during an exchange of fire with police in Islamabad a day ago.
Laiba's father told The Express Tribune that the interior minister handed him Rs5 million recovered by the police from the primary suspect.
Naqvi was accompanied by Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry during the visit to Laiba's residence in G-10, Islamabad.
Read: PM takes notice of gold medallist's suicide
Naqvi expressed his condolences to the bereaved family and offered prayers.
The interior minister informed Laiba's family about the progress made in the investigation of her case/
“The entire team worked day and night on the Laiba Ejaz case. Fulfilling the promise made to you was our duty,” Naqvi said.
Read More: Primary suspect in Laiba Ejaz suicide case dies after being shot by accomplices: police
Laiba's father expressed his gratitude to PM Shehbaz and the interior minister for their support and efforts in the case.
“We had heard that the state is like a mother. Today, we have come to believe it,” he said.
Suspect killed
According to a police spokesperson, the primary suspect, identified as Muhammad Nauman, was in custody and was being taken to a location for recovery on the basis of information provided by him when the incident occurred.
The spokesperson said four of Nauman’s accomplices, travelling on two motorcycles, had been lying in wait along the route. They opened indiscriminate fire on the police team in an attempt to secure his release.
Nauman was wounded by gunfire from his own accomplices, the spokesperson said, adding that police personnel remained unharmed due to their bulletproof jackets and other precautionary measures.
The injured suspect was taken to a hospital for medical treatment but later succumbed to his injuries, the spokesperson confirmed.
Search operations were under way to arrest the remaining suspects, according to the police.
The Federal Investigation Agency’s (FIA) Anti-Human Trafficking Circle in Islamabad had registered a case against Nauman and Fatima Sarwar under Sections 419 (cheating), 420 (cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property) and 109 (abetment) of the Pakistan Penal Code, read with Sections 18 and 22 of the Emigration Ordinance, 1979.
Preliminary investigations revealed that the suspects allegedly acted in connivance to deceive Laiba with promises of a US visa and scholarship. They allegedly received a total of Rs9.3 million from the family.
The FIA said the suspects allegedly prepared fake scholarship award letters, university admission offer letters and fee payment receipts to keep the family under the impression that the process was genuine. Of the total amount, Rs2.9m was transferred through Laiba’s personal bank account, while the remaining sum was received in cash, according to the agency.
Also Read: Islamabad court grants five-day remand of suspect in Laiba suicide case
Laiba's family stated that she had aspired to enrol at Harvard University for further studies and that they had made significant financial sacrifices to secure Laiba’s academic future and fulfil her dream. Laiba’s father sold his plot and pitched in Rs2.1 million from the sale’s proceeds, while her mother sold her gold jewellery.
According to the family, the suspect who reportedly defrauded them claimed to be an accounts officer at the Islamabad High Court and at other times presented himself as an employee of the superior judiciary or an officer of a sensitive institution. The family claimed that despite the substantial payment, the promises regarding admission and the scholarship given to Laiba were never fulfilled.
Laiba’s maternal uncle, Rana Amjad, stated that the Harvard University admission letter, scholarship letter and other documents provided by the suspect turned out to be fake upon verification.
He said that Laiba suffered severe distress and mental anguish after the alleged fraud came to light. Her family demanded a thorough investigation into the matter, the arrest of all individuals involved in the alleged fraud, and the recovery of the money.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Federal Minister for Information Technology Shaza Fatima Khawaja has said that Pakistan must establish strong digital infrastructure before expanding the use of artificial intelligence (AI). Shaza Fatima shared these views during a discussion on digital public infrastructure and AI at the Global AI and Digital Summit 2026 in South Korea.
Speaking on the third day of the summit, Shaza Fatima explained that AI represents the final layer of digital development. She stressed that countries need reliable digital systems, secure data-sharing mechanisms, and effective public services to make the best use of AI.
Shaza Fatima Highlights Pakistan’s Digital Transformation at Digital Summit 2026 in South Korea
The minister highlighted Pakistan’s ongoing efforts to build its national digital public infrastructure. Under a World Bank initiative to support the development of the digital economy, Pakistan is working to establish its first national digital public infrastructure system.
She said the National Database and Registration Authority (NADRA) provides verified digital identity services to more than 10 million Pakistanis. This identity system serves as an important foundation for delivering digital public services.
The minister also highlighted Raast, the State Bank of Pakistan’s instant payment system, which enables digital payments across the country. She said such systems are essential for improving access to financial services and supporting the growth of the digital economy.
Shaza Fatima also discussed Wasil, Pakistan’s national data exchange system. The platform enables government institutions to share information securely under clear rules and procedures. It aims to improve coordination between public sector organizations and make digital services more efficient.
According to the minister, work is also underway to develop a central mobile application for citizens and a national open data system on top of Wasil. These initiatives are expected to make public information and government services more accessible.
She further noted that the Pakistan Digital Authority has issued a National Data Governance Policy to establish a clear framework for managing and sharing data. The policy is intended to promote responsible data use and provide clear rules for digital governance.
See Also: Pakistan Highlights Sovereign AI Vision at Global AI and Digital Summit 2026 in Seoul
The minister emphasized that Pakistan’s approach to AI would keep human decision-making at the center. She said AI would assist people in making decisions but would not independently determine anyone’s rights or entitlements.
This approach aims to ensure that AI supports public services without replacing human judgment in decisions that directly affect citizens.
Pakistan is also working to develop sovereign AI infrastructure and Buraq, a Pakistani language model designed to support the Urdu language. These efforts could help the country build local AI capabilities and develop technology that better serves its linguistic and digital needs.
The Global AI and Digital Summit 2026 provides a platform for countries to discuss the future of AI, digital governance, and public digital infrastructure. Pakistan’s participation reflects its efforts to strengthen digital public services, improve data management, and build the foundations needed for wider AI adoption.

items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
The federal government on Wednesday decreased the price of petrol by Rs2.71 per litre while increasing the price of high-speed diesel (HSD) by 31 paisas per litre for October 22.
According to a notification issued by the Petroleum Division, the price of petrol was fixed at Rs379.31 per litre, while HSD would cost Rs390.11 per litre for Thursday.
The latest revision comes a day after the government increased the price of petrol and HSD by 88 paisas and 53 paisas per litre, respectively, for October 21.
Read: Govt increases petrol by 88 paisas, diesel by 53 paisas per litre for Oct 21
On July 17, the government announced a new pricing mechanism under which petroleum product prices would be reviewed and notified daily, replacing the weekly pricing mechanism, as renewed tensions between the United States and Iran continued to drive volatility in global oil markets and raise concerns over fuel supplies.
On September 13, PM Shehbaz announced a special relief scheme offering Rs100 per litre off petrol for motorcycles, three-wheeler rickshaws and cars with engines up to 800cc, in an attempt to shield lower-income consumers from the impact of rising petroleum prices.
Under the proposal, an estimated 11.8 million beneficiaries would be covered. Around 10 million two-wheeler users and 800,000 three-wheeler users would be entitled to relief on 20 litres of fuel per month, translating into a maximum monthly benefit of Rs2,000 per beneficiary.
Another one million users of cars up to 800cc would receive relief on 30 litres per month, providing them with a maximum benefit of Rs3,000 each.
On Sept 17, the government reintroduced austerity and fuel conservation measures amid rising fuel prices, tightening business operating hours and restricting public events.
Under the measures, notified with immediate effect, shops, markets, shopping malls, bazaars, departmental stores, grocery stores, general stores and kiryana shops would close by 9pm throughout the week, according to a notification issued by the Cabinet Division.
Marriage halls, marquees and other commercial venues hosting festive events would close by 10pm, while restaurants, cafes, eateries, food outlets and standalone fruit and vegetable shops would be allowed to operate until 11pm. Takeaway and home delivery services would remain exempt from the timing restrictions.
Global geopolitical developments continue to pose significant risks. International oil prices are influenced by decisions taken by OPEC+, conflicts in the Middle East, sanctions on oil-producing nations, and disruptions in critical shipping routes such as the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea. Any interruption in these supply chains can immediately increase crude oil prices and freight costs. Since Pakistan imports the majority of its petroleum requirements, these developments quickly translate into higher domestic fuel prices.
Oil prices were little changed on Wednesday ‌as investors weighed possible progress toward Russia-Ukraine talks against declining US oil stocks and a lack of US-Iran dialogue.
Brent crude futures gained 27 cents, or 0.2%, to $109.04 a barrel by 10:50 am ET (1450 GMT). US West Texas Intermediate crude was down 11 cents, or 0.1%, to $97.72.
"Crude futures are trading both sides of unchanged this morning but well below the overnight highs as attacks in the ​Strait of Hormuz look to be continuing with at least two more ships being struck overnight," said Dennis Kissler, senior vice president of ​trading at BOK Financial, in a note to clients.

items.title: SBI Reports Suspected Data Exposure Affecting 3,897 Customer Records
items.summary: SBI received alerts about the suspected exposure on October 16 from its Threat Intelligence Service Provider, the Defence Cyber Agency and CERT-In. Its preliminary review covered around 375,000 records available on the dark web, of which 3,897 contained personally identifiable information. The exposed details reportedly included names, contact information, residential addresses and identifiers linked to branches and loan records. SBI activated its cyber incident response procedures and appointed an independent CERT-In-empanelled agency to investigate the incident and assess potential risks.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Global shipments of foldable smartphone displays are expected to increase significantly in 2026, with a growing interest in wide foldable devices. Market research firm Omdia forecasts a 44% rise in foldable display shipments this year, following a 12% decline in 2025.
According to the forecast, manufacturers will ship around 29 million foldable displays in 2026. However, this figure refers specifically to the inner screens used in foldable smartphones, not the final devices. Display shipments and smartphone sales may differ because manufacturers usually ship components before completing and releasing their products.
Despite this difference, the forecast suggests that 2026 could be a strong year for the foldable smartphone market.
Foldable Display Shipments to Increase 44% in 2026 as Wide Foldables Gain Popularity
One of the most notable findings in Omdia’s report is the growing demand for wide foldable displays. These displays are expected to account for 44% of total foldable display shipments in 2026, putting them close to half of the market.
The foldable smartphone market currently includes three main designs: wide foldables, book-style devices with larger and squarer inner screens, and compact flip-style phones.
The increasing popularity of wide foldables is expected to reshape competition among smartphone manufacturers. Devices such as the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 and Apple’s reported iPhone Duo are among the products driving interest in this design.
As more companies explore wider foldable phones, manufacturers may place greater emphasis on screen proportions and usability to attract consumers.
Samsung Display Expected to Lead the Market
Samsung Display is expected to benefit considerably from the growing demand for foldable screens. According to Omdia, the company could capture 66% of the foldable display market in 2026.
Samsung Display manufactures panels for both the Galaxy Z Fold8 and Apple’s iPhone Duo, putting it in a strong position as demand for wide foldables increases.
Meanwhile, competing display manufacturers, including BOE, China Star, Tianma and Visionox, are expected to see their market shares decline.
The forecast highlights Samsung Display’s strong position in the foldable screen industry, particularly as more smartphone brands consider adopting wider foldable designs.
Chinese Manufacturers May Increase Competition
Although demand for foldable smartphones remains weak in China, Omdia expects competition to increase as more Chinese manufacturers enter the wide foldable segment.
Huawei was among the early companies to introduce this form factor. However, other manufacturers appear to be taking a more serious interest in the design as its market potential becomes clearer.
Greater participation from Chinese brands could lead to more product choices and increased competition in the coming years.
LTPO Displays Expected to Dominate
Another important trend is the expected dominance of LTPO display technology in foldable smartphones. Omdia forecasts that most foldable displays manufactured in 2026 will use LTPO rather than LTPS technology.
LTPO displays offer more precise refresh-rate control, allowing screens to adjust their refresh rates according to the content being displayed. This can help reduce power consumption while maintaining a smooth viewing experience.
Although LTPO panels generally cost more than LTPS displays, their benefits make them an attractive option for premium foldable smartphones.
Since foldable devices already occupy the higher end of the smartphone market. Manufacturers are likely to continue using advanced display technologies to improve performance and user experience.
Foldable Smartphone Market Outlook
Omdia’s forecast points to renewed growth in the foldable display market during 2026. Rising demand for wide foldables, Samsung Display’s strong position and the wider adoption of LTPO technology are expected to shape the industry.
However, display shipment figures do not directly represent the number of foldable smartphones sold. Actual device sales will depend on product availability, pricing and consumer demand.
If the forecast proves accurate, 2026 could mark an important step forward for foldable smartphones, with wider designs becoming a more significant part of the market.

Industry executives including Norwest Venture Partners’ George Still Jr, ServiceNow CPO and COO Amit Zavery, and Charlesbank Capital Partners’ MD Giacomo Santina also joined the startup’s cap table.

It helps enterprises accelerate AI deployment with Damia, a platform it describes as an “AI workbench for enterprise delivery”. It combines a pre-built skill catalogue with tools that capture institutional knowledge to build a context layer.
AuxoAI says that it is an AI-native Google Gemini Enterprise Transformation partner and an AWS advanced-tier partner. The San Francisco-based startup operates engineering and operational hubs in Mumbai, Bengaluru and Hyderabad.
Over the past three years, the startup claims that it has worked with over 40 clients across manufacturing, healthcare, consumer goods, and telecom sectors to turn AI into measurable business outcomes.
Early adopters, such as marketing firm Athlonearth and restaurant group Fogo de Chao, have deployed AuxoAI’s infrastructure to automate manual tasks, make better informed decisions, and shorten strategy-to-launch timelines.
As enterprises increasingly turn to AI adoption to boost productivity, FDEs are becoming increasingly critical for customising AI deployments to the company’s needs. According to staffing firm TeamLease Digital, demand for FDEs has jumped nearly 800% over the past year.
Startups such as Bolna use FDEs to accelerate enterprise onboarding and shape product development. While better automation could eventually reduce deployment complexity, fragmented enterprise systems make FDEs increasingly important to AI adoption.
